body:
The front end re-typed panel_core's words and constants by hand. Now Rust is the one source; `crates/panel_gen` (`nix run .#gen`, ev_lib `ts_gen`) writes them, and a `generated` pre-commit hook re-runs it and re-stages the output.

**Role / permissions / caller**
- `panel_core::role::Permission` + `Role::may(Permission)` replace six per-permission methods; call sites updated.
- `/me` answers the gate's `Caller` (Serialize + ts-rs); `MeDto` deleted.
- TS: `managesX(role)` → `MAY[role].x` (the evaluated table); `Me` → `Caller`; `role.ts` keeps only `startRouteFor`.

**Word sets and constants** (`frontend/src/**/generated.ts`): STAGES, SUSPECTS, FLOWS, BOOKING_STATUSES, BOOKING_MATCHES, DAY_PARTS, BOOKING_PROVIDERS, PAGE_PROVIDERS (`Provider::has_page`), SOURCE_KINDS, KEYED_SOURCE_KINDS (`SourceKind::keyed`, used by the API's add-source check), CURRENCIES, QUOTE_CURRENCY (`pricing::CURRENCY`), CONTACT_SLA_SECONDS (from `funnel::CONTACT_SLA`, in seconds like the API's `waiting_seconds`), IDEMPOTENCY_HEADER. The dev stub reads FLOWS / BOOKING_STATUSES from the same output.

**Drift fixed. In both cases Rust was right:**
- Currencies: TS offered **CHF**, while the API accepts EUR, USD, GBP, **AUD**. The API list is what's enforced (`api.rs` CURRENCIES, 400 otherwise) and what docs/ARCHITECTURE.md ("The operator API") states. Both lists were written the same evening (6784ca3 server, da10089 front end), so the front end's CHF was a typo-level divergence. A CHF quote/payment was a guaranteed 400. The form now offers AUD.
- SourceKind: TS lacked **booking**, added to Rust in 7990c6b (2026-10-04, the booking events). TS also offered **panel** in the add-source form, which the API refuses (`kind panel → 400`, as is booking). The parser now takes all eight kinds, and the form offers only `SourceKind::keyed()` ones.

**Blocked on EV-invest/lib#191:** ev_lib is a git dependency on that branch, because CI's pre-step strips `[patch]`. After it merges and 0.24.1 is published, go back to `version = "0.24.1"` and run `cargo update -p ev_lib`. Until then `nix build` (cargoLock without outputHashes for a git dep) won't build the binary.

Checked locally: `cargo b --workspace --all-targets` and clippy clean, `cargo test --workspace` green, frontend typecheck/lint/vitest (384) green, `next build` ok, dev stub boots.

## Scope

Rust SDK delivery for [Fitz #358](https://github.com/cntryl/fitz/issues/358), following broker [#374](https://github.com/cntryl/fitz/pull/374). Stable publication remains pending.

## Changes

- Negotiate RPC cancellation and remaining budgets before connection readiness; preserve explicit legacy capability zero.
- Expose synchronous cooperative worker cancellation and explicit parent links for downstream calls.
- Retain execution credit until cleanup acknowledgment, and remove buffered request payloads immediately when canceled.
- Reject downstream calls under an already canceled parent and document indeterminate effects and retry boundaries.
- Add candidate-only hosted chain acceptance while preserving published-main conformance qualification.

## Evidence

Independent immutable review cleared `ffc9f4eeb3b65158eaecef898fa8d1dff66cfe14` after focused red/green regressions. Final local tests: 108 unit tests, all-target/all-feature tests including 12 lifecycle tests, formatting, strict pedantic Clippy and 85/85 validation guidelines. Three real chain/opaque-response scenarios passed in all four TCP/WebSocket × anonymous/JWT modes against source-equivalent merged broker `f4b39e0b`.

## Hosted qualification and release boundary

Candidate Spec is dispatched with `broker_tag=develop` (broker manifest `sha256:c651e80d56c0e1126d9d7b78418de72a5b719cb18e0691137def703d926dc59b`), including all four chain modes. Published-main conformance remains separate. No stable tag, crate publication or broker Publish workflow is included.

Cancellation remains best effort; it does not prove execution stopped, roll back side effects or authorize retry after dispatch. Jev supplied design questions; source and tests establish acceptance.

Final hosted CI passed stable and MSRV1.88.0 plus security checks; Rust and Actions CodeQL passed. [Candidate Spec](https://github.com/cntryl/fitz-rs/actions/runs/37247658967) passed canonical conformance and all four live chain modes at the exact source. body:
## Purpose

Build the first real substrate bridge from Weaver execution into SolSpire observability, while adding the missing governance records identified by PR #292.

### Implemented

- Explicit `ExecutionAttempt → WorkEvent` bridge
- Durable `execution_attempt_ref` on the existing WorkEvent spine
- Idempotent execution-to-WorkEvent capture
- Acceptance record gated by VERIFIED result
- Review record referencing immutable WorkEvent
- Completion record gated by accepted review + explicit supporting evidence
- Production-acceptance record gated by COMPLETED result
- Optional acceptance binding on Weaver Authorization
- Regression/invariant tests
- Architecture documentation

### Preserved boundaries

`Acceptance ≠ Authorization ≠ Execution ≠ WorkEvent ≠ Review ≠ Completion ≠ Production Acceptance`

The historical 144-cell Oversoul Prism lattice remains research-only and gains no runtime authority.

### Verification target

CI should prove:
1. terminal Weaver execution creates exactly one causally linked WorkEvent;
2. replay is idempotent;
3. WorkEvent capture does not imply completion;
4. governance records cannot skip their preceding boundary.

body:
## Summary

Implements the game engine: the rules, the state machine, the views that decide what each seat and the client may see, and the 30-set daily word bank. Nothing in it calls a model or does I/O.

## Context

Plan §02 (rules), §04 (data model), §05 (engine). ADR 0002: the code is the referee and the model only gets a seat.

## Changes

- `words.ts`: 30 hand-written sets with same-category decoys and generic fallback clues; the daily rotation starts at set 0 on 2026-10-05 and numbers puzzles from there; a seeded PRNG for role dealing.
- `validate.ts`: clue rules (one word, letters/hyphens, not the word or its 4-letter stem, no repeats), vote validity, last-guess matching with plurals, and a scrub of the secret word from public text. Secret-word checks are skipped for the imposter, since refusing its clue as "too close" would tell it the answer.
- `game.ts`: `createGame`, sequential clue rounds with order rotation, capped discussion, plurality vote (ties favor the imposter), last guess, scoring, grudge changes, watch-mode calls and Take a seat. Pure functions that throw `EngineError` on invalid moves.
- `view.ts`: `seatView` (imposter's `word` is `null`) and `publicView` (roles, traces, and others' votes hidden until due; watch-mode audience sees the word).
- `types.ts`: adds `grudges` to `GameState`.

## Validation

Automated, on this commit's worktree:
- `pnpm test`: 42 passed, including the hidden-information test that serializes `seatView` for every word set and every imposter seat and checks the word never appears.
- `pnpm typecheck`: clean. `pnpm lint`: 0 errors (remaining warnings are unused args in other modules' stubs).

Not tested: no model, route, or UI code exists yet; nothing here is simulated or played.

## Notes & Risks

None for this layer. The decoy and generic lists are hand-picked and will be judged by the sim in the agents PR.

author: roberth-souza
body:
## Summary
- Thumbnail, preview and first-frame caches are content-addressed (abspath+mtime+size+dims), so every edited/renamed/deleted wallpaper and every target-size change left an orphan forever. On the author's machine that was ~230 MB for a 54-wallpaper library (448 thumbnails, 24 previews, 26 first frames).
- New `core/cachegc.py`: each cache dir keeps an `index.json` manifest (digest → source path, last seen). Pruned once per library reload on a single-thread pool, off the UI thread (~25 ms total here).
- Deleted: files with no manifest record, whose source was removed or changed, or superseded by a new target size; abandoned atomic-write temps older than 1 h.
- Kept: the current library (never evicted), sources in other intact folders (switching folders doesn't regenerate everything) and sources whose folder is unreachable (unmounted drive). Those are evicted least-recently-seen past a per-dir cap (200 MB thumbnails / 100 MB previews / 200 MB first frames).
- Each cache only indexes the kinds it generates (`supports()`), so image entries don't bloat the preview/first-frame manifests.
- Only filenames the cache writers produce (`<sha1>.<ext>`, their temps) are ever deleted, so a misconfigured cache dir can't touch user files.
- Result here: ~230 MB → ~30 MB, identical whether migrated from the dirty cache or rebuilt from scratch.

- `Shift+D` now moves the wallpaper to the trash (`QFile.moveToTrash`, freedesktop spec, no new dependency) instead of unlinking it, so a stray chord is recoverable. If the file can't be trashed it is left in place with a status message — never a permanent-delete fallback. Its cache entries are left to the GC, so restoring the file before the next reload keeps them.

author: teknium1
body:
## Problem

`agent/image_routing.py:339-341` (`_lookup_supports_vision` docstring) says the lookup ends with a "registered `ProviderProfile.supports_vision` declaration" probe, and `tools/vision_tools.py:562` (`_accepts_tool_result_images`) says the same ("→ probes → profile"). `_VISION_PROBES` (`agent/image_routing.py:323-327`) has no such probe. It was added in 9de45d95951 and **deliberately removed** in 08feaa98b5b. `ProviderProfile.supports_vision` is a provider-wide flag meaning "tool-result messages may carry images" (`providers/base.py:78-85`). Relays such as `router` set it over mixed catalogs, so using it to route attachments sent images to text-only models.

The stale docstring caused a misdiagnosis. Triage of NousResearch/hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk#67 read it as an attachment-path bug and proposed adding the probe back.

Real probe on `origin/main` (1fd75357e92) with a fake registered profile and the catalog stubbed out:

```
probe-wide     (supports_vision=True)                      attach: text   | tool-result media: True
probe-permodel (model_capabilities={m: supports_vision:True}) attach: native | tool-result media: False
```

Both results match the intended design. Only the docs are wrong.

## Fix

- Correct both docstrings. The attachment lookup uses the config override, then the managed runtime, then the catalog (which includes the profile's `model_capabilities`), then Ollama. The provider-wide flag is intentionally not consulted, and the docstring now says why.
- Add one guard test (`tests/agent/test_models_dev_provider_capabilities.py::test_provider_wide_vision_flag_gates_tool_results_not_attachments`). It registers a profile with `supports_vision=True` and one `model_capabilities` entry, then checks three things: tool-result media is on, an undeclared model's attachments stay `text`, and the declared model's attachments go `native`. This pins the contract so the probe isn't brought back.

There is no runtime behavior change. For the plugin issue, the fix belongs in the plugin: declare per-model `model_capabilities={...: {"supports_vision": True}}` (see `website/docs/developer-guide/model-provider-plugin.md` § "Declaring model capabilities").

## Tests (A/B)

- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_models_dev_provider_capabilities.py tests/agent/test_image_routing.py tests/tools/test_vision_native_fast_path.py tests/agent/test_custom_providers_vision.py`: 79 passed, 0 failed.
- Mutation A/B: putting the reverted `_probe_provider_profile` back into `_VISION_PROBES` makes the new test fail (1 failed, 2 passed). It passes again with the probe removed (this branch / main).
- Since this is a docs + guard-test change, the test passes on main by design. It fails if someone brings back the reverted behavior.

body:
## What changes

### Time limits

- Every compiler the speed suite starts runs under a build limit.
  The default is 900 s, and `$DEWASM_BUILD_TIMEOUT` sets it in seconds.
- Every process a pair starts shares one run limit, `--timeout`.
  It applied to each process alone before; its default is now 600 s.
  So the worst cost of one pair is the two limits together.
- At either limit the process is killed with every process below it.
  Killing it alone left a child holding the output pipes, and the reader waited for that child.
- A pair past a limit is recorded as `timed_out`, with the phase and the limit.
  It is not a failure, and the run continues.
- `results.md` lists it under "Not measured" with the kind `time limit`.
  Its chart shows `(build timeout)` or `(timeout)` where the rule and dot would be.

The builds had no limit at all.
The newest Spinel stayed in one analysis pass over the SQLite source for more than 30 minutes.

### Records

A full speed record and a size record, with `results.md` and the charts of each.

- `cowsay` is cowsay.wasm 0.3.0, a different program, so its rows are a new baseline.
- The tools come from `mise.toml` and `mise.bench.toml`.
  Binaryen 133 built the apps.
  CPython is the prebuilt 3.14.8 for both `dewasm-python` and `dewasm-python-jit`.
  JRuby is the 10.1.2.0 release.

## What the speed record shows

| Outcome | Pairs |
| --- | --- |
| measured, `stdout` equal to `wasmtime`'s | 566 |
| declared exclusion | 69 |
| timed out | 3 |
| failed | 0 |

- The three timed-out pairs are Spinel builds: both SQLite queries and `minigzip`.
  The previous record measured all three.
- `wasmtime` reads 1.00x of the previous record, and the other native runtimes 0.97x to 1.01x.
- `dewasm-python-jit` reads 0.76x and `dewasm-python` 0.90x, on the new CPython build.
- `wat/eh_try` on `dewasm-graalpy` does not reproduce between runs.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

KUU-1093: bundled `kotlin.time.Duration` now declares `: Comparable<Duration>` like upstream (previously `compareTo` existed only as an extension, so `<`/`>` worked but every generic `Comparable` context failed: `val d: Comparable<Duration>`, `.sorted()`, `maxOf`, `compareValues`, `sortedWith`/`compareBy`).

Making a value class implement an interface flips its representation to a real boxed object (`resolveValueClassKind` → `.classType`), so every producer/consumer that treated `Duration` as a raw `Int64` payload had to move to the boxed regime. After the merge with `a814e9f62` (tagged nanos/millis storage), the payload is the *tagged* rawValue and `compareTo` must use the tag-aware form (ms-tag ⇒ |value| > MAX_NANOS ⇒ same-sign ms-tag always wins; cross-tag same-sign comparisons by raw bits would be wrong):

- `HeaderHelpers+SyntheticDurationStubs`: `__kk_duration_*` stubs return raw `Long` payloads again; removed the member-method registrations and `zero`/`infinite` stubs that re-entered Duration space.
- `TimeSources.kt` helpers do plain Kotlin ops on objects (`d.isInfinite()`, `l.compareTo(r)`, `Duration(0L)`).
- `Instant.minus`/`elapsed` wrap `__kk_instant_until`'s raw `Long` in `Duration(...)` (stub retyped to `Long`).
- `runtimeDurationRawValue` (RuntimeDuration.swift) reads boxed objects via the stable nominal typeID of `kotlin.time.Duration` (`count==3`, field slot 2), so every `runtimeDurationWholeValue`/component consumer (`kk_duration_inWhole*`, `toString`, `instant ± duration`, coroutine conversions) accepts object handles alongside tagged raw and legacy `RuntimeDurationBox`.
- Coroutine lowering: `delay(duration)`/`withTimeout(duration)` convert via `kk_duration_inWholeMilliseconds`, and the emitted `kk_kxmini_delay` call drops the source `symbol` (`loweredSuspendSymbol = nil`) so `applyArgumentBoxing` never sees the stale `Duration` parameter and re-boxes the primitive millis the raw bridge expects (delay was silently ~0ms before this fix).
- `runtimeAnyHashCode` now checks `runtimeObjectHashCodeOverride` before structural hashing, so `(d as Any).hashCode()` matches `d.hashCode()` for classes with overrides.

Regression case: `Scripts/diff_cases/kuu_1093_duration_comparable.kt` (byte-diff against kotlinc). Uses an object-literal `Comparator` + `compareValuesBy` instead of `compareBy` — `sortedWith(compareBy { ... })` is independently broken on master (unsorted output), filed as KUU-1204.

Verified locally: the KUU-1093 repro and probes (cross-tag ordering at ms-tag boundary, parse/ISO, Instant±, boxed `as Any` ops/hashCode, coroutine delay/withTimeout Long-vs-Duration timing) byte-match kotlinc/master; the duration/time/coroutine diff subset (23 cases incl. `duration_storage_*`, `instant_basic`, `kotlinx_coroutines_timeout_*`) and `SmokeTests` (12/12) pass. `enum_comparable_bound` fails identically on master (pre-existing enum-Comparable gap). Full suite/goldens/diff corpus not run — CI scope.

author: stevejcl
body:
## Summary
A program, or a run resumed after a restart, holds the command slot for its whole duration, by design, to avoid racing the client. Meanwhile `maybe_check()` asked for the slot on every poll tick of every open page, was denied, and logged `slot busy: 'health_check' denied …` at INFO. A user log had 478 such lines in a few minutes, about one per second all night.

- `maybe_check()` skips the health check while `scheduler_runner.is_running(uid)`. The run follows the device itself, and the check could never run during it anyway.
- A check denied by a one-off command now sets `_last_check_at`, so it retries after `_CHECK_INTERVAL_S` instead of on every tick.
- Stop is unaffected: `request_stop()` only sets the run's `stop_requested` flag, which the resumed wait already checks.
- CHANGELOG entry.

## Test
With a fake slot:
- a running program gives 0 slot requests over 10 ticks;
- a busy one-off command gives 1 request over 10 ticks.

author: przemyslawklys
body:
CT precertificate binding and platform certificate loading can select different certificates from a PKCS#7 container. This can associate names from an unrelated signer with a verified log entry on Windows. The reader now requires one complete DER-encoded X.509 certificate and checks that the materialized record matches those exact bytes.

The same boundary applies to RFC6962 and Static CT ingestion, dedicated precertificate signer/issuer certificates, names-only records and full record hydration. PKCS#7, PEM, BER, concatenated certificates and trailing data are rejected; decoding failures retain the existing entry payload evidence. No dependency or public package pin changes.

Validation: 51 focused CT tests pass on .NET 8 and .NET 10. Regression fixtures cover both ingestion paths and include a native Windows assertion for the different container-selection rules. Complete source-integration suites against merged DnsClientX pass on both targets (2,569 passed, 16 skipped each). Independent read-only review and the targeted repair confirmation found no remaining actionable defects. The .NET Framework 4.7.2 test assembly also compiles with zero warnings or errors. author: stranske
body:
## What was wrong

`tick.remote_tick` deferred the rest of the backlog once `len(chosen)` reached `ORCH_MAX_REMOTE_PER_TICK` (default 3). Its docstring says the cap exists "so a large backlog can't fan out unbounded autonomous spend". But `chosen` also held every row `dispatcher.delegate_remote` **refused**: paused, already carrying an `agent:*` label, or (since stranske/Orchestrator#451) with labels GitHub did not return. A refusal spends nothing remote. It still held a slot, and `production_reserve` reserved research capacity for an agent that would not run.

The latch is structural. `backlog.build_backlog` lists a closer item only when its PR already carries an `agent:*` label (`backlog.py:332`), and it appends the closer items before the opener items. `_remote_skip_reason` refuses any `agent:*` label. So in a live tick the head of the backlog is refused by construction, the refusals fill the cap, and every item behind them waits until keepalive finishes the PRs in front.

**Production use, in the situation the lane exists for.** These come from the tick logs of the live period, 2026-06-15 to 09-02: 1,857 active ticks with a plan, `dry_run: false`. Read-only scripts parsed the plans the tick printed, and label timelines were replayed through GraphQL.

| | count |
|---|---|
| cap slots that went to refusals (2,825 "already in agent pipeline", 1 paused) | 2,826 |
| cap slots that went to delegations that applied | 25 |
| ticks that deferred an item while every slot held a refusal | 546 of 558 ticks with a deferral |
| deferred targets never examined in any tick | 143 |
| … of those, carrying no `agent:*`/`agents:paused` label when first deferred (64 issues, 1 PR) | **65** |
| … their deferrals that came in a tick whose cap was full of refusals | 1,062 of 1,113 |
| applied targets that had been deferred first | 14 of 23 (334 deferrals, median 21 h from first deferral to label; Manager-Database#1279 waited 138 ticks over 21 days) |

**The shadow plan since 2026-09-03.** The same counting over the JSON plans until `--summary` replaced them gives 694 refused rows (all ownership, deduplicated by tick; 697 counting one doubled tick) against 1 would-apply (Workflows#3420, 09-13). The 142 headline-only ticks after that could not tell the two apart: in shadow, "skipped" lumped a refusal with a delegation that would have applied. The current plan is unchanged every hour. It has 3 rows refused for ownership, Ready#578 deferred, and `production_reserve` {cursor: 1, gemini: 2}. All four targets are closed PRs, because discovery is skipped while the lane is shadow. The chip's counts (698; Manager-Database#1686 in 115 ticks, Ready#579 112, Ready#580 111) are each one higher than mine, which matches one tick printed twice.

**Today, if `ORCH_DISPATCH_LANE=1` were set.** A read-only replay of live discovery (`build_backlog` with the live fetchers, nothing written) returns 5 items. All are closer PRs labelled `agent:auto` + `agent:codex`, and there are 0 opener items. The old cap would hold three refusals and defer two more. Nothing is delegable right now, so this change unblocks no item today. It removes the reason one would be held tomorrow.

## The fix

- **One predicate, `tick.is_delegation(row)`**: the dispatcher neither refused the row (`skip`) nor rejected it (`error`). In shadow it would apply; in an active tick it was attempted and its run recorded. The cap counts exactly these rows, and so do `production_reserve`, the rejected-role influence edge, the plan counters and the headline. A row with no `labels_read` still counts, because the safe error for a spend bound is to count a row that spent nothing.
- **A second bound on examination.** `EXAMINED_PER_DELEGATION` (4) times the cap, 12 by default. It counts every item that enters the per-item pipeline, from the claims check onward, so a backlog of owned items costs at most 12 label reads and hook passes per tick. The size comes from the live period: the items that were not owned numbered p90 3, p99 15, max 29 per tick, and examined first they fit inside 12 in all but 25 of 1,857 ticks. `delegation_bounds()` resolves both numbers once, and the plan carries them to the headline.
- **`tick.examination_order`.** Items that `dispatcher._remote_skip_reason` would refuse on their *discovery* labels are examined after the rest, each group in backlog order. The live read inside `delegate_remote` still decides every delegation. The order only stops owned closer PRs from holding a delegable item behind the bound. Without it the examination bound would latch exactly as the cap did.
- **The plan says what it held back.** New keys: `examine_cap`, `delegations`, `refused`, `errors`, `examined`, and `deferral: {delegable, drainable, by_cap, by_examine_cap, delegable_targets}`. `delegable` is the blocking quantity: deferred items the rail would not refuse on their discovery labels. `drainable` is the part of those that waits only on this tick's own delegations. In an active tick that needs at least one cap-filling label to have applied: a failed POST leaves its target unowned to take its slot again (`58ff89a`, refined in `5e4f081`). A delegable item deferred by the examination bound waits behind examined items that did not delegate, so it is not drainable. A cap of 0 drains nothing.
- **The headline** reads those numbers from the plan, never recounting them, and prints `?` for any it lacks (unknown is not zero). The line the shadow tick would print today:
  `TICK-PLAN: delegations 0/3 would apply (shadow); 4 refused; examined 4/12; label reads 4 answered, 0 unanswered (refused); 0 no capacity, 0 blocked; deferred 0 (delegable 0, drainable 0) -> …/tick-plan.json`
  The old latch would have read `delegations 0/3 …; 3 refused; …; deferred 1 (delegable 1, drainable 0)`.
- **Rejected-role influence edges, decided in.** They are now written only for a delegation, because only a delegation records the `remote:{repo}#{num}:{agent}` run they point at. It is the same refused-row population in the same block. In the Brain (read-only snapshot, 2026-10-04), 210 rejected `remote:` role edges exist. Only 2 were written in the tick that recorded their run. 78 point at a run id that was never recorded. 51 were written before their run existed and were inherited by 3 later delegations, and 79 were written after.
- A selftest fixture was itself an instance of the defect. The production-before-research case used the target `o/r#production-range`, which has no PR number. That is a dispatcher **error** row, and its truthiness check on `production_reserve` passed only because error rows reserved capacity. It now uses a numbered target, asserts the exact reserve, and also asserts that a refused row reserves `{}`.

## Latched-gate check: two bounds, four questions each

**The delegation cap** (`ORCH_MAX_REMOTE_PER_TICK`, default 3)

1. *What decrements it?* It restarts at 0 every tick. A deferred item is freed by this tick's own delegations. A label that applies makes its target owned, so the next tick's dispatcher refuses it, and a refusal takes no slot. The next discovery also lists it with its `agent:*` label, so it is examined after every delegable item. `test_items_deferred_by_the_cap_drain_on_the_next_tick` runs both ticks.
2. *Can that run while the cap is closed?* Yes. The cap closes only when `cap` delegations were made this tick, and those delegations are the drain. A refusal can no longer close it.
3. *Does the measuring window equal the draining window?* One predicate, `is_delegation`, is what the cap counts and what the plan, headline, reserve and edge consume. The drain turns a delegation row into a refused one through the dispatcher's own `_remote_skip_reason`. There is no second copy to drift. `test_every_item_is_examined_or_deferred_and_the_counts_are_the_rows` pins the counters to the rows, and every item is either examined or deferred.
4. *What does it print fully drained, and has an input produced it?* `deferred 0 (delegable 0,

author: foxinthehenhouse
body:
## What and why
Shape now asks only what's expensive to change on day 0, at most 7 questions in total. It states the rest as defaults ("I'm assuming…, say if not") or parks them in a decision ledger for the phase where they matter.

- **Day-0 set** (in `skills/shape`):
  - who, the moment and how often
  - the problem and today's alternative
  - the payoff
  - social shape (community or two-sided always gets the cold-start question)
  - how the first 100 users find it
  - the money model
  - sensitive data

  Everything else is deferred to `prototype`, `scaffold`, `first-feature`, `pre-launch` or `post-launch`.
- **The ledger:** `design/brief.json` gains `decisions` (`id`, `question`, `answer`, `status` asked|default|deferred, `ask_at`, `why`) plus new top-level `context`, `payoff`, `social`, `distribution` and `money`.
  - It's documented in `docs/COST.md`, and `scribe`, `product-advisor` and the interview's Output 1/2 carry it. `appbox.yaml` gains `product.context`, `payoff`, `social` and `distribution`; BRIEF.md gains Payoff, Social shape, Distribution and "Decisions still to make".
  - The interview gains three questions (payoff, who else is in it, first 100 users), so it now has 17, plus a table of when each question is asked.
- **Validator:** new `scripts/check_intake.py`.
  - `brief` checks that the ledger and the five new sections are present, the enum values are valid, nothing is deferred to "shape", every default has an answer, and at most 7 questions were asked at shape. Shape and the prototype freeze run it.
  - `defaults` checks that every DEFAULTS.md row names real files or says "on the roadmap".
- **Just in time:**

  - `next/signals.py` reports `decisions_due`. The `next` table ranks it 9th, below a p0 ticket, and the session-start line mentions it when nothing else is pressing.
- **Ledger in the app:** `design/brief.json` already lands in the repo, because shape writes it in the folder the scaffold commits. It's now also on render.py's protected list, so `--force` can't overwrite it.
- **Defaults:** new `docs/DEFAULTS.md`, copied into the app as `docs/DEFAULTS.md` the same way TASTE.md is. It has 15 rows, each naming real template files or marked "on the roadmap". Things that don't exist are marked roadmap:
  - the review prompt
  - a first-run onboarding flow
  - enforced quiet hours and a daily notification cap
  - a share action for content
  - a privacy policy template
  - an in-app feedback row

## Verified with
- `scripts/selftest.sh`: `selftest: 330 passed, 0 failed, 5 skipped`.
- The new area, `scripts/selftest.d/intake.sh` (23 checks), also passes in isolation against a rendered app. Each guard passes on the kit and is planted to fail, matching on the specific message:
  - shape without the cap, and shape without the pre-launch deferral
  - COST.md without `payoff`
  - a brief missing `decisions`, missing `payoff`, with a decision deferred to shape, with an unknown phase, with a default that has no answer, with a bad social shape, and with 8 questions asked at shape
  - signals fixtures: an overdue first-feature decision surfaces; pre-launch waits until setup is done; answered decisions never show; a negative control with the phase not yet arrived
  - a DEFAULTS.md row with a nonexistent path, and one that names nothing and isn't on the roadmap
  - one phase vocabulary shared by COST.md, check_intake.py and signals.py; money and social words match appbox.yaml's
  - the interview's question count matches its numbered questions

- `ruff check` is clean on `check_intake.py`, `render.py` and `signals.py`.

## Not verified
- **Kit evals are not run** (paid; can't run here). Added cases:
  - `07-new-app-one-liner-states-defaults`: stated defaults and at most 3 questions.
  - `08-new-app-two-sided-asks-cold-start`: the cold-start question.

**⚖️ Calls I made:**
1. **Area file name:** `intake.sh`, as your prompt said, rather than the BRIEF's `<slug>.sh`. The alternative was `intake-decision-ledger.sh`.
2. **When a phase "arrives" for `next`:**
   - prototype once the interview is done, scaffold once the prototype (design) is done, first-feature once verify is done

   - post-launch once a `v*` release tag exists

6. **DEFAULTS.md path in the app:** `docs/DEFAULTS.md`, also protected like TASTE.md (never overwritten). The alternative was `docs/product/DEFAULTS.md`.

author: michiexile
body:
## What and why

Three follow-ups to #40/#41.

1. **Distance matrices are read from the lower triangle**, as `ripser.cpp` and GUDHI read them (project lead's call; closes the paper plan's decision 0.6).
   - Before, `ExplicitMetricSpace` read the upper triangle.
   - On a matrix that is not exactly symmetric (the Ripser benchmark's fractal-r: 1.6% of pairs differ by up to 1e-5), we and the other tools computed from different inputs.
2. **The benchmark's alpha rows match the new default.**
   - `tda4j-fastalpha` still built `HelixDelaunay` directly, but every alpha case is now triangulated by Bowyer–Watson by default.
3. **`PLAN-paper.md` gets a dated update section** listing what #40 and #41 made out of date.

## Changes

- **`ExplicitMetricSpace.distance(x, y)`**
  - is now `dist(max)(min)` (was `dist(min)(max)`);
  - full-matrix inputs (CSV, DIPHA, MATLAB's `computeFromDistanceMatrix`) follow;
  - the lower-triangular formats were already read that way.
- **`PackedRipserCohomologyEngine`** reads any metric that is not symmetric by construction as `d(max, min)`, the same triangle.
- **Behaviour change** for non-symmetric matrices only: their diagrams now match Ripser's and GUDHI's. Symmetric inputs are unaffected. 0.5.0 makes no compatibility promise with 0.4.x.
- **Benchmark harness:**
  - `PaperBenchmarkDriver`'s `engine=fastalpha` runs on the chosen backend's triangulation, with `backend=default|bowyer-watson|helix|dqp`;
  - new tools `tda4j-bw` and `tda4j-helix` in `bench/bench.py`;
  - `bench/README.md` updated.
- **Docs:**
  - user guide (Vietoris–Rips, MATLAB) and developers guide (persistence engines) state the lower-triangle read;
  - `rules/streams.md` and `rules/engines.md`.

## Checks (run locally before requesting review)

- [x] `sbt scalafmtAll`
- [x] `sbt "scalafmtSbtCheck ; scalafmtCheck ; Test / scalafmtCheck"`
- [x] `sbt testFull`: 953 passed, 0 failed, 11 skipped
- [x] `TDA4J_SCALA_VERSION=3.8.4 sbt doc` (after `sbt clean`)
- [ ] `sbt mimaReportBinaryIssues`: not run. No API signature changed, and there is no released 0.5.x baseline.

## Notes for the reviewer

- **The new test discriminates.** `MetricSpaceSpec` uses a 4×4 matrix whose two triangles give different answers:
  - the lower triangle is a square with diagonals 2, giving one `H_1` bar `[1, 2)`;
  - the upper triangle has every distance 1, giving no loop.

  Reading the wrong triangle fails it.
- **`PackedWorkingColumnSpec`'s symmetrized reference** now reads the lower triangle too. Its skewed space perturbs exactly that triangle, so the comparison is still exact.
- **The benchmark driver was run on 200 uniform 3-D points with each variant:**
  - default, `bowyer-watson` and `fastalpha` give the same 813 bars;
  - `helix` gives the same bars within 8e-17.

  No benchmark timings were taken; that needs a quiet machine (`bench/README.md`).
- **Not changed:** `DtmMetricSpace`'s `(min, max)` canonicalization. It fixes the evaluation order of a formula and doesn't read a matrix.
- **A possible spurious CI failure, not from this PR:** `PersistenceThresholdCLISpec`'s `System.err` race; a separate task for it is queued. It passed here.

## Bookkeeping

- [x] Rules updated, each with a pointer and no narrative. `PLAN-paper.md`: decision 0.6 closed, plus the dated update section.

author: lalalune
body:
Expose SqliteInteractiveTaskStore.readOwnerHistory for complete, bounded owner-scoped history projections. It reuses validated event pages, rejects revision changes between pages, and invalidates publication when SQLite data/schema versions or same-connection change counts move. Host projections remain synchronous and read-only; no new transaction wraps existing page transactions and no effect authority is added.

The bill-outcome store also exposes loadEvidence(), distinguishing the selected observation from the exact record persisted in SQLite. Pending observations that conflict with a saved record are not reported as durable. Hosts can now report evidence without knowing journal/outcome table schemas.

Validation: 28 native-host/real SQLite integration tests pass, including multi-page histories, cross-owner exclusion, global limits, writes/external commits, revision changes between pages, corrupt persisted events and failed/conflicting outcome persistence. The task-store module passes strict typecheck with its actual core protocol implementations through a narrow source alias. Changed files pass Biome with two existing optional-chain warnings in the outcome module. Root verification remains limited by sparse missing UI locales.

body:
## Product defect and dependent scope
The #888 Agent Builder compiler silently collapsed duplicate registered tool IDs with last-writer-wins semantics, leaving risk classification ambiguous. It also held mutable caller-owned `ToolSpec` objects and returned the original nested `AgentDefinition` in `CompilationResult`; post-construction mutation could drift persisted draft authority from the compiler's decision. Additionally, Pydantic `ToolGrant.max_risk` accepted boolean, float and numeric-string coercion as permission tiers.

## Implementation
- Exact parent **#888 HEAD `8a39ab3eba0238a778855e33b139c3eec19a157e`**; no writes to #888, #192 or main.
- Reject duplicate tool identities before the compiler becomes usable. Snapshot registered per-ID `RiskTier` rather than keeping externally mutable `ToolSpec`. Preserve exact risk, scope catalog and R4 approval checks.
- Require Pydantic `StrictInt` for `ToolGrant.max_risk`, preserving ordinary integer/IntEnum tiers and the serialized document format.
- Deep-copy the compiled `AgentDefinition` so caller-side nested `ToolGrant` mutation after compile cannot corrupt metadata passed to the existing durable draft repository.
- Exactly **three changed paths**: `src/nika_core/builder/compiler.py`, `src/nika_core/builder/spec.py`, `tests/test_agent_builder_registry_authority.py`. No new dependency, schema, authorization service, model runtime or UI.

## Exact checked-in source and evidence
Head **`a355a1be562b4ed55617409b476dd995c2157d39`**, ahead five/behind zero relative to frozen #888 parent. Local `git hash-object` exactly matched GitHub blob identities for compiler **`7d31c077949cb294a8ba6b42a50cf49322ff9d92`**, spec **`217b7d0a8e3ba34db5d89903c1b1943441738941`**, and new test **`c45bf558c10ad1ef2ed1b571a500cc683ecc79d5`**. **10/10 actual checked-in new tests pass in isolated pytest**, using exact compiler/spec, real Pydantic 2.13.4 and a minimal class-equivalent `ToolSpec`/`ToolRisk` stub in place of the large incumbent `tools.py`; `compileall` passes. Prior six focused reproduction tests also passed on the preceding version. This does **not** establish whole-repo pytest/Ruff, dual-OS, packaged Windows, full authorization integration or human NVDA.

## Integration gate / remaining work
Stacked draft PR **against #888**, not an independent main candidate. Exact-head Core Ubuntu/Windows **37247807517** and M12 **37247807481** are **QUEUED**, not passed; PF3 is skipped and out of scope. Local GitHub checkout remains unavailable due to DNS failure.

author: maksymenkoyr
body:
## What changes for the user

A new **RECORD** button, bottom right next to the fullscreen button, saves a clip of the visuals with the sound, ready to post. While recording it shows a red dot and the elapsed time; click again to stop and the file downloads as `sine-visuals-lab-<scene>-<date-time>.mp4` (or `.webm` where the browser cannot write MP4).

- A chip beside it picks the shape: **Screen** (the canvas as it is), **9:16** or **1:1** (the middle of the picture, scaled to a fixed size). The choice is remembered on this device only (it never reaches the output window or a room's TV) and is locked during a take.
- Only the picture is recorded, never the panel or the HUD. With a pop-out output open, the output window's picture is recorded (the main window only shows a small preview then); otherwise the main canvas.
- The sound is whatever the visuals hear (mic, line input, tab share). With synthetic or no audio the clip is video only.
- The clip is saved if the output window closes, the canvas loses its GL context, or the page is hidden mid-take.
- No keyboard shortcut. Trimming and uploading are out of scope.

I put the button bottom right rather than in the scene row beside POP OUT, because that row runs under the CUE / PLAY bar once an output is open and the buttons were covered (found in the headless run).

## Files

- `src/ui/clipFormat.ts`: the pure parts (format pick, crop maths, file name, elapsed time); `tests/clipFormat.test.ts`
- `src/ui/clipRecorder.ts`: the recorder; its header says why the output canvas is preferred
- `src/ui/recordControls.ts`: the buttons and the remembered shape
- `src/net/outputBridge.ts`: the pop-out bridge now hands out its window (`popupWindow()`)
- `src/net/syncedStores.ts`, `tests/syncedScope.test.ts`: `vibe.recordAspect` is private
- `src/app.ts`, `index.html`, `docs/architecture.md`: wiring, markup, a pointer

## Checked

- Both typechecks and the full test suite pass (two long-run tests, moire and music profile, time out under load and pass alone, as they have before).
- Headless Chromium on the real GPU with the fake mic, about 4 s each at Screen, 9:16 and 1:1, both with the main canvas and with a pop-out open. Every file saved as MP4 (H.264 + AAC, a video and an audio track), 4.3 to 4.4 s long, at 1000x700 / 1080x1920 / 1080x1080 for the main canvas and 1280x720 / 1080x1920 / 1080x1080 for the output (so the output's canvas is the one recorded). Decoded frames are not black.
- Closing the pop-out mid-take, losing the GL context, and the page turning hidden each saved a file. Synthetic audio saved a video-only clip.
- Not run: Safari/Firefox; a take is held in memory until it is saved (about 120 MB a minute at the video bitrate).

This PR includes the following fixes to make the Security lane green:

* **fix(security): allow the GCP lab harness in the no-SSH gate**
  - scripts/run-gcp-kvm-test.sh drives a disposable Compute Engine host with gcloud compute ssh/scp and waits for that host's sshd. The session ends at the cloud KVM host; no guest image or microVM gains SSH. Rewording the comment would not help: the scp transport lines match the gate too.
  - Also pass -I so binary files are skipped. BSD grep reports case-insensitive matches inside public/public/banner.png, which made the gate fail on macOS while CI's GNU grep passed the same tree.

* **fix(fuzz): stop requiring an empty Basic credential to round-trip**
  - basic_header("") is "Basic ": a scheme with no token, which basic_credential reads as no credential. The target asserted it decoded to Some("") and libFuzzer's first, empty input crashed the lane. Both answers leave the header searched as written, since an empty credential cannot hold a placeholder, so the target now accepts either for the empty case and keeps the exact round-trip for every non-empty one.

* **test(admission): witness that a plain pinned bundle needs no backend**
  - Nothing exercised admission with a bundle pin, so deleting either negation on the embedded-image-set checks in admit_plan_for_boot_with_ingress survived the mutation lane. Admitting a signed kernel+rootfs bundle with no backend selected now fails under both mutants: one demands a backend, the other panics building an image contract for a set that does not exist.

* **fix(audit): drop the unreachable single-file chain read; witness session mutants**
  - read_lines_from_genesis fell back to reading <tenant>.jsonl when the segment set reported NoChain, but the live file is a member of that set, so NoChain means the file is absent and the fallback could only fail. Its line filter was therefore an equivalent mutant. The function now reports the set's own error.
  - New session tests kill the remaining surviving mutants: seal digests need both length and hex alphabet, a uniformly shifted seal (a recorded prune) still verifies, the listing counts a session's events, and a selector one character under the minimum is refused even when unique.

* **test(bundle): witness the embedded image-set cache from the public API**

### Testing
All tests pass and the Security lane should now be green.

### Integration
This PR includes security-related fixes and tests that ensure the Security lane runs without failure.

author: dakimura
body:
Phase 8, PR 5 of 15 (`docs/PHASE8-LEDGER.md`, staticcheck-checks #1, #2, #4, #8). Follows #479.

## SA1019

staticcheck v0.8.1 (golangci-lint 2.14.0) changed SA1019 in three ways:

- **Message name**: it names the deprecated object with `code.SelectorName` (the declaring type, package-qualified) instead of the source spelling.
- **Package name**: a deprecated package is named by its unquoted path.
- **Position**: it reports at the selected name when the selector's `X` is a type.

guff already checked struct-literal keys. What it was missing were `SelectorName`'s two new fallbacks: an `X` that is a type name, and a nested selector. They are added to `knowledge_selector_name`, which only SA1019 calls.

With that, the seven ways the fixtures spell a promoted or embedded selector collapse onto three names, as upstream does. The six SA1019 cases go **42/42 → 0/0** and their ratchets are deleted.

## SA4003 and SA6005

- **SA4003** names the operand's own type (`example.com/x.Level`) instead of its underlying basic type (`uint32`).
  - Checking a type parameter's type set is DEFERRED. v0.7.0 didn't handle type parameters either, so guff is still silent there, as before.
- **SA6005** writes `!strings.EqualFold` for `!=`, both in the message and in the fix title, which is now lower-case.
  - guff wrote it this way until 2026-08-27 and was changed then to match v0.7.

## Effect on staticcheck-sa

staticcheck-sa goes **16/17 → 0/1**. The one remaining entry is SA5005, which is documented as an architectural difference. The three entries that were missing even before the pin bump are closed along with the rest.

Four unit tests that asserted v0.7.0's wording were updated.

## Gates run locally

All passed with golangci-lint 2.14.0:

- golden: all 265 cases
- fix
- isolate
- OSS (pr + nightly)
- guff-staticcheck tests: 371 / 371

author: genesiscz
body:
Small fixes found by re-checking the tools after the Arwen96 issue stack merged. Each commit is one fix, and nearly all of them make a tool print the right thing when it has no terminal.

## Stack
`master` <- #443 <- #462 <- this PR. This branch applies cleanly on the tip of #462 and touches 33 files.

## What changed
- **No terminal:** `tools qr` draws with block characters instead of invisible colour escapes. A clack spinner prints one plain line per message. Bare `voice-memos` lists the memos instead of waiting on a picker. `macos-resources` names `tools doctor cpu` as the one-shot alternative.
- **Errors and hints:** an uncaught tool error prints one ERROR line (the stack with `-v` and in the log). `envdiff` prints a returned error once. `jev` and `control` config hints keep the user's global flags through `suggestCommand`'s `replaceCommand`, and `config show` uses a fixed example.
- **Help text and listings:** `tools --help` sorts the tool list case-insensitively. A `src` folder with no entry file says "No entry point" and how to run a file by path. `scripts list` prints the list on stdout and only the count on stderr. The reminders doctor help says that the status read never prompts.
- **`ask`:** the usage database opens on first use, so `ask --help` writes nothing.
- **`task`:** the first task run no longer warns with a stack trace about a sessions folder that does not exist yet.
- **`control`:** preflight gets 30 s and passes its deadline to the native walk, which bounds each AX read and returns what it read instead of timing out with nothing.
- **`npm-package-diff`:** installed files are read after the install instead of by a watcher with fixed sleeps that missed fast installs, and an unmatched filter or no difference is said.
- **`chrome-devtools`:** `status` hides leftover capture dirs that have no recorder, buffer or CDP (`--all` shows them).
- **Hooks:** after a partial commit the index gets HEAD's formatted blob back, so the "MM" state is gone.

## Left out on purpose
The original branch had a fix for `mcp-ripgrep --help` and the `mcp-tsc` start log. I dropped it, because the dead-tools stack (#464 and #465) deletes both tools and that commit would conflict with the deletion.

## Verification
- `tsgo --noEmit`, `check-tool-commands --strict`, `check-plugin-standalone`, `lint-rules`, `check-package-boundaries`, `logging-guard` and `placeholder-check` all exit 0.
- `bun run test` on the touched areas (`ask`, `chrome-devtools`, `control`, `envdiff`, `macos`, `macos-resources`, `npm-package-diff`, `qr`, `scripts`, `task`, `utils/cli`, `utils/ai/evaluation` and `scripts/`): 2367 pass, 33 skip, 0 fail.
- Not proven live: the `control` preflight change touches the Swift `ax-tool` and needs a native rebuild to run.

author: dimkox
body:
## What

Trust CI verifies **every repository of an owner** that has Getzilla installed, not only repositories listed one by one.

- `owner_profiles` in catalog policies: `{owner, commands, holdout}`. Exact repository profiles win; any other repository of a listed owner uses the owner profile; every other owner is still rejected before enqueue. No global wildcard; legacy policies still refuse `*`; adding an owner profile keeps existing exact-profile epochs.
- `trust-ci/holdout.consumer.example`: generic holdout for Getzilla-installed repositories (change specs, approval disclaimer, grant binding, no GitHub Actions). It refuses repositories without Getzilla.
- `python3 -m adaptive_trust_ci.onboarding`: reads the deployed policy (never writes it) and writes a new catalog. It keeps each existing repository's commands and holdout digest, adds `Dimkox/Getzilla` and the `Dimkox` owner profile, moves a legacy holdout under `<root>/<repository>` (catalog holdouts must be strict subdirectories of the trusted roots), and prints before/after check names and the bundles to install.
- `branch-protect` resolves the repository's own profile in catalog mode. Before, it could not parse a catalog policy at all.
- Operator runbook: `engineering/runbooks/getzilla-trust-ci-onboarding.md`. Steps 2–3 were rehearsed against a simulated legacy deployment.

Also on #1's branch: the rule "vibe-code first, then apply the factory" in AGENTS.md, the consumer AGENTS template and the README; plus a fix for the example holdout digest, which had been computed with a stray `__pycache__` present.

## Verification

Same environment as #1 (no PyPI: no pytest, coverage or fastapi).

- `trust-ci/tests`: 238 run; only `test_api` errors (fastapi missing, same as baseline). New: owner resolution, validation, epoch stability, legacy wildcard refusal, planner conversion, planner CLI.
- Root suite: 1203 run; failure set identical to the unmodified predecessor baseline.
- Consumer holdout passes on Getzilla and on a fresh Getzilla install, and refuses a plain repository.

Base: `port/from-adaptive-grok-242` (#1). Retarget to `main` after #1 merges.

body:
vCenter alarms only appeared on the vSphere page's fourth tab, Health.
The Overview fetched hosts and VMs alone, so a host tinted yellow there
had no visible reason and datastore or network alarms were not on the
page at all.

While the Overview is open it now also reads the Health tab's resources,
and when vCenter reports any signals the existing health table leads the
page above the hosts, without its filter toolbar. Nothing is added when
vCenter is quiet, and filtering stays on the Health tab. This is the
pattern the TrueNAS Overview already uses for its health alerts.

Verified in a browser on a mock vCenter at 1440 and 390 (receipt included); full frontend suite passes apart from the known Mac-only agentInstallCommand cases.

author: foxinthehenhouse
body:
## What and why
PR 3 of 3 in docs/specs/high-end-design. The generated Expo app now uses the motion, atmosphere and glass that the founder froze in the prototype.

- **Settle motion:**
  - `render.py` writes a `settle` spring into `lib/tokens.ts`. It is the `gentle` spring damped to at least critical, computed by the prototype's own `settle_spring()`, so there is one implementation.
  - In `lib/motion.ts`: `spring("settle")`, a new `dampingRatio()`, and `entrance()` now uses settle instead of the timing curve.
  - New `screenEntrance()`: Screen's content fades in on settle underneath the native push/sheet transition. It is a fade only, so it doesn't fight the native transition over position. Under reduce motion it does nothing.
  - Overshoot stays with small elements (`snappy`/`bouncy`).
- **Haptic map:** `hapticFor` maps each control role to a haptic (primary is medium, chip is selection, and so on). Button and Choice use it.
- **Atmosphere tokens:**
  - The template's `design/tokens.json` gets a default `atmosphere` block (glow, medium, grain on, solid). Its colours are exactly what `atmo_lights()` gives for the template palette, so the untouched template works.
  - The prototype's `merged_tokens` passes only the knobs on to directions. Without this, every direction failed `prototype check` with "unknown key", because the template's light colours leaked in.
  - `render.py` writes a typed `atmosphere` into tokens.ts:
    - Frozen values pass through unchanged.
    - A hand-written block with no colours gets them from `atmo_lights`, so they are still contrast-capped.
    - A tokens.json from before atmospheres gets mode none.
    - A bad knob fails the render with exit 2 and a named error.
  - A fixed film-grain tile (generated by `make_icon.grain_png()`) ships as a data URI, so there's no binary file in the repo.
- **ScreenAtmosphere:**
  - New `components/ui/ScreenAtmosphere` paints the prototype's own `radial-gradient()` strings through RN 0.86's `experimental_backgroundImage`. No Skia and no new rendering dependency. Mode `field` falls back to the glow.
  - Each light fades to its own colour at alpha 0 rather than to `transparent`, so the edges don't go grey.
  - Grain is laid on top at the prototype's opacity and blend per mode.
  - It is hidden from screen readers and ignores touches.
  - `Screen` mounts it behind the content, but not on sheets.
- **Glass:**
  - `expo-glass-effect` is added to `mobile-deps.sh`.
  - `useGlassChrome()` is true only when all three hold: the theme chose glass surfaces, Liquid Glass is available (iOS 26+), and Reduce Transparency is off. Reduce Transparency is read reactively.
  - When true, `SheetHeader` renders a `GlassView` and the native tab bar stays glass. Otherwise both are solid `surface`.
- **Docs:** the SCREENS.md motion and atmosphere rows in `_platform_and_motion` now name settle, `screenEntrance`, `ScreenAtmosphere` and `hapticFor`. Template `AGENTS.md` is updated.
- **Tests:**
  - New jest tests:
    - settle is at or above critical damping and tied to the tokens.
    - the painted gradient carries the frozen geometry, colours and alpha (exact CSS string).
    - mode none and alpha 0 paint nothing; field paints the same as glow; grain follows its knob.
    - both entrances are dropped under reduce motion.
    - reduce transparency is reactive and overrides glass.
    - `SheetHeader` falls back to solid.
  - New `scripts/selftest.d/app-motion-atmosphere.sh` (11 checks):
    - the template agrees with the prototype.
    - freeze to tokens.ts parity on a lively theme (whose gentle spring is under-damped before settle).
    - older and hand-written token files.
    - a planted bad knob makes the render refuse.
    - who wires what.
  - `check-test-presence.js`: removed Screen, Sheet and Text from `NO_TEST_NEEDED`, because they now have tests and the guard required it.

## Verified with
- `scripts/selftest.sh`: `selftest: 318 passed, 0 failed, 5 skipped`
- `scripts/selftest.sh --mobile`: `selftest: 322 passed, 0 failed, 5 skipped`, including "npm run gates green" on a real Expo SDK 57 / RN 0.86.3 app.
- `npm run gates` on my own scaffold: 33 suites, 210 tests passed. Coverage is 77.8 / 70.6 / 73.0 / 79.6, above the 74 / 66 / 68 / 76 floor. `check-design-tells.js` is green.
- The 5 skips are the expected local ones: maestro, Postgres ×2, actionlint, zizmor.

## Not verified
- Nothing was run on a device or simulator. These are untested: how the gradient and grain look (including `mixBlendMode`), `GlassView` on iOS 26, and how iOS 26's tab bar responds to `backgroundColor` / `blurEffect: "none"` (it may ignore them).
- Web: react-native-web probably drops `experimental_backgroundImage`, so web likely shows no atmosphere.
- The prototype's slow light drift is deliberately not ported. The app's atmosphere holds still.

**Decisions for you**
- ⚖️ **Tab bar on the default theme.** The default surface is "solid", so a new app now asks the native tab bar for solid `surface` on every platform, including iOS 26. I did this to match the prototype ("what you click ships"). The alternative is to always leave the iOS 26 tab bar as the system's Liquid Glass and let the surface knob only control our own chrome.
- ⚖️ **Old token files get no light.** A tokens.json without an `atmosphere` block renders mode none with grain off, so existing apps look the same after re-rendering. The alternative is to give them the glow default.
- ⚖️ **Settle comes from the frozen spring.** It is computed from the already temperature-adjusted `gentle` spring in the frozen tokens. The prototype CSS computes it from the raw direction spring. The result is identical with the default springs. It could differ only if a calm direction sets gentle's damping above critical.

**Outside my scope**
- The shared scratchpad `scratchpad/m` is being used by another worker. Before I noticed, I ran one `render.py --force` into it, so their copy may need re-rendering. I did everything after that in `scratchpad/motion-atmo-app`.

author: bg-bc
body:
Addresses MemberJunction/bc-aidp-next-golive#301.

## Problem
`OrdersEngine` loads Products once per process and afterwards only sees rows saved through that process's entity layer (or a Redis remote-invalidate). A product written by a catalog loader, raw SQL or another API replica stays invisible until a restart. `OrderLineEntityServer.stampCompanyFromProduct` returned on that cache miss without stamping, so the line failed with `CompanyID: Company cannot be null`, a message that names neither the product nor the cache. Subscription lines skipped the product the same way (no term, no service period), and the recognition lookups read null.

A missing price row is not the cause: products with and without one fail the same way, and adding a price row does not refresh Products.

## Change
- `OrdersEngine.EnsureProducts(ids)` reloads Products once, straight from the database, when any requested product is missing. `RequireProduct(id)` does the same and throws naming the product if the reload doesn't find it. Concurrent misses share one reload; a failed reload reports that the catalog could not be read. A fully cached call costs no query.
- `OrderEntityServer.Save` ensures every line's product before subscription decisions, so one reload serves the whole save.
- The line's company stamp, `subscriptionLines`, `OrderJournalEntryFactory.loadProducts` and `RecordProgress`'s recognition lookup use them, and fail naming the product instead of skipping it.

No schema or metadata changes.

## Tests
- `OrdersEngine.productMiss.test.ts`: the real engine against a fake database that gains a product with no entity event. Covers the reload, `BypassCache`, one shared reload for concurrent misses, no query when cached, a single reload then a named failure, and a failed reload.
- `OrderLineCompanyStamp.test.ts`: the stamp reloads and takes the product's company, and fails naming line and product when the product is still missing.
- Integration OB27 (draft) and OB28 (confirm): warm the cache, insert a product by raw SQL with no price row, save a line at a stated price. On `next` both fail with `Failed to save order line 1: CompanyID: Company cannot be null`. With this change both pass, and the line carries the product's company.
- Unit: 4026 passed. Integration, full suite on a fresh database: 554 passed, 10 failed (EN4, EN9, EN22, PC5, PC15, TX7, TX8, TX10, TX12, TX15). Run alone, those 10 give the same result with and without this change: 9 fail, and EN4 passes. All but TX15 are listed in #416 (raw-SQL writes the cache never sees); TX15 fails the same way on `next`.

author: rickbassham
body:
Stacked on #20.

`parse_request()` read the device type with `%32[^/]` into `char device_type_str[32]`, which can write 33 bytes. The compiler warned about it. It read the device number with `%hhd` into the `uint8_t` field, so device 256 wrapped to device 0.

- The device type now reads at most 31 characters.
- The number is read into an `unsigned int`, and a number above 255 gets a 404 before it is stored. The public `alpaca_request_t.device_number` stays `uint8_t`.

Handlers run only for registered routes, which name a known device type (at most 19 characters) and an existing device. So this matters only for a firmware with more than 256 devices of one type, and no test can reach it through the fake server. `pio test -e native`: 28 tests pass, and the overflow warning is gone. The ESP32 build passes.

author: pasidu-mihiranga
body:
Workstream F of the enterprise UI plan: **F1, F2, F4 and F5 land. F3 was measured and the gate is deliberately still red** — see below, it is the most important thing in this PR.

## F4 — the `embed` role has an implementation

`ModelRole.EMBED` was a declared name with nothing behind it, and the reason was structural rather than neglect: `RoleRouter.invoke` returns text, a vector is not text, so the embed role could never have gone through the seam every other role uses.

- **`clarity/ai/embedding.py`** (new): the `Embedder` port, `HashingEmbedder`, `fit_idf`, `cosine`. Deterministic via `blake2b` because `hash` is salted per process and replay must be exact (I11) — proven by a subprocess test.
- **`clarity/modules/knowledge/semantic.py`** (new): `VectorSemanticRanker`, the first implementation of the `SemanticRanker` protocol, exported through `public.py` (I5).
- The container wires it beside the lexical index and refits on every corpus republish, so both halves rank the same world.
- **`hybrid.min_semantic`** (new config key) — needed because turning the semantic half on *removed* a safety, see F3.
- `scripts/evaluate.py` now builds the hybrid retriever, so the gate measures what the deployment runs.

## F3 — measured, and the threshold has **not** moved

The plan permits "improve retrieval **or** move the threshold with a documented reason". Retrieval was improved and it was not enough, so the gate stays at 0.98 and stays failing. `make eval` still exits non-zero, by choice.

| retriever | citation_accuracy | recall@5 |
|---|---|---|
| lexical only (before) | 0.931 | 0.967 |
| hybrid, no score floor | 0.900 | **1.000** |
| hybrid, floor at 0.25 (shipped) | 0.931 | 0.967 |

Three findings, all recorded in `config/ai/gates.yaml` and `config/ai/retrieval.yaml` so nobody repeats the experiment:

1. **The two failing queries are a synonym gap, not a morphology gap.** `turned on` shares no substring with `activated`; `crawling in the evenings` shares none with `speed may be reduced`. A hashed n-gram space cannot connect those, and no tuning of it will. It *can* connect `renewed` to `renewal`, which BM25 scores at zero. There is a test asserting each of those two facts, including the negative one.
2. **The local embedder's signal sits inside its own noise band.** Unrelated clause pairs: median cosine 0.089, p90 0.250. Deliberately irrelevant questions ("recipe for chicken curry") reach 0.107–0.202 against their best match — while `SIM-HELP-NETWORK-SLOW`, the *correct* answer for the evening-speeds query, scores 0.214. Relevant and irrelevant overlap, so no floor separates them.
3. **Semantic ranking without a floor is worse than leaving it off.** With no floor, recall@5 hits a perfect 1.000 and citation accuracy *drops* to 0.900, because queries that previously returned no sources — and were honestly refused — now ground themselves on an unrelated clause. `min_relative_score` cannot catch this: it is a share of the best hit, so it cannot tell "all weak" from "one strong". Hence the absolute floor, derived from the noise band above rather than against the golden queries.

Closing this gate needs a learned multilingual embedder. The `Embedder` port exists for exactly that and needs no further change to accept one.

## F1 — cassettes can be recorded, and **none are committed**

`scripts/record_cassettes.py` plus `make cassettes` / `make cassettes-dry`. It builds the prompts the system actually sends for `extract`, `guard` and `reason` — including the planner prompt in `validate_plan`'s real JSON grammar — calls the configured provider once per prompt and writes the recordings.

**No cassettes are committed by this change, deliberately.** Recording needs a real provider key, which this environment does not have. The script refuses without `CLARITY_RECORD_CASSETTES=1` and refuses when no provider is configured; there is no `--offline` mode and no placeholder mode. A cassette whose `response` a developer typed is not a recording of anything, and a suite replaying one asserts what somebody imagined a model would say.

So F1's machinery is done and repeatable; the recordings themselves need somebody with a key to run `make cassettes`.

## F2 — the bounded agent step runs for the first time

`tests/unit/test_agent_planner.py` (11 tests). `_planner` returns `None` without a remote `reason` model, so `BoundedAgent`'s loop had never executed in CI — every existing test asserts the `NO_PLANNER` fallback.

These drive it through a `ScriptedPlanner` test double and pin the agent's half of the I1 contract: a well-formed plan runs its tool, the result comes back delimited as untrusted, and a plan naming a tool the state did not declare, **carrying an amount**, missing a reason code, or written as prose changes nothing about the turn. A test double rather than a cassette for the reason above, and named for what it is.

## F5 — the corpus is no longer English-only

The five simulated help articles now exist in Sinhala and Tamil too (15 sources, 5 per language). K03 quotes a retrieved clause verbatim, which is what makes a citation checkable — and the consequence was that a Sinhala customer asking in Sinhala got a correct answer quoting English. Retrieval already prefers the query's language without filtering the others out, so a Sinhala question still reaches an English-only clause when that is all there is.

Flagged in the source: the si/ta copy is a translation of an English draft and has **not** been reviewed by a native speaker. The real corpus is CX-approved copy per language.

## Decisions

- **No heavy ML dependency.** A learned embedder means torch, which breaks `lite`'s "Python only, no services" (ADR-0006) and an offline-safe build. The port accepts one; the default does not pull one. No licence check needed — nothing added to the runtime path (I17).
- **IDF is in, although it scores one query *worse* on the golden set.** Unweighted, the space measures "written in English" more than topic. IDF is the standard correction. Picking the unweighted variant because it scores 0.9333 vs 0.9000 on 30 examples would be fitting the model to its own test, and the difference is one query.
- **An architecture test caught my vector cache** (`test_module_state.py`) and it was right to. The cache meets both conditions that rule sets for a derived index rather than business state, so it was renamed `_vectors` and registered with the justification, rather than the rule being loosened.
- **No pgvector driver yet** — the rest of F4. Writing a vector store now would be building persistence for an embedder whose limits are the reason the gate still fails. Deferred explicitly, recorded in the devlog.

## Verified

- `tests/unit`: full suite passes (exit 0), including the 25 new tests.
- `tests/architecture`: 131 pass — after the one above was fixed properly.
- `pytest -k "knowledge or retrieval or rag or cassette or embed"`: 164 pass, 1 skip.
- `ruff check backend/src backend/scripts backend/tests`: clean.
- `mypy --strict` clean on both new modules (the 2 errors in the knowledge/container run are pre-existing missing optional extras: playwright, opentelemetry).
- `make eval` runs: `rag.recall_at_5` PASS 0.967, `rag.citation_accuracy` FAIL 0.931.

Not run: the full `make check`. This was asked for quickly and without the wider suite; the blast radius was run instead.

## Next

1. A learned multilingual embedder behind the `Embedder` port — nothing else in F moves `citation_accuracy`.
2. The pgvector store for `full`.
3. `make cassettes` with a real key, after which F2's assertions can run against a real planner answer.
4. An ADR is arguably owed for "the embed role is a port with a local non-learned driver". Not written; flagged.

author: foxinthehenhouse
body:
## What and why
`design/tokens.json` is still the source of truth. Agents now also get a one-page DESIGN.md at the repo root, written from it in Google Stitch's open DESIGN.md format.

- **Generator.** `plugins/app-in-a-box/template/scripts/design_md.py` ships with every app, so the app can regenerate its own file. The kit's `scripts/design_md.py` is a small shim that loads it, the same way `check_design.py` works, so there is only one copy.
- **Frontmatter.** It uses only Stitch's allowed top-level keys:
  - colours from the home mode's palette (accent → `primary`, bg → `background`, …)
  - the type roles, `rounded`, `spacing`
  - component recipes (primary/secondary button, input, chip, card)
  - Stitch's own linter (`npx @google/design.md lint`) reports **0 errors** on the template's output. It gives 4 "orphaned token" warnings for colours no component uses.
- **Body.** Stitch's eight sections in order, then Dark Mode (both palettes), Motion, Atmosphere, Iconography, Agent Prompt Guide, and a hand-written Decisions log.
- **What gets rewritten.** Only the frontmatter and the text between `<!-- design.md:generated:KEY -->` … `<!-- /design.md:generated:KEY -->` markers. Anything written outside the markers is kept. A deleted block is put back under its heading, or added as a new section before Decisions.
- **`--check`.** It exits 1 when a generated part no longer matches tokens.json, either from a hand edit or a token change nobody regenerated. It names the block, e.g. `DESIGN.md: generated block 'colors' differs from design/tokens.json`.
- **Freeze.** `prototype.py freeze` writes DESIGN.md along with the other three files, all-or-nothing as before. A re-freeze keeps existing prose.
- **Render.** `render.py` creates DESIGN.md when it's missing. When it exists, it refreshes only the generated parts, with or without `--force`.
- **App guards.** The app's `ci.yml` and `.githooks/pre-commit` run `python3 scripts/design_md.py --check`. The pre-commit only runs it when tokens.json or DESIGN.md is staged.
  - `test_guards_wired.py` now counts `design_md.py` as a guard. It fails if either place stops running the `--check` form, and has its own negative control.
  - New `tests/test_design_md.py` gives the app its own negative controls.
- **Agent docs.** AGENTS.md (rule 7) and mobile/AGENTS.md now say: read DESIGN.md before any UI work, and change tokens through the design flow, never by hand. The prototype skill's freeze step mentions DESIGN.md.
- **Credit.** THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md credits Stitch's format, with the Apache-2.0 text in `licenses/Apache-2.0-design-md.txt`. No Stitch code is copied.

## Verified with
- `selftest: 326 passed, 0 failed, 5 skipped` (full run)
- `selftest: 330 passed, 0 failed, 5 skipped` (`--mobile`)
- New area `scripts/selftest.d/design-md.sh` has 19 checks, all passing against a real rendered app. They cover:
  - freeze writes the file
  - the frontmatter parses as YAML and uses only Stitch's keys
  - section order
  - a re-freeze keeps a planted prose paragraph and a Decisions entry
  - `--check` fails on a planted edit inside a generated block, a frontmatter edit, a changed token, a deleted block, and a missing file; it passes when prose is added outside the markers
  - re-rendering with `--force` refreshes the blocks and keeps prose
  - the app's guard-wiring test fails when CI drops `--check`
  - the app's pre-commit refuses a stale DESIGN.md, then accepts the regenerated one
- The rendered app's own pytest suite is green. ruff and pyright are clean on the new files.

## Not verified
- These were skipped locally, as expected: actionlint, zizmor, maestro and Postgres. That includes actionlint on the edited `ci.yml`.
- I ran Stitch's linter by hand once; nothing runs it in CI.

⚖️ **Calls I made:**
- **Render refreshes an existing DESIGN.md**, rather than only creating it when missing. This keeps the drift gate green after a token change plus re-render, and still never touches prose. The alternative was to skip any existing file.
- **Frontmatter uses Stitch's colour names** (`primary`, `on-surface`, …) so Stitch tools and its linter recognise them. The Colors table maps each one back to its code name (`color.accent`, …). The alternative was code names in the frontmatter, which would fail Stitch's "missing primary" lint.
- **CLAUDE.md is unchanged.** It already imports AGENTS.md and says to edit AGENTS.md instead.
- **AGENTS.md is now exactly at the selftest's 150-line cap.** To fit the new rule, I folded it into rule 7 and shortened that rule's wording ("accessibilityLabel on every control, never colour alone").
- **Iconography uses only tokens.json.** The prototype direction's icon style (rounded/sharp) isn't in tokens.json, so DESIGN.md doesn't show it.

**Out-of-scope finding:** `scripts/render.py` and `scripts/prototype.py` were already not ruff-format clean on main. I left them alone.

author: lathrys-at
body:
This pull request delivers both steps of the plan `ci-efficiency` (#56). Merge #56 first.

## What changes

- **The daily run also runs the jobs that restore a cache.** The build jobs, the format check, the coverage job, and the bridge crate job lose the line `if: github.event_name != 'schedule'`. The daily run then reads each cache of `main` every day. GitHub removes a cache that no run reads for seven days. From 2026-09-17 to 2026-10-03, 16 days passed with no push and no pull request. Every cache of these jobs was then gone, and the first four runs took 9 to 11 minutes to turn green, against about 45 seconds when the caches hold. The plugin job restores no cache, and it still skips the daily run.
- **The CLI tests check a child process sooner.** `outcome_within` in `test/test_cli.ml` sleeps 1 ms before its first check of the child process, and doubles the pause after each check, up to 50 ms. Before, it slept 50 ms before each check. The time limit of each test does not change.

## Measurements

The CLI test group, 10 runs on one machine: a median of 0.69 s before and 0.40 s after. The full suite varies more than that between runs, because the property tests draw new inputs on each run.

## What it costs

The daily run gains four jobs, about 2.5 minutes of runner time a day, which costs nothing on a public repository. A daily build also shows a change in a runner image that breaks the build on the day it comes.

## Where to look first

The comment on the schedule at the top of `.github/workflows/build.yml`. The next daily run after the merge is the first to run the four jobs.

## What changed (v1.182.0)
- **Android app:** during a call, a **🔊 Speaker** button now sits between Mute and Hang Up. Tap it to put the call on the loudspeaker; it turns blue while the speaker is on. Tap again to go back to the earpiece.
- The button always shows what the phone is really doing, because it asks the phone instead of guessing.
- The website doesn't show the button: a browser can't switch the speaker. An app installed before this build doesn't show it either, until it updates.

## Why
You asked for a speaker button after calls started working in the app (#329). A web page can't choose between the earpiece and the loudspeaker, so the app now does it with a small piece of its own Android code.

## Where
- `mobile/android/.../CallAudioPlugin.java` (new): the app's own Android code that switches the call between the earpiece and the loudspeaker, and reports which one is on.
- `mobile/android/.../MainActivity.java`: turns that code on when the app starts.
- `src/lib/call-audio.ts` (new): how the CRM talks to it. It only says "available" inside an app build that has it.
- `src/app/(app)/voice-dialer.tsx`: the Speaker button. It checks the speaker when the call rings, when it's answered, and after every tap.
- `src/app/globals.css`: the blue "on" look. Mute is also no longer nudged off-centre.
- Docs: DECISIONS #111, `docs/features/scheduling-communications.md`, `docs/MOBILE_RELEASE.md`.

## Proof
- Test written first (`call-audio.test.ts`). It checks that the CRM and the app use the same name and the same two commands, that the app turns the code on at startup, and that the button only shows where it works. It failed before the code existed.
- `npm test`: ✅ 1382/1382 pass
- `npm run lint`: ✅ only the one existing warning
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: ✅
- `npm run build`: ✅
- **The Android app compiles.** The "Android App (test build)" workflow ran on this branch **before** this PR was opened and passed: [run #12](https://github.com/asherperetz18-dot/contractor-CRM/actions/runs/37247428526). The new Java was also compiled locally against Android 15's own classes.

- **Not tested on a real phone:** the cloud can't run an Android phone. The switch itself is standard Android. Please try it on your phone (below).

## How to test it yourself
1. **This needs a new app build, like last time. After merging: Actions → "Android App (Play release)" → Run workflow on `main`. Then, in Play Console → Testing → Internal testing → Create new release, upload the new `.aab` from the run's Artifacts (ai-build-pros-crm-play-4) → Next → Save → Start rollout.**
2. On your phone, update the app from the Play Store (Manage apps → Updates).
3. Place a call. When it rings, a **🔊 Speaker** button appears between Mute and Hang Up.
4. Tap it. The sound moves to the loudspeaker and the button turns blue. Tap again: back to the earpiece.
