author: dannysmp
body:
This pull request makes every way a request can fail in sign-in and chat say what did not work, why, and what to do next, and returns a customer whose session has ended to the sign-in with a note in their own language instead of a dead chat.

### Summary of Changes

- **Failure model**:
  - `lib/failure.ts`: classifies a failed request as unauthorized, rate limited, unavailable, timed out, offline or other from its HTTP status and the two ways `fetch` fails before one exists; every request now carries a 30 second timeout so a stalled connection never leaves a spinner running.
  - `i18n/failureReason.ts`: turns a failure kind into the sentence that explains it and names the way forward, in Spanish, Portuguese or English.
- **Chat**:
  - `useConversation.ts`: keeps the kind of failure instead of an error string; `retry` on a conversation that never started asks for the opening message again rather than doing nothing.
  - `ChatFeature.tsx`: the could-not-start and could-not-send states use the shared `ErrorState` (what failed, why, Retry); a start failure keeps the page region and the header's Sign out; an unauthorized answer hands control back to the app instead of offering a Retry that cannot work.
  - `TurnForm.tsx`: the hidden announcement states the characters that are really left when a step is reached, and clears once the message is sent.
- **Sign-in and shell**:
  - `SignInScreen.tsx`: a refused code, a limit, an unavailable service and an offline browser each get their own message; the persona directory failing shows its own state with a Retry; the access code stays after a refusal so it can be corrected; autocomplete is off for the shared demonstration code; the submit label changes while the request is in flight; a new `preferredLang` prop selects the first persona in a given language.
  - `App.tsx`: when the chat reports the session has ended, the person returns to the sign-in with a warning note in the language the conversation was last in, the persona picker already on that language and on the same persona when they speak it and the keyboard on the form.
  - `components/ui/ErrorState.tsx`: one layout for a failure: title, reason, actions, announced as an alert.
- **Messages**: `app.sessionExpired`, `failure.*`, `signin.accessCodeHint` and `signin.submitting` in all three languages; the parity test covers them. `LANGUAGE_NAMES` is shared.
- **Tests**: `failure.test.ts`, `ErrorState.test.tsx`, `App.expiry.test.tsx`, `ChatFeature.failures.test.tsx`, `SignInScreen.failures.test.tsx` and extended `useConversation`, `TurnForm`, `client` and `api` tests. A flaky language assertion in the chat test now waits for the conversation to report its language.

### Motivation and Context

The interface review marked every failure as below the bar: one generic "could not" for a wrong code, a limit and a dead network alike; a session that ended left the customer in a chat that could not work; the sign-in showed English-only or empty states when the directory failed. Decisions a reviewer should know:

- No "Back to sign-in" button on a chat that failed to start: the header already has Sign out, and a second route to the same place would compete with Retry.
- An expired chat returns to sign-in rather than offering Retry, since the same token would be refused again. The note names the language the session was in and the persona picker preselects a persona in that language, so the note and the form always agree.
- The shared out-of-band access code is not stored by the browser (`autocomplete="off"`), and is kept in the field after a refusal so a typo can be fixed.
- The announcement of remaining characters states the true count at the step; earlier it announced the step value, which was wrong when a paste jumped past it.
- Depends on the conversation interface pull request (#391): this branch is stacked on it and its base merges first.

### Claims

1. A 401, 429, 5xx, a timeout, an offline `fetch` and any other failure each map to their own kind, and the chat and sign-in show the matching sentence in the active language (`failure.test.ts`, `failureReason`, the failure tests in all three languages).
2. A request that takes longer than 30 seconds fails as a timeout.
3. When the chat reports the session ended, `App` renders the sign-in with a `status` note in the language the conversation had reached (which can differ from the persona's when a reply moved to another language), a picker whose value is the same persona when they speak that language, else the first persona who does (the first persona when none), and focus on the form.
4. A conversation that failed to start shows Retry (unless unauthorized); pressing it asks for the opening message again and the failure state is replaced by the conversation.
5. A failed send keeps the customer's words and offers one Retry; an unauthorized one offers none.
6. The sign-in keeps the access code after a refusal, switches the submit label while submitting, and shows a separate state, with Retry, when the persona directory cannot be loaded.
7. The announcement of remaining characters states the count the field really has and is cleared after sending.
8. Axe reports no violations on any of the failure states in all three languages, at 375, 768 and 1440 (99 frames, light theme).
9. The behaviors the new tests name were mutation-checked one at a time (the source line removed or changed, the suite re-run): `preferredLang` selection, retry-on-start, the 429 classification, clearing the announcement on send, the language the note follows, the persona kept after expiry, the focus on Retry after a failed start and the 30 second limit each fail at least one test.

### Verification

| Check | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Type-check | `npx tsc -b` | clean |
| Lint | `npx eslint .` | clean |
| Format | `npx prettier --check .` | clean |
| Tests and coverage | `npx vitest run --coverage` | 400 passed in 48 files; statements 98.45%, branches 95.28%, lines 98.99% |
| Build | `npm run build` | built |
| Accessibility | axe-core (wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa, best-practice) on the built app against a mocked backend, 11 failure states x 3 languages x 3 widths | no violations in 99 frames |
| References | `thot-check-references --base origin/fix/e10-ui-chat-conversation` | clean |
| Manual check | before and after screenshots at 375, 768 and 1440 in Spanish, Portuguese and English for sign-in (refused, limited, unavailable, offline, directory down), chat start failed, offline, expired at start, send limited and expired at send | reviewed; no clipping, no mixed-language note and form |

### Security, Privacy and Observability

- **Data handled:** the demonstration access code, held only in the field's own state and sent to the sign-in endpoint; nothing new is stored or logged.
- **Controls:** the browser is told not to save the shared code; a failed request never prints a response body or the token into the page; an ended session drops its token from memory.
- **Telemetry:** none.

### Risks and Rollback

- **Risks:** the 30 second timeout aborts a genuinely slow turn and shows the timeout message; the retry resends under the same turn id, which the endpoint treats as a repeat. The timeout is one constant.
- **Rollback:** revert the commits; no contract or data change.

### Known Gaps and Follow-ups

- A connection-level `TypeError` of any origin reads as offline.
- Screen-reader behavior was checked through role and live-region assertions and axe, not with a physical screen reader.
- Before-state captures exist in Spanish only for the failure states (the previous screens could not render some of them at all).
- The result card and the remaining copy and locale fixes are separate changes; the console's content is part of this branch.
- Stacked on #376; its base merges first.

author: foxinthehenhouse
body:
## What and why
Generated directions kept landing on the same handful of faces, and the founder had no way to try other type without another design round.

- **The library.** `plugins/app-in-a-box/scripts/proto/fonts.json` lists 46 Google Fonts families in eight personality groups: humanist, grotesk, geometric, condensed, rounded, serif display, serif text and mono.
  - Each family records the roles it suits, its weights and axes, licence `OFL-1.1`, `rfn: false` and its google/fonts source folder.
  - Every family was checked against its `OFL.txt` and `METADATA.pb` on google/fonts main.
  - Dropped because their `OFL.txt` reserves a font name: IBM Plex Mono ("Plex") and Varela Round.
  - Dropped because it has no `OFL.txt` to check: M PLUS Rounded 1c.
  - 15 other families passed the check but were cut to keep the list near 45. Each is recorded under `excluded` with the reason.
  - There are 34 pairings, including all the suggested ones.
- **The guard.** A new command, `prototype.py fonts`, fails if any family isn't OFL-1.1, reserves a font name, is on `OVERUSED_FONTS` or is built into the phone. It also fails if a pairing uses an unlisted family or a family in a role it doesn't suit, or if the design-directions archetype table names a family that isn't listed or built in.
  - The table now suggests Fredoka / Nunito, Azeret Mono, SF Pro, Petrona / Public Sans and Syne. It no longer names Baloo 2 or IBM Plex Mono, or "SF" on its own.
- **The prototype.** A "Type" knob sits under Direction.
  - It offers "Direction default" plus up to three pairings whose display face shares the direction's personality, each shown in its own face. Picking one swaps the phone's fonts live.
  - The pick is remembered with the other settings and resets when the direction changes.
  - A direction on the system font, or on a face outside the library, offers nothing to swap and says so.
- **Font loading.** The alternate fonts load through the existing per-family mechanism. They are inlined up to a 400 KB budget; past that they load as Google Fonts links.
  - Google Fonts URLs now ask only for weights the family has. Asking Young Serif for 700 used to fail the whole family.
- **Choices and freeze.**
  - "Copy my choices" emits `font: {pairing, display, body[, mono]}`.
  - `resolve_choices` accepts only a pairing that was offered for that direction.
  - `frozen_tokens` writes the pairing into `tokens.font` and moves each type role to the nearest weight the new family has, so `mobile/lib/fonts.ts` can register every one.
  - Choices with no `font` freeze exactly as before.
  - SCREENS.md gets a Type row.
- **Docs.** The prototype and design-directions skills and `agents/visual-designer.md` now point at the library and the knob.

## Verified
- `selftest: 324 passed, 0 failed, 5 skipped` (full run from the worktree).
- New area `scripts/selftest.d/font-library.sh`: 17 checks, all passing in isolation through mini.sh. Each guard is planted and must fail with its specific message:
  - an overused family, a reserved name, a non-OFL licence
  - a pairing using an unlisted family, or a display-only face as body
  - an unlisted family in the archetype table, or the table missing
  - freeze given a pairing that wasn't offered, or a malformed `font`
- I also broke the weight clamping on purpose and its check failed.
- One check in `prototype.sh` assumed exactly 4 font links offline. It now counts the directions' families plus the alternates.
- Drove the rendered prototype in headless Chromium (Playwright) with real inlined fonts:
  - the Calm direction offers Red Hat, Wix Madefor and Golos
  - picking Red Hat changes the computed font-family
  - `choices().font` is correct
  - the pick survives a reload
  - switching to Athletic resets it, with no options and no console errors
- The generated app still registers whichever family is chosen: frozen `tokens.font` drives the existing `fonts.test.ts` check, and the existing `_fonts_wired` check passes.

## Not verified
- Skill evals were not run (they run in CI's evals workflow).
- `--mobile` was not run: nothing under template/mobile or mobile-deps.sh changed.
- actionlint, zizmor, maestro and Postgres were skipped locally.

**⚖️ Calls I made**
- **About 45 families.** I cut 15 verified families (Gantari, Radio Canada, Rethink Sans, Commissioner, Inclusive Sans, Afacad, Saira, Pathway Extreme, Anybody, Crimson Pro, Piazzolla, Brygada 1918, Reddit Mono, Spline Sans Mono, Victor Mono). The alternative was to ship all 61 that passed.
- **Which pairings the knob offers.** It works them out from the display face's personality, takes them in file order and stops at 3. The alternative was a per-direction list of pairings in the spec, which would mean a schema change.
- **Size budget.** Inlining stops at 400 KB of alternates, and the rest load from Google Fonts, so previewing those needs a connection. With fonts cached, the fixture page went from about 340 KB to about 815 KB at the earlier 480 KB budget. The alternative was to load every alternate as a link (smallest page, no offline preview) or inline them all.
- **Weights.** Freeze moves each role to the nearest weight the family has (ties go heavier). The prototype turns off faked bold while a pairing is active, so it shows the same thing. The alternative was to exclude single-weight families like Young Serif, Gloock, Hedvig Letters Serif and Fragment Mono.
- **Choice shape.** The choice also carries `pairing` (the pairing id) next to `display` and `body`. The alternative was the bare `{display, body}`, which is still accepted.

**Out of scope, not fixed**
- The comment at the top of `template/mobile/lib/fonts.ts` uses Fraunces as its example, and Fraunces is on `OVERUSED_FONTS`.

author: huntharo
body:
## Summary

Git 2.56.0 changed `git push <url>`: when exactly one configured remote has that push URL, Git now moves that remote's remote-tracking ref (`refs/remotes/<name>/*`, `@{push}`) the way a push by name always has ([RelNotes/2.56.0.adoc:734](https://github.com/git/git/blob/master/Documentation/RelNotes/2.56.0.adoc?plain=1#L734)). That broke a PwrAgent fixture (pwrdrvr/PwrAgent#2543). This PR is the PwrGit audit.

**Nothing in PwrGit depends on the old behaviour: no fixture, and no product path.** So this PR adds no fixture or product fix. It adds:

- a test that pins `pushPlannedRefs`' refetch no matter which Git runs. That refetch is the one product line that 2.56 makes look removable, and removing it would be wrong.
- `AGENTS.md` guidance on making a tracking ref stale (`src/main/git`, plus one line in `e2e`). It also records the finding below: the unit suite runs product code on the **bundled** Git, not the one on `PATH`.

## What 2.56 actually does (probed locally, Homebrew 2.56.0 vs Apple Git 2.50.1)

| Push | 2.50.1 | 2.56.0 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `git push origin …` (by name) | moves `origin/*` | moves `origin/*` |
| `git push <url byte-identical to origin's push URL> …` | unchanged | **moves `origin/*`** (source a ref, `HEAD` or a raw object ID; creates and deletes too) |
| `file://` URL, `./` in the path, trailing `/`, relative path | unchanged | unchanged |
| URL equal to `remote.origin.url` while a separate `pushurl` is set | unchanged | unchanged (it matches push URLs) |
| two remotes with the same URL | unchanged | unchanged (no unique match) |
| from a linked worktree | unchanged | moves it (worktrees share `refs/remotes`) |
| from a separate clone | unchanged | unchanged |

## Fixtures

Every test and E2E push whose destination is not a literal remote name:

| Site | Destination | Depends on 2.56? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `remote.test.ts` "plans and pushes against a remote's configured push URL" | `fetch.git`, the remote's `url`, while its `pushurl` is `push.git` | No. Git matches push URLs, and `planPushRefs` fetches the remote before it reads anything |
| `tag.test.ts` (push URL review) | `fetch.git`, `refs/tags/*` | No. The default refspec maps no tags |
| `open-pr-service.test.ts` `addUpstream` | `upstream.git` from `seed`, a separate clone with no remote at that URL | No (this is already the separate-clone pattern) |
| `repository-maintenance.test.ts`, `auto-remote-check.test.ts` (`remote` variables) | remote names | No |

The `update-ref refs/remotes/...` fixtures (`fork-tracking`, `fork-remotes`, `worktree-untracked-commits`, `bulk-sync`, `auto-remote-check`, `remote`, `repository-maintenance`, `worktree-state`, `repo-indexer`, mcp-server `git-metadata`) write the ref directly. They behave the same on every Git, so I left them alone. `existing-fork-recovery.spec.ts` makes `origin/main` with `update-ref` because its `origin` is a fake GitHub URL, and the app pushes by name. `git-sandbox.ts` and `docs-world.ts` push only by name.

Evidence:

- **Unit suite: 383 files, all green in four runs.**
  - Fixture helpers on Git 2.56.0, then on 2.50.1, with the product-side `GitExec` on the bundle as committed: 4804 passed, 1 skipped, before the new test.
  - Both again with the product `GitExec` on the `PATH` Git (local patch, not committed; see below): 4805 passed, 1 skipped, with the new test.
- **E2E fixtures:** I built every `git-sandbox` maker plus `createDocsWorld()` headlessly under each Git and diffed `for-each-ref` (subject, upstream, ahead/behind) per repo. The refs are identical. The only diff is `origin/HEAD` in `makeRepoBehindRemote` / `makeRepoWithRewrittenDivergence`. Apple Git's built-in `init` default is `main` and Homebrew's is `master`, and those makers don't set the bare's `HEAD`. That has nothing to do with push.
- **Negative control on the method:** a PwrAgent-style fixture (`git push <remote path> HEAD:refs/heads/feature`, then assert `origin/feature` unchanged) **fails on 2.56 and passes on 2.50**, both from the repo and from a linked worktree. The separate-clone version passes on both. So the version switch is real and would have caught a dependent fixture.

## Product audit

| Code path | Pushes to | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Toolbar Push / Publish, `pushRemote` (`remote:push`) | upstream, or `--set-upstream -- <remote> HEAD` | **Unaffected.** By name. `refreshRemoteBranches` only re-indexes local refs |
| Leased push, `pushBranchWithLease` (reset dialog, fork-sync push-back, rebase `pushTo`) | remote name | **Unaffected.** Its doc already relies on a named push moving the ref |
| Push to… review, `pushPlannedRefs` (`remote:pushRefs`) | the remote's push URL, then `fetch --prune <remote>` | **Unaffected; keep the refetch.** 2.56 makes it redundant only when exactly one remote owns that push URL, and the bundle is 2.53 with no enforced floor. Now pinned by a test |
| Remote tag push / delete, `applyRemoteTagPlan` | the remote's push URL, `refs/tags/*` | **Unaffected with the default refspec.** With `+refs/tags/*:refs/tags/*` configured, a 2.56 delete also removes the local tag. That is what the next PwrGit fetch (always `--prune`) does on any Git, and what `git push <remote> :tag` has always done |
| Fork in place / fork-tracking repair (`fork-remotes.ts`, `fork-tracking.ts`, `ForkService`) | no push | **Unaffected.** It reads `refs/remotes/<fork>/<branch>`; a user who pushed to the fork's exact URL from a terminal now passes "Fetch first" sooner |
| Denied-push fork recovery (`pushWasDenied`) | named push | **Unaffected.** Keyed off stderr |
| Background tip check (`auto-remote-check.ts`, #386 counterparts) | none (`ls-remote`, refspec fetch, CAS `update-ref -d`) | **Unaffected.** Still needed for pushes from other clients and non-matching URLs |
| No-upstream local-commit count (`worktree-state.ts`, #386) | — | **Unaffected.** `--not --remotes` just becomes accurate sooner after a matching URL push |
| SSH remote recovery, bulk sync, branch lifecycle, maintenance | none | **Unaffected** |

No product code runs `update-ref` against `refs/remotes`, except the tip check's compare-and-swap delete of a branch the remote no longer advertises.

**Minimum Git version.** PwrGit does not declare or enforce one. It bundles Git **2.53.0** (dugite 3.2.3, the newest release). Settings → Git runtime accepts any installed Git that answers `git --version` and has working Git LFS (`probeGitRuntime`). The newest features the code depends on are `fetch --atomic` (bulk sync) and `show --diff-merges=first-parent`, both Git **2.31**, so in practice the floor is 2.31, unchecked. Nothing can rely on the 2.56 behaviour until both the bundle and an enforced floor reach 2.56.

## Found along the way: unit tests run product code on the bundled Git

`createSystemGit()` merges its environment through `gitExecutionEnvironment` (#261, to keep prompting off). Since #303, that also puts dugite's `bin` and `libexec/git-core` first on `PATH` and sets `GIT_EXEC_PATH`. So every product call under test runs **Git 2.53.0 whatever is installed**. Only fixture helpers (`execFileSync("git")`) follow `PATH`. In the same vitest worker, `createSystemGit()(["--version"])` printed `git version 2.53.0` while `execFileSync("git", ["--version"])` printed `2.56.0` / `2.50.1`.

The new `AGENTS.md` bullet records this. I did not change it here, because which Git the suite should run is a decision for you. To get the "both Gits" product numbers above, I used a local patch (not committed) that strips the bundle variables from `createSystemGit`'s environment.

## The new test

`remote.test.ts` › "refreshes the pushed remote-tracking ref whichever Git runs": push to `target` through `pushPlannedRefs`, then assert `refs/remotes/target/main` is the pushed head. A second remote, `mirror`, has the same URL, so 2.56 declines to pick one. A probe push (run through the same `GitExec` as the product code) first asserts that nothing moved, so the test fails loudl

## What

This is option (a), as Pete approved on #528: when Romper can't save which local store to use, it now says so and keeps what it built.

- **End of setup** (`useLocalStoreWizard`): `setLocalStorePathHelper` now resolves `false` when the save fails. That covers `setLocalStorePath` returning false or throwing, the `api.setSetting` fallback rejecting, and no way to save at all.
  - On `false`, the new `saveFinishedStore` keeps the finished store and doesn't run `cleanupPartialInit`. The wizard shows "Couldn't save the local store setting. Try again."
  - The store's target path and setup summary (truncation warnings, stereo notices) are kept in a ref. The next **Initialize Local Store** for that path calls `retrySavingStore`, which retries only the settings save: no copy, download, database or import step runs again.
  - Once the save works, the wizard ends as setup would have, with the guidance or `onSuccess`.
  - `initialize` is now a small dispatcher over `runSetup`, which is the previous body. Its catch block moved to `handleSetupFailure` and `cleanUpPartialStore`, with no change in behavior, to clear a SonarCloud S3776 cognitive-complexity finding.
- **Message reuse**: the text is now `LOCAL_STORE_SETTING_NOT_SAVED`, exported from `useChooseExistingLocalStore.ts` (#474). Choose Existing Store, the wizard and the dialog all use it. No new wording was added.
- **Set Up a New Local Store** (`KitsView`'s `onRerunWizard`, `setLocalStorePath(null)`): the result is no longer discarded with `void`. `InvalidLocalStoreDialog` types the prop as `() => Promise<boolean>`. If clearing fails, the dialog stays open and shows the same message under the button (`rerun-wizard-error`).
- **Type**: `useLocalStoreWizard`'s `setLocalStorePath` parameter changes from `(path) => Promise<boolean> | void` to `(path: string) => Promise<boolean>`.

**Screenshots:** none regenerated. No `SCREENSHOT_TARGETS` entry shows the setup wizard or the Invalid Local Store dialog.

**For Pete:** if the setting still can't be saved and the user quits, main's quit-time `cleanupUnfinishedSetups` still removes the store. `markSetupComplete` only runs after a successful `write-settings`. This PR doesn't change that, since it's a separate product choice.

## Siblings

- **Into the create flow.** Both ways in end in `setLocalStorePathHelper`, so the one fix covers both:
  - first run: `KitsView` → `LocalStoreWizardModal` → `LocalStoreWizardUI`;
  - from the kit browser: `KitBrowserContainer.handleSetLocalStorePath` → `KitBrowser` → `useKitDialogs`. Its `async () => false` fallback now shows the message instead of passing silently.
- **Choose Existing Store** (wizard and Preferences, through `useChooseExistingLocalStore`) already checked the result.
- **`ChangeLocalStoreDirectoryDialog` and `InvalidLocalStoreDialog.handleUpdatePath`** already checked it too.
- **`setLocalStorePath(null)`** has one caller, `KitsView`'s `onRerunWizard`, which is fixed here.
- Bank-name code is unchanged; #567 is working there.

## Verified

- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint:check`, `npm run test:fast` and `npm run trace:check` all pass. The pre-commit hook passed too.
- Unit tests:
  - `useLocalStoreWizard` (`[UC-01]`): the store is kept with no cleanup when the save returns false, throws, or the `setSetting` fallback rejects. Try again calls only the save (no `ensureDir`, download, `createRomperDb` or `setupImportKit`) and returns the setup summary.
  - `InvalidLocalStoreDialog` (`[UC-05]`): it shows the message when clearing fails and clears it on a retry that works.
- New e2e spec, `tests/e2e/store-setting-save.e2e.test.ts`. It makes the save fail by putting a non-empty folder where `romper-settings.json` goes, which works on every platform, and removing the folder lets the next save through.
  - `[UC-01] [UC-03]`: blank setup shows the message and keeps `.romperdb/romper.sqlite`, with nothing moved aside. Try again saves the setting and shows the guidance.
  - `[UC-05]`: Set Up a New Local Store shows the message and keeps the dialog open. Once the save works, it opens the wizard.
- `npm run build`, then `npm run test:play` on the new spec plus `sd-card-setup`, `onboarding-errors`, `choose-existing-store`, `factory-archive-errors`, `missing-store`, `preferences-local-store` and `settings-persistence`: 18 passed. The #518 `test.fail()` is still expected to fail on this branch.
- Ran the built app headless (temp `ROMPER_USER_DATA_DIR`) and checked screenshots of the wizard and the dialog with the message showing.

body:
## SAYURI self-development

Adds MemRL-based episodic reinforcement without destabilizing the normal assistant or EvoAgentX optimizer stack.

### Three-runtime architecture
1. **Sayuri Core** — lightweight chat/runtime; records reward-labelled episodes in MemRL-compatible shadow mode.
2. **Evolution Worker** — isolated `.venv-evolution` with EvoAgentX heavy optimizers.
3. **MemRL Worker** — isolated `.venv-memrl` with pinned MemRL.

MemRL and EvoAgentX heavy extras are deliberately not co-installed because their current transitive OpenAI SDK version ranges conflict.

### Learning pipeline
Evaluator → Teacher/Reflection → Experience → MemRL reward episode → Evolution Gate → Evolution Lab → benchmark gates → strategy version / rollback.

### Safety
- no self-modifying source code;
- MemRL cannot auto-promote strategies;
- evidence + confidence + positive reward are required to reinforce a strategy;
- regression/safety/quality gates remain authoritative;
- atomic rollback restores the prior verified strategy.

### MemRL
Pinned to `MemTensor/MemRL@c1b322ca43de36ddf64c6712f89d0095bfc35ce0`.

### CI
Normal core, EvoAgentX Evolution Worker and MemRL Worker are verified independently.

author: foxinthehenhouse
body:
## What and why
The app's AGENTS.md stated three rules as prose: backend computes, routers do I/O while services hold logic, and the LLM is fenced in one module. They now fail the build.

**Backend:** contracts live in the template's `pyproject.toml` under `[tool.importlinter]`, and `lint-imports` is a new step in the CI python job.
- **Layers contract:** `main → routers → services → db → config`, never upward. Indirect chains count. `auth`, `ratelimit`, `middleware` and `observability` are shared helpers outside the layers.
- **Forbidden contract:** `anthropic` and `openai` can't be imported anywhere in `backend/`. The AI recipe (or scaffold step 7) adds its one fenced module to `ignore_imports`, e.g. `backend.services.ai_summary -> anthropic`. Taking that one import out of the graph also lets callers of the AI module pass. An entry that matches no import fails the check, so the fence can't go stale.
- `import-linter>=2.15,<3` is in `requirements-dev.txt`. `.import_linter_cache/` is added to `.gitignore`.
- `test_guards_wired.py` now checks that CI runs `lint-imports` and that both contracts still say what AGENTS.md says. Five negative controls cover the ways to weaken them: contracts removed, layers inverted, an SDK dropped from the fence, external packages turned off, indirect imports allowed.

**Mobile:** a new `mobile/eslint.boundaries.js`, spread into `eslint.config.js`. It uses core ESLint rules only, so nothing new is installed.
- Only `lib/api.ts` calls `fetch`. That covers the bare global and `globalThis`/`window`/`global`/`self.fetch`. Tests may stub it.
- Nothing under `app/` imports `lib/supabase` or `@supabase/supabase-js`.
- Nothing under `components/ui/` imports `lib/api`.

**Selftest:** a new area, `scripts/selftest.d/architecture-boundaries.sh`, with 16 checks.
- **Python, using the app's own venv:** the pristine render keeps both contracts. Plants each fail with the specific message:
  - a service importing a router
  - an indirect upward chain (config → unlisted helper → router)
  - `anthropic` in a router
  - `openai` in a service
  - a stale fence entry

  The recipe's fenced module passes once it is listed.
- **ESLint:** `eslint@^9` and `@typescript-eslint/parser@^8` are installed from npm into the temp dir, which takes about 20s. They lint a copy of the rendered app's `app/`, `components/` and `lib/` with the boundaries file alone. The pristine copy passes and five plants fail with their messages:
  - `fetch` in a screen
  - `globalThis.fetch` outside `lib/api.ts`
  - `lib/supabase` in `app/`
  - `supabase-js` in `app/`
  - `lib/api` in `components/ui`

  The full Expo config is proven green by `npm run gates` under `--mobile`.

**Docs:** template AGENTS.md (rules 1 and 8), backend and mobile AGENTS.md, the `recipe-ai-feature` step 1 and the scaffold step 7 now point at the checks. The README CI line is updated. Template AGENTS.md stays at the 150-line cap; to fit, I rewrapped "How work flows here" item 6 with no wording change.

## Verified with
- `scripts/selftest.sh --mobile`: `selftest: 327 passed, 0 failed, 5 skipped`. The skips are maestro, Postgres ×2, actionlint and zizmor, all expected locally. This one run covered the full non-mobile selftest, the new area, `npm run gates green` and `eslint catches hex literal`.
- The new area on its own: 16/16 passed.
- Template pytest on a fresh render: 670 passed. `lint-imports` reports "2 kept, 0 broken". ruff, black and pyright are clean on the edited test file.
- By hand, in the kept `--mobile` app with the real `eslint-config-expo` config: the pristine `app/`, `components/` and `lib/` pass, and the fetch, `lib/supabase` and `components/ui → lib/api` plants each error with the boundary message.

## Not verified
- The generated CI step `run: lint-imports` has not run on GitHub Actions.
- In the default (non-`--mobile`) selftest, the ESLint plants need npm registry access. They skip without it, and under strict mode (`APPBOX_SELFTEST_STRICT=1`, kit CI) a skip counts as a failure.
- The real-Expo-config plants were checked by hand only. They are not automated, because adding them meant editing `selftest.sh`'s mobile block, which other workers share.

**⚖️ Calls I made:**
- **Fence lives in `ignore_imports`.** The recipe or scaffold names the AI module there explicitly. The alternative was a sub-package fence (`backend/ai/**`), but import-linter wildcards can't match part of a name like `ai_*`, and the recipe already uses `backend/services/ai_<feature>.py`.
- **`main` and `config` are layers too,** not only routers/services/db. Nothing currently breaks this, but it is stricter than the ticket asked.
- **The fence also bans `@supabase/supabase-js` in `app/`,** not just `lib/supabase`.
- **`components/ui` may import `lib/query`.** `OfflineBanner` uses `useOnline` from it, so only `lib/api` is restricted.
- **The selftest installs eslint from npm** into the temp dir, rather than adding a package to `mobile-deps.sh` or relying on `--mobile` alone.
- **Coordination:** I edited `recipe-ai-feature/SKILL.md` step 1, which the parallel `ai-recipe-rag` worktree may also touch. If that worker renames the fenced module, its recipe needs a matching `ignore_imports` line.

**Out-of-scope findings (not fixed):**
- The scaffold step 7 names the AI module `backend/services/<name>_service.py`, but the `recipe-ai-feature` skill names it `backend/services/ai_<feature>.py`. The two disagree.
- Run outside its venv, `pyright` in the rendered app reports 71 missing-import errors. With `--pythonpath .venv/bin/python` it reports 0. CI is fine because it installs into the runner's Python.

body:
## Why

On PR #5376, `gh pr ready` was blocked with "This change is not finished. Repair ticket 0FPHQM so Safeword can read it". That happened even though the ticket was done and had a valid `verify.md`. The session was working in `.claude/worktrees/interesting-bardeen-368e8a`.

Delivery ticket: **EZD55Y** (`.project/tickets/EZD55Y-worktree-pr-ready-gate/`).

## Root cause

When a Claude Code session moves into a git worktree, `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` still points at the launch checkout. #5247 fixed this for edit gates by resolving the project from the edited file. Two paths were left on the launch checkout:

- **Bash gates in `pre-tool-quality.ts`.** The PR-readiness gate read tickets, session state, and `.project/readiness-ticket.json` from the main checkout. The ticket was not there, so it denied.
- **The `post-tool-quality.ts` observer.** It wrote session state and the readiness receipt into the main checkout. It also watched the main checkout's HEAD, so a commit in the worktree never triggered `finalizeReadinessReceipt`. Fixing only the gate would still have left it reading a receipt that never existed.

## What changed

Both hooks now use shared helpers in `hooks/lib/namespace-root.ts`, so the gate reads exactly where the observer writes:

- **`resolveToolProjectDirectory`** picks the project for each tool call:
  - Edits resolve from the edited file. This is the #5247 behavior.
  - Bash resolves from the hook input's `cwd` to the enrolled worktree containing it. This builds on `resolveWorkingProjectDirectory` from #5362.
  - Anything else falls back to the launch checkout.
- **`canonicalEditTarget`** resolves a relative edit path against the session `cwd`, then takes its real path. `canonicalPathForGate` moved here from pre-tool so both hooks share it.
- **Symlinks and path aliases.** Ownership compares real paths, so macOS `/var` vs `/private/var` spellings match. A shell `cwd` reached through a symlink belongs to the tree it lands in; the host spelling is kept unless the real path names a different owner. Post-tool now recognizes ticket and verify artifacts by their canonical path, matching pre-tool.
- **Closeout.** The session binding stays on the launch checkout, so closeout behavior does not change.

Excluded: Codex and Cursor adapters do not forward `cwd`, so they keep their current launch-checkout behavior.

## Verification

- Integration tests in `pr-readiness-delivery-gate.test.ts` use the main checkout as launch directory and an enrolled worktree as the session. Ready is allowed when the worktree ticket is done and verified, including when it was closed:
  - through a symlinked ticket folder under `.project/tickets`;
  - through an alias outside `.project/tickets`;
  - through edit targets relative to the session cwd;
  - and when the shell cwd is reached through a symlink.
- Ready is still denied from the unfinished launch checkout, and when the worktree ticket is unfinished.
- Unit tests for the helper are in `namespace-root-helpers.test.ts`.
- Every fix was written test-first and seen failing before it passed.
- Targeted vitest on `bdd78a97c`: 557/557 across 22 files (gate, hooks, closeout, review-stamp, Codex/Cursor adapters, lifecycle contract). The tsup build, `tsc --noEmit`, the parity check and the generated-surface check are all clean.
- The Cursor lifecycle fixture hashes were refreshed because the hook template bytes changed.

## Risks and review focus

- Blast radius: every Claude Code Bash and edit hook call now resolves its project through the shared helper. For a session in the launch checkout, or with no `cwd`, the result is the same as before.
- Rollback: revert this PR.
- Out of scope, reported for follow-up:
  - `readConfiguredPathValue` throws when `.safeword/config.json` is the JSON literal `null`. This is pre-existing; Codex review `a4e654f7`.

**Thinking level stays per conversation**: Improves predictability of Claude Code sessions through keeping each conversation's effort setting separate. Before, changing the thinking level in one window changed it in your other windows too; now each conversation keeps its own. Fixes #1202.

## What
- Store Claude effort on the conversation and persist it through the existing reasoning-effort field, including session-index restoration. No persistence-schema migration.
- Use that conversation's value in runtime configuration, the conversation picker, and Settings controls. Shared preferences remain last-used defaults for new conversations, not overrides of existing conversations.
- Preserve explicit encoded-model selection and MCP effort pins.
- Defer legacy/default effort adoption until an existing conversation's authoritative payload has hydrated. Resolving cold Settings controls must not save a partial conversation.

## Why
- Separates conversation state from shared defaults so changing one window cannot change another conversation's thinking level.
- Ports fork #61's production fix and essential regressions with upstream `626d8cc6` merged forward, with one narrowly scoped hydration correction found during review. The original fork delta otherwise remains intact; this is not a byte-identical port.

## Tests
- Before the merge-forward, coordinated fake-only focused tests on `3d3a8a23d`: **20 passed, 0 failures** across `ClaudeNativeEffortResolutionTests` (12), `ClaudeNativeAutoFallbackTests` (6), and `AgentSessionLinkHandoffInheritanceTests` (2).
- The added cold-conversation regression fails on the uncorrected fork port: projecting controls saves an incomplete existing conversation. It passes after the hydration guard, and verifies the eventual adoption save preserves transcript and provider identity.
- SwiftFormat 0.61.1, SwiftLint strict, repository guardrails, and staged/outgoing gitleaks checks passed.
- Validation used the unchanged upstream dependency lockfile. No dependency updates are included.
- No live provider processes or app lifecycle actions were performed. Earlier live acceptance applies to fork #61, not this upstream build. Compatibility review passed on `3d3a8a23`; the feature delta remains unchanged. Hosted CI evidence and the final ratchet-only merge-forward are recorded below.

## Ratchet
- App Swift line delta: **+95** (+93 from fork #61, +2 for the hydration safeguard).
- Inherited stored App baseline: **650075 -> 650170**; upstream's existing 2000-line advisory headroom and policy are unchanged. Measured tree: **653212 -> 653307**.
- Test-import allowance stays **333**, with measured count **332** inherited from current main. Wrong-way-edge allowance stays **1079**, with measured count **1069** inherited from current main. The previous main had measured counts 333 and 1067 respectively; #1216 adds no change to either, and no allowance is increased.

## Merge-forward validation
- Exact-head [hosted CI](https://github.com/repoprompt/repoprompt-ce/actions/runs/37258460941) on `159b7b540a97f39ae5ab5e7c0e7a89a424b17098` passed **7/7**, including all four test shards and Style.

author: niiyeboah
body:
## Summary
- Validate `@prnt/dagr-explorer` in real browsers (M5.6f-2): a committed harness, `bench/browser/explorer-check.mjs`, drives the docs demos in Chromium and WebKit at 1440 and 390 wide. 48 checks pass on the final run. It found two bugs, fixed test first in `989234c`.
- State the measured SVG ceiling: smooth panning to about 4,000 nodes on an Apple M4.
- Add the explorer to the `@prnt/dagr` umbrella as `@prnt/dagr/explorer`, with `@prnt/dagr/render/core`, and mark `three` an optional peer of the umbrella. This is option A, approved by the maintainer on 2026-10-04. React 18 sites install `@prnt/dagr-explorer` directly, because the umbrella requires React 19.
- Remove `"private": true` from `@prnt/dagr-explorer`, as the spec's approval allows. **No version changes and nothing is published.**
- **Two things need the maintainer.** Spec amendment 17 records that the first `Escape` with the drawer open now keeps focus, which reverses part of amendment 15. And `three`: the explorer never loads it at runtime, but `@prnt/dagr-render` declares it as a required peer, so package managers still install it. The docs say so. Making it optional in `@prnt/dagr-render` is an open question to the maintainer.

## Verification
- Local gate at `5e202c8` on Node v25.6.1: `pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm lint && pnpm build && pnpm bench:ci`, all five pass, bench at a load of 3.3. At `4bf84a0`, before the documentation-only `5e202c8`, the same plus `verify:tools` passed: `publint` and `arethetypeswrong` on all seven tarballs, the scratch install, `tsc` and the runtime smoke.
- 437 explorer tests under React 19 and the same under React 18.

**Browser results** (Chromium 153, WebKit 26.6, Playwright 1.63; 48 results, 0 failed):

| Check | Cr 1440 | Cr 390 | WK 1440 | WK 390 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| mount, no overflow, no console errors | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| wheel and Ctrl wheel act only when focused | pass | pass | pass | n/a* |
| drag pans 1:1, no click | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| touch: first tap focuses, pinch zooms | n/a | pass | n/a | pass |
| keyboard: Tab, arrows, Enter, Space, Escape | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| search, more-matches line | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| mounted nodes within cap plus pins | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| reduced motion; resize keeps place; no `will-change` at rest | pass | pass | pass | pass |

\* Playwright has no wheel input in mobile WebKit.

**The two bugs the browsers found:**
- With the drawer open, `Escape` on a node closed the drawer and also released the graph, so keyboard focus fell to the page body. Now the first `Escape` closes the drawer and keeps focus on its opener; a second leaves the graph.
- In WebKit, an unfocused graph stopped the page from scrolling under the pointer, because WebKit will not scroll past any non-passive wheel listener when the page sets `overscroll-behavior: none`, as the docs site does. The camera now holds its wheel listener only while the graph has focus.

**Measured ceiling** (Apple M4, Chromium 153 headed on Metal, DPR 1, panned at 1.56 times the fit zoom; two runs agreed):

| Nodes | Median | 95th percentile | Dropped |
|---|---|---|---|
| empty control | 16.7 ms | 18.2 ms | 0% |
| 2,000 | 16.7 ms | 18.1 ms | 0% |
| 4,000 | 16.7 ms | 18.4 ms | 1% |
| 8,000 | 16.7 ms | 33.4 ms | 11% |

Headed, because headless Chromium on this machine paces frames at 67 to 100 ms even on an empty page. A size counts as smooth when its 95th percentile is within one display frame; the empty control sets that floor.

## Reviews
Per `AGENTS.md`. One implementer (Opus) from a design brief. One fresh reviewer read the diff and the merged tree, aimed at anything a consumer of the published packages would hit.

**Diff and tree review.** No Critical findings. It verified both browser-driven fixes: the root's capture-phase `Escape` acts only on the graph and leaves the search field's close-then-clear order and host controls alone; the wheel listener is added on focus-in, removed on every path, and a focused graph's wheel cannot scroll the page. It found the explorer's manifest ready for npm. Two Important findings:
- The docs said the explorer does not load three.js, true at runtime and misleading at install time, since `@prnt/dagr-render`'s required peer still installs it. Reworded in `5e202c8`; the manifest question is open to the maintainer.
- The explorer README said "not published yet", which would have appeared on its own npm page. Removed in `5e202c8`, with the matching notes in the docs page and the root README.

Minor, fixed in `5e202c8`: the docs intro's umbrella subpaths and install line, two spec sentences still describing the old `Escape` rule, two harness comments. Accepted: if a focused node's element is removed without a `focusout`, the wheel listener lingers until the next focus cycle; behavior stays correct because the handler checks focus.

All five of the implementer's unplanned choices were judged sound: following the brief's `Escape` check over amendment 15, the headed ceiling run, judging smoothness in frames, an overlay bound of cap plus four pins, and harness dependencies kept outside the workspace.

<sub>[Preview](https://allthings-web-pr-89-q3ng3b434yvpxzzv.allthings.workers.dev) · [Change Stack](https://app.coderabbit.ai/change-stack/allthingsweb-dev/allthingsweb/pull/89) · [Checks](https://github.com/allthingsweb-dev/allthingsweb/pull/89/checks) · [Files](https://github.com/allthingsweb-dev/allthingsweb/pull/89/files): +303 −32 in 13 files</sub>
<!-- allthings:pr-header:end -->

PR previews and staging now render real data. Every stage but `prod` gets its own Hyperdrive in front of production's Neon database, connecting as the read-only `reader` role, and the Web Worker reads through it.

## What changes
- **Infra** (`infra/src/web.ts`, `infra/src/reader.ts`):
  - each non-prod stage gets a `Database` Hyperdrive bound to the Web Worker as `HYPERDRIVE`. It is per stage, so a `pr-<n>` Hyperdrive is destroyed with its stage. A config shared by all stages would need its own stack and owner just to save a few configs;
  - the origin is `NEON_READER_URL`, passed as a `Config`. Alchemy resolves it only when it plans the Hyperdrive, so a deploy without it fails before it changes anything, and `alchemy destroy` doesn't need it. The stack refuses a connection string for any role other than `reader`, and its error messages never include the string. The password reaches the Hyperdrive only as a `Redacted` value: Alchemy's state store encrypts it, and it never appears in plan or deploy logs (checked by grepping the deploy logs);
  - caching is on: results are cached for 60 s and may be served up to 15 s stale while Hyperdrive refreshes them. Each stage holds about 5 origin connections, Hyperdrive's minimum.
- **Worker** (`web/src/database.ts`): reads the binding's connection string on every request and sets `ssl: false` explicitly. The Worker's connection goes to Hyperdrive inside Cloudflare, and a deployed binding's string says `sslmode=disable`. Alchemy's local runtime instead passes the origin through with the origin's own `sslmode` (`require` by default). That mode describes Hyperdrive's TLS connection to Neon, but `@effect/sql-pg` applies a URL's `sslmode` to its own socket. Setting `ssl` explicitly overrides the URL's value. Without a binding, the Worker still reads `DATABASE_URL`.
- **CI**: `deploy.yaml` passes `NEON_READER_URL` to the deploy step only. `infra/ci-token.json` adds **Hyperdrive Write**. Infra CI now runs the new `infra/tests`.
- **Tests**: the Worker parity suite (`web/tests/worker.test.ts`) now reads PGlite through a local Hyperdrive binding. Without the explicit `ssl: false`, 34 of its 61 tests fail.

## Verification
- I deployed `live_esthor` with the reader URL from `neonctl`. `/`, `/api/v1/events` (35 events), `/api/v1/speakers` and MCP `list_events` all returned production data. I then destroyed the stage without `NEON_READER_URL` set, which removed the Worker and its Hyperdrive.
- Timings measured inside the Worker (edge PHX), warm: Worker to Hyperdrive connect + auth + first query **3–7 ms**, cached query **1–3 ms**, uncached round trip to Neon **55–99 ms**. A new isolate's first connect took about 100 ms.
- From the client over a kept-alive connection, warm time to headers at p50: 123 ms for a route with no database query, `/api/v1/events` **166 ms**, `/` **207 ms**. The first request after a deploy took about 0.6 s TTFB including TLS setup, and about 1.5 s on a brand-new Hyperdrive.
- Repo-wide `bun run lint` passes. In `web`: check, typecheck, xss-scan and test pass (403 pass). In `infra`: check, typecheck and test pass.

* **New Features**
  * Preview and staging environments now access production data through dedicated read-only database connections. Production deployments remain maintainer-managed.
* **Documentation**
  * Updated deployment and local-stage guidance to cover database connections, setup requirements, and stage cleanup.
* **Chores**
  * Added automated infrastructure tests to the CI workflow.

The signed production audio test delivered text and voice successfully using Render, but its Node-compatible webhook environment dropped the native SELF binding and fell back after HTTP 404. Retain the normalized native binding in the Worker runtime and recover it when the voice router receives the Node environment. The primary path then uses authenticated SELF chunk orchestration for both the protected stress route and actual WhatsApp replies.

Add a regression test for loss of SELF across the bridge. Existing CPU termination recovery, three chunk attempts, bounded Render fallback, HMAC verification and Gemini rate-limit failover remain intact. Repeat the twenty-conversion stress and final signed owner delivery after all gates pass and central deployment succeeds.

author: lovelle-cardoso
body:
## Summary

A Luau declaration or reassignment whose `=` ends its line no longer reports its value as missing when the value lines end with commas (`read(1),` on the next line). The validator now uses the same statement-boundary rule as the type checker's reading, so the complete `native_integer_spills.luau` input agrees with the official parser and its known-disagreement row is gone. Performance cost not measured: the fix adds a walk over one construct node's children, only when the next line is an assignment's targets in Luau code; no benchmark was run.

Closes #1306

## Motivation

The ticket body is partly stale: on current main the four original examples already compile and run correctly. What remained was a false `Expected identifier when parsing expression, got 'read'` (or `'hash'` in the upstream fixture) on a line-ending `=` whose next line is a call or name followed by a comma. Values, call order and call counts were already right on both engines. Only the diagnostic was wrong.

The cause is at the validator/checker boundary, not in the grammar. The tree reads a comma-ended line like `read(1),` as the target list of a `LuauReassignment`. `checkerReadsOnTo` ([`LuauUnitNodes.ts:204-217`](https://github.com/ImpowerGames/impower/blob/4de40453b/packages/sparkdown/src/compiler/typecheck/LuauUnitNodes.ts#L204-L217)) counts every node in `STATEMENT_BREAKS`, reassignments included, as a statement the checker stops before. The checker's reading does not stop there: [`readLuauAst.ts:609-611`](https://github.com/ImpowerGames/impower/blob/4de40453b/packages/sparkdown/src/compiler/typecheck/readLuauAst.ts#L609-L611) inserts a break before a `LuauReassignment` only after an empty `then`/`else` arm. So `validateAssignmentValue` concluded that Sparkdown had to report the missing value, while the checker read the next line as the value. The same mismatch also doubled the error on `a =` followed by `b = 2`: Sparkdown reported `got 'b'` at the `=`, and the checker separately reported Luau's own `got '='`.

## Changes

- `packages/sparkdown/src/compiler/typecheck/LuauUnitNodes.ts`: `checkerReadsOnTo` treats a `LuauReassignment` (or its explicit twin) as read on, unless the construct ends with `then` or `else`, which is the rule `readLuauAst.ts` applies. Narrative `LuauSparkdownReassignment` lines and every other statement break keep their behavior.
- `packages/sparkdown/src/compiler/typecheck/readLuauAst.ts`: imports the shared `COMMENT` comment-node pattern from `LuauUnitNodes.ts` instead of defining it, so the checker's reading and the empty-arm check classify comments the same way. No behavior change in the reading.
- `packages/sparkdown/src/tests/compiler/luauFixtures.ts`: removes only the #1306 `conformance/native_integer_spills.luau` row. The #1304 and #1305 rows arrive removed through their own merged PRs; the two #1309 integer limitations are unchanged.
- `packages/sparkdown/src/tests/compiler/MultilineAssignment1306.test.ts`: reshaped from the inherited 31-case reproduction (see Notes).
- `repro/1306/` removed: it held handoff notes and an editor fixture that no committed test reads.

Rejected: restoring an assignment-operator rule in the grammar that spans the line break. The grammar is not what decides this diagnostic, and that rule would let `name =` take the next line's `end` as its value, which `reproEmptyRhs.test.ts` guards against. Also rejected: a special case inside `validateAssignmentValue` alone, because `checkerReadsOnTo` serves four other callers that should agree with the checker's reading too.

## Type of change

Type: bug fix

## Testing and verification

Regression test `packages/sparkdown/src/tests/compiler/MultilineAssignment1306.test.ts` (52 cases after the round 1 correction):

- Next-line values on both engines (`Story` and `ProgramStory`), LF and CRLF: the four ticket examples, names on comma-ended lines, a reassignment of comma-ended call lines, and the eight-call list (`Value 12345678:12345678:8.`, each call once and in order). Each asserts no errors, no runtime errors and the exact output.
- Luau errors after a line-ending operator, LF and CRLF, each compared with the pinned official parser's message, line and column: before `end`, `else` and `until`, after a comma-ended line before `end`, at a second operator on the next line, and after an empty `else` arm. Also the missing `else` of an empty `then` arm, and a message-only check at end of file. That case's position differs from Luau's for an unrelated reason: Sparkdown also reports the unclosed function.
- Story after an unfinished `& x =` or `& local x =`, top level and in a scene: prose, a value-looking line, comma-ended prose, and a following reassignment all stay story or their own statement. Each keeps exactly one missing-value error and its output. A complete marked assignment still runs.

Red/green through `driver.mjs redgreen --files packages/sparkdown/src/compiler/typecheck/LuauUnitNodes.ts`, running this file plus `luauSyntaxAgreement.test.ts`. Restore hash verified.

- Red on the base: `Tests  13 failed | 164 passed (177)`. Failures: the comma-ended next-line cases on both engines (`expected { errors: [ { …(3) } ], … } to deeply equal { errors: [], … }`, message `Expected identifier when parsing expression, got 'read'`), the two official-agreement cases (`expected [ { …(3) }, { …(3) } ] to deeply equal [ { …(3) } ]`), and `luauSyntaxAgreement > conformance/native_integer_spills.luau` (`Sparkdown and Luau's parser disagree on whether it has a syntax error`).
- Green on the fix: `Tests  177 passed (177)`.

Other named-file runs on the fix, all through `node scripts/test-suite.mjs run packages/sparkdown …`:

- `luauTreeAst.test.ts` 169 passed, `luauOfficialAst.test.ts` 169 passed (no "comparison SKIPPED" warning, so the pinned official parser loaded), `reproEmptyRhs.test.ts` 2 passed, `emptyAssignmentRhs.test.ts` 17 passed.
- Other `checkerReadsOnTo` callers and neighbors: `danglingMemberAccess`, `MalformedExpressionAtEveryPosition`, `TernaryExpression`, `invalidStatementInFunctionBody`, `BoundedDiagnostics931`, `luauBlockMissingEnd`, 1289 passed.
- `npm run typecheck -- --jobs 1 packages/sparkdown/tsconfig.json packages/sparkdown-language-server/tsconfig.json`: both clean.

After the round 1 correction and the merge of #1304 (head 06cf9d48b): `redgreen --base origin/main` over `LuauUnitNodes.ts` with this file and `luauSyntaxAgreement.test.ts` gave red `Tests 17 failed | 166 passed (183)` and green `Tests 183 passed (183)`. `luauTreeAst` 169, `luauOfficialAst` 169, `reproEmptyRhs` 2, `emptyAssignmentRhs` 17, `repeatUnitUntil1304` 14 and `invalidStatementInFunctionBody` 105 all passed, and the filtered typecheck was clean. The `local x, y = -- then` input was checked live: No Problems in VS Code, and in the web editor no error count with the preview printing `Values 12.`.

CI on the final head 12771aa17: every run check passed, including the Test Suite package jobs (`packages/sparkdown`, `packages/spark-engine`, `packages/sparkdown-language-server` and the rest, which ran because the change touches `packages/`), the `test-suite` gate, `tsc`, `typecheck`, `build`, `linked-issue`, `hook-tests` and `notifier-tests`. `driver-checks`, `skills-checks` and `notifier` were skipped as outside this change's paths.

Review: round 1 (gpt-6.1-sol at high, two reviewers) found one blocking defect and one quality finding, both fixed; round 2 (gpt-6.1-sol at high, one undirected reviewer) reviewed 12771aa17 with no findings.

Web editor (driver `verify`/`ui`, same worktree; before evidence taken with the base `LuauUnitNodes.ts` swapped in and the servers rebuilt):

![Web editor before: squiggle under the line-12 equals sign, 1 Error, preview prints the correct call values](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4a447a4c-62c6-4e01-bd36-ed9a45130f40)

![Before: the rendered diagnostic tooltip on the equals sign](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3a4d0ffa-4ac4-4103-8548-e

## B10 — register the Kernel v1.0 freeze-remediation status; fix the known-failure-list header

**Documentation only. No code, test, workflow or contract change.** 2 files: `KNOWN_ISSUES.md` (+45/−1 pure insertions), `docs/architecture/D10_KNOWN_ENVIRONMENTAL_FAILURES.txt` (header comment only).

### What changes
1. **`KNOWN_ISSUES.md` — new section "Kernel v1.0 Freeze Remediation (Oct 2026)"** with a status table for FZ-01..FZ-07:
   - **FZ-04 (B1, PR #51 → `1a09941`), FZ-03 (B8, PR #53 → `80a1bb8`), FZ-07 (B9, PR #55 → `e438387`): FIXED + VERIFIED**, each with its evidence and its explicit residuals (B8: `cleaner.run_all` still blocks the loop, `print()` handlers unchanged, 60 s floor is a behaviour change, test-suite file mutation; the Graphify result recorded as an *accepted evidence exception*, never "green on `0ff0937`").
   - **FZ-01, FZ-02, FZ-05, FZ-06: OPEN and NOT STARTED**, blocked on D1–D3 as before. They are described as measured, re-confirmed **by code inspection on `e438387`** (still valid on `7464a84`: no cited file changed since) (not by re-running repros), and no outcome is assumed. The D1–D3 options are listed neutrally; none is chosen.
   - **FZ-07 residual R-1** recorded as an open follow-up (the `FAILED` node-ID ` - ` truncation), plus the two observations (list root-cause label still unverified; the runner's 2 warnings not traced).
   - The section states in its first paragraph that it is **a status register, not a freeze verdict; no FREEZE READY claim is made or implied.**
2. **`DEBT-031` addendum** — pure insertion (786 chars). The row called the CI gate "genuinely, correctly enforced" while it gated on the allowlist alone; FZ-07 showed otherwise and B9 replaced it. The allowlist root-cause mislabel in that row is untouched and still open.
3. **`D10_KNOWN_ENVIRONMENTAL_FAILURES.txt` header wording** — now describes the gate as it behaves (exit 0/1 only, errors/INTERNALERROR/empty runs/other exit codes cannot be listed, exact-ID matching, and "do not add an entry containing ` - `"). **The 34 entries are not touched.**
4. A "Last synchronized" line.

### Non-goals / explicitly not done
- **Known-failure list not modified or widened, not pruned.** Proven below.
- **`CURRENT_STATE.md` untouched.** Its Sept 23 freeze-verdict wording ("down to REM-004 and CTX-EXPORT-001") predates the Oct 1 audit and is **not reconciled**; the new section says so in plain words instead of papering over it.
- **`DEBT-033` text untouched** (it says `main` has no branch protection). Live API on Oct 5 shows required checks `tests` + `drift-and-ownership`, strict, enforce-admins, no required reviews, no force-push/deletion. That is recorded as an observation under FZ-07, but the row's disposition is the maintainer's to change.
- No invented conclusions for B2–B7; no decision D1–D3 pre-empted; ADR-KERNEL-07 D-4 strict xfail untouched.
- Credential hygiene is deliberately **not** mentioned in this public repo's docs.

### Evidence
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| allowlist entries before vs after | **34 / 34, identical sequence and bytes**; `parse_allowlist` sets equal; file CR-free and ASCII |
| `KNOWN_ISSUES.md` diff shape | 3 hunks, **0 deletions**: sync line inserted, DEBT-031 one pure insertion, 27-line section inserted |
| every SHA cited in the new text | resolves to a commit in `main`'s history (`ecddbff`, `9b172d0`, `e1293f4`, `0ff0937`, `80a1bb8`, `1a09941`, `c4d62b3`, `e438387`, `7cefd6d`) |
| test counts cited (21 / 35 / 67) | match `--collect-only` on the merged tree; B1 test list and B8 events/defaults checked against the code |
| new table | 9 rows, 5 cells each (no stray `|`) |
| claims about open items | FZ-01/02/05/06 re-checked on `e438387` by inspection (K4.2 `wf_result.output or ""`; `except Exception` in-band error token; `ModelRouterAdapter` `success=True` with no read of `execution_detail`; `ExecutionRegistry` has only `create/get/ids`; 16 `_emit_event` sites, 1 mentions `execution_id`) |
| `scripts/check_drift.py` | 15/15 PASS (DRIFT-13 reads `KNOWN_ISSUES.md`) |
| full suite, local | on the merged tree `5e173d4`, system Python 3.12: **1967 passed, 1 xfailed**, 0 failed (this PR adds no tests: its diff is two documentation files). The count is higher than the 1904 I measured before the merge because `main` gained tests via #56 in between. With a venv interpreter 8 `tests/core/sandbox/test_namespace_backend.py` tests fail (`execvp` ENOENT inside the sandbox chroot); the same 14 tests pass with the system interpreter — environmental (known tooling trap), not a product failure |
| new gate on this run's real pytest output | passes |

### Review notes — a correction I owe you
While proofreading the R-1 text I found that my PR #55 wording overstated the protection: "the new gate closes the old masking path". Probed with real pytest: it **does** go red when ≥2 failing ids collapse to one truncated prefix, and when the real id is listed — but a **hand-truncated** entry (`tests/x.py::test_p[a`) **can still tolerate a single failing ` - ` id** (1 failed, entry listed → gate passes). R-1 in the register states exactly that, and the list header says not to write such an entry. No current entry is affected (0 of 34 contain ` - `). The fix (bracket-aware split) remains a separate, reviewed follow-up.

### Update after opening: `main` moved, conflict resolved by a merge commit
While this PR waited, `main` advanced from `e438387` to `7464a84` (PR #56, the `/import` boundary fix, and the documentation PRs #58, #48 and #49; none touches a file or symbol cited here: orchestrator, model_router, registry, resilience, scheduler, event_stream, ci_test_gate, ci.yml). The PR became `dirty` with **one** conflict: the top-of-file `Last synchronized` chain in `KNOWN_ISSUES.md` (main added its own Oct 5 line above the same Sept 16 entry). I merged `main` into this branch (merge commit `5e173d4`, parents `bdbe51a` + `7464a84`; no rebase, no force-push) and kept all three lines byte-identical to their sources, newest first: this PR's line, main's Oct 5 CodeQL line, main's already-prefixed Sept 16 line. Re-verified on the merged tree: diff vs `main` is still exactly the two files (+45/−5); the 34 allowlist entries are identical to `main`'s; `check_drift.py` 15/15 PASS.

### CI result (real GitHub runners)
| head | tests | drift-and-ownership | CodeQL | Analyze (python / actions) | Graphify |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `5e173d4` (current head) | success | success | success | success / success | no new run (Graphify reviews a PR once, on its first head) |
| `bdbe51a` (superseded by the merge) | success | success | success | success / success | neutral ("No PR-changed functions were verified"; no findings, no review comments) |

**Runner pytest summary — still awaiting the maintainer's log confirmation (I cannot read runner logs).** Because `main` gained tests, the number is no longer `1890`. My *derived, unverified* expectation: local 1967 − the 14 tests the runner skips (the same offset as before: local 1904 vs runner 1890 + 14 skipped) = **`1953 passed, 14 skipped, 1 xfailed`**, which should equal the number in `main`'s own post-merge run for `7464a84`. Gate step: `pytest exit code: 0` / `Test gate passed`.

### Merge gate
`tests` and `drift-and-ownership` green on the head; runner summary equal to `main`'s at `7464a84` (expected `1953 passed, 14 skipped, 1 xfailed`, derived — to be confirmed by the maintainer from the log) and gate line `pytest exit code: 0` / `Test gate passed`; allowlist entry diff empty (re-checkable; prints nothing when only comment lines changed: `git diff origin/main -- docs/architecture/D10_KNOWN_ENVIRONMENTAL_FAILURES.txt | grep -E '^[+-]' | grep -vE '^(\+\+\+|---)' | grep -vE '^[+-]#'`; a negative control with an appended entry prints that entry); branch contains `main` (`7464a84`); no force-push. **Not merged without the maintainer's go-ahead.**

Content commit: `bdbe51a`; head: `5e173d4` (merge of `main` `7464a84`). Rollback: reve

## Problem and motivation

Rail tooltips had grown explanation clauses ("Hide from the rail (History keeps it)", "Add project: open a folder that already has agents"). Rule from the flow: a tooltip names the action in one to three words; the aria-label may add the object's name.

Kept unchanged on purpose:

- `BrandHeader.tsx` aria-label `Collapse workspace panel` (only its tooltip changed). The button only collapses; the expand control is in `SessionBar.tsx`, outside the rail and this PR.
- aria-labels that name the object: `New chat in <project>`, `Remove <project> from the rail`, `Hide <session> from the rail`, `End <session>`, `Open Agent Map for <project>`.
- Session mark aria-labels keep their meaning (`Live: the agent is working`, etc.): the mark is a `role="img"` dot, so the aria-label is the only thing a screen reader gets. Only its tooltip shortens. This splits the old `MARK_TITLE` into `MARK_TOOLTIP` and `MARK_LABEL`.

**Owns / Off limits as built.** Diff: `WorkflowsRail.tsx`, `RailProjectRows.tsx`, `BrandHeader.tsx` (the collapse tooltip only; widened by the planner), `e2e/rail-grammar.spec.ts` (new guard), `e2e/smoke.spec.ts` (Search aria assertion), `e2e/rail-live-indicator.spec.ts` (Idle tooltip). **Not counted as an action tooltip:**

- `WorkflowsRail.tsx:971` the "N checkouts not searched" note's `title` ("Open one as its own project to see its agents:" + the paths). It is a content tooltip listing paths, not an action tooltip, and is not in the flow's table.

Counted: every `data-tooltip`, `title` and stashed title in the rail, brand header included. Row `title`s that show a path or cwd are content and not counted.

## What changed

One test in `tests/test_budget.py`, nothing else. `docs/runbooks.md` and the `Budget.alert_if_crossed` docstring now promise that the `budget.alerted` AuditEvent is written when an execution ends because the Run paused on an Approval (or was escalated), but the budget tests only drove completed Runs. This pins that path (issue #232, found in review of #230). No production code changed — the Runner already called `alert_if_crossed` outside the status branch (`src/cograil/runner.py:202`); the test only asserts the documented promise, and it holds.

The test:

- seeds the month with $0.40 of a $1.00 cap (`alert_at` 0.5), then drives a Run through `Runner.run` whose single Step plans `@hris.submit_leave` (a write Tool with `confirm_before_write`), so the Run **pauses** on its Approval with the month at $0.60;
- asserts exactly one `budget.alerted` AuditEvent on that Run, its `principal_id` (`alice@example.com`, the Run's principal) and its `detail["contact"]` (the Colleague's `escalation_contact`), plus `month` and `spend_usd`;
- runs the month's second execution — `Runner.resume` deciding the Approval, which completes the Run at $0.70, still over the threshold — and asserts no second event is written.

## Why

Test only; the behaviour was already correct but undocumented-by-test, so a future refactor could drop the call outside the completed branch without failing anything.

## How it was tested

`scripts/check.sh quick` (format, lint, types, tests for the changed file) — **PASS**, including the new test. Run three times while iterating: the first caught a >100-column line in the new `Tool(...)` constant, fixed; the second and third passed. Working tree clean at `04736f7`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The test drives a paused Run through the Runner and asserts the event, its contact and its principal. — `tests/test_budget.py`, `test_one_alert_is_sent_when_the_run_pauses_on_a_gate_over_alert_at`: `Runner.run` leaves the Run `awaiting_approval`, and the test asserts the one `budget.alerted` event's `principal_id`, `detail["contact"]`, `detail["month"]` and `detail["spend_usd"]`.

## Follow-ups

None needed; the test confirmed the behaviour rather than contradicting it.

- Full local acceptance also covered Python, architecture, source types, localization completeness/review fingerprints, generated consistency, multilingual search, Support, player import/history, and 84 Indonesian surface/engine/width states. The [dated local acceptance record](https://github.com/arussin/maimai-chart-browser/blob/28ec5cb0f6df25fb976d2b224ab2fb76bb715512/docs/localization-review/CODEX-VALIDATION-INDONESIAN-20261004.md) preserves exact commands and the earlier readiness-failure history.

Translation review is contextual AI self-review; native-speaker certification is not claimed.

author: mikelane
body:
## Summary

A per-mutant timeout shorter than the tests' own runtime made every gremlin time out. TIMEOUT counted as a kill, so a suite that asserts nothing could score **100%**, in all three execution modes. After this PR, a TIMEOUT counts as a kill only when a confirmation shows the mutant caused it. The design follows the maintainer decisions on #565: A+C first, then an amendment after adversarial QA.

- **Solo re-run (parallel and batch only).** A gremlin that timed out in the pool is re-run alone with the same selection and limit. If it finishes, the timeout came from contention, and the solo result is scored normally: a failure is a kill, a pass is a survivor.
- **Unmutated confirmation with headroom (all modes).** The selection is run without the mutant. The timeout stays a kill only if that run finishes within **half** of `mutant_timeout` (`TIMEOUT_CONFIRMATION_HEADROOM`). Otherwise the result becomes **ERROR**, which stays in the denominator, so a bad timeout can only lower the score. The message gives the measured time and the limit, and explains how to raise the limit.
- **A confirmation that can't be launched** becomes ERROR with its own message. It is never a kill.
- **Warning.** When any timeouts were downgraded, the terminal summary prints one line and the JSON report carries a `timeout_warning` object.
- **Cache.** Downgraded and launch-failure results are not cached. `RUNNER_FIDELITY_VERSION` is bumped to `rf6`, so unconfirmed TIMEOUTs cached by v1.10.1 are retired and are not replayed.
- **Memoization.** Each distinct selection is confirmed once, however many gremlins share it.

| Repro: a test asserting nothing that sleeps 2s, `--gremlin-mutant-timeout 1` | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| sequential / `--gremlin-parallel` / `--gremlin-batch` | 100% | 0% plus the warning |
| 4 workers contending on a 5s lock, 15s limit (parallel / batch) | 42.9% (fake TIMEOUT kills) | 0 timeouts, 7 survived |

## Also in this PR

- **isort fix for #568's test file** (3423039). `tests/plugin/test_gremlins_option_stripping.py` failed the pre-push isort hook, while CI's ruff-only check passed it, so every branch rebased onto main failed pre-push. This applies isort's own output.
- **CI cost.** One end-to-end fake-score regression (sequential) runs in the PR gate. The parallel and batch matrices and the contention tests are marked `large`. The gate-tier time for the timeout tests is roughly back to main's level.
- **Docs.** Configuration, troubleshooting, reports, reporting API and parallelization pages describe the confirmation. The troubleshooting page no longer says the timeout is fixed at 30s.

This PR takes `RUNNER_FIDELITY_VERSION = 'rf6'`. If it merges first, #554 needs `rf7` (and its test pin moves accordingly).

author: orbit-agent-01
body:
## Task ORB-14057 — [code-review] `orbit web connect` concludes nothing is running remotely while ssh is still authenticating, so attach fails for passphrase/password/2FA logins slower than 5s ### Description Found by the full code review (surfaces and composition) at pinned commit `72f19081288d44b7093121255ed8918cf04c3b8f`; all `file:line` references are at that SHA. ## Defect `establish` (`crates/orbit-web/src/ssh_tunnel.rs:86-130`) first starts a bare `-N` probe forward and polls `/healthz` through it for `ATTACH_PROBE_TIMEOUT = 5s` (`crates/orbit-web/src/connect.rs:52`). `poll_until_ready` (`ssh_tunnel.rs:237-256`) only distinguishes "ssh exited" from "`/healthz` answered". OpenSSH binds the local `-L` listener only after authentication, so while the user is still typing a key passphrase/password or answering 2FA every probe sees connection-refused, indistinguishable from "forward up, nothing listening". ## Failure scenario User needs >5s to authenticate. The probe ssh is shut down mid-prompt (`ssh_tunnel.rs:99`), a second ssh prompts again and runs `orbit web serve --port

` remotely. If a dashboard was already running there, the new remote serve fails to bind: either connect reports "remote `orbit web serve` exited with status 1 before it became ready", or a `/healthz` probe reaches the existing server first, connect prints "Dashboard tunnel ready", opens the browser and then tears the tunnel down when the failed ssh exits. The attach feature (ORB-10708) fails, and every slow login is prompted twice. ### Acceptance Criteria - The attach window does not depend on authentication time: e.g. the 5s attach window starts only once a TCP connect to the local forwarded port succeeds (ssh has authenticated and bound the forward). - A test with a stub `ssh` that delays binding the forward past the attach timeout, with a healthy server behind it, returns `Attached` and spawns ssh only once. ## Execution Summary

Click to expand Outcome: success Changes: - `ssh_tunnel::establish` waits until a TCP connect to the local `-L` port succeeds, or the probe ssh exits, before starting `attach_timeout`. OpenSSH binds that listener only after authentication, so a passphrase, password, or 2FA prompt no longer consumes the 5s attach budget or kills the probe. An ssh exit before the listener is up is a connection failure and does not spawn a remote serve. - The post-bind `/healthz` budget stays 5s. If nothing answers, the probe is shut down and one command-forward ssh is started, as before. - `TunnelSpec.ssh_program` names the tunnel executable (`ssh` for `orbit web connect`) so the regression test can pass a stub without changing process PATH. - Added `delayed_forward_bind_attaches_without_a_second_ssh`: a stub ssh sleeps 2s, past a 500ms attach budget, before binding; a healthy `/healthz` server sits behind the forward; `establish` returns `Attached` with exactly one spawn, the bare `-N` probe. - Updated the remote-access design note and SSH tunnel spec so the five-second poll is measured from the listener accept. Assessment: The attach decision now uses the listener accept, which is the signal that authentication finished. The 30s spawn budget still includes the second ssh session's own connect time, and that session runs only after the post-bind probe finds nothing listening. Criteria: - Attach window does not depend on authentication time: met. `wait_until_forward_bound` has no deadline; `poll_until_ready` with `attach_timeout` runs only after `forward_listener_up`. - Stub ssh that delays the bind past the attach timeout, with a healthy server behind it, returns `Attached` and spawns ssh once: met by `tests::ssh_tunnel::delayed_forward_bind_attaches_without_a_second_ssh`. Validation: - `cargo test -p orbit-web --lib -- --test-threads=8` — passed (25 tests, including the new one). - `cargo clippy -p orbit-web --lib -- -D warnings -D clippy::disallowed_methods` — passed. - `cargo clippy -p orbit-web --all-targets -- -D warnings -A clippy::disallowed_methods` — passed. - `./scripts/generate-doc-indexes.sh --check` — passed. - `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on the edited Rust files — passed. - `git diff --check` — passed. - `make ci-fast`, `make ci-lint`, `make goldens` — not run. The edit is orbit-web's tunnel plus two design docs; full workspace gates stay on the PR. The doc-index check, which is the ci-fast step this edit could affect, passed. Reconciliation: - Baseline HEAD `1e63ddda22000ba36927e51911a0df4dccf3ea87`, clean `git status --short`. - Delivery paths: `crates/orbit-web/src/connect.rs`, `crates/orbit-web/src/ssh_tunnel.rs`, `crates/orbit-web/src/tests/mod.rs`, `crates/orbit-web/src/tests/ssh_tunnel.rs` (new), `docs/design/remote-access/2_design.md`, `docs/design/remote-access/specs/ssh-tunnel.md`. - Every delivery path is already in `context_files`. No paths outside those selectors. - Cleanup: no run-owned output outside the deliverable. `.orbit/tmp/` scratch is gitignored. - Leftovers: none. Changes left uncommitted for the pipeline. Risks: - Authentication has no separate deadline. A probe that never binds and never exits waits until Ctrl-C. That replaces the old 5s cutoff, which was killing the prompt. - When nothing is listening, the second ssh still counts its own authentication against the 30s ready budget. The reported failure is the attach path, where a server is already up. - The regression test needs `python3` on PATH (the Makefile already uses it) and is compiled only on unix.
## Validation - Not reported ## Branch Freshness - Base ref: `origin/agent-main` - Head ref: `orbit/ORB-14057-4fbe67b9` - Behind base: 0 - Ahead of base: 1
