author: wyuc
body:
## Summary

The push CI run of the 1.2.0-rc.1 release commit failed in Unit Tests although every test passed. A log line landed after the access-code startup test file had finished: `EnvironmentTeardownError: [vitest-worker]: Closing rpc while "onUserConsoleLog" was pending`. Because the publish workflow requires a green CI run on the release commit, it refused to publish `@openmaic/storage@0.37.1` until both runs were re-run.

Cause: five boot test files call `register()` from `instrumentation.ts`. That starts the generation runner, the owner material extractor, the legacy classroom import and the instance secret check against a database the tests never provide, and they keep polling and logging after the tests end. With `resolveAssetPendingTtlMs` mocked to `undefined`, the runner's asset keep-alive interval is `NaN`, so it fires every millisecond (tens of thousands of warnings per file in a few seconds).

## Change

Mock the four background starters in the five boot test files: `access-code-startup`, `database-requirement`, `identity/boot`, `model-config/boot` and `persistence/asset-collector-schedule`. `access-code-startup` already did this for the instance secret check. Tests only, no product code changes.

## Verification

- Appended an `afterAll` that records console calls for 4 s after each file's tests. Before the change, five files logged late (`[GenerationRunner] claim scan failed` / `keeping run assets alive failed`, `[SecretBox] ...`). After the change, none do.
- `vitest run`: 887 files / 10128 tests pass. `prettier --check`, `eslint`, `tsc --noEmit` clean.

This PR builds on #456, which adds the "Model predictions" permission, so its base branch is that PR's branch. Merge #456 first; GitHub then moves this PR onto `main`.

## What changes
**Data Management** gets an **Upload Model Predictions** button next to Update Metadata. It shows for superusers and anyone granted "Model predictions".

The dialog looks like the Update Metadata one:
- icon, short explanation and size limit;
- **Download CSV Template** (new `predictions_upload_template.csv`) and **Field Definitions**;
- file, model name and version, and "Check only, don't save";
- a **progress bar**: the upload takes the first 30%, then checking and saving fill the rest.

When the job finishes, the result shows in the dialog: counts, or every problem with its row number. The separate Model Predictions section is removed.

**Background job:**

body:
<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"fernandolisboa"} -->
_Requested by **Fernando** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01DYnXVAhcvgPbH7BwLt4Poa?thread=cmsg_01DYnXVAhcvgPbH7BwLt4Poa2JvUuQ4TPKSemJQyjG1K8o)_

Before: the Listing draft's title and description were written by hand. The title came from the Product name and the description field started empty.

After: the draft has a "Gerar título e descrição com IA" button. It writes both fields with the Claude API, using the Product name, the Supplier Offer titles, the category, the condition and the technical sheet typed in the draft. The title stays within the category's limit and favors the category's trending terms. The text only fills the fields; nothing is saved or published without the owner's click. Without an Anthropic key, without a Mercado Livre connection or without a category, the button is disabled and a line says why. The model is set in Configurações › Títulos e descrições com IA, defaulting to `claude-sonnet-5-5`.

Closes #17

## How

- **Marketing** owns Listing Copy (ADR 0028), fed by its caller like Quality and Questions. It has two ports:
  - `CopyChannel` gives the category's limits and trending terms.
  - `CopyWriter` turns a `CopyRequest` into text.
- `ListingCopy::write` builds the prompt, writes, tidies, and checks with `check_copy`. The check catches an empty field, an overlong title or description, and contact data (phone, e-mail, external link, social network), using the same `contact_in` rule as answers to questions.
  - A rejected text is written once more, with the reason.
  - A title that is still too long is cut at a word and flagged.
  - Anything else that still breaks a rule is `Rejected` and never reaches the draft.
- The model setting lives in `marketing_copy_settings` (Marketing migration v5).
- **Integrations**:
  - `Anthropic` sends `POST /v1/messages` over ureq. The JSON schema in `output_config.format` shapes the answer. It retries 429, 529 and other 5xx after 2, 4 and 8 s. A 401 maps to `Expired`, other 4xx to `Refused` with the API's message, and the `refusal` and `max_tokens` stop reasons are handled.
  - `MercadoLivre` implements `CopyChannel`. Limits come from `/categories/{id}` `settings` (default 60/50000), and trends come from `/trends/MLB/{id}` (a 404 means none).
- **Platform**: `slow_http_agent` adds a longer answer timeout (5 min) for the writer.
- **App**:
  - The button sits in the draft editor, with its outcome right below it.
  - The model field is in Configurações.
  - The dev-only `MASCATE_ANTHROPIC_API_URL` variable is documented in `docs/credentials.html`.

## Tests

- `crates/marketing/tests/copy.rs` (15) runs on a real temp DB with fake channel and writer. It covers:
  - the exact prompt and the instruction rules;
  - tidy and trends in the title;
  - retry with the reason, cut at a word, contact retry, and rejected twice;
  - Mercado Livre links being allowed;
  - empty and overlong texts;
  - trends 404, channel and writer errors;
  - model default, save and invalid names;
  - a property test that a returned title never exceeds the limit.
- `crates/integrations/tests/listing_copy.rs` (10) runs against `FakeHttpServer` with fixtures from the documentation (README says so). It covers:
  - request shape and headers, and no key leading to `NotConnected`;
  - 429→529→200 retries and repeated 529;
  - 401, 404 and 400, refusal and max_tokens;
  - category rules, and trends with the token;
  - end to end with both adapters.
- The migration sample test checks the new default and saves a custom model.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` are green locally.

## Self-review (five lenses)

1. **Correctness**:
   - Title length is counted in chars, not bytes.
   - The cut drops trailing punctuation and dashes.
   - The writer is never called when the channel fails.
   - Found and fixed: a writing failure showed at the bottom of the editor, far from the button. It now shows under the button.
2. **Security**:
   - The key is read from the OS store per request and only sent in `x-api-key`. It is never logged or put in errors.
   - Platform data goes inside `<dados>` with `<`/`>` stripped, and the instructions tell the model that this data is information, not orders.
   - Contact data is checked after writing, whatever the model says.
3. **Architecture**:
   - Marketing does not read Catalog or Commerce; the app passes the brief.
   - `integrations → marketing` was already allowed, so no new dependency or crate edge was added.
   - ADR 0028 records the decision.
4. **Style**: clippy-clean; comments only on non-obvious whys (timeouts, retries).
5. **Context**:
   - Uses "Listing Copy" from CONTEXT.md.
   - Covers each acceptance criterion of #17.
   - Things that need a real key or account are listed for #37: a real generation, `/trends` auth, and real MLB title limits.

Screenshots (cloud, fake APIs): in the project's `screenshots/issue-17/` folder.

author: jacoby149
body:
## What

A user uploads a group cover photo; the avatar (pfp) renders but the cover stays on the default purple gradient.

## Root cause

The group face is a **replace-on-write doc stream** — every `writeGroupIdentity` is a `w.create` (a NEW doc, never an update), and the reader's contract is "the latest doc wins" (KB `groups/identity.md`). But `readGroupIdentity` took `docs[docs.length - 1]` — the **oldest** doc — while the node orders `created_at DESC` (newest first, `clickhouse.py:2425`), so `docs[0]` is the newest.

The avatar was written in an *earlier* save than the cover, so the reader returned that first doc (which carries `avatar_ref` but not the later `banner_ref`) → the pfp rendered, the cover fell back to the gradient.

## The fix

`readGroupIdentity` takes `docs[0]` (the newest), matching the server's `created_at DESC` order + the "latest doc wins" intent. One line, D60-clean (zero node surface).

The **same latent bug** is fixed in lockstep in `marketing-ui` (`GroupDetail.tsx`, `GroupDirectory.tsx`, `ProfilesBrowser.tsx`) — the identical `docs[docs.length - 1]` "latest doc wins" read on the same DESC-ordered `/v3/read` stream. It's masked there because marketing-ui faces are written once (so `docs[0] === docs[len-1]`), but it would surface the moment a face is edited twice.

## Tests

- `data/groupsDraft.test.ts` +2 — the reader returns the NEWEST doc (banner+avatar over avatar-only; **fails pre-fix**) + the empty-doc case.
- 1308 web10-social + 284 marketing-ui green, `tsc` clean.

## Acceptance bar

A group whose cover was added in a *later* save than its avatar shows the cover (not the gradient); the avatar + cover both come from the newest face doc; the marketing-ui group face reads return the newest doc.

author: mgwedd
body:
Introduces fine-tuned model support via LoRA adapters, with strict compatibility validation to prevent silent failures when an adapter is applied to the wrong base model.

## Summary
Adds a complete LoRA adapter system that reuses the existing model-download seam (`ModelAsset`) while enforcing that adapters can only be applied to their trained-for base model. Compatibility is validated at `ModelLoadPlan` construction time, ensuring mismatches fail closed with clear error messages before any weights load.

## Key changes
- **`LoRAAdapter` struct**: Represents a downloadable adapter with metadata (id, display name, file name, remote URL, SHA-256, size, and the base model ID it targets). Maps directly to `ModelAsset` for download reuse.
- **`LoRACompatibilityError`**: Localized error type that surfaces base mismatches to users with both the expected and actual model names, so the pairing can be corrected.
- **`ModelLoadPlan`**: New value type that encapsulates what the engine should load—a base model with an optional adapter. The throwing initializer validates adapter compatibility against the base before construction, making it impossible to create an unsound plan.
- **`LlamaRuntime` extensions**: Added `modelsDirectory` property and `adapterURL(for:)` method to resolve adapter file paths in an `Adapters/` subfolder, keeping adapters separate from base weights.
- **`LocalLLMEngineFactory.make(plan:sampling:)`**: New factory method that accepts a `ModelLoadPlan` instead of a raw model URL, routing both base and adapter to the runtime without requiring call-site changes.
- **Comprehensive test suite**: `FineTunedModelTests` validates the adapter-to-asset mapping, base model resolution, compatibility checks (both positive and negative cases with clear error messages), `ModelLoadPlan` construction and URL resolution, storage layout, and engine factory integration.

## Implementation details
- Adapters are small (~tens of MB) compared to base models (multi-GB), making them practical to download and swap.
- The `baseModelID` field is a raw string to allow graceful degradation: an adapter naming an unknown base resolves to `nil` rather than crashing, but compatibility validation still fails it closed.
- Storage layout isolates adapters in `Models/Adapters/` to avoid file-name collisions with base weights.
- The engine factory currently returns `UnavailableLocalLLMEngine` with a TODO comment pending runtime integration; the plan routing is in place and fully testable without the runtime.

body:
The corrections after the supervised play of 2026-10-05. In that play the bot sent 811 lines to the owner's chat in under two hours, dumped code, was kicked 3 times, and was killed once by its own loop guard. `!stop` through `run` never ran, and the supervisor saw ore through the rock. Details and decisions: `docs/releases/0.1.4.13/DECISIONS.md`, section "Fix 1".

## What changes

- **Quiet supervisor.** The commands of the watch server's `run` and `say` run quiet (`src/agent/chat_gate.js`, AsyncLocalStorage). Their echo, their results and the texts of their skills go to the supervisor's answer and to the bot's log as `[quiet] ...`. They never reach the game chat, the page or the voice. The watch still records the lines, so the digest has them. The bot's answers to the owner, its reflexes and the commands the owner types are said as before.
- **No code in the chat.** `chatText` leaves every code block out of the lines the bot says; the model's history keeps the code.
- **No kick from generated code.** `bot.chat` and `bot.whisper` inside generated code go to the code's output. A server command (`/...`) still goes to the server.
- **`!stop` through `run`.** As the first command of a run, it stops the running command at once instead of waiting behind it.
- **The loop guard.** Quiet commands no longer count. A run is bounded to 10 commands, each sent after the previous one's result.
- **No x-ray.** `look` and the digest's lava hazard list only blocks with an open side (`isExposed`), as a player sees them.
- **Death drops.** The step away from a death drop at the bot's feet goes away from all of that death's drops (`awayPoint`). Before, a step away from the boots once walked over the ingots, and the server gave them to the bot.
- **`/supervise` skill.**
  - It speaks in the chat only for danger, when the goal is done or stuck, and to answer the owner; at most one line per 5 minutes.
  - Underground only `!mineOre`, never `!collectBlocks` or code actions to fetch ore.
  - It keeps the bot out of caves.
  - "Check" never moves the owner's things.
  - It claims nothing before a tool showed it.
- **`start-gpt.ps1`** no longer loads the watch token, like `start-claude.ps1` after b6639e8. That commit had broken `rtd_launch` on `main`.
- **Docs.** CHANGELOG (in the 0.1.4.13 entry), PLAYTEST section 5b, ROADMAP (the play's other findings, planned for 0.1.4.14), SUPERVISOR.md.

No new setting: these are corrections.

## Tests

- **New:**
  - unit tests `xw_chat_gate` (14), `xw_drop_step` (4), plus tests in `xt_look` and `xs_digest`;
  - world scenario W119 `quiet_supervisor`: 8 quick failures, code that calls `bot.chat` three times, a long skill and then `!stop`. The player hears nothing of them and is still answered;

  - W113 then passed 3 of 3.

author: zupengwang
body:
## Overview

Fix benchmark sweep cleanup when a server exits before its workers: terminate the surviving process group and reap the directly owned server process.

## Claims

- `ServerProcess.stop()` terminates workers that remain in the original process group after its leader has exited and been reaped.
- Cleanup reaps the direct child and remains safe to call again after successful cleanup.

## Validation

Base: `0c16eee3f1ff777298cc894c3eeb85f3880c6d6a`. The identical regression uses real subprocesses, a forked worker, and a socket handshake; it mocks no production logic.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| macOS ARM64, Python 3.12.14, unmodified production code + regression | 2 failed: surviving worker socket; unreaped direct child |
| Same environment, patched production code + regression | 2 passed using the standard pytest entry point |
| Existing and new sweep tests with `--noconftest` | 28 passed |
| Standard collection | 28 tests collected |
| Applicable pre-commit hooks and manual mypy 3.12 | Passed |

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/sweep/test_server_process.py -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest tests/benchmarks/sweep -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --collect-only tests/benchmarks/sweep -q
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/benchmarks/sweep/server.py tests/benchmarks/sweep/test_server_process.py
.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/benchmarks/sweep/server.py tests/benchmarks/sweep/test_server_process.py
```

The full standard sweep directory aborted during an existing parameter test's global teardown in PyTorch 2.13.0 `empty_host_cache` on macOS. Its root cause remains uninvestigated. The 28-pass result above excludes global conftest fixtures and is not a full standard-suite pass. The new test uses the existing `skip_global_cleanup` marker because it creates no distributed/GPU state; both new cases also passed with normal conftest loading.

The existing Buildkite benchmarks CLI step collects this directory; the test-tethering hook passed. A Linux attempt stopped before test execution because package initialization required PyTorch, which was not installed on the memory-constrained host. No Linux test pass, upstream CI, native vLLM rebuild, model inference, GPU resource-recovery test, or performance benchmark is claimed.

## Details

`start_new_session=True` makes the server PID the process group ID. Previously, cleanup depended on `poll() is None`, so a reaped leader prevented cleanup of surviving workers. Looking up its PGID also requires the leader to exist. Signal the known group ID directly, retain the existing SIGKILL behavior, then wait for the direct child. A per-start completion flag prevents subsequent calls from signalling the old group again. Only a missing process group is suppressed; other errors still propagate.

The scope is workers that remain in the server's group. This does not wait for every grandchild, cover detached sessions, or guarantee GPU-memory release. Waiting for the direct child adds synchronous shutdown waiting. Numeric PGID reuse remains a consideration if the whole group disappears long before the first cleanup call.

Duplicate checks on 2026-10-05 covered open/closed/merged PRs, related issues, file history, and the submitter's existing PRs. No matching cleanup fix was found. [#55716](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55716) handles address parsing in the same module; this regression uses a separate filename. [#59816](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59816) handles resume/warmup/failure records. This change is independent of both.

**AI assistance:** Codex investigated, authored, reviewed, and ran the recorded checks. The submitter has confirmed human review of the change. The test results above were obtained by Codex; independent human-run testing is not asserted. This PR is a draft while human-run checks and full standard-suite validation remain outstanding.

author: shubhamtaywade82
body:
## Summary

Two independent changes on one branch.

### 1. Ollama calls now go through `@nemesis-oss/ollama-sdk` (`65b9eb0`)
- `OllamaAdvisor` (veto / advise / ask / the council's `generateJson`) and `SmcExecutionAdvisor` use the SDK's `OllamaClient`; the `ollama` dependency is removed.
- The advisor keeps its own API-key pool (round-robin + failover), so each SDK client runs with `retries: 0` and a 5s timeout instead of nesting retries under the pool.
- **The SDK refuses any `format` request (including `format: "json"`) against a non-local endpoint**, and `.env.example` defaults to `OLLAMA_HOST=https://ollama.com`. A plain swap would have silently disabled the veto and the council on cloud. JSON mode is therefore requested only from local hosts (`jsonFormatFor`); elsewhere the prompts already demand JSON and replies are parsed tolerantly (`parseJsonLoose`: code fences / prose around the object). `parseVerdict` stays fail-closed on prose with no JSON.
- Verified end to end against a local fake Ollama server (ping `/api/tags`, `/api/generate` with the bearer key, `format: "json"` + `stream: false`, fenced reply parsed).

### 2. CROWDING-ι targets and setup-card TP2 (`f51d3e7`)
- CROWDING-ι took profit at the range midpoint with a stop >= 1.2 ATR away. The midpoint is a fixed price, so the reward collapsed as price drifted toward it (SOL alerts: RR 1.17 -> 0.89 -> 0.42), and no RR floor applies by default (`MIN_RR=0`, `CANDIDATE_MIN_RR=0.25`). It now targets the nearest untaken liquidity pool paying at least `CROWDING_MIN_REWARD_RISK` (default 1.5) times the stop, walking outward past pools that are too close, and emits nothing when none qualifies.
- Setup cards could show TP2 a few ticks past TP1 (SOL: 121.5700 / 121.5750) because the next pool of an equal-high cluster counted as a second target. TP2 must now sit at least 0.5 ATR beyond TP1, else it is omitted. TP1 and the displayed RR are unchanged.

## Behaviour changes worth reviewing
- Crowding will fire less often (that is the point); lower `CROWDING_MIN_REWARD_RISK` to trade more.
- On non-local Ollama hosts JSON mode is no longer enforced by the server.
- The existing Crowding test asserted the midpoint target and was rewritten around pools.

## Known limitation
The SDK classifies bracketed IPv6 loopback (`http://[::1]:11434`) as cloud, so no `format` is sent there. Fix is in the SDK (separate PR).

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck`
- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test` (1120 passing)
- [x] TP2 tests fail on the old engine and pass with the fix
- [ ] Not run against real Ollama Cloud or live market data

body:
Under `--follow`, the warning that the daemon failed a rules reload and is running with NO rules is now written when the first corrupt record arrives. Before this change it appeared only at EOF or Ctrl+C. S10 of #150.

- `Analyzer::record` sets the new `Step.corrupt` on the run's first record with unreadable field names. `write_step` writes it for every action, run-level (so `why` shows it too), and does not count it toward the `(xN)` totals. The EOF count note is unchanged. Both notes share one `NO_RULES` const.
- Batch reads only `Step.diagnostics`, so its output is byte-identical. No snapshot changed. A review compared master and this branch over 456 batch runs and found 0 differences.
- `a_follow_run_writes_the_result_before_stdin_closes` gains a row per action. Each row writes one corrupt record, reads the warning while stdin is still open, writes two more records, and expects exactly the "3 records" count note at EOF. The rows fail under the `== 2`, `!= 1` and `>= 1` variants of the condition.
- DESIGN.md §9: the corruption warning is the one run note written live.

Gate: `just check` green. A local `cargo mutants --in-diff` on the change caught 2, 1 was unviable, 0 missed and 0 timed out.

- #1595/#1598 refuse edits while a registration is pending or in flight, but a failed registration leaves the draft editable and retry re-sends the old payload, and an edit during the relay attempt that ends in queueing it passes the check too

- a cancelled or no-longer-draft po keeps the existing quiet skip
- money compared by value (12 = 12.00000); a row queued before the digest has none and drains as before
- not done: refusing edits while a failed registration is held - the digest already stops the stale push and says so
- tests: changed draft held as failed with a notice, retried failed registration after an edit not pushed, unchanged draft pushed, legacy row drains, digest ignores money scale, pre-flight hands the digest back beside the payload; backend suite 3417 passed

body:
## Why

Setup keeps a lasting proof that each connector works, kept together with the tunnel it came through (#1049): evidence for another tunnel proves nothing about the current one. The Plugins connector runs on its own Secure Tunnel ID (`pluginsTunnelId`, `connection.ts`), but `connectorTunnelKey()` keyed its proof to Core's `tunnelId`. So a Plugins proof survived a change of the Plugins tunnel (Setup could show Plugins as working on a tunnel ChatGPT never reached), and was dropped when only Core's tunnel changed. Noted in the #1049 review as a follow-up after the series.

## What changed

`connectorTunnelKey()` uses `pluginsTunnelId` for the Plugins connector, like `desktopTunnelId` for Desktop. An empty Plugins tunnel ID keeps no proof, as for the others.

No contract change: the proof file's key is internal; a Plugins proof keyed to Core's tunnel simply no longer matches and is recorded again on the next request.
No visual change: Setup status logic only.

author: tunglambk
body: ## What the bug is On a versioning-enabled bucket (posix backend with `--versioning-dir`), `PutObject` with `If-None-Match: *` on a key whose current version is a delete marker fails with `412 PreconditionFailed`. Every read of that key reports it as missing (`HeadObject` and `GetObject` return `404 NoSuchKey`), so the conditional write contradicts the read path. On AWS S3 the same request succeeds: the key has no current object when its latest version is a delete marker. This breaks Terraform/OpenTofu S3 state locking (`use_lockfile = true`). Terraform creates `.tflock` with `If-None-Match: *` and deletes it on unlock. On a versioned bucket the first apply works; every later apply then fails with `Error acquiring the state lock ... PreconditionFailed`, because the lock file key now has a delete marker. ## Reproduction ``` aws s3api put-object --bucket b --key l --body x.txt --if-none-match '*' # OK aws s3api delete-object --bucket b --key l # creates a delete marker aws s3api head-object --bucket b --key l # 404 Not Found (correct) aws s3api put-object --bucket b --key l --body x.txt --if-none-match '*' # 412 PreconditionFailed (unexpected) ``` Reproduced directly against the posix backend in `TestPosixConditionalPutIfNoneMatchDeleteMarker`, which is added by this pull request. On `main` without the fix: ``` --- FAIL: TestPosixConditionalPutIfNoneMatchDeleteMarker (0.09s) --- FAIL: TestPosixConditionalPutIfNoneMatchDeleteMarker/xattr (0.01s) posix_conditional_put_test.go:870: if-none-match put after delete marker: PreconditionFailed412 --- FAIL: TestPosixConditionalPutIfNoneMatchDeleteMarker/sidecar (0.07s) posix_conditional_put_test.go:870: if-none-match put after delete marker: PreconditionFailed412 FAIL ``` ## Root cause `Posix.checkPutPreconditions` (`backend/posix/posix.go`) decided whether the key had a current object from the etag attribute at the object path alone: ```go _, err := p.statLiveObject(bucket, object) if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) { return backend.EvaluateObjectPutPreconditions("", ifMatch, ifNoneMatch, false) } etagBytes, err := p.meta.RetrieveAttribute(nil, bucket, object, etagkey) if err == nil || errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) || errors.Is(err, meta.ErrNoSuchKey) { return backend.EvaluateObjectPutPreconditions(string(etagBytes), ifMatch, ifNoneMatch, err == nil) } ``` On a versioning-enabled bucket, `DeleteObject` does not remove the entry at the object path: it copies the current version into the versioning directory and marks the surviving entry with the `delete-marker` attribute (`createObjVersion` plus `StoreAttribute(..., deleteMarkerKey, ...)`). The entry is therefore still live for `statLiveObject`, and the old etag attribute is still readable, so `objExists` came out `true` and `EvaluateObjectPutPreconditions` returned `412` for `If-None-Match`. Reads do not have this problem because `GetObject` and `HeadObject` consult `isObjDeleteMarker` and report the key as `NoSuchKey` when the marker is the current version. The conditional write path never made that check, so it treated the hidden version as the current object. Traced directly, for the key created by the test above: ``` before delete: etag attr = "\"f97c5d...\"" err = after delete: statLiveObject fi = &{lockfile 3 420 ...} err = after delete: etag attr = "\"f97c5d...\"" err = after delete: isObjDeleteMarker = true err = after delete: head err = NoSuchKey (404) after delete: attrs = [etag delete-marker checksums version-id] ``` The etag attribute and the live entry are both still there; only the `delete-marker` attribute distinguishes the state, and `checkPutPreconditions` did not look at it. ## The fix In `checkPutPreconditions`, after confirming the key has a live entry and when gateway versioning is configured, check `isObjDeleteMarker`. A delete marker is not a current object, so the preconditions are evaluated with `objExists = false` and an empty etag, exactly as for a key that has no current version: ```go // a delete marker is not a current object: the key was deleted on a // versioning-enabled bucket and reads report it as missing, so the // conditional write must see it as absent as well if err == nil && p.versioningEnabled() { isDelMarker, derr := p.isObjDeleteMarker(bucket, object) if derr != nil && !errors.Is(derr, s3err.GetAPIError(s3err.ErrNoSuchKey)) { return derr } if isDelMarker { return backend.EvaluateObjectPutPreconditions("", ifMatch, ifNoneMatch, false) } } ``` With `objExists = false`, `If-None-Match: *` proceeds and the object is re-created, while `If-Match` fails as it does for a key that has no current object. `NoSuchKey` from the marker lookup is tolerated rather than propagated: it means the entry disappeared between the two lookups, and the etag lookup that follows already handles that case. `checkPutPreconditions` is the single precondition entry point shared by `PutObject`, `PutObjectWithPostFunc` and `CompleteMultipartUpload`, so all conditional write paths are covered by this one change. This keeps conditional writes consistent with the read paths, which report a delete-marked key as missing. ## Validation ``` go build ./backend/... ./s3err/... # OK go vet ./backend/posix/ # OK gofmt -l backend/posix/ # no output go test ./backend/... ./s3err/... -count=1 ok github.com/versity/versitygw/backend 0.540s ok github.com/versity/versitygw/backend/azure 0.206s ok github.com/versity/versitygw/backend/meta 0.017s ok github.com/versity/versitygw/backend/posix 1.328s ok github.com/versity/versitygw/backend/s3proxy 0.015s ? github.com/versity/versitygw/backend/scoutfs [no test files] ? github.com/versity/versitygw/s3err [no test files] ``` Regression test, before the fix (posix.go at `main`, test kept): ``` go test ./backend/posix/ -run TestPosixConditionalPutIfNoneMatchDeleteMarker -count=1 --- FAIL: TestPosixConditionalPutIfNoneMatchDeleteMarker (0.09s) --- FAIL: .../xattr (0.01s) -> PreconditionFailed, 412 --- FAIL: .../sidecar (0.07s) -> PreconditionFailed, 412 FAIL ``` Regression test, after the fix: ``` go test ./backend/posix/ -run TestPosixConditionalPutIfNoneMatchDeleteMarker -count=1 ok github.com/versity/versitygw/backend/posix 0.076s ``` The new test builds a posix backend with a versioning directory, enables versioning on the bucket, creates the key with `If-None-Match: *`, deletes it so the current version becomes a delete marker, asserts that `HeadObject` reports `NoSuchKey`, and then asserts that the conditional create succeeds and the object is readable again. It runs for both metadata backends exercised by the existing conditional-put tests (`xattr` and `sidecar`). Note that `go build ./...` cannot be used in this repository: packages under `plugins/` are built with `-buildmode=plugin` and `tests/conditionalrace` contains only test files, so the touched packages were built explicitly. The `tests/integration` suite needs a running gateway and credentials and was not run here; the behaviour is covered by the backend-level regression test instead. Fixes #2480

author: prateekm1007
body:
## What
C2 (founder Round 16): the C8 cadence rule moves from a red-main alarm to a REQUIRED PR merge gate. Push-time runs report-only (`--report`, never fails main); the PR check blocks the merge button (`--pr`) when a production-relevant PR would land inside the one-per-hour budget; the post-deploy smoke runs for ANY completed production deployment state (no silent skips).

## Why
Founder Round-16 defect 2: "The cadence gate turns main red after the fact. Five red main runs trace to 'Deploy cadence gate'... A failing push check can't undo a merge, it skips the post-deploy smoke, and it trains everyone to ignore red." Verified in-repo: CI runs on main failed at 9f8f729/b3003f2/77a5ede/6232d09 on the push-time cadence step; smoke runs skipped on 9f8f729 and 62fd623 (deployment-state filter).

## Proof
Fail-first (rule 24), raw output on this branch before any merge:

```
$ node scripts/ci/deployCadence.mjs --report --base origin/main
::warning::deploy-cadence: C8 VIOLATION ON THE RECORD — production-relevant merge 6232d098b09f landed 3.1 min after c7b8d17454a3 — C8 allows at most one per 60 min
deploy-cadence: report-only — main stays green; record this in docs/RELEASE.md cadence ledger
exit: 0
```
The exact history that turned main red this morning (#165 03:07:21Z -> #177 03:10:25Z, 3.1 min gap) now prints a warning and exits 0.

```
$ node scripts/ci/deployCadence.mjs --pr --base origin/main   # on this branch, 51 min after 6232d09
deploy-cadence: BLOCKED — this PR is production-relevant and the last production-relevant merge landed 51 min ago — C8 allows at most one per 60 min
deploy-cadence: earliest safe merge time 2026-10-05T04:10:25.000Z (re-run this check then merge)
exit: 1
```
The gate BITES: exit 1 names the earliest safe merge time (founder acceptance: "a PR opened within an hour of the last production merge shows a failing required check" — this PR itself demonstrates it in CI).

Fast gate: `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0; `npx eslint .` 0 errors / 290 warnings (ratchet holds); `npx vitest run test/r15.deployCadence.test.mjs` 9/9 (5 pinned + 4 new prGateDecision cases).

## Risk
The required check reads the wall clock at CI time; a PR green at T-50 min merged at T-59 min would still slip — the push-side report + cadence ledger keep that residual on the record (documented in the script header, same as R15-F's honest scoping). Before merging inside the window's tail, re-run the check: it passes once the hour has elapsed. Paired guard (C9): the smoke now runs on failed/canceled deployments too, so report-only cadence cannot hide a broken deploy.

## Rollback
`git revert <merge-sha>` restores the R15-F behavior (push-blocking, PR advisory). Branch-protection change (adding the required check + enforce_admins) is one API call to reverse; recorded in the round-16 evidence file.

🔧 Fix: Implemented `isSameDevice` in `tools/lib/aas-v1/transaction/safety.js` and updated `tools/lib/aas-v1/transaction/runtime.js` to verify parent directory device equivalence for transaction files.

author: jhyoo1203
body:
## 배경

`GET /api/users/10/followings` 응답의 `totalElements` 는 5인데 `content` 에는 3명만 내려왔다. 프로필의 팔로잉 수도 같은 쿼리로 세서 5로 보인다.

`follows` 테이블에는 `users` 로 가는 FK 가 없어, 상대 사용자 행이 없거나 탈퇴한 팔로우 행이 남을 수 있다. 수(`countByFollowerId`)와 목록 페이지의 `totalElements` 는 이런 행까지 세고, 목록은 사용자를 조회한 뒤 찾지 못한 사람만 응답에서 빼고 있어서 둘이 어긋났다.

고치다 보니 회원 탈퇴도 항상 실패하고 있었다. `User.withdraw()` 가 닉네임을 `withdrawn-{id}` 로 바꾸는데, id 가 한 자리여도 11자라 `users.nickname` 의 2~10자 CHECK 제약(`ck_users_nickname_length`)에 걸린다. 이 오류로 탈퇴 트랜잭션 전체가 롤백된다.

## 변경 내용

- `FollowRepository`
  - 팔로워·팔로잉 **수와 목록**을 모두 "상대 사용자가 존재하고 탈퇴(`DEACTIVATED`)하지 않은 행"만 세도록 `EXISTS` 조건을 넣었다
  - 메서드 이름을 `countFollowers`·`countFollowings`·`findFollowers`·`findFollowings` 로 바꿨다. 파생 쿼리 이름(`countByFollowerId`)이 실제 조건과 달라지기 때문이다
  - 검색 결과의 팔로워 수(`countByFollowingIdIn`)도 같은 기준을 쓴다
- `FollowService`·`MyPageService`·`UserProfileService`: 새 메서드를 쓴다
- `FollowService.follow()`: 탈퇴한 사용자를 팔로우하려 하면 `USER_NOT_FOUND` 를 반환한다. 그대로 두면 수와 목록 어디에도 보이지 않는 행만 쌓인다
- `User.withdraw()`: 탈퇴 닉네임을 `탈퇴_{id 36진수}` 로 바꿨다 (예: id 12345 → `탈퇴_9ix`)

## 동작 방식

- 정지(`SUSPENDED`) 사용자는 아직 존재하는 계정이라 수와 목록에 그대로 보인다
- 탈퇴 닉네임은 id 가 약 780억 미만이면 10자 안에 든다. 가입 닉네임 규칙(`^[가-힣a-zA-Z0-9]{2,10}$`)에 없는 `_` 를 넣어서 일반 사용자 닉네임과 겹칠 수 없다
- 이미 쌓인, 상대 사용자가 없는 팔로우 행은 지우지 않았다. 조회 기준을 맞춰 화면 숫자는 일치하고, 데이터 정리는 prod 데이터를 확인한 뒤 따로 결정한다

## 확인 방법

- `FollowRepositoryTest`(Testcontainers PostgreSQL)
  - 정상·탈퇴·존재하지 않는 상대를 섞어 팔로우한 뒤, 팔로잉·팔로워 수와 목록, `totalElements`, 검색용 팔로워 수가 모두 1로 같은지 확인
  - 탈퇴 상대는 실제 `withdraw()` 로 만든다. 수정 전 코드에서는 닉네임 제약 위반으로 실패하던 경로다
  - 탈퇴 익명화한 사용자가 DB 제약을 통과해 저장되고 닉네임이 `탈퇴_{id 36진수}` 인지 확인
- 전체 테스트 통과

author: jessica12ryan
body:
# fix(developer): Empty branch dropdown when GitHub User Fork remote is selected

## Summary

On `settings.php#settings-developer`, entering a GitHub username + PAT and then
selecting **GitHub User Fork** from the remote repository dropdown left the Git
Branch dropdown showing only `-- Select Branch --`, with none of the fork's
branches listed.

## Root cause

`GET /api/git/branches?remote=<user>` lists only local remote-tracking refs
(`git branch -r` filtered by `<user>/`). The git remote for a fork is created
lazily at branch-switch time (`changebranch.php`), so a freshly-entered
username/PAT has zero local refs and the endpoint returns `[]`.

Two compounding issues made it worse:

1. `PrintGitBranchOptions()` (initial page render) had the same flaw — it
   fetched `--all` but the fork remote didn't exist yet.
2. The generic `PrintSetting` select renderer treated a saved username as a
   stale value (not one of `origin`/`newfeatures`/`pull-requests`), auto-selected
   `origin`, and overwrote the saved `gitRemote` via `SetSetting` on page load.

## Changes

**`www/api/controllers/git.php`**
- `GitBranches()` now detects when the requested remote matches the saved
  `gitHubUser` and ensures the git remote exists (`remote add` / `set-url`
  with PAT auth, mirroring `changebranch.php`) and fetches it under the shared
  `fpp-git-repo.lock` before listing branches.
- Falls back to the GitHub branches API via the new `GitHubForkBranchNames()`
  helper (same obsolete/dependabot filtering) when local refs are still empty.
- Guarded so reserved names (`origin` / `newfeatures` / `pull-requests`) are
  never treated as a fork — the real remote URLs can't be rewritten.
- Non-fork remotes execute byte-identical logic to before (no behavior change).

**`www/settings-developer.php`**
- `PrintGitBranchOptions()` gets the same ensure-remote + GitHub API fallback
  (with the same reserved-name guard), so the branch list also renders on first
  load with a fork selected.
- The saved fork value is injected into the `gitRemote` select options before
  `PrintSetting()`, preventing the auto-reset-to-`origin` clobber.
- `reloadGitBranches()` now URL-encodes the remote, shows a loading state,
  builds options safely (no string-concat HTML), shows a "No branches found"
  hint instead of failing silently, and falls back to `api/git/forkBranches`
  data when the local listing comes back empty for a fork remote.

## Behavior preservation

- Response shape of `GET /api/git/branches` is unchanged (JSON array).
- `origin` / `newfeatures` / Pull-Requests flows are untouched.
- `openapi.json` needs no regeneration (verified: generator output diff is
  limited to pre-existing drift in unrelated endpoints).
- Other `api/git/branches` consumers (`multisync.php`) only gain populated
  results where they previously got `[]`; `changeRemoteBranch.php` already
  forwards fork remotes to `changebranch.php`, which handles them.

## Testing

- `php -l` clean on all touched files.
- `node --check` clean on the page script.
- Username/regex boundary checks pass (valid/invalid/reserved names, 39 vs 40
  char limit).
- Spec-regeneration check: no drift attributable to this change.
- Verified on Pi4B running FPP 10.2-3

author: rlronan
body:
Closes the last open item of #2963. `libchelis_runtime.a`, the runtime linked into every built executable, no longer imports any host libm transcendental.

**Before.** The runtime's exact decimal parser (`decimal_parse.rs`, used by `to_float`, Std.Decimal ingress and JSON and CSV float text) used num-bigint. num-bigint and num-integer pulled in `cbrt`, `exp`, `log` and `log2` from the system math library. A built executable imported `_cbrt _exp _fmodf _log _log2`. Measured with `nm -A`/`nm -u` against all 613 exports of the SDK `libsystem_m.tbd`.

**Fix (the dependency is removed).** `decimal_parse.rs` gets its own small natural-number type with u32 limbs (about 140 lines). Every caller scales the quotient below 2^(mantissa+2), so rounding is binary long division into a u64, with ties to even. num-bigint is now only a dev-dependency of chelis-runtime, used as a test oracle. The runtime archive now imports no libm symbol, and a built executable imports only `_fmodf`, which comes from the generated C and is exact under IEEE 754.

**Guard.** `crates/chelis-runtime-bundle/tests/runtime_no_host_transcendentals.rs` parses every object in the carried runtime archive with `object`, and fails on any undefined C23 <math.h> transcendental, power, error or gamma function, or a common libm extension. It covers the f/l, `__*_finite`, `_stret`, `_r` and `@GLIBC` spellings. sqrt, fma, fmod and the rounding, scaling and min/max families stay allowed. With crates/chelis-runtime reverted to origin/main, the guard fails and lists the symbols above; with the fix it passes.

**Parity: bit-identical results.** The old num-bigint implementation stays as a `#[cfg(test)]` oracle (`decimal_parse_reference.rs`). Differential tests compare, bit for bit at every width, against the reference, and at f64 and f32 against `str::parse`:
- 20k random spellings, with exponents from -380 to 340;
- exact halfway points m·2^e and their neighbours, normal and subnormal, at all four widths;
- 700- to 900-digit spellings around the 800-digit sticky cut;
- 20k malformed spellings.

Mutation check: tie-to-odd fails 6 of 9 tests, and an off-by-one in mul_pow10 fails 4.

**Validation.**
- chelis-runtime lib, explicit_text_parsers and runtime_storage_narrowing: 62/62.
- chelis-runtime-bundle: 26/26.
- chelis-cli issue_2870_text_parser_lane_parity and csv_io: 5/5.
- `gate.py --fast`: passes.
- phase3: passes, 0 changed identities.

The compile_fail fixture lock drops num-bigint from the runtime entry.

Resolves #2963 (closed manually after merge). Part of #2957.

## Red-team record

Round 1 was run by a fresh local Opus reviewer on head `331023f24`. It found no P0, P1 or P2:
- An independent `fractions.Fraction` oracle agreed with the new parser on all 121,861 cases at all four widths. Those covered halfway cases, ±1 ulp, subnormals, the overflow threshold, ties past the 800-digit cut, huge exponents and malformed text.
- The release archive shares no undefined symbol with libsystem_m, and a built executable imports only `_fmodf`.
- The guard fails on the old runtime and on an injected `exp` call, and it ran on Linux CI in this PR.
- Callers' behaviour is unchanged.

Two P3s are recorded, not repaired:
- CI checks the debug test-profile archive only.
- `_FloatN` spellings and `dlsym` are not in the name list; Rust emits neither.

The reviewer is satisfied, and the round is closed.



Package expansion at `821d4f6ec` (run https://github.com/Chelis-Lang/chelis/actions/runs/37270330941) reported 0 introduced, 0 inherited and 70 unrun targets, because of the deadline.

Rebase onto main `4ec7e8c57`, for a conflict with #3186. #3186 made `rounded_quotient` pub(crate) and split out `ratio_to_ieee_bits` so that its new `host_round.rs` ([05-OP-1] `round_to`) could reuse them. `host_round.rs` itself used num-bigint, a second runtime user. The rebase keeps #3186's API on the runtime-owned `Natural` (`rounded_quotient` now returns a `Natural`, because round_to coefficients reach about 2,600 bits) and rewrites `round_to_bits` without num-bigint: powers of two are shifts and powers of ten use `mul_pow10`, with the operation sequence unchanged. The old BigUint `round_to_bits` stays as a test reference. A new differential test compares it bit for bit with the new code over 16k random operands at f64, f32, f16 and bf16 (normal, subnormal and non-finite, places -330..1110), and an off-by-one mutation fails it. Checks: runtime lib and parsers 81/81, the bundle with the guard 26/26, cli text-parser and csv 5/5, compiled_host_effects round_to 3/3, the representation oracle passes, the release archive shares no symbol with libsystem_m, the locks are `--locked` OK, and gate --fast passes.

Candidate-base-update: d8c9c071ebe39f00689c7038adddc7bedcb0917d rebase onto main 4ec7e8c57 to resolve the decimal_parse.rs conflict with #3186 and remove the second num-bigint user it added (host_round.rs round_to)



Targeted rebase review, by a fresh reviewer on `d8c9c071e`, found no P0, P1 or P2:
- `round_to`: an independent `fractions` oracle checked 614,619 cases at all four widths, with 0 mismatches against the head and 0 between the head and main `4ec7e8c57`.
- The decimal parse differential found 0 mismatches against Python `float()` and against main.
- The release archive has no num_* objects and no libm symbols, and the same scan detects both in main's archive.
- The `round_to` tests and an adversarial probe give identical output in eval and C.

author: jmejiaes
body:
Per-case-type AI stages (ADR 0006). Contract: `docs/platform/api/slice-21-stages.md`.

- **Model:** each case type has a stage (0–3) and an agent status (none / ready / active). The case's copilot mode follows its type: 0 none, 1 Copiloto, 2 + Herramientas, 3 + draft. An untyped case gets no copilot (like stage 0).
- **Signals** from the event log since the type reached its stage: cases resolved, closed cases with copilot questions, tools proposed/used, last decided drafts (as is / edited / discarded). Nothing counts while AI is off.
- **Team rule** (canvas defaults, `CC_STAGE_*`): 0→1 10 resolved; 1→2 20 cases with questions; 2→3 tools used in ≥70% of ≥10 cases; 3→ready ≥80 of the last 100 drafts as is or minor edits. Automatic, one step at a time, audited, live on `ai:stages`. Supervisión can move a type back.
- **API:** `GET /ai/stages`, `POST /supervision/ai/stages/{caseType}/move-back`, `POST /cases/{caseId}/copilot/suggestions/{suggestionId}/tools` (platform-side `copilot.tool_used`). Automatic suggestions start at stage 2 (gate wraps the AI team's process at the composition root).
- **Screens:** stage strip under the case header; Herramientas "Usar" records the tool; Inicio sums up the assistant and gives its hand-overs their own row.
- **Fixes:** Traspaso "Verificado" renders nested facts as a readable list; Inicio no longer 500s for an assistant hand-over.
- **Seed:** types at every stage, matching the canvas story.

Gates: backend ruff, format, mypy, pytest 1553, OpenAPI check; frontend typecheck, lint, format, test 1075, build, check:api, e2e 16/16.

For the AI team (in the slice doc): enforce the mode on manual copilot routes, pass the stage to the copilot, per-item feedback, question grouping.

author: shreeshailaya
body: ## Why contextpack already has a sharp CLI (`pack` with `--budget` / `--focus` / `--since` / `--diff` / `--paths-from` / `--list` / `--format json`, plus `compare` and `init`). Agents could only use it by shelling out and reading files. Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, VS Code Copilot, Windsurf, and others now expect a one-line MCP config. This is the missing first-class agent integration. ## What `contextpack mcp` runs a Model Context Protocol server on stdio. **Tools** (small set; `compare` is not included — it is a human-facing naive-vs-packed table, not something an agent needs in the loop): | Tool | Role | | --- | --- | | `pack` | Token-budgeted digest as text (`md` or `json`) | | `list` | Dry-run preview / digest map (no file bodies). Default `json`. | Shared args: `path` / `root`, `budget`, `focus`, `since`, `diff`, `paths`, `ignore`, `include`, `noMap`. Default root = server cwd. Reuses `pack()`, `formatPack`, `formatList`, `loadProjectConfig` / `mergeConfigWithCli`. Redaction defaults **on**. Project config (`.contextpack.json` / `contextpack.json` / `package.json#contextpack`) is respected the same way as the CLI. **Path jail:** tool `path`/`root` must stay inside the server cwd. Listed `paths` use the existing `--paths-from` rules (`looksAbsolute` / `resolveListedPath`). Absolute paths and `..` traversal are **rejected** (not silently skipped). stdout is protocol-only. Logs go to stderr. ## Dependency decision **No `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`.** The official SDK works on Node >=18, but it is not light: current versions pull Express, Hono, CORS, AJV, EventSource, and land in the multi-MB unpacked range, plus a `zod` peer. This package currently depends on `commander` and `ignore` only. Instead: a small, tested JSON-RPC 2.0 stdio loop covering `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `notifications/initialized`, and `ping`. Newline-delimited messages (MCP stdio spec). Protocol versions echoed when the client sends `2024-11-05` / `2025-03-26` / `2025-06-18`; otherwise `2024-11-05`. `contextpack init` mentions MCP in the Cursor rule / skill / help text. It does **not** write `.cursor/mcp.json` (that would clobber an existing host config). ## Docs / version - README: "Use with agents (MCP)" high up, with copy-paste config for Claude Code (`claude mcp add …`), Cursor (`.cursor/mcp.json`), and a generic `mcpServers` block — all `npx -y -p @shree_vitkar/contextpack contextpack mcp` - `docs/agents.md` updated - Version **0.1.17** in `package.json` / lockfile, pack-pr Action pin, and dogfood workflow Not published to npm from this PR. ## Tests Vitest drives the server in-process (plus a PassThrough stdio loop): initialize, tools/list, pack on `fixtures/demo-project` under a budget, list, path-traversal rejection. Also config respect and default-on redaction. `npm run lint`, `npm test` (225 tests), and `npm run build` all passed. ## Manual verification From the repo root, after `npm run build`: ```bash printf '%s\n' \ '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"verify","version":"0"}}}' \ '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"}' \ '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list"}' \ '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"list","arguments":{"path":"fixtures/demo-project","budget":500}}}' \ '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":4,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"pack","arguments":{"path":"fixtures/demo-project","budget":500}}}' \ '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":5,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"pack","arguments":{"path":".."}}}' \ '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":6,"method":"ping"}' \ | node dist/cli.js mcp ``` Results: - stderr empty (protocol stayed on stdout) - 6 JSON-RPC responses (the `initialized` notification produced none) - `initialize` → `2024-11-05`, `serverInfo: { name: "contextpack", version: "0.1.17" }` - `tools/list` → `pack`, `list` - `list` on `fixtures/demo-project` budget 500 → 5 entries, 5 included, no file bodies - `pack` → markdown digest with `README.md`, vendor/build filtered out - `path: ".."` → `isError: true`, `rejecting path outside server cwd: ..` - `ping` → `{}`

author: nsmith-gd
body:
This round has three commits. It finishes audit order P4, and the ROADMAP now marks P4 done.

### The VR body (T82, M4; ARCHITECTURE note 210)

**What other players see of a headset crewmate.** This is presentation only, in `Game/VrBody.cs` (pure functions) and `CreatureArt.HeadsetBody`:
- **Lean, then crouch:** for the first 0.25 m the head drops below `Eyes.Height`, the torso leans forward, up to 35°. Below that, the knees bend, up to 0.5 m.
- **Twist:** the hips keep their facing until the head turns more than 35° off them. The torso takes 0.6 of the twist, and the neck takes the rest plus the headset's pitch.
- **Feet:** they're planted in the car's frame. A foot steps when the hips move 0.2 m or turn 30° away from it: one foot at a time, 0.28 s per step, lifted 9 cm. The legs use the same two-bone IK as the arms.
- **When it applies:** only when the crewmate is standing still and not acting. Walking, running and actions keep their clips.
- **Tuning:** in `content/tuning/vr.json body`, flagged as our own reading. The GDD and spec give no VR numbers (note 40).

**Protocol 24.** Other players weren't being sent the head's height, so I added it.
- **On the intent:** `PlayerIntent.Head` rides in the hand block, flagged by a spare bit and sent as one I16 in centimetres.
- **On the player record:** `PlayerState.Head`. It's zero for keyboard players and bots.
- **In the sim:** it's clamped, and nothing acts on it.
- **Limitation:** a headset with no controllers tracked shows a standing body.

**Fixed along the way:** the app only ever copied the reaching hand into the intent, so the host never had both hands for two-handed grips (T43).

**Headless check:** `dt screenshot --view crew --vr-body` shows three headset crewmates: one leaning with a hand reaching down, one crouched deep, and one with the head turned 100°, hips following and a foot mid-step. I re-rendered it after the latest merge with main and looked at it.

### A crewmate's gait on a moving car (note 211)

**The bug:** a keyboard player or bot standing still on a train at 15 m/s played the run clip, because `SceneArt.Crewmate` took their pace from world-space feet.

**The fix:**
- `Crewmate` now carries `Car` and `Local`, from the snapshot's `PlayerState.Parent` and `Position`.
- The pace is measured in the car's frame for everyone, and this replaces the VR body's headset-only measure.
- The Passenger had the same bug and is fixed the same way.
- No protocol change.

**Test:** `CrewActsTests.ACrewmateStoodOnAMovingCarIsIdleNotRunning`. It failed before the fix with "Expected Idle, Actual Run".

### The look-out: the sweep's dormant kinds come on (note 212)

**Why:** the combination sweep (`dt balance --pairs`) reported the Gaunt, the Draggers and Ribbits as dormant. They were placed but never came on, because bots never went near them.

**What the look-out does.** It only runs in insisted harness nights (`HarnessOptions.Insist` + `Look`). The crew's last walker becomes the look-out:
- **On the ground:** it walks to within 3 m of a sleeping Gaunt, or 5 m of a Ribbit pack.
- **On the roofs:** it stands 0.6 m from the lip on an insisted Dragger's side.
- **Afterwards:** it goes back to its post.
- **Rules:** it acts through intent only, and it's deterministic. No enemy rules changed. The bots' normal counters answer the threat.
- **Tuning:** `balance.json combinations.look`, citing GDD §34.

**`dt balance --pairs --only Gaunt,Dragger,Ribbit,Climber`:**

| | Verdicts | Never exercised |
|---|---|---|
| Before | dormant 6 | Dragger 3, Ribbit 3, Gaunt 3 |
| After | fair 3, trivial 3 | none |

The sweep now flags three trivial verdicts: bots beat a Dragger or a Ribbit pack cleanly in 90 s. This is a balance finding for the director, and I haven't hidden it:
- Dragger+Ribbit / dark
- Dragger+Climber / clear
- Ribbit+Climber / wet

**Not yet:** a crew of 2 has no walker to send.

**Test:** `AuditTests.TheLookOutGoesAndLooksAtWhatLiesInWait`. Without the look-out, the Gaunt and the Dragger are placed but never come on; with it, both do.

### Checks
- Build has 0 warnings, and format is clean.
- Sim: 800 passed, including `NetcodeTests`.
- Game: CrewActs, VrBody and CreatureArt classes pass. 1 skipped (needs the xr-sim headset).
- Notes were renumbered after the art pass's 205–209 on main.

author: hobeone
body:
Closes #726

## Problem

A retry restored `_FAILED_<name>` to `download/<name>` before its `Dispatcher.Add`. An ingest that had chosen the same name while nothing was on disk could register it in that window and start writing. The retry's `Add` was then refused, and its undo renamed `download/<name>` back to `_FAILED_<name>`, taking the other job's early files with it.

## Premise check

With the new reservation call neutered, a hook between the restore and the retry's `Add` (an `AddJob` registers the name and writes a file) reproduces the loss:

- `RetryHistoryJob = dispatch: register ... as "name-claim": ... has that name ... want the retry to keep its name`
- `the other job's early file is no longer in its directory`

## Design

New exported method: `Dispatcher.ReserveName(id, name) (release func(), err error)`. It is a new cross-package method on `*dispatch.Dispatcher`, called from `internal/app`; the maintainer approved adding it. No interface changes, because `app.dispatcher` is the concrete type.

- `nameHolderLocked`, the registry's one test of name uniqueness, treats a reservation as a holder. `register` (Add and restore), `SetName` and `ReserveName` all go through it, so a reserved name is refused to every job but its holder, whose own `Add` is admitted.
- A reservation is not re-entrant: any existing reservation of a name is refused, even for the same ID.
- `retryHistoryJob` reserves before `restoreFailedDir` and defers the release, which runs after the restore's undo. A holder now refuses the retry before anything moves, so `restoreFailedDir` no longer takes a `nameQueued` callback and the retry's post-`Add` name refusal is removed as unreachable.
- Reservations are in memory only, released by a defer (also on panic), and cleared by a restart.
- `claimJobName` remembers names the registry refused, so an ingest that meets a reservation while nothing is on disk takes the next suffix instead of offering the same name 32 times.

Why no smaller design keeps ownership in the dispatcher:

- Restoring the directory under `d.mu` would be disk I/O under a lock.
- Registering the job before the restore would let it launch before its bytes are back.
- An app-level lock would be a second owner of name uniqueness.

Behaviour change: an ingest that takes the retry's name during the retry window now loses and gets the next suffix. The retry keeps its name, because the name is the directory holding the bytes its retained progress describes. The test `TestRetryHistoryJob_RefusesWhenAnotherJobTookItsName` is deleted for that reason.

## Unwinding

- Every return after `ReserveName` runs the deferred release.
- A holder refuses the retry before anything moves, so a refused retry changes no state.
- `RenameJob` and `AddJob` racing a reservation get `ErrJobNameTaken` and choose again.
- Concurrent retries of one ID are already refused by the job transition claim, and a same-ID second reservation is now refused too.
- A retry of an entry whose name collides with a directory in the complete or a category directory is not checked, as before.

## Enumeration

Re-derived from source:

- `git grep -n 'd\.nameHolderLocked(' -- 'internal/dispatch/*.go' ':!*_test.go'` returns 3 lines (`register`, `SetName`, `ReserveName`).
- `git grep -n 'delete(d\.reservedNames' -- 'internal/dispatch/*.go' ':!*_test.go'` returns 1 line, inside the release closure.
- `restoreFailedDir` has 1 production caller.

## Red checks

Mutations run with `scripts/mutate`, all KILLED:

- reserve skipped: `RetryHistoryJob = dispatch: register ... as "name-claim-held" ... want errRetryDirConflict wrapping ErrJobNameTaken`
- reserve skipped, window test: `RetryHistoryJob = dispatch: register ... as "name-claim" ... want the retry to keep its name`
- release skipped: `the aborted retry still holds its name`
- registry ignores reservations: `Add under a reserved name = <nil>, want ErrJobNameTaken`
- release without holder check: `a stale release freed another job's reservation`
- holder refused its own name: `the holder's own Add = ... want nil`
- same-ID re-reservation allowed: `a second ReserveName by the same id = <nil>, want ErrJobNameTaken`
- refused name offered again: `AddJob under a reserved name = ... no free job name from "reserved" after 32 attempts`

## Other design choices

- Registry-owned reservation rather than an app lock or add-then-restore.
- The retry keeps its name and the ingest yields.
- Removed the `nameQueued` check and the post-`Add` name branch.
- `claimJobName` remembers refused names.
- Re-reservation is refused.

## Notes

- The error text of `ErrJobNameTaken` still wraps `invalid job name`. That wording is pre-existing and out of scope.
- `queuedName` now has one caller (`jobNameTaken`) and could move to `rename.go`.
- Docs updated: the retry and name-uniqueness paragraphs in `docs/post-processing-contract.md`, and the teardown enumeration comment in `dispatch.go`.

## Gates

After the last edit: `go fix`, `goimports`, `go build`, `go vet` (including `-tags=integration,uitest,crash`), `golangci-lint`, `check_citations`, `check_doc_citations`, `check_dup_comments`, `check_test_doubles --all`, `mutate --check-all`, the touched specs, and `go test -race ./internal/dispatch/ ./internal/app/`. `go test -race ./...` and `./scripts/run_tests.sh` ran green on the previous head.

author: montricwang
body:
## Goal
Make the private EPUB corpus pipeline understandable and reproducible without keeping one-off investigation scripts and generated reports in the active tool layout.

## What changed
- Move reusable source-inspection tools from `analyze/` into `diagnostics/`.
- Move manual image-glyph review helpers into `review/`.
- Extract the 15 supported source-volume definitions into `config.py` so production import no longer depends on an audit module.
- Remove obsolete one-off EPUB probes and their unused DOM prototype modules.
- Remove accidentally committed temporary inspection archives (`data.zip`, `scripts.zip`, `project-structure.json`) from the current tree.
- Update corpus tests to import the reorganized modules.
- Add `scripts/corpus/epub_import/README.md` to explain the tool boundaries.
- Add `data/README.md` to distinguish irreplaceable private inputs from reproducible outputs.
- Update corpus/development/database docs to reflect the current DB pipeline and new module paths.

## Rebuild model
- From scratch: exact private EPUB + `data/raw/glyph_maps/` + matching Git revision -> `import_poems --all` -> `all_normalized.json` -> private PostgreSQL.
- Fast DB rebuild: trusted `all_normalized.json` -> `db_import`.
- Public corpus: private PostgreSQL -> `public_corpus_transfer` -> Railway PostgreSQL.

## Non-goals
- No extractor semantics changes.
- No database schema changes.
- No production data mutation.
- No attempt to commit private corpus artifacts.

## Validation
Draft until Python tests and frontend checks pass. After CI, review the moved diagnostics/review modules and documentation together before merge.

This pull request introduces several enhancements and fixes related to AI validation for evidence and population submissions in the GRC audit module. There are also minor fixes to due date warnings and refactoring for clarity.

**AI Validation Opt-Out and Result Handling**
- Added a `skipAiValidation` option to the payloads for evidence and population submissions (`SubmitEvidencePayload`, `AddEvidenceFilesPayload`, `SubmitPopulationPayload`), allowing users to opt out of AI validation for individual submissions. The backend receives this flag in the POST body. author: ram0verflow
body: ## What New blueprint `bitcoin-multisig-psbt-cosigning`: a multisig Bitcoin treasury where every spend goes through Kestra and no private key ever touches the server. - A spend request arrives by webhook and is checked against policy - Kestra builds a PSBT from a watch-only multisig wallet and reserves the coins - Signers sign on their own devices and paste the signed PSBT into the resume form - Each upload is verified, and the transaction is broadcast once the quorum is reached - Reserved coins are released on every path that does not end in a broadcast Defaults to signet and refuses mainnet unless `allow_mainnet` is set. It complements the merged `bitcoin-fee-aware-payout-batching` (#346), which spends from a hot wallet with a single approval. ## Flow 1. `spend_request` (`Webhook`, event-based) receives `{"to_address", "amount_btc", "memo", "requested_by"}` 2. `node_check` + `mainnet_guard` (`If`): fail fast if the node is down, refuse mainnet unless allowed 3. `record_request`: logged in Postgres with bound query `parameters`, so webhook data is never pasted into SQL 4. `policy_check` (`If`): invalid address or amount above `max_spend_btc` → rejected before any coins are reserved 5. `create_psbt` (`walletcreatefundedpsbt` with `lockUnspents`) → `psbt_built` (`If`) turns wallet errors into a clear message 6. `fee_guard` (`If`): above `max_fee_rate` → deferred, coins released 7. `unsigned_psbt_file` (`storage.Write`) + `ask_signers` (Slack): the PSBT as a file and in the message 8. `collect_signatures` (`LoopUntil`) around a `Pause` with `onResume` inputs (Sign / Reject, signed PSBT, note). Each upload: - must decode as a PSBT for exactly the proposed transaction; anything else is refused and the flow keeps waiting - is combined with the signatures so far, and signers are named from the key fingerprints in the PSBT - ends the loop once `analyzepsbt` reports the transaction complete 9. `finalize` → `test_accept` (`testmempoolaccept`) → `broadcast` → `mark_broadcast` → Slack The resume form each signer sees: ## Error handling - **Deliberate outcomes end as `WARNING` via `Exit`:** policy rejection, signer rejection and fee deferral. Each releases the reserved coins and says why in Slack and in the `spend_requests` table. - **Bad uploads do not end the request.** A paste that is not a PSBT, a PSBT for a different transaction (for example a swapped destination) or a duplicate signature is reported, nothing is recorded, and the flow waits for the next upload. - **The `errors` block runs on every failure** (wallet errors, an expired 48-hour signing window, node down): - it releases the coins using the inputs of the decoded PSBT, so it works even if Postgres is the failing part - it marks the request failed (`allowFailure`, so the alert still goes out) - it posts the failing task and cause - **Bad signatures cannot reach the network:** `testmempoolaccept` must accept the transaction before `sendrawtransaction`. Kestra quirks I hit and handled: - Postgres `::type` casts conflict with named `parameters`, so the SQL uses `CAST()`. - `JSON` input defaults arrive as a string on webhook runs and as an object on manual runs; the SQL accepts both. - Wallets often finalize a PSBT when they add the last signature, which removes the per-key signatures. Completion therefore accepts `analyzepsbt` `next` values `finalizer` and `extractor`. ## Why it is different No blueprint or open PR covers multisig, PSBTs or multi-party signing. It shows a human-in-the-loop pattern the catalog does not have yet: a `Pause` inside `LoopUntil` that collects several approvals, validates each one, and loops back when an approval is invalid. ## Hacktober requirements - **3+ runnable tasks:** `node_check`, `record_request`, `validate_address`, `create_psbt`, `decode_psbt`, `analyze_psbt`, `save_psbt`, `combine`, `record_signature`, `finalize`, `test_accept`, `broadcast`, notifications - **Flowable tasks:** `LoopUntil`, `Pause`, eight `If`s - **Triggers:** `Webhook` (event-based) - **Non-core plugins:** `plugin-jdbc-postgres`, `plugin-slack` ## Testing Tested on `kestra/kestra:latest` (2.0.4 OSS) with Bitcoin Core 28.1 on regtest and Postgres 16. The treasury is a real 2-of-3 `wsh(sortedmulti(...))` watch-only wallet; Alice, Bob and Carol are three separate wallets that sign with `walletprocesspsbt`, as a hardware wallet would. All runs below are on the final revision: | Scenario | Result | |---|---| | Alice and Bob sign the unsigned PSBT independently | ✅ "signature from Alice recorded (1 of 2)", "from Bob (2 of 2)", broadcast at 10.0 sat/vB (1,890 sats / 189 vB), RBF on, no coins left locked | | Bob signs Alice's copy and his wallet finalizes it | ✅ Recorded as "Alice, last signer (finalized PSBT)", broadcast | | While waiting: duplicate upload, garbage paste, a signed PSBT paying a different address; then Carol signs | ✅ "added no new signature (already signed by Alice)"; "not a valid PSBT (TX decode failed invalid base64)"; "signs a different transaction (5e43… instead of 60c7…)"; then broadcast signed by Alice and Carol | | A signer rejects with a note | ✅ `WARNING`, coins released, "rejected by a signer: Vendor not on the approved list" | | 0.8 BTC with a 0.5 BTC limit; a mainnet address on regtest | ✅ Rejected by policy before any coins were reserved | | `max_fee_rate=5` with a 10 sat/vB estimate | ✅ Deferred, coins released | | 3 BTC from a 1.75 BTC wallet | ✅ Failed with "Bitcoin Core could not build the transaction: Insufficient funds", nothing locked | | Webhook request with `'); DROP TABLE spend_requests; --` in the memo, plus a second request while it waits | ✅ Memo stored verbatim; the two requests reserved different coins; signed by Bob and Carol, broadcast | | Signing window expires (test copy with a 15 s window) | ✅ Failed, coins released, "the signing window expired before enough signatures arrived" | | Bitcoin node stopped | ✅ Fails at `node_check` after 3 attempts: "Connect to http://127.0.0.1:18443 failed: Connection refused" | The first run, from request to broadcast: ## Notes - Coin locks from `lockUnspents` live in the node's memory, so they are cleared if bitcoind restarts while a request is waiting. That is safe: the next PSBT simply selects again. - If **Validate Blueprint Tags** is red: it checks every file in `flows/`, and `docker-image-size-regression-guard.yaml` and `llm-evaluation-regression.yaml` in main use tags outside the allowed list. This blueprint uses `Business, Infrastructure`.

author: aldoruizluna
body:
Lane **P6-JOINT**, PR 3, phase 6c. `--collision` is no longer a stub: the phase-4 lanes' scratch clash probes are promoted into the keystone. These were P4-ASM2's render probe and P4-AUTH-E's `authe_probe_clash.py`, both OCCT booleans.

## What it does (ASM-1 §3.7, package 0.9.0)

- **The bodies.** Each component becomes a solid:
  - a cartridge is **rendered** at the assembly's parameters (full injection, every part the component produces), through the sandboxed execution `check --render` uses;
  - a standard part is its catalog **`envelope`**;
  - an external design is its declared **`envelope`**, an original proxy body (D3).
- **The poses.** The solids are placed at **home, every limit and every Halton sample** of the §9 sweep.
- **The test.** Pairs whose bounding boxes overlap are intersected (OCCT common), once per relative placement. A pair that does not move against itself costs one boolean for the whole sweep.
- **The verdict.**
  - An undeclared overlap above **1 mm³** (a convention: the phase-4 probes' bar) is a `collision` error, naming the pair, its worst volume, its pose and how many poses it occurs at.
  - `allowed_overlaps: [{a, b, max_mm3, reason}]` declares designed interference.
  - `allowed-overlap-unused` and `collision-unchecked` are warnings; `allowed-overlap` is an error.
  - `report.collision` is `checked`, `partial` or `unavailable`, never a silent pass.
- **Catalog `envelope`** (rule 10): boxes and cylinders, each naming the **cited `dimensions`** it is built from.
  - 16 entries have one. `mgn12h-carriage` gains the cited `rail_width` (HIWIN WR 12), so its envelope leaves the rail channel open.
  - Entries without a cited bound are listed in docs/STANDARD_PARTS.md with the missing fact, and stay unchecked: microswitch body height, T-nut height, whether the 2207's 33.1 includes the shaft, the 5" frame class, the camera body position, the SMA jack.

## Exit criteria

| Criterion | Evidence |
|---|---|
| **Negative controls fail** | A slider driven into a stop fails at `slide@upper` with exactly 2000 mm³. An undeclared overlap fails, and an overlap above its allowance fails. Tests: `tests/test_assembly_collision.py`. |
| **A rendered cartridge against a catalog envelope** | The test bracket and a NEMA 17: the shaft through a hole-less test plate measures π·2.5²·5 = 98.17 mm³. |
| **A and B pass with `--collision`** | On solid main 76dee64 with this keystone. A: 29 components, 7.3 s, nine designed overlaps declared (in the companion solid PR). B: 16 components, 2.9 s. Both are `partial`, with their body-less components named. |
| **The probe numbers reproduce** | The roller-bracket key in the slot measures 208.8 mm³, and the M5 axle in the Ø4.2 pilot 57.8 mm³. These match P4-ASM2 and P4-AUTH-E. |

The companion solid PR turns on `--collision` in the assemblies job (with the geometry extra and a kernel import guard) and declares A's overlaps. It waits for the pin.

**Digest move (ordinary).** Fixture A goes from `35867ffd…` to `8172f814…` through catalog digests. `PROJECTION_VERSION` stays 2.

## Gates (local)

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| ruff | clean |
| `pytest -ra` | 1690 passed, 2 skipped. The two former stub tests now assert `partial` and `unavailable`. |
| goldens | projection and pose: `drifted=0` |
| reader counts | `--check` ok |
| vocab | `parts=22 failures=0` |

author: scarmonac
body:
Closes #150

## Qué cambia

- **`src/sw.ts`**: `skipWaiting: true` → `false`. El SW nuevo queda en *waiting*. Serwist ya atiende el mensaje `{ type: "SKIP_WAITING" }` cuando `skipWaiting` es `false` (llama a `self.skipWaiting()`). Se mantiene `clientsClaim: true` para que el SW activado tome las pestañas abiertas y dispare `controllerchange`.
- **`src/lib/pwa/actualizacion.ts`** (nuevo, sin React): `vigilarActualizaciones()` escucha el registro y devuelve `actualizar()` y `detener()`.
  - Hay versión nueva cuando existen un SW en espera y uno activo (`hayVersionEsperando`). Se revisa al registrar (`registration.waiting`) y durante el uso (`updatefound` y después `statechange` → `installed`). En la primera instalación no hay SW activo, así que no sale el aviso.
  - Al volver a la app, `visibilitychange` llama a `registration.update()` si pasaron **15 minutos** desde la última revisión. Registrar ya cuenta como revisión. Si falla por falta de señal, no pasa nada.
  - **Actualizar**: espera a que termine una subida de la cola sin señal que esté a medias (máximo 10 s), manda `SKIP_WAITING` y, con `controllerchange`, recarga **una sola vez** (`crearRecargaUnica`).
  - **Otras pestañas**: cuando otra pestaña activa la versión nueva, esta no se recarga sola, porque podría haber un formulario a medio llenar. Muestra el mismo aviso y su botón solo recarga.
- **`src/lib/sin-senal/subir.ts`**: nueva `esperarSubidaEnCurso()`. Termina cuando no queda ninguna subida a medias en la página.
- **`AvisoActualizacion`** (`src/components/pwa/aviso-actualizacion.tsx`): tarjeta compacta con "Hay una versión nueva de Pura Vida Split." y los botones **Más tarde** (fantasma) y **Actualizar** (primario: índigo en claro, índigo claro con texto azul oscuro en oscuro).
  - Va **arriba**, `sticky top-0` y dentro del flujo, antes del contenido. Empuja la página en vez de taparla, así que no choca con la barra flotante de #148 ni con los avisos cortos (que van abajo).
  - `role="status"` y los botones se alcanzan con Tab (son lo primero que se enfoca).
  - Entrada con `animate-aviso-entrar` (200 ms). Con `prefers-reduced-motion` dura 0 por los tokens.
  - El aviso solo se monta mientras es visible. Una región `status` vacía en todas las páginas rompería los `getByRole("status")` estrictos de las e2e (invitaciones, borrar cuenta).
- **`RegistrarServiceWorker`**: registra el SW igual que antes y muestra el aviso. "Más tarde" lo esconde hasta la próxima visita, es decir, la próxima carga de la app. En `pnpm dev` no hay SW (se quitan los que hubiera), así que no aparece nada. En `src/app/layout.tsx` el componente pasa a ir antes de `{children}`.

Sin cambios de base. No se toca `supabase/`.

### La cola offline (#48)

La cola vive en IndexedDB (`pura-vida-split-sin-senal`). Activar un SW nuevo no la toca: Serwist solo limpia sus cachés de precache viejos. Un gasto sale de la cola solo cuando el servidor confirma, y el servidor usa `clientId` como clave de idempotencia, así que una recarga a mitad de un envío no pierde ni duplica nada. Igual, antes de activar se espera a que termine la subida en curso, para no cortarla. Background Sync va atado al registro y no al SW, así que sigue igual con la versión nueva.

## Contraste (WCAG 2.2 AA)

| Combinación | Razón |
| --- | --- |
| "Actualizar" claro: blanco sobre índigo | 6.29:1 |
| "Actualizar" oscuro: azul oscuro sobre índigo claro | 5.88:1 |
| "Más tarde" claro: índigo sobre blanco | 6.29:1 |
| "Más tarde" oscuro: índigo claro sobre superficie `#1D1D4D` | 5.17:1 |
| Texto claro: azul oscuro sobre blanco | 17.9:1 |
| Texto oscuro: crema sobre `#1D1D4D` | 14.8:1 |

## Cómo se probó

- `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm format:check` y `pnpm test` en verde (51 archivos, 690 pruebas). Pruebas nuevas:
  - `src/lib/pwa/actualizacion.test.ts`, con objetos falsos de `EventTarget`:
    - aviso al registrar con un SW en espera, y durante el uso;
    - nada en la primera instalación ni mientras se instala;
    - `controllerchange` de otra pestaña pasa a `activa`;
    - el mínimo de minutos de `visibilitychange` (también con fast-check);
    - `SKIP_WAITING` y una sola recarga aunque `controllerchange` llegue dos veces;
    - se espera la subida de la cola, con límite si queda trabada y aunque falle;
    - `detener()` quita los oyentes.
  - `cola.test.ts`: `esperarSubidaEnCurso()` espera la subida a medias, y lo que no subió sigue en la cola.
- `pnpm build-storybook` + `pnpm test:storybook` en verde: 156 pruebas. Incluyen axe en claro y oscuro para las historias nuevas `PWA/Aviso de versión nueva` (Visible, Cerrado), los 44 px y una prueba de teclado nueva (`role="status"` con el texto y Tab → Más tarde → Actualizar).
- **Flujo real con `pnpm build` y `pnpm start`** (Chromium de Playwright, 390 × 844, página `/sin-conexion`):
  1. Primera instalación: el SW se activa solo y **no** sale el aviso. No hay ninguna región `status`.
  2. Se guarda un gasto de prueba en la cola de IndexedDB y se abre una segunda pestaña.
  3. Se cambia `public/sw.js` (versión 2) y se llama a `registration.update()`. Queda `waiting=installed` y el aviso sale en **las dos pestañas**.
  4. En la pestaña 1, "Actualizar": **1 recarga**, `waiting=null`, el aviso desaparece y la cola sigue con el gasto ("Birras en el Lagarto").
  5. La pestaña 2 **no** recargó sola y muestra el aviso. Al tocar "Actualizar" recarga 1 vez.
  6. Versión 3: una pestaña nueva que carga con el SW ya en espera muestra el aviso. "Más tarde" lo esconde y al recargar vuelve a salir.
- No se puede esperar 15 minutos en la prueba real, así que el camino de `visibilitychange` se cubre con la prueba unitaria.
- Las e2e no corren en este entorno (Turnstile); las corre el CI. La de PWA (`pwa.telefono.spec.ts`) espera `serviceWorker.ready` en la primera instalación, y eso no cambia.
