author: vasanthamana
body:
## Intent Install a modern bash on this laptop with Homebrew. That was the immediate remedy chosen for a fault found on 5 Oct 2026 after upstream firstmate was merged into this copy; the recommendation it was chosen from was "install bash, followed by a proper fix sent through the normal PR route so the next macOS user does not hit it". This task is that proper fix. The fault: on macOS's built-in /bin/bash 3.2.57, `bin/fm-spawn.sh` launched a worker and then failed with "backlog item could not be moved to In flight (bin/fm-timeout-lib.sh: line 224: BASHPID: unbound variable)", removed the task's record, and left the worker's window and local copy to close by hand. Line 224 is `[ "$owner" != "$BASHPID" ] || owner=$PPID` inside `fm_exec_timed`; bash 3.2 has no `BASHPID`, so under `set -u` the function dies. `bin/fm-backlog-transition-lib.sh:347` runs `tasks-axi` through `fm_exec_timed`, so every backlog transition is affected - spawn's move to In flight and, by the same path, cleanup's close. Other scripts already write `${BASHPID:-$$}`. The original project (kunchenguid/firstmate) has the same line, and `bin/fm-wake-lib.sh` already branches on `BASH_VERSINFO`, so bash 3.2 is meant to work. ## What Changed - `fm_exec_timed` in `bin/fm-timeout-lib.sh` no longer reads `$BASHPID` directly, which is unset on stock macOS bash 3.2 and aborted under `set -u` ("BASHPID: unbound variable"). It now uses `${BASHPID:-...}` and, when `BASHPID` is missing, recovers the current shell's real pid by exec'ing a throwaway `sh` and reading its `$PPID`. The owner-pid logic is the same as on bash 4+: a subshell keeps the script as owner, and the main shell falls back to its parent. - `tests/fm-timeout-lib.test.sh` adds cases that run the production library under `/bin/bash` when it is older than bash 4. They cover a bounded command called from the main shell and from a subshell, passing through output and exit status, and the subshell-owner behavior. The cases print a skip message on hosts where `/bin/bash` is not bash 3.x. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The fix only changes how fm_exec_timed obtains its own pid when BASHPID is unset. Bash 4+ takes the same path as before. The bash 3.2 fallback gives the same value as BASHPID, and the new tests exercise it behaviorally. ## Testing I ran the timeout-library test file on the real macOS /bin/bash 3.2.57. It passes, including new regressions for main-shell and subshell calls, owner-death handling, and a backlog transition that bounds tasks-axi. I also called the base-commit library directly under `set -u`, and it fails with "BASHPID: unbound variable" as reported. The fixed library runs the same call cleanly. I did not run bin/fm-spawn.sh or cleanup end to end, and I did not run the full suite. - Live validation: ✅ go - 3 of 3 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Reproduce the fault: old fm_exec_timed on bash 3.2 under set -u | ✅ pass | live | The base-commit lib run under /bin/bash prints 'line 224: BASHPID: unbound variable' | | Fixed fm_exec_timed runs a bounded command on bash 3.2 from the main shell | ✅ pass | live | direct-bash32.txt shows main-ok | | Fixed fm_exec_timed on bash 3.2 from a subshell, owner-death handling, and a backlog transition bounding tasks-axi | ✅ pass | live | timeout-lib-test.txt: the four bash 3.2 regression cases pass on the real /bin/bash |

author: mkerian10
body:
The module system is about to carry the protocol thesis (the protocol is the module), and it currently rests on four defects and two undecided semantics. One RFC so the library wave builds on decided ground.

The spine: three mechanisms, three jurisdictions — the solver guards what values can be (at every site in every module, and provably at decode), field privacy guards where values come from (opt-in `priv`, default public; provenance for evidence types falls out since a literal must name every field), fencing guards what values may do. Entities speak in messages, with a steelman-earned carve-out: external reads of scalar-shaped fields stay legal, lowered through the read lock; reference-shaped fields go through methods; writes stay banned.

Also: #421 reframed as a grammar fix sequenced with evidence-field migration (so the File-forgery door never opens), the decode coverage theorem + an analyze perception report (the systematic fix for the silent-skip family), cycle rejection ratified as doctrine (library layering is a DAG), the #413/#437 resolution fixes, and minimal named re-exports (`pub import fs.SyncError`).

Explicitly rejected: a sealed/evidence class marker — hiding and correctness are separate concerns, and contracts will be common on ordinary data.

Five decisions at the end (two already ratified in discussion, recorded). Doc-only.

body:
New tests spanning multiple source campaigns could lose a current positive witness when a newer receipt classified the same node differently in another source context. Hosts can now declare exact node-to-required-source bindings, and review checks each context against original, independently native-validated receipts with current manifest/source/test/runner hashes. A newer failed or partial attempt blocks historical fallback within its context; unrelated positive evidence cannot satisfy a missing required source.

Unwaived new tests also require complete automatic PASS evidence: a successful baseline, no survivors/timeouts/errors/unviable outcomes, complete kill attribution, and current PASS test-value data. Diagnostics preserve original receipt references and hashes. The native receipt validators, canonical verifier output, eleven hashed runner components, and existing external invariant waiver rules are unchanged.

Validation: nine contextual regressions plus 27 existing consumer/policy contracts pass; full `make local-check` and `make local-verify` pass on commit 612432cb2aa0a9122114deef11d5a22a7a40d56a. author: xuzhenkai818-design
body:
## 这个 PR 做什么

`TimmVisionTransformer` 遇到 CNN 时的报错是：

> `...the framework needs a token sequence [B, N, D]. Use the **timm_cnn** encoder for a convolutional backbone.`

**但 `timm_cnn` 没有注册。** 这个 PR 补上它：一个普通的 ImageNet ResNet（timm），不依赖 torchxrayvision。

## 刻意贴着 `XRayVisionDenseNet` 写

没有另立一套约定：

- 同样的 `[B, C, h, w]` → `[B, h*w, D]` 展平 + 前置摘要 token（让 `pooling="cls"` 看到图像而不是常数）
- 同样的 `project_to`，让 CNN 和 ViT 能对齐到同一个融合宽度
- 同样的 `train()` 覆写，把冻结的 backbone 钉在 eval

最后一条对**对照本身**有意义，不只是整洁：BatchNorm 在训练模式下用 batch 统计量归一化并持续更新 running 估计，**不受 `requires_grad` 影响**；而 ViT 全是 LayerNorm，是真的冻住。不加守卫的话，"冻结的 ResNet"会悄悄变成另一个特征提取器，两臂的 "frozen" 就不是同一个意思。

## 改动范围

**只碰一个既有文件**：`encoders.py`（+106 行，类 + builder）。

`tests/test_encoders.py` **一行未动** —— 它自己的测试归它的作者管。我的测试放在新文件 `tests/test_encoders_resnet.py`。

这样也顺带解决了可运行性：`test_encoders.py` 里第 263 行有一句**模块级**的 `pytest.importorskip("torchxrayvision")`，在没有 torchxrayvision 的机器上会跳过**整个文件**（包括写在它前面的测试）。把新测试放在独立文件里，它们就不会被牵连。

> 那个 `importorskip` 是个真实的收集缺陷，但它该由文件作者决定怎么改。我单独提出来，不在这个 PR 里顺手改。

## 配置

`configs/icu/metra_resnet.json` **逐字段镜像** `configs/icu/metra_joint.json`，只改 `image_encoder`：

| | `metra_joint` | `metra_resnet` |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `timm_vit` | `timm_resnet` |
| backbone | `vit_base_patch16_224` | `resnet18` |
| `project_to` | 64 | 64 |
| image token 数 | 197 | 50 |

两个 backbone 都投到同样的 64 宽融合，因此两臂**参数量也基本对齐**。

**消不掉的残余差异**：50 个 image token（7×7 + 摘要）vs 197 个（14×14 patch + CLS）。这是 CNN 网格与 ViT patch 网格的固有差异，报告里必须写明，不能说"只差 backbone"。

## 验证

在目标机器上（Python 3.11、torch 2.5.1+cu121、timm 1.0.30）：

```
全套        149 passed, 1 skipped
新模块      11 passed
```

新模块里每个编码器都用 `pretrained=False` 构造，不触网。

## 数据合规

只提交代码与配置，没有 `index.csv`／`predictions.csv`／`clinical_features.csv`／checkpoint。

---

## 附带的说明（不是本 PR 的改动）

这个 PR 还带了一份 `benchmark-evaluation/RESULTS_icu_frozen_backbones.md`，是**之前一轮真实数据运行**的记录（那时 fusion 宽 768、无缓存、无增强）：

```
ViT-B/16 冻结     test AUROC 0.7045
ResNet-18 冻结    test AUROC 0.6250
配对 bootstrap    ΔAUROC = +0.080  95% CI [−0.442, +0.599]  P(Δ>0) = 0.612
```

**测不出差异。** 文档开头已标明它来自被取代的配置，并列出不能由此得出的结论（尤其：训练脚本的 `val_auroc` 不是结果 —— ViT 验证集 0.839、测试集 0.705）。

如果这份文档不该放在这个 PR 里，我可以拆出去。它的主要价值是实证了为什么需要交叉验证：实测 CI 宽达 [−0.44, +0.60]。

author: bnimit
body:
VRT has never been able to pass on a pull request from a fork. The latest example is #809, whose unit CI passes while VRT fails without a single changed screenshot.

## Why fork PRs fail

#803 fixed *which code* a fork PR checks out. Everything after the checkout still assumed a same-repo PR:

1. **Baselines were read from the fork.** `reg-publish-github-plugin` infers its repository from `origin`, and on a fork checkout that's the fork. It asked `zigzagdev/resium` for the `reg-snapshots` release (404) and fell back to reporting every screenshot as *new*.
2. **The baseline key came from the fork's stale `main`.** `reg-keygen-git-hash-plugin` picks the baseline from merge-bases with `origin/*`, which on a fork checkout are the fork's branches. For #809 it chose `ca777713` (v1.25.0), even though the branch had just been updated to current `main`.
3. **Publishing can't work.** `reg-suit run` always publishes a snapshot, and fork PRs get a read-only `GITHUB_TOKEN`, so creating the release returned 403 and failed the job. Repository variables aren't exposed to fork runs either, so `reg-notify-github-plugin` can't initialize (it decodes `REG_NOTIFY_CLIENT_ID`).

## Fix

- **`regconfig.json`:** `repository: "reearth/resium"`, so snapshots always come from the base repo.
- **Fork PRs only, before capture:** delete the fork's remote-tracking refs, fetch the base repo's branch as `origin/<base>`, and use a `pr-<number>` local branch. The name matters: reg-keygen ignores any branch whose name ends with the current branch's name, so a fork branch called `main` (the common case, and the original #803 trigger) would hide `origin/main`.
- **Fork PRs only, comparison:** `reg-suit sync-expected` + `reg-suit compare`, using a temporary copy of the config without the notifier. The step fails only on **changed** screenshots (new or deleted ones are reported but don't fail). The HTML report is in the existing `reg-report` artifact.

Same-repo PRs and pushes to `main` take the existing `reg-suit run` path unchanged.

## Verification

Simulated locally against #809's real fork branch: cloned `zigzagdev/resium` at the PR head, then applied the new steps and ran the comparison step's script extracted verbatim from the workflow.

- The baseline key now resolves to `e75965db` (current `main`), not `ca777713`.
- The baseline downloads from `reearth/resium` and the comparison runs. Five screenshots match. One, the "CESIUM ion" logo text in `geojsonprimitive--default`, differs because of macOS-vs-Linux font rendering; in CI both sides are Linux-rendered. The gate correctly failed on that change, which shows the failure path works.

This PR is same-repo, so its own VRT exercises only the unchanged path plus the `repository` setting. The fork path takes effect for a fork PR once this is on `main` and the PR's branch is updated; #809 will be the first real run.

## Purpose
Clean-room assimilation of Unfenced.ai's publicly documented browser-agent capability surface into Magnanimous AI without making Unfenced a runtime dependency or copying proprietary implementation.

## What this adds
- 25 provider-neutral Unfenced benchmark capability contracts with official-source provenance.
- Full-brain manifest integration and capability-research visibility.
- A first-class `native-web-browser` realization target mapped to the existing Magnanimous Native Web runtime.
- Tamper-evident per-device browser-task receipts wired into the real Local Bridge completion path.
- Owner-only receipt retrieval and chain-verification routes.
- Optional HMAC-SHA-256 receipt signing through the `MAGNANIMOUS_RECEIPT_SIGNING_KEY` secret binding; unsigned state is reported truthfully when the key is absent.
- Regression locks proving the benchmark maps to real Magnanimous native/hybrid execution surfaces.
- Documentation of public Unfenced patterns and exact Magnanimous overlap/gaps.

## Existing Magnanimous capabilities reused
- Chromium-based search and JavaScript-rendered fetch.
- Batch fetch and source-backed research.
- Multi-step browser read/action flows.
- Persistent browser sessions and local profiles.
- Manual visible profile login, screenshots, monitoring and webhooks.
- Confirmation-gated page actions and private/local target blocking.

## Truth boundaries preserved
- No Unfenced source code, hidden prompts, anti-bot internals, credentials, private browser infrastructure, datasets, or residential proxy supply chain are copied.
- Magnanimous does not claim an owned residential/geo proxy fleet.
- Remote browser tasks still refuse password/secret filling; model-invisible vault-to-browser injection remains a target contract until a separately verified safe local vault path exists.
- Hash-chained browser receipts are live in the branch; keyed signing only becomes active when the signing secret is actually configured.

author: isaquesr
body: ## Summary This PR adds the v2 prompts the user approved after the Mac trials, and raises the vision adapter's `max-tokens` default from 512 to 1024. No contracts, schemas or configs change. **Canonical M08 runs must use v2.** The earlier trial runs (`trial-football-01`, `trial-all-02`) used `vision-frame-v1` and `context-reasoning-v1` and are not comparable with canonical results. `promptVersion` in ContextEvent provenance now reads `context-reasoning-v2`. The vision prompt version is recorded in code and the README, because the observation provenance contract has no prompt field. ## Changes ### `vision-frame-v2` (`internal/vision/llamamtmd`) - **Compact JSON.** A hand-written GBNF grammar (`--grammar`) replaces `--json-schema`. llama.cpp's grammar derived from a JSON schema allows line breaks and indentation, and the trials showed the model pretty-printing (about 30 tokens per detection). The new grammar admits only compact JSON. - **Cap.** At most 12 detections per frame, enforced by both the grammar and the parser (previously `maxItems` 24). - **Repetition.** Later frames of a window are told which `ENTITY`, `BRAND` and `TEXT` values an earlier frame already reported, so scoreboards and boards are not repeated unless they change (`FramePrompt`). The prompt also asks the model to skip running clocks and to list each item only once. - **Brands.** The prompt asks for brands and sponsors as `BRAND`, never `TEXT`. - **Label form.** Values for `OBJECT`, `TOPIC`, `SCENE` and `ACTION` must be lowercase snake_case (grammar plus parser), and string lengths are bounded. `ENTITY`, `BRAND` and `TEXT` stay verbatim; this is perception evidence. - **Default `max-tokens`:** 512 → 1024. ### `context-reasoning-v2` (`internal/context/llamacpp`) - **Sources.** The reasoner sees the window as keyed sources: `a1…` for transcripts, `v1…` for frames with description and detections. Observation IDs and **perception confidences are not sent**, so a perception score cannot be copied. The M07 override §12 sentence that confidences are uncalibrated and not probabilities stays in the prompt. - **Labels.** Topics, objects and brands must be English lowercase snake_case (schema `pattern` plus parser). Entity values keep proper names as written, except countries and national teams, which use their English name (Germany, Serbia). - **Entity types.** Restricted to the closed list in `ANNOTATION-GUIDELINES` v1.0 (`PERSON`, `SPORTS_TEAM`, `ORGANIZATION`, `PLACE`, `EVENT`), via the schema `enum` and the parser. This needs no schema change: ContextEvent v1 allows any non-blank entity type, and the adapter only narrows it. - **Per-item citations.** Every item must list its `sources` (the schema enum is the window's keys). A candidate's evidence is the **union of its items' sources**, so a label read from a frame always brings that frame into the event's evidence, alongside the transcript when the label is heard as well. The core still grounds every candidate. - **Confidence.** C1-A still applies: every item has its own stated 0–1 confidence, required and uncalibrated. The prompt asks for each item to be judged on its own, not with one uniform value. - **Strictness.** Unknown source keys, open entity types, non-snake labels, items without sources, events without items and v1-shaped answers (`evidence` field) are all rejected. ### Docs The README and both package docs describe v2. The README states that canonical runs must use v2. ## Points to note - **Country names.** "Countries and national teams in English" goes slightly beyond the guidelines' "proper names keep their original spelling". The guidelines' examples are Palmeiras and Maracanã, which have no English form. If you agree, `dataset/ANNOTATION-GUIDELINES.md` should state the same rule before annotation is finalized. - **No compact grammar for the reasoner.** It still uses a JSON schema (with `pattern` and `enum`), so its output may be indented. A hand-written per-window grammar would save more tokens, as an optional follow-up. - **Trial-run labels.** Earlier v1 results contain labels such as "soccer match", "UEFA NATIONS LEAGUE" and "Sérvia". The v2 schema now rejects all three. ## Tests / Verification With `GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.25.0`: - `gofmt -l .` is empty. - `go vet ./...` and `go vet -tags integration ./...` pass. - `go test ./...` and `go test -race ./...` pass. `bash -n` passes on the scripts. New and updated tests: - **Vision:** grammar and prompt cover every contract type; the cap appears in the grammar; `FramePrompt` lists repeated values once, quoted; the parser rejects more than 12 detections and non-snake values; the default is `-n 1024`; the per-frame arguments carry the dynamic prompt and `--grammar`. - **Reasoner:** - The exact v2 sources document has no IDs and no confidences. - The schema carries the key enum, the entity-type enum and the label pattern. - Evidence is the union of item sources, in order, and grounds in the core. - The rejection cases above are covered. ### VM smoke run (3B models, CPU) The setup: `scripts/m08-run.sh --experiments E04 --no-vod`, live 1×, on the synthetic `poc-smoke` clip. - Tools: llama.cpp `b11295` and whisper.cpp `v1.9.4`. - Models: Qwen2.5-VL-3B Q4_K_M, Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct Q4_K_M and whisper `small`. Results: - **4 of 4 windows OK, 0 failures.** The v1 smoke on the same clip lost 1 of 4 E04 windows to duplicate-label rejections. - **The grammar parses.** Vision answers are single-line compact JSON. Labels come out in English (`TOPIC football` for on-screen "FUTEBOL"; v1 gave `"FUTEBOL"`). - **Events.** Every topic is `football`. Entity types are all from the closed list. The two speech windows cite the transcript and both frames (A1V2); the silent windows cite the frames only. - **Metrics:** `schemaCompliance` 1, `evidenceTraceability` 1, `contextStability` 0.53 (the v1 smoke had 0.38). - **Quality limits of the 3B models, as expected.** - Entity values are poor: `SPORTS_TEAM "time a"` and `"time vermelho"` from a garbled transcript, `PERSON "eu"`, `SPORTS_TEAM "football"`. - Confidences are no longer copied from perception, but they are still high and uniform (0.9–1). - The 3B VLM reported only `TOPIC football` per frame and missed the scoreboard text. - The 7B models on the Mac are what count. ### Same frame, same VM: v1 vs v2 One frame, `llama-mtmd-cli` run directly with the 3B model: | Prompt / constraint | Total | Image encode | Output | |---|---|---|---| | v1 prompt + `--json-schema` | 28.6 s | 13.6 s | 190 chars, pretty-printed, `"FUTEBOL"` | | **v2 prompt + grammar** | **26.6 s** | 13.5 s | 138 chars, compact, `"football"` | | v2 grammar without length bounds | 25.8 s | 12.6 s | identical answer | The bounded repetitions cost under 1 s. On this CPU, image encoding dominates. On the Mac (Metal), generation dominated v1, so the compact output and the cap should save proportionally more there. The higher per-frame time in the smoke run (about 29 s vs about 22 s in the earlier v1 smoke) comes from this different VM; the same-frame comparison above shows no regression.

This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Type | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| [go.opentelemetry.io/otel](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go) | require | minor | `v1.46.0` → `v1.47.0` |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go (go.opentelemetry.io/otel)</summary>

### [`v1.47.0`](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/releases/tag/v1.47.0): /v0.69.0/v0.23.0/v0.1.0

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/compare/v1.46.0...v1.47.0)

This release contains the first stable release of the OpenTelemetry Go Logs API and SDK.
Our project stability guarantees now apply to the following modules:

- `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/log`
- `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log`

See our [versioning policy](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/blob/main/VERSIONING.md) for more information about these stability guarantees.

##### Added

- Add `String` method for `KeyValue` type in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/attribute`. ([#​8205](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8205))
- Add `String` method for `Set` type in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/attribute`. ([#​8347](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8347))
- Add `WithMaxExportBatchSize` to `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric` to configure the maximum export batch size for `PeriodicReader`. ([#​8960](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8960))
- Add `WithAttributeValueDepthLimit`, `DefaultAttributeValueDepthLimit`, and `SpanLimits.AttributeValueDepthLimit` in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace` to configure the maximum depth of span, event, link, and instrumentation scope attribute values. ([#​8938](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8938))
- Add `WithAttributeValueDepthLimit` in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log` to configure the maximum depth of log record and instrumentation scope attribute values. ([#​8938](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8938))
- Add `WithMaxResponseSize` to `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracehttp`,
  `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlpmetric/otlpmetrichttp`, and
  `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlplog/otlploghttp`. ([#​8941](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8941))
- Add experimental `ProbabilitySampler` in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace/x` that conforms to the [OpenTelemetry specification's threshold-based sampling algorithm](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/trace/sdk/#probabilitysampler). ([#​8123](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8123))
- Add experimental `*Binder` extension interfaces in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/metric/x` for instruments that support binding attributes ahead of time. ([#​8760](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8760))
- Add the experimental `Finisher` synchronous metric instrument extension interface to `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/metric/x`. ([#​8906](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8906))

##### Changed

- Use the [OpenTelemetry Attribute Collection representation for non-OTLP protocols](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/common/#attribute-collection-representation-for-non-otlp) for metric data diffs in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric/metricdata/metricdatatest`. ([#​8993](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8993))
- Apply a maximum depth of 64 by default to span, event, link, log record, and instrumentation scope attribute values in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace` and `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log`. ([#​8938](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8938))
- Reduce allocations when applying attribute value length limits in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace` and `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log` by rebuilding composite values only when truncation is needed. ([#​8912](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8912))
- Decode `traceparent` using a hex lookup table in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/propagation`, which rejects the specification-disallowed upper-case characters without a separate scan of the header. ([#​8739](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8739))
- Decode all characters at constant indices in `TraceIDFromHex` and `SpanIDFromHex` in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace` to eliminate bounds checks. ([#​8740](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8740))

##### Fixed

- Count valid U+FFFD replacement characters toward attribute value length limits in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace`, `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace`, and `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log`.
- Truncate string attribute values to empty strings when the configured length limit is zero, including malformed UTF-8, in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace`, `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace`, and `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log`. ([#​9054](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/9054))
- Fix a data race in `NewPeriodicReader` where `r.inst` was assigned after the background goroutine was launched in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric`. ([#​9028](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/9028))
- Prevent precision loss for large `int64` values in `Sum`, `Histogram`, and `ExponentialHistogram` aggregations in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric`. ([#​8981](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8981))
- Ensure `grpc.DialOption` values passed via `WithDialOption` take precedence over conflicting internally-computed defaults in
  `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlplog/otlploggrpc`,
  `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlpmetric/otlpmetricgrpc`, and
  `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracegrpc`. ([#​8805](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8805), [#​8834](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8834), [#​8836](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8836))
- Treat overflowing `OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL` and `OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_TIMEOUT` values as invalid in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric`. ([#​8800](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8800))
- Prevent a panic in `NewFixedSizeReservoir` and `FixedSizeReservoirProvider` when given a negative size in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric/exemplar`; negative sizes are now clamped to zero, consistent with a size of zero. ([#​8832](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8832))
- Preserve exponential histogram `ZeroThreshold` during OTLP metric export in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlpmetric`. ([#​8801](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8801))
- Ensure metric helpers in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/semconv/v1.32.0`, `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/semconv/v1.33.0`, and `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/semconv/v1.34.0` record measurements only once when no attributes are provided. ([#​8849](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8849))
- Treat empty `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER` and `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG` values as unset in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace`. ([#​8873](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8873))

author: geeihadagoodtime
body:
## Customer-visible correction
Rapid Repeat or Shuffle clicks previously sent concurrent writes. An older failure could erase the newest pending choice, and failed requests could leave a state the server never saved.

Serialize each control's writes independently while preserving responsive optimistic choices. Restore confirmed/server-reported state on failure, preserve newer intent during an older server echo, handle same-render clicks, allow retry, and drop queued writes after unmount. Existing rating and principal-boundary protections remain.

## Exact source and evidence
- Base: e882490494bbc0208664d2bb10dd54f4260612ba
- Source-only commit: b2e00b55bbe82db8fad1fd8dc19d49f79e99e9ca
- Final bound head: b078fc3147dae1ddabe4f7d6e5b349c195bb1fcf
- Reviewed patch SHA256: cd844b8c923dcf3765de781533718d4fc16d9f91574599dc8ab0729823e0e262
- Original SmartDisplay baseline: 96 passed; four new negative controls fail on original production bytes.
- Corrected SmartDisplay: 123 passed, including 27 added cases covering all eight three-write outcome permutations for both controls, retry, pending server echo, rapid clicks, independent queues and unmount. Independently replayed 123/123 with no blocking finding.
- Complete frontend: 149 files / 1247 tests pass, zero failures/skips/errors. Production Vite build passes with upload credentials disabled. Scoped ESLint: zero errors and 11 inherited SmartDisplay warnings.
- Canonical source binding verifier: 2504 source files and 6 unchanged SBOMs, zero failures. Final Git tree preserves 2526 original leaves and changes only 3 source paths plus 2 canonical metadata files. Dependency inputs, workflows, licenses and models unchanged.

## Boundaries
Draft source publication only. Exact-head hosted checks, private composition/adoption, signed packaging and installed Repeat/Shuffle behavior remain pending. No merge, deployment, customer release, physical-audio or hardware qualification is claimed. Private adoption needs one explicit mapping for ui/react-app/src/hooks/useOrderedPreference.js and must preserve the current pin lineage.

author: khjohns
body:
Closes #168
Closes #186

## Vedtak (oppdragsgiver 05.10)

Spørsmålene ble stilt i økta og svarene ført inn i hovedplanen 3.1 under B-13:

1. Vederlag eller frist besvart når grunnlaget er avslått eller prekludert (§ 32.2): journalen og sporstatus beholder resultatet av beløpene og dagene, som subsidiært standpunkt. Brev og fullmakt sier «Prinsipalt avslått (ansvarsgrunnlaget)» med det subsidiære resultatet.
2. At hele svaret er subsidiært, **lagres ikke** i hendelsen. Det utledes av grunnlaget. Datamodellen og `hendelser.toml` er uendret.

## Hva som er endret

- **Én regel** (#186): `regler.grunnlag.er_grunnlag_subsidiaert` sier at grunnlaget er avslått, eller prekludert etter § 32.2, bare ved endring uten formell endringsordre. Speilet i TS er `erGrunnlagetSubsidiaert` og `erPrekludertEtter32_2` (`grunnlagDomain.ts`), og `forsteUnderkategori` speiler `forste_underkategori`. Regelen brukes av:
  - `approval_authority.exposure` og `calculateAuthority` (fullmakt)
  - `approval_letter.decision_summary` og `decisionSummary` (brev)
  - `SakState.er_subsidiaert_vederlag`/`_frist` og `visningsstatus_*`
  - `regler.vederlag.er_hele_vederlaget_subsidiaert`
  - `deriveVederlagDomainConfig` (`grunnlagVarsletForSent`, også i begrunnelsesteksten) og `deriveFristDomainConfig` (`erHelFristSubsidiaerPgaGrunnlag`), den siste for fristdelen av #168
- **Låsing av grunnlaget** (`timeline_service._handle_respons_grunnlag`): en eldre hendelse med `grunnlag_varslet_i_tide=false` ved EO prekluderer ikke lenger. Grunnlaget låses.
- **Basis i godkjenningspakken** får `underkategori`, i backend (`ApprovalService.basis`) og frontend (`context.svelte.ts`, `types.ts`). Mangler feltet i en eldre pakke, gjelder § 32.2 som før (konservativt).
- **Brevet** ved avslått grunnlag sier «Prinsipalt avslått (ansvarsgrunnlaget) · Subsidiært <resultat>: X kr». Et subsidiært standpunkt i svaret selv (§ 33.4, § 34.1.2) står etter som «Atter subsidiært …». `hold_tilbake` vises med tekst, ikke som kode.
- `SakState.er_subsidiaert_*` leser `grunnlag.bh_resultat`, ikke `grunnlag.status`, slik brev, fullmakt og regelmodulen gjør. Se åpent spørsmål 2.
- `REGELVERSJON` er 2 i `src/lib/domain/regelversjon.ts` og `backend/regler/__init__.py`. Fixturen `skjemaenes_nyttelast.json` er regenerert.
- Hovedplanen har en ny rad i 3.1 for vedtaket 05.10, og en datert merknad på B-13-raden om `grunnlag_varslet_i_tide` (#186).

## Sjekker

- `cd backend && pytest -q`: 2256 passed, 9 skipped, 38 xfailed.
- `npm test`: 609 passed (63 filer).
- `npm run check:error`: 0 errors.
- `ruff check backend/`: ren. `eslint` og `prettier` på endrede filer: rene.
- Nye tester:
  - `test_grunnlag_subsidiaert.py`: regelen, låsing ved EO og ved IRREG, projeksjonen, og at avslaget står mens TE oppdaterer
  - `test_approval_letter.py` og `test_approval_authority.py`: § 32.2 ved EO og IRREG, og «atter subsidiært»
  - `letter.test.ts`, `authority.test.ts`, `grunnlagDomain.test.ts`, `vederlagDomain.test.ts` og `deriveConfig.test.ts`
- **Nettleser mot den ekte saksruta (`/[prosjektId]/[sakId]`) er ikke kjørt: blokkert av #57.** `repositories/postgres/` har fortsatt ikke prosjektlageret, så `/api/projects` gir 503 under `DATALAG=postgres` (`core/container.py`). Containeren har ingen Supabase-nøkler. Samme blokkering som i #185 og #188.

## `/code-review high`

Første runde, ti funn:
- **Rettet:**
  - `grunnlagVarsletForSent` var uten avgrensning, så begrunnelsesteksten i VederlagForm kunne si § 32.2 ved EO.
  - Brevet mistet byggherrens eget standpunkt, for eksempel § 33.4; det står nå som «atter subsidiært».
  - `hold_tilbake` sto som rå kode i brevet.
  - Underkategorien ble normalisert inline fem steder; nå brukes `forsteUnderkategori`.
  - Docstringene i `sak_state` var foreldet.
- **Egne issues:**
  - #213: `overordnet_status` blir `OMFORENT` når grunnlaget har `AVSLATT_AKSEPTERT` og vederlaget er subsidiært `GODKJENT`. Kjørt mot `SakState`. Fantes før denne PR-en.
  - #214: saksvisningen (`derive.ts`, `LeftSidebar`, `*Overview`) viser «Godkjent». Filene tilhører en parallell økt.
  - #215: låsingen settes ved svaret og følger ikke en senere endret underkategori.
- **Avvist, se åpne spørsmål:** den strenge sammenlikningen av basis med eldre pakker (3), og `bh_resultat` i stedet for status (2).

Kontrollrunde, ni funn:
- **Rettet:**
  - Fallback for `total_godkjent_belop: null` i brevet.
  - Planteksten påstod at visningen var bygget.
  - § 32.2-uttrykket sto tre ganger i TS; nå `erPrekludertEtter32_2`.
  - `hold_tilbake` har samme tekst som tidslinjen.
  - Kommentaren i `sak_state` sa det motsatte av docstringene.
  - En kommentar gjentok linja under.
- **Ikke rettet, fantes før:**
  - TS og Python formaterer tall forskjellig i forhåndsvisning og PDF.
  - Den ikke-subsidiære stien skriver «Subsidiært: X» uten resultat.
  - `er_subsidiaert_*` slår ikke ut når vederlaget selv er avslått.

## Funn utenfor oppdraget

#213, #214 og #215 (etiketter `review-oppfølging`, `spor-d`).

## Åpne spørsmål

1. **«Atter subsidiært» i brevet** er ikke avgjort av oppdragsgiver. Det er valgt fordi det andre alternativet var å la byggherrens eget prinsipale standpunkt (for eksempel § 33.4-preklusjon) falle ut av brevet. Er ordlyden riktig?
2. **`er_subsidiaert_*` leser `bh_resultat`, ikke `status`.** Mens TE oppdaterer et avslått grunnlag (status `SENDT`), viser vederlaget fortsatt «Avslått pga. ansvar (subsidiært …)». Før viste det «Godkjent». Valgt fordi byggherrens standpunkt gjelder til et nytt svar, og fordi brev, fullmakt og regelmodulen allerede leser `bh_resultat`. Det samme gjelder etter `AVSLATT_AKSEPTERT`.
3. **Pakker som er laget før denne PR-en** har basis uten `underkategori` og avvises ved pakking med «Ansvarsgrunnlaget er endret». De har også regelversjon 1. Ingen reelle data, så det er ikke laget noen overgang.

author: kwuangyong
body:
## Thay đổi
Trang Quét toàn sàn chỉ mở danh sách sau khi bấm **Kích hoạt kết quả**. Nút gọi GET `/api/scan/latest` để đọc bản công bố có sẵn; không tạo job hay chạy lại engine Python. Có metadata, bộ lọc sàn/khuyến nghị/trạng thái, tìm doanh nghiệp không dấu, sắp xếp điểm và mở chi tiết mã. Đổi trang giữ kết quả; reload quay lại trạng thái chưa kích hoạt. Lỗi đọc báo để thử lại; lỗi refresh giữ bản cũ; mẫu chỉ được chọn rõ ràng khi API không hoạt động.

Toàn bộ giao diện chuyển sang nền gần đen, các mảng xanh rừng và vệt cam theo standee. Giữ **IBM Plex Mono**, bảng/popup nền đặc, chế độ sáng và bố cục điện thoại.

## Nối vòng chạy Python 2 giờ
Adapter đọc JSON từ biến môi trường `QUANTIK_SCAN_SNAPSHOT`, hỗ trợ công bố file nguyên tử và kiểm tra dữ liệu/timestamp/phạm vi. Hướng dẫn và contract: [docs/scan-snapshot.md](https://github.com/kwuangyong/QuanTik-website/blob/feature/scan-activation-brand/docs/scan-snapshot.md).

**Giới hạn:** repo chưa chứa scheduler hoặc snapshot/report của bản VPS trong ảnh. Mặc định dùng 21 mã fixture có nhãn mẫu; không giả lập 1.523 mã hoặc khuyến nghị. Cần ánh xạ kết quả Python thật theo contract trước khi dùng trên VPS. Nút hiện là bước mở giao diện; Premium cần kiểm tra tài khoản/quyền gói ở backend sau này. Chưa triển khai lên quantik.io.vn.

## Kiểm tra

- Python unittest: 7/7, gồm đọc file đã công bố không chạy engine/job, bản mới qua thay file nguyên tử, metadata không bị đổi, lỗi không fallback/lộ đường dẫn, null/false/0 và file lỗi.

Closes #4055

# Description

Adds `OTILabs_DomainIntelligence`, an observable analyzer for the [OTI Labs Domain Intelligence API](https://oti-labs.com/domain-intelligence-api). Disclosure: I run this API.

For a `domain` (or a `url`, looked up by its hostname) one request to `GET /lookup/{domain}` returns WHOIS/RDAP registration data, DNS records, the TLS certificate the domain serves, subdomains (with the live ones and their IPs) and SPF/DMARC/DKIM. - `api_app/analyzers_manager/observable_analyzers/otilabs_domain_intelligence.py`: the analyzer, with a `url` attribute for health checks, a 30 s request timeout and clear errors for rejected keys (401/403), quota (429) and other statuses.

body:
## Summary

PR 3 of 3 for end-to-end tests: the recipe importer tested for real. **Nothing is stubbed.** The page is fetched from the web, Claude cleans it up, and the import job runs in the background while the Draft box updates live.

```text
Importing a recipe from a link (spec/system/import_recipe_spec.rb)   video: import_recipe
  log in → All Recipes → Import recipe
  paste yummytoddlerfood.com/apple-oatmeal-cake → Import
  Draft box: card shows Reading… → turns Ready without a reload (Turbo Streams)
             (stops waiting as soon as it's Ready or Failed; a failure reports the card's reason)
  Review → Create recipe → "Recipe saved from your Draft box." → Apple Oatmeal Cake, Draft box empty
```

**Only runs when asked**, because it costs a Claude call and depends on the site being up:

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `bundle exec rspec` | **skipped**: "live import: set LIVE_IMPORT=1 …" |
| `LIVE_IMPORT=1 bundle exec rspec spec/system/import_recipe_spec.rb` | real import with Claude |
| `LIVE_IMPORT=1` with no Anthropic key | fails with "LIVE_IMPORT needs an Anthropic API key …" |
| add `RECORD_VIDEO=1` | also records `tmp/videos/import_recipe.webm` for the README |

**Background job:** the test env only records jobs, so this spec switches Active Job to its in-process `:async` adapter and restores it afterwards. The job runs in a background thread like it would in Sidekiq, so the live Reading… → Ready update is what's tested and recorded. When the example ends, the job runner is shut down, so a job still running finishes before the test data is rolled back.

**Why not 下厨房 too:** a 下厨房 example was dropped. 下厨房 currently serves a captcha to the importer's fetch, so the import correctly fails with "The site blocked automatic reading…". That makes it unsuitable for a test that has to pass.

## Evidence

**Real run with Claude** (owner's checkout): the Yummy Toddler Food import **passed**, including the live Reading… → Ready update.

```
$ bundle exec rspec
4 examples, 0 failures, 1 pending      (the live import, skipped)

$ LIVE_IMPORT=1 bundle exec rspec spec/system/import_recipe_spec.rb      # worktree without a key
RuntimeError: LIVE_IMPORT needs an Anthropic API key (Rails credentials or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
```

**Failure path:** with the key check disabled and the blocked 下厨房 link swapped in, the example failed after **9.7 s** instead of waiting 2 minutes, with `Import failed: xiachufang.com/recipe/107110062 …` and the card's reason.

RuboCop finds no problems.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. Tests only.

**Blast Radius:** none. The live example is skipped by default, and CI skips `spec/system/` anyway.

<!-- planwright:flight-record id=reland-570-signed-a94fef45 home=pr -->
## Summary

Supersedes #570 (https://github.com/inkatze/planwright/pull/570), which cannot merge because the repository requires signed commits and its first commit, `9bed10e1`, is unsigned. This PR carries the same 18 commits, cherry-picked in order onto current main and each signed. The change is identical apart from signing: every cherry-pick applied without a conflict, and the added and removed lines match #570's diff exactly. The only difference is surrounding context, because main gained #569 next to one of the edited spots in `scripts/orchestrate-state.sh`; #569's new remote-branch arm reads the `marker_fresh` value this change still computes, so the two compose without any edit. #570's branch is left untouched.

What the change does, as #570 described it:

Dispatch markers now live under the repository's common git directory (`.git/planwright/orchestrate/SPEC/markers`), so every worktree of one repository counts the same markers. A meta-tower running from one worktree now sees a marker a subordinate dropped from the primary checkout, and the reverse, so it no longer under-counts in-flight work and over-dispatches. Another clone has its own git directory and sees none of them, which keeps cross-clone visibility out of scope as asked.

The writer still drops a copy in the old checkout-local `specs/SPEC/.orchestrate/markers`. Readers read that location too, plus the primary checkout's copy when they run from a linked worktree. A marker written by a planwright version that only knows the old location therefore keeps counting while old and new versions run side by side.

A new helper, `scripts/orchestrate-marker-home.sh`, resolves the directory list once for the writer (`orchestrate-marker.sh`), the state engine (`orchestrate-state.sh`) and the dispatch liveness probe (`fleet-dispatch-worktree.sh`). It costs one or two git calls per use. If the shared home is unusable (it cannot be created, is not writable, or is reached through a symlink), the writer skips it with a warning and still writes the local marker, and the dispatch path now shows that warning to the operator. Checkout-local directories keep the symlink tolerance they had before.

Three adjacent gaps are recorded as observations rather than fixed here:
- the per-spec lock is still checkout-local;
- the failover and ask-state records stay per checkout;
- a leading-zero marker timestamp is read as octal.

## Verification

Signing was confirmed before any commit: `gpg.format` is `ssh`, `user.signingkey` is set, and a throwaway `git commit-tree -S` commit verified as `G`. After the cherry-picks, `git log --format='%h %G? %s'` over the branch shows `G` for all 18 commits.

Identity with #570 was checked three ways. Every cherry-pick applied without a conflict. The added and removed lines of this branch's diff against its base (`e9335871`) match #570's diff against its own base (`bffc8864`) exactly. `git range-diff` reports 17 commits equal and one, the first, differing only in a context line: main's #569 added a remote-branch arm right after the marker loop in `scripts/orchestrate-state.sh`, and that arm reads the `marker_fresh` value the loop still sets, so the two compose unedited.

The full gate (`mise run check`, under umask 022) passed every lint, check and scan task, and the change's own suites (`test-orchestrate-marker-home.sh`, `test-orchestrate-marker.sh`, `test-orchestrate-state.sh`, `test-fleet-dispatch-worktree.sh`, `test-fleet-adversarial.sh`) passed inside it. The test task failed on seven timing-ceiling tests under a load average near 40 on a shared host: `test-fleet-stop-hl.sh`, `test-fleet-stop-sj.sh`, `test-fleet-streamjson-steer.sh`, `test-fleet-throttle.sh`, `test-tower-queue-log-lock.sh`, `test-tower-queue-store-lock.sh` and `test-tower-statusline-waiting.sh`. None of them touches the changed scripts, and #570's own gate runs hit the same family. Rerun serially at a load near 10, all seven pass. **The local gate is therefore not green**; PR CI on this head is the authoritative run.

No review round ran on this PR, since the content is #570's reviewed head unchanged (see Rigor scoping). The PR is based on `e9335871`; main has since gained #573, which this branch does not include.

PR CI passed on head `d02a0bc7`: the full `check` job (run 37262816260) concluded success, and GitHub reports all 18 commits as verified signatures.

- **Flight:** `reland-570-signed-a94fef45` on `planwright/flight/reland-570-signed-a94fef45` · **Worker:** `tmux-flight-reland-570-signed-a94fef45`
- **Pending sign-off:** PS-15, PS-23, PS-33, PS-34, PS-37, PS-38, PS-41 (see the collapsed checklist)

Before: tapping the search field in the "Add your own" sheet opened the keyboard and the page slid up, cutting off the "Add your own" heading and most of the search bar. On the web build the search input also had a blue focus box inside the rounded search field.

After: the sheet sits just above the keyboard with the heading and search field fully visible, and the result list scrolls inside the sheet. The blue box is gone.

The Stats day sheet uses the same `BottomSheet` and is unaffected apart from the height cap.

Checked with the web build in a phone-sized browser in light and dark mode, with the keyboard simulated by shrinking the visual viewport. Labeled screenshots are in the project thread. Not yet tried on a real iPhone.

author: its-banana-coder
body:
Found by running Postgres's own regression suite (pg_regress runs with `DateStyle = Postgres, MDY` and `intervalstyle = postgres_verbose`, so nearly every date/time test failed on output format alone).

- **DateStyle** `SQL` / `Postgres` / `German` output for date, timestamp, timestamptz (MDY/DMY order, zone abbreviation, BC), and `SET DateStyle` normalization as in `check_datestyle` (German implies DMY, conflicts error).
- **IntervalStyle** `postgres_verbose` (`@ 1 day ago`) and `sql_standard`.
- **Startup `options`** (PGOPTIONS, `-c name=value` / `--name=value`) now applied.
- **Bug: timestamptz zone offsets** were looked up at the wrong instant (PG epoch subtracted instead of added when converting to Unix time, ~60 years off), so DST edges were wrong for current dates (e.g. 2026-03-09 in America/New_York). Fixed in output, AT TIME ZONE, casts, to_char TZ, timetz.
- **Bug: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX on an expression** re-bound the expression (cloning the catalog) for every pair of rows — minutes for 10k rows, which wedged the server. Now bound once and each key computed once.
- Expression index names follow FigureIndexColname (`t_abs_idx`, not `t_expr_idx`).
- `DROP/ALTER ... IF EXISTS` emit Postgres's "does not exist, skipping" NOTICEs; DROP of a missing table/view/sequence names its kind.

Tests: unit tests with values taken from Postgres 14; new failure-diff scenario (34/34 match against PG 14).

author: mohammadhijjawi97
body:
## What

`_delta()` in the OpenAI-compatible chat provider now raises `StreamedError`, carrying the endpoint's message, when a stream chunk carries `error`. Before, it read that chunk as an empty delta. Chat then takes its existing mid-reply failure path: an `error` frame, with the partial text kept. One line in `docs/architecture/chat.md` states this.

## Why

Once the first token has gone out, the status is already 200, so a later failure arrives inside the stream:

- llama.cpp sends `data: {"error": {"code": 500, "message": …, "type": …}}` (`format_oai_sse` in `server-context.cpp`)
- OpenRouter sends a chunk with a top-level `error` and `finish_reason: "error"`, and its streaming docs say to treat it as a failure

The provider skipped that chunk, so the stream closed as if the model had finished:

- chat stored the cut-off text as a completed reply, with no error and no Retry
- Studio passed the truncated JSON to `parse_json`, which reported "model did not return valid JSON"

Repro against a mocked endpoint (partial text, then OpenRouter's documented error chunk):

Before:

    stream ended normally; reply = 'Revenue climbed after'

After:

    reply failed: StreamedError Provider disconnected unexpectedly | partial = 'Revenue climbed after'

The error reaches the chat as `unknown`, which offers Retry, because `classify_chat_error` sorts by exception type and status, never by message text.

Fixes # (no issue)

## How to test

    cd surfsense_local/backend
    uv run pytest tests/unit/llm/providers/openai_compatible/test_streamed_error.py
    uv run pytest -m unit
    uv run ruff check .
    python scripts/check_docs.py   # from the repo root

The new tests cover llama.cpp's and OpenRouter's error shapes and a bare string error. They fail without the change ("DID NOT RAISE StreamedError"). Locally `pytest -m unit` passed (3285); the chat streaming integration tests skipped without the real embedding model.

<!-- RECURSEML_SUMMARY:START -->
## High-level PR Summary
This PR fixes a bug where the OpenAI-compatible chat provider incorrectly treated mid-stream errors from endpoints like llama.cpp and OpenRouter as successful completions. The fix introduces a `StreamedError` exception that's raised when an error chunk is detected, allowing the chat system to properly handle partial replies with an error state and offer retry options instead of treating truncated responses as complete.

⏱️ Estimated Review Time: 5-15 minutes

body:
Native profiles can install human questions without Cordis: a scoped answerer registry validates the exact root Agent and active Session, a separately selectable broker owns pending answers, and `ask_user_question` records its canonical result through the existing Program writer.

Removing the broker or answerer cancels and drains accepted requests. Submitted answers are validated without consuming an invalid request, and random branded request identities reject late or duplicate replies. Compatibility entries share the same question vocabulary and errors. This PR targets `codex/p4-native-session-authority`; it adds no default roster or SDK, ACP, terminal, or Web answering transport.

Validation:

- Normal offline installation with lifecycle hooks enabled; affected compiler faces pass after merging Session authority.
- One real NativeHost/Headless/JSONL case passes, including answers reaching the next controlled model request, durable recording, broker removal and late-answer refusal. One existing compatibility projection case also passed before integration.
- Strict native dependency and workspace constraint checks pass. Built entries import under Cordis denial; the actual CLI profile resolver separately starts and removes the real selected installers.
- Canonical type equivalence passes for 423 primary and 423 paired blocks; owned bilingual pairs and scoped lint pass. The Cordis catalog generator computes 101 artifacts with no changes. Known Session event types remain byte-identical.

The loader smoke proves manifest selection and lifecycle, not complete answering UI or SDK acceptance. No committed Session generation changes.

author: justinlindh
body:
## What

Part of #1340 (local CI per-step time). Render-checks' longest part is the sweep's screen step, which played every mock, moment and snapshot and only then the seed, in one serial line. The seed already gets a browser of its own, so it now plays alongside the mocks. Also, `--seeds abc` no longer hangs the run.

## Changes

- `blender/checks/sweep.mjs`: in a browser run (the screen step, `--browser`), the seeds start as the run starts, one at a time, each in its own browser with its time limit as before. Their rows join the report after the other rows, in the order a serial run gives, so the report is unchanged. A run that fails before the seeds' rows join ends the seed that is still playing. The engine path is unchanged.
- `--seeds` and `--seed-limit` take whole numbers only. Before this, `--seeds abc` opened a page on seed NaN that never became ready, so the run hung until its timeout; it now exits 2 naming the bad value.
- `docs/toolkit/sweep.md`: says that the seeds play alongside the mocks in a browser run.

- **Tests:** `npx vitest run tests/tools/sweep-engine.test.js`: "Tests 8 passed (8)" (gated each commit; `test:push` selects nothing for `blender/checks`).
- **Screenshots or clips:** not a visual change.
- **Gates run:** `sweep.mjs --gpu` (the CI command), on main and on the branch alternately with `HITL_NO_CHECK_CACHE=1`. All four reports are identical (9 violations; the same keys, checks and states, compared by hash).
- **Tool runs:**
  - Documented usage: the default run below, and `--screen-only` (the step itself) on main and the branch alternately. All reports are identical (1 violation, same hash).
  - Bad input: `--seeds abc`, `--seeds 1,x` and `--seed-limit 5m` each exit 2 with `sweep: --seeds takes whole numbers, got "abc"` (main hangs until its timeout). `--seeds none --mocks none --seed-limit 30` still exits 0.
  - Interrupted run: SIGTERM to the process group 20 s in, with the mocks and the seed both playing. Main and the branch both exit 143, with no process left in the group.
  - Older checkout: the sweep runs from its own checkout and reads no state an older checkout writes, so there is nothing to check.

| default 1 | 49 | 38 | 47.6 | 29.7 |

author: widgetii
body:
The MIS2009 answers on the MIS2008's I2C address with the same ID, so cameras built on it (Zenointel SD-2N-4G, gk7205v510) have been running `libsns_mis2008`. It works, but it is a different part's driver, and the picture shows it.

`libsns_mis2009` follows the MIS2009 driver in that camera's stock firmware:

| | vendor MIS2009 (now) | MIS2008 driver (before) |
|---|---|---|
| Init | vendor 1080p30 RAW10 table | 2008 table |
| Analog gain | 128 steps, 1x–15.75x, index in `0x3102` | 63 steps |
| Sensor digital gain | none | `0x3700/01` |
| Gain/exposure-dependent analog | `0x3A02`/`0x3A1C`, `0x3A07` at vendor thresholds | none |
| Integration time | up to VMAX−2 | clamped to 1349 |
| VMAX | 33780 / fps | 1126·30 / fps |
| AE, AWB, CCM, saturation | vendor | 2008 |
| ISP tuning | vendor blob, decoded | 2008 |

The tuning tables (DRC, demosaic, gamma, sharpen, LDCI, DPC, GE, AFC, BayerNR, CA, WDR, dehaze, noise calibration, CCM, AGC) were decoded from the vendor's tuning blob using these headers' struct layouts. Every table compiles to bytes identical to the blob, against both the XMedia (gk7205v500) and V4 (hi3516ev200/gk7205v200) headers.

Two MIS2008 driver bugs do not carry over:
- Register slot 8 (`0x3007`) lay past `u32RegNum`, so it was never synced.
- Unused slot 2 wrote register `0x0000`.

Mirror/flip is done on the sensor and shifts the readout window by one pixel per flipped axis, which keeps the Bayer phase at GRBG.

`sys_config` (gk7205v500): `mis2009` runs at 27 MHz, like `mis2008`.

## Tested on an SD-2N-4G (gk7205v510)
- Builds with no warnings under `-Wall -Wextra` for gk7205v500 and gk7205v200.
- Registers read back as the vendor programs them (`0x3011`, `0x3C20`, window 8/7).
- AE flips `0x3A02`/`0x3A1C` and `0x3A07` at the vendor thresholds: index 127 with integration 34 gives `0A/30` and `CC`; index 0 with integration 1105 gives `0B/1F` and `4C`.
- VMAX follows the frame rate: 1351 at 25 fps, 2252 at 15 fps.
- Mirror+flip keeps correct colours.
- Same scene against the MIS2008 driver: neutral white balance and natural colour, where the MIS2008 driver gives a dark grey cast.

author: joeychilson
body:
OpenCode Go's usage answer doesn't say which plan a key belongs to, so every key was its own account. With OpenCode and Pi each holding their own key to one plan, you got two "OpenCode Go" accounts with the same limits. Worse, each one shared the plan's rises only among its own agent's sessions, so each agent got credited with the other's use.

**What tells two keys apart.** Each key's monthly window renews on the plan's anniversary, to the millisecond. Measured 2026-10-05: OpenCode's key and Pi's both reset at `2026-10-18T16:37:32.000Z` through ~1,100 reads each, and the answers contain nothing else that could identify the plan. Accounts whose latest reads renew at the same time of day (midnight excluded, since calendar months share it) are one plan, under the lesser of their ids. The time of day stays the same from month to month, so a key that's no longer kept stays with its plan.

**Where it applies.** It is worked out from the ledger's readings whenever asked and never stored, so history recorded before this change counts toward the plan too:
- the timeline the cache attributes usage from, so usage, sessions and limit shares are the plan's;
- the account list, which merges the keys' agents, folders and readings;
- the early-reset alert's "reading before".

When a Go key reads a new monthly reset, or is read for the first time, sign-ins are marked changed, so the cache attributes usage again. The cache `SCHEMA` goes 16 → 17.

**On this Mac's history:**
- `check_limits` lists "OpenCode Go (OpenCode, Pi)" once at 87% left, where it listed two.
- September's 160.7M tokens of OpenCode use are now the plan's. Pi's 824K stay with the old key Pi held then, which Go now refuses as "subscription required", so it was most likely a separate plan that lapsed.
- Usage totals are identical to v0.3.1's.
- The plan's id is now `…8b66` (it was `…b139`). Hiding and alerts are keyed by id, so a Go alert may repeat once.

**Performance.** Finding each key's latest reset takes 9 µs. Reading every reset took 1 ms of 12.5K readings and would grow with the ledger's 90 days.

**Tests.** Unit tests of the rule: the lesser id wins, the result is the same in any order, a key read at two times of day joins both, and midnight joins nothing. An integration test reads real OpenCode and Pi history. While Pi's key hasn't answered there are two accounts; once it answers there's one plan with both agents and both sessions, and a rebuilt cache agrees. Turning off the re-attribution, or the merging, makes it fail.

Left for later: Pi's old lapsed key still appears in `check_limits all` as "no limit read yet", since it has September usage to its name.

author: daghostman
body:
Before: under `--hir`, a body that called a function or method declared further down the file fell back to the AST path with `callee-arity` (93 bodies in the corpus, including most of the `macro::` prelude).

After: those bodies lower from HIR, and the corpus goes from 5013 to 5095 lowered bodies.

A later callee has a reserved entry label, but its arity is only recorded once its body is compiled. The HIR call planner now reads the arity from the signature (`fn_param_names`, no rest parameter, not overloaded), as the AST call does. The callee's two-word return kind is not known before it is compiled either. Passing that check let `nested_method_try.hy` miscompile forward `Result` returns, so only callees that return no enum qualify.

How:
- `hir_call_abi` in `codegen/emit_hir.rs` has the new arity fallback.
- `tests/positive/hir_forward_calls.hy` covers mutual recursion, a forward string call, a forward `Option` call that stays on the AST, and forward methods.

Checks run locally:
- `coil test` (also under `--hir` and `--hir -O 0`), workspace tests, vm-wire, gc-stress and clippy are clean.

author: delcado19
body:
## Description

test.yml never reads the local `tests` gitlink — it always resolves the tests repo fresh by branch name, falling back to `main` (see `tests-pointer.yml`). A feature branch bumping the pointer by hand (the old habit `tests-pointer.yml` replaces) buys nothing for CI and only invites a submodule merge conflict whenever the automated workflow bumps the pointer on `dev` at the same time.

That's exactly what happened to #2175: its branch picked up tests#34 by bumping its own `tests` pointer, while `ci/tests-pointer` independently merged into `dev` via #2177 — both sides touched the same gitlink from a common ancestor, and GitHub flagged the PR `CONFLICTING` even though one pointer was a plain descendant of the other.

## Change

Adds a `tests-pointer-guard` job to `test.yml`: for any PR into `dev` other than `ci/tests-pointer` itself, it fails if the `tests` submodule pointer differs between PR base and head, with an error explaining why the commit isn't needed and should be dropped.

## Test plan

- [x] YAML validated (`python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/test.yml'))"`)
- [ ] Open a throwaway PR into `dev` that bumps the `tests` pointer and confirm the guard fails it
- [ ] Confirm a normal PR (no pointer change) passes the guard
- [ ] Confirm a PR from `ci/tests-pointer` itself is exempted

body:
# Description
Run-stage and job-card side of the STOFS-3D-ATL bad-day checks. Pairs with mansurjisan/nos-utils#68 (pinned here at its branch head 7390436; re-pinned to the merge commit once #68 merges). ATL only; SECOFS, AK and Pacific are unchanged. Production references are from the production v3.1.5 package (NCO code mirror).

What changed:
- **Run gate** (`prep_processing.sh:425-700`): `_validate_atl_inputs` also requires non-empty bctides.in, the four OBC `*.th.nc` and TEM_nu/SAL_nu before mpiexec, so a bad staging stops before the 41-node allocation.
- **Model success** (`now_forecast.sh:564-615`, `post_1.sh:375-383`, `post_2.sh:224-229`): the model job still fails on a non-zero mpiexec rc and only logs a missing completion signal, as production does. `archive_outputs` writes `mirror.status` next to the archived mirror.out: standalone looks for "Run completed successfully"; the coupled mirror.out has no such line, so its last `TIME STEP=` must equal rnday*86400/dt from param.nml. Post stops at the start when either phase's mirror.out is missing or incomplete. Cycles archived before this change have no `mirror.status`; post then judges the archived mirror.out directly (coupled: nowcast param.nml from `rerun/`, the forecast step count from LEN_FORECAST and dt from the archived nowcast param.nml).
- **Restart search follows COMOUT**: when `COMIN` is unset or still the `COMROOT/NET/RUN.PDY` default and COMOUT is overridden, prep sets `COMIN=$COMOUT`. An explicit COMIN or `RESTART_DIR` wins.
- **Separate COMROOT on WCOSS2**: the standalone cards use `COMROOT=${COMROOT_SA:-/lfs/h1/nos/ptmp/$LOGNAME/com_atl_sa}`, the coupled cards keep `/lfs/h1/nos/ptmp/$LOGNAME/com` behind `COMROOT_UFS`. Both launchers forward the override.

Path change to note (WCOSS2): standalone ATL COMOUT moves from `/lfs/h1/nos/ptmp/$LOGNAME/com/nos/stofs_3d_atl_ufs.<PDY>` to `/lfs/h1/nos/ptmp/$LOGNAME/com_atl_sa/nos/stofs_3d_atl_ufs.<PDY>`. This matches the Hercules default (`COMROOT_SA`); the coupled path is unchanged. After a pull, the next standalone cycle reads `com_atl_sa/nos/stofs_3d_atl_ufs.<PDY-1>`, which is empty, so:
- the restart gate fails in prep (no restart and no seeded init file);
- the dynamic adjust loses `COMOUT_PREV/staout_1` and `rerun/<run>.t12z.avg_bias`;
- the previous-cycle rerun fallbacks (St. Lawrence, OBC QC, NWM vsource) have nothing to read.

Before the first standalone cycle, either seed `com_atl_sa` (the init file plus the previous-cycle layout, e.g. with `tools/hercules_atl_seed_prev.sh`) or set `COMROOT_SA=/lfs/h1/nos/ptmp/$LOGNAME/com` to keep the old shared tree.

- **COLDSTART pin:** the shared `versions/run.ver` and `versions/run.hercules.ver` export `COLDSTART=YES`. The ATL restart gate refuses YES, as production does. Without the pin, every ATL prep on both machines would stop, which a normal-day test on Hercules showed. The 4 ATL prep cards now `export COLDSTART=NO` right after sourcing run.ver. run.ver itself is unchanged, so SECOFS is unaffected.

# Type of change
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

# Change characteristics
- Changes outputs (values, COMOUT files or names, archives)? YES: `mirror.status` in `*.restart_outputs` and `*.forecast_outputs`; standalone COMOUT path (above).
- Breaking change to existing functionality? NO for other systems. ATL post now refuses a run with no completed mirror.out.
- Requires a nos-utils submodule bump (nos-workflow) or a paired nos-workflow change (nos-utils)? YES: pinned to the nos-utils bad-day commit 7390436.
- Requires new or regenerated fix files on the machine? NO
- Requires a re-prep or a new hotstart before the next cycle? YES for standalone (new COMROOT).
- Machines affected: WCOSS2 (cards); the rest both

New file `nos_workflow/tests/test_atl_bad_day.py` (24 tests: mirror check standalone/coupled, archive verdict, post stop, model stage warns but still fails on rc, COMIN follows COMOUT, card COMROOT) plus 9 in `test_standalone_mode.py` (each required file missing or empty).

## Summary

Splits `InputBar`, `RestTimer` and `TempoDisplay` (custom/Workout) so no function exceeds 100 code lines (the largest is now 71). Behaviour-preserving: no prop, export, className, style, token or DOM change.

- **InputBar** stays one file, with in-file `InputBarLabel`, `InputBarFields` and `RecordButton`. `RecordButton` reads the theme itself, so `InputBar` drops its hook read and the "before the early return" comment.
- **RestTimer**: the bar card moves to an unexported `RestTimerBar.tsx` (plus `RestBarReadout`). The controls go in through an `actions` slot, so `RestActions` and `RestTimerRing` stay unchanged in `RestTimer.tsx`. All hooks still run before any early return.
- **TempoDisplay**: `TempoLivePhase`, `TempoLiveState`, `tempoColors` and `numberPalette` move to a JSX-free `tempoDisplayModel.ts`, which has its own 3-test file. The cells and the live row move unchanged to `tempoDisplayParts.tsx`. `TempoDisplay.tsx` re-exports the two types (`export type { … } from`), keeps the chip, the label, the chrome maths and the tooltip wrapper literal, and gains in-file `useTooltipToggle`, `StaticTempoRow`, `TempoTooltip` and `TooltipLine`. `TooltipLine` takes its content as children, so React keeps the same text nodes per line.
- **Lint baselines**: the `MetricCell` deprecated-import entry and the `toFixed(1)` no-local-formatter entry move from `TempoDisplay.tsx` to `tempoDisplayParts.tsx`, along with the code. These are key renames only, and both update scripts report `delta 0`.
- **Spacing rule coverage**: `RestTimerBar.tsx` and `tempoDisplayParts.tsx` join their parents in the `titan/no-raw-spacing` per-file enrolment in `eslint.config.js`. Without that, the JSX that moved would no longer be checked. The earlier splits did not do this. It is a two-line addition.
- No change to any `index.ts`, the barrels or `arch-graph.json`. `InputBar.test.tsx`, `RestTimer.test.tsx` and `TempoDisplay.test.tsx` are unedited.

## Characterisation

Commit 1 (`bda66ee3`) adds `*.characterise.test.tsx` for all three components. Each one snapshots the DOM and the className captured per testID, on dark and light Surfaces, under fake timers fixed at `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`. Coverage:

- every composed story;

- a typed reps value;
- a paused RestTimer whose DOM does not move over 5 s;
- the default story rendered the same under `prefers-reduced-motion` and without it.

The three files ran whole each time, never filtered. 171 tests passed after the InputBar/RestTimer split commit (`eb1a6abc`), and 174 (the 171 plus the model tests) after the TempoDisplay split (`e79e3b10`). No snapshot was written or updated after commit 1. `git diff bda66ee3 5a310211 --stat -- '*.snap'` is empty: byte-identical. The last commit deletes the characterisation tests and snapshots, as the owner decided.

## dist export parity

The re-exported types are listed as `type TempoLivePhase` and `type TempoLiveState` in `dist/index.d.ts`. After `pnpm build`, `src/test/dist-export-parity.test.ts` passes (2 tests).

Browser API calls use one origin; root Compose builds the static frontend/Nginx and Java runtime with internal DB/backend ports and health checks. Removes the legacy duplicate HTTP connector so the configured HTTP/TLS port is authoritative.

Validation passed on implementation commit 799d996919aa49b82be57f4d3800769108cfe639: 92 backend unit/MVC tests, six real PostgreSQL 16 integration scenarios, seven frontend tests, TypeScript and frontend build (existing CRA/UI warnings). author: passw0rds
body:
## Motivation

Ports forwarded by container runtimes used to scatter across **Apps** (Docker Desktop, OrbStack) and **Dev Servers** (colima), named after the forwarder process (`OrbStack Helper`, `com.docker.backend`). That hid the actual owner: you see a runtime, not the container — and the group's close hint was wrong too, because signalling the forwarder only breaks the port mapping while the container keeps running.

Since the group is how a port is closed for good, containers deserve their own group with their own close path: `docker stop`.

## What it does

- **New Containers section** (between Background Services and Apps). Rows follow the owner a human thinks in:
  - compose containers of one project sit in a single row named after the project, each container as its port row;
  - a plain `docker run` without `--name` is listed by its image (a generated `nostalgic_turing` says less than `redis` does);
  - the runtime's own ports keep the runtime's name.
- **Port page locates the origin**: reveals the compose project directory (from the `config_files` label, falling back to `working_dir`) or a bind-mounted host directory — no more opening Docker.app/OrbStack.app as "the folder".
- **Stop Container** (port page + context menu): a review page showing the exact `docker stop` command, image, compose project, every port that closes with it, and a note when `--restart=always` will resurrect the container on daemon restart (`docker update --restart=no` hint). Execution goes through the docker CLI and the result is verified by a rescan. Signalling the forwarder itself stays refused, exactly like launchd KeepAlive jobs.

## How resolution works

`ContainerResolver` tries the **Engine API over the daemon's unix socket** first — one `GET /containers/json`, ~10 ms, no process spawn — then `docker ps` (which understands contexts and remote daemons), then degrades to the runtime's name. Foundation has no unix-socket transport, so a minimal `NWConnection` HTTP client (~80 lines, zero dependencies) does the job; it decodes chunked transfer encoding, which the daemon uses even for HTTP/1.0 requests. Socket and CLI failures back off separately for 60 s, and a socket failure never disables the CLI fallback. No new macOS permissions are involved — same process-spawn and socket semantics the scanner already uses.

`PortCategory`'s doc comment said the category "never" rests on program-name lists; container runtimes are now a documented exception, because the forwarder *is* the port holder — the row should name the runtime (or the container), never the mapping process.

## Verification

- 40 unit tests (8 new): Engine API and `docker ps` parsing, chunked decoding including truncated streams, socket-failure fallback, generated-name heuristics, restart-policy plan, category classification, localization.
- Live-checked against OrbStack (compose projects with labels/mounts, a `docker run` demo, the runtime's own ports) and via the CLI: full scan stays ~0.28 s with containers resolved.

Closes nothing; opened after testing the debug build on macOS 15 with OrbStack.

author: jpegthedev
body:
## What changed

Adds the `greenfield-bootstrap` skill. After the `greenfield-discovery` skill has produced a `## Domain Model` block and the `greenfield-architecture` skill has produced a `## Architecture Decision` block, it writes a runnable starter project into the current directory with tool calls: a stack-specific `.gitignore`, `README.md`, `.github/workflows/smoke.yml`, three issue templates, the stack's build manifest when the build step needs one, and a hello world. It then runs the hello world and reports a `## Bootstrapped Files` block. Seven stacks are supported: Python, TypeScript/Node.js, Rust, Go, C#, C++, C/embedded C.

Files:
- `skills/greenfield-bootstrap/SKILL.md` (new, 13227 bytes): procedure and gates.
- `skills/greenfield-bootstrap/references/SHARED_TEMPLATES.md` (new, 8893 bytes): the name tokens, the Language-value mapping (each row names the stack file to open), the action versions, and the stack-independent templates (README.md, .gitignore rule, smoke.yml frame, three issue templates).
- `skills/greenfield-bootstrap/references/stacks/` (new, one file per stack: python.md, typescript-node.md, rust.md, go.md, csharp.md, cpp.md, c-embedded.md; 921 to 1745 bytes each): each holds that stack's one `## Stack:` section (toolchain probe, hello world files, ignore entries, lockfile, smoke workflow steps, local-run commands).
- `skills/greenfield-bootstrap/references/INDEX.md` (new): reference index the writing-skills rules require.

## Scope change after this pull request opened

The launcher that runs this story relayed this change to me as approved by the owner; I have not seen the owner's own message. Relayed text: "split references/STACK_TEMPLATES.md so each stack has its own file, to make it easy to grep", with the stated shape: one file per stack under references/stacks/, each holding exactly one of the existing `## Stack:` sections with the same field numbering; the Tokens and Language Mapping section and the `## Shared:` templates kept in the remaining file, renamed references/SHARED_TEMPLATES.md, with the mapping naming the stack file to open; every SKILL.md pointer and the INDEX.md rows updated; no template content changes. The relay said "five" `## Shared:` templates; the file has six (README.md, .gitignore, smoke.yml and three issue templates), and all six were kept.

Done in commits e76346d (the split) and 69b1a2a, a2d70bd, 9447246, 107b07e (review fixes, see Review record). Every stack section and every `## Shared:` section is byte-identical to the single-file version at 529fae1. SKILL.md changed only on its pointer lines (24, 50, 66, 75, 77, 83, 96). Added after the relay, my own wording in prose the relay did not cover: the SHARED_TEMPLATES.md title and introduction, the mapping column header "Stack file", the Action versions sentence (now says the stack files use the setup actions, and expands SDK), and the INDEX.md descriptions.
- `README.md`: skills-table row; skill count 38 -> 39.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: skill count 38 -> 39.

## Why

The two greenfield skills already on main end with a domain model and a stack decision, but nothing turns them into a repository that is ready for issue-driven work. This skill closes that step.

## Decisions that need your sign-off

The issue leaves gaps; each was filled with a reversible decision. I need your sign-off on the list below so that the skill keeps this behavior; any item you reject becomes a follow-up change. The items that change or relax what the issue asks for are marked (changes the issue).

1. (changes the issue) Manifests are written when the stack's build step needs one (package.json + tsconfig.json, Cargo.toml, go.mod, a .csproj, CMakeLists.txt). Python's install step runs only when requirements.txt exists, so Fixture A on Python is exactly 7 files; the issue table lists the unguarded `pip install -r requirements.txt`.
2. Project name = the target directory's name. Manifests and package names use an identifier: lowercase; every run of characters outside a-z, 0-9 and hyphen becomes one hyphen (underscore included); leading and trailing hyphens trimmed; `app-` prefixed before a leading digit; `app` when empty. (The plan first described this rule as keeping underscore; the Signoff review found the mismatch and this line states the shipped rule.)
3. Target directory = the current working directory, named in the block.
4. Any listed target file already exists: write nothing, ask once whether to overwrite the listed files or stop; never merge.
5. (changes the issue) Toolchain absent: write the files, report the hello world NOT RUN naming the tool, never install a toolchain. This relaxes "verified by running it locally" on machines without the toolchain.
6. (changes the issue) Local run failure: at most one fix to a file the skill wrote, then exactly one re-run, also when no fix applies (a failure can be transient); report the last run, PASSED when it exited 0, otherwise FAILED with the command and exit code. At most two runs.
7. No Domain Model (bare invocation, or an Architecture Decision alone): write nothing and point to `greenfield-discovery`.
8. A hook denies a write (this repository's inline-edit guard denies the main session's non-prose writes and writes over 10 lines inside a git repository): never retry in another form; dispatch one subagent to write the remaining files into the same directory, then run the hello world and emit the block.
9. No user able to answer a question (for example inside a subagent): stop, write nothing, name the missing fact.
10. Language mapping: the value before ` -- `, version numbers and parenthetical notes ignored (`C++20` -> C++, `C# (.NET 8)` -> C#); `Golang` -> Go; `C`, `C99`, `C11`, `Embedded C` -> C/embedded C (a hosted gcc build); JavaScript and every other language -> the refusal.
11. Python's local run uses python3 when python is absent; smoke.yml uses python after actions/setup-python.
12. (changes the issue) Branch `feat/7-greenfield-bootstrap` from main instead of `claude/greenfield-app-skills-nx9Q4`: that branch exists only locally, not on origin, is 112 commits behind origin/main, and holds no plan.md.
13. (changes the issue) Reference layout: per the scope change above, `references/SHARED_TEMPLATES.md` plus one file per stack under `references/stacks/`, in place of the one `STACK_TEMPLATES.md` the issue's Technical Notes and Definition of Done name. The content is the same; only the file split differs. `references/INDEX.md` is added because writing-skills requires an index.
14. The README row and the 38 -> 39 skill counts are included, because the counts become false otherwise; routing rows are not (follow-up).
15. (changes the issue) `user_story.md` follows the user-story-generator story template (As a / I want to / So that, Acceptance Criteria, Technical Notes, Definition of Done), copied self-contained. The issue's "story format in this repo's plan.md" names an untracked scratch file that no new project has.
16. The TypeScript local run runs the stack's build step (`npm install && npm run build`), which fetches the declared typescript devDependency.
17. `## Bootstrapped Files` lists skill-written files only; lockfiles the run creates (package-lock.json, Cargo.lock, go.sum) go on their own line.
18. Only `bug_report.md` carries a `labels:` line (`bug`); `user_story.md` and `spike.md` carry none, because the skill does not create labels in the new repository.
19. A Language value naming more than one language (for example `Go or Rust`) gets the one stack question; the answer then goes through the stack gate.
20. (changes the issue) A language version is not carried into the scaffold: `C++20` maps to the C++ template, which pins C++17, and the skill does not tell the user. Carrying or reporting the version is a follow-up.
21. C# targets the installed .NET SDK's major version (`dotnet --version` major M -> netM.0 and setup-dotnet M.0.x; net10.0 and 10.0.x when dotnet is absent); go.mod's `go` line takes the installed G
