body:
## What

`/nl/om-uit-te-printen/letters-overtrekken/` mirrors `printables/letter-tracing` as it stands today:
- `genLetters: true`, so a typed "Noor" prints as `N o o r`
- no class roster; the name job stays on `naam-leren-schrijven`
- A–Z + 0–9 picker, whole-alphabet ruled and outline PDFs, the 7-level ladder, Dutch school-group presets (groep 1 to 4+), and the stroke-direction overlay

nl now has both tracing pages English has, like de, es, fr, it, pl and pt.

- **Slug.** "overtrekken" is the verb Dutch teachers use for tracing (juf-milou.nl), and "schrijfletters overtrekken" shows up in live NL autocomplete. `schrijfletters` is already the cursive page.
- **Rule 3.** The name page gets a one-line pointer to the letter page, and the letter page's FAQ and editorial text point back for class name sets. The nl hub gets a card.
- **Generated, scoped.** Reciprocal hreflang across all 8 letter-tracing pages (`sync:locale-mesh --fix --files`). Sitemap and llms.txt carry only this page's entry; the rest of the regen was lastmod churn that the daily `update-sitemap` workflow owns, so I dropped it. Hero/OG come from `generate-locale-art --only`. The sheet preview is page 1 of the page's own PDF.
- **Ledger.** One `printable_tool_duplication_exclusions.json` entry for the nl name/letter pair. Dutch uses "overtrekken" for both sheets, so the signature collides the same way it did in de/es/fr. The gate flagged the pair on this branch, and the owner approved the entry before it was written (2026-10-05).

## Verified

- The rendered sheet shows Dutch labels, `A a` split into letters, Naam/Datum, and a QR code that encodes this page's URL
- The OG card renders cleanly
- Merged `main` to fix a conflict in the generated `llms.txt` files; I took main's side and regenerated them. After the merge, `npm run check:ci-gates` passes every gate except `test:text-object-grids`.
- **Correction:** an earlier version of this description said `test:text-object-grids` was red on `main`. That was wrong. It fails only under the session's local Node 22, and it passes on CI's Node 24 (it's green in other PRs' Validate runs today). This diff doesn't touch that code.

## Not built, deliberately

- **id:** `/id/printables/menebalkan-huruf/` already owns the letter-formation job ("menebalkan huruf" is the head term). A second page would cannibalise it.
- **tr:** the TR printables pilot has a readout due 2026-11-09. More tr families wait for that result.

**Draft, held for the maintainer:** this changes the shipped `x-deal-v0` profile schema, so it is not for an ordinary merge. Against origin/main `adf2990`; the findings are verified at v0.1.0-rc6 (`14bf3bc`).

## The ruling

The deal path claims no pack:
- **The code:** `capsulectl` stops writing `pack_id` (`deal_profile.go:26`, `:571`, `:615`).
- **The schema:** `pack_id` is dropped from **both** required lists, `body_check.required` (schema `:268`) and `body_verdict.required` (`:285`). The verdict is the stronger false claim of the two, because it carries the result.
- **Kept:** `pack_digest` keeps its meaning for a producer that really reads a pack. Nothing here vendors, embeds or path-reads one.

## Why: the deal path loads no pack (scoped negative at `14bf3bc`)

| Command | matched = raw | sha256(output)[:16] |
|---|---|---|
| `git grep -niE 'packPath\|pack.json\|loadPack\|readPack\|packDir' 14bf3bc -- internal/cli ':!*_test.go'` | 0 = 0 | `e3b0c44298fc1c14` (empty) |
| `git ls-tree -r --name-only 14bf3bc \| grep -i pack` | 0 = 0 | `e3b0c44298fc1c14` (empty) |
| `git grep -nE 'dealPackID' 14bf3bc -- 'internal/cli/*.go'` | 3 = 3 (the constant, `:571`, `:615`) | `2457661facc1d45d` (no trailing newline) |

Each digest is SHA-256 over the command's output **without its trailing newline**, i.e. `printf '%s' "$(<command>)" | shasum -a 256`. For the third row, the raw output, which ends in a newline, gives `f3f12930f16bcb66`. The two empty outputs give the empty-input digest either way.

`deal check` runs the CLI's own built-in rules (`deal_rules.go:725-852`). So `pack_id` on a check or verdict asserts that a pack governed a verdict no pack governed. Adding a digest would make that assertion checkable, not true.

**The root cause is related but separate:** the deal rules are Go code with no published definition and no definition digest. There are no bytes a record could name, which is why no `pack_id` or `pack_digest` can be honest here. That is tracked as its own item: pinning the Go rules to digested definitions.

## Why this breaks no existing record

Removing a field from `required` only **loosens** the schema. A record that carries `pack_id` still matches its (unchanged) `pack_id` definition, so every record sealed so far keeps validating. This is proved, not argued:
- **`internal/cli/testdata/deal/rc6-records/jet-ski-deal.json`:** the DEMO jet-ski deal, sealed and exported by a binary built from `14bf3bc`, kept byte for byte (sha256 `2b0972fc…a009`). Its check and verdict carry `pack_id`. `TestDealSchemaStillAcceptsRecordsThatNameAPack` validates all 8 records against the new schema and runs `check_profile.py` over the deal: **ALL OK**.
- **`TestDealRecordsFollowTheProfile`:** seals a full deal with this branch, validates every record against the new schema, and now also asserts that no record contains `pack_id` or `pack_digest`. Under the old schema these records would fail, because `pack_id` was required.

## Also changed

- **`skills/deal/profile/check_profile.py`:**
  - the verdict/check `pack_id` rule compares only when one is present, where it used to raise on a missing key;
  - `--regen` no longer reads a `pack.json` from outside the repository, and no longer writes `pack_id` or `pack_digest`.

  The fixtures are regenerated. Apart from the pack fields, their digests and one story line ("names the pack it runs"), they are unchanged; this was checked field by field.
- **`PROFILE.md`:** `pack_id` is optional, `capsulectl` names no pack after rc6, and older records keep theirs. `rule` ids are described as the producer's own rules, and normalization points to the profile's own section, not to a pack.
- **`deal_share.go`:** its list of fields allowed in a shared copy still includes `pack_id`, so shared copies of older records stay unchanged.

**Checks:**
- `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...` pass, and `skillgen --check` passes.
- `check_profile.py` reports ALL OK, and `skills/deal/scripts/run-demo.sh` passes.

body:
## Summary

This PR implements Step 9.8 of the research methodology: a structured evaluation of the three candidate gaps (GC-01, GC-02, GC-03) identified in Step 9.7. The step evaluates candidates against an explicit framework and targeted disproof searches, but does not rank, score, or select a final research gap.

## Key Changes

- **`configs/gap_evaluation.yaml` (new)**: Declarative framework defining:
  - Frozen corpus boundary (54 records, SHA-256 hash)
  - 14 evaluation dimensions with evidence requirements and assessment criteria
  - Allowed vocabularies for evidence levels, counterexample strengths, and qualitative assessments
  - Guard-rails enforcing no ranking, no novelty claims, and no `Unknown`-to-`No` conversion

- **`src/literature/gap_evaluation.py` (new)**: Read-only validator that enforces:
  - Frozen corpus integrity (hash, record count, schema)
  - Counterexample file structure and vocabularies
  - No conversion of `Unknown` to `No` without explicit basis
  - Search-log completeness (required fields, limitations documented)
  - Matrix coverage (each candidate × 14 criteria)
  - Forbidden ranking and novelty language

- **`research/gap_analysis/counterexample_candidates.csv` (new)**: 39 rows documenting:
  - 9 corpus records with values reproduced unchanged
  - 30 external papers (23 distinct sources) assessed as potential counterexamples
  - None added to the frozen `papers.csv`

- **`research/gap_analysis/targeted_search_log.md` (new)**: 27 logged searches (S01–S27):
  - 24 WebSearch queries (8 per candidate)
  - 2 alphaXiv discovery searches
  - 1 verification lookup
  - Each search documents: date, candidate, exact query, engine, results returned, relevant results inspected, strongest papers, potential counterexamples, unresolved items, and limitations

- **`research/gap_analysis/candidate_gap_matrix.csv` (new)**: Qualitative assessment of each candidate on 14 dimensions:
  - Evidence, evidence level, supporting papers, counterexamples, unknown burden
  - Qualitative assessment (supports/weakens/mixed/unresolved/feasible/difficult) with confidence (low/moderate/high)
  - No numeric scores or weights

- **`research/gap_analysis/candidate_gap_evaluation.md` (new)**: Comprehensive written evaluation:
  - 15 required sections (Purpose, Frozen corpus boundary, Methodology, per-candidate evaluation, etc.)
  - Qualitative analysis of corpus evidence, counterexample risk, research feasibility, and engineering complexity
  - Ends with: "Final research-gap selection remains a researcher decision and is outside Step 9.8."

- **`tests/test_gap_evaluation.py` (new)**: 20+ test cases verifying:
  - Frozen corpus integrity
  - No ranking or selection language
  - No `Unknown`-to-`No` conversion
  - Counterexample data does not modify `papers.csv`
  - Forbidden novelty language is rejected
  - Search-log completeness and limitations
  - Matrix coverage and assessment vocabularies

- **`docs/agent_sync/CHANGELOG.md` (modified)**: Added entry documenting Step 9.8 changes

## Notable Implementation Details

- **Frozen corpus**: `papers.csv` is locked at 54 records with SHA-256 `c8fac51d5d80abd25f09816eace1ab840c498af76ade913ce7f7f1ecdc7da521`. No modifications allowed.
- **Guard-rails**: The validator rejects ranking columns, novelty phrases ("novel", "first", "only"), and any `No` value from snippet-level evidence without explicit justification.
- **Counterexample classification**: Four strength levels (full, partial, potential, not_counterexample) with evidence levels (verified_full_text, abstract_only, search_snippet_only, unresolved).

body:
## What changed
A deploy can now accept GitHub's browser-test result for the exact commit being deployed, when this server's own record has none. The code checks still have to pass on this server, and GitHub's answer is only trusted from the reviewed test setup on that same commit.

## Why
A deploy ignored GitHub's browser-test result and had to be pushed through by hand, which records it as unchecked.

## What you'll notice
Nothing until your one-time step: create a fine-grained, read-only GitHub token (checks: read and actions: read) on the repositories you want covered, and place it at /etc/fleet/github-e2e/token, owned by root, mode 600. Each such app also gets a small root-owned settings file beside it. Until then nothing changes.

## How it was checked
The library's own tests feed it saved GitHub answers. Each safety check was deleted in turn and the tests went red. Full gate green on this commit.

Technical detail: commits and docs/DECISIONS.md.

## Issue

Fixes #444

Change folder: `.agent/changes/444-web-order-line-total/`

## Summary

On the web order form, a FIXED line on a product whose default option is per-day showed "/ngày" and unit × qty × days, while the order saved unit × qty. The row checked `item.pricingType === 'DAILY' || item.product?.pricingType === 'DAILY'`, and `product.pricingType` only mirrors the default option. The line pricing rules now live in one pure helper (`packages/utils/src/core/order-line-pricing.ts`). The line's own type wins (`item.pricingType ?? option ?? product.pricingType ?? FIXED`, per day only for RENT), and the row toggle, the displayed total, the subtotal and the saved payload all use it. Switching the order back to RENT now uses the selected option's price and the per-day rule, not `product.rentPrice` × qty.

Commits: change folder → refactor (rules moved into the helper, no behavior change) → failing test → fix.

## Test plan

- [x] `cd tests && yarn test order-form-line-pricing`: 12/12 pass (5 failed before the fix: FIXED line on a DAILY-default product, DAILY toggle without a DAILY option, display ≠ saved total ×2, RENT reprice)

No API, schema or mobile change. One saved total changes on purpose: a line switched to "Theo ngày" on a product with no DAILY option used to show a per-day total and save a FIXED total. It now saves the per-day total it shows.

**Open product question (not changed here):** the web still starts a new rent line on the FIXED option (`getPreferredPricingOption`), while iOS/Android start on the merchant default. The owner chose iOS as the reference for mobile; the web default is unchanged and needs a decision.

body:
رفع #44 — آگهی‌ای که بدون شماره ذخیره می‌شود دلیلش را می‌گوید، شمارهٔ بدون tel: خوانده می‌شود، و نرخ موفقیت پازل از لاگ قابل محاسبه است.

> **روی PR #68 (رفع #39) ساخته شده و باید بعد از آن ادغام شود.** diff این PR تا ادغام #68 کامیت‌های آن را هم نشان می‌دهد؛ کامیت‌های خود این PR دو تای آخرند.

## علت
- تنها ردّ آگهی بدون شماره خط «No phone element found after clicking contact button» بود و در فهرست «ردشده‌ها» برای همه یک جمله: «ذخیره شد ولی شمارهٔ تماس گرفته نشد».
- شماره‌ای که در پنجرهٔ تماس به‌صورت متن (با فاصله، خط تیره، یا تلفن ثابت) و بدون پیوند `tel:` نشان داده می‌شد خوانده نمی‌شد؛ جایگزین صفحه فقط `09…` پیوسته را می‌گرفت.
- اطلاعیه‌ای که هیچ دکمه‌اش با کلمه‌های شناخته‌شده جور نبود روی شماره می‌ماند.
- کد ردشده از کد تایپ‌شده جدا نمی‌شد.
- پازلی که در آخرین تلاش حل می‌شد هم کنار پازل‌های «ناموفق» ذخیره می‌شد.

## تغییر
- `contact_extractor.py`: واژگان ثابت `MISS_REASONS` — `code_rejected` (کد رد شد)، `code_lost` (کد رسید و خانه نبود، #39)، `code_missing` (کد خواسته شد و وارد نشد)، `puzzle_failed`، `notice`، `no_tel`، `safe_call` («تماس امن»)، `identity_required`، `no_button`، `error`، `unknown`. `get_phone_number` روی هر None یک `miss_reason` می‌گذارد (به ترتیب علت: اول کد، بعد پازل، بعد آنچه جلوی شماره بود) و یک خط در لاگ همان اجرا می‌نویسد (stage `item`، details `{miss, divar_id}`).
- بعد از فرستادن کد، اگر خانهٔ کد هنوز هست و کلمهٔ ردّ تازه‌ای («اشتباه»، «نامعتبر»، «منقضی»…) ظاهر شده، کد «ردشده» است؛ کلمه‌ای که از اول روی پنجره بوده حساب نمی‌شود.
- شمارهٔ نوشته‌شده در پنجره‌های روی صفحه خوانده می‌شود (رقم فارسی/عربی، فاصله/خط تیره، +98، تلفن ثابت)؛ شمارهٔ ستاره‌دار `no_tel` نام می‌گیرد. فقط متن پنجره، نه کل توضیح آگهی.
- اطلاعیه‌ای با دو دکمه یا بیشتر که هیچ‌کدام قابل حدس نیست با Escape بسته می‌شود (هیچ دکمه‌ای زده نمی‌شود)؛ اگر نماند همان دلیل ثبت می‌شود. پنجره‌ای که شماره را به هر شکل بالا نشان دهد دست نمی‌خورد.
- یک خط `[captcha] puzzle n/3: solved|failed` برای هر پازل کشیده‌شده. خود حل‌کننده تغییری نکرده است.
- `divar_scraper.py` (دو ویرایش کوچک، چون PR #55 این فایل را بازنویسی می‌کند): دلیل هر آگهی نگه داشته می‌شود و `detail` ردیف `no_phone` می‌شود `no_phone_detail(reason)`، مثلاً «شماره گرفته نشد: دیوار کد تأیید را نپذیرفت — در اجرای بعدی دوباره تلاش می‌شود». **سطل `reason` همان `no_phone` می‌ماند**، پس `AWAITING_PHONE` و تلاش دوبارهٔ #55 دست نمی‌خورند. migration ندارد.
- `scripts/captcha_success_rate.py`: فقط‌خواندنی؛ فایل لاگ (ساده یا ‎.gz) یا stdin می‌گیرد و تلاش‌ها، حل‌شده، ناموفق، نرخ موفقیت، نرخ تلاش اول، جدول روزانه و دفعه‌های حدس حل‌کننده را می‌دهد. لاگ قدیمی را با جفت کردن «Captcha slider dragged» با اولین نتیجهٔ بعدش می‌خواند و آنچه را نمی‌شود قضاوت کرد جدا گزارش می‌کند.

## برخورد با PR #55
- خط `detail=` ردیف `no_phone` در `start_scraping_job` را #55 هم عوض کرده (`… — {_next}`). هر کدام دوم ادغام شود: `detail=no_phone_detail(...)` بماند و `_next`/`RETRY_HINT` به‌جای پایان ثابت در `no_phone_detail` بنشیند.
- مسیر تلاش دوبارهٔ #55 (`settle(item, old_rows, "no_phone", …)`) روی main نیست؛ بعد از ادغام هر دو، همان‌جا هم `no_phone_detail` با `_last_contact_miss` استفاده شود.

## تست
- `tests/test_no_phone_reason.py` (تازه): `get_phone_number` روی صفحهٔ ساختگی — شمارهٔ فاصله‌دار بدون tel:، تلفن ثابت، شمارهٔ خود حساب، شمارهٔ ستاره‌دار، اطلاعیه‌ای که بسته نمی‌شود، اطلاعیه‌ای که Escape می‌بندد و شمارهٔ پشتش خوانده می‌شود، پازل ماندگار، تماس امن، نبودن دکمه، نامعلوم، و هر سه نتیجهٔ کد؛ یک اجرای یک‌آگهی‌ای از `start_scraping_job` که دلیل را روی ردیف `no_phone` می‌گذارد؛ خط‌های پازلِ واقعی extractor که به اسکریپت داده می‌شوند (۱ حل، ۱ ناموفق) و فقط پازل ناموفق نگه داشته می‌شود. تست‌های شماره/اطلاعیه/ردیف اجرا پیش از تغییر شکست خوردند.
- `tests/test_otp_box_rebuilt.py`: کد ردشده، کلمه‌ای که از قبل بوده، کد پذیرفته‌شده.

author: freeqaz
body:
## Problem

Names are documented as at most 200 characters. The JSON Schema `maxLength` counts code points and PostgreSQL's `char_length(name) BETWEEN 1 AND 200` constraints count characters, but `validName` in `packages/occ/src/index.ts` and the in-memory Secret, ServiceAccount and credential source checks in `platform-state.ts` used `String.length` (UTF-16 code units). A name of 101 to 200 astral characters (emoji, CJK Extension B, mathematical letters) passes the schema and is then refused:

- `POST /namespaces`, `/secrets`, `/service-accounts`, `/agents`, `/credential-sources`: **404 NOT_FOUND** "The requested platform resource was not found." (`ScopeViolationError`), which reads as a missing Namespace;
- Presets and IAM Roles: 400 with a generic "name is invalid".

## Change

- Count code points (`Array.from(name).length`) in `validName` and in the three in-memory adapter checks, which say they mirror the PostgreSQL constraints.
- The ChatGPT ServiceAccount Driver cut the provider account name with `String.slice` to a 200-unit budget, which can end inside a surrogate pair and send a lone surrogate to the provider. It now cuts by whole characters within the same budget (review follow-up).

## Verification

- New `occ-api-security` case: a Namespace and an Agent named with 200 emoji are created (404 on main), and 201 emoji gets 400 `TOO_LONG`.
- New shared store contract case `verifyNameLengthContract`: Secret, ServiceAccount, credential source and Preset with a 200-character / 390-code-unit name are stored and read back; a 201-character Secret, ServiceAccount or credential source is refused with `ScopeViolationError` (the memory adapter has no Preset name length check; the controller and PostgreSQL enforce it).
- New `service-account-driver` case: a 200-character name of one ASCII character and 199 emoji is cut to `x` + 79 emoji + `-<id>`, with no lone surrogate. Fails on main. Fails on main for the memory adapter; passes for memory and for a real PostgreSQL 18.6 database (the full `verifyPlatformStateStoreContract`, fresh migrated database).
- occ-api-security, service-account-driver, secret-occ, presets, credential-source-occ, service-account-driver, iam, occ-read, platform-state-memory: pass. `pnpm typecheck`, eslint and Prettier on touched files: pass.

## Risks

- Low. Only names of astral characters between 101 and 200 code points change outcome, from refused to accepted; PostgreSQL already accepted them. Names that exceed 200 code points are still refused by the schema first.
- Follow-up, not in this PR: the console's Agent name field uses HTML `maxlength="200"`, which browsers count in UTF-16 units, so the console still stops at 100 emoji.

author: abu-lina
body:
## Summary

Fixes #527. Migrates zod 3.25.76 -> 4.6.5 (exact pin) so Dependabot #506 can close — this PR supersedes it.

```diff
 validation fails on a route
-  details: validation.error.errors        # raw zod issue object on the wire
+  details: toValidationDetails(error)     # [{ path, message }], owned shape

 src/lib/validations/
+└── errors.ts           # the seam: ZodError -> ValidationDetail[]

 z.enum([...], {
-  errorMap: () => ({ message }),          # dropped in v4
+  error: 'reviewStatus must be one of: approved, rejected, needs_revision',
 })
```

```text
400 bodies on 3 routes — element shape only, envelope untouched
POST /api/admin/badges/verify    { error, details: [{path,message}] }
POST /api/admin/badges/unverify  { error, details: [{path,message}] }
PATCH /api/waitlist/update       { data:null, error:{ message, details:[{path,message}] } }
```

## Deliberate API change

The three routes above used to return zod's raw issue array in `details`. They now return `[{ path: string, message: string }]`. Same status, same keys, same sibling fields; only the element shape changed, and zod internals (`code`, `origin`, `format`, `pattern` — which would leak the validation regex) stay off the wire. Byte-identical replication of the v3 body was impossible: v4 renames `invalid_string`->`invalid_format`, drops `received`, `validation`, `type` and `exact`, and rewrites every default message. Nothing in this repo consumes these bodies; external clients are the only exposure. Example:

```json
v3: {"error":"Validation failed","details":[{"validation":"uuid","code":"invalid_string","message":"Invalid badge ID format","path":["badgeId"]}]}
v4: {"error":"Validation failed","details":[{"path":"badgeId","message":"Invalid badge ID format"}]}
```

`POST /api/providers` and `POST /api/city-interest/subscribe` keep emitting a single `error` string, but the text of schema-default messages changes (e.g. `String must contain at most 200 character(s)` -> `Too big: expected string to have <=200 characters`, `Required` -> `Invalid input: expected string, received undefined`, `Unrecognized key(s) in object: 'x'` -> `Unrecognized key: "x"`). Accepted deliberately; both are pinned by tests.

## Evidence

- **Before:** 7 failing tests under zod 4.6.5 — six in `community-service-schemas.test.ts` (non-RFC-4122 UUID fixtures that v3's loose `.uuid()` regex accepted) and `adminSchemas-cs.test.ts > rejects an invalid reviewStatus value` (`errorMap` silently ignored at runtime).
- **After:** `npx vitest run` — 301 files passed, 2727 tests, 0 failed. `npm run type-check` clean. `npm run lint` = 0 errors, 131 warnings (unchanged from main, cap 131). `npm run build` green. `npm ls zod` = single `4.6.5`, no 3.x tree.
- New tests pin the post-migration 400 JSON exactly on badges/verify, badges/unverify, waitlist/update, providers (incl. `.default(null)` omitted-vs-null) and city-interest.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** one-way on the wire — the three 400 bodies' element shape and the two message strings do not revert without a code change once clients observe them. Code itself is a clean two-way revert.

**Blast Radius:** API surface of 5 routes; in-repo consumers: none. Log-only sites (waitlist/join, subscribe-city) changed `.errors`->`.issues` with no body change. Both `reviewStatus` enums keep the deliberate 3-of-5 subset of `public.review_status`; the custom message is byte-identical.

Notes for reviewers:

- The Prettier reformatting in the five route files is the repo's `lint-staged` hook (`eslint --fix` + `prettier --write`) acting on pre-existing drift on main, not hand reformatting. Read the diff with `-w` for the substance.
- The ~25 `devOptional`->`dev` lockfile hunks are pre-existing `main` staleness — reproducible with `npm install --package-lock-only` on main, no zod involvement.
- The global `vi.mock('zod')` stub in `src/__tests__/setup.ts` was deleted and all 14 now-dead `vi.unmock('zod')` calls removed.
- Deprecation sweep (`.uuid()`, `.email()`, `.url()`, `.datetime()`, `.strict()`, `ctx.addIssue`) is intentionally out of scope — tracked in #531.
- `security/snyk` passed on this PR. #529 reports an exhausted private-test quota reddening PRs repo-wide; that turns out to be scoped to the Dependabot fleet, and a normal PR still gets a real Snyk result. Evidence noted on #529.

author: pelleoe
body:
## Changes
- **perf:** `counter:sync` buffers matched keys across SCAN pages and syncs them in deduplicated batches of `sync_batch_size`. On a Redis DB holding 500k unrelated keys, 1k counter keys synced in 1,558 ms over 434 batches; now 405 ms in one batch (e-papi container benchmark). With a dedicated DB nothing changes. `sync_batch_size` < 1 is clamped to 1 (it would hang otherwise).
- **fix (data safety, from review):** in 2.6.0 an instrumenter throwing *after* a committed upsert skipped the Redis drain, so the next sync double-counted. Every phase now runs through `measurePhase()`: an instrumenter failure before the phase runs it uninstrumented, one after keeps its result, and both log a warning. Phase exceptions still propagate.
- **fix:** the instrumenter is resolved lazily, so subclasses or tests calling the sync methods without `handle()` don't hit an uninitialised property.
- **docs:** the interface docblock lists every data key; README Sentry example imports `Closure`; CONTRIBUTING release steps updated for the removed composer `version` field.
- CHANGELOG 2.6.1 entry included, so tag `2.6.1` on the merge commit.

## Review
Three subagent reviews covered sync correctness, API/docs and test quality, over everything since 2.5.1. All found were addressed except these, which were already true before this release:
- the per-row upsert fallback on drivers without bulk upsert (sqlsrv) can double-count rows committed before a failing row;
- after a failed drain, rows count as both synced and errors in the summary;
- with `--dry-run`, a SCAN duplicate across a batch boundary counts twice in the summary only.

## Tests
208 passed locally (phpredis + Predis on a private Redis 7), PHPStan and Pint clean. New tests from the review were mutation-checked:
- removing the dedupe fails the duplicate-key test;
- removing the clamp hangs the batch-size test;
- removing the failure isolation fails all 12 instrumenter-failure cases;
- per-page flushing fails the batching tests.

author: dannysmp
body:
This pull request makes the deploy script start only the database first, migrate and seed it, and then bring up or replace the rest of the stack, so a new backend image never serves requests against the previous release's schema.

### Summary of Changes

- **Deployment**:
  - `infra/scripts/05-deploy.sh`: the remote script now runs `pull`, `up -d postgres`, the readiness wait, the password rotation, the seed sync, the migration and the seed load, then `up -d` for the whole stack and the closing `restart backend`. Before, `up -d` replaced the backend first, and the migration ran several steps later.
  - `infra/README.md`: the command listing says the full `up -d` runs after the migration and seed.
- **Tests**:
  - `tests/test_deploy_step_order.py`: reads the real script and checks the order of pull, database-only start, rotation, migration, seed load, full start and restart, and that nothing before the migration starts any other service.
  - `tests/test_deploy_postgres_rotation.py`: the extractor of the rotation block now anchors on `up -d postgres`; the Docker-backed tests still run the real block.

### Motivation and Context

A new image on the previous schema fails every dialogue read (an undefined-column error) from the moment `up -d` recreates the backend until the migration finishes: a window of the image-pull-complete `up -d`, the Postgres readiness wait (up to 30 s), the password rotation, the seed sync and the migration. Migrations are additive and idempotent (applied once, recorded, refused if an applied file changes), so applying them while the previous release still serves is safe: it ignores columns it does not know. A fresh host is unaffected: the database is started first and the backend starts on a migrated, seeded database, so it no longer crash-loops until the restart.

### Claims

1. The commands run in the order pull, `up -d postgres`, `ALTER ROLE`, migrate, load seed, full `up -d`, `restart backend`.
2. Nothing before the migration starts a service other than Postgres.
3. The rotation block still runs against real Postgres containers from the real script.
4. Reverting the script to the previous order fails both new tests.

### Verification

| Check | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Format / lint / type-check | `make lint` | clean |
| Tests | `uv run pytest tests/test_deploy_step_order.py tests/test_deploy_postgres_rotation.py -q` | 4 passed |
| Revert-check | script restored to `origin/main`, new test file run | 2 failed |
| Syntax | `bash -n infra/scripts/05-deploy.sh` | ok |

### Security, Privacy and Observability

- **Data handled:** none new; the same secrets are resolved in the same place.
- **Controls:** unchanged; no new permission, secret or network path.
- **Telemetry:** none.

### Risks and Rollback

- **Risks:** a migration that removes or renames a column the previous release reads would now break the previous release during the window before the new image starts; the migrations in this project are additive. The extra `up -d` is idempotent.
- **Rollback:** revert this commit; the previous order is restored with no data change.

### Known Gaps and Follow-ups

Only the order is verified here; the first deploy that uses it is the proof on the live host.

author: apowers313
body:
The review server's inbox put a pull request under "Ready for you" even when one of its stories failed to capture, and the notifier announced it. Example: #617 was announced as ready while graphty-element's data--cytoscape-session had failed with "page.screenshot: Timeout 30000ms exceeded". The inbox only checked whole-project problems (a failed job, a failed download), never the items inside a capture.

What changes:

- A pull request with any item whose status is "failed" goes to "Not ready" with the project, the story and the reason ("capture failed: menu--open: story render errored", plus "(and N more)"). The notifier reads only the ready list, so it never announces it. Unstable items are unchanged: they stay reviewable, as the design describes.
- Opening a failed item showed "the downloaded copy is damaged; reload the page to download it again". A failed item carries its baseline's hash, but capture never copies that baseline into the artifact, so the page asked for a file that is not there, and the server reported damage and deleted the capture's results.json. The server now answers "no such image" for a failed item and makes no thumbnail of it; the page fetches nothing for it and shows "No capture: it failed" with the reason, beside "Baseline not shown: the capture failed".

Tests: the server holds a failed-story pull request in "Not ready" with its reason, the notifier sends nothing for it, and an image request for it is a 404 with no damage message; the page lists it under "Not ready" and shows a failed item with no damaged-download message.

author: bolgunn
body:
## HU 15 — Dashboard de conversión y tiempos del proceso comercial

New page **Métricas** (`/metricas`) for ejecutivos and tenant admins. It shows:

- capture, the stage funnel with the overall conversion, and leads that went from "En plan de mejora" to a sale;
- plan → venta;
- the sales cycle, plus the time in each stage and between consecutive stages;
- engagement and contact follow-up;
- a per-project comparison, and affinity / capacity bands;
- a breakdown by project, affinity, capacity and priority;
- an **Evoluciones históricas** tab with the same metrics by week, month or year.

- **Plan:** `docs/stories/HU15-dashboard-conversion-tiempos/PLAN.md`
- **Algorithm:** `docs/algorithms/ALG-18-commercial-funnel-metrics.md` + `ALG-18-cases.json` (37 cases), the spec for every number on the page
- **Demo data:** `docs/stories/HU15-dashboard-conversion-tiempos/DEMO.md` (seed, check and teardown scripts in `backend/scripts/`)

### How it works

1. **`commercial_funnel_facts()`** (`security definer`, granted to `authenticated` only) returns `{ now, proyectos, facts }`. Migration `20261005150000` creates it; `20261005160000` redefines it so the plan comes from the plan acceptance (G32).
   - **Scope:** the caller's inmobiliaria. An ejecutivo gets only the projects where they are `vinculado`. A global admin, or an ejecutivo without an inmobiliaria, gets `forbidden`.
   - **Privacy:** no profile id, email, stage reason or actor leaves the database. `lead_id` is a row number, and "made by me" (`por_mi`) is computed in SQL. Another inmobiliaria's project ids are sent as `null`.
   - **`now`** is the database's clock (G27).
   - **Universe:** a lead stays in the dashboard while it has a stage record on one of your projects, even if it no longer belongs to that project (G28).
2. **`computeFunnelMetrics()`** (`frontend/src/lib/commercial/funnelMetrics.js`) implements ALG-18 R0–R14 as a pure function. Bands come from ALG-10 unchanged, and the overall stage from `overallStage()`.
3. **`CommercialMetrics.jsx`** only renders, following the reviewed mock (`frontend/mockups/hu15-metricas.html`). Charts are inline SVG, with no new dependency.

### Acceptance criteria

| AC | Where on the page |
| :- | :---------------- |
| **E1** — capture rate, overall conversion, conversion between stages, "En plan de mejora" → "Venta cerrada" | Funnel card (rates on top, conversion from the previous stage on each bar) and KPIs. The funnel bar counts leads that skipped "En plan de mejora" and says how many; the "Registrados en 'En plan de mejora' que cerraron venta" figure counts only recorded stages (R12). "Ventas con plan de mejora" (R4) shows the accepted-plan impact |
| **E2** — average days from preevaluación to sale, times between states | "Ciclo de venta" KPI (average, median as hint); "Tiempo en cada etapa" and "Tiempo entre etapas" tables, both average first. Skipped stages are counted apart, never given an invented time (R13) |
| **E3** — filter and break down engagement and conversion by project, capacity, priority, affinity | Filter bar, and the "Desglose de engagement y conversión" table with all four dimensions side by side (R14). **Selecting a project narrows the universe to that project's leads** (G33), so the page matches that project's breakdown row |
| **E4** — week / month / year evolution of engagement, conversion and times | **Evoluciones históricas** tab: cohorts, conversion rates per cohort, active and contacted leads, and times. The AC text says "evaluaciones históricas"; the tab is named for what it shows |

### Decisions taken during the build (recorded in ALG-18 and the plan)

- **G26:** in the history tab, leads still in a stage count as "en curso" only in the running period.
- **G27:** `now` comes from the database, not the browser clock.
- **G28:** a stage record on one of your projects keeps the lead in the universe and in that project's row.
- **G29–G31:** overall conversion, "En plan de mejora" → venta (R12), time between stages (R13) and the breakdown (R14), added from the AC wording.
- **G32:** the plan is the lead's accepted plan (`plan_accepted`), not the HU 13 tracking baseline, which every lead gets on its first evaluation.
- **G33:** a selected project narrows the universe to its leads, and the comparison and breakdown tables show only that project. Supersedes D3 (AC review, 2026-10-06).
- **Step 12:** ALG-18's note added to ALG-10's A1 assumption (text only, no number changed).

### Verification

- **vitest:** 506 tests pass, including:
  - all 37 ALG-18 cases, with invariants 1–21 checked on every output, plus determinism, frozen input, facts after `now`, and filter monotonicity;
  - the priority-label parity test against `constants.py`;
  - the Santiago calendar (ISO weeks, DST changes);
  - the service, and the `/metricas` routes.
- **SQL:** `supabase/tests/commercial_funnel_facts.sql` passes on a disposable postgres:16 with bootstrap + `schema.sql` + migrations.
  - Four deliberately broken versions of the function each fail a test.
  - The rollbacks remove what they should, and the migrations re-apply idempotently.
  - `commercial_stage*.sql` and `evaluations_staff_select.sql` pass.
- **Browser:** checked with fake facts: both tabs, filters, best-leads switch, band click-to-filter, week/month/year, empty / forbidden / ejecutivo states, no horizontal scroll at 375 px. The AC-review changes (G33, E1 wording, E2 column order, tab name) were checked by rendering the page with fake facts in a throwaway test, not in a browser.
- **Pre-existing, unrelated:** `hu13_tracking.sql` fails on clean `develop` too ("authenticated can UPDATE evaluations").

### Migrations and deploy

| Migration | In production? |
| :-------- | :------------- |
| `20261005130000_restore_evaluations_staff_select` (also on `main` via PR #113) | ✅ applied |
| `20261005150000_hu15_commercial_funnel_facts` | ✅ applied |
| `20261005160000_hu15_funnel_plan_accepted` | ❌ **not yet** |

Checked with `supabase migration list --linked` on 2026-10-06.

The preview already loads against production. Until `20261005160000` is applied, though, "Ventas con plan de mejora" and the plan engagement actions read the old source (`tracking_plans`), which counts every lead as having a plan. After merge, the CTO applies it with `supabase db push`, never through the SQL editor. Every rollback is in `supabase/rollback/`.

author: albert-gao
body:
## Summary
- BA stores no message queue now. While a Turn runs, a message steers it (`submitInput`) or waits in the client, then goes out as ordinary chat, one message at a time or as a `chat({ messages })` batch.
- Session inputs only steer now. They return `steer_not_available` when no Turn can take a steer. Receipts end `committed`, `not_placed`, or `uncertain`. `stop` returns as soon as the stop is recorded.
- Tool approvals use one `continueChat` / `continue_chat` call that carries the whole round and streams the Turn. The docs no longer mention resumeChat, runInputs, promote/delete/resume inputs, decide/join, whenBusy, or paused.
- The chat recipe's React client holds its own queue. It removes a message from the queue before sending it and never rebuilds the queue from receipts.
- The snippet type-check now pins `@blazingagents/sdk@0.20.0` and `blazing-agents==0.14.0`. Before the doc edits, 28 snippets failed against the new SDKs.

author: fol2
body:
Part of #660, step R3.2: the floor. Evidence and every launch are in [`docs/design/2026-10-02-map-living-land/r3/r3-2-floor/`](docs/design/2026-10-02-map-living-land/r3/r3-2-floor/README.md).

Act I's forest floor is now baked once per land, at run time, behind the veil. The bake draws a top-down world-space picture of the lit floor at 16 texels a metre, with a mask at 8. The picture holds:

- the soft key shadows of every static caster;
- contact occlusion;
- an analytic pool under every lamp.

The bake copies on the GPU, with no readback.

The live floor is unshaded and takes no live shadow. It draws one sample of the picture, one of the mask and one of a tiled micro detail. The detail's grain is the gravel. Each pool flickers with its own flame's phase. Standing water is darker ground that glints. Reduce Motion holds both still.

The pilgrim stands on a soft blob shadow. The live shadow pass keeps only the gateway arch, the slate outcrops and the bridges' parapets. Terrain_paint lite no longer draws Act I's ground; it stays as the fallback and for the bridge decks.

Acts II–IV keep their floors. They are painted landscapes with no 3D land to bake.

## Round 3 (head `c7646869`, code `0fb33aed`)

Round 3 accepted the art and asked for two things. Both are measured on the iPad 8 with the QA app only, under the device lock.

### 1. The title after an install or an update

**How a fresh install was made.** Each "fresh" QA build had its five floor shaders (`floor_paint`, `floor_mask`, `floor_caster`, `floor`, `floor_mip`) changed in a scratch worktree before export, by `shader_nonce.py`. It adds one uniform, `uniform float qa_nonce_<tag> = 1.0;`, multiplied into each shader's output. The picture is unchanged, but the shader source and every pipeline's hash are new. Each build had its own tag (`r3a`–`r3m`), never reused, and was installed over the QA app as an update is, with its data kept. The cached launch is that build's second launch. Main's build is the same throughout, so main is always cached. Nothing was deleted on the iPad or the Mac to make this condition.

**The change.**

- `presentation/map/landscape/floor_warm.gd:40` (`warm`) and `:87` (`draw_now`): draws a sample of every pipeline the bake and the floor use, twice, with `RenderingServer.force_draw(false)`. That happens before the title's first frame, behind the launch screen, on meshes of the bake's own kinds.
- `floor_warm.gd:108` (`_canvas`): the 2D samples, in views of the bake's kinds, with the bake's own mip chain. Each sample's command goes to the renderer as it is built (`:126`, `:141`). A node sends its 2D commands only in the next frame's redraw, so the 2D samples had been drawing nothing. That left a 0.4–0.5 s frame at the bake's last step (batches O–Q).
- `presentation/map/landscape/floor_bake.gd:268` (`mip_views`) and `:322` (`texture_rd`): the mip chain and the picture's format, shared with the warm-up.
- `application/main.gd:1330` (in `_show_title`): a title with no run to resume warms too.
- Proofs, each mutation-proven: `tests/test_map_floor.gd`, and `tools/check_floor_bake.gd`. The latter checks that every 2D view of the warm-up draws in its forced draws (4 of 4), the warm-up's mip chain, and that its picture is freed.

**The title-path table** (ms; fresh launches; main in the same batch in brackets):

| Batch | Build: the warm-up | Frame 0, fresh (main) | Frames after frame 0 over 100 ms | First open, worst frame (main) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T | `2c759d39`: drawn on the title's first frame | 3140.0 (569.8, 542.1) | 1368.6 | 173.4 (302.9, 210.0) |
| G | scratch: surfaces no view draws | 1904.8 (489.2, 537.9) | 2177.9, 1709.2 | 199.1 (180.9, 195.1) |
| I | scratch: materials only | 890.2 | 2718.8, 1883.4 | 672.2 |
| K | scratch: a sample a visible frame | 3630.3 (499.2) | 1052.5, 803.7 | 176.6 (193.5) |
| M | `a2a86ad9`: forced draws, launch screen | 5390.7, 5596.0 (333.4, 368.1) | 401.9, 417.4 | 185.7, 194.3 (195.2, 200.0) |
| O | `afeaf175` | 5362.8, 5483.8 (483.8, 368.2) | 408.9, 407.1 | 180.6, 183.4 (177.0, 199.4) |
| P | `f1f074ac` | 5874.5, 5779.4 (341.6, 363.5) | 424.6, 436.9 | 174.8, 175.7 (188.3, 239.6) |
| **R** | **`0fb33aed`** | **6588.1, 6424.1** (361.4, 499.1) | **none** (worst 52.5, 49.7) | 208.3, 176.6 (166.8, 192.4) |
| R, cached | `0fb33aed` | 549.2, 386.9 | none (46.9, 42.4) | 167.7, 172.5 |

**Against the acceptance (batch R):**

- **No title frame after frame 0 over 100 ms: met.** Fresh 52.5 and 49.7; cached 46.9 and 42.4.
- **Frame 0 within 1 s of main's: not met on a fresh install.** It is +5.9 to +6.2 s, behind the launch screen. Cached, it is +0.19 s at most.
- **First open's worst frame no worse than now (173.4): not met on one fresh launch, 208.3.** The open compiles nothing now. Over M, O, P and R its median is 182.0 ms (main's: 193.8).

**Why frame 0 cannot come within 1 s.** The floor's cold compile on the iPad 8 is about 6 s. A sample that compiles costs 0.8–3.2 s (batch K). Making pipelines ahead without drawing did not cover the bake: materials alone (I) and undrawn surfaces (G) both left 1.7–2.7 s stalls. So with every visible frame under 100 ms, the compile can only sit before the title's first frame. On this engine the first two acceptance lines conflict, and the head keeps "nothing visible waits".

Two design calls could reconcile them:

- **Fewer floor pipelines.** The bake could keep the platform's soft-shadow quality. That is unmeasured for compile time, and it changes the baked shadows' filter.
- **No bake under the title on the first launch after an update.** That moves about 6 s into the first open, behind the veil.

### 2. The cold open

**The change.** `presentation/map/landscape/floor_bake.gd:199` (in `_start`): behind the veil the bake's throwaway first draw shares the set-up frame. Paced under the title, it keeps its own frame. `tools/check_floor_bake.gd` expects the new frame count.

**The levers** (batches H and J; ready − built, ms):

- **V0**, round 2: 164.9, 164.8.
- **V1**, the merged set-up frame: 150.1, 146.6, 119.2, 150.0. **Taken.**
- **Four tiles a frame, tall tiles, one view** (V2–V4): 152.9–168.6, with frames of 81–98 ms. No faster.
- **The platform's soft shadow** (V5): 129.7, 133.3.
- **V5 plus the mask in the set-up frame** (V7): 103.5, 100.8.

V5 and V7 change the baked shadows' filter, so they are not taken without the owner's eye.

**The cold-open table** (ms; two interleaved installs each):

| Batch | Head | Branch | Branch median | Main median | Branch − main | Bake wall; worst frame |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E (round 2) | `2c759d39` | 2632.4, 2613.2 | 2622.8 | 2322.8 | +300.0 | 142.6, 138.2; 64.7 |

**The floor reached.** The branch costs +126 to +149 ms over main in every batch (+300 in E). Nearly all of it is the bake: 117–132 ms over four vsync frames, the largest the lit tiles' 62–67 ms. The absolute median follows main's own cold open, which moved from 2250 to 2476 ms between batches on the same iPad.

- Under 2.5 s: in N, in N3 and pooled.
- Over 2.5 s: in N4, where main itself took 2475.7.

So 2.5 s holds only while main stays under about 2.35 s. The one lever left, the platform's soft shadow, saves about 15–45 ms and changes the accepted picture.

Run 37265259209 (fleet-converge mode=gcp_iam_converge, srv1) failed filing: POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/approvals → 503 'writer authority is held by the approval broker process'.

**Root cause.** `gunbc.auth.approval_request_client` `approval_loopback_origin` read the roadmap instance's listen bind (`srv1_live_dashboard_instance`). That was right while the roadmap held the store; #12747 flipped `approval_cutover_posture` to `BrokerServesAndWrites`, so writer authority (`gunbc.auth.approval_writer_authority`) and the front-door mounts (`approval_broker_cutover` `approval_front_door_mounts_installed`) both moved to the broker — but the client's origin was a second, undeclared answer to "who writes" and stayed on the roadmap.

**Fix (no cutover state changed).** The origin is now `approval_loopback_origin_for(approval_writer_process(approval_writer_authority))`: roadmap bind for `RoadmapProcess`, `approval_broker_endpoint` `approval_broker_loopback_base_url(approval_broker_listen_port)` for `BrokerProcess`. The submit path is `approval_broker_submit_path` (the existing path authority) instead of a second `/approvals` literal. Consumers `approval_gate` (submit + status poll) and `spark.pair_serving_d0_door` follow unchanged.

## Scope

Inspect CommonStopState and extract only its genuinely neutral dispatch-once latch. Not general LoopOutcome, full CommonStopState neutralization, neutral processAgentPrompt, or completed PR3. Draft pending required CI.

## Exact files changed

- src/core/agent/stop_control.zig (new)
- src/core/agent/runtime/orchestrator.zig
- src/core/agent/agent_runtime.zig (test import)
- docs/stop-control.md (new)

## Inspection and boundary

CommonStopState has four fields:

- dispatched: neutral once-per-turn control; two successful dispatch writes and four redispatch/steering-phase checks.
- retained_candidate: assistant/history/result materialization, deliberately excluded.
- latest_partial: streamed assistant materialization, deliberately excluded.
- terminal_materializing: finalization/persistence effect state, deliberately excluded.

Stop dispatch outcomes use lifecycle, provider disposition, assistant text and allocated hook continuation messages; they remain outside. Cancellation still belongs to LoopControl/TurnCoordinator, not a second flag.

`StopControl` imports only std and contains exactly one bool, dispatched=false, with needsDispatch and idempotent markDispatched. CommonStopState.control owns the sole latch. The old direct bool is removed. No hidden references, generic context, job/deps/config, model/history/result/persistence/authority data.

Construction stays at the existing per-turn CommonStopState initialization in processQueuedPromptInner. This is the natural owner of a fresh latch; no captured host data is required, so no unnecessary compatibility projection is introduced.

The two successful stop checkpoint returns call markDispatched at the same location as prior assignment. Cancelled dispatch branches still exit/continue before marking. Existing continuation keeps the latch set, preserving once-per-turn semantics. Four checks preserve the same polarity and branch timing.

Before: CommonStopState owns dispatch latch alongside materialization.
After: CommonStopState owns typed neutral StopControl plus unchanged materialization fields; loop consumes the sole control state.

No loop ordering/retry/attempt/step/steering/tool/stream/cancellation/recovery/compaction/finalization algorithm changes. Queue/ingress/ModelProvider/adapters/auth/billing/tools/MCP/skills/TUI/storage/distribution/Compute/PAX/FeltDB/AppPort/WASM and guard are untouched.

## Validation

- zig build -Doptimize=Debug -j1: passed with Zig 0.16.0.
- bun test tests/e2e/configured-providers.test.ts: **53 passed, 0 failed, 254 assertions**, against freshly built binary. Includes real coding loop and existing streaming/error/authorization/cancellation regressions.
- Focused stop/finalization/interruption/orchestrator gateway-flow/Agent/worker suite: **510 passed**, including real dispatch, continuation/cancel steering, retained-candidate materialization and relevant passing allocation failures.
- Independent zig test src/core/agent/stop_control.zig: **1 passed**, validating exact single-bool surface, initial eligibility, idempotence and no marking for cancelled dispatch. No allocations introduced.
- Manual rebuilt binary localhost PTY: omitted Authorization, response rendered, /quit exit 0.
- Formatting/whitespace/public-surface/compactor-boundary checks: passed.

No full repository suite, broad allocation sweep or exact Linux/macOS CI success claimed. Known tool_host.zig:938 broad allocation failure remains out of scope.

## Guard and remaining execution environment

Guard byte-for-byte unchanged (SHA-256 verified): **1,509 before → 1,509 after**. New module is std-only. Existing compatibility/provider/history/recovery/usage closures remain reachable, and no guard findings were excluded/reclassified.

The loop still carries legacy job/deps/config/capabilities, conversation/replay/images/grants/context/skills, transport/results, recovery, lifecycle/finalization and stop candidate/partial/materialization. This extraction intentionally does not create completed/cancelled/failure outcome enums because their current consumers couple them to lifecycle and materialization; a later slice should first isolate typed decisions from those effects rather than drag them into neutral control.

body: _Requested by **jimmy**_ Before: When the server couldn't be reached, Home showed nothing but a full-screen "Can't Reach the Server", after waiting up to a minute for a server that didn't answer. With no connection at all, it said the same. On every launch, Home showed placeholders until the server answered. After: - **Home opens on the rows it last showed**, kept on the device, and swaps in the server's rows when they arrive. - **When the server can't be reached, those rows stay**, under a banner saying what's wrong and when they're from, such as "Last updated 9:41 AM", with Try Again. - **Home asks again by itself** after a failure, when the device joins a network or Serafin comes back to the foreground. - **With no connection at all**, every screen now says "You're Offline" instead of "Can't Reach the Server". - **A server that doesn't answer is given up on after 30 seconds** instead of a minute. - **Clear Cache also deletes the saved Home**, and signing out or removing a server deletes that account's. Completes `docs/PLAN.md` task **2.11 Error and offline behaviour**. Stacked on #24. | Server off | Dark | Largest text | | --- | --- | --- | | | | | In the iPhone 17 simulator, against the stand-in server, with the server stopped. ### Tried in the simulator - With the stand-in server stopped, Home opened on the last rows with the banner. A refused connection fails at once, so the banner showed straight away. - With a stand-in that accepts connections and never answers, the saved rows showed at once. There was no banner at 25 seconds, and the banner was there at 33. - After starting the server again, Try Again brought fresh rows and took the banner away. So did leaving Serafin and coming back, both for the banner and for the full-screen failure Home shows when nothing is saved. - Pull to refresh with the server off kept the rows and showed the banner, dated from the last load that worked. - Clear Cache deleted the saved Home and the artwork. With the server off, Home then showed the full-screen failure. - "You're Offline" itself can't be shown in the simulator, which uses the Mac's connection. Tests cover it. ### A fix along the way On cellular, the first video after each launch streamed under the Wi-Fi cap. The network watcher started at that video, and a new watcher reports no network until the system first answers it, a moment later, so the video didn't count as on cellular. The watcher now starts with the tabs. ### How - **`HomeSnapshotStore`** in SerafinCore keeps each account's last Home as JSON in Caches, one file per account, named by a SHA-256 hash of the account. - Files are written with complete file protection, are never backed up, and iOS may delete them when space runs low. - A file that's too large, won't decode, or is in another format version is deleted and ignored. One that can't be read yet, as while the device is locked, is kept. - **`LibraryRepository.home()`** now loads Home's rows itself, moved from `LiveMediaSource`, and saves them. A failed or cancelled load never replaces the saved Home. `savedHome()` reads it back. - **`HomeModel`** shows the saved rows while the first load runs. A failed load keeps the rows on screen with a notice, or fills the screen when there are none. - **`NoticeBanner`** in SerafinDesign is a plain panel that scrolls with the content rather than glass, since it's content. - Its button sits beside the text where it fits, and under it where it doesn't. At accessibility sizes the symbol moves above the text. - When it appears, Serafin posts it as a VoiceOver announcement. I haven't heard that with VoiceOver, which the simulator doesn't have. - **`NetworkWatcher`** now publishes whether the device is online and through what. After a failure, Home asks again when that changes. - **`SerafinError.offline`** covers no connection, cellular data turned off for Serafin, and roaming turned off. Adding a server stops there instead of trying the other port. - **`ClientFactory`** gives requests to the server a 30-second timeout. Images and streams keep their own. ### Choices worth a look - **The saved Home is a file format on disk**, which AGENTS.md asks you to approve. It's a cache, though: a file in another version is deleted and rebuilt from the server on the next visit to Home, so nothing ever needs migrating. I treated it as reversible. Say if you'd rather approve it first. - **Saved rows show on every launch**, not only offline, so Home appears at once and updates a moment later. The banner appears only once a load fails, so a server that's slow to answer shows the saved rows without a banner until the timeout. - **30 seconds** is half URLSession's default, and still gives a slow server time for its first answer after a library scan. - **Only Home is saved.** Library, Search and detail screens still need the server, and say "You're Offline" or "Can't Reach the Server" with Try Again. ### Definition of done - [x] `xcodegen generate` and the build succeed with zero warnings, in Debug for the simulator and in Release for devices (Xcode 27.0) - [x] `swift test` passes, with 31 new tests: - the saved Home: kept per account, replaced, removed, cleared, damaged, in another version, oversized, unreadable for now, and its file names - Home loading from the server and keeping what it loaded, one library failing, and a failure keeping the saved Home - signing out, removing a server and Clear Cache deleting saved Homes - offline and unreachable errors, the 30-second timeout, and adding a server while offline - Home's saved rows, the notice, the full-screen failure, and the banner's dates - [x] `xcodebuild test` passes on an iPhone 17e simulator (365 tests) - [x] `swift format lint --recursive --strict` is clean - [x] The banner has light, dark and largest-text previews - [x] No new dependencies, ATS keys or entitlements - [x] Public API has doc comments - [x] CI green on this PR 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: petec4244
body:
Z2-I2 (PLAN-z, hand test 2026-10-04 CONSEQUENCE line): a driver for the **built app in its real window**. Tools only; no crate is touched.

## What it is

`tools/real_window/driver.py --app <hiwave binary>` starts a fresh app per check on a throwaway profile (`HOME` set for the app process only, so the person's tabs and vault are untouched), restored on a page from `tools/real_window/pages/` served by a local fixture server, and asserts on:

- the fixture's request log (pages report what their scripts did with `fetch('/beacon?name')`),
- the app's log,
- the window's pixels (`screencapture -l <window id>`, counts of flat colours),
- after real input: `hwdrive.swift` posts HID events at the window and resizes it through Accessibility.

Checks: `h1`, `h1_slow`, `h2`, `h3`, `h4`, `h4_slow`, `h6` for hand-test items H1-H4 and H6. Every assertion ends PASS, FAIL or NOT RUN; NOT RUN names what the seat lacks and is not a pass. `tools/real_window/README.md` has the rest.

## What has run and what has not

This seat (the Z lane's launchd session) has **no Accessibility, post-event or Screen Recording grant, and the screen was locked**:

```
{"accessibility": false, "display_asleep": false, "display_points": [3440, 1440], "display_scale": 1, "post_events": false, "screen_capture": false, "screen_locked": true}
```

- **Run:** launching the app from this worktree's build, the isolated profile, the fixture server, every request-log and app-log assertion, `hwdrive preflight` and `hwdrive window`.
- **Never executed, not once:** `hwdrive move / click / press / release / scroll / key / type / resize / activate / request`, the driver's `frame()` and every assertion on pixels. They compile. Expect fixes the first time they run. The colour counter was checked on one generated 200x100 PNG (20000 magenta pixels counted).
- A locked screen stops input and capture whatever the grants: posted events go to the login window and `screencapture` answers `could not create image from display`. So the pixel and input half needs the grants **and** an unlocked Mac.

## What it found on the real app (develop 15d2c3a6)

Not reproduced at the level this seat can see (requests and logs; the window was not seen):

- **H1, simple case:** after the load, one-second ticks keep running, a fetch started by a tick reaches its `then()`, and an image a tick adds is requested and logged as `Loaded images added by live page scripts`.
- **H4:** all five images of a five-image page are requested, and the engine logs `Loaded images count=5`.
- **H2, script side:** when the side panel takes 220 px after the load, the page hears `resize` with `innerWidth` 1060 (was 1280). That is the same `apply_layout -> set_bounds` call a window resize makes.

Reproduced, red:

- **`h1_slow`: one request held for 3 s stops the page for exactly 2.00 s, and never settles.** A 200 ms tick was steady (widest gap 0.20 s). From the moment the page's `fetch('/slow?ms=3000')` reached the server: no tick for 2.00 s, then ten ticks within 10 ms, then 200 ms spacing again. Neither `then` nor `catch` of the slow request ran in the following 6.6 s.
  - Where the 2.00 s comes from, read in the code and not measured beyond the number matching: `RustKitView::process_events` runs `runtime.block_on(engine.pump_live(..))` on the app's event-loop thread, and `pump_live` awaits `script_net::pump_all` with `LIVE_NETWORK_BUDGET` = 2 s. While it waits, the loop handles no input and renders nothing.
  - Not shown: that this is what Pete saw as H1, H3 or H6 on real sites. It would fit (a page with a request in flight most of the time has a loop that is mostly waiting), and the driver's `h3` and `h6` can say once they can run.
- In `h1` the same thing shows as a late sixth tick: five ticks run inside the load at +0.1 s (the load's timer rounds), the fetch a tick started is answered at +2.2 s, and tick six comes at +3.2 s instead of one second after tick five.

- **`h4_slow` (added in 15b79643): an image a script adds after the load, held for 3 s, stops the page for the whole 3.00 s.** Run on the app built from #533's branch (c6b81875, app sha256 `6170232e...9732`), where `h1_slow` passes: no tick at all in the 3 s the image was out (`0 ticks in the 3 s it was out, widest gap 3.00 s`), then the engine logs `Loaded images added by live page scripts`. Read in the code: `pump_live` awaits `load_images_added_by_scripts` on the same thread.

author: amahpour
body: The second of #80's three MVP pull requests: the board's page in the web UI, and the person's moves on it. Agents already work the board through the `review` tool (#149). Now the person sees it as lanes, and does their 10%: answers the questions, rules on findings the agents couldn't agree on, drops what isn't worth doing, and closes the board. ## Assumptions This follows the plan the maintainer approved on 2026-10-04 ("Yes, build it"; screen D of #80, the lanes with the person's lane on top). The choices below are mine: - **A person's decision is their own message in the room.** For example: "Review board: Q1 (Discount before or after tax?) answered: Before tax". That way it reaches the agents the way anything a person says does, with their name on it. A notice wouldn't wake anyone, and an answered question usually means an agent has work to do. - **The board replaces the log, behind a header button.** The composer stays, so the person can still talk to the agents. The button shows only in a room that has a board. - **Closing is behind a confirm, and dropping needs a reason.** Both match the agents' rules from #149. - **Not yet:** Post, which is the third PR. ## What it does - **The page.** A header button swaps the log for the board. - **Lanes:** Needs you (open questions and contested findings, first and full width), then Raised, Being fixed, Done and Dropped. - **Cards:** each shows its label, state, title, file:lines and who raised or owns it. Clicking one opens its detail: the evidence through md.js, the reason or commit, and the person's moves. - **Layout:** the lanes fit any width, and the detail moves below the lanes on narrow screens. - **The moves.** - A question: one button per option, with the recommended one marked. - A contested finding: pick an agent in the room and **Concede**. - Any open item: **Drop**, which needs a reason. - The whole board: **Close board**. - **The data.** - `GET /api/rooms/{slug}/review` returns the board to any signed-in session. - `POST /api/rooms/{slug}/review` takes `action`, `item`, and then `option`, `owner` or `reason`. It needs a signed-in person and the `X-Switchboard` header, like `say`, and unknown fields are refused. - The web subscriber now takes the hub's `review` frames, so the board updates live. A closed board's frame is `null`. - **Text stays text.** Every string on the page comes from an agent: plain text through `textContent`, the detail through md.js, and the pull request's URL through `externalLink`, the one link path. ## Previews There's no before: no page showed a board until now. The made-up shop pull request (#80's mockups), seeded by two scripted agents through the real tool from a throwaway home (`docs/media/ui_shots.py`), with Q1 open: ## Verification ```console $ uv run python scripts/lint.py ruff: 96 existing findings, 0 new mypy: 39 existing findings, 0 new $ uv run pytest -q -n auto 2858 passed, 7 skipped $ uv run pytest -m e2e tests/e2e 50 passed $ # the board tests, 20 times each, alone e2e board: 20/20 integration: 20/20 ``` New tests, each failing on `main`, which has no routes and no page: - **`test_a_person_answers_rules_and_closes_from_the_web`** (integration): - the board as JSON with what needs the person; - a bad option and a wrong move refused; - the answer and the ruling posted as the person's own messages, which the agents read; - close, then a new board for another pull request. - **`test_the_board_routes_need_a_signed_in_person_and_the_write_header`:** 401 with no session, 403 without `X-Switchboard`, 400 for unknown fields. - **e2e, a room seeded by two scripted agents through the real tool** (`UIWorld.seed_review`, the made-up shop pull request from #80's mockups): - **Lanes:** the button and the lanes, each item in its lane, and the URL as a checked external link. - **Answer and ruling:** answering Q1 and conceding F3 move the cards at once, and both decisions show in the log. - **Drop and close:** a drop needs a reason, and close asks first. - **Phone:** light and dark, with no sideways scroll. - `UIWorld.add_agents` now keys its agents' sessions by room too, so a name like `claude-1` can be used in more than one test room. ## Docs - **DESIGN §37.5:** the page, the data, the person's moves and the tests. It was marked "next" before. - **USAGE:** "Review a pull request in a room" now covers the page, with a screenshot (`docs/media/ui/board-light.png`). - **`docs/media/ui_shots.py`:** board shots in light, dark and on a phone, in a room of their own so no #build shot changes. - **`changes/review-board-page.md`:** the release note. - **Checked and unchanged:** SECURITY.md. No new authority: the moves are the person's, through the same checked write path as `say`. Part of #80 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: azality
body:
## Why

Office, 5 Oct: *"if I want to select class 1 to class 6 for the same announcement there should be a way to multi select"*. The **Whole class** and **Parents of a class** audiences took exactly one class from a dropdown, so the same notice had to be posted once per grade.

## What

**One announcement, many classes** — picked as chips:

- The class dropdown is now a **chip multi-select** (with Select all / Clear all). The hint names every picked class and the publish button previews the reach: `Publish → ~84 students' families` for Classes I–III.
- The announcements **list and detail view name the targeted classes** ("Parents of a class — Class I, Class II") instead of just the kind.
- Works for **repeating announcements** too (the standing-rule instances copy the full class list).

## How

- **DB** (already applied live; `20261005_announcement_multi_class.sql` is the record): `audience_class_ids uuid[]` on `announcement` + `announcement_recurrence`. The legacy `audience_class_id` keeps mirroring the **first** pick, and matchers treat a missing array as `[audience_class_id]` — so every existing row renders and matches unchanged, and an old bundle mid-deploy still posts fine.
- **Edge** (`v1.25.0-multi-class-announcements`): POST validates every id is org-owned in one query; the portal feed matches class kinds on array overlap via a single `audienceClassIdsOf()` helper.
- **Suite check 138**: a post to `[other, Sandbox]` reaches the Sandbox parent even though Sandbox is *not* the mirrored first id (proves matching reads the array); `[other]` alone stays invisible; empty list → 400.

## Verified

Dev server as the QA admin (screenshot in session): chips toggle, hint + reach preview update live. Nothing was published to real parents — the end-to-end path is check 138's job after the edge deploy.

**On merge: edge deploy + regression suite** (check 138 needs the new edge), then frontend build + deploy.

body:
## What

`setup-multiplayer` 2.0.0 (#50) tells agents to set `max_view_age_msec = 250` and to **leave `retention_msec` at its default of 350**.

Only engine `main` defaults to 350 (SummerEngine #492). Every released engine still defaults to **250**; the newest runtime candidates, from 2026-09-26, do. On those engines the skill's settings leave no dispatch budget:
- a shot near the view-age cap has to wait behind queued input before it resolves, and by then its history has expired, so it fails as `historical_history_unavailable`;
- the `HIT_HISTORY_DISPATCH_BUDGET` startup warning the skill points to doesn't exist yet in those builds, so nothing explains the failures.

## Change

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `setup-multiplayer` SKILL.md | Step 8 sets `retention_msec = 350` explicitly and says why: an explicit value works on every engine. The startup warning is marked as newer-engine only. |

| `evals/skills/specs/setup-multiplayer.md`, `tests/specs/setup-multiplayer.md` | Now expect the explicit value. |

author: omelei
body:
## Probleem

Het e2e-project `ipad-landscape` (WebKit) faalde steeds weer, en elke keer op een andere plek:
- run 754 op `main`: de uitreiking bereikte de knoppen niet, een tegel op de diplomamuur werd nooit "stabiel", en `page.goto('/')` naar localhost liep na 30 s af;
- run 737 op `main` en runs 740 en 742: `sums.spec.ts:421` en `premium.spec.ts:682`.

Een herhaling van dezelfde commit slaagde wel. De andere vijf projecten faalden nooit op deze manier.

## Oorzaak

De browser krijgt te weinig processortijd. De app zelf wacht nergens op iets dat niet komt. In WebKit tekent elke eindeloze lus van Denker (ADR-259) zijn SVG op de processor opnieuw. Op 1080 px breed met dubbele pixeldichtheid staan de meeste Denkers tegelijk in beeld. Vier workers op één runner, samen met het Android-project, krijgen dan te weinig rekentijd. Een `goto` naar localhost die uit de tijd loopt, past alleen bij die verklaring.

## Oplossing

- `ipad-landscape` draait met `reducedMotion: 'reduce'`. De app kent die stand al (`rustig`): de lussen staan stil en de uitreiking begint meteen aan het eind.
- Er wordt geen test overgeslagen of uitgezet. Alleen de beweging valt weg, en alleen in dit project.
- De beweging blijft getest op de drie Chromium-projecten, op `ipad-portrait` en `iphone` (allebei WebKit), en in de unit-tests van het draaiboek.

## Getest

- `typecheck` en `eslint` zijn groen.
- Lokaal heb ik WebKit niet: die browser is niet geïnstalleerd in deze omgeving. Daarom heb ik `sums`, `doel`, `premium` en `shell` gedraaid op het iPad-liggend-formaat met minder beweging, in Chromium: 38 geslaagd. De ene fout kwam alleen doordat het testproject een andere naam had (de test slaat `ipad-landscape` op naam over).
- De echte bevestiging is deze CI-run. Faalt `ipad-landscape` hierna nog op dezelfde manier, dan klopt de verklaring niet. De volgende stap is dan minder workers op die runner (zie ADR-271).

<!-- 작성 기준과 필수 메타데이터(라벨 구성·예외, assignee)는 docs/pr-checklist.md를 단일 출처로 둡니다. -->

## 의도

계획서에 스크롤백 Find(⌘F)의 잔여 항목으로 「fuzzy」가 남아 있었다. 검토해 보니 터미널 스크롤백에서 fuzzy(검색어 글자가 순서대로만 있으면 매치)는 효과보다 해가 커서, **두지 않기로 결정**하고 그 사유를 문서에 남긴다. 코드 변경은 없다.

## 구현

- 변경한 책임 영역: 계획 문서 세 곳의 「잔여/후속: fuzzy」를 「두지 않는다 + 사유」로 바꿨다.
- 중요한 트레이드오프 (결정 사유):
  - 스크롤백은 긴 줄이 수천~수만이라 `err` 같은 짧은 검색어도 거의 모든 줄에서 순서대로 흩어져 맞는다(오탐).
  - 흩어진 글자는 화면에 칠할 매치 범위가 애매하다(글자만? 첫~끝?).
  - 줄여 찾기는 이미 있는 정규식 모드(`app.*sess`)가 대신한다.
  - fuzzy 점수(`fuzzyScore`)는 짧은 이름 목록에서 하나를 고르는 커맨드 팝업에만 쓴다 — 그쪽은 그대로.
- 의도적으로 하지 않은 것: 단어 시작 글자만 맞추는 절충 모드(필요가 생기면 별도 제안으로).

## 다이어그램

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["⌘F 검색 모드"] --> B["평문 부분일치 (기본)"]
  A --> C["PCRE2 정규식 (⌥⌘R)"]
  A -.->|"두지 않음"| D["fuzzy"]

body:
Brings `main` up to date with `redesign-phase-1`: 12 commits made since 28 September. `main` has no commits of its own, so this merges cleanly.

## What is in it

- **Guest site:** the redesign, room pages with shareable dates, GST shown in prices, gallery and room filters kept in the address, readable colours, search-engine details.
- **Booking:** the booking panel, room holds, a status page for guests, front desk bookings.
- **Food ordering by QR code:** one code per table, one for the counter and one per hotel room. Each code carries a key and orders without it are refused. Guests follow an order by a private link.
- **Paying for food online:** the restaurant kiosk at `/dine-in` and a room's "Pay now" take payment first. The order reaches the kitchen only after the payment is verified. Cancelling a paid order refunds it.
- **Kitchen display:** live updates, a "to cook" summary, room and kiosk orders, cash collected at the door for room orders.
- **Staff:** sign-in by cookie, name tiles and PINs for the kitchen and housekeeping, the front desk's Food orders tab, problem reports from housekeepers, approving a cleaned room when no inspector is on shift.
- **Admin:** resort settings, offers, QR codes to print, dashboard figures, staff and PINs.
- **API:** rate limits per visitor, stricter validation, an activity log for money and cancellations.

## What merging does

- Vercel publishes this version as the live site.
- Render tries to deploy the API from `main`.
- The database needs nothing. Every schema addition here is already applied to the hosted database.

## Before relying on the live site

- **One domain for the site and the API.** Staff sign-in uses cookies, which the browser only sends when both share a domain, for example `yourdomain.in` and `api.yourdomain.in`. On the default `*.vercel.app` and `*.onrender.com` addresses staff cannot sign in. See the notes in `render.yaml`.
- **The API on Render.** Its last deploy from `main` on 28 September is marked failed. Check the service and its environment settings after merging.
- **One API at a time.** The API runs scheduled jobs against the database. A copy running on a laptop with the same database should be stopped once the Render one is up.
- **Payments.** Set `RAZORPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and the webhook before taking real payments. No real payment or refund has been tried yet, only a stand-in.
- **Always-on plan.** `plan: free` sleeps, and the scheduled jobs sleep with it.

## Checks

- Vercel's preview build of the last commit succeeded.
- API changes were exercised in transactions that were rolled back, and the screens were clicked through in a headless browser against a read-only copy of the API.
- The housekeeping approvals were tested in their own session, not as part of the checks above.

body:
## Before

Entry with two declared models, discovery answers 500, non-silent provide (host sweep, Test Connection):

```
1) a non-silent discovery failure serves the declared set, expected or not; only an empty set throws:
   RequestError: The LiteLLM server hit an internal error while listing models.
2) an expected model-listing failure does not soften an unresolved-credentials failure:
   MirroredError: This server entry's credentials could not be resolved ...
```

The provide threw: 0 models registered, while the next silent pass served both.

## After

```
served:  ["gw-model", "gw-model-2"]
status:  state=error  expected=undefined  classification={kind:"http",status:500}  declaredModelCount=2  servedModelCount=2
55 passing (54s)
```

## How

- **One failure rule**: declared models register on every failed serve, silent or not; the failure is still logged and recorded.
- **Nothing declared, non-silent**: still throws, record still names the stale set.
- **Credential preflight failure**: declared models register under an unexpected error; `chatClient.ts` re-resolves credentials before sending.
- **Comments**: the test seam and two fixtures no longer name `expectedFailures` as the prerequisite.

## Proof

- Red on origin/main's `groupDiscovery.ts`: 53 passing, 2 failing (the two cases above). Green with the fix: 55 passing.
- Full host suite: 2475 + 16 + 45 + 3 passing; bun tree 2280; docker serversync, resolution, group-path: 15 + 11 + 1.
- typecheck, biome, knip, l10n, manifest and settings-reference checks green.

body:
## What changes

- **Stand-in picture.** Before an `ard-high-performance` session's media stream delivers, across a display change and across a stream the Mac restarts, the Mac's ZRLE rectangles are decoded and encoded as VP9, as on `ard` with `virtual_display = true`. The stream takes over at its first picture (decoded) or at an IDR (passed).
- **Resize notice.** It covers only a resize in progress and comes down when the display settles, no longer held until the stream's first picture. `DesktopState::covered`, `VideoSink::uncover` and the tab's cover are removed.
- **Slow pacing kept.** The Mac stays armed at one push a second for these sessions.
- **Fast encode.** Stand-in rounds are encoded at `screen-vp9`'s `Speed::Fastest` (`VideoSink::stand_in`); a decoded stream's own pictures stay at the usual speed. Pins `screen-vp9` v0.0.7.
- **While the stream flows** the rectangles are decoded and dropped rather than stepped over, since ZRLE's deflate stream cannot be inflated across a gap. `Decoders::step_over` is removed.
- **Two virtual displays.** Stand-in rectangles are cut to the canvas's display and the second display's tab, and each keeps them until its own leg of the stream has delivered.

## Testing

- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --lib` pass.
- Live on `macvmhighperf` with a `--profile qa` build, before the per-leg liveness commit: a `vp09` `videoFormat` first, then the stream taking over, both decoded and passed (`hev1`).
- Not tested: the two-display target live (unit tests only), a real browser, a physical Mac.

author: rajsinghtech
body:
The web UI is now read-only, and it's published in every connected tailnet as before.

**What changed**

- The server keeps `/`, `/api/status`, `/api/bridges`, `/api/connections`, `/api/logs` and `/api/events`. Every other method gets 405. The config, settings, tailnet/rule CRUD and detect routes are gone, and so are the forms, modals and setup wizard in the page.
- The config file is the only way to change anything. `config.Store` loses `Update` and `save`, `Get` returns a deep copy, and `Watch` gives each listener its own copy. Rule validation moved from the server into `config.Validate`, so a bad rule now fails at load time (unknown source/dest tailnet, ports out of range, duplicate rule names, duplicate short names per destination, local source checks).
- The UI VIP serves the handler directly instead of proxying TCP to the local listener.
- `ui.enabled: false` or `-ui=false` turns off both the local listener and the VIP. Turning `ui.enabled` off in a running instance deletes the UI services it owns (through the ownership guard); turning it on again republishes them.
- The config view in the UI and SSE stream leaves out every tailnet's `oauth` block, so no client ID or secret path is served either.

**Breaking:** editing the config through the UI is gone. That was decided in the roadmap.

**Tests**

- Flips `TestKnownBad_SnapshotsShareState` into `TestStoreGetIsDeepCopy`.
- Unit: every non-GET method on every path (old routes included) gets 404/405, removed routes 404, no secret/client ID/path in any response or the SSE init, no write controls in the page, `-ui=false` and `ui.enabled=false` leave the UI port closed, turning the UI off in a reconcile deletes only our UI service, file watch reloads (and ignores a broken file), rule validation table.
- e2e (testcontrol): the UI is reachable locally and through `svc:tailnetlink` from a client in each tailnet, read routes work, writes are refused, nothing private shows up in any response or a few seconds of SSE; `ui.enabled=false` creates no UI service, toggling it on and off publishes and removes it; editing the config file moves a bridged service to a new port and traffic flows there.
- e2e (real): `TestRealReadOnlyUI` replaces `TestRealNoSecretsOverHTTP` with the same reachability, write-route and secrets checks, from a client in both tailnets.

Coverage is 87.9%, so the floor goes to 87.
