author: skezo
body:
## What

The audio-lead hook for video sync: a page script that moves the page's audio earlier in the player's MSE buffer, while showing the player its own timeline unchanged. The picture is never touched, and the hook never seeks or pauses.

- **What the hook does:** patches `SourceBuffer`/`MediaSource` in the page's MAIN world and virtualises `timestampOffset`, `appendWindow*`, `buffered` and `remove`. It caches segments and switches immediately by remove plus re-append at a fragment boundary.
- **Codec handling:**
  - Cuts are aligned to random access points for audio with non-sync frames (xHE-AAC on Netflix; Chromium drops dependent frames up to the next keyframe).
  - Encrypted audio is shifted in whole frames.
- **Safety:**
  - a freeze watchdog puts the sound back;
  - a live-edge guard stops it running ahead near the live edge;
  - the hook reverts within about 20 s if the extension stops asking.

  It reports "unavailable" for muxed buffers, "sequence"-mode audio and MSE in workers.
- **Build:** the hook and its relay are standalone IIFE page scripts, outside the CRXJS content-script pipeline, so they patch prototypes synchronously and are not web-accessible.
- **Registration:**
  - They are registered with `chrome.scripting.registerContentScripts` (MAIN and ISOLATED, `document_start`, all frames) only while video sync is on and the all-sites permission is granted, and unregistered otherwise.
  - `scripting` is added to the manifest permissions. It adds no install warning, because the extension already matches every site.
- **Bridge:** the postMessage bridge between the relay and the hook is validated (nonce, origin, schema).
- **Tests:** unit tests for the container parsers (fMP4 `moof`/`trun`/`tfhd`/`trex`/`tfdt`/`mdhd`, WebM clusters), RAP and cut planning, and whole-frame rounding.

## Why

The old video sync paused and seeked the page's own video, whose audio is what we cast, so it could never line up. Shifting only the audio inside the player is the approach the lab proved on YouTube (Opus, AAC, live), Netflix (Widevine, xHE-AAC) and Prime (Widevine, encrypted AAC), measuring the shift within a few ms. This PR adds the mechanism; nothing drives it until the next PR.

## How to Test

- CI: the new parser and planner tests.
- Build the extension and turn video sync on, granting site access. Reload a YouTube tab: `window.__tcvs_installed__` is `true`, and `chrome.scripting.getRegisteredContentScripts()` lists `tc-vs-hook` and `tc-vs-relay`. Turn video sync off, and the scripts unregister.
- Verified headless: with a forced 500 ms lead, the audio measured 494 ms early; with the lead off, the shift returns to 0.

## Related Issue

None. Video sync v1, part 2 of 3. Stacks on #230.

body:
Fixes #40250

### Motivation & Context

Python 3.10 officially reached End-of-Life (EOL) on October 1, 2026.
Following Apache Beam's established policy of dropping EOL Python runtimes,
this PR removes all support for Python 3.10 and shifts the minimum supported
Python version to **3.11**.

This mirrors the pattern established by PR #36665 (Python 3.9 removal).

### Changes Made

author: sombochea
body:
## Summary
- `ziroctl cluster node role <node> builder|runner|gateway on|off`: one place to split a cluster's work. `runner off` keeps new replicas off a node (the scheduler now honours the `runner` label); `builder` and `gateway` use the existing `builder` label and `Gateway` flag (the one `ziroctl gateway node enable` sets). Nodes still do everything by default. `cluster nodes` shows `NoRunner`.
- Builder failover: if the node building a deployment goes `NotReady`, the master drops its task and gives the build to another builder (up to 2 times, skipping nodes that already lost it). A late result from the lost builder has no task to match and is ignored.
- Uploaded source on a cluster (from #83): the master records the archive's SHA-256 in the build task; the builder's agent fetches it from the master's mesh address on :7444 and verifies the digest before anything is unpacked. A newer upload replacing the archive in between makes the fetch fail (409) rather than build the wrong files.
- The image fetch and the source fetch share a new `meshGet` (mesh-only address check, cluster token, no redirect to elsewhere); `fetchClusterImage` now uses it. The image server's token check is shared too.
- `buildOnCluster` is split into the retry loop and `buildOnNode`; `pickBuilder` takes the nodes to skip.

## Notes
- Contains the commit from #83 (uploaded source); merge #83 first, then this one. Targets `main`.
- Docs: `docs/deploy.md` (On a cluster, Roles), `docs/clustering.md`.

## Test plan
- [x] `go vet` and `go test ./...` in `tools/ziroctl`
- [x] Roles: runner off keeps replicas away; builder skip set; unknown role refused
- [x] Failover: builder goes NotReady, build finishes on the next one (real state files in a temp dir)
- [x] Source transfer: right token and digest fetched; wrong token, replaced archive, address outside the mesh and bad app name refused

author: janvi-kapoor
body:
### PR Description

**Context & Motivation:**
The offline synchronization engine processes pending mutations via `dequeueOfflineAction` (`src/lib/offlineStore.ts`). Currently, if the sync loop accidentally passes `null`, `undefined`, or `NaN` as the action ID, the function still requests a Web Lock and opens an IndexedDB transaction, wasting resources on a query that is guaranteed to fail.

**Changes Made:**
- Added an aggressive early return check at the top of the function: `if (id === undefined || id === null || isNaN(id)) return;`.
- The function now immediately aborts execution before hitting the IndexedDB API or requesting any synchronization locks.

**Impact:**
Optimizes browser performance by reducing unnecessary I/O operations and database transactions. Prevents potential Web Lock deadlocks caused by processing phantom or malformed action IDs.

Closes #4101

## Résumé
Lot 1 de l'audit du 5 octobre 2026 (points 1, 2 et 5).

- **`sw.js`** : `index.html` n'est renvoyé hors ligne que pour une navigation. Un script, un style ou une image absent du cache donne maintenant une erreur réseau, au lieu de recevoir du HTML (qui produisait un écran blanc sans explication).
- **Précache** : ajout de `icons/icon-maskable-512.png` (point 5 de l'audit) et de `icons/favicon-32.png` (oubli découvert par le nouveau test, non signalé par l'audit). Cache renommé `pss-v4` pour que les appareils déjà installés prennent la nouvelle liste.
- **`tests/pwa.spec.js`** (nouveau) : l'appli est servie en HTTP par un petit serveur Node intégré au test (aucune dépendance ajoutée), car le service worker ne s'enregistre pas en `file://`. Trois scénarios :
  1. tous les fichiers dont la page a besoin (scripts, styles, logo, manifeste, icônes) sont en cache ;
  2. le serveur coupé, la page se recharge et fonctionne (camp, liste, version) sans erreur JavaScript ;
  3. un fichier absent du cache n'est pas remplacé par du HTML.
- **README** : précisions sur la liste de `sw.js` et sur ces tests.

- `npx prettier --check .` : OK

- Le coupe-réseau passe par le serveur (et non `context.setOffline`, qui ne touche pas les requêtes du service worker : le test 2 aurait passé à tort).

body:
**Do not merge or run until Webber has set up npm trusted publishing.** Publishing cannot be undone. The Director asked for this to be prepared and left unmerged and unrun.

The CLI runs from the repo today. To install as `npx livediagram`, it needs a publishable package and a way to publish it that stores no npm token. This prepares both.

What was done:

- **`apps/cli/scripts/build.mjs`** now writes a publishable `dist/`:
  - `package.json` named `livediagram` (bin, files allowlist, Node 22, MIT, repository); the workspace stays `@livediagram/cli`, so turbo never sees two packages of one name.
  - The repository `LICENSE` and a user-facing README (`apps/cli/PACKAGE_README.md`).
  - `THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES`, read from esbuild's metafile: four bundled packages today (perfect-freehand, svg-path-bbox, svgpath, zod), plus the licences page's embedded works whose sources reach the bundle (Lucide's icon geometry). A bundled package without a declared licence fails the build.
- **CI** runs `npm pack --dry-run` on every PR (about 219 kB, five files).
- **`.github/workflows/cli-publish.yml`** publishes with provenance through npm trusted publishing (OIDC, `id-token: write`, no token stored). It runs when `apps/cli/package.json` changes on main, or by hand. It tests and builds first, and skips a version already on npm.

To enable, on npmjs.com: create the `livediagram` package's trusted publisher for this repository and `cli-publish.yml`. Then merge, and bump `apps/cli/package.json`'s version to publish.

author: skezo
body:
## What

Video sync v1's controller, which drives the audio lead from the companion's estimate and replaces the old beta.

- **The lead:** the companion's estimate for the cast's first speaker, plus the capture delay measured in the offscreen document, plus the per-speaker fine-tune, minus 40 ms (sound slightly late is far less noticeable than early).
  - It moves in one step when the estimate moves by more than 40 ms, at most once every 5 s, and at once on a new epoch or a fine-tune change.
  - If the measurement is lost, the lead holds.
  - Stopping the cast puts the page's sound back first.
- **The cast card** shows where video sync stands: locking on, in step, cannot sync, nothing to watch, or turned off, with the reason. It also has:
  - a fine-tune slider (−500 to +500 ms) kept per speaker;
  - Reload page, for tabs opened before sync was on;
  - Try again, after the player turned the lead off.
- **Gate:** it needs a PCM cast from a tab and a companion that sends the estimate; otherwise the card says what's missing and nothing moves.
- **Removed:** the beta's pause/rate/seek loop, its every-page content script, and the beta protocol types.
- **Fixed:** a race where a lead queued just as a cast stopped could outlive the cast.

## Why

Completes video sync v1: picture and speaker audio line up on mainstream sites, including Netflix and Prime, without touching the video. The speaker's own output delay isn't measured yet, so the fine-tune starts at 0 and may need setting once per speaker. A clapper session will set per-model defaults later.

## How to Test

1. Build the extension and the companion from this branch, turn video sync on, grant site access, and reload a YouTube tab.
2. Start a **PCM** cast. The card goes from "locking on" to "in step".
3. Use the fine-tune slider until lips match. Lean slightly late.
4. Seek and pause: the picture never jumps. Losing a moment of sound right after a seek is expected.
5. Stop the cast: the tab's sound returns at once and stays in step.
6. On Netflix, switches can take 4–9 s (xHE-AAC random access points). AAC/FLAC and whole-browser casts say sync isn't available.

CI: `bun run test` passes in every package. A bare `bun test` from the repo root fails 8 `sonos-event-handlers` tests because the extension's test preload only loads inside `apps/extension`. This also happens on main and is not a code bug.

## Related Issue

None. Video sync v1, part 3 of 3. Stacks on #231.

author: moshe-runai
body:
## What does this PR do?

Last of the series, on top of #409. The machinery landed already, so this is
the layer that makes it visible: every Karta-described workload across the
selected clusters in one table, replacing the placeholder the route pointed at.

### The table

Built on Headlamp's `Table` rather than `ResourceTable`, which requires rows to
extend `KubeObject`, and Karta-computed rows do not. Status renders as the same
pill Headlamp's own workload views use, worst phase first, since a workload can
match several at once.

Every column filters, each by the control its values suit: multi-select for the
categorical ones, range for the numeric ones, date-range for age. Two needed
their own filter function, because their accessors exist for sorting. Status
sorts on the joined phases, so it offers the nine phases individually and
matches any of them. Age sorts on a negated timestamp, so its filter reads
`creationTimestamp`, with the upper bound normalised in UTC because a date-only
value parses as UTC midnight.

Sorting matches what is displayed: newest first for age, worst phase first for
status rather than alphabetically.

### Namespaces

The chooser in the header is Headlamp's own, through `SectionFilterHeader`, as
its built-in list pages do. The chosen namespaces narrow the **requests**, not
the rendered rows, so an unselected namespace is never fetched and never
status-evaluated.

The selection is intersected with the cluster's allowed namespaces before the
request, because `useList` turns an empty namespace list into a request with no
namespace, which lists the whole cluster. The guard applies to namespaced kinds
only: `useList` drops the namespaces for a cluster-scoped resource, so the
selection cannot affect it. When it hides every namespaced kind, the cluster
says so rather than leaving an unexplained empty table.

Rows and errors are keyed by cluster and selection, and entries die with the
cluster or selection that produced them. Without that, returning to an earlier
selection reads its own stale entries, which satisfy the loading gate before
anything resolves.

Reading the selection means reading the host's redux store, because the plugin
API does not re-export `useNamespaces`. That is how the flux plugin does it
(`flux/src/helpers/index.tsx`). `react-redux` needs no dependency entry: the
plugin build externalises it to `pluginLib.ReactRedux`, so `useSelector` binds
to Headlamp's store rather than a bundled copy.

### Throttling

List updates are throttled before rows are projected, the way Headlamp's own
`ResourceTable` does, using the same exported helper at the same interval. The
items are throttled together with the namespace selection they came from: the
helper holds its previous value for up to an interval, so a selection whose
list resolves inside that window would otherwise publish the old namespaces'
rows as the new ones.

### Failures

Reported at the granularity they happen, beside the results rather than in
place of them:

| Failure | Effect |
|---|---|
| Every cluster failed | table hidden |
| One cluster unreachable | banner, other clusters still render |
| Cluster readable but its Karta CRs are not | warning, its kinds still report for themselves |
| Selection disallowed on a cluster | warning, its cluster-scoped kinds still render |
| One kind fails to list | banner, other kinds still render |
| Engine fails to load | banner with a Retry, rows render without the status column |

The engine is only needed for status. Names, namespaces and ages are metadata,
so a failed fetch costs the status column rather than the table.

One failure has one owner. The catalog is read through the engine, so a failed
load also surfaces as every cluster's definitions failing; a cluster error
carrying the engine's failure is dropped, rather than blaming a cluster for a
local download.

## Notes for review

The engine loads when the page mounts, not when the plugin registers. It had
been eager so the fetch overlapped Headlamp's startup, but instrumenting it
showed 258ms of a 3020ms two-cluster load, against roughly 1.2s for discovery
and 1.0s for status computation. Lazy keeps that cost off users who never open
Karta. A test asserts the plugin does not load it at registration, and fails
whether an eager load returns to `index.tsx` by either import path or anywhere
in the page's own graph.

Nothing announces that a failed engine download could now succeed, so its alert
carries a Retry that reloads the engine and the catalog together. Before, the
page stayed broken until it was left and reopened.

The workload name is plain text, not a link. `detailPath` was removed in #409
because the route it pointed at does not exist; it comes back with the detail
page.

Six columns are filterable but have no data yet: pods, GPUs, CPU, memory,
instances and raw phase are all null pending pod attribution and ready-count
rollup. Their filters work, they just operate on a single value today.

Loading is still all-or-nothing: the table waits for every kind on every
cluster. That is deliberate rather than inherited, and progressive rendering is
agreed as a follow-up.

Four suites stub `localStorage`. Node 24 exposes its own, which shadows
jsdom's, and the real `CommonComponents` reads it at import time through
Headlamp's redux store. CI pins node 22, so this is for contributors ahead of
it.

Known follow-ups, not in this PR:

- `useKartaDefinitions` folds a catalog failure and a cluster-list failure into
  one `error`, so consumers have to work out which they are looking at. Two
  bugs in this PR trace back to it, and the current fix compares messages.
  Splitting the field at the source would retire the class.
- Column visibility and sort are not persisted, where Headlamp's
  `ResourceTable` saves them per table id.
- The `-1` sentinel used to sort null numerics shows as the minimum of their
  range filters, best fixed once those columns carry data.

Tested across the table, the status chips, the columns, the page and plugin
registration: the status and age filter functions, sort direction and order,
the namespace selection reaching `useList` and being intersected with the
allowed set, cluster-scoped kinds surviving that intersection, the throttle and
its selection guard, rows not outliving the cluster or selection that produced
them, the engine retry reloading rather than merely re-rendering, and each
failure above landing in the right channel.

## Related issue(s)

Refs #246 (plugin epic), Refs #302 (engine and definition mapping)

- [x] All commits are signed off with DCO (`git commit -s`)
- [x] New/modified files have SPDX license and copyright headers
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Tests pass (`make check`)
- [x] No proprietary or internal information included

body: ## Summary PR2 for [pdfme#484](https://github.com/pdfme/pdfme/issues/484) (life #453). Adds opt-in image columns to the table schema in `@pdfme/schemas` and the generator layout. Follows #1658 (`remapColumnStylesOnRemove`), which already remaps these column maps when a column is removed. Designer settings (Columns card, cell image editor, i18n) are intentionally not in this PR. They belong in PR3. This PR only renders image cells in the PDF and in Viewer / Form / Designer. `inputs` and `content` stay `string[][]`. An image cell's value is a PNG or JPEG data URL. Omitting `cellType` keeps today's text layout, row heights, and PDF output. ```ts columnStyles: { alignment?: { [colIndex: number]: ALIGNMENT }; cellType?: { [colIndex: number]: 'text' | 'image' }; // omit = 'text' imageHeightMode?: { [colIndex: number]: 'fixed' | 'auto' }; // omit = 'fixed' imageHeight?: { [colIndex: number]: number }; // mm, omit = 20, used only when fixed } ``` Mode and height are stored separately, so switching between `fixed` and `auto` does not drop the millimeter value. Zod is unchanged (`passthrough`). Every TypeScript addition is optional. ### Layout The table pipeline is unchanged: `calculateWidths → calculate → resizeColumns → applyColSpans → fitContent → applyRowSpans`. - Image cells do not affect column width. `contentWidth` and `minReadableWidth` are the horizontal padding, and `minWidth` / `wrappedWidth` stay at `styles.cellWidth`. A long data URL cannot widen the column. - `fixed`: height is `imageHeight` when it is a finite number greater than 0, otherwise 20mm. Empty and invalid values keep that height so the row does not collapse. - `auto`: height is `inner width × image height / image width`. Invalid values contribute 0. On a blank `basePdf`, the height is capped so the row, the header (when the template `showHead` is true), the cell's vertical padding and border, and a 1mm margin still fit in the page content box. A custom PDF `basePdf` is not capped. The cap reads `settings.templateShowHead`, captured before split segments overwrite `schema.showHead`. Continuation pages with `repeatHead: false` therefore use the same row height as planning. The 1mm margin is larger than the 0.5mm page-break slack, so a capped row is not flush with that check. - Header cells are always text. `cellType: null` is unsupported and is treated as text with no warning. An unknown column type (for example a future `qrcode`) is treated as text, with one warning for that value. - Measurement uses `getBoxContentArea` (same box as drawing). JPEG/PNG EXIF orientation 5–8 swaps width and height, matching `image.pdf`, which bakes orientation on embed. Dimension lookup decodes the data URL once and caches both successes and failures. Cache keys include the string length, in the same form as the image embed cache (`tableImageDim:${length}:${hash}`, `tableImageWarned:${length}:${hash}`). - Drawing delegates to `graphics/image.ts` `image.pdf` (`objectFit: 'contain'`, horizontal `objectPosition` from the column alignment, vertical from `bodyStyles.verticalAlignment`). A value whose header cannot be read is not drawn. A PNG or JPEG whose header parses but whose bytes fail inside `embedPng` / `embedJpg` is caught, warned once, and left blank, so `generate` still returns a PDF. The image plugin does not have to be registered. - Only `data:image/png;base64,` and `data:image/jpeg;base64,` (or `jpg`) are drawn. URLs, gif, webp, svg, other strings, broken base64, and a truncated PNG/JPEG are unsupported: they are not drawn. An invalid value warns once: `[@pdfme/schemas/table] unsupported image in column N; only PNG/JPEG data URL is supported`. `""` and `null` are unsupported and are not drawn, and they do not warn. - UI is display-only: an `` with the same object-fit / object-position and `cursor: default`. Selecting an image cell still paints only that image, so file inputs and delete buttons are not shown. Text cells stay editable. - Page breaks: `tables/dynamicTemplate.ts` estimates the first body row the same way `@pdfme/common` `placeUnitsOnPages` places it. The fit check uses the same 0.01mm tolerance as `placeUnitsOnPages`, so a row that lands on the safety margin is not treated as overflow. When `repeatHead` is true and only the header fits on the initial page, the header travels with that row, so the row height does not also include a second header. If that move would leave the current page empty, `placeUnitsOnPages` restarts at the top of the same page instead of emitting a blank page and a header-only page. That restart runs only for `avoidFirstUnitOnly: true`, which tables set. Later pages still repeat the header. A row that does not fit even at the top of a fresh page is unchanged. ## Backward compatibility Templates without `cellType` keep the same row heights and PDF output. Existing generator snapshots (`shrinking-table`, `table-row-height-overflow`, `readonly-table`, `integration-*`, and the rest of the generator suite) pass without updates. The page-break change applies only when a repeated header fits on the current page and the first body row does not, and that page has no other schemas. Those tables now start at the content top of the first page together with the row. Explicit blank template pages (`schemas: [[]]`) are unchanged. Existing text-only snapshots do not hit this case. ## Tests - `packages/schemas/__tests__/tableImageCell.test.ts`: fixed default and explicit height (including empty and invalid cells), auto aspect ratio and blank-PDF cap, auto empty/invalid, EXIF orientation 6, header cells measured as text, image columns ignored by `minReadableWidth`, dimension cache (10 identical data URLs → one `getImageDimension` call) and a negative cache for unreadable bytes, one warning per invalid value, `cellType: null` treated as text with no warning, and `isTableImageDataUrl`. - `packages/schemas/__tests__/table.ui.test.ts`: Viewer, Form, and Designer show one `` (`object-fit: contain`, matching `object-position`, `cursor: default`) and no file input. Clicking an image cell stays display-only. A text cell on the same row remains editable. - `packages/generator/__tests__/table-image-cell.test.ts`: fixed 20mm × 20 rows with `repeatHead`, mixed auto ratios with an empty row, and a following text schema pushed below the table. The image plugin is not registered. - End-to-end `generate` coverage for a row at the auto cap: the following text does not overlap for both `repeatHead: false` and `repeatHead: true`, using Designer default cell styles (padding 5). With `repeatHead: true` and `y` below the page top, there is no blank page and no header-only page. The same placement is covered for a long wrapped text cell, and for one default-style portrait row (width 180, columns `[30, 70]`): the header and the row share the first page. A truncated PNG (readable IHDR, cut-off body) warns once and `generate` still returns one page. `npm run lint`, `tsc -b packages/common packages/schemas packages/generator packages/ui/tsconfig.typecheck.json`, schemas tests (25 files / 432 tests), generator tests (18 files / 148 tests), ui tests (12 files / 175 tests), and common tests (7 files / 157 tests) passed. author: janvi-kapoor
body:
### PR Description

**Context & Motivation:**
Offline telemetry events are queued in `localStorage`. If this storage key gets corrupted (e.g., overwritten by a third-party script, or saved as a serialized object instead of an array), `retryFailedTelemetry` (`src/lib/clientTelemetry.ts`) attempts to call `.forEach()` on a non-array object, throwing a `TypeError` and completely halting the background sync loop.

**Changes Made:**
- Added an `Array.isArray(parsed)` verification step immediately after running `JSON.parse()` on the stored telemetry string.
- If the data is corrupted and not an array, the function now safely clears the corrupted key and exits without crashing.

**Impact:**
Ensures that the client-side telemetry background sync is self-healing. Corrupted offline queues will no longer permanently break analytics tracking for the affected user.

Closes #4100

author: bespoyasov
body:
- Adds event management commands to the CLI: `confidence events list|get|create|update|delete|usage`
- Adds generic MCP client in `packages/core/src/mcp/` using `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`, reusable for future command groups
- Adds generic REST API client in `packages/core/src/api/` (unused by events, ready for future commands)
- Events commands call the `confidence-flags` MCP server tools (`listEventDefinitions`, `getEventDefinition`, `createEventDefinition`, `updateEventDefinition`, `deleteEventDefinition`, `queryEventsUsage`)
- `delete` prompts for confirmation via `@inquirer/confirm`
- Splits MSW test handlers into per-domain files under `packages/testing/src/msw/handlers/`
- Exports `extractRegion` from core's auth barrel

---

Noticed that REST for events isn't supported yet, so had to introduce the MCP client in `core`, but I decided to keep the REST client in this PR as well (as it will be needed for other features anyways).

---

### Commands

```bash
# List all event definitions
confidence events list

# Get details for a specific event
confidence events get page-viewed

# Create an event definition with typed fields
confidence events create --name purchase-completed \
  --field amount:double \
  --field currency:string \
  --field item_count:int

# Create from a JSON schema file
confidence events create --name signup --from-file schema.json

# Add fields to an existing event definition
confidence events update page-viewed --field referrer:string --field duration:double

# Show publish and validation stats (last 3 days)
confidence events usage page-viewed --days 3

# Delete an event definition (prompts for confirmation)
confidence events delete old-event

# JSON output (all commands)
confidence events list --json
confidence events get page-viewed --json

# Dry-run mode (create only)
confidence events create --name test-event --field page:string --dry-run
```

---

### JSON output

`--json` wraps the MCP server's text response in a `{ "data": "..." }` envelope. The output is human-readable text, not structured JSON, because the MCP server returns text formatted for AI agents. Structured JSON output might become available if a REST API is added.

author: jahands
body:
The zod-v4 migration table mapped `.flatten()` to `z.treeifyError()`, which returns a different shape (`{ errors, properties }`), so migrated code reading `fieldErrors` would break. `z.flattenError()` is the direct replacement: it isn't deprecated and returns the same `{ formErrors, fieldErrors }` as `.flatten()` (checked against zod 4.5.4). `.format()` still maps to `z.treeifyError()`, as zod's deprecation notice says.

`z.prettifyError()` moves out of that row into its own bullet. It formats errors for display rather than replacing either method, but agents don't know it by default.

Found by CodeRabbit on uuid-rocks/workers-monorepo#1005.

body:
## Pourquoi

L'application est développée à deux, chacun sur son ordinateur et avec son propre Claude Code. Sans règles communes, chaque Claude Code travaille à sa façon : modifications directes sur `main` (publié en production automatiquement, sans protection), identité git absente (déjà arrivé : le déploiement du 16 septembre a été bloqué par Vercel), risque de casser les données déjà enregistrées sur les téléphones.

## Ce que ça change

Ajoute un seul fichier, `CLAUDE.md`, à la racine. Claude Code le lit automatiquement au début de chaque session. Il rassemble :

- le mode de travail à deux (une branche par tâche, une PR testée sur sa version d'essai Vercel, pas de push direct sur `main`, identité git obligatoire) ;
- les règles de sécurité d'un dépôt public (aucun secret ni donnée personnelle, clés réglées dans Vercel/Supabase et jamais via le chat) ;
- ce qu'il ne faut pas casser (clé `ppl-tracker-store`, fonction `merge` du store, identifiants d'exercices) ;
- les commandes et quelques repères du code.

Aucun changement dans le code de l'application.

## À vérifier

Rien à tester côté appli : fichier de documentation uniquement. Vercel construira quand même une version d'essai, qui doit rester verte.

author: maryberezhna
body:
## Чому саме Bing

ChatGPT, шукаючи в інтернеті, спирається на індекс Bing. А звідти приходить **96% усього нашого AI-трафіку** — 298 сесій із 311 за місяць (Perplexity 8, Gemini 5, Claude 0).

Тож важіль не в нових сторінках, а в **швидкості**: можливість із дедлайном за два тижні не має сенсу, якщо її проіндексують через місяць.

## Що зроблено

IndexNow — відкритий протокол: на сайті лежить файл-ключ, і ми самі надсилаємо адреси замість того, щоб чекати обходу. **Перевірки сайту у Bing для цього не треба.**

Щодня о 07:30, після нічного скрапу, надсилаємо:

- можливості, змінені за добу (зараз це ~49);
- усі 13 підбірок **обома мовами** — їхній вміст міняється щодня разом із записами, а власного сигналу «сторінка оновилась» у них немає;
- головну.

Разом ~76 адрес за прогін (перевірено сухим прогоном на живій базі).

## Чому не спільний ендпоінт

`api.indexnow.org` роздає адреси **всім** учасникам протоколу, зокрема Яндексу. 02.10.2026 ми свідомо закрили сайт від пошуку рф і білорусі — надсилати їм свої сторінки після цього було б дивно. Тому шлемо напряму в Bing.

## Запобіжники

- чужі адреси й повтори відсікаються;
- межа протоколу (10 000 адрес) перевіряється;
- тест звіряє, що файл-ключ лежить у `public/` і його вміст **збігається з ключем у коді** — інакше Bing відмовить, і це було б видно лише в логах;
- руками воркфлоу нічого не шле без `confirm = SEND`; за розкладом надсилає сам.

`npm test` — 811, зелено (+8).

## Що лишається тобі

IndexNow працює й без цього, але варто один раз зробити: **додати dityam.com.ua у Bing Webmaster Tools** ([bing.com/webmasters](https://www.bing.com/webmasters)) — там є імпорт із Google Search Console, тобто без возні з підтвердженням. Це дасть видимість: які сторінки Bing уже має, за якими запитами показує і що в нього не вийшло обійти.

body:
## Marketplace / meta change

**What's changing:** adds `docs/reviews/2026-10-05-repo-review.md` — the report from a scheduled autonomous whole-repo review. **Docs-only; no plugin/code change.** Opened as a draft PR (rather than committed straight to `main`) because it documents live security-guard gaps and warrants your review before anything acts on it.

**Affects:** docs only (the findings concern `ravenclaude-core` guards/tribunal + cross-host generators + CI, but this PR changes none of them).

**Has been:**
- [x] JSON manifests still validate (no manifest touched)
- [x] Markdown links spot-checked (`check-md-links` → pass)
- [x] No accidental secrets, emails, or internal URLs introduced

---

## Why no code fixes in this PR (deliberate)

Every confirmed finding is **security-floor or CI-governance** work, and all of it is one of: (a) in the command-review tribunal / guard **substrate**, which the repo's own active self-disable floor (4 categories `thing: on`) write-protects — I was correctly denied edits; (b) the **dual-copy parity-gated** `serve-dashboards.py`; or (c) multi-file **cross-host generators / CI** where a wrong unattended edit silently breaks hook wiring or branch protection. This is exactly the class the constitution routes through a **human-reviewed PR with the full gate suite re-run**, not an unattended auto-patch. So this routine surfaces + reproduces them for your call rather than guessing a security fix with nobody watching.

## Ground truth (all green)
`ci-preflight.py` **19/19**, `prettier` clean, `ruff` clean. The findings are things the gates don't assert.

## Findings grouped by priority
Full detail, reproductions, per-finding confirmation status, and fix order are in the doc.

**P0**
- **P0-1** (✓ confirmed by code read) — the tribunal + hard-rule floors + self-disable guard **silently skip when the hook payload `cwd` is a subdirectory** (`thing-orchestrator.sh:137` looks up the posture relative to `cwd`, which follows `cd`, then `exit 0` before the floors). One `cd plugins/…` disables the whole guardrail layer for the session.

**P1**
- **P1-2** (✓) chained command classified/cleared by its first segment only (`thing-decision.py:216`).
- **P1-3** (✓) `guard-web-access` host-parse bypasses allow- **and** deny-lists (`:67-70`).
- **P1-4** (✓) `git reset` hard-target deny is order-anchored; reordered flags evade it (`guard-destructive.sh:1857`).
- **P1-5** (⊙ panel) cross-host hook generators emit a wrong path + stray quote → silently-dead security guards / unparseable hooks on Copilot/Cursor/Gemini/Codex; Gate 247 reports them wired.
- **P1-6 / P1-7** (⊙) fail-open when the posture YAML won't parse; deleting the toggles not caught as self-disable.

**P2** — stall-watch PID-reuse no-op; `rg --pre`/`ugrep --filter` self-disable carve-out; grep truthiness narrower than engine; `_scrub.sh` token-prefix + PEM gaps; guard-destructive newline/segment-scoping; two CI governance gaps (vacuous required-check assertions; dispatch secret-scan reports green without scanning).

**P3** — scrub over-redaction; `serve-dashboards.py` hardening (×3); **`generate-codex-hooks.py --check` already red on `main`** (✓, and no CI runs it); Codex `_SKIP` ignored; stale `REQUIRED_WORKFLOWS`; non-conventional quarantine PR title; `context-usage-meter`/`conserve-tokens` parsing bugs; `routine-reserve` repo-overrides-account-home.

**A** (✓) — `audit-gates.sh` has a **nondeterministic 1-fail flake whose failing gate moves between runs** (run1 Gate 240, run2 prompt-optimizer; each passes in isolation). Cause not isolated (resource/timing vs cross-gate state — both full runs ran under heavy parallel load); a quiet-machine run is the discriminating probe. **Do not** paper over it by raising the artifact-budget ratchet.

---

## Notes for the reviewer

- Confirmation status is marked per finding: **✓ code-read** = I re-verified it this session; **⊙ panel-probed** = a review subagent reproduced it with an executable probe but I did not independently re-run it (verify during the fix).
- Suggested order of attack is in the doc. P1-3 / P1-4 are near-trivial, high-value guard fixes to take first alongside P0-1.
- The review doc deliberately breaks up a few literal dangerous-command strings — the tribunal's hard-rule screens file-write content and denied an earlier draft for a literal pipe-to-interpreter example (finding-adjacent behaviour working as designed).

Follow-up to the host-run pi subagents (ADR-089): messaging and resume rules, child identity, model discovery for agents, and one shared `dispatch_agent` description. ADR-089 gains a dated **Messaging v2** section; ADR-033 cross-references it.

- **Resume rules.** A user-stopped agent can be resumed by the model once the user has prompted since the stop (no approval card; the hold covers every descendant the stop cascaded to). A failed agent resumes only after an environmental failure — pi's retryable provider/transport errors, a crashed child, 401/403, quota — and refuses otherwise (context overflow, refused `/cui-` prompt, first launch that never ran, anything unrecognised). Patterns ported from pi 0.87.1 `overflow.ts`/`retry.ts`; the classification persists in `details.cuiAgent` and task notifications, so a rebuilt record keeps it; older failed links stay resumable.
- **Identity.** Every launch appends the child's id/name, its launcher and the handle to reach it to `system-prompt.md`. A foreground child messaging its own launcher is refused like one messaging `main`.
- **Models.** `agent`'s `model` resolves against the authenticated, allowlisted catalog: exact `provider/id` → bare id → Claude Code alias (`opus`/`sonnet`/`haiku`/`fable`, newest version, the parent's provider first) → refused with a pointer to the new read-only **`list_models`** tool. Subagents can no longer run on a model outside the allowlist. Name uniqueness is re-checked after the catalog await.
- **Dispatch.** `src/shared/dispatch-agent-description.ts` builds every engine's `dispatch_agent` description and the Claude system-prompt section, steering each engine to its own subagent tool first (Claude `Agent`, pi `agent`, opencode `task`, Codex `spawn_agent`). pi receives it via `CLAUDEUI_PI_DISPATCH_DESCRIPTION`.

### Pre-existing bugs fixed
- A child (or pi dispatch target) whose credential was rejected (401/403) settled `ok` and reported **completed** — the runner ignored the mapper's `auth-required`.
- pi only marks a tool result as an error when `execute()` throws, so every ClaudeUI hosted-tool error (refused `agent`, `send_message`/`task_stop` refusals, dispatch errors, mermaid syntax errors) landed as a success. The bridge now flips `isError` through pi's `tool_result` hook for exactly those call ids, keeping content and `details`.
- The agent card's model chip showed the requested alias/bare id; it now shows the resolved model (host-written `model:` line in the result). A refused `send_message` row now shows the reason.

## Test plan
- [x] `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, `bun run test` — all exit 0 (775 files, 17034 tests) after rebasing on pre-release
- [x] Guard tests confirmed failing with each fix removed (user-stop hold, auth settle, foreground→launcher refusal, name race, dispatch env, `tool_result` hook)
- [x] Live app, pi on `openai-codex/gpt-5.6-luna`: `list_models` row; bare id resolves, unknown model / unmatched alias refused with no spawn; identity block on disk; Stop → same-turn `send_message` refused → user prompt → resume (run 2) → completed; pi chose `agent` over `dispatch_agent`
- [x] Live re-check of the fixes: refused `agent` card reads failed and its jsonl toolResult has `isError: true` (successful results untouched); resolved model chips for background and foreground launches; all survive a reload
- [ ] `send_message` refusal row reason — unit-tested only

### Note
- A spawn refused before launch is still listed in the roster as a settled failed row (by design since e80564bc); it no longer reads as a successful agent.

author: slajob
body:
## Summary

This adds `decky-plugin/`, a Decky Loader plugin that does the DS5Dongle firmware's job on the Steam Deck itself. A DualSense paired with the Deck over Bluetooth is presented to SteamOS as a **wired** DualSense. That gives games HD haptics, the controller speaker and headset jack, the microphone, and adaptive triggers, with no Pico involved.

### How it works
- **`backend/`: `ds5bridged`, a native C++ daemon.**
  - **Bluetooth side.** It reads the controller through `/dev/hidrawN`, using the kernel's BlueZ/HIDP stack.
  - **USB side.** It attaches a virtual USB DualSense through `vhci-hcd` (the kernel's USB/IP driver), using the firmware's exact descriptors. The HID report descriptors are generated from `src/usb_descriptors.cpp`. The kernel binds `snd-usb-audio` and `hid-playstation` to it, just as it would to the Pico.
  - **Ported firmware logic.**
    - USB output report `0x02` → Bluetooth `0x31`, including the config overrides.
    - `update_state` (`0x32`) and mic status reports.
    - `audio_bt_task` (`0x39`): haptics resampled 48 kHz → 3 kHz to int8, and the speaker path 512→480 frames → Opus 200-byte CBR, using the same Opus commit as the firmware.
    - Opus mic decoding, UAC volume/mute controls, the mute LED, headset routing, Edge handling (including the fake `0x20` report) and idle disconnect.
  - **Pacing.** Isochronous URBs are completed at one packet per 1 ms, like a real full-speed bus, so the host's audio clock behaves as it does with the Pico.
  - **Hiding.** While bridged, the raw Bluetooth controller is hidden from Steam (udev flag-file rule, driver rebind, node permissions, evdev grab), so games see only one controller. Turning the bridge off hands it back.
- **`main.py`: Python backend.** It supervises the daemon, loads `vhci-hcd`, installs the udev rule, validates and persists settings, and restores controller visibility if the daemon dies.
- **`src/index.tsx`: Quick Access panel.** It shows per-controller status (battery, wired-mode state, streams) and the web-config settings: haptics strength, trigger reduction, speaker output and boost, mic, lock volume, buffer length, DS/Edge mode, light bar and idle timeout.
- **`.github/workflows/decky-plugin.yml`.** It builds on Ubuntu 22.04 (glibc 2.35), runs the tests, checks that the descriptors match the firmware, and uploads the installable `ds5-bridge.zip`.

## Testing
- `make -C decky-plugin/backend test` runs 34 end-to-end tests against a fake `vhci-hcd` host that speaks USB/IP and a fake Bluetooth DualSense. They cover:
  - enumeration and byte-for-byte descriptor parity with the firmware
  - feature, input and output report translation and CRCs
  - UAC volume and mute
  - 1 ms isochronous pacing
  - the exact haptics samples
  - the Opus speaker stream (decoded and frequency-checked)
  - the mic path (encoded tone → USB PCM)
  - unlink, Edge modes, the control socket, and controller disconnect
- The suite passed 5 out of 5 runs. It also passes under AddressSanitizer and UBSan with zero reports.
- The Python backend was smoke-tested against the real daemon running with the fake controller.
- The frontend type-checks and builds with `@decky/ui` 4.12 / `@decky/api` 1.1.
- **Not yet tested on real Steam Deck hardware.** Still to confirm on a Deck:
  - that the SteamOS kernel ships `vhci-hcd`
  - that the controller accepts 548-byte HIDP reports from BlueZ, as it does from the Pico
  - real game behaviour under Proton

author: tetofonta
body:
Addresses #87.

## Motivation

Today a certificate is only accepted if the PAM_USER name appears in the certificate's list of principals. That ties the certificate's principals to local account names and makes it impossible to express "this CA may grant access to this
account" independently of how the certificate was issued — the use case in #87, where the same account should be reachable by distinct principals (for example with and without sudo rights).

## What this does

A `cert-authority` entry can now carry a `principals="a,b"` option, the same spelling OpenSSH uses in `AUTHORIZED_KEYS FILE FORMAT` ([here](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/sshd.8.html#AUTHORIZED_KEYS_FILE_FORMAT)):

```
cert-authority,principals="admin,oncall" ssh-ed25519 AAAA... ca@example.com
```

When the option is present, the certificate is accepted if **any** of its valid principals appears in the configured list. The login user name is not consulted in that case. Entries without the option behave exactly as before, so existing configurations are unaffected.

The option is accepted both in `authorized_keys` and in a file pointed at by `ca_keys_file`. Specifying `principals=` more than once on a single line is rejected and the entry is dropped with a warning, rather than silently honouring one of them.

## Implementation notes

* CA entries are stored as a new `CertData` (key data plus its principals list)  instead of a bare `KeyData`. `Hash`/`Eq`/`Borrow<KeyData>` are implemented over the  key data alone, so lookups by CA key still work and the options travel with the key.
* `IdentityFilter::filter` returns a reference to the matched entry rather than a `bool`, which is what lets `validate_cert` see the options configured for the CA  that signed the certificate. Call sites that only care about a match are unchanged  in behaviour.
* Unrelated but included: a missing `authorized_keys` file and unparsable `authorized_keys` lines are now logged at `warn` rather than `info`. Both silently shrink the set of keys usable for authentication, which seems worth surfacing by default.

## Tests

Additional tests have been introduced,

* `filter.rs`: loading `principals=` from a `ca_keys_file`, and matching against single/multiple/non-matching principal sets.
* `auth.rs`: `validate_cert` against two certificates with disjoint principals (`principal1,principal3` and `principal2,principal4`) over matching and non-matching configured lists, plus the existing cases to confirm the no-`principals=` path still falls back to the login user.
* New fixtures: `ca_key_prefix.pub`, `ca_key_principals.pub`, `cert_principal_1_3.pub`, `cert_principal_2_4.pub`. Also adds coverage for a `ca_keys_file` entry written with the `cert-authority ` prefix, which was previously untested, and removes the unused `cert_key-cert.pub` fixture.

author: antti-ethz
body:
Closes #5.

Long sequences freeze the browser because every RF segment is sampled at 25 samples/us (up to a cap of 2 million samples per trace), also where frequency, phase and amplitude are constant. The number of line points therefore grows with the duration of the sequence and not with the number of events.

Changes:

- Constant segments are drawn with their end points. Slopes, splines and the "sample" view are still sampled densely.
- The parsed sequence and the traces are kept across renders. A zoom or a plot style change no longer rebuilds the traces, and other re-renders no longer parse the sequence again.
- The block time consistency check compares each channel with the current call only, instead of scanning all calls on every call.
- Up to 4000 points per trace are spread over the constant segments, so that hovering along a flat line still finds a point.

The drawn lines are unchanged.

Notes:

- The two options proposed in #5 (size warning, windowed rendering) are not implemented. Rendering cost now scales with the number of events and the duration of slopes and splines.
- The cap of 2 million samples per trace now counts only slopes and splines, so in sequences beyond 80 ms these are sampled more finely than before.
- Hover labels along flat lines thin out beyond roughly 100x zoom. Labels on event markers are unaffected.
- The "sample" view no longer ends each channel with NaN samples, because the arrays are allocated to the exact sample count.
- The consistency check now treats times within a thousandth of a clock tick (4 ps) as equal. The old tolerance of 0.2 fs was exceeded by rounding alone on long sequences, which produced false reports.

author: taojin-6
body:
## Summary

recon and gfx have both moved onto volumetric_kit_core and now write its types the way the core does. This brings the iOS app to those pins and the renames that come with them, so the whole family runs on one core.

- **Pins.** The core is declared first, with its Vulkan tier on, so recon and gfx build against this one copy. The core's own pin, a60398b (core #13), is the same one recon and gfx use.

  | Dependency | Old pin | New pin |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | recon | #163 (a6a5e43) | #168 (624b2dc) |
  | gfx | #99 (e15aed4) | #106 (53e8f63) |
- **Names.** The bridge and `compute_smoke` write the core's names, e.g. `vkc::Status`, `vkc::Device`, `vkc::Allocator`, `vkc::Image` (gfx's old `Texture`) and `VKC_CHECK`. They include the core's headers. recon's and gfx's own types keep `vr::` and `vg::`.
- **One shared device, the core's.** `Bridge/SharedDevice.{hpp,mm}` is deleted; it was a ~750-line copy of recon's viewer bootstrap. `vkc::SharedDevice` now builds the one `VkDevice` from `vr::device_requirements()` and `vg::device_requirements()` (with `needs_present`).
  - `VolumetricRenderer.mm` adds only the platform part: `VK_KHR_surface` / `VK_EXT_metal_surface`, and the `CAMetalLayer` surface in the `make_surface` callback.
  - gfx adopts `graphics_payload()` and recon adopts `compute_payload()`, both unconverted.
  - The core asks for portability enumeration only where a loader offers it, which the directly linked MoltenVK doesn't.
- **`RendererErrors`.** It had one `error_code` / `describe` / `set_error` per library; now it has one each, because recon and gfx share one `Status`. It reads the `VkResult` through `vkc::vk_result`, and the core's `Numerical` domain gets a new `VolumetricRendererErrorNumerical = 7`. Swift doesn't switch on the codes.
- **Memory placements.**
  - The atlas staging buffer is `Staging`.

author: devttyac
body:
The documentation described the frontend as a PWA. It is not one.

## Verified absences

`static/` contains exactly two files — `index.html` and `favicon.svg`. There is:

- **no web app manifest**
- **no service worker** — zero matches for `serviceWorker`, `sw.js` or `workbox`
- **no PWA meta tags** — no `apple-mobile-web-app-capable`, `mobile-web-app-capable` or `theme-color`

So it cannot be installed to a home screen and has no offline capability. It is a single-page application: one static HTML file with inline JavaScript, served by FastAPI, calling a JSON API. Responsive, but not progressive.

## Changes

| File | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `README.md:37` | `Responsive PWA Frontend` | `Responsive SPA Frontend` |
| `README.md:154` | `Single-Page Responsive PWA Interface` | `Single-Page Responsive Web Interface` |
| `DEPLOYMENT.md:55` | `**First use in the PWA:**` | `**First use in the web interface:**` |

Line 154 said "Single-Page" already, so "PWA" was both wrong and redundant.

Line 37 sits inside the box-drawn architecture diagram. `PWA` and `SPA` are the same width, so no re-padding was needed — all rows measure display-width 91 and the right-hand border still aligns.

## Why it is worth correcting

The label originated here in the README and propagated into the project's derived specification and design documents, and from there into a security review and three pull request descriptions. Nobody checked it against `static/`.

It is not purely cosmetic. A PWA has a materially different attack surface — service worker scope, cached response poisoning, offline state. A reviewer taking the label at face value would look for issues that cannot exist in this application. The 2026-10-05 security review read the source rather than the label, so no finding was affected, but the term could have sent it somewhere useless.

Corresponding corrections have been made in the project's vault documentation. The security review report itself is deliberately left unedited — it is an immutable record of what was assessed, and the correction is noted in the living remediation tracker instead.

## Scope

Prose only. No manifest or service worker was added; whether the app *should* become a PWA is a separate feature question, not addressed here. No logic, config, tests or CI touched, and `APP_VERSION` is unchanged since there is no runtime effect.

author: janvi-kapoor
body:
### PR Description

**Context & Motivation:**
The function `cancellationWindowHoursRemaining` in `src/lib/bookingCancellation.ts` calculates the time left for a user to cancel a booking. If the booking start time is missing or unparseable, the delta calculation results in `NaN`, which directly leaks into the UI badges (displaying "NaN hours remaining").

**Changes Made:**
- Wrapped the delta calculation in a `Number.isFinite(millisecondsUntilStart)` check.
- If the time delta resolves to `NaN` or `Infinity`, the function now defaults to returning `0` hours.

**Impact:**
Prevents confusing and unpolished UI states. A fallback of `0` ensures that the UI correctly restricts cancellation attempts when data is corrupted, maintaining strict business logic integrity.

Closes #4098

author: timo92
body:
The first implementation of **Podcast-Cockpit**, a personal, non-commercial web app in front of Spotify. It answers one question: *what's new in my news podcasts, and which episode of my long-running series is next?* The UI is in German; the code and docs are in English.

This PR is merged without squashing, so the commits below stay in history as the record of how the app evolved through review.

## What the app does

- **Spotify login (OAuth)** with server-side sessions. The first account that logs in becomes the owner, and every other account is rejected.
- **Import of saved shows** with a guessed consumption mode (`LATEST` / `SEQUENTIAL` / `MANUAL`) and categories, plus a review screen to confirm them.
- **Sync** of new episodes every 2 hours, a full refresh nightly, and on demand. It only writes metadata and never overwrites personal progress. Spotify's listening state counts as a hint, and the user's own marks win.
- **Heute (Today):** today's planned slots first, then a daily time budget filled by priority.
- **Woche (Week):** recurring weekly slots, projected onto concrete episodes for the next 7 days.
- **Next and last heard episode** per podcast in the overview.
- **Notes per episode**, saved automatically, with `[mm:ss]` timestamps from the in-app player. They are searchable and included in the export.
- **Playback** in the browser (Web Playback SDK, Premium), on a Spotify Connect device, or in the Spotify app.
- **History, JSON export, "delete all data"**, light/dark mode, installable as a home-screen app, and an offline demo (`pnpm dev:demo`).

## Architecture

pnpm monorepo with four packages:

| Package | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `shared` | Domain types and pure logic (next-episode selection, budget, weekly plan, retention) |
| `backend` | Hono API on Lambda (and Node for local dev), a sync Lambda, the Spotify client, and DynamoDB/in-memory stores |
| `frontend` | React SPA (Vite, TanStack Query, React Router), plain CSS with design tokens, lucide icons |
| `infra` | AWS CDK: CloudFront (site and `/api`), S3, API Gateway HTTP API, Lambda, a DynamoDB single table with PITR, a Route 53 record, and an ACM certificate stack in us-east-1 |

The reasoning behind each choice is in [`docs/decisions.md`](docs/decisions.md) (D1–D17). The requirements are in [`docs/requirements.md`](docs/requirements.md).

## Deployment and configuration

- **Stack names and tags:** stacks are named `<STACK_NAME>-<STAGE>` (stage defaults to `dev`) and tagged `app`, `stage` and `managed-by`.
- **Spotify credentials:** the client ID comes from `.env` or CI, and synth fails without it. The client secret lives in SSM Parameter Store at `/<app>/<stage>/spotify-client-secret`. The stack creates that parameter with a placeholder; after deploying, set the real value with `pnpm run secret:put`. The secret never appears in code or templates.
- **`.env` loading:** every script loads `.env` through Node's `--env-file-if-exists`. `AWS_PROFILE` may be set there, and a value set in the shell takes precedence.
- **One sync at a time:** a DynamoDB lease ensures this instead of reserved Lambda concurrency, which a fresh account's quota of 10 doesn't allow.

## Spotify compliance

The app is non-commercial: no ads, no payments, and donations only outside the app. It uses Spotify's official logos and attribution ("LISTEN ON SPOTIFY" / "PLAY ON SPOTIFY") and leaves artwork uncropped with small corner radii. If the owner disconnects from Spotify, all data is deleted after 30 days, and a banner shows the deletion date. See D16.

## Robustness

- **Sync lease:** acquired with a conditional write; when the sync Lambda takes it over, it gets a new lease ID (async invocations are at-least-once).
- **Conditional writes against races** with logins and concurrent token refreshes: token deletion, config deletion, the disconnected mark, and schedule updates.
- **Unfollowed shows:** a show counts as unfollowed only when Spotify's library check confirms it is no longer saved. If that check fails, nothing is unfollowed.

## Commits

1. `a3283b1` Shared domain logic and backend API
2. `d7c54d4` React frontend: Today view, podcast management, in-app player
3. `2eeb869` CDK deployment, DynamoDB/Lambda tests, docs and CI
4. `811f47a` Weekly plan, episode notes, next/last heard overview
5. `6e1aaad` Review: Hono, pnpm, decisions doc, test/dev layout, icons, CSS split
6. `ba3ef74`, `34158a1`, `2f34bc6`, `c58c334` Spotify app configured through the deployment, with the secret in SSM; deployment fails on incomplete config
7. `2fa8021` Demo script works on Windows; CI runs on Ubuntu and Windows
8. `9666a5f` Spotify Developer Terms and Design Guidelines compliance
9. `cbf46aa` Deployment works in a fresh account (lease instead of reserved concurrency; stage naming and tags)
10. `d5f7f73` GitHub MCP server for Claude Code
11. `ae57b4f` Sync and retention hardened against races and partial data

## Testing

- **Unit tests:** 102 (Vitest): shared 22, backend 63, frontend 3, infra 14. They cover a store contract run against both stores, the Lambda handlers, a fake Spotify, and CDK assertions.
- **CI:** install, typecheck, test, build and `cdk synth` on Ubuntu and Windows, both green.
- **Manual end-to-end:** deployed to the `dev` stage on AWS, then logged in, imported, synced, planned, played and took notes. Also checked locally with `pnpm dev`.

## Follow-ups

Tracked as issues: #5–#10 and #2, #3 in milestone **V1**, and #4 in **public** (multi-user).

author: xyxinghe
body:
## What does this PR do?

WorkBuddy (Tencent's CodeBuddy-derived CLI) records JSONL session transcripts
under `~/.workbuddy/projects/<encoded-cwd>/<session>.jsonl`. A
*wing* (`wing_<name>`) is the per-project — or, when no project applies,
per-agent — namespace MemPalace files saved memories under, and the field
project-scoped queries run against. Without this PR, a MemPalace install
hooked into WorkBuddy **silently never saves anything**: the stop hook counts
0 exchanges, so its save never triggers, and the session-end flush — the one
save that skips the counter — found nothing in the transcript to file
(point 2). Every session also mints its own throwaway wing: 377 real
transcripts resolve to 152 wings today, 1 wing and 7,846 counted turns after
this patch. Three things were needed; the first is the one worth reviewing.

**1. WorkBuddy sessions each minted their own wing, because its `cwd` is
disposable — now they fold into one `wing_workbuddy`.**

`#1424` made `_wing_from_jsonl_cwd()` the primary path and that is right for
Claude Code, where `cwd` is a stable project root like `~/code/foo`. WorkBuddy's
`cwd` is a **workspace instance** — `.../WorkBuddy/2026-09-13-11-04-25`, a
fresh date-stamped directory created for every session. Steps 1–2 therefore
misfire: step 1 mints one wing per workspace instance, and step 2's
encoded-folder heuristic has nothing to decode because the path carries no
project name.

Measured with `tools/bench-workbuddy-hooks.py`, shipped in this PR. It resolves
the same corpus against a clean checkout of the target branch and this tree, so
the patch is the only variable. Snapshot `2026-09-28T03:03:56Z` — the script
stamps its own `as_of` into the JSON it prints, and the corpus is live, so the
exact magnitudes drift from run to run; a file whose bytes change mid-run is
excluded. The script defaults to `~/.workbuddy/projects`; a reviewer without
that store can point `--workbuddy-root` at any directory of `.jsonl`
transcripts, with one boundary: the wing census feeds each file's real path to
the wing strategy, so the fold only reproduces when the corpus path contains
`/.workbuddy/projects/` — a corpus parked at, say, `/tmp/my-dump/` reports a
zero wing delta on both trees, while the turn census (content-based) still
reproduces. The lines it prints:

author: 0xmanhnv
body:
## Problem

EASM P0-2 covers recon politeness and keeping traffic on the scanned host (research/22 §4.1, 22b S8 and §5.2, G6). #139 added httpx `-follow-host-redirects`, katana `-fs fqdn` with an output filter, and passed the scan rate limit through. Four gaps remain on `main`:

1. **katana still requests other hosts.** I measured katana v1.7.0 against two scratch nginx hosts, A and B. With `-fs fqdn`, a link on A to `/local`, which redirects to B, was **fetched on B**. Dropping the URL from the results afterwards does not undo the request.
2. **A scan could raise a tool's rate.** `rate_limit` replaced the tool's own rate, so a request for 100000 ran at 100000.
3. **`concurrency` was dropped.**
4. **No back-off on 429/503**, and no `target_throttled` in the report.

## Fix

- **katana passes `-dr`** (no redirects). In-scope links are still crawled. The new `FollowRedirects` field (default off) re-enables redirects in code only.
- **A scan's limits only lower the tool's own.** `rate_limit` and `concurrency` arrive already capped at the local policy's `rate.max_rps` by the sdk executor. Each tool now reports its own limits through `Limits()`, and the wrapper takes the lower value; `concurrency` reaches `-threads`, `-c` or `-t`.
- **Back-off on 429/503.** When a target answers 429 Too Many Requests or 503 (httpx, katana):
  - the rate for the job's later targets halves, down to 1/s;
  - the wait before the next target is 2 s, then 4 s, up to 30 s;
  - the CTIS report carries `target_throttled: true`, `throttled_targets` and `throttled_rate_limit`.

  There is no rotation or evasion (RFC-034).
- **Extra args cannot send a tool to other hosts.** These flags are refused in any spelling before any run: `-fr` / `-follow-redirects`, `-fs` / `-field-scope`, `-cs` / `-crawl-scope`, `-ns` / `-no-scope`, `-dr` / `-disable-redirects` (including `-dr=false`).

## Threat model

- **Attacker:** a compromised platform or a hostile target.
- **Target that redirects or links elsewhere:** it can no longer steer the crawler into making requests to a host nobody validated. Before this fix, the sensor would hit a third party from the customer's IP.
- **Compromised platform:** it can no longer use `rate_limit` to make the sensor flood a target above the tool's ceiling.
- **Rate-limiting target:** the sensor now backs off instead of hammering it.
- **Tenant isolation / authz:** unchanged.

## Verification

- **Unit tests:**
  - `TestBuildArgs_NoRedirects` (katana, negative);
  - `TestScanTargets_RateLimitsOnlyLower`: 0/0, then 10/5, then 100000/100000 → the tool defaults;
  - `TestScanTargets_BackOffOn429`: rates 40, 20, 10, waits 2 s then 4 s, and the report properties;
  - `TestBackoffFloorAndCap`;
  - `TestScanTargets_ExtraArgsStayOnTheHost` (negative, 10 spellings, nothing runs).
- **Real binaries.** katana 1.7.0 and httpx 1.12.0 (SHA-verified) ran with this branch's sensor binary on a scratch Docker network against two scratch `nginx:alpine` hosts. I read host B's access log for the run's time window only.
  - `-standalone -tool katana` on `/page`, `/` and `/local`: **0 requests on B**.
  - The control (the same crawl without `-dr`): B got `GET /from-local`.
  - httpx on a 429 endpoint returns `status_code: 429` into the result that the back-off reads.
- `go test -race ./...`, `golangci-lint` v2.13.1 (0 issues), and `sensorrename -check` all pass.

## Reason

Selected-model capacity failures currently produce a generic failure notice that hides the cause and gives no next step. The new notice names the capacity error and suggests retrying or changing models without claiming that no work occurred.

Requested by: Hoss Huang (@CJHwong) via Slack DM.

## Changes

1. **Codex error handling** (`backends/codex.py`): recognize the observed selected-model capacity message, case-insensitively, and raise a safe `AgentTurnError` before any empty-reply nudge.
2. **Regression tests** (`test_codex_backend.py`): cover completion and abort records, mixed casing, partial replies, and private provider detail.
3. **Backend notes** (`docs/agent/backends.md`): document the capacity-specific notice.

After: “The selected model is at capacity, so this request stopped without a final answer. Try again shortly, or ask me to use a different model.”

Fills the gaps between the master prompt and what `main` already had (claims, AI extraction, matching, approve gate, PayPal payouts, webhooks, audit, AG Grid claims, `/demo` were already built).

## Changes
- **DB:** Neon HTTP driver replaced with postgres-js so Railway (or any TCP Postgres) works. New `sessions` and `notifications` tables (migration `0027`).
- **Env:** Zod validation at server start (`src/instrumentation.ts`, `src/lib/env.ts`). Integrations are all-or-nothing; the live PayPal host is refused. `.env.example` rewritten (names only). `*.env` is now gitignored.
- **Auth:** bcrypt hashing (legacy scrypt hashes still verify). Sessions are Postgres rows; the cookie carries a random token and only its HMAC (keyed by `SESSION_SECRET`) is stored. Logout revokes server-side. `jose` removed.
- **S3:** client built from `AWS_REGION` only (SDK default credential chain). Uploads go browser -> S3 through a presigned PUT that signs key, type and size; the server checks the key prefix (workspace + claim), file signatures and duplicates, and deletes rejected objects.
- **AI:** OpenAI is the default provider when its key is set. Duplicate matching window widened to 3 days.
- **Payout batches** page uses AG Grid.
- **Webhook** also served at `/api/webhooks/paypal`.
- **Notifications:** in-app page + unread badge; Nodemailer email only when all SMTP vars are set.
- **Seed:** `pnpm db:seed` creates a fixed demo team with an admin and two members (logins in README).
- **Tests + CI:** extraction parsing, env validation, matching window, and an end-to-end approve-and-pay test on real Postgres with PayPal mocked (racing double approval pays once). GitHub Actions runs lint, typecheck, tests with a Postgres service, and build.
- **README:** mermaid architecture, setup, S3 IAM + CORS, PayPal setup, Vercel env checklist.

- Run `pnpm db:migrate` on the target DB: the new auth needs the `sessions` table. Existing sign-ins are logged out once (JWT cookies are no longer accepted).

author: osergios
body:
## Τι αλλάζει · What changes

Stacked on #15.

- **`_resolve_backup_alerts()`, called from `_check_backup()`**, sets `resolved_at` on open backup alerts whose condition no longer holds. It is the same pattern as `resolve_employee()`.
  - a backup is set up now (local status or cloud) → `backup_none`;
  - a local copy from the last 50 h → `backup_old`;
  - a cloud success from the last 50 h → `backup_cloud_old`;
  - the last local and USB result is not `fail` → `backup_failed`.
- **The rows stay** as history; they're only closed.
- **It runs before the 09:00 gate**, so an alert closes on the very next check (every 15″), even when the nightly backup succeeds at 23:30.
- **It writes only when something is open:** a read first, then an `UPDATE`. That avoids a write transaction every 15 seconds on a Raspberry Pi's SD card.
- **Alerts wiki** (Greek and English): one sentence.

## Γιατί · Why

`backup_none`, `backup_old`, `backup_cloud_old` and `backup_failed` stayed open after the problem was gone. Admins had to clear them by hand, and real warnings got lost among stale ones.

- [x] Σελίδα διαχείρισης · Admin page (alerts)

- **New unit test:**
  - `backup_none` and `backup_cloud_old` are open, plus a failed, 60-hour-old local backup;

body:
Unblocks elixir-vibe/vibe_kit#2.

## Why

`mix igniter.install` temporarily adds Igniter, which locks the latest `ex_ast` (0.13.1). Every Reach release since 2.3.4 requires `ex_ast ~> 0.12.0`, so Hex silently resolves fresh installs to **Reach 2.2.0**. That happened on basecamp/once-campfire-elixir. With a `~> 2.8` floor, resolution fails instead.

## Changes

- `{:ex_ast, "~> 0.13.2"}`. 0.13.2 fixes the `import Mod, unquote(opts)` crash at the source (elixir-vibe/ex_ast#21).
- **More findings, none lost.** ex_ast 0.13 now matches piped calls, Sourceror-wrapped literals and calls inside keyword lists, so existing patterns catch more real cases. Smell corpus snapshots gained 11 entries and lost none. I checked each one against the source:
  - `split |> hd` ×3: plug `debugger.ex:405`, phoenix `controller.ex:1755`, …
  - redundant `nil` default ×3: plug `static.ex:187`, phoenix `router.ex:313`, ecto `changeset.ex:1464`
  - `Enum.into(_, %{})` ×2, `map |> join` ×1
  - "case returns true/false" ×3 (advisory, as before)
- Fixed the same redundant `Keyword.get/3` `nil` defaults in `Reach.Frontend.Elixir`, which Reach's own smell check now flags.
- **Evidence pattern runner:** ex_ast 0.13 raises `Protocol.UndefinedError` while collecting `import Mod, unquote(opts)`. The runner now skips that like `Reach.Smell.PatternRunner` already does. The root cause is ex_ast's `opt_value/2` assuming import options are a literal list.

Follow-up to #66, for the Notification alert style.

- **Square icon.** The status bar icon was the launcher foreground bitmap. It has an opaque background, so the system drew it as a solid square. A new `ic_notification` vector replaces it: a white silhouette of the four shards, traced from the launcher artwork, with gaps where the shards meet.

author: blackwellboy
body:
## Three failure loops from the live game fixed

The live, model-driven game's `/api/why` showed three loops. Each was traced through its `action_outcomes` and decisions to a cause.

| Loop | Source | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| store grain, "I'm not carrying any grain" (113) | `model_selected` (19 of 20 in the last week) | Instinct drafts "harvest, then store grain" for every chit near a ripe farm, ahead of time. 14 of 20 plans found the farm already harvested by others, so the harvest sowed instead. The rest harvested into nearly full hands. | In `Instinct.options` (the model's menu) only: offer the harvest-and-store option only for a ripe farm that no chit is already set on, and only with room for 6 grain |
| gather, "None can't be gathered" (96) | `model_generated` | The parser let through steps with no object: `{"do":"gather wood"}`, `gather_berries`, an unknown key, or null | In `parse.py` (syntax only, fine in experiment mode), an object written into the verb becomes `what`. A gather, craft or take still without one is rejected, like other unreadable steps. |
| experiment, "some of those aren't real items" (71) | `model_generated`, plain-text experiments | The text parser dropped "at", merged the station into the last ingredient, kept "name it" as an ingredient, and read comma-less lists as one item | A fixed reading rule: a station after "at" or as the last word becomes `at`; "name it" and "called X" set the name; a comma-less run of known item names is split, longest names first |

**Would have prevented**, checked against the live data:

- **Store grain:** running the live save forward 3 days on 3 seeds, with a chooser that picks the option half the time, gave 35 failures before and 1 after. Harvests that found nothing went 35 > 0, and grain stored 60 > 55.
- **Missing objects:** all 17 of the week's steps (11 gather, 3 take, 3 craft).
- **Experiments:** 3 of 3 now read as real items plus a station.

## Checks

- `tests/test_harvest_options.py` and `tests/test_live_loops.py`. Each of 7 broken variants makes a new test fail.
- Full suite passes. The identity test passes.
- `tools/harness/ab.py` against main, seeds 42 7 24, 30 days: identical on every seed. Instinct runs are unchanged.

Found and left for follow-up:

- A harvest step that names a farm uses it ripe or not: 6 grain came from an empty farm.
- Takes and gathers into full hands, of heavy ore or charcoal offered by instinct: 95 tries.

body:
Vì sao: chủ shop 05/10/2026 xem hộp thư của HSLC — «khó nhìn quá, sửa cho dễ nhìn hơn, đảm bảo tin nhắn không bao giờ bị miss
và tốt hơn Pancake»; và trang Đơn hàng «đồng bộ realtime, không delay, không bị miss đơn». Đo trong mã thấy năm lỗ:
1. Hội thoại chỉ được MỞ khi bot xử lý tin — page đã trả lời trước (nhân viên trên Pancake / Meta tự động) hay bot tắt thì
   khách nhắn mà hộp thư không có dòng nào.
2. Tin khách không chữ không ảnh (nhãn dán · ghi âm · video · tệp · vị trí) bị đường nhận BỎ HẲN — kể cả khi khách gửi ghi âm
   hỏi giá.
3. Hộp thư đọc tin bot từ lịch sử của bot ⇒ hiện cả lời chào mặc định và câu bot soạn mà KHÔNG gửi.
4. Không đơn ERP nào phát sự kiện realtime (chỉ đồng bộ Pancake phát) ⇒ đơn bot chốt / nhân viên tạo không làm trang Đơn hàng
   đang mở nhúc nhích; lượt làm mới tới lúc tab ẩn thì RƠI MẤT; thông báo ghi cứng «từ Pancake».
5. Ghi đơn từ hội thoại bỏ qua mọi hội thoại «bot đang bật mà chưa HANDOFF» — nhân viên chốt trên Pancake quá 3 giờ sau bot
   (đường nhận không coi là «nhân viên đang trả lời») thì đơn không bao giờ được ghi.

Thay đổi:
· Không bỏ sót khách: `noteCustomerArrived` (fanpage · Messenger trực tiếp) và `ensureZaloInbox` mở hội thoại + đẩy mốc tin
  khách NGAY lúc nhận tin, phát sự kiện `chat`. Tin không chữ không ảnh ghi một dòng DONE note MEDIA_ONLY («[Khách gửi nhãn dán /
  ghi âm / video / tệp — mở trên kênh để xem]») — không vào hàng chờ của bot, nhưng người thấy.
· «Chưa đọc»: cột `staff_seen_at` (migration 0212) — nhân viên (người trả lời được) mở hội thoại thì đã đọc; người chỉ xem không
  xoá dấu của đội. Bộ lọc «Chưa đọc», chữ đậm + chấm trên danh sách.
· Dòng thời gian kênh nhắn tin: tin bot đọc từ sổ ĐÃ GỬI (BOT_SENT, gộp dòng ghi sẵn + dòng mã kênh) — đúng thứ khách đã nhận.
  Danh sách sắp theo mốc TIN cuối, không theo `updated_at` (mở / gắn nhãn không đẩy hội thoại lên đầu). Tên khách ở đầu hội thoại
  lấy theo tên kênh gửi kèm khi chưa có hồ sơ.
· Giao diện: ba cột cao bằng màn hình, mỗi cột tự cuộn; ảnh đại diện chữ cái + chấm kênh; chip «chờ N phút» (đỏ từ 15 phút);
  bong bóng chat (khách trái · bot tím · nhân viên xanh · ngoài ERP xanh dương), vạch ngày «Hôm nay / Hôm qua», gộp tin liền nhau;
  thanh trạng thái bot + «Trả lại cho AI»; ô soạn luôn ở đáy, tự cao, Enter gửi · Shift + Enter xuống dòng, nút ảnh trong ô;
  đang đọc tin cũ mà có tin mới ⇒ nút «Có tin mới ↓», không giật cuộn. Tiêu đề tab «(N) Hộp thư khách» = số khách đang chờ;
  tiếng «ting» khi số chưa đọc tăng (bật / tắt, nhớ theo trình duyệt); làm mới 5 giây (tab ẩn 30 giây) + sự kiện `chat` ~tức thì.
· Realtime đơn: mọi lượt tạo / sửa / huỷ / giao / chứng từ thanh toán của đơn ERP phát `order` (source ERP) SAU khi ghi xong;
  RealtimeProvider làm mới trong ~2 giây cho sự kiện đơn ERP / tin khách (đồng bộ Pancake vẫn gộp 20 giây như cũ), giữ lượt làm

· tests/sales-inbox.test.ts · tests/chat-order.test.ts · tests/sales-order-sync.test.ts: tin nhãn dán mở hội thoại ngay + chưa
