author: freshlybrewedcode
body:
`room.ts` was one `Room` class of ~2120 lines holding three of the roles ADR 0013 names: board authority, gateway and participant. This PR splits it into modules along those roles. **Nothing changes in behaviour or on the wire.** `Room` is now a composition with the same public API, so components and hooks keep working unchanged. The authority module depends on no DOM and no React, and a separate typecheck enforces that, so it can later run in Bun inside `canvas serve`.

Closes #110
Part of #78

## Module map

| Module | Lines | What lives there |
|---|---|---|
| `web/lib/room.ts` | 530 | `Room`: builds the parts, wires them, sequences `canvas serve`'s `welcome`, and keeps the public API (mostly one-line delegations). It also re-exports the types (`Presence`, `Peer`, `Approval`, …) |
| `room/authority.ts` | 700 | **Authority** (host only). It checks and applies guests' updates and sends them on to the others, saves the board (`board-save`) and runs `tidy`. It also holds admission (`Admissions`, `PeerIdentities`, hello/identify), the signed member list, the handover (`reset` → `move`, `relocated`), `execute` and guests' requests and reads (with approvals), the snapshot a guest gets, and `hostcast` |
| `room/gateway.ts` | 342 | **Gateway** (host only). It owns the `ServerLink` and its status, takes what `canvas serve` sends, puts it in the mirror and passes it on to guests, and runs `sync` (formerly `syncResources`: files, tree, PTYs, logs, kind probes, `Releases`). It also runs agents' board tool calls, `answerPermission` and `resizeTerminal` |
| `room/participant.ts` | 942 | **Participant** (every browser). It holds the transport (`join`, `relocate`, `leaveTransport`), presence and the member-list gate on it, frame focus, the connection log and relay watch, `act`, and a guest's side: hello, admission, broadcasts, the log asks. `boardHeight`, the one DOM read, lives here |
| `room/mirror.ts` | 360 | **Mirror** (shared). Sessions, kinds, terminals, files and trees, keyed by address (`keyOf`). It is filled by the gateway on the host and by the participant on guests, and `snapshot` builds what a new guest gets |
| `room/reach.ts` | 47 | `runtimeOf`, `addressOf`, `here` (the own-runtime frame filter), `agentFrame` |
| `room/channels.ts` | 40 | The `Channels` type, `Joined`, `Hello`, `Identify` and `json` |
| `room/topics.ts` | 35 | `Topic` and `Emitter` |

### The interfaces between the parts

- **Participant → authority:** when the participant joins a room, it passes `attach({channels, peers})` (`null` on leaving). The authority sets its own handlers on `identify`, `sync`, `update` and `request`, so all guest traffic it receives reaches it directly. The participant also asks the authority who is in: `admitted()` decides where presence goes, `isIn(peer)` whose presence is taken. It reports peers coming and going with `arrive(peer)` and `leave(peer)`, and calls `relocated(next)` after moving. Its join uses `ownRelay()`.
- **Authority → its surroundings (`Surroundings`):** one object with `doc`, `mirror`, `selfId`, `fingerprint`, `identity`, `link()`, `state()`, `screen()`, `emit` and `record`, plus two ports:
  - `Presences`: `send`, `drop`, `nameOf`, `showFingerprints`. The participant implements it.
  - `RuntimeDoor`: `{open, send(ClientToServer)}`. `Gateway` implements it. `execute`, `board-save` and the `member-*`/`room-reset` messages go through it.
- **Gateway → the room (`GatewayEvents`):** `welcome`, `members`, `room`, `forward(message, to?)` (→ `Authority.hostcast`), `claim` and `idle` (→ the participant's agent claims), `replaced`, `record` and `emit`.
- **Mirror:** `Emitter` and `{host, runtime(), onGap}`. Reads are by address. Writes are `put*`/`push*`, plus `welcome` (host), `heads` (guest), `restartTerminal` and `clear`.

The risks flagged in #113 are covered:
- The address checks stay where they were: `execute` and `onGuestRequest` in the authority, `answerPermission` and `resizeTerminal` in the gateway.
- `shownSessions`, `Releases`, `opened` and `watched` still go only through `here()`, the own-runtime filter in `reach.ts`. They still key by bare id.
- The guest snapshot still sends one `sessions` message per runtime, now built in `Mirror.snapshot`.
- `metaLists` is still cleared before any `sessions` listener runs: the mirror subscribes first.

## How the DOM-free guard works

`tsconfig.authority.json` extends the main config and typechecks `room/authority.ts` and everything it imports. Three settings make it a guard:
- `lib: ["ESNext"]` and `types: ["bun"]`, so there is no DOM lib.
- `react`, `react/*`, `react-dom` and `react-dom/*` are mapped through `paths` to an empty stub (`room/no-dom/no-react.d.ts`). Without the stub, `paths` falls back to `node_modules`.
- `room/no-dom/env.d.ts` declares only `JsonWebKey` and `BufferSource` from `node:crypto`'s webcrypto. Bun has these at runtime, but TypeScript keeps them in the DOM lib. The main `tsconfig.json` excludes `room/no-dom`.

`bun run typecheck` is now `tsc --noEmit && tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.authority.json`, so `bun run check` runs the guard. I checked that it fails: importing `useState`, `document`, `window` or `showLink` from `link.ts` into the authority makes it fail.

To pass the guard, the authority's imports had to lose their DOM and React, through moves only:
- `useBoard`/`useFrames` (`board.ts`), `useComments` (`comments.ts`) and `useDrawing` (`drawing.ts`) moved to `hooks/use-doc.ts`. The lib files keep their stores and export them (`boardStore`, `commentsStore`, `drawingStore`). Imports are updated in `board.tsx`, `file-frame.tsx`, `drawing-frame.tsx` and `room-context.tsx`.
- `BoardLink`, `RelayLink` and `Identity` moved to `link-types.ts`. `link.ts` re-exports them.
- `Channel`, `RequestChannel` and the related types moved to `transport/channel.ts`. `transport.ts` re-exports them; it still names `RTCPeerConnection` in its diagnostics.

## Validation

- `bun run check`: format, lint, both typechecks and the unit tests pass: **451 tests**, 0 failures.
  - New: `room/authority.test.ts`, 4 tests. They run in Bun with no DOM, on fake channels, with real keys and proofs:
    - a guest's updates count only once it is in and only with `edit`;
    - a member is let in at once, and its updates go on to the others only;
    - a request is checked against the role, and another runtime's request is refused (`NOT_REACHABLE`) without reaching `canvas serve`;
    - nothing runs while `canvas serve` isn't open.
  - No existing unit test changed.
- `E2E_WEB_PORT=4537 E2E_RELAY_PORT=4539 nix develop -c bun run e2e`: **49 passed**. The only ✘ is the existing `test.fail()` for the tree-resize bug (finding 05). No cassettes were re-recorded.
  - A first full run had 2 failures (`agent-sessions` "new conversations…", `agent-board` "…draws a flowchart…"). I had edited files under `src/` while it ran, and Vite's HMR reloaded the pages; the console showed yjs's "Tried to remove event handler". Rerun alone, both passed. The second full run, with nothing being edited, passed completely.
  - `e2e/tests/members.spec.ts`: no expectation changed. The tampered-client hooks used the guest's internals on `room` directly (`leaveRoom` stubbed out, `actions`, `hostPeer`, `sendPresence`, setting `access`). They now reach them on `room.participant`, where those internals moved.
- Manual run: Vite on :4547, `canvas serve` on a copy of `e2e/projects/basic`, and a headless Chromium host tab paired by the link's code, driven with Playwright.
  - I added a Files, a Terminal and an Agent (claude) frame. The status showed connected to canvas serve, the runtime id came from the welcome, and the tree arrived.
  - In a freshly paired tab after a reload, the board had been saved and came back. Typing into the terminal round-tripped the PTY. The agent frame showed the settings its kind offers (model, mode) from the kind probe. Pointing the file frame at `README.md` opened it.
  - No console errors.

## AGENTS.md

AGENTS.

author: jamesperenchio1
body:
## GPS accuracy circle The ring around the position dot used to be a fixed screen-pixel size, so it looked the same at every zoom and told you nothing about how accurate the fix was. It's now drawn as a polygon whose radius is the browser's reported accuracy in meters, like Google Maps. It grows when you zoom in and shrinks when you zoom out. It sits under the station markers so a wide circle from a poor fix doesn't wash them out. The dot itself stays a fixed size. ## EN/TH toggle - A small EN | TH switch in the header. English is the default, and the choice is saved per device in `localStorage`. The saved choice is restored after hydration so the prerendered page doesn't mismatch. - New `lib/i18n.ts`: a zustand store, a string table and `stationName()`. It's a store rather than React context because station popups are separate React roots. - What gets translated: the header, hints, chips, the nearest-station pill, the route sheet, station cards, search results, ETA labels and clock times. Arrival directions now show the Thai half of upstream's `"เคหะฯ | Kheha"` string. - Map: station labels switch to `nameTh`/`nameEn`. The basemap's bilingual place labels (`name:latin` + `name:nonlatin`) become single-language for whichever is selected. - Search still matches both languages. ## Testing - `npm run build` passes (webpack + Serwist, TypeScript). - Checked in headless Chromium with a faked GPS fix (120 m accuracy): the ring is large at zoom 16 and small at zoom 14. Switching EN → TH → EN changes every label and switches them all back. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01HAb3jdQSAp2bbC9yBUMNCB --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01HAb3jdQSAp2bbC9yBUMNCB)_

Confidence Score: 4/5

The PR appears safe to merge, with non-blocking map presentation and metadata consistency issues.

Findings

1.  **English Names Lose Priority** ▶ 2.  **Accuracy Ring Tints Routes** ▶ 3.  **Thai Metadata Stays English** ▶
Fix with agent prompt `````markdown ### Issue 1 components/TransitMap.tsx:46 If a place has both `name:latin` and `name_en`, English mode now chooses the Latin transliteration first. That can show a transliteration instead of the English place name. Prefer `name_en` when it is available. ```suggestion : ["coalesce", ["get", "name_en"], ["get", "name:latin"], ["get", "name"]]; ``` Note: If this suggestion doesn't match your team's coding style, reply to this and let me know. I'll remember it for next time! ### Issue 2 components/TransitMap.tsx:459 The accuracy fill and outline sit below station markers but above the transit lines and highlighted route. With a wide accuracy circle, the blue overlay reduces the contrast of the route the user is following. Place both accuracy layers below the route layers while keeping station markers on top. Note: If this suggestion doesn't match your team's coding style, reply to this and let me know. I'll remember it for next time! ### Issue 3 lib/i18n.ts:25 Switching to Thai changes the visible heading and document language, but the browser-tab title and description remain in English. Updating that metadata with the selected language would keep those entry points consistent with the page. --- For each issue above, determine whether it is valid and should be fixed. author: udondan
body:
The AWS service authorization reference lists these condition keys as `String`, but their values are numbers. With the type `String`, the methods default to `StringLike`, which cannot compare numbers. This PR sets them to numeric in `lib/generator/fixes.ts`:

| Key                           | Evidence                                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `iam:DelegationDuration`      | The description in the IAM docs says the key works with numeric operators                                                                    |
| `glacier:ArchiveAgeInDays`    | The vault lock examples of AWS use `NumericLessThanEquals` / `NumericGreaterThanEquals`                                                       |
| `redshift:DurationSeconds`    | The number of seconds until the temporary credentials expire                                                                                 |
| `ec2:ReplayWindowSizePackets` | The number of packets of the replay window of a VPN tunnel, like the other numeric tunnel options (`ec2:Phase1LifetimeSeconds`, `ec2:DPDTimeoutSeconds`, …), which are already numeric |

The four methods now default to `NumericEquals` and take a number (`number | number[]`) instead of a string. Code that passes the value as a string no longer compiles in TypeScript, Java, C# and Go; it would not have matched numerically before anyway.

The models are the same as a regeneration of the four services from the AWS docs with the fixes.

This is the outcome of a review of all condition keys for #6: no other `String` key needs a different type. ARN, Bool and enum-like keys work with the string operators, and no AWS managed policy uses a non-string operator on a key typed `String`. The example of #6, `s3:object-lock-remaining-retention-days`, is already numeric.

Closes #6

author: tobiaslaross
body:
Shows a lock-screen and Dynamic Island Live Activity while music plays and the user is home (their HA away boolean is off).

- **Controls:** play/pause, previous and next, plus volume −/+ buttons. These are `LiveActivityIntent`s, so they work without opening the app. Each volume step moves the whole group by 5 % and sets every grouped speaker to the same level, the way the app's group slider does.
- **Progress:** the bar and the elapsed and remaining times are timer-driven, so they keep moving between updates.
- **Long titles:** the title wraps to two lines and can shrink a little. A Live Activity can't scroll or animate custom text.
- **Updates:** the Navigator reload loop starts, updates and ends the activity while the app is open. While the app is closed, a button press updates the activity optimistically, and after a skip it re-reads the new track.
- **Ending:** the activity ends when music stops, when the user is away, or when the geofence exit fires.
- **Artwork:** the album art is cached as a small JPEG in the app group so the widget can draw it.

**Background updates:** the activity is requested with a push token, and the app registers that token and its state with IntelliNest-API (TobiasLaross/IntelliNest-API#5). A Home Assistant automation forwards every `media_player` change to the relay, which pushes the update to the activity. On a track change the relay also sends a background push, so the app can fetch the new album art.

body:
## Problem

`antigravity` was a registry key for `GeminiAdapter`. Its discovery cascade looked for a binary named `antigravity` (none exists) before `gemini`, and passed the Gemini command line. The Antigravity CLI ships as `agy`; `agy --help` (1.2.11) has `-p` and `--output-format` but not `-m` (it uses `--model`) or `--yolo` (it uses `--dangerously-skip-permissions`). So `cli: antigravity` could not spawn the tool its name refers to.

## Change

Option chosen: make the key resolve to the agy adapter (no deprecation error; existing configs keep working and now spawn the right binary).

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| `registry.py` | `antigravity` → `AgyAdapter`; `gemini` unchanged |
| `gemini.py` | cascade = `BERNSTEIN_GEMINI_BINARY` → `gemini`; `ANTIGRAVITY_BINARY` removed; errors point to the `agy` adapter |
| `_contract.py` | `antigravity` strategy = agy's (text-signals); removed from prompt-append addendum set |
| `contracts/antigravity.yaml` | mirrors `agy.yaml` (binary `agy`) |
| `report.py`, `adapter_cmd.py` | `antigravity` binary override → `agy` |
| `multimodal.py` | `antigravity` dropped from multimodal-capable set |
| docs | `antigravity.md` = alias page + changed behaviour; install/discovery/override moved to `gemini.md`; lane tables updated |
| tests | gemini cascade, registry name resolution, admission evidence, identity cache, golden argv |

`cli: gemini` and `BERNSTEIN_GEMINI_BINARY` behave as before.

## Depends on

Stacked on #6408 (contract header wording); this PR also replaces the `antigravity.yaml` body from that branch. Merge #6408 first, or close it in favour of this one.

## Verification

- 5470 passed / 123 skipped across every test file touching gemini/agy/antigravity/addendum/multimodal/strategy/adapters-check
- `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on changed files

author: thayorns
body:
rubocop-performance 1.27 reports `Performance/ChainArrayAllocation` on five lines of `lib/factbase/indexed`, and that is what fails the Renovate pull request #697.

`sortable?` in the `gt`, `gte`, `lt` and `lte` terms chained `sort` after `flat_map`. It sorts only to learn whether the values compare, so it now calls `sort!` on the array `flat_map` has just built. `IndexedAnd` chained `uniq` and `sort_by` after `flat_map`, and now calls `uniq!` and `sort_by!` on `j` as separate statements, since `uniq!` returns nil when nothing changes.

The arrays come out the same as before with fewer allocations, and the code passes lint with both 1.26.1 and 1.27.

Closes #1320

## Summary

Follow-up to #116: a bank-transfer order that hasn't been paid 72 h after the buyer chose « Virement » is now cancelled automatically.

author: icekryptor
body:
## Что

- Миграция `AddProductCategorySeoBlocks1790740000000`: только `ALTER TABLE product_categories ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS seo_blocks jsonb` (nullable, без default). down — `DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS`.
- Сущность `ProductCategory.seoBlocks`, DTO (`z.array(z.unknown()).nullable().optional()`, как `blocks` у страниц и статей), `shared` (`ProductCategory.seoBlocks?`), публичная выдача (`/api/public/categories/:slug` отдаёт поле как есть).
- Админка категорий: секция «SEO-текст и FAQ» с тем же `BlockEditor`, что у страниц и статей; поле необязательное (нет блоков → `null`).
- Витрина `/categories/[slug]`: после сетки товаров `seoBlocks` через общий `BlockRenderer` (блок `faq` даёт FAQPage JSON-LD). Только на первой странице (`page` нет или 1; мусорный `page` трактуется как 1, как и сама пагинация). Нет валидных блоков — секция не рисуется. В `en` берётся `translations.en.seoBlocks`, иначе русские блоки.
- Черновики `api/data/seo-category-texts.json` (все `draft: true`) для `kits`, `combo`, `reagents`, `equipment` и сид `import:seo-category-texts` (`--dry-run`, `--include-drafts`): заполняет ТОЛЬКО пустые `seo_blocks`, `meta_title`, `meta_description`, не перезаписывает, неизвестные slug пропускает с отчётом.

Реальные названия категорий в каталоге: `reagents` = «Реактивы» (не «Реагенты»), `equipment` = «Лабораторное оборудование», `kits` = «Наборы», `combo` = «Комбо». Тексты привязаны к этим slug.

## Зачем

SEO-план Q4 2026: у категорий нет места для текста под ключи «химические реактивы» (638), «лабораторное оборудование» (331), «набор юного химика» / «набор для опытов…» (238/216/166). У `combo` своего кластера нет, там без искусственных ключей. Каждый текст 250–400 слов, 4 раздела, раздел «Безопасность», FAQ из 4 вопросов, 3–5 ссылок на товары своей категории и 2–3 на соседние категории (относительные). Факты только из `tilda-catalog.json`.

## Как проверено

TDD: каждый тест сначала красный.
- `npm run lint` (0 ошибок; 6 старых предупреждений в чужих файлах), `npm run typecheck` (3 workspace) — чисто.
- `npx prettier --check .` — чисто.
- `npm run test -w web` — 190 файлов, 1445 тестов зелёные (в т.ч. `page.seoBlocks.test.tsx`: первая/вторая/третья страница, `page=1&sort`, мусорный `page`, нет блоков, только невалидные блоки, FAQPage, порядок после сетки, локали; `CategoryForm.test.tsx`: секция, круг блоков, `null`).
- `TEST_DATABASE_URL=…/ximi4ka_shop_test_cattexts npm run test -w api` — 79 файлов, 883 теста зелёные (миграция up/down/идемпотентность; роуты `seoBlocks`; сид на реальной БД с кругом через jsonb; контракт данных: slug, длины, структура, ссылки, запрещённые фразы, безопасность). Своя одноразовая БД удалена после работы. Один раз «socket hang up» в чужом тесте лимита вебхука Telegram под нагрузкой полного прогона, отдельно и в повторном полном прогоне зелёный.
- Живой прогон: сид `--dry-run`, боевой, повторный (0 заполнено, 4 «уже заполнено») на локальной БД; API + `next dev`: `/categories/reagents` отдаёт `data-seo-blocks` и один FAQPage, `?page=2` — ни текста, ни FAQPage; снимок секции отрисован нормально.

## Что проверить владельцу

- Вычитка текстов (`draft: true`): факты и безопасность. Не подтверждено данными: состав комплекта «Все три набора!» (в тексте только «максимальная скидка, состав в карточке»), состав «Запаса всех реактивов» кроме «по 2 шт.», комплектация «Набора для электролиза» (в описании «3АА-батарейки, блок питания, крокодилы», так и написано с оговоркой). Из каталога взята пометка «вещество ядовито» у хлорида бария, дихромата калия и нитрата никеля.
- Публичный список `/api/public/categories` теперь тоже отдаёт `seoBlocks` (около 3 КБ на категорию); при необходимости можно отрезать в списке отдельным PR.
- Админ-сохранение формы категории теперь всегда шлёт `seoBlocks` (`null`, если блоков нет).

## Как запустить на сервере

Каталог — ядро магазина: `deploy.sh` сначала переключает контейнеры и только потом гоняет миграции, так что упавшая миграция = новый код на старой схеме, API категорий и товаров отвечает 500. Поэтому колонку добавляют ДО мёржа.

1. Владельцы таблиц (ожидаем только `ximishop_user`; пустой вывод второго запроса — норма):
   ```bash
   docker exec -i supabase-db psql -U supabase_admin -d ximi4ka_shop \
     -c "SELECT tablename, tableowner FROM pg_tables WHERE schemaname='public' AND tablename IN ('product_categories','migrations');" \
     -c "SELECT tablename, tableowner FROM pg_tables WHERE schemaname='public' AND tableowner <> 'ximishop_user';"
   ```
2. Только если владелец другой (для остальных таблиц из вывода — то же самое):
   ```bash
   docker exec -i supabase-db psql -U supabase_admin -d ximi4ka_shop \
     -c 'ALTER TABLE product_categories OWNER TO ximishop_user;'
   ```
3. Колонка заранее, от superuser, ДО мёржа (идемпотентно, мгновенно):
   ```bash
   docker exec -i supabase-db psql -U supabase_admin -d ximi4ka_shop \
     -c 'ALTER TABLE product_categories ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS seo_blocks jsonb;'
   ```
4. Мёрж (= деплой). Миграция при деплое станет no-op и отметится в `migrations`.
5. Проверка после деплоя: в логе деплоя `миграция применена: AddProductCategorySeoBlocks1790740000000`, и
   ```bash
   docker exec -i supabase-db psql -U supabase_admin -d ximi4ka_shop \
     -c "SELECT name FROM migrations ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1;" \
     -c "SELECT column_name, data_type, is_nullable FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name='product_categories' AND column_name='seo_blocks';"
   for u in /categories/reagents /categories/kits /api/public/categories /api/public/products?limit=1; do
     echo -n "$u "; curl -s -m 20 -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" "https://new.ximi4ka.ru$u"; done
   ```
6. Импорт текстов (после вычитки; порядок как в шаге 4 `deploy/SEO-LAUNCH.md`, в контейнере нет `api/data` и `tsx`):
   ```bash
   docker cp api/data/seo-category-texts.json ximishop-api:/app/api/data/seo-category-texts.json
   docker exec ximishop-api node api/dist/seeds/import-seo-category-texts.js --dry-run --include-drafts | tail -n 6
   docker exec ximishop-api node api/dist/seeds/import-seo-category-texts.js --include-drafts
   ```
   В dry-run ожидаем 4 `would fill` и 0 `unknown`. Сохраните вывод боевого запуска: по нему делается откат.
7. Откат: старый код новую колонку игнорирует, откат кода безопасен без правок схемы. Тексты — `UPDATE product_categories SET seo_blocks = NULL, meta_title = NULL, meta_description = NULL WHERE slug IN (…)` только для slug из вывода импорта, у которых поля были заполнены импортом. Саму колонку при необходимости снимает `ALTER TABLE product_categories DROP COLUMN seo_blocks` от `supabase_admin`.

`deploy/SEO-LAUNCH.md` в этом PR не менялся: шаг про категории добавляет владелец-сессия.

body:
Refs #3685 (ADR-308 §4.3, §8.2; S7).

**Problem:** Das M0-Profil der Sandbox-Org (#3712, #3715) gilt nur, solange Actions aus sind. Das Merge-Werkzeug misst das bei jedem Merge. Die Selbstprüfung hat bisher aber nicht belegt, dass der Sandbox-Token Actions gar nicht erst einschalten kann.

**Änderung:**
- Neue Probe je Repo der Org: `PUT /repos/{r}/actions/permissions` mit einem Nicht-Boolean als Wert.
  - 403 oder 404 heißt: kein Recht.
  - Jeder andere Status ist ein Befund (fail-closed).
  - Die Probe ändert nie etwas, weil GitHub den Wert nicht übernehmen kann.
- Ist in der Org kein Repo sichtbar, gibt es keinen Beleg. Das ist ebenfalls ein Befund.
- `probe_status` nimmt jetzt auch die Methode als Parameter.

**Prüfung:**
- Mit dem Sandbox-Token gemessen (2026-10-05): 403 auf allen fünf Spiegeln, kein Befund.
- Dass mit Recht 422 kommt, ist **nicht gemessen** (Hypothese). Ein Test mit Owner-Rechten auf einen Actions-Schalter wäre ein Eingriff in Security-Config. Fail-closed deckt diesen Fall ab: Ein unerwarteter Status ergibt immer einen Befund.
- `make test`: 6601 passed, 3 skipped.

- `Not Connected` 오류에는 해결 안내(잠금 해제, 솔라나 계정 선택, 다른 지갑 확장 프로그램과의 충돌) 표시
- 지갑 선택 창을 모달이 아닌 일반 창으로 변경(모달이면 MetaMask SDK가 띄우는 안내·QR 창이 가려지고 눌리지 않음)

- 수정: "MetaMask 불러오는 중" 비활성 버튼 때문에 다음 갱신에서 모든 지갑 버튼이 눌리지 않던 버그
- 스마트폰: MetaMask 앱 열기 링크, Jupiter/Backpack 설치 링크

**기타**
- `vercel.json` 추가(출력 폴더 `.`, Netlify와 같은 보안 헤더)와 README의 Vercel 배포 절차

## 테스트
가짜 Wallet Standard 지갑 + 실제 MetaMask SDK 번들로 확인: 허용된 3개만 표시(Phantom/Solflare/타 체인 지갑 제외), 정상 연결·해제, 거절/일반 실패/계정 없음/`Not Connected` 메시지와 안내(한/영), 동일 이름 지갑 순차 시도와 거절 시 중단, Backpack 구형 연결 방식 대체, 응답 없음 안전장치, 비모달 창에서 페이지 위 요소 클릭, 모바일 링크, 7가지 화면 크기에서 경전 맨 아래까지 스크롤, 콘솔 오류 없음.

author: lcrzhang
body:
Closes #66

## What

`read_file` returns `.tex`, `.bib`, `.md`, `.csv` and friends verbatim.

```json
{"file": "template.tex", "part": "1 of 1",
 "text": "--- BEGIN UNTRUSTED CONTENT (template.tex, a course file, ...) ---\n\\documentclass{article}\n..."}
```

A PDF still comes back through the extractor with `pages` and `entries`,
unchanged.

## Why

A homework assignment with a PDF and a LaTeX template attached: the template is
the thing to work in, and this refused it as "not a PDF".

**Nothing is done to the bytes.** No markup stripping, no reflowing. On source,
the sanitizer's job is the boundary and the attribution — a backslash and a `%`
comment are what the question is about.

**The name may overrule a type that says only "bytes".** Canvas types by
extension and gives up often: a `.tex` arrives as `application/octet-stream` as
readily as `text/x-tex`, so content-type alone fails the common case.
`application/pdf` and `image/png` still decide for themselves. This is also the
only signal there will be inside a zip, where a member has a name and no type,
so the zip step inherits the rule rather than inventing one.

**Encoding is guessed in a fixed order and cannot fail:** UTF-8 with a BOM
stripped, then latin-1, which maps every byte. `errors="replace"` was the
alternative and drops characters out of the middle of somebody's source without
saying so.

**Parts rather than a cap**, reusing step 21, at 20 000 characters rather than
`MAX_CHARS`. That constant bounds a description sitting beside other fields in
a JSON answer; this bounds a whole answer, and the PDF path next to it is
bounded at 20 slides rather than at a character count.

## How tested

317 passing (9 new), `ruff` clean.

Cases: a `.tex` returned verbatim with its backslashes and comments intact, the
same file read when Canvas calls it `application/octet-stream`, an untyped blob
with no known suffix still refused, a long file arriving in parts with the last
one saying so, a part that does not exist refused with the count, the verifier
absent from a text answer, latin-1 and a BOM decoded rather than raising, and
the type-versus-name rule asserted directly.

One existing test changed its example: `test_a_refusal_says_what_to_do_instead`
used `SETUP.txt` as the unreadable thing, which is readable now, so the case
moved to an image. What it pins — that a refusal names a way forward — is
untouched.

## Docs

`README.md` and `SCOPE.md` both claimed "only PDFs" and are corrected.
`SCOPE.md` section 3 also still said a file id can only come from the module
tree; #65 established that an assignment description carries one, measured
against the live course, so that is fixed where it was claimed.

## What was left out

- The zip. `HW Week 5 - LaTeX template.zip` is still refused — that is the next
  step, and this one is the half that does not depend on it.
- No fixture carries a text file, so the tests build one through the mock
  transport and demo mode still serves only a PDF.
- Line ranges. A long text file is read in parts, not by line number; nothing
  has asked for the finer control yet.

agent: claude (cloud session vikingai-be, anthropic|claude-code-cloud|claude-opus-5.5) · role: IMPLEMENTATION_ENGINEER · TAKING (the earlier author went silent after the CRs)

## What and why
The branch's first fix (`4156a0d`) was blocked by two CRs (Claude-Cloud-Opus55, plus Codex-PC with an IL read of `ZoneSystem.GetSolidHeight`): it moved the effective ray origin to `routeY + 2.6 m`, which brings back the #248 false-safe where an overhead dock hides deep water.
- **Reverted** (`18fb28a`). The look-ahead is identical to main again.
- **Measure first.** Both CRs asked for the cause from data, and the issue's own diagnostics direction says the same.
  - `WaterSafety.FirstUnsafeSample`: the first unwadeable sample in walking order, the start included. It's pure. `PathSafe` is now "no failing sample", so its behaviour is unchanged.
  - `WaterSafetyMonitor.ExplainRefusal(a, b, step)` gives that sample's `x/z`, `routeY`, `rayOriginY` (route + 0.6), `solidHitY` (or null), `terrainY`, `waterLevel`, `walkDepth`, `terrainDepth` and `maxWadeDepth`. It's read-only.
  - `PlayerMovement` records **`move_water_refusal {taskId, position, waypoint, sample}`** right before `Blocked "Next step enters swimming-depth water"`.
- **No decision changes.** The refusal still happens exactly where it did.

## Evidence (harness; pwsh 7.4 + .NET 8 in the cloud container)
- `Test-WaterSafety`:
  - a wadeable step → no sample;
  - a 3 m shelf → the sample at x=3 is reported;
  - standing in swimming depth → the start itself is reported.
- `Test-MovementLogic`: the deep-water-ahead row now also asserts one `move_water_refusal` carrying a sample (the double's `ExplainRefusal`).
- `Test-Logic` 111/111 PASS, `Test-ProjectIntegrity` PASS (188 plugin sources; 112 no-Unity as net48/C# 7.3).

## Not tested / risks
- No native build (cloud). `ExplainRefusal` uses only API the file already uses (`GetSolidHeight`, `GetGroundHeight`, `m_waterLevel`). It runs only on a refusal, so it adds no per-tick cost.
- **Live repro for Opus-PC (step 2's data):** VikingAITest, stand at (-124.6, -252.6) on the lake's west shore, then `player_move_to -124.5 -256.5` a few times.
  - Read `move_water_refusal.sample`.
  - If `walkDepth > maxWadeDepth` while `terrainDepth` is wadeable, compare `solidHitY` with `terrainY`. A hit **below** the terrain means the ray origin was under the bank (CR hypothesis a).
  - If both depths are deep, the sample lies on the lake side (hypothesis b).

body:
## Summary

Adds the **Upgrade Bot**: `hath0r upgrade` installs a new CLI release, tests it, rolls back automatically if the tests fail, and announces what happened. On failure it can open (or comment on) a GitHub issue describing what to fix.

- **Bots** (`src/hath0r_cli/bots/upgrade_bot.py`, stdlib only): `UpgradeBot` (detect → check → preflight → snapshot → install → rollback), `UpgradeVerifierBot` (runs the installed CLI in a fresh subprocess and checks the version, that every registered command imports, doctor failures against the pre-upgrade baseline, factory validation, and optionally the unit tests), `UpgradeAnnouncerBot` (console, `~/.hath0r/upgrade/` report and history, voice queue, de-duplicated GitHub issue).
- **CLI**: `hath0r upgrade check | run | verify | rollback | status | schedule`, with JSON envelopes and exit codes 0, 1, and 6 (rollback failed).
- **Install methods**: source checkout (fast-forward only; clean tree on `development`/`master`), pip, pipx, and standalone binary (the downloaded binary is tested before it replaces the live one). SHA-256 verification is mandatory, using the GitHub asset digest or the `.sha256` sidecar.
- **Factory**: `cfg/factories/upgrade-factory.yaml` with workflows `upgrade-check`, nightly `upgrade-and-verify`, and `verify-install`, registered in `step_runner.py`.
- **Bootstrap**: `scripts/install_hath0r.py`, a checksum-verified first-time installer that hands off to `hath0r upgrade verify`.
- **Docs**: GUIDE-049 plus strategy, procedure, playbook, runbook, checklist, and bot spec (CR-CLI-FEATURE-STANDARD-001); CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]`; cross-link from GUIDE-047.

## Issue
Fixes #328

## PR class
- [x] **Feature/work** → base `development`
- [ ] **Release/promotion** → base `testing`|`staging`|`master` (use release template)

## Version Impact (SemVer)
- [ ] `major` — Breaking change
- [x] `minor` — New feature / capability
- [ ] `patch` — Bug fix / minor update
- [ ] `none` — Maintenance / doc chore

## Verification
- `tests/unit/test_upgrade_bot.py`: 34 passed. Full `tests/unit` + `tests/contract`: all pass except `test_dynamic_mcp_security.py::test_mcp_policy_blocking`, which also fails on `development` without this change.
- `ruff check` and `mypy` are clean on the new and changed files. Errors elsewhere in the repo (`cccd/`, `cli.py`) were there before this change.
- `hath0r factory validate`: `upgrade-factory` is valid. All three workflows run with `--dry-run`.
- **Live end-to-end on macOS** (throwaway venv, real GitHub and pip):
  - upgrade 0.8.0 → 0.9.0: `upgraded`, all required checks pass
  - verification failure forced by the test harness (everything else real): `rolled-back`, 0.8.0 restored and re-verified, issue body drafted

## Findings surfaced by the bot (not fixed here)
- The 0.9.0 wheel does not declare `jsonschema`, so `hath0r factory validate` crashes on a clean pip install. The bot reports this as an advisory check.
- Releases have no `darwin-x64` binary, so Intel Macs can't use the standalone binary.

## Checks
- [ ] `validate-promotion-path`
- [ ] CI
- [ ] CODEOWNERS when required
- [ ] Human gate if staging/master

## Quality gates
- [ ] CI / tests
- [ ] **SonarCloud Quality Gate** green (hard stop if failed; do not weaken thresholds)

author: cheongmyungj
body:
## 요약

VS Code 기본 테마를 그대로 쓴 듯하던 화면을 정리하고 라이트 테마를 더한다. 흐름과 동작은 그대로이며, 새 설정 `theme` 하나가 생긴다.

### 1. 시각 정리
- 바탕을 세 겹(가운데 터미널 < 옆 패널 < 카드)으로 나누고, 색을 `:root` 토큰으로 모아 하드코딩 색을 없앤다
- 상태 배지와 탭의 점은 `--tone` 하나로 색을 정한다(옅은 바탕에 같은 색 글자). **사람이 필요한 상태(승인 대기, 질문 등)의 진한 호박색(`#d7ba7d`) 배지는 그대로 두며 두 테마에서 같다.** Codex 스모크의 색 검사도 그대로 통과한다
- 사이드바: 선택한 Work에 왼쪽 강조 막대, [새 Work]는 점선 버튼, 맨 위에 relay 로고를 둔다
- 탭은 배경 대신 밑줄로 고른 것을 보인다. 작업 중인 점은 천천히 깜박인다
- 버튼에 hover와 focus 링을 넣고, [Work 포기]는 옅은 빨강으로 한다
- 대화상자: 둥근 모서리, 그림자, 흐린 뒤 배경. 업무 유형 고르기는 붙은 버튼 묶음으로 바꾼다
- 한글은 어절 단위로 줄을 바꾸고(`word-break: keep-all`), 넘치는 긴 낱말만 끊는다

### 2. 화면 구성
- 프로젝트가 없으면 가운데에 첫 사용 안내(프로젝트 등록 → 새 Work → 단계 승인)와 [프로젝트 추가]를 보인다
- 머리 띠에서 상태 배지를 앞으로 옮긴다. 승인 대기로 패널이 넓어지면 전에는 상태가 잘렸지만, 이제는 설명 글이 줄어든다
- **Work 완료 화면**: 판정표의 판정을 색으로 구분한다(통과는 초록, 실패·판정 불가는 빨강). 작업 브랜치와 worktree는 전달 버튼 위 카드로 보인다
- **PR 패널**: 요약을 카드로 감싸고, PR 상태(열림/닫힘/머지됨)를 색 배지로 보인다. 대응·머지·항목 묶음은 선으로 나눈다

### 3. 라이트 테마 (D335)
- 설정에 **테마**를 더한다: 시스템 설정 따름 / 다크 / 라이트, 기본 `system`
- main이 `nativeTheme.themeSource`로 정하고, CSS는 `prefers-color-scheme`만 본다. 라이트는 같은 토큰을 다시 정한다
- **터미널은 테마와 관계없이 어둡다.** claude와 codex가 어두운 바탕을 전제로 색을 쓰기 때문이다
- `docs/design.md`에 D335와 설정 표의 `theme` 행을 더했다

## 테스트

- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check` 통과
- `npm test`: 991 passed / 2 skipped. 테마 설정 단위 시험 2개(기본값, 바꾸기, 틀린 값)를 더했다
- `npm run test:smoke` (Linux, xvfb): `app.spec`, `codex.spec`, 새 `theme.spec` 모두 통과
  - `theme.spec`: 설정에서 다크 → 라이트로 고르면 바로 바뀐다. 터미널은 어둡게 남고, 다시 켜도 라이트다. Playwright는 페이지에서 라이트를 흉내 내므로 이 시험은 흉내를 끄고(`emulateMedia({ colorScheme: null })`) 앱이 정한 테마를 본다. 설치본(`RELAY_APP_EXE`)도 지원한다
- 화면 확인: 흐름 시험의 하네스(실제 `Relay` + 가짜 gh)로 Work 완료와 PR 진행(CI 실패, 리뷰, 받지 않은 코멘트) 상태의 스냅샷을 뽑았다. 이 스냅샷으로 빌드한 렌더러를 띄워 두 테마의 화면을 찍어 비교했다(커밋하지 않은 임시 도구)

## 남은 확인

- Windows 설치본에서의 눈 확인(특히 라이트 테마의 select 같은 기본 컨트롤)

author: leusd100
body:
## Що в цьому PR

Продовження блоку «Як ми дивимося на об'єкт» на головній, після #143.

### Оптимізація руху шва фото/схема
- **Права сторона тепер «вікно».** Обгортка зсувається трансформацією, її вміст — назад, тож схема стоїть на місці, а вікно її відкриває. Кліп-маски, які перемальовували всю схему (фото з фільтром і маскою, сотні SVG) на кожному кадрі, прибрано.
- **`--split` більше не успадковується.** Він живе лише на 4 елементах (вікно, його вміст, рейка шва, ручка) і пишеться напряму, без рендеру React.
- **React оновлюється не частіше ніж раз на 100 мс**, поки шов рухається, і одразу після відпускання.
- **Шов за курсором** доганяє курсор легкою JS-анімацією замість CSS-переходів, які перезапускались на кожен рух.

Заміри: 1440×900 @2x, 3 проходи по 120 рухів, CPU 4× сповільнений (як слабкий ноутбук).

| | було | стало |
|---|---|---|
| перерахунок стилів за серію | 3,1–6,0 с | 0,32–0,40 с |
| час головного потоку за серію | 6,1–9,7 с | 2,0–2,5 с |
| кадрів > 20 мс (шов за курсором) | 83–99 | 0 |
| найдовший кадр | 66–83 мс | 17 мс |

Без сповільнення стилі впали з 1,0–1,6 с до 0,2–0,25 с.

### Виправлення, знайдені перевіркою після #143
- **Ланцюжок навантаження в легенді компактніший** (2 рядки замість 3–4): аркуш знову влазить під шапку на 1280×720.
- **Цифра «Схил даху» на «Каркасі»** стоїть у небі двома рядками і не ховається через штамп на 900–1366 px. Мітка шва «Схема ›» тепер поступається цифрам і підписам, а не навпаки.
- **Якщо цифру сховано, ховаються й її мітки та виносна лінія.**
- **Сховані підписи перераховуються** і при зміні лише висоти вікна.
- **Підписи «Прогони й в'язі» та «Стіни — газобетон»** — на стіні праворуч, «Центральний ряд колон» — нижче в отворі воріт. На планшеті вони не злипаються.
- **Розмірна лінія ширини в «Контурі»** піднята, щоб не обрізалась на ноутбуках.
- **Телефон:**
  - ручка на 320–389 px менша й не накриває основу та низ воріт;
  - кадр показує рядки 92–738;
  - верхівка «гребінки» снігу не обрізається.
- **Стартова висота аркуша без JS** виміряна по ширинах (169/170/230/260 px), тож картинка не стрибає при завантаженні.

## Перевірки
- `home-proof-contour.spec.ts` + `pr-critical.spec.ts`: 163 пройшли, 15 пропущено, 0 впало. Тести блока переписано під нову будову шва: шов читається з чотирьох елементів, права сторона перевіряється як вікно, плавне ведення курсором перевіряється покадрово, а оновлення раз на 100 мс — під час неперервного руху.
- `vitest run`: 1123 пройшли.
- `tsc`, `eslint` чисті.

Перевірка тестами знайшла й закрила ще 4 речі:
1. Решта аркуша оновлювалась лише після паузи. Тепер це throttle раз на 100 мс замість debounce.
2. Після наведення повзунок показував проміжне значення.
3. Клавіші не рухали шов, поки миша лежала на кадрі.
4. На ≤1024 px підписи заходили на одвірок. Тепер на вузькому кадрі вони у два рядки, а на ≤900 px мають свої місця.

Деплою немає. Мердж — на рішення Дмитра.

author: lebgaaabderrahmane
body:
Mobile auth polish carried across the app, plus the dev-server login probe that logged members out everywhere.

## Why

Four things came out of testing on a phone and a laptop:

- the LAN session fix only worked while the dev server's module graph stayed intact — any hot reload silently broke login;
- markdown typed into a description reached readers as literal syntax (`# عنوان`);
- the landing's **لبنة المجتمع** button pointed at `#`;
- the member portal scrolled as a page on mobile instead of inside its own panel;
- card buttons had no press feedback, and the landing activity cards went nowhere.

## What changed

**`fix(auth)` — the login probe no longer depends on module state.** `probePassword` marks its request and `beforeLogin` aborts on that mark; the mark lived in a module-level `WeakSet`. Next.js evaluates the server action's graph and Payload's config graph independently, so after an HMR edit of `shared/lib/account-security.ts` the module existed twice, the mark never crossed, `payload.login` issued a real session — and the probe's safety net revoked **every** session for the account. Symptom: the phone got "فشل تسجيل الدخول" *and* the PC session died. The capability now rides on the request object under `Symbol.for`, and the abort is recognised by a symbol on the error instead of `instanceof`, so duplicate module copies agree.

**`fix(auth)` — LAN sessions survive dev reloads.** `EXTRA_CSRF_ORIGINS` for the local LAN origin, plus a development-only synthesis of the `Sec-Fetch-Site` proof Chromium withholds on `http://<ipv4>:3000`. Cross-site requests and production are untouched; that rule now lives in `shared/lib/browser-origin-proof.ts` so it is testable without booting Payload.

**`feat(auth)` — mobile polish.** Bigger logo and text floor on login/register, Material press ripple through the shared `Button`, loading states on every form button, eager `login.jpg`.

**`fix(ui)` — portal scroll containment.** An `sr-only` label in the dashboard's mobile activity list was absolutely positioned with no positioned ancestor, so its containing block was the viewport: it escaped the page's scroll container and stretched the document (1062px on an 844px screen). The scroll container is now the containing block. Verified across all ten portal pages at 360/390/768/1280 — the document never scrolls, the panel does.

**`fix(ui)` — markdown descriptions.** `withMarkdownSyntax` upgrades admin-typed lines (`# عنوان`, `- نقطة`, `1.`, `>`, `---`, `**bold**`, `*italic*`, `` `code` ``) into lexical headings, lists, quotes, rules and formatted runs before Payload's renderer draws them, wired into the book, activity and article detail views. Blocks that are already lexical nodes — seeded and CMS-authored rich text — pass through untouched, so RTL Arabic and existing formatting are unaffected.

**`fix(ui)` — card press feedback.** Book and article card CTAs are `pointer-events-none` (the whole card is the link), so the press never reached them; a press landing on the CTA is now rerouted into the button.

**`fix(ui)` — landing.** The **لبنة المجتمع** CTA goes to `/about-us` (it was `#`), and `SectionBlock` requires `ctaHref` so a section cannot ship a dead button. The activity bento is one link to `/activities`: all four cards and the featured card's two action labels navigate there, and the labels stay decorative (`<span>`, not `<button>` — interactive content is invalid inside an `<a>`) while inheriting the navigation and rippling on tap.

**`fix(ui)`** — the validation `FormMessage` body was never mounted.

## Verification

`format:check`, `lint` (0 errors, 5 pre-existing warnings), `typecheck`, `test` (140 files / 1302 tests) and `test:coverage` (100% on `shared/lib/**`, `features/*/server/**`, `collections/**`) all green on this branch, rebased onto `dev` after #220.

Behaviour was verified headlessly, not by inspection: ripple fires on card CTAs in visitor and member pages; the two-device login scenario now succeeds and leaves the existing session alone, with the WeakSet version failing it on purpose as a control; `/articles/11` and `/activities/15` render a real `<h1>` with no literal `#`; every landing activity card and action label lands on `/activities`.

## Notes for review

- the featured card's **سجل الآن** label now leads to `/activities` — copy may deserve rewording;
- markdown is not rendered in the short text fields (`shortDescription`, article `description`); none of them contain markdown today;
- visual baselines for the auth pages will drift (#193); CI skips the visual project (`E2E_SKIP_VISUAL=1`).

author: objectstack-fleet[bot]
body:
Fixes #21834
Clause-②: no

## What changed

`POST /api/v1/marketplace/install-local/:manifestId/reseed-sample-data` and `POST …/:manifestId/purge-sample-data` now run ADR-0087 D1's handshake (`checkProtocolCompat`) on the ledger entry right after reading it. An entry whose declared range excludes this runtime gets the install route's answer for the same manifest: `422 OS_PROTOCOL_INCOMPATIBLE`, the error's own message, and the diagnostic's five fields in `error.details`. The answer is shaped by the producer's `protocolIncompatibleAnswer`, so there is no second copy of the shaping. Nothing happens before that answer: no translation load, no seed-dataset merge, no seed-row read or delete, and no ledger write.

- `packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts`: one private helper, `refuseProtocolIncompatibleEntry`, called by both doors right after `ledger.read`. Admission, the 404 and the unreadable-ledger answer still come first, because there is no manifest to judge before them. Only a positive incompatibility is refused. An absent or unreadable range is admitted as before, with no new warning.
- No change to DELETE, the install route, the rehydrate or the listing. No `packages/spec` path. No new error code.
- Changeset: `@objectstack/cloud-connection` `patch`, carrying the same `Clause-②: no` line.
- `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`: one generated row recording the new suite's `delete` double, which routes through `assertEngineDeleteDispatch`. The gate prescribes this (`--write`). It is not part of the claimed surface.

## Mechanism assumptions, measured on `origin/main` `5b2d189e`

- **H1, confirmed.** Neither `handleReseed` nor `handlePurge` called a handshake. The reseed reached `applySideEffects`, whose step 1 loads translations and step 2 merges seed datasets (and registers the replayer) before the seed run.
- **H2, confirmed.** The install route refuses through `assertProtocolCompat` + `protocolIncompatibleAnswer`. `protocolIncompatibleAnswer` takes a `ProtocolIncompatibleError`, and `checkProtocolCompat` returns the diagnostic. The helper builds the producer's own error from that diagnostic (`new ProtocolIncompatibleError(compat.diagnostic)`, the same construction `assertProtocolCompat` throws) and answers through the shared helper. Per the ruling, the check is `checkProtocolCompat`, not `assertProtocolCompat`, so the doors add no grandfathering warning on loadable entries.
- **H3, measured: the doors and the rehydrate's record can disagree.** Suppose a protocol-incompatible entry is written to the ledger after this boot's rehydrate, for example by another runtime sharing the ledger. The GET listing then serves it as loaded: `withSampleData: false`, no `notLoaded` marker, and its per-request seed-row `warn`. Both doors answer it `422`, because they judge the entry themselves, as the ruling directs. This was measured with a throwaway probe in the unit harness, which was not committed. The doors' half is pinned (case 5 below). The listing's half is unchanged and noted under Acceptance notes.
- **H4, measured.** In the reseed, both the organization wall's refusal (`mode: 'refused'`, 403) and the `skipped` answer (`400 RESEED_SKIPPED`) are decided inside `applySideEffects`, after steps 1 and 2. So the handshake sits before that call. In the purge, the wall check precedes the engine deletes and the ledger write, and the handshake sits before both. Pinned: on a walled boot with no active organization, a refused entry gets `422`, not `403`, and nothing moves (case 4).

## Tests (`92261ad5`)

- New unit suite `packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-sample-data-not-loaded.test.ts`: 10 passed. It uses the real plugin `start()` + `kernel:ready` over a pre-written ledger and the real `SeedLoaderService`, over an in-memory engine that answers only for registered objects. Its probes are the `i18n` service's `loadTranslations` call count, the length of the shared `seed-datasets` list, the engine's writes, and the ledger directory's bytes. The cases:
  1. Precondition: the rehydrate refused the old entry and loaded the current one.
  2. Reseed on the refused entry: `422`, byte-identical to the install route's answer for the same manifest. Every probe unchanged.
  3. Purge on the refused entry: the same `422`, no delete, `withSampleData` still `true`.
  4. Walled, with no active organization: `422` ahead of the wall's `403`, nothing moves. Control: the loadable entry meets the `403`.
  5. An entry written after this boot's rehydrate is refused by both doors.
  6. DELETE still works after both refusals.

body:
Server half of backlog §87 #7 (SG-7): hold and recall a counter bill, and a cashier's shift counted at close. The counter screen's Hold, Recall and Shift panel follow in a desktop PR; the API client calls are in this one.

## What changed

**Hold and recall**
- `sales_invoices.is_held`, `held_at`, `held_note`. `POST /api/v1/sales-invoices/{id}/hold` `{note?}` and `POST /api/v1/sales-invoices/{id}/recall`, both audited (plus a timeline event), both under the scope that edits a draft (the author, or `SALES_UPDATE`).
- A flag, never a status. Only a draft can be held. `stage_approval` refuses a held bill ("Recall it first"), so the single approval and bulk approve both refuse it. A held draft can still be edited; cancelling one clears the flag.
- `GET /api/v1/sales-invoices?is_held=true|false`; the response carries `is_held`, `held_at`, `held_note`, `counter_shift_id` (columns of the row, no extra statement).

**Shifts** (`app/counter_shifts`, `/api/v1/counter-shifts`)
- `counter_shifts`: branch, cashier, cash account, `SHIFT-000001` number, float, and at close the counted cash, the expected-cash snapshot, the difference and its journal. One open shift per cashier per firm by partial unique index `UQ_counter_shifts_open_cashier` (PostgreSQL and SQLite), with a service check for the 409 message.
- `sales_invoices.counter_shift_id`: a bill with `received_now_amount > 0` is stamped with its approver's open shift inside `stage_approval`. Nobody is refused for having no shift.
- Expected cash is derived on every read: float + CASH tenders of the shift's approved/closed bills whose receipts are still posted. Four statements however many bills; a page of shifts costs what one does.
- Routes: `POST /open`, `GET /current`, `GET ""`, `GET /{id}`, `POST /{id}/close`, `GET /{id}/report` (PDF).
- Close posts one journal for a non-zero difference through `DocumentPostingService.post_cash_short_and_over`: short Dr *Cash short and over* / Cr the shift's cash account, over the mirror; reference = the shift number; `source_module = counter_shift`. Exact posts nothing. Still-held bills are reported as `summary.held_bills`, not blocked.
- New control purpose `CASH_SHORT_AND_OVER` (*6960 Cash Short and Over*, indirect expense), seeded with the chart and backfilled by the migration.

**Migration** `20261005_0324` (`down_revision = "20261005_0323"`), firm-owned and idempotent; CHECK constraints named with `op.f`.

## Decisions
- **Permissions:** open / current / close use `SALES_INVOICE_CREATE`, not `SALES_CREATE` -- that is the code a bill is actually raised under (D-ROLE-2). Closing somebody else's till needs `SALES_APPROVE`. List, one shift and the report open to `SALES_VIEW`, `REPORT_VIEW` or `SALES_INVOICE_CREATE` (so a cashier can print their own). No new code.
- **Numbering** is counted from the firm's shifts, not the document framework: a shift has no lifecycle configuration.
- **A reversed receipt drops out of expected cash**, not only a cancelled bill: cancelling requires the receipts reversed first, and the money is handed back at the reversal.
- **No counter refund tied to a bill exists** in the codebase, so nothing is subtracted.
- **The shift's cash account** defaults to the firm's `CASH` control account; another active ASSET account may be named, but receipts still book cash to the control account -- per-till receipt routing is not built and the docs say so.
- **Draft stock:** a draft counter bill's order is approved at save, which reserves stock; holding changes nothing about that. Documented, not changed.
- `app/counter_shifts` has `api`, `models`, `schemas`, `services` and no empty `repositories` package, as `app/collections` does.
- `CASH_SHORT_AND_OVER` may be mapped to an INCOME or EXPENSE account (as rounding and exchange difference are); the seeded account is EXPENSE.

## Tests and tools
- `pytest` by name, 22 files: `test_counter_hold_and_shifts.py` (new, 22 tests), `test_counter_tenders.py`, `test_walk_in_cash_sale.py`, `test_sales_chain_synthesis.py`, `test_sales_invoice_module.py`, `test_invoice_charges.py`, `test_control_accounts.py`, `test_firm_readiness.py`, `test_finance_module.py`, `test_schema_registry.py`, `test_route_declaration_order.py`, `test_routes_have_a_caller.py`, `test_identity_hardening.py`, `test_pagination_conventions.py`, `test_list_pages_are_batched.py`, `test_time_conventions.py`, `test_claude_md_names_real_things.py`, `test_history_reset_tables.py`, `test_desktop_preference_payloads_are_accepted.py`, `test_every_role_can_open_something.py`, `test_platform_only_routes.py`, `test_migration_chain.py` -- **361 passed, 1 failed**.
- The one failure is `test_migration_chain.py::test_every_parent_revision_exists_and_there_is_one_head` with `KeyError: '20261005_0323'`: this migration's parent is being written in parallel and is not on `main` yet. It passes once 0323 lands; do not merge before it.
- `ruff check .` clean, `black --check .` clean (1,628 files), `mypy app` clean (910 files).
- `flutter analyze lib/core/api/api_client.dart`: no issues.
- No existing test expectation was changed.

## Not tested
- **The migration has not been run** on any database: `alembic` cannot walk the chain until 0323 exists. Its SQL is the shape of `20261005_0319` and `20261005_0322`.
- `tests/integration/test_multi_schema_tenancy.py` (5 tests, local PostgreSQL): 4 pass, `test_live_firm_schemas_match_the_orm` fails naming exactly the four new `sales_invoices` columns in the unmigrated local stores -- expected until `migrate_all_stores` runs. No other integration file was run.
- The row lock between stamping a bill and closing a shift is not exercised (SQLite ignores `FOR UPDATE`).
- Nothing was driven against a running backend, and there is no screen yet.
- The full unit suite and the desktop suite were not run.

author: domer2103-bit
body:
## Problem
Reported while testing the wizard with 3 photos of a living room:
1. After choosing a style the other style options stayed on screen, and there was no way to design the remaining photos in the same style.
2. Generated designs did not keep the room: shapes of bay windows, the chimney breast, shelving and the camera angle changed.

## Changes
- **Choose a style.** Once a style is chosen the page shows only that design ("Your chosen design — *Style*", ★ Chosen style). The other options are hidden, not deleted, so history and the per-project cap are unchanged. "Choose a different style" (`?styles=all`) restores them. Per-photo "Generate design concepts" buttons disappear once a style is chosen.
- **Design my other photos in this style.** New `generateRemainingPhotos` designs each remaining photo from its own photo, with the chosen design passed as a *style-only* reference (nano-banana-pro `image_input`). Failed attempts are retried first. Providers that take a single image (flux-kontext) fall back to the text style direction.
- **Keep the room the same.** Every prompt now names the fixed features (room shape, camera, windows, doors, chimney breast, alcoves, stairs, boundary walls, roofline) and only lets an explicit request change them. The output now keeps the source photo's aspect ratio (nearest supported ratio via `image-size`); before, nano-banana-pro defaulted to a square, which re-framed wide room photos. If the provider rejects the request with the ratio, it is retried once without it.
- Private pipeline: contractors see only the chosen style's renders.
- New dependency: `image-size`.

## Verified
- `tsc`, eslint (0 errors) and 83 unit tests pass; the same 2 `fees.test.ts` tests that fail on `main` still fail. 6 new integration tests for `generateRemainingPhotos` pass against Postgres (chosen-style gate, reference passing, idempotence, retry after failure, text fallback, cap).
- **Real model runs on the three living-room photos** (nano-banana-pro, 4:3 accepted): the style options keep the bay window, chimney breast and alcoves in place, and the second and third photos come back with their own TV wall, window, sofas and shelves in the same positions, in the chosen palette. A first attempt with looser reference wording copied the reference's dining table and fireplace into the wrong room, hence the stricter "style reference only" prompt.
- Browser check on a scratch database: the choose-a-style screen, the chosen-style screen with the "Design my other 2 photos" button, and "Choose a different style" all render correctly.

## Not verified / worth knowing
- The "Design my other photos" button itself was exercised by the integration tests and by direct model runs, not clicked end to end on the live site.
- Not tested with flux-kontext models. They are more literal about the source (see §17) and are worth an A/B for the first batch.
- A deploy needs no migration.
- Separate issue: the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the local `.env` is rejected by Anthropic ("API key is invalid").

body:
## What changes for the user? | 使用者会感知到什么

`npm run map:serve` 现在默认**只监听本机**，写接口需要本次启动生成的一次性 token（页面自带，无感）。想用手机或局域网访问仍然可以：`--host 0.0.0.0`，但启动时会打印中英双语警告说明暴露范围。

`npm run map:serve` now binds **127.0.0.1** by default and its write endpoints need a per-run token that the served page carries automatically. LAN/phone access still works via `--host 0.0.0.0`, which prints a loud bilingual warning about what it exposes.

Nothing changes for the static page (`npm run map`) or for the TUI dashboard, which only reads `GET /api/data`.

## Type | 类型

- [x] `fix` (security / privacy)

## Why | 为什么要改

ClawHub 的安全审核给出 `suspicious`，原文：*"its map server can expose and overwrite private buying-profile data without authentication"*。核实属实，三个洞叠加：

1. `server.listen(servePort)` 没指定 host → 绑定所有网卡；
2. `POST /api/profile` 与 `POST /api/geo-cache` 无鉴权即可写 `config/profile.yml`；
3. `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` → 任意网站的脚本都能跨域发起上述写操作。

1+3 意味着**打开任意网页**都可能改写你的购房画像，与「数据不出仓库」的口径直接冲突。

## What changed | 具体改动

- 默认 `127.0.0.1`；新增 `--host <addr>`，非回环地址启动时打印警告。
- 写接口校验 `X-House-Ops-Token`（每次启动随机生成，注入页面）。GET 不受影响，dashboard 照常工作。
- CORS 收成同源：页面本服务提供，`*` 从来不需要。

## Checklist | 检查清单

- [x] `npm run selftest` passes / 通过
- [x] `npm run doctor` shows no blocking ⛔ / 无阻塞项
- [x] Real server tested end-to-end on a throwaway copy: page loads, POST without token → 401, cross-origin preflight → 403, LAN address unreachable, POST with token accepted
- [x] Verified the new assertions FAIL when the bind is reverted (not a no-op test) / 已实测断言在回退时会失败
- [x] No user-layer data committed / 未提交用户层数据

## Notes for reviewers | 给评审者的备注

The new selftest section spawns the real server on port 38765 and tears it down. It only ever sends a **token-less** POST (expecting 401), so it never touches `config/profile.yml`. The port is read from the startup log because the server auto-increments when the port is busy.

If the LAN check has no non-internal IPv4 to test against it is skipped rather than failed — that is the only soft spot.

body:
## Summary

`PostgresEventStorageAdapter` now names the `StoredEvent` columns in every query whose rows reach `class_row(StoredEvent)`, instead of using `*`. An `events` table with a column the installed `StoredEvent` does not know no longer breaks reads or writes.

Closes #130.

## Motivation

psycopg's `class_row` calls `StoredEvent(**row)`, so any extra column becomes an unexpected keyword argument:

```
TypeError: StoredEvent.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'metadata'
```

This turns additive schema changes into read-time and write-time breaks. It forced a read shim onto both sides of a downstream 0.1.11 → 0.1.12a3 upgrade.

The issue names the `SELECT *` reads. Two more wildcards fed `class_row` and are fixed here too: `RETURNING *` (every save) and `SELECT DISTINCT ON (...) *` (save to a category).

## Changes

### Key Changes

| Path | Query builder | Before |
| --- | --- | --- |
| every `save` | `insert_batch_query` | `RETURNING *` |
| `latest`, `save` to an existing stream | `read_last_query` | `SELECT *` |
| `scan` | `scan_query` | `Query().select_all()` |
| `save` to a category with existing streams | `read_last_category_batch_query` | `SELECT DISTINCT ON (category, stream ) *` |

- The column list comes from one place: `EVENT_COLUMNS`, derived from `dataclasses.fields(StoredEvent)`, and its SQL form `EVENT_COLUMNS_SQL`. `class_row` already relies on field names matching column names, so this adds no new coupling.
- New changelog fragment for this fix and its limits.
- Corrected the existing `metadata` changelog fragment (see below).

### Implementation Details

- `scan_query` uses `Query().select(*EVENT_COLUMNS)`, so the constraint appliers (which only add `WHERE`/`ORDER BY`) are unaffected.
- `Star`, `select_all()` and the generic query converters are unchanged. Their other users never build `StoredEvent`.
- The projection, subscriber and subscription stores already use `dict_row` and pick columns by name, so they are unchanged.
- Deliberately not done: a row factory that ignores unknown columns. It would silently drop data and hide column typos.

### Changelog correction for `metadata`

The `metadata` fragment said the previous version "ignores the extra column", so an application-only rollback could leave it in place. That is not true: 0.1.11 reads with `SELECT *` and `RETURNING *` and fails as soon as the column exists. The fragment now:

- splits the migration into two steps, keeping `DEFAULT 'null'::jsonb` until every writer supplies `metadata`;
- states that old and new versions cannot run side by side against the migrated table, and that this fix cannot change that retroactively;
- keeps the data-loss warning for `DROP COLUMN`.

## Breaking Changes

None. No API or schema change. Queries now fetch only known columns, so an extra column is no longer read.

### What this does and does not guarantee

- From this release on, the *running* version tolerates an extra column. That makes additive migrations safe during a rolling deploy, provided a new `NOT NULL` column keeps a default while old and new versions overlap, and the migration runs before the new version starts.
- It does **not** make the 0.1.11 → 0.1.12 `metadata` upgrade rolling-safe. Pods still on 0.1.11 break once `metadata` exists. A 0.1.11.x backport of this fix, deployed first, would make that upgrade safe.
- Non-additive changes (renames, drops, type changes) are still out of scope.

## How to Verify

- `mise run --force`: 1747 unit, 143 integration, 3 component tests pass; lint, format and types clean.
- `TestPostgresStorageAdapterUnknownColumns` adds `unknown_column TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unknown'` to a real table and covers every `class_row` path: save to a new stream, save to an existing stream, `latest` (log, category, stream), `scan` (log, category, stream), and save to a category with existing streams. Each test was seen failing with the `TypeError` before its query change.
- `test_batch_insert_query_builds_correct_sql` now pins the explicit `RETURNING` list.

The plan and research for this change are in `meta/plans/` and `meta/research/`.

body:
This PR introduces three research-grade quantitative models that were validated on the reproducible lock-step simulator before adoption. Each model improved results over the previous tuned baseline.

## Summary

Added three theoretically-grounded models to replace hand-tuned heuristics:
1. **Almgren-Chriss optimal execution** (liability) - derives unwinding schedule from market volatility and impact
2. **Bertram optimal mean-reversion thresholds** (ETF) - fits OU process to premium and trades at statistically optimal bands
3. **Bayesian learning of news impact** (commodity) - online conjugate update of price impact from actual market reactions

All three adapt to market conditions rather than using fixed parameters, and are validated with comprehensive test coverage.

## Key Changes

### Core Algorithm (`core/algo.py`)
- Added `ac_kappa()`: computes Almgren-Chriss urgency parameter from volatility, impact, and risk aversion
- Added `book_eta()`: extracts temporary impact coefficient from visible order book depth

author: berndhueckstaedt
body:
## What the member object handed out

The GraphQL type `User` is shared by wallet and admin, and it is built from a whole `users` row wherever a member appears. Its field `userLocation` — the place a member has pinned for the member search (`users.location`) — had no guard, so the type answered it to whoever asked:

- **to every signed-in member**, through `user(identifier)`, which finds a member by alias, gradido ID or confirmed e-mail address;
- **without a login**, through `queryTransactionLink(code)` (an inalienable right), for the member who made a link (`senderUser`) and, once the link is taken, for the member who took it (`redeemedBy`).

It is the pinned point as stored, whichever of exact and approximate the member chose for the member search (`gmsPublishLocation`). Affected is who has saved a position. Neither wallet nor admin asks for the field about anybody but the member themselves.

The line has been in `model/User.ts` since 21.02.2025 (`7a4fadea1`); every release tag from `2.6.1` on carries it, `v3.0.0` included.

## What changes

**Commit 1 — the position.** A field resolver answers `userLocation` to its owner and `null` to everybody else, the moderation included: the form `aboutMe`, `avatar`, `avatarVisibleToMembers` and `transfersInChat` already have. `null` rather than an error, so a query that merely asked for too much does not lose the whole member.

Only the field is closed. How the object is built does not change, `user` and `queryTransactionLink` are untouched, and the printed schema is the same line for line before and after this commit. The member's own views answer as before: `login`, `verifyLogin`, and the `userLocation` query the map and the settings read (another type, `UserLocationResult`, not part of the guard).

Two details of the guard:

- The resolver method is called `ownUserLocation` and carries `name: 'userLocation'`, because `UserResolver` already has a method `userLocation` — that query.
- It asks for a caller before it compares: `!context.user || context.user.id !== user.id`. The two ids compared alone read an object without an id as the own view of a caller without a login (undefined on both sides). No such object carries a position today; a test asks the guard directly so that it does not rest on that.

**Commit 2 — seven settings of a member's own account**, under the same rule: `hideAmountGDD`, `hideAmountGDT`, `gmsAllowed`, `humhubAllowed`, `gmsPublishLocation`, `gmsPublishName`, `humhubPublishName`. Measured before building who asks for them: the wallet reads five of them off `login` and `verifyLogin`, the e2e login query the two about the balances, `gmsPublishName` and `humhubPublishName` no client at all; the admin interface asks for none. What the server itself decides by them (GMS, HumHub) it reads off the user row.

For this the four booleans become nullable in the schema, as the two guarded switches are — the only change in the printed schema:

```diff
-  hideAmountGDD: Boolean!
-  hideAmountGDT: Boolean!
-  humhubAllowed: Boolean!
-  gmsAllowed: Boolean!
+  hideAmountGDD: Boolean
+  hideAmountGDT: Boolean
+  humhubAllowed: Boolean
+  gmsAllowed: Boolean
```

A member reading their own settings is answered as before.

## Evidence

The tests were written first and run **on unchanged master** (`1a8336237`, tests only, no guard), with the database, in the fork: https://github.com/Gradido-Akademie/gradido/actions/runs/37283519056

```
userLocation visibility
  ✓ shows a member their own position
  ✓ hands a member their own position with the login itself
  ✓ answers the query the map and the settings read as before
  ✕ hides the position from another logged-in member
  ✕ hides the position from the moderation as well
  ✕ hides the position of the member who made a link from whoever holds its code
  ✕ hides the position of the member who took the link as well

● hides the position from another logged-in member
    expect(received).toBeNull()
    Received: {"latitude": 49.679437, "longitude": 9.573224}
● hides the position of the member who took the link as well
    expect(received).toBeNull()
    Received: {"latitude": 52.520008, "longitude": 13.404954}
```

The fourteen cases for the seven settings (another member, and a link without a login) were red in the same run, each with the stored value as `Received`; the fourteen own-view cases were green. The cases added since (the moderation for the seven settings, the guard asked directly) were not part of that run.

With the two commits, on master `6bb22078d`: https://github.com/Gradido-Akademie/gradido/actions/runs/37288561723 — 138 suites, 2451 tests passed, 5 skipped, none failed; all 50 new cases green, the end-to-end run of the same commit as well.

Whether the field was ever asked for about another member is not known, and not examined here.

## Still answered to others, without a guard

Not part of this PR — a list for a decision of its own: `createdAt`, `emailChecked`, `language`, `role`, `creationAllowed`, `deletedAt`, `id`, `publisherId`; and `userIdentifier`, which is computed from `humhubPublishName` and so still tells whether that setting stands at its default.

## Not part of this

- No rebuild of the member object, no slimmer type for the link query, no change to `queryTransactionLink` or `user`.
- No change to the member search, the GMS or the settings.
- No wallet or admin change, no table, no column, no migration, no new text.

author: nikolainyegaard
body:
Both version checks run once, half a second to a second after the GUI starts, with a one second request timeout. With autostart on login the network is often not up yet, so the lookup fails on DNS or connect and the GUI shows "Unable to check for latest OneDrive client version!" with the warning icon for the rest of the session. The GUI's own version check fails silently in the same situation, so a new release goes unnoticed.

This makes both checks retry every 60 seconds, up to 10 attempts, by re-arming their existing single-shot timers. The client warning is only shown once the last attempt has failed. The request timeout goes from 1 to 3 seconds, which copes better with a VPN or Wi-Fi that is still coming up.

Tested on Fedora 45 KDE by starting the GUI with networking removed and watching both checks retry at 60 second intervals, and by a normal start where both checks succeed on the first attempt.

body:
## Summary Adds S3 object storage to the Mentorship backend for **program logos**, **profile logos** and **task submission files**, implementing the contract in #161: - `docs/rewrite/02-target-architecture.md` §Object storage - `docs/rewrite/06-route-matrix.md` §File routes The core rule is that **the database row is the source of truth and the bucket follows it**: - Objects are never overwritten. Every upload mints a fresh key. - Nothing is deleted while any row still references the object. - Every delete goes through a durable queue, so a crash at any point leaves at most an orphaned object that is reclaimed later. It never leaves a row pointing at a missing file. ## Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR client([Browser / BFF]) subgraph gw[Gateway] traefik[Traefik
upload routes: Buffering + 120s] heimdall[Heimdall
OpenFGA relation per route] end subgraph api[mentorship-api] fh[FileHandler
multipart / raw body,
Range, nosniff] fs[FileService
type sniffing, size caps,
ownership, replace protocol] repo[(FileRepository
ObjectDeletionRepository)] relay[[Object deletion relay
every 10s]] end pg[(Postgres
file columns +
object_deletions)] logos[(S3 logos bucket
public, CDN-fronted)] att[(S3 attachments bucket
private)] cdn[CDN] client --> traefik --> heimdall --> fh --> fs fs --> repo --> pg fs -- PutObject / GetObject --> logos fs -- PutObject / GetObject --> att relay -- claim / IsReferenced --> pg relay -- DeleteObject --> logos relay -- DeleteObject --> att client -. logo image .-> cdn -.-> logos ``` | Layer | What changed | |---|---| | `domain` | `ObjectStore` interface, `ObjectBucket`, `ObjectDeletion` queue types, `FileRepository`. New sentinels `ErrFileNotFound`, `ErrPayloadTooLarge`, `ErrUnsupportedMedia`, `ErrRangeNotSatisfiable`. | | `infrastructure/objectstore` | `aws-sdk-go-v2` S3 client (default credential chain, optional custom endpoint for local S3), and the deletion `Relay`. | | `infrastructure/db` | `FileRepository` (conditional replace and clear), `ObjectDeletionRepository` (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` claim with retry and dead-letter). Parent-delete paths now queue the files they drop. | | `service` | `FileService`: byte-level type detection, size caps, ownership and state checks, and the replace protocol. Generic services reject file columns. | | `handler` | `FileHandler`: upload/download/delete routes. `respond.go` maps the new errors to 404/413/415/416. | | `cmd/mentorship-api` | Storage config, bucket checks at startup, relay goroutine, per-route timeouts. | | `charts` | Heimdall rules, the upload `HTTPRoute` rule with Traefik `Buffering`, storage values, and render-time guards. | | `db/migrations` | `005_object_deletions.up.sql` | ## File classes | | Logos (program and profile) | Task submissions | |---|---|---| | Bucket | `LOGOS_S3_BUCKET`, **public**, behind a CDN | `ATTACHMENTS_S3_BUCKET`, **private** | | Column stores | Full CDN URL `{LOGOS_CDN_URL_PREFIX}/{key}` | Object key | | Key | `{uuid}-logo.{png\|jpg}` | `{uuid}-{sanitized filename}` | | Allowed types (detected from bytes, not the filename or header) | PNG, JPEG (no SVG) | PDF, DOC, DOCX, plain text | | Max size | 2 MB | 20 MB | | `Cache-Control` | `public, max-age=86400` | `private, no-store` | | Served by | CDN; API download route as a fallback | API download route only | The object key never leaves the backend: - Task JSON replaces `file` with its download route (`/mentorship/v1/tasks/{id}/file-download`). - The search index carries `has_file: true|false` instead of the key. ## Routes | Method & path | Who | Relation (Heimdall) | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | `POST /programs/{id}/logo-upload` | Program Admin | `writer` | raw body | | `DELETE /programs/{id}/logo` | Program Admin | `writer` | | | `GET /programs/{id}/logo-download` | anyone who can see the program | same as `GET /programs/{id}` | CDN fallback | | `POST /me/profiles/by-id/{id}/logo-upload` | profile owner | `allow_all` + ownership check | also sets `users.avatar_url` | | `DELETE /me/profiles/by-id/{id}/logo` | profile owner | `allow_all` + ownership check | clears `avatar_url` if it holds this logo | | `GET /user-profiles/{id}/logo-download` | anyone | anonymous | only for publicly listed profiles | | `POST /tasks/{id}/file-upload` | task assignee | `assignee` | multipart part `file`; not after the task is complete | | `GET /tasks/{id}/file-download` | assignee or reviewer | `auditor` | streams with `Range` support; `Content-Disposition: attachment` | | `DELETE /tasks/{id}/file` | task assignee | `assignee` | only while `incomplete` / `in_progress` | Generic routes now reject the file fields with `400`, so files can only change through the routes above: - `logo_url` on program create, enrollment and update - `avatar_url` on `PATCH /me` - `logo_url` on profiles; `profile_links.resumeLink` is dropped rather than rejected - `file` on task update and submission ## Replace protocol Uploading over an existing file is a three-step protocol. A failure at any step leaves the row consistent, and any orphaned object is reclaimed by the queue. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber participant C as Client participant S as FileService participant DB as Postgres participant S3 as S3 participant R as Relay C->>S: POST …/logo-upload (bytes) S->>S: sniff type, check size, check ownership / state S->>DB: Schedule(new key, delay = 15 min grace) Note over DB: object_deletions: new key, pending S->>S3: PutObject(new key) S->>DB: BEGIN S->>DB: UPDATE row SET file = new
WHERE file IS NOT DISTINCT FROM previous alt row changed under us DB-->>S: 0 rows → ROLLBACK → 409 Note over R: after the grace period, the relay
reclaims the orphaned new object else row updated S->>DB: DELETE grace entry WHERE state = 'pending' alt relay already claimed it DB-->>S: 0 rows → ROLLBACK → 409 else cancelled S->>DB: queue previous locator for deletion S->>DB: COMMIT S-->>C: 201 {public_url, filename, content_type, size} end end ``` - The **15-minute grace period** is much longer than the 120s gateway upload timeout, so the relay can't reclaim an upload that is still in flight. - A crash between `PutObject` and `COMMIT` leaves an unreferenced object, which the grace entry cleans up. - Two concurrent uploads to the same row: one wins and the other gets `409`. The loser's object is reclaimed. ## Deletion queue and relay Every object delete, whether from a replace, a `DELETE` route, or a parent delete (program, task, application, reapply, user, profile), inserts a row into `object_deletions` **in the same transaction** as the row change. The relay drains the queue in the background: ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> pending: Schedule / queue
(same tx as the row change) pending --> [*]: grace entry cancelled
(upload committed) pending --> in_flight: Claim configured buckets only
(FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED,
next_attempt_at ≤ now) in_flight --> in_flight: reclaimed after 5 min
(relay pod died) in_flight --> [*]: still referenced → skip
foreign URL → skip
DeleteObject OK
(row deleted) in_flight --> pending: DeleteObject failed
(retry in 1 min) in_flight --> dead_letter: 10 failed attempts
(logged as error) dead_letter --> [*] ``` Before any delete, the relay re-checks `IsReferenced` across `programs.logo_url`, `user_profiles.logo_url`, `users.avatar_url`, `tasks.file` and `quarantined_tasks.file`, each with a partial index. A locator that some row still points at is never deleted. This covers: - avatar
