> **Retarget to `main` after PR #1272 merges.** This branch is based on `docs/human-review-verdicts` because the explorer reads the final reviewer worksheet.

## What

A public explorer at `/lab/` over the Harvey LAB litigation audit, with two first-class views and a tab bar to switch between them.

- **Hand-audited** (`/lab/`): counts, the rubric-verdict by environment-verdict table (cells link to items), a 25-row table, and a walk-through at `/lab/review/1..25/` with previous/next, a position indicator and a 25-square pager. Each item shows the reviewer's verdict, environment verdict, category and note first, then the rubric, AI findings and all four run grades with judge reasoning.
- **Full runs** (`/lab/runs/`): run totals, a 52-task directory, and a scanner over all 2,858 criteria with filters (hand-audited, defective per reviewer, AI-flagged, failed by any run, judges disagree), search and a task selector, with state in the URL.
- Task pages (`/lab/tasks/<task>/`): instructions, document links, both runs, every criterion as an expandable row; rubric text, findings and reasoning load lazily. Deliverable renderings are separate pages (noindex).

Design, data model, size budget, accessibility and link placement are in `docs/lab-explorer.md`.

## Decisions to check

- Vendored Harvey `task.json` (52 files, 1.5 MB, MIT license file alongside, pinned commit, refreshed by `site/scripts/fetch-lab-upstream.ts`). Source documents are linked to the pinned upstream, not copied.
- Not in the primary nav (a layout test counts its links) and not in agent-markdown negotiation. Linked from `/analysis/` (replacing the GitHub folder link), a `/paper/` button, and a sentence in `/approach/`. The `.tex` is untouched.
- Only the reviewer's verdicts are presented as human; everything else is labeled AI-generated and unverified. Copy makes no claim about the reviewer's process.
- The protocol's confidence bound is not shown on the page.

## Verification

Ran locally: `pnpm site:check` (biome, astro check, tsc, contract check, 73 unit tests), `pnpm test:browser` (new end-to-end explorer test plus existing nav and tooltip tests), `bash site/scripts/check-withdrawal-build.sh`, and the docs-index and publication-guardrail pytest files. Full site build about 3.5 s for 245 pages. Sizes (gzip): landing 10 KB, runs page 12 KB, largest task page 13 KB; scanner index 70 KB and largest per-task detail 48 KB, both fetched on demand.

**Este PR sustituye a #854 si se fusiona primero**, o se rebasa sobre él si #854 entra antes.

## Arreglos sobre #854 (HU-PRD-013, autoría de la gestión: Melipete12)

El CI de #854 estaba en rojo por tres guardianes de `CI - frontend app-web` (no uno) y por el laboratorio visual:

| Guardián | Causa | Arreglo |
|---|---|---|
| `acceso.test.js` (vista fuera de la matriz) + laboratorio visual (vista sin catalogar) | `banners.html` no estaba en `comun/matriz-acceso.js` | Entrada `banners` con nivel de administración (`ADMINISTRADOR`/`SUPER_ADMINISTRADOR`, el mismo que exige `SeguridadConfig`); la vista usa `exigirAcceso('banners')`. El laboratorio la cataloga solo (deriva de la matriz) |
| `sin-dialogos-nativos.test.js` | `window.confirm('¿Retirar este banner?')` | Diálogo del kit (`confirmar`), inyectable; un fallo al retirar se explica |
| `clases-del-kit.test.js` | `class="home__banners"` en `cuentas/index.html`, sin CSS | La zona pasa a ser un `div` sin clase (va en el commit del banner) |

Además:
- **Borde**: `location /api/v1/banners` → productos (`34.193.90.11:8103`, mismo patrón que `/api/v1/productos`). Sin ella la consulta pública caía en el 404 genérico y la home se quedaba sin banner en DEV. Reparto en `comprobar-rutas.sh` (5 rutas) y fila en el README del borde. Los bancos de rutas y E2E ya sustituyen ese destino.
- **Contrato** (`productos.yaml` 1.6.0, aún no publicada en develop): `Banner` era `allOf` sobre `SolicitudBanner`, que tiene `additionalProperties: false` → **ninguna respuesta real cumplía el esquema**. Se declara completo; `ContratoDeBannersTest` lo fija contra lo que serializa el servicio.
- Vista de gestión: fechas con el formateador común, errores sin jerga técnica; `cliente-banners.js` tolera cuerpos no JSON y expone `listarVigentes()`.
- La vista se encuentra desde la consola en **Productos → Banners** (enlace de #854 en la cabecera de Productos). No se añadió entrada propia a `SECCIONES_CONSOLA` para no chocar con el PR de la consola, que toca la misma lista.

## Banner rotativo (RF-NOT-002, Grupo 6)

`plataforma/notificaciones/banner-rotativo.js|css` + pruebas, montado en la home en lugar de la carga del primer banner:

- CA-01 rota los vigentes y retira en el cliente el que vence con la página abierta; CA-02 uno solo se ve fijo, sin controles; CA-03 sin vigentes o con productos caído la zona queda oculta (`console.warn`, la home sigue entera); CA-04 cada mensaje dice «Publicado el …» y «Vigente hasta el …» (`fechaHora`, zona del navegador, `<time datetime>`).
- Carrusel WAI (mismo patrón que el banner de misiones): pausar/reanudar, anterior, siguiente, puntos; se detiene con foco y ratón; con `prefers-reduced-motion` no arranca; `aria-live` solo cuando lo mueve la persona.
- Intervalo de 8 s: **constante de interfaz** documentada (la misma de `banner-misiones.js`); ni admin-parametros ni las decisiones del PO fijan uno.

## Cómo se probó

- Jest completo: 2959 en verde; fallan solo las 3 suites que necesitan git en el sandbox (`marcado-sin-plantillas`, `tokens-sin-sombra`, `publicar-subasta`, 10 pruebas), cuyas reglas se comprobaron a mano sobre los archivos nuevos. ESLint y Prettier (`src/`) limpios.
- Nuevas: `banner-rotativo.test.js` (23), `banners.test.js` (5), +3 en `home.test.js`, +2 en `cliente-banners.test.js`, +1 en `acceso.test.js`. Mutaciones del componente (sin caducidad, aria-live fijo, sin pausa por foco, sin reduced-motion, sin filtro de vencidos) ponen la suite en rojo.
- axe-core (jsdom, sin contraste) sobre el carrusel de 1 y 3 anuncios y sobre la vista de gestión: 0 hallazgos.
- productos (sandbox, sin Docker): 257 pruebas, 238 en verde, 0 fallos; 4 clases con Testcontainers no corren aquí (las corre el CI). `ContratoDeBannersTest` falla con el contrato anterior y pasa con el nuevo.
- Guardianes: `validar-contratos` ok; `rutas-contrato-codigo` ok (243 llamadas); `cambios-de-contrato` ok contra la base de la rama (contra `origin/develop` actual marca `salas-partidas.yaml` 1.9.0→1.8.1 porque develop avanzó con #863 después de integrarlo aquí; se va al integrar develop).
- Borde: `nginx -t` y tráfico real contra ecos locales: las cinco rutas de banners llegan a productos y un prefijo desconocido sigue en 404.
- Playwright (solo listado, sin navegador): E2E nuevo `banner-rotativo.e2e.spec.js` (4 pruebas); el laboratorio cataloga `banners` en accesibilidad, auditoría visual, CTA y permisos, y `axe-con-datos` añade `home-poblada` con banner y `banners-admin`.

## Fuera de este PR

- La home no vuelve a preguntar por banners nuevos mientras está abierta (solo retira los que vencen).
- `productos.yaml` también sube a 1.6.0 en el PR de NOT-001 (`/alertas/cambios`): el segundo que entre tiene que pasar a 1.7.0 y unir el changelog.

---
@Melipete12: tus tres commits de #854 van intactos aquí; lo nuevo son los arreglos de CI/borde/contrato y el carrusel. Si prefieres fusionar #854 primero con esos arreglos, lo rebaso encima. Revisa sobre todo el cambio del esquema `Banner` en `productos.yaml`.

author: leghadjeu-christian
body:
## 1. Summary

This PR changes:

- Sets `enabled: false` on the `neo4j` controller and on `service.neo4j` in `charts/lightbridge-code-intelligence/values.yaml` (two lines).

It is **step 1 of 2**. Step 2 flips both back to `true`, and the StatefulSet is then created from the current chart — with the 20Gi `volumeClaimTemplates` from ai-helm#1138 and the memory/CPU from ai-helm#1143.

It solves:

- `spec.volumeClaimTemplates` is immutable, so the live StatefulSet cannot accept the 20Gi size. ArgoCD's server-side diff is rejected and the **whole Application** fails to compare, so no change to this app can sync — including ai-helm#1143. Part of https://github.com/ADORSYS-GIS/lightbridge-code-intelligence/issues/662.

```text
Failed to compare desired state to live state: … StatefulSet.apps "lightbridge-ci-neo4j" is invalid:
spec: Forbidden: updates to statefulset spec for fields other than 'replicas', 'ordinals',
'template', 'updateStrategy', 'revisionHistoryLimit', 'persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy'
and 'minReadySeconds' are forbidden
```

---

## 2. Intent

The intent of this PR is:

> Let ArgoCD prune the StatefulSet so it can be recreated from the chart, because an immutable field cannot be updated in place.

---

## 3. Scope

### In Scope

- `enabled: false` on the `neo4j` controller and its service, using the chart's existing disable convention (`a2a`, `mcp`, `notifier` use the same), so step 2 is a two-line revert.

### Out of Scope

- Any other value (sizes, resources, env) — unchanged.
- The `NEO4J_URI` / `NEO4J_USERNAME` / `NEO4J_PASSWORD` env on `control-plane` and `mcp`: deliberately left in place so step 2 is a pure revert of step 1.
- The live PVC, which is already 20Gi and is **not** touched by this PR.

---

## 4. Verification

I verified this change by:

- [x] Rendering the chart and diffing the resource set per `(kind, name)`
- [x] Checking what owns the PVC and whether ArgoCD tracks it
- [x] Comparing against the alternative of commenting the blocks out

Commands run:

```bash
$ helm template lightbridge-ci charts/lightbridge-code-intelligence -n converse -f ai-helm-values/environments/prod/values/lightbridge-code-intelligence.yaml   # origin/main vs this branch
$ kubectl --context hetzner-prod -n converse get pvc data-lightbridge-ci-neo4j-0 -o jsonpath='{.metadata.ownerReferences}{.metadata.annotations}{.metadata.finalizers}'
$ kubectl --context hetzner-prod -n converse get sts lightbridge-ci-neo4j -o jsonpath='{.spec.persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy}'
$ kubectl --context hetzner-prod get storageclass hcloud-volumes -o jsonpath='{.reclaimPolicy}'
```

Results:

```text
render rc=0
resources: 41 -> 39
PRUNED (would be deleted):
  - StatefulSet lightbridge-ci-neo4j
  - Service     lightbridge-ci-neo4j
ADDED: none

PVC ownerReferences: <empty>          # nothing can cascade-delete it
PVC annotations: pv.kubernetes.io/*   # no argocd tracking-id -> ArgoCD does not manage it -> prune cannot touch it
PVC finalizers: ["kubernetes.io/pvc-protection"]
persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy: {"whenDeleted":"Retain","whenScaled":"Retain"}
storageclass hcloud-volumes: reclaim=Delete
```

**The graph data is retained.** The PVC has no owner references, carries no ArgoCD tracking annotation, and the StatefulSet's retention policy is `Retain` on both paths, so pruning the StatefulSet leaves `data-lightbridge-ci-neo4j-0` (20Gi, bound) in place. Step 2's StatefulSet adopts that existing PVC rather than provisioning a new one, because `volumeClaimTemplates` is only consulted for PVCs that do not exist.

**The `neo4j-auth` Secret is also retained**, which is why `enabled: false` was chosen over commenting the blocks out. The ExternalSecret is gated on key existence rather than on `.enabled`:

```gotemplate
{{- if (index .Values "lci" "controllers" "neo4j") }}
```

so with `enabled: false` the key still exists and the ExternalSecret still renders (39 resources, not 38). Commenting the blocks out pruned it, and with `creationPolicy: Owner` that would have deleted the Secret that `control-plane` and `mcp` read `NEO4J_PASSWORD` from. Credit to the review bot for the suggestion.

---

## 5. Screenshots / Evidence

* Storage analysis and the three incidents behind this work: `NEO4J_STORAGE_GROWTH_REPORT.md` and lightbridge-code-intelligence#662.
* Current state: the database is already in its panicked state and rejecting every graph read and write (17,239 `TransactionStartFailed` errors in the current container log), so pruning the pod does not interrupt working traffic — the failure mode changes from a database panic to DNS resolution failure.

---

## 6. Risk Assessment

Risk level:

* [ ] Low
* [x] Medium
* [ ] High

Potential risks:

* **Neo4j is down for the whole window** between step 1 and step 2, and the Service is gone, so `control-plane` and `mcp` get DNS failures on `bolt://lightbridge-ci-neo4j:7687`.
* `storageclass hcloud-volumes` has `reclaim=Delete`: if the PVC were deleted at any point in this window, the Hetzner volume and the entire graph would be destroyed. Nothing in this PR deletes it, and no object can cascade to it, but the window is the time to be careful.

Mitigation:

* **Keep the window short.** Step 2 should be open, reviewed and ready to merge before this one is merged.
* Do not touch `data-lightbridge-ci-neo4j-0`.
* The `neo4j-auth` Secret now survives, so a `control-plane` or `mcp` restart during the window is no longer fatal.
* A lower-risk alternative needs no PR at all: `kubectl -n converse delete sts lightbridge-ci-neo4j --cascade=orphan`, which prunes nothing, keeps the pod serving, and lets ArgoCD recreate the StatefulSet and adopt the running pod. It requires `delete statefulsets` in `converse`, which the requester's account does not hold (`auth can-i delete statefulsets` → `no`), so this PR pair is the path available through Git.

---

## 7. AI Usage Declaration

AI was used for:

* [x] Understanding existing code
* [x] Generating code
* [ ] Refactoring
* [ ] Generating tests
* [x] Drafting documentation
* [x] Reviewing the diff
* [ ] Not used

Human verification:

* [ ] I understand every meaningful change in this PR
* [ ] I checked generated code manually
* [ ] I checked generated tests manually
* [ ] I removed unsupported AI assumptions
* [ ] I accept responsibility for this PR

---

## 8. Reviewer Focus

Please focus your review on:

* [x] Correctness
* [ ] Architecture
* [ ] Security
* [ ] Performance
* [ ] Tests
* [ ] Maintainability
* [x] Edge cases

Specifically: that step 2 is merged promptly after this one, and whether the `--cascade=orphan` alternative should be run by someone with the RBAC for it instead of merging this pair.

body:
## K2 из `docs/systems/IMPLEMENTATION.md`: PIN командира

**Что меняется для вас (командира):**
- PIN хранится как PBKDF2 с солью (раньше SHA-256 без соли, 10 000 вариантов перебирались мгновенно). Старый PIN работает и сам переносится в новый формат при первом верном вводе.
- 5 неверных вводов подряд без паузы, дальше пауза 60 с и вдвое длиннее за каждый следующий промах, не больше 15 минут. Полчаса без промахов: счёт заново.
- Задать и сменить PIN можно только с паролем облака. «Сменить PIN» больше не стирает PIN (раньше после этого любой ввод был «неверным»).
- Командир запирается после 10 минут простоя (касания продлевают), стрелка «назад» и кнопка «Закрыть командира» закрывают сразу. Возврат из «Звука и музыки» PIN снова не просит.

**Что сделано по итогам проверки ломающим проверяющим** (нашёл 12 замечаний, существенные закрыты и покрыты тестами): перебор пачкой параллельных вводов обходил лимит; без записи в `localStorage` лимит не работал; открытый экран не запирался сам; смена PIN при медленной сети могла открыть командира после ухода с экрана; импорт копии без PIN стирал PIN; PIN, поставленный ребёнком на устройстве без облака, перетягивал облако брата; испорченное значение PIN из облака; равенство при слиянии.

**Проверка:** 70 файлов, 2082 теста проходят (было 2057 + 25 новых), сборка проходит; в браузере прогнаны: задание PIN, лимит и рост паузы, сброс после верного ввода, перенос старого формата, смена без облака и с «облаком», возврат из «Звука», запирание по простою, пачка из 301 ввода (принято 2), импорт без PIN.

**Известно и не сделано**
- **Временная оговорка до S2:** на устройстве без облачного входа первый PIN задаётся без пароля (иначе из экрана «Данные», где вход, не попасть); такой PIN помечается слабым и при слиянии уступает PIN с паролем. Сменить PIN без облака нельзя.
- **Успешная ветка проверки пароля** (`reauth` в Firebase) в браузере не прогонялась: настоящего пароля у меня нет и вводить его нельзя. Проверены код, ветки отказа и логика на тестах. **Перед слиянием стоит один раз проверить на вашем телефоне:** войти в облако, «Сменить PIN», ввести пароль и новый PIN.
- Для аккаунта, вошедшего через Google или ссылку на почту (в интерфейсе остался только вход паролем), смена PIN не сработает, пока не войти по паролю.
- Защита от младшего брата, а не от взломщика: хэш лежит в сохранении на устройстве.

author: kshot3000
body:
Fixes #1849.

## Bug

`mergeTags` unconditionally deleted the source tags and then created a brand-new tag with `newTagName`:

1. **Crash on the primary use case** — merging tags into a name that already exists for the user (e.g. merging `reactjs` into the existing `react`) made `tx.tag.create` violate `@@unique([name, ownerId])` (Prisma `P2002`), the transaction rolled back, and the API returned HTTP 500.
2. **Silent settings loss** — when the destination tag was itself included in `tagIds`, it was deleted and recreated with blank defaults, erasing its `archiveAsScreenshot` / `archiveAsMonolith` / `archiveAsPDF` / `archiveAsReadable` / `archiveAsWaybackMachine` / `aiTag` settings.

## Fix

Inside the same transaction, resolve the destination first:

- `findUnique` on `name_ownerId` for `(newTagName, userId)`.
- If it exists: exclude it from `deleteMany` and `tag.update` it to connect the affected links — the tag row and its settings are preserved.
- If it doesn't exist: create it exactly as before.

The `indexVersion` reset for affected links is unchanged, and the lookup is scoped by `ownerId`, so another user's same-named tag is never touched.

## Verification

- **Red → green on the real controller code**: I ran `mergeTags.ts` (transpiled verbatim, only its two imports stubbed) against an in-memory Prisma fake that enforces the `@@unique([name, ownerId])` constraint with `P2002` and transaction rollback. Unpatched: merge-into-existing throws `P2002` and rolls back; destination-in-`tagIds` succeeds but returns a new tag with `archiveAsPDF: null` (settings erased). Patched: both scenarios return 200 with the destination tag and its settings preserved, source tags deleted, links relinked, `indexVersion` reset; fresh-name creation and the 400 validation path are unchanged.
- **New integration tests** in `mergeTags.test.ts` (same style as the existing `importFromHTMLFile` integration tests) cover all three cases against a real database. **Honest limitation: I could not run them locally** — this sandbox has no Postgres/`DATABASE_URL` and no pnpm — so they are for CI to execute; the harness above is what I verified locally. Prettier passes on both changed files.

No bounty on the issue — fix offered freely. Tips welcome: PayPal kyleblake0659@gmail.com · BTC 3GnR7TWBXAB3pPztBWpNF4LMNEX5yX8vZK — GitHub @Kshot3000, X @kshot9000.

**Closes #311** · WP-3 of epic #308 · **PR 3 of 4, stacked on #315** (base `feat/issue-310-survey-runs`). Review and merge in order. After the PR below this one squash-merges, rebase this branch onto `main` and retarget its base.

> ⚠️ **Before merging: snapshot the database.** Migration `00026_job_kind_survey_analyse.sql` **rebuilds `job` again** to add `survey_analyse` to its CHECK. #315's `00023` is the first rebuild. Since `00023`, nothing references `job`, so no cascade fires, and every row is copied by name. The Down is `SELECT 1`, so a `git revert` cannot undo it. Per `backend-code-style.md` rule 8, run `docker compose exec backup /usr/local/bin/backup.sh` on the Jetson before merging, and read `infra/local/DEPLOY-JETSON.md` §Rollback. If #315 and this PR deploy together, one snapshot taken before the first of them covers both.

## Summary

A survey run's sheets now come back:

- **Upload:** the professor uploads a scanned batch on screen 10. The server writes the batch on the request goroutine, then queues `survey_analyse`. That job runs one `/analyse` on the same runner and the same worker lock.
- **Storage:** the report is stored **without identity**: copies, one `survey_mark` per recorded alternative, and review items.
- **Review:** the professor resolves the doubtful answers on screen 11, next to the scanned page image.
- **Reset:** the professor can erase the whole capture ("Borrar escaneos": the worker first, then the copies).
- **Closing:** the professor closes the run once nothing is left to review. Only closed runs will count in the results (#312).

Decisions (ADR-0081, amends ADR-0075 §5 and ADR-0050):

- **Per answer, never per copy.** A survey copy reads `needs_review` because there is no ID grid, so the copy's status, RUT and score are ignored.
  - `ok` → marks.
  - `blank` → nothing.
  - `ambiguous` / `doubtful` → a review item and **no** mark.
  - A name, answer number or status the run never printed refuses the whole batch before any write.
- **A later batch replaces only the copies it re-captured, and re-reads what is still undecided on the others.** Every decision is kept, and a pending item keeps its id. Review fix COR-1: a page that arrives in a later batch was being dropped.
- **A resolution is recorded once:** exactly one alternative on a single or scale question, at least one on a multi, the question's own alternatives only, or "Descartar".
- **"Borrar escaneos" is the second synchronous worker call.** It has the same two properties as the first: it only removes files, and it never waits on the lock. It is called through `Client.ResetSurveyScans` with the survey's own error values; `survey` still never imports `controls`.
- **A run with scans cannot be cancelled. A closed run refuses every mutation, and there is no reopen in v1.**

## Slices completed

- [x] S1 copies, marks, review items (migration `00025`) — `03b271d`
- [x] S2 the survey `Analyzer` port and `ReadReport` on the S0 fixture — `8a7bff5`
- [x] S3 `survey_analyse` in its four places (migration `00026`) and `AnalyzeBatch` — `73ad0ea`
- [x] S4 upload and screen 10 — `74bf1da`
- [x] S5 review queue, screen 11, page images — `2f665ae`
- [x] S6 "Borrar escaneos" and no cancel with scans, plus ADR-0081 — `474112d`
- [x] S7 "Cerrar pasada", with screen 9's counts and actions live — `4587b67`
- [x] S8 docs and the live check — `5874a01`. **PAPER-CHECK was not run** (see Notes). The issue's S8 line says so.
- Fixes from the browser check: `39e109d` (flash on screens 10 and 11), `3e682aa` (a decided item now names what it recorded).
- Review fixes: `cd118da` (Round A), `a042479` (Round A rechecks), `e13c2e7` and `13d70d7` (Round B and its rechecks).

## Acceptance criteria

1. **The batch is written before the job; a refusal or an outage leaves it intact.**
   - `TestAnUploadWritesTheBatchBeforeQueueingItsReading` covers the order.
   - `TestABatchThatStoresNothingSaysWhy` covers the worker refusing or away: the run is untouched and the banner shows the failure.
   - The browser check confirmed both against the real worker. ✅
2. **One copy per present copy and one mark per alternative, through the printed order, on the S0 fixture.**
   - `TestAnalyzeSheetsReadsTheS0ReportInSurveyTerms` uses the real S0 report.
   - Also `TestEachAnswerStatusBecomesMarksOrAnItem` and `TestAnAnalysedBatchStoresMarksAndItemsAndSaysWhatItRead`. ✅
3. **Ambiguous and doubtful answers create items and no marks; blank answers create nothing.** `TestEachAnswerStatusBecomesMarksOrAnItem`, `TestADoubtfulAnswerWithAConfidentMarkRecordsNothingYet`. ✅
4. **Re-capture resets that copy, and a batch that captured nothing is refused in Spanish.**
   - `TestALaterBatchReplacesOnlyTheCopiesItRecaptured`.
   - `TestARecapturedCopyIsReadAgainThroughTheJob`, which goes through the job.
   - `TestALaterBatchRefreshesWhatIsStillUndecided` and `TestALaterBatchKeepsPendingItemIDs`.
   - The "Ninguna página…" failure in `TestABatchThatStoresNothingSaysWhy`.
   - Browser check: re-scanning copy 2 alone replaced only copy 2. ✅
5. **Screen 11 resolves items, and resolving the last one enables closing.** `TestResolvingACopyRecordsTheChoiceAndMovesToTheNextOne`, `TestAMultiSelectRecordsSeveralAlternatives`, `TestAStaleDecisionShowsTheCopyAgain`, `TestARunClosesOnceReviewedAndThenRefusesEveryChange`, plus the browser check. ✅
6. **"Borrar escaneos": worker first; refused with a job in flight, a busy worker, or a run that is closed or cancelled.** `TestBorrarEscaneosErasesWorkerFirstThenTheCopies`, `TestResetSurveyScansSpeaksTheSurveyDomain`. ✅
7. **Closing is refused with pending items, no copies, or a job in flight, and a closed run refuses every mutation.** `TestARunClosesOnceReviewedAndThenRefusesEveryChange`, `TestARunWithNothingReadDoesNotClose`, `TestARunDoesNotCloseUnderAQueuedReading`, `TestCloseRunNeedsReadCopiesAndNothingPending`, `TestSaveReadingsRefusesARunThatIsNotOpen`. ✅
   - 7b. **A run with scans cannot be cancelled.** `TestARunWithScansIsNotCancelled` covers it, including a batch whose reading failed. ✅
8. **`survey_analyse` in all four places, and `NewRunner` boots.**
   - `TestEveryValidKindHasASubject`.
   - `TestTheSurveyAnalyseKindRebuildKeepsEveryJob` checks that both subjects' rows survive verbatim.
   - The branch image boots over the WP-2 database: 00025 and 00026 applied over existing jobs. ✅
9. **`survey ↛ controls`, no `.Store.` in handlers, new routes gated with CSRF, nothing on `/api`.** `TestTheSurveyDomainDoesNotImportControls`, `TestEveryRouteIsGatedUnlessItSaysWhyNot`, `TestEveryStateChangingRouteVerifiesCSRF` (9 new routes), plus a grep; confirmed by the security lens. ✅
10. **Protocols:** see Tests. ✅ (compose step substituted, see Notes)
11. **Checks:**
    - Browser check (Playwright, Chromium, 1440 px light and dark, plus 390 px) against the **real** worker: screens 9, 10 and 11, the full flow. ✅
    - **Real paper check: ❌ not run, owed by a human.** See `apps/amc-worker/PAPER-CHECK.md` §7.
12. **README routes and `apps/server/CLAUDE.md`:** the survey bullets for batch-survives and for the four reset rules, and "two named exceptions". ✅

## Tests

Pre-PR battery in the pinned `golang:1.25-alpine` image, on `e13c2e7`:

- `gofmt -l .` is empty.
- `go vet`, `go build` and `go test -race -count=1 ./...` (CGO + build-base) all pass.
- `govulncheck@v1.7.0`: "No vulnerabilities found".
- `13d70d7` changes only a doc paragraph and one test assertion; vet and the full suite are green on it.
- `docker build` on the tip.
  - The image boots over a copy of the WP-2 database: `/health` and `/api/health` both return `up`.
  - The run, scans, review and page-image routes return 200.
- Every new guard was seen failing before its fix, or under a mutation; each commit message names how.

## Reviews run

`review-pipeline`, mode **full**, integrated. Performance lens not spawned: no hot path, one aggregate per page. Miguel delegated the verifier tables for this epic.

- **Round A (code):** gat

author: upd4ting
body:
## Summary

Beta polish for the French console: translated invoice statuses and automation labels, plus a confirmation before plan downgrades.

**Invoice statuses are translated.** The status columns of the invoice tables (tenant billing history, platform invoices, a user's invoices) and of the credit notes table rendered the raw Stripe value (`paid`, `open`, ...). They now use a `SelectType` whose items carry `$saas.invoices.status.*` / `$saas.credit_notes.status.*` labels (`src/utils/billing-document-status.ts`), so every status goes through i18n. English and French translations are added for every status a row can hold (`draft`, `open`, `paid`, `void`, `uncollectible`, plus `issued` for mirrored credit notes). `paid` now renders as "Payée" in French.

**Downgrades ask for confirmation.** In `PlanComparisonModal.vue`, choosing a plan that lowers the monthly price (Free included) now opens a confirmation modal instead of changing the plan at once. It warns that features outside the target plan are switched off and the permissions that rely on them are removed, that members, resources and data beyond its limits may be restricted or lost, and, for a free target, that the paid subscription ends. Cancelling leaves the plan unchanged; confirming runs the existing `changePlan` call with the same toasts and error handling. Upgrades keep their current flow. The downgrade rule (`usePlanDowngrade.ts`) mirrors the server's `isDowngrade` (monthly price comparison), with a paid-to-Free fallback when the current plan is no longer in the catalog.

**Automation catalog labels are translatable.** The automation triggers registered by dms-saas (subscription started, subscription cancelled, payment failed, trial ending, workspace deleted) and its actions (suspend workspace, notify workspace owners) now register their `name` and `description` as `$`-prefixed locale keys, `$saas.automation.<trigger|action>.<key>.name` / `.description`. The key comes from the node id: `saas.trial-ending` becomes `trial_ending`. English and French entries live under `saas.automation` in both locale files.

**Deferred:** role names (`src/roles/standard-roles.ts` in the `cloud` repo) stay untranslated: DMS `Role.name` has no i18n support yet.

## Merge order

This PR must be merged **after** the dms-automation PR that resolves `$`-prefixed `TriggerType` / `ActionType` names and descriptions through `processI18n()` is merged **and released**. Until then, the automation catalog would show the raw `$saas.automation...` keys in place of the trigger and action names. That PR must cover action types as well as trigger types, because this PR also moves the two action labels to keys.

## Related issue

Beta polish unit B·1·02 (French translations + downgrade confirmation). No GitHub issue. Depends on the dms-automation `processI18n` PR (see Merge order).

## Verification

All CI steps from `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, run locally:

- `pnpm --filter @antelopejs/interface-dms-saas build`
- `pnpm --filter @antelopejs/interface-dms-saas lint`
- `pnpm --filter @antelopejs/dms-saas lint` (oxlint, oxfmt, interface ranges, frontend eslint)
- `pnpm --filter @antelopejs/interface-dms-saas typecheck`
- `pnpm --filter @antelopejs/dms-saas typecheck`
- `pnpm --filter @antelopejs/interface-dms-saas knip`
- `pnpm --filter @antelopejs/dms-saas knip`
- `pnpm --filter @antelopejs/dms-saas build`
- `pnpm --filter @antelopejs/interface-dms-saas check:exports`
- `pnpm --filter @antelopejs/dms-saas test:unit`: 77 files, 701 tests passed
- `pnpm --filter @antelopejs/dms-saas test:frontend` (DMS source compiled with the frontend module)

New tests:
- `test/billing-document-status.test.ts`: every invoice and credit note status has an item, and every label resolves in both locales ("paid" gives "Payée" in French).
- `test/automation-node-labels.test.ts`: every registered trigger and action label is a `$saas.automation.` key that resolves in both locales ("Abonnement démarré" in French).
- `test/plan-downgrade.test.ts`: covers downgrades to Free and to a cheaper paid plan, upgrades, comparison across billing intervals, equal prices, and a current plan missing from the catalog.

No manual browser check was done.

## What
Adds **KANNA / 花守りの神機 GARDEN GOD-MACHINE**, a giant (~2.5× a person) pearl-and-gold god-machine who fights with flowers, as the 9th fighter.

| Special | 花弁射出 | 5 homing petal-blade projectiles from her wings (clashable) |

author: cagnulein
body:
## Summary

On Android, the Virtual Echelon advertiser set the Bluetooth adapter name but did not include the device name in the BLE advertising data. As a result, scanners such as nRF Connect could discover the Echelon service UUID while showing the device name as `N/A`.

This change keeps the 128-bit Echelon service UUID in the primary advertising packet and places the device name in the scan response.

## Why

Keeping the name in the scan response avoids risking the 31-byte legacy advertising payload limit while still exposing the expected Echelon name (for Fake Bike, currently `ECHEX-5s-113399`).

## Change

- add a scan response with `setIncludeDeviceName(true)`
- use the 4-argument `startAdvertising()` overload with primary ADV + scan response
- leave the Echelon GATT services and UUID advertising unchanged

## Expected result

With Virtual Echelon enabled on Android, nRF Connect should display the advertised Echelon device name instead of `N/A`.

body:
The Renovate pull requests #679 and #682 each bump one of simplecov and simplecov-cobertura, and neither can produce a lockfile alone: simplecov-cobertura 3 needs simplecov 0.x, while simplecov-cobertura 4 needs simplecov 1.x. This bumps both together, to simplecov 1.3.2 and simplecov-cobertura 4.0.0, which also drops docile, simplecov-html and simplecov_json_formatter from the lockfile.

simplecov 1.x no longer has `SimpleCov.running`, which `test__helper.rb` used so it would not start coverage twice. The helper now asks the stdlib `Coverage.running?`, the same check simplecov makes internally.

simplecov 1.x also prints deprecation warnings for `add_filter`, `track_files` and `minimum_coverage_by_file`. Their replacements change which files get measured, so that move is left to #1323. Once this lands, #679 and #682 have nothing left to do.

Closes #1322

author: tgoodyear
body:
This sets the default `USNM_COMPUTE_CONCURRENCY` (the number of search slots) from 4 to 2: one per searcher vCPU, the point past which more slots add no throughput. It also records the second production load test in 06 §6.5.

## Why

That test ran with Quickwit no longer cancelling searches at 30 s, after #146 and #150. Throughput was flat whatever the concurrency, so the searcher's 2 vCPUs are the limit: about 16 s of CPU per cold search, however many share it.

| Searches at once | Searches/s | Speedup | Median s | Slowest s | Mean backend s | Failed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.063 | 1.00 | 9.0 | 66.2 | 15.5 | 0/10 |
| 2 | 0.065 | 1.03 | 19.7 | 72.7 | 28.8 | 0/10 |
| 4 | 0.060 | 0.96 | 44.3 | 120.5 | 46.7 | 1/10 |
| 10 | 0.064 | 1.03 | 67.3 | 140.0 | 41.4 | 1/10 |

With 4 slots, four heavy searches split the CPU four ways and two ran past the API's 120 s limit. With 2, each running search gets half the CPU instead of a quarter. Throughput stays the same, heavy searches stay inside the limit, and the first searches in the queue finish sooner. The queue (#142) keeps up to 16 more waiting in order.

## Also recorded in 06 §6.5

A phrase containing a common word costs 4–5 times the rest. Over 1896, run alone:

| Search | Backend time |
|---|---|
| phrase "cross of gold" | 41 s |
| `cross gold` within 2 words | 9 s |
| phrase "yellow fever" | 8 s |
| `gold` alone | 4 s |

A phrase reads the positions of every word in it, and "of" is on almost every page. Fixing that changes what a phrase matches, so it's left for a separate decision.

## Testing

- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p usnm-api --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test -p usnm-api` pass. The config test asserts the new default; the queue tests set their own slot counts.
- After merge, a rerun of `scripts/load-cold-searches.py` against production will confirm it. The API reads this setting from the image, so the change ships with this merge's deploy.

author: gpsm2
body:
## Summary

Three problems found while checking a 17 km night on the production instance. That night itself was real — the integration's 17.157 km matches the device's own counter exactly (18,832 rotations on a 29 cm wheel), with no step-backs and normal running speeds across eight nights of history. The check turned these up anyway.

- **Closes #167** — a small counter step-back was treated as a full reset, booking the *entire* counter as tonight's distance and adding it to the lifetime total. Reproduced: 40 rotations back from 20,100 → 17.6 km out of nothing; on the production counter (230,075) it would be ~210 km, permanently. Only a drop below half the previous value counts as a reset now; a smaller step-back re-anchors and shifts the window baselines so tonight keeps what it already showed.
  - Same block, found by the reload test: `async_create_task` starts the save immediately, so saves inside that block wrote updated baselines next to the *old* comparison value, and a reload detected the same reset/step-back twice. Saves there now run after `_last_known_count` is updated.
- **Closes #168** — speed records took the maximum *single* reading. On ~126,000 production readings the median is 2.87 km/h and the 99th percentile 3.82 km/h, yet the nightly maximum was 11–12.8 km/h every night (lifetime record 13.1) — isolated glitch pulses at the firmware's 250 ms cooldown. Records now need the speed held over 3 consecutive readings (the lowest of them); replayed on the same history that gives 4.7–6.2 km/h per night. Old records are cleared once via `SPEED_TRUST_VERSION`, since the new rule could never beat them; night distances in the history are kept, only their speed figure goes.
- **Closes #169** — the 0.11.2 "no data" summary checked whether the sensor is readable *at send time*, so a device rebooting after the hamster had finished threw a fully recorded night away. Replaced by `night_has_wheel_data`: any readable counter since the night window began, persisted with the night baseline. Restoring a paused hamster's frozen snapshot now ignores unknown keys, since removing the old field would otherwise have broken setup for every hamster paused under 0.11.2.

## Test plan

- [x] New regression tests, each confirmed to **fail against the previous code**: step-back is not a reset, step-back survives a reload, a reset isn't counted twice after a reload, glitch doesn't set a record, sustained sprint counts, a stop breaks the run, re-reading one value isn't "sustained", upgrade discards old records once, night flag survives a later dropout, night without readings is flagged and survives a reload, summary keeps a night the sensor dropped out after.
- [x] Snapshot regression test confirmed to fail (`TypeError: unexpected keyword argument 'wheel_sensor_available'`) with the key filter removed.
- [x] Full suite (276 tests), `ruff` clean, `mypy` only the known pre-existing `OptionsFlowWithReload` finding.

author: idangib
body:
### Motivation
- Mobile browsers were shrinking the game canvas to fit the viewport height which caused its width to no longer align with the top toolbar. 
- The intent is to have the canvas span the full available width on mobile while preserving aspect ratio and letting the page grow vertically.

### Description
- Replace fixed viewport-height rules on `body` with `min-height: 100svh` / `min-height: 100dvh` to avoid forcing the page to shrink on mobile. 
- Set `main` to `min-height: calc(100dvh - 16px)` so the content can grow vertically while keeping the toolbar spacing. 
- Change `#game` flex from `flex: 1 1 auto` to `flex: 0 0 auto` so the game container does not force-fit to the viewport height. 
- Force the canvas to fill the available width and preserve its aspect ratio by adding `width: 100% !important; height: auto !important; max-height: none;` in the mobile media query.

### Testing
- Ran `npm test` and all tests passed (5 passing tests). 
- Ran `npm run lint` (TypeScript `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`) with no issues. 
- Ran `npm run build` (`vite build`) and the site built successfully.

author: padrio
body: Nachzieh-PR zum Merge von Stack 1 ([PRI-160](/PRI/issues/PRI-160), PR #65). Herkunft ist Finding F5 des Code-Reviews PRI-288: der Stack brachte ein neues Top-Level-Verzeichnis, eine neue Datei unter `public/` und ein drittes automatisches Qualitätsgate auf `main`, ohne `CLAUDE.md` anzufassen — `git diff --stat origin/main...origin/stack/pri-14-baseline-1 -- CLAUDE.md` war leer. **Nur `CLAUDE.md`, 59 Zeilen rein / 13 raus.** Kein gerenderter Code, kein Verhalten der Plugins angefasst. ## Der folgenreiche Teil: das dritte Gate steht jetzt im Abschnitt *Befehle* `plugins/assert-content-images.mjs` wirft in `astro:build:done` und macht damit `npm run build` rot — liegt aber in keinem Workflow. Wer ein Markdown-Bild anfasste, konnte die Pipeline rot machen und fand in `CLAUDE.md` keinen Hinweis, dass dieses Gate existiert. Es ist jetzt nach Ort, Auslöser, Prüfgegenstand sowie grüner und roter Ausgabe beschrieben, samt der einen fail-open-Lücke, die die Datei selbst benennt (handgeschriebenes `` im Markdown). Die grüne Zeile im PR-Body und in `CLAUDE.md` ist nicht abgeschrieben, sondern aus dem Build dieses Branches: ``` [assert-content-images] 8 markdown image(s) carry loading="lazy" and their file's width/height; every hero is eager ``` ## Die Zwei-Gate-Zahl stand an sechs Stellen, nicht an einer Alle sechs ziehen mit: der Codeblock in *Befehle*, die Beschreibung darunter, Regel 3, deren Markdown-`throw`-Absatz, der Stack-Abschnitt *Das Gate* und — vom Code-Review in Runde 1 gefunden — der Satz „was die beiden Gates sehen (Regel 3)" in **Arbeitsablauf, Schritt 5**. Dort wird aus „beide" zusätzlich **„alle drei"**, weil das Bild-Gate *innerhalb* von `npm run build` feuert und bei einem fehlenden Check mit demselben Griff ausfällt wie die anderen zwei. **Eine Stelle ist bewusst unangetastet:** der Satz „Beide Gates greifen erst zusammen" in Regel 3. Er meint den `strict`-Schalter und das Grep-Gate im PR-#13-Fall und ist dort richtig. ## Der Markdown-`throw`-Absatz war nicht nur ungenau, sondern falsch Er verneinte für `main` beides, was Stack 1 mitbringt — ein Markdown-Plugin und ein Gate gegen genau diese Fehlerklasse. Sein in [PRI-282](/PRI/issues/PRI-282) ausdrücklich gesetzter Vorbehalt „auf dem heutigen `main`" wird hier eingelöst. Die Messwerte aus PRI-126/278/279 bleiben unberührt. Neu dazu kommt die **Grenze der Deckung**, damit der Absatz nicht in die andere Richtung überzieht: das Gate prüft das gebaute `dist/`, deckt die Fehlerklasse also nur so weit, wie sie die Projekt-Bilder betrifft. Rot wird eine ausgeweidete `.prose-project` dabei nur dort, wo das Markdown überhaupt ein Bild referenziert — heute `konteo-panel.md` (6) und `konteo-provision.md` (2), zusammen die acht aus der grünen Zeile; die drei übrigen Projekt-Markdowns tragen nur das Frontmatter-Hero, das außerhalb von `.prose-project` liegt und die Ausweidung überlebt. Ein `throw` an einer Stelle ohne Markdown-Bild kommt ebenfalls weiter mit Exit 0 durch; die Lücke am glob-loader selbst ist nicht geschlossen. ## Struktur-Block - `astro.config.mjs`: jetzt **drei** Integrationen (`icon`, `sitemap`, `assertContentImages`) plus den neuen `markdown.processor`-Schlüssel. - `plugins/satteri-content-images.mjs` und `plugins/assert-content-images.mjs` als neues Top-Level-Verzeichnis, mit dem Grund, warum das Gate nicht im Plugin liegt. - `public/robots.txt`. Der Verweis auf `sitemap-index.xml` ist gegen die Build-Ausgabe geprüft (``[@astrojs/sitemap] `sitemap-index.xml` created at `dist` ``), nicht aus der Datei abgeschrieben. Kontrolle gegen `git diff --diff-filter=A 856fcb7^1 856fcb7`: der Stack brachte genau diese drei neuen Dateien, alle drei sind dokumentiert. ## Verifikation - `npm run build` fehlerfrei auf dem Commit dieses Branches, 9 Seiten. Der Content-Layer-Cache (`node_modules/.astro`) war vorher gelöscht — den Hinweis gibt der Kopf des Gates selbst. - Reihenfolgebedingung aus der Triage erfüllt: `main` ist `856fcb7 Merge pull request #65`, der Stack ist also drin. Der Branch-Ref `origin/stack/pri-14-baseline-1` ist nach dem Merge gelöscht, deshalb schlägt der `merge-base --is-ancestor`-Test aus dem Triage-Kommentar mit „Not a valid object name" fehl — nicht, weil der Stack fehlt. Geprüft wurde statt dessen die Existenz der Dateien in `git ls-tree origin/main`. - Koppelprüfung: kein anderer offener PR berührt `CLAUDE.md`. ## Nicht in Scope - Plugin-Verhalten (in PRI-285 in vier Runden reviewt). - Die vier Redirects in `astro.config.mjs` — das ist PRI-168. - Die übrigen Findings aus PRI-287/288. Zwei angrenzende Befunde gehen als Kommentar ins Issue statt in diesen Diff: eine veraltete Zwei-Gate-Aussage im Kopf von `assert-content-images.mjs` und das im Struktur-Block fehlende `src/pages/projects/index.astro` (vorbestehend, nicht von Stack 1). ## Review-Runde 1 abgearbeitet (PRI-292, PASS mit Findings, 0 blocking) Alle fünf Findings sind umgesetzt: die Deckungsaussage in Regel 3 ist auf die zwei bildtragenden Projekt-Markdowns begrenzt (F1), Schritt 5 auf drei Gates nachgezogen (F2), die Gate-Aussage im PRI-126-Absatz an den Messzeitpunkt gebunden (F3), der `satteri`-Eintrag im Struktur-Block auf `/…`-Pfade aus `public/` begrenzt (F4) und der zweite `throw` des Gates (`no .md files under `) genannt (F5). Eine Abweichung vom vorgeschlagenen Fix-Text, bewusst: F4 nannte zusätzlich „ein vom Autor gesetztes Attribut gewinnt". Dieser Halbsatz stand kurz im Diff und ist wieder heraus — der Kopf von `satteri-content-images.mjs` hält ausdrücklich fest, dass Markdowns `![]()`-Syntax diese Attribute nicht tragen kann, die Guards aus einem `.md` also unerreichbar sind. Im Struktur-Block hätte der Satz genau die Pauschale ersetzt, die F4 beanstandet.

author: breferrari
body:
`resolveQmdEntry` now prefers a qmd install that actually starts over one that only exists. Before, the first `@tobilu/qmd` entrypoint that resolved was used. A broken local copy (missing dependencies, a half-finished install, a native binding built for a different Node ABI) therefore shadowed a working global install, so the MCP wrapper launched something that could not start and the refresh worker failed without a message.

Both copies change the same way: `lib/qmd.ts` and `qmd-mcp.mjs` (the `.mjs` cannot import the `.ts` lib at strip-types runtime). Candidates are still tried in the old order, local then `npm root -g`, and `pickQmdEntry` decides:

| Present candidates | Result | Probes |
|---|---|---|
| none | `null` (the shell `qmd` fallback, as before) | 0 |
| only one | that one | 0 |
| first runnable | the first; `npm root -g` is never spawned | 1 |
| first broken, second runnable | the second | 2 |
| all broken | **the first**, not `null` | 2 |

The last row is deliberate. SessionStart's ABI self-heal finds the package to `npm rebuild` from the entry it is given (`qmdPackageRootFromEntry`). Returning `null` when everything is broken would switch off the only repair path that exists. The second row keeps the common single-install case (CI, and most machines) free of an extra spawn. The probe is `node <entry> --version` with a 10 s timeout.

Not in scope, as the issue says: trying the `PATH` `qmd` as a candidate.

Tests (`tests/qmd.test.ts`) run every row above against both copies. They also check that the real probe accepts a script that exits 0 and rejects one that throws on load. Against `main` the file fails to import, because the seam does not exist there.

Mutation check: each of these fails one test and nothing else:
- Return the first present candidate without probing (the old behaviour), in the `.ts` copy and, separately, in the `.mjs` copy.
- Return `null` when every candidate is broken.
- Probe a lone candidate.
- Make the probe ignore the exit status.

Closes #283

author: tsundancek
body:
For Cowork's preview (owner ruling (a) in COWORK #144: overlap only, no Stretched page). Merge only on the owner's GO.

**Stacked on #757 (FVG):** the base is #757's branch, so this diff shows only the stretch change. Once #757 merges I'll rebase this onto main, retarget it to main, and re-run the gates before merging.

**What changes**
- **The picker column:** a "Stretch (z20)" column on `/oversold-stocks-today` and `/overbought-stocks-today` only, General tab, after % Change.
  - It reads "-2.3" / "+2.3" and sorts on the number.
  - Its header tip says what it measures; an empty cell says why.
  - Computed from each row's 72 stored closes (the chart points the page already ships), never the live pool price. **No new payload field, no fetch, no Redis command: 0 commands a day.**
- **The stock-page line:** on `/stock/[symbol]`, inside B's chart component above the gap toggle; C's header strip is untouched.
  - **The reading:** "ABC closed 2.3 standard deviations below its 20-day average."
  - **The history, at |z| ≥ 2:** "The last N times ABC was this far below its 20-day average, it was back to it within 10 sessions M times." The mirror reads "above".
  - **Under 5 past cases:** "Too few past cases to say."
  - It reads at `--fs-read`.
  - **The tap note** ("How is this counted?") explains the measure and states the survivorship limit, per the ruling: the note, not the page.
  - Built from the page's own history, completed sessions only. Past tense; no "will".
- **No line on SPX:** that chart is passed no bars.

**Definitions (`lib/stretch.ts`, pure)**
- **z20:** (close − SMA20) ÷ the population stdev of the last 20 closes.
- **A case:** the first day of a run at |z| ≥ 2 on today's side. The current run is excluded, and a case needs 10 sessions after it.
- **"Back":** a later session's range reached that day's SMA20 within 10 sessions; the 10th counts.

**Checks:** `check-stretch` (in check-all), 13 mutants, all caught. It covers:
- z20 against a by-hand computation;
- the zone edge (−1.65 → the reading only);
- re-arming;
- a long current run not counted;
- the 10th session counted and the 11th not;
- the follow window;
- "Too few";
- the mirror;
- the wording and the note;
- the column only on the two pages, from stored closes, with its column set following the page;
- the line at `--fs-read`, the note closed, and none on SPX.

`measure-chart-readout` now also checks the line reads at 16 px inside the column at 320–430 and 1280 px.

**Three source-pinned checks adjusted, with the same intent:**
- `check-pickers-cell-why` parses the literal `general:` column list, so the column is spliced in after it rather than with a ternary;
- `check-chart-gaps`' note-size mutant is anchored to `.chart-gap-note`;
- `check-stretch` avoids an escaped-quote label that `check-security-spellings`' comment stripper misreads.

**Gates:** `tsc --noEmit` clean; check-all 270/270.

author: curphey
body:
The migration runner remembers what it has run by filename. So a renamed migration runs a second time, and a low number runs out of order on a database that's already ahead (split plan §4.2, Codex finding 2). This adds the checks §4.2 lists, plus the per-worktree database helper.

What CI now checks, all in `scripts/ci/check-migrations.mjs`:
- **On a pull request:** every new migration is numbered above `main`'s highest, each number is used once, and names follow `NNN_words.sql`. Files already on `main` must not be renamed, deleted or edited.
- **On a pull request:** a fresh database is migrated at `main`, then at the pull request, and the second run must apply exactly the new files.
- **A backstop on every push to `main`:** migration numbers are unique and were added in increasing order. It should never fail. If it does, stop and ask Jack rather than renaming anything.
- Each check fails if it reads nothing. A pull request is compared against `HEAD^1`, the exact `main` GitHub merged it with.

`scripts/new-db.sh <name>` makes a database for a worktree or a review, with the same rights for `epos_app` as `epos` has. It uses Node and `pg`, not `psql` or the Docker CLI. A new CI step proves it: on a database it makes, every migration runs and the row-level security check passes. Without its grant, migrating fails with "permission denied for schema public". The README explains how to use it. CI now checks out full history (`fetch-depth: 0`), since the checks need to read `main`.

Watched failing first:
- Unit cases for each rule.
- A throwaway git repository with a renamed file and a low number.
- Locally, a branch that renames `039`. The `pr` check names the frozen file, and the upgrade check reports `040` failing because its column already exists.

The fresh review found three things, now fixed:
- The repository's own backstop test failed on a branch that had merged `main` in. It now reads `origin/main`.
- A wrong cause was named when `main` moved during a run. CI now compares against `HEAD^1`.
- The `new-db.sh` proof wasn't in CI. It is now a CI step.

One known limit: a rename whose SQL happens to run cleanly twice gets past the upgrade check. The `pr` check catches it by naming the missing original.

Locally, `npm test` passes 1,671 of 1,671 and `npm run test:browser` passes 34 of 34. An earlier browser run passed 33 while the full suite was running alongside. It looked like a flake, but that run kept only its summary line, so I can't name the test.

@JackCurphey, this edits `.github/workflows/test.yml`, which §4.2 names, so it's yours to review as part of WP-0.4.

author: devthejo
body:
Closes #2195 · Closes #2196 — epic 🩺 CI health #1410. Two ways `task check` reddened for reasons unrelated to the diff, both measured on 2026-10-04. 6 files, +66, all additive; production untouched.

## Fixes

- **#2195** — golangci-lint's default cache is keyed on absolute paths, so sibling worktrees poison each other (a run in one worktree failed on findings pointing at a *deleted* sibling's tree). The `lint` task now keys `GOLANGCI_LINT_CACHE` on a hash of the worktree's top-level path: stable per worktree (warm runs still pay off — 272s cold → 14s warm), disjoint across siblings, XDG-based, never in the tracked tree. CI is unaffected — it invokes `golangci-lint` directly (verified: `.github/workflows/tests.yml`, no workflow calls `task lint`).
- **#2196** — under devbox, `sh` is nix bash, so the tests' spawned login shells (`runshell`'s `$SHELL -l`, `schedgate`'s `sh -lc`) read the operator's `~/.profile`: pyenv init wrote into captured streams and contended on the shim lock under suite parallelism (60s rehash timeouts reddening pkg/runshell, pkg/schedgate, pkg/trigger). The tests now scrub `HOME` to an empty dir (the repo's existing `detect_test.go` idiom) — production deliberately untouched: real guards and run shells legitimately inherit the operator's env. The class is covered at choke points: every gate-exec path in `pkg/cli` goes through `newGateFixture`.

## Proofs

- Lint green from two worktrees with disjoint caches; garbage planted in a sibling's cache ignored.
- The three packages green with the host pyenv active; zero pyenv strings in a full `task test`.
- A/B on the exact-equality test round 1 caught unscrubbed: main reddens under a noisy HOME (`Vars[greeting] = "PROFILE-NOISE-ON-STDOUT\nv42\n"`), the fixed tree stays green.

## Review cost

Adversarial-Rounds: 2 local (announced 3, ceiling 10 — the diff touches the lint gate). R1: 1 HIGH (class under-covered: pkg/cli's gate tests missed by the site-grep, A/B-proven by the reviewer) + 2 LOW, fixed at the fixture choke point and in comments. R2 (re-attack of the fix): sterile — effectiveness re-proven, fixture proven the only gate-exec path in the package, every new comment clause executed true.
Adversarial-Model: kimi-code

`task check`: all tasks green except the known pre-existing `bots/TestModernizeLotVerifyReadsTheContractOrRefuses`. The lint task's green run used the new per-worktree cache — the feature exercised by its own check.

author: kim-em
body:
This PR proves that an exact character-table certificate has distinct central-character rows after reduction into any commutative ring without zero divisors in which the group order is nonzero. Derive distinctness at every conjugate primitive root modulo a good Dixon prime, and remove the separate residue-row injectivity hypothesis from `ClassData.isSome_dixonCyclotomicCharacterTable_of_spec`.

Advance `RepresentationTheory/CharacterTheory/README.md`, Layer 6, “The executable Burnside-Dixon-Schneider algorithm (the summit)”, specifically the certified Dixon-prime condition that reduced central-character tuples remain injective and its consumption by “The assembled solver”. The concrete consumer is the solver's row-alignment construction: its exact certificate and coefficient-window hypothesis now suffice to prove success at the supplied Dixon prime. This discharges an independent obligation on the general completeness path using the already-merged exact checker and modular search, rather than supplying another worked table. After this PR, unconditional success of the assembled solver still needs certified exact table data and control of the central power-basis coefficients; this PR does not assert the unverified universal `2⌊√|G|⌋` coefficient bound.

Add `TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/CharacterTable/Dixon/Cyclotomic/Reduction.lean` (50 lines) and update five existing Dixon modules. The public additions are `IsExactCharacterTableSpec.map_central_injective` and `IsCyclotomicCharacterTableSpec.conjugateResidueRow_injective`. Equal central rows force proportional ordinary rows because class sizes divide the group order. Applying mapped orthogonality then contradicts the nonzero degree and group order. The map need not preserve conjugation. Replace the rational solver's integer-only proof with the general theorem and delete the now-unnecessary bespoke modular-row arguments in the C₃ and A₄ completeness proofs. No obsolete theorem or compatibility wrapper remains.

Reuse `ConjClasses.card_carrier_cast_ne_zero`, `ne_zero_of_dvd_ne_zero`, the existing exact conversion and orthogonality identities, and `Cyclotomic.reduceRingHom` at conjugate primitive roots. The general argument extends the existing rational solver's integer-row proof. Dixon's 1967 character-table algorithm is cited in the new module. No Mathlib infrastructure is vendored, and no material is derived from the supplementary source snapshot.

Read the shared review protocol and all ten rubrics: scope, correctness, reuse, attribution, api-design, generality, placement, naming, documentation, and proof-quality. Self-review found no existing replacement for the modular reduction result, removed the redundant integer proof, and weakened the target-ring assumption from `IsDomain` to `NoZeroDivisors`, since nonvanishing of the group order supplies all the required nontriviality. The existing examples consume the strengthened completeness API. Foreground Mathlib cache retrieval, full library build, and axiom audit pass, as do scoped environment lint, source-style checks, and the dot-notation check.

author: mivek
body:
## Problem

The v1.0.0 GHCR image contains only `linux/amd64`. On an arm64 Raspberry Pi node, the exporter immediately exits with `exec /usr/local/bin/python: exec format error`, leaving the Prometheus scrape target at `up=0`.

## Change

- Build and publish one manifest list with `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` variants for each semantic-release version and `latest` tag.
- Initialize QEMU and Buildx in CI; build both platforms in the PR test job.
- Document the published architectures.

## Validation

- Four Python unit tests passed.
- Workflow YAML and shell syntax checks passed.
- A mocked publish run produced one Buildx command with both platforms and the versioned and `latest` tags.
- The PR CI multi-platform build will validate the image before merge.

After merge, semantic-release should publish a patch release. The homelab Deployment should then move from the amd64-only v1.0.0 image to that release and remove its temporary amd64 node selector.

body:
## Summary

- add fixed Kakao OAuth callbacks with atomic state and browser binding for external login and explicit identity linking
- add ten-minute external signup tickets with claim, idempotent complete, and interaction resume for passwordless Auth users
- protect external IdP client secrets with the existing AES-256-GCM adapter, fail closed on plaintext/corrupted values, and backfill legacy values during the compiled migration runner
- widen `identity_provider.client_secret` to 2048 characters for encrypted valid 255-character multibyte secrets
- release the linked Auth workspaces as `0.3.0`

## Security boundaries

- Auth receives no CI, DI, DI HMAC, terms, or consumer-domain identity payload
- unlinked Kakao identities do not create users before the service provisioning flow completes
- existing-account linking requires an authenticated Auth session and browser-bound callback
- redirect URIs remain exact registered values; OAuth state is server-controlled and one-time
- provider secrets and tokens are never returned or logged
- the pre-registered `gaegaeting-dev` Kakao provider remains disabled until the 0.3.0 migration and rollout are verified

## Migrations

- `Migration20261005000000`: external signup completion persistence
- `Migration20261005010000`: widen IdP client-secret ciphertext storage
- `dist/cli/migrate.js` applies schema migrations, then idempotently protects legacy IdP secrets with `JWKS_ENCRYPTION_KEY`

Operational order is migration Job first, then API/worker rollout using the same immutable service image digest. The provider is activated separately after all ready pods support `enc:v1`, the runtime key and stored ciphertext are verified, and exact-origin credentialed CORS succeeds.

## Verification

- pinned Node 24.13.1, Yarn 4.12.0, TypeScript 5.9.3
- focused security/migration/container tests: 5 suites, 60 tests passed
- isolated main-based release candidate: 178 suites, 1,774 tests passed; 23 opt-in tests skipped

- user E2E: 15/15 passed

- TypeScript 5.9.3 check passed; architecture: 468 modules, 1,365 dependencies
- changed-file ESLint/Prettier and `git diff --check` passed

## Consumer dependency

The external signup Account/UI integration is deployed separately after this Auth release and provider activation. RP-initiated logout remains isolated in PR #35 and is intentionally not part of this change.

자율 개선 에이전트가 생성한 PR입니다. (run 2026-10-05-211728-umm-improve, base 6aaf940)

## 2026-10-05
- 선택: 이름 없는 공간의 대체 이름이 한국어 UI 에서도 영어 `My Space` 로 뜨고 내려받기 파일 이름에까지 들어간다 (가치 3 / 위험 1 / 작업량 S)
- 결과: 성공

author: pme123
body:
Workers can require roles for the synchronous call through `/worker/{topic}`, e.g. a UI calling through the gateway. Callers without one of them get **403** and the worker does not run.

```scala
class KontenWorker extends CompanyCustomWorkerDsl[In, Out]:
  override def requiredRoles = Set("kundenberater")
```

## Changes
- **`WorkerDsl.requiredRoles`** (default empty: every caller with a valid token). The user of the Bearer token needs at least one of the roles; names are compared exactly.
  - Only for the synchronous call. A job of a process engine runs with the identity of the engine; who may start or advance the process is decided there.
- **Fails closed.**
  - While tokens are not verified, a worker with roles refuses every call; `WorkerApp` warns at startup.
  - Whether tokens are verified is decided by the new `TokenValidation.verifies`: an exhaustive match on the sealed trait, used by `WorkerRoutes`, `WorkerApp` and `PersistenceWorkerDsl`.
  - A malformed role claim gives no roles → 403.
  - A failing `rolesOf` (e.g. the IdP is down), or one that takes longer than `WorkerConfig.rolesTimeout` (default 5 s), → **503**, logged as error with its cause, so it is distinguishable from "no role". The worker does not run either way. An interruption (the request was cancelled) is passed on, not turned into 503.
- **`WorkerConfig.rolesOf(token)`** – the roles of the user. It runs on the blocking pool, because an override may do blocking IO. `rolesTimeout` is a hard bound: the call is disconnected, so the 503 comes in time even if an override ignores the interrupt. An override that asks the IdP should cache the roles per token or subject. The default `RoleClaims` reads:
  - `roles` (app roles of Entra ID)
  - `realm_access.roles` (Keycloak realm roles)
  - `resource_access.{client}.roles` only for `WorkerConfig.roleClients` (default none), so a role of another app does not count

  Override it for another IdP.
- **Audience.** App and realm roles hold for every token of the issuer. To accept only tokens issued for this app, set the `audience` of `TokenValidation.Jwt` (in Keycloak: an audience mapper on the client). This is documented on `requiredRoles` and `RoleClaims`.
- **`WorkerRoutes`** checks after token validation and before the worker runs. The 403 says only `Not allowed to call worker '…'`; the required roles and the token fingerprint go to the log.
- **`WorkerEndpoints`**: a 403 and a 503 variant. Before, an error code without its own variant went out as 400, and every 5xx as 500; the gateway already passes any status through.

## Compatibility
- New members only, all with defaults (`requiredRoles`, `rolesOf`, `roleClients`, `rolesTimeout`); existing workers and configs compile and behave unchanged.
- `TokenValidation.verifies` is a new member with an implementation; the 403 and 503 variants only add statuses.

## Tests
- **`WorkerRolesSpec` (19)** runs with **verified tokens**: its own JWKS endpoint as a scoped layer, and RSA-signed tokens.
  - `RoleClaims`: app and realm roles; client roles only for configured clients; all three together; malformed claims → no roles.
  - `TokenValidation.verifies` for all kinds.
  - Routes:
    - with the role → 200
    - without it → 403; a counter proves the worker did not run, and the roles are not in the answer
    - one of several roles is enough
    - a client role counts only for a configured client
    - a malformed claim → 403
    - a token without any role claim → 403
    - a failing `rolesOf` → 503, and the cause stays out of the answer
    - a hanging one ends after `rolesTimeout` with 503, also one that ignores interrupts
    - `AnyOf` verifies as well
    - with an audience, a token issued for another app → 401, even with the role
    - an unknown topic → 404, before any role check
    - without verified tokens → 403 (fails closed)
    - no `requiredRoles` → 200
- **Totals:** `engine/test` 23, `worker/test` 104, `gateway/test` 56, `persistencePostgres/test` 28; `companyCheck` green.
- **End to end** in [z9nai/orch-platform `preview/`](https://github.com/z9nai/orch-platform/tree/main/preview) (Keycloak, gateway, worker app, Postgres in docker compose), with audience `esprit-preview` required:
  - `anna.berater` (with `kundenberater`) gets 200
  - `beat.test` (without it) gets 403 on every worker
  - a correctly signed token of another client of the same realm (`admin-cli`) is rejected with 401 ("The Claim 'aud' is not present")

body:
## Summary

Repositions the site to serve **both audiences** now that OST Consultancy is re-registered as a ZZP eenmanszaak: freelance clients/intermediaries **and** recruiters for senior internal roles. Previously the site read as a job-seeker CV ("Seeking a ... position", primary CTA = Download CV).

## Changes

- **New Services section** (between About and Experience): Solution & Enterprise Architecture, Senior JVM Engineering, Cloud Migration & Platform, AI-Assisted Delivery. The site previously never said what OST *does* for clients.
- **About copy** — dropped the job-seeker framing ("Seeking a Software Engineer / Solution Architect position") in favour of neutral availability wording that works for both audiences.
- **Hero CTAs** — primary is now **Work with OST** (→ #services); **Download CV** stays as the secondary recruiter path. Nav gains a Services link.
- **AI repositioned** from identity to leverage: `AI & Emerging Tech` → `AI-Assisted Engineering`; `AI Agent Development` → `LLM Integration` / `Agent Workflows`. The JVM / distributed-systems core stays as the anchor so recruiter keyword searches (Scala architect, JVM engineer) still land.
- **Meta alignment** — title, meta description, og:title and the hero typing strings all updated to "Senior Solution Architect & Software Engineer".
- **Company identity** — contact section gains a Company line; footer gains a KvK placeholder (number pending, expected within days). No BTW placeholder.
- **Responsive** — services grid: 4 / 2 / 1 columns.

## Verification

- Served locally (`python3 -m http.server`), confirmed the Services section renders as a grid with 4 cards, nav link works, hero CTA resolves to #services, footer line renders.
- HTML tag balance checked programmatically (section/div/p/h3/span/footer/nav all balanced).

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Fill the KvK number in the footer once issued, then add BTW-id later.
- Optional: **case studies / outcomes** section (anonymized wins) and **company email on the domain** instead of gmail — both flagged in discussion but out of scope here.

Screenshots/review welcome — no merge.

body:
First Light (`itaipu-1`) pass 2: the list pass 1 left, each item verified on main (6812a7e4 and later) before anything was built. No screenshots committed; pictures are in `~/Desktop/fdfpv-loop/first-light/pass2/` (before/after of the full run, the explosion views, the film frames).

## What was found and done

| # | Pass 1 said | Verified on main | Done |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Countdown camera inside the Striker, freestyle overlays | True. It was the pad shot (the orbit and dolly into the FPV lens) whose radii are a quad's, so round the Striker it sat in the fuselage for 4 s; "Flying Acro" was the tune swap's notice; the "Air" airtime clock was the plain OSD, up whenever the Avionics HUD was not (the pad shot, a chase camera, a wreck: it read "Air 2:42" over the loss) | A war skips the pad shot; the tune notice is not said in a war room (the war's own "you are in the Striker" line now shows instead); `#ui.war-on` hides the OSD clock from the briefing until the room is back in its lobby |
| 2 | Take-off hint all mission, over the loss banner | True, and over the loss it was also "Wrecked. R back to the pad" (the parked Striker had been hit), with the last hits' calls showing through the banner's scrim and "OUTPUT UNDER 7 / 700 MW" wrapped | The take-off line holds through the countdown and the war's first 30 s; no flight banner under a won, lost or ended war; the calls hide under the end banner; the floor is kept on one line (mw()'s thin space is a break; the banner uses a narrow no-break space) |
| 3 | Music picker top left in a war | True ("Gritty Breakbeats" while the war's own music played) | Hidden from the briefing until the room is back in its lobby (the Music row under Pilot still sets the level) |
| 4 | "Flying Itaipu (in development)" in the lobby | True. The tag was part of the map's name since its skeleton commit, whose note said the dam, towns and forests were to come; all three are built and the released mission flies on it | Name "Itaipu" / "Itaipú", note describes the map as it is. Every place the map is named changes (title, loading screen, Flight Club), not only the war: say if the tag should stay outside wars |
| 5 | Other pilots show their old aircraft | True: the lobby named this pilot's seat by `warCraftOf` and the others' by their profile's last-flown airframe | Off the air (no poses) in a war room the profile names the war aircraft; in the air it is what flies. Client only: the room passes the airframe through |
| 6 | Dark half disc in the water under a low explosion | True, reproduced (new `water` view). Cause: Itaipu's mirror is drawn without the sky and reads its alpha as how much shore it holds; the additive pool blended an alpha of 1 in, so the glow quad took the sky out of the reflection | Additive pool blends One, One for colour and leaves the alpha; the main picture is the same |
| 7 | Step at the fireball's edge in front of a wall | Not found. The `wall` view (fireball 25 m in front of the face 400 m out) cannot show one, so a `face` view puts it 90 m from the lens with the face 360 m behind: no step at the rim. Seen instead: the flipbook quad's bottom is cut straight where it goes under the water, a low fireball reads with a flat base (0.08 to 0.7 s). Not changed here; it wants a soft fade against the depth | `water`, `wall` and `face` views added to explosion-shots |
| 8 | wave contacts ~64 px, defenders not seen; line deck overexposed | True: 63.7 to 83 px; the defenders climbed due north, 12 degrees off the long lens's axis, above the frame until its last second (measured from film.js's own camera); line's deck filled half the frame, near white | wave: **two** contacts (was three) under a 540 mm lens, 115 to 164 px (`minPx` 60 to 110, a tightening), look lowered onto them, the defenders fly out along the lens's axis and rise into frame over the last four seconds; the high and west groups' anchors moved to when the narrower lens holds them. line: 0.3 m over the deck on a 75 mm lens down the row, under a new graduated grade `warm-grad`: deck rows 106 to 119 of 255 (were 132 to 154). author: sbihaiko
body:
## What

#861 released a `DynamicCroppedBitmap` when a picture was **replaced**, but a tooltip discarded **whole** still leaked its last entry's subscription. Both drop shapes in the tree leak: popup sites clear the tip (`X = null`) and inline preview panels drop their `ContentControl`. The source `ViewerBitmap` keeps one handler per discarded tooltip.

Fixes #872.

## How

`DynamicTooltip` now owns the release — it implements `IDisposable` and disposes every `TooltipEntry` it holds, so no caller needs to know which entry owns a subscription. Two automatic triggers cover both drop shapes with **no edit at any drop site**:

- **Popup tooltips** funnel through `TooltipHelper`: `HideTooltip` disposes the tip it clears, and `ShowTooltip` disposes a tip it replaces — reference-checked, so a tooltip re-shown as the same instance is never torn down.
- **Inline preview panels** are bound to a `ContentControl`; dropping one removes the control from the visual tree, so `OnDetachedFromVisualTree` disposes. The existing `X = null` pattern therefore releases on its own.

Only what the entry created is released: `TooltipPictureEntry` wraps the caller's shared source in its own `DynamicCroppedBitmap`, and only that cropped bitmap is detached — never the shared `ViewerBitmap`. `Detach()` is idempotent, so the popup's double path (detach + `HideTooltip`) is safe. `DynamicCroppedBitmap.cs` is untouched, BOMs intact.

## RED

Both new tests present, both source files reverted to their pre-fix state:

```
  Failed Mesen.HeadlessTests.DynamicTooltipBitmapLeakTests.Hiding_a_popup_tooltip_releases_its_picture_subscription [454 ms]
  Error Message:
   Assert.Equal() Failure: Values differ
Expected: 0
Actual:   1
  Stack Trace:
     at Mesen.HeadlessTests.DynamicTooltipBitmapLeakTests.Hiding_a_popup_tooltip_releases_its_picture_subscription() in UI.HeadlessTests/DynamicTooltipBitmapLeakTests.cs:line 126
...
  Failed Mesen.HeadlessTests.DynamicTooltipBitmapLeakTests.Discarding_the_tooltip_whole_releases_its_last_picture_subscription [8 ms]
  Error Message:
   Assert.Equal() Failure: Values differ
Expected: 0
Actual:   1
  Stack Trace:
     at Mesen.HeadlessTests.DynamicTooltipBitmapLeakTests.Discarding_the_tooltip_whole_releases_its_last_picture_subscription() in UI.HeadlessTests/DynamicTooltipBitmapLeakTests.cs:line 104

Failed!  - Failed:     2, Passed:     2, Skipped:     0, Total:     4, Duration: 616 ms - UI.HeadlessTests.dll (net10.0)
```

## GREEN

```
$ MESEN_CORE_LIB=<main checkout>/bin/osx-arm64/Release/MesenCore.dylib \
  dotnet test UI.HeadlessTests/UI.HeadlessTests.csproj -p:RuntimeIdentifier=osx-arm64 \
  --filter "FullyQualifiedName~DynamicTooltipBitmapLeakTests"
Passed!  - Failed:     0, Passed:     4, Skipped:     0, Total:     4, Duration: 302 ms - UI.HeadlessTests.dll (net10.0)
```

`NativeCoreCollectionGuardTests`: `Passed! - Failed: 0, Passed: 4, Skipped: 0`.

The two tests need a visual tree, so they live in `UI.HeadlessTests` rather than `UI.Tests` (per `UI.HeadlessTests/AGENTS.md`, host-free rule assertions belong in `UI.Tests`; a window-hosted tooltip is not that). They run with `MESEN_CORE_LIB` set — 0 skipped is the point, since the headless suite otherwise passes vacuously.

## Found, not fixed

`TileEditorWindow.ShowColorTooltip` and `PaletteSelector._tooltip` reuse one tooltip instance after a hide, which now disposes it. Both are palette-only (`PaletteHelper.GetPreviewPanel` adds no `<picture>`), so `Dispose()` is a no-op there and reuse still repopulates. If a future change gives either a picture, reuse after a hide would need re-subscribing.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


---

## Review response (commit `2f37c7d1c`)

An independent adversarial review (CodeRabbit came back rate-limited on this PR)
enumerated **every** site that drops a `DynamicTooltip` and checked each against
the two triggers. CodeRabbit never landed, so this pass stood in as the gate.

**Confirmed:**

- **No drop site is missed.** Every popup site funnels through `TooltipHelper`
  (`IMouseOverViewerModel.cs:50,58`, `SpriteViewerViewModel.cs:468`,
  `MemoryMappingViewer.cs:122,130`, `PaletteSelector.cs:324,331`,
  `CodeViewerSelectionHandler.cs:135`, `EventViewerWindow.axaml.cs:90,114`,
  `MemoryToolsWindow.axaml.cs:137`, `PaletteViewerWindow.axaml.cs:63,83`,
  `TileEditorWindow.axaml.cs:73,80,106,112`); every inline site assigns a
  `ContentControl`-bound property, so the detach hook fires
  (`TileViewerViewModel.cs:286,453`, `TilemapViewerViewModel.cs:432,567`,
  `SpriteViewerViewModel.cs:677`, `PaletteViewerViewModel.cs:208`). No `X = null`
  site bypasses both.
- **`Detach()` is idempotent** (`DynamicCroppedBitmap.cs:45-55`) — double
  dispose 1→0→0, no exception.
- **The palette reuse-after-hide is genuinely safe.** `PaletteHelper.GetPreviewPanel`
  builds only `AddEntry` values and `TooltipColorEntry`, which is
  `ObservableObject`, not `IDisposable`, so `TooltipEntry.Dispose` is a no-op
  there. No picture entry reaches those tooltips.
- **Dispose reaches Detach**: `DynamicTooltip.Dispose` → `TooltipEntry.Dispose`
  → `TooltipPictureEntry.Dispose` → `_croppedSource.Detach()`. Only the entry's
  own cropped bitmap; `ViewerBitmap` is never touched. `Items` is null-guarded and
  is not mutated during the loop.
- **Test placement is right** — `DynamicTooltip` is a `UserControl` and the
  behaviour under test is a visual-tree event, which `UI.Tests` is host-free by
  construction and cannot assert without a refactor. The class pre-dates this PR
  (#861), so this only appends.
- **GREEN and RED reproduced independently**: `Passed: 4, Skipped: 0`; with the
  `HEAD~1` sources in place, `Failed: 2` — exactly the two new tests.

**Two latent hazards, neither reachable today, both now recorded at the site:**

1. **One instance, two targets.** Handing the same tooltip to a second target
   disposes subscriptions it may still need on the first. The mechanism is *not*
   the reference check — it is `OnDetachedFromVisualTree` firing as the instance
   leaves the first target's popup, which the check cannot see because it reads
   the **new** target's previous tip. Every call site uses one target per
   instance. Recorded in `TooltipHelper.ShowTooltip` so a future change re-shows
   instead of re-hosting.
2. **A host that never enters a visual tree** makes the detach hook a silent
   no-op. Proven by probe; no live picture-bearing site does it today
   (`PaletteViewerViewModel.PreviewPanel` is the one inline host that can stay
   unrealised, and its content is palette-only).
