author: raulmoracode
body:
## OpenType feature detection and Features view

> **Do not merge yet.** Stacked series — merge in order with the previous PRs.

Parses the `GSUB` and `GPOS` layout tables so the app can report which
OpenType features a font **actually** implements, rather than assuming a
standard set is present.

**Parser**
- Script and language systems, feature tags, and the lookup types each feature
  points at
- Walks each lookup's subtables instead of trusting the directory, including
  extension lookups (type 7)
- A lookup that cannot be walked is reported as unknown, never guessed
- A damaged layout table no longer invalidates the rest of the font

**View**
- Every implemented feature with its registered description, the table it
  comes from, and its lookups
- Unregistered tags are labelled `custom` rather than described
- Script systems and lookup types listed per table
- Fonts with no `GSUB`/`GPOS` say so in one plain sentence

The `ss01`–`ss20` and `cv01`–`cv99` series are generated by pattern instead of
being listed one by one.

### Validation

`pnpm check`, `pnpm test` (36 passing, +3 new) and `pnpm build` all pass.

The in-memory fixture gained a real `GSUB` table with three features wired to
three different lookup types, built with computed offsets. Three tests cover
it: a font with no layout tables, the declared features, and — importantly —
an assertion that six common features the font does **not** declare
(`smcp`, `onum`, `tnum`, `frac`, `calt`, `ss02`) never appear.

Writing the fixture caught two bugs this PR fixes: `ss01` was missing from the
registered-feature table, and a `scriptOffset` in the fixture that overlapped
its own record.

author: danbarker
body:
Dan wants to type text or paste a link, then record a voice note, and have both reach the agent as **one** message. Today on web the typed draft stays in the field and the voice note goes out on its own. Spec: https://github.com/Matronhq/matron-bridge/pull/375 (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-05-voice-note-with-draft.md`).

### Changes
- `sendVoiceNote` takes an optional `caption` (trimmed; nothing is sent when it is blank). It rides as `payload.caption` on the voice note's `file` event, the same field image and file captions already use.
- The composer passes the typed draft as that caption when the recording is sent. The draft clears once the voice note is in the outbox, using the same unchanged-draft check as the send button. If the voice note can't be saved, or the recording is discarded, the draft stays.
- No caption is attached when a text send of the same draft is already in flight, or when the recording finishes after switching to another conversation.
- The caption already renders under the file tile (`mj_FileCaption`).
- Photos on web still go through the confirm dialog. Web has no attachment tray, so the photo + voice batch is an Apple and Android feature.

### Merge order
Merge after the bridge PR has rolled out. An older bridge ignores the caption on a voice note, so the typed text would be lost.

### Tests
- New cases in `composer-voice-test.ts`: draft sent and cleared; kept when the save fails; kept when the recording is discarded; no caption when the draft is empty.
- New case in `client-test.ts`: caption trimming.
- `pnpm lint` and `pnpm test` pass (1339 tests).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches outbox/upload and draft persistence in the message composer; wrong caption or draft timing could drop user text or double-send, though behavior mirrors existing text-send paths.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Voice notes from the composer can now carry the trimmed text in the draft as a caption**, so the agent receives typed text (or a pasted link) and the recording in one turn, using the same `caption` field as file/image attachments.
> 
> `sendVoiceNote` accepts an optional `caption` and forwards it to `sendAttachment`. The composer reads the live draft when recording is sent (via `bodyRef`), skips the caption if a text send is already in flight or the conversation changed, and **reuses shared `clearSentDraft` / `restoreDraft` helpers** with the normal send button: the draft clears when the send starts and comes back if the voice note fails to save; discard leaves the draft untouched.
> 
> Unit and composer voice tests cover trimming, empty captions, early draft clear, failure restore without overwriting new typing, and discard behavior.

author: syn7xx
body:
## What and why

With the plugin loaded, the built-in `question` tool stopped rendering in the parent/main client window: the form was emitted but the option list never appeared, so the session hung. Reproduced in an ordinary session with no Workflow running — merely having the plugin connected was enough.

Root cause: the plugin wrapped the built-in `question` tool with `ctx.tool.transform` → `editor.update("question", …)`. On OpenCode 2.0.23 that makes `form.created` fire **without a `location`**. A location-scoped client (every ordinary session) then drops the form, so the options never render. Even a no-op update triggered it; `editor.update("bash", …)` and `editor.add(…)` did not.

The fix stops transforming `question` globally:

- adds a dedicated `workflow_question` tool that routes a Unit's questions through the Run's broker (broker-routed, so the answer reaches whatever surface is watching — TUI, web, or any RPC client — instead of a blocking native form);
- in the `context` hook, hides `workflow_question` outside Unit sessions and hides the native `question` inside Units;
- pushes a `QUESTION_INSTRUCTION` to Units and allows `workflow_question` / denies `question` in `ENGINE_UNIT_RULES`;
- drops the now-unneeded `execute.after` fallback hook.

Ordinary sessions keep the untouched native `question`, so its form renders with the full `location`.

## How I tested it

- `bun run check` — format, lint, typecheck, 292 tests, 0 fail.
- Live, through a symlinked checkout plugin on a real OpenCode 2.0.23 (Linux):
  - ordinary session: `/question`… native `question` renders options in the TUI ("1. Red / 2. Blue / 3. Type your own answer"); `form.created` carries `location={directory:"/tmp/wf-repro"}`.
  - headless Unit: `workflow_question` reports nobody available and the Unit proceeds (`COLOUR=none`).
  - attached Unit: answering the broker interaction via `replyInteraction` returns the answer (`COLOUR=Blue`).

## Checklist

- [x] The title follows [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix:`)
- [x] `bun run check` passes
- [x] Protocol changes are additive and the schemas are regenerated (`bun run schemas` — no diff)
- [x] Docs (README, skill, protocol) updated if behavior or options changed

author: daniduwijendra
body:
## Purpose
Comments of type `WORK_NOTE` are the support team's internal notes. The customer portal backend already leaves them out of the case timeline in Go, but the `comment` row-level-security policies only checked project membership, so the database itself did not distinguish them. Anything that reads comments without that Go filter, and the activity total (counted before the filter), treated them like any other comment.

## Goals
- The comment policies agree with the portal backend: for an external caller, a work note is not readable, writable or re-typable.
- Internal callers, the announcement child-row rules and customer comments behave as before.
- Customer-triggered requests that record an internal note keep working.

## Approach
- **Migration `0191_comment_work_notes_internal_only.sql`**: `ALTER POLICY` on `comment_visibility`, `comment_write` and `comment_update` adds `comment.type IS DISTINCT FROM 'WORK_NOTE'` to the external branch (one transaction, safe to re-run). Internal callers short-circuit on the first branch. A NULL type stays visible, as in the portal backend today. `comment_edit_history` follows through its join on `comment`; `comment_delete_internal_only` is already internal-only.
- **Two internal writes go through a system-identity operation**, because they would otherwise be refused for the customer who triggered them:
  - the case work note recorded after an escalation is created (`caseEscalationService.CreateCaseEscalation`), through the new `CaseService.CreateInternalCaseComment`;
  - the mirror of ServiceNow's initial comments on case creation (`caseService.mirrorInitialSNComments`, dual-write), through the new `CaseRepository.CreateCaseCommentAsSystem`, which keeps ServiceNow's original timestamps.
  The identity is stamped in the repository (`CreateCaseCommentAsSystem` wraps `CreateCaseComment`), not in the service layer, like the other system writes. The service layer passes the caller's context down unchanged, and the escalation and the case creation themselves still run under the caller's identity. Both operations are used only by those two call sites (no route reaches them), and both act on a case the caller has just escalated or created (the escalation path authorises the case first).
- **Read side effects for external callers** beyond the portal timeline: the comment counts and first-message lookup in conversation message stats, and the case activity totals, no longer include work notes. This is intended.

## Automation tests
- Unit tests: the escalation note uses the internal operation and the escalation keeps the caller's identity; the case-creation mirror uses the system repository method with ServiceNow's timestamps; the ordinary and internal comment operations each reach only their own repository method; a failing note does not fail the escalation. Each was checked to fail when the behaviour is broken (wrong operation, system identity ignored or always used, timestamp dropped).
- Integration tests (`comment_work_note_rls_integration_test.go`, `CASE_STATS_TEST_DSN`): member vs internal vs outsider for read (list and by id), insert (plain and in the exact `INSERT ... SELECT FROM work_item` shape `CreateCaseComment` uses), update, re-typing a comment to a work note, a comment with no type, edit history read and write, the system-identity write, and the real `CreateCaseComment` / `CreateCaseCommentAsSystem` repository methods under a member's identity. Against a scratch Postgres built from the migrations the tests that assert the restriction fail before the migration and pass after it. The announcement visibility integration tests pass before and after, and no other repository test changed result.

## Security checks
 - Followed secure coding standards in http://wso2.com/technical-reports/wso2-secure-engineering-guidelines? Not separately reviewed
 - Ran FindSecurityBugs plugin and verified report? N/A (Go)
 - Confirmed that this PR doesn't commit any keys, passwords, tokens, usernames, or other secrets? yes

## Migrations
**Deploy entity-service first, then apply `0191`.** Applying the migration first makes two best-effort writes fail with a permission error until the new build is live: the escalation work note and the mirrored ServiceNow work notes. Both are only logged and do not fail the request, so those notes would be lost silently. The new build works under the old policies. Tested on PostgreSQL 17 built from the migrations, applied twice.

## Test environment
Go, PostgreSQL 17 (Docker), macOS.

## Related PRs
Independent of the other open `0190_*` migrations (#2368, #2377, #2313); touches only the `comment` policies. Overlaps in `case_service.go` with #1673, #1714 and #2314 add no new merge conflicts.

author: noelkirthiraj
body:
## What happened

Pressing **Search web** on an accepted tender took the whole dashboard offline with `502 Application failed to respond`. The Mission Control stats showing zeros were a symptom of the same outage — `loadData()` swallows fetch failures and falls back to the empty state.

`api.py` ran a plain `HTTPServer`, which serves **one request at a time**. The new external-supplier search calls Claude web search synchronously inside the request handler, and that takes 30–120 seconds. For the whole of that window the server answered nothing — including Railway's `/api/health` probe, so the health check failed and Railway restarted the container.

This was my own oversight. The supplier scope said *"matching is SQL only and runs in well under a second, so unlike PO extraction there is no async job to poll"* — true of the registry match — and I then put web search on that same synchronous path without revisiting the reasoning. `po_jobs.py` exists because PR #61 hit this exact symptom.

## The fix is two changes, because the obvious half alone makes it worse

**1. `ThreadingHTTPServer`** with `daemon_threads` for clean shutdown.

**2. A lock around the shared asyncio loop.** A single loop cannot be driven concurrently, and the asyncpg pool is bound to the loop that created it — so a loop per thread would strand the pool.

Threading *without* the lock would have traded an outage for data corruption. Measured against the pre-fix code path, 16 concurrent callers produced **2 correct results and 14 `RuntimeError: This event loop is already running`**.

Database work therefore still serialises, which is fine at this scale. What matters is that it's *only* the database: the slow third-party call happens outside the lock, so it no longer stalls the health probe or anything else.

## Tests

9 new (497 total). They use the real `APIHandler` on a real socket rather than mocks, because the thing that broke was socket-level behaviour:

- health answers in **under 2s while the loop lock is held** — the actual regression
- 10 concurrent requests served in parallel, not serialised
- 16 threads through `_run_async` each get their own correct result
- the lock is released when a handler raises, so one failure can't wedge every later request
- `test_server_is_threaded` fails if anyone reverts to `HTTPServer`

## Follow-up, not in this PR

Moving external search onto the existing `po_jobs` async pattern would let the browser poll instead of holding a 2-minute request open. Worth doing — but threading turns that from an outage into an optimisation, so it isn't urgent.

author: changhansung
body:
Closes #1205.

## Bug

After a restart, `finishTargetReconciliation` looks for each in-flight delivery's `[agend-delivery-id:…]` marker in the CLI's transcript, and `transcriptDeltaHasDeliveryMarker` only accepted a marker at the very start of a user entry. Claude Code persists every pasted message as `"\n\n<pasted_content id=\"<hex>\">\n" + text` — **all 640** delivery entries in 28 real transcripts (2.1.284–2.1.289, small and large pastes alike) look like that, and none starts with the marker. So for claude-code the marker was never found: a delivered message looked like *complete transcript, no marker* and, with the old CLI gone (`idle_submit`, pid dead), `finishTargetReconciliation` chose `retry_wait` — the message is sent again. (Codex is fine: 431 of 434 entries lead with the marker; the 3 others are pre-#1197 steer entries.)

## Fix

`leadsWithMarker`: the CLI's own wrapper, `^\s*<pasted_content id="<hex>">\r?\n`, is allowed in front of the marker — **claude-code only**, exact shape — and the marker must still lead the body inside it. No wider prefix: a quote, a mention, text before the tag, a different tag or id shape, another delivery's marker, or any other backend's entry still does not count.

## Tests
- Matcher: wrapper accepted (both real shapes); only the exact wrapper (text/other tag/other id shape/bare tag/text *before* the tag all refused); marker must lead inside it; Codex gets no allowance; first-user-text rule unchanged.

author: vancinis
body:
﻿## Summary

OpenCode V2 changed the plugin API, so the current V1-only plugin cannot load there. This PR makes one package work on both hosts:

- **OpenCode V1 >= 1.18.29** via `server()`
- **OpenCode V2 2.0.22** via `setup()`

The default export is one object with a stable plugin ID and both entrypoints. Each host gets a thin adapter (`src/v1.ts`, `src/v2.ts`). The header, system-prompt, tool-casing and SSE streaming logic moved into a shared `src/transport.ts`, so neither adapter duplicates it.

## Changes

- **V1:** behavior is unchanged. The plugin still prefers Claude CLI credentials and falls back to its own OAuth flow, with the same retries. The token cache now belongs to each plugin instance instead of the whole module, and the refresh timer stops when the plugin is disposed.
- **V2:** adds **Claude Pro/Max** as an integration OAuth method and keeps the API-key methods. OpenCode resolves, refreshes and stores tokens for the selected account. The adapter does not read Claude CLI credential files.
- **Anthropic HTTP hooks on V2:** they apply only when the outgoing bearer matches the selected OAuth account. API-key requests, non-SSE responses and error responses pass through untouched.
  - Request-only bodies, methods and signals are kept.
  - Rewritten response streams are cancelled when the request is aborted or the plugin unloads.
  - A response is rewritten according to the request that was sent, even if the user switched accounts before it came back.
- **Pricing:** model pricing is zeroed only while an OAuth account is active, and account events reload it.
- **Packaging:** both `@opencode-ai/plugin` and `@opencode/plugin@2.0.22` are optional peers and are imported as types only. A V1 install does not need the V2 SDK, and a V2 install does not need the V1 SDK.
- **Custom endpoints:** the policy is unchanged. A configured custom Anthropic endpoint still receives the OAuth bearer, as it does today. The README says this explicitly.
- **README:** install instructions for V2 (`plugins`) and V1 (`plugin`), a table of host and credential behavior, and a guide to running the tests.

## Tests

Adds an offline suite using Node's built-in test runner (`npm test`). It runs against synthetic credentials, mocked `fetch`, a fake home directory and a fake clock and timers. It never reads real credentials or touches the network.

- OAuth exchange and refresh
- V1 regression coverage
- The dual entrypoint
- V2 hook registration, account switching, API-key passthrough, split UTF-8/SSE chunks, cancellation and cleanup
- A package test that runs `npm pack`, installs the tarball in a throwaway consumer and imports it without either host SDK installed

Result: `npm test` passes 34/34 on Node 26.9.0 / npm 11.19.1.

The V1 and V2 hosts were also tested manually with a real login and real requests to Anthropic. Everything worked.

## Notes

- Only V2 **2.0.22** has been checked. Other V2 releases have not been tested.
- The V2 host must support the standard Fetch APIs and `AbortSignal.any`.
- `package-lock.json` grows mostly because of the V2 SDK dev dependency.

author: samienne
body:
Routes `lw reset [<profile> | --all] [-y]` through the workspace daemon (spec 19.15 "Reset", 16.30; step 5d). Three commits: the approved spec draft, phase A (host-neutral `reset_plan.lua`), phase B (routing).

## Protocol 9
- Request `reset { args = { profile?, all?, yes?, plan? }, interactive, env, command }`.
- Outcomes: `refused` (nothing to reset: exit 0 + `stream = "out"`; changed plan: `the build directories to reset changed since they were listed - run lw reset again`, exit 1), `declined`, `confirm { lines, plan, profile_key? }` (no lock, nothing changed), `accepted { task_id, profile_key?, pid }`.
- Task `start` meta `{ kind = "reset", profile?, scope = "all"?, name = <profile>|"--all", units }`; the `status` reply's `tasks` carry `scope`.

## Client
Without `-y`: first request -> `confirm` -> listing printed, question asked (non-interactive: the in-process refusal; declined: `aborted`), then a second request with `yes` + the token. The daemon re-plans and refuses a changed plan. If the second request cannot be routed (daemon stopped / retired), `cmd_reset(..., { plan = token })` runs in-process without asking again and refuses a changed plan. `-y`: accepted at once, the task prints the listing. `lw: resetting through the workspace daemon (pid N)` is printed on acceptance.

## Daemon
`runner.reset`: workspace operation lock, then exclusive build-directory locks of the plan's lock set (record operation `reset`, shared `take_locks` with build/test/run/clean), then `reset_plan.execute` with the run's cancellation as the stop predicate. Locks are released only when the task ended AND the deletion settled (new `opts.settled` hook in `reset_plan.execute`), so a timed-out deletion keeps its locks. Deletion path unchanged (Profile:reset / Workspace:reset_all).

## Observer / status
`kind = reset` -> units `deleting` (fidget `Resetting`, verbs `reset` / `reset failed`); scope-`all` tasks resolve units among the workspace's config units and attach to every profile with one of them; `lw status` running row shows `--all`.

## Tests
New `tests/daemon_reset_service_spec.lua` (7) and `tests/daemon_reset_cli_spec.lua` (5, real processes, parity both ways incl. prompts via stdin, changed plan, fallback after the daemon stopped, Ctrl-C during removal); additions to `cli_reset_spec` and `cli_status_build_state_spec`; `daemon_helpers` gains stdin support. The `--all` listing is now sorted by project/configuration key (it depended on load order).

author: kims34
body:
# Late fill after zero-fill release — offline safety correction

A previously complete zero-fill cancellation snapshot can be crossed by a late fill after local principal release. The old journal retained the fill but did not restore the released reservation, allowing understated local exposure after another claim reused capacity.

Every new execution crossing a confirmed CANCELLED terminal now atomically retains the fill, restores any previously released principal once, records the revocation without deleting the original release audit, advances the capital revision, clears settlement snapshot bindings, blocks batch reconciliation and stops SHADOW. Full fills retain terminal_status=FILLED while state remains RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED until a newer complete matching batch. Duplicate executions do not restore or stop again. Later fills cannot restore twice. The whole restoration shares the native bridge transaction, so a source-binding insert failure rolls back both fill and capital changes. A direct journal persistence constraint conflict stops local claims after rollback.

Restore exposure even when it exceeds the configured ceiling: rejecting that fill would conceal the liability. Aggregate reservation reporting uses Python integer summation so representable individual reservations remain exactly reported even when the total exceeds SQLite int64. This does not increase the user ceiling or authorize over-budget claims. Existing reservation validation and fail-closed controls remain in force.

Validation: 131 offline tests, including eight new regressions covering capacity already reused, replay/restart, full late fill, atomic failure/retry, native binding rollback, cancellation without release and aggregate overflow. No provider network, broker request, stock order, sale, funds transfer, fee settlement or source/LIVE admission. No frozen model, threshold, cutoff, holdout or gate changes.

author: pablobagliere
body:
## Qué cambia

- **plugin-vue-axios 2.1.0** (minor): `HttpClient` suma la firma invocable `(config: HttpRequestConfig) => Promise<HttpResponse>`; una instancia de axios ya la cumple. Los tipos HTTP (`HttpClient`, `HttpRequestConfig`, `HttpResponse`, `HttpInterceptorManager`) se mueven a `src/http.ts` y se publican también como **`@mundoit-lib/plugin-vue-axios/http`**: sólo tipos, sin import de `axios` ni la augmentación `$axios` de Vue. Siguen exportados desde la raíz.
- **plugin-vue-auth 2.0.4** (patch): borra su `HttpClient` propio y re-exporta el del subpath con `import type`. Su `HttpRequestConfig` extiende el base con `url`, `_retry` y `_skipAuth`. `createHttp` de `test-utils.ts` cumple el contrato completo (`put/patch/delete`, `eject`).
- Tests de tipos nuevos: `http.test-d.ts` en axios (invocable, `AxiosInstance` lo cumple) y `types.test-d.ts` en auth (mismo `HttpClient`, `HttpRequestConfig` extiende al base).

## Por qué así (opción 1 del ticket, con devDependency en vez de peer)

- `@mundoit-lib/plugin-vue-axios` va en `devDependencies` (`workspace:*`) de auth, **no como peer**: una app puede usar auth con otro cliente http y no tiene por qué instalar el plugin de axios.
- tsdown bundlea las devDependencies, así que los tipos quedan **inlineados** en `dist/index.d.ts` de auth. Lo publicado no depende de plugin-vue-axios ni de axios, ni en runtime ni en tipos. `check:exports` pasa igual.
- El subpath `./http` hace falta porque inlinear `dist/index.d.ts` completo arrastraba `import ... from 'axios'` (rompe el build de auth, que no tiene axios) y la augmentación `declare module 'vue' { $axios }`, que auth no puede publicar. Además le sirve a `histrix-component-vue` para tomar el contrato sin el plugin.
- La opción 2 (paquete `@mundoit-lib/http` sólo `.d.ts`) queda descartada: un paquete más para publicar y versionar, cuando el contrato ya vive en axios.

## A tener en cuenta

- Quien haya implementado el `HttpClient` chico de auth con un cliente propio (sin `put/patch/delete` ni `eject`) deja de compilar. Con axios no cambia nada.
- `pnpm test:watch` desde la raíz necesita `pnpm build` antes (auth resuelve los tipos desde el `dist` de axios); turbo ya lo encadena con `dependsOn: ["^build"]`. Anotado en AGENTS.md.

## Checks

`pnpm lint && pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm check:exports` en verde. El `dist/index.d.ts` de auth no tiene referencias a `axios` ni `$axios`.

author: beatrice-b-m
body:
<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"beatrice-b-m"} -->
_Requested by **Bea**_

**Draft: needs a hands-on pass on a real trackpad and a real mouse before it merges. Nothing here was tried on hardware; every wheel trace in the tests is constructed, not recorded.**

Before: each wheel event was classified on its own, so a fast two-finger swipe could flip from panning to zooming halfway, and in the Scroll tool trackpad momentum ran through dozens of frames. A rectangle could only be drawn by dragging. The right button did nothing.

After:
- The viewer keeps a mouse or trackpad profile for the session. A gesture is classified once from its first events and keeps that meaning to its end, and the profile switches after two confident gestures of the other kind.
- In the Scroll tool a trackpad scroll steps one frame per 30 px and slows to a stop as the momentum tail decays; a mouse notch is still one frame. Alt+wheel steps frames in every tool.
- Right-drag zooms about the point where it started, in every tool. A right click without movement still does nothing.
- A rectangle (ROI or Redact) can be placed with two clicks: the first fixes a corner, the shape follows the pointer, the second places it, Esc cancels. Dragging works as before. A press and release that moves less than 4 screen pixels now always starts a placement and never saves, at any zoom; before, at low zoom it could save a box about one screen pixel wide.
- Handles are easier to grab in the trackpad profile (10 px instead of 8).
- Fixed: a pinch in the Scroll tool zooms instead of stepping frames; a second pointer's middle press during a ROI move no longer leaves the ROI drawn moved but unsaved; a lost pointer release no longer leaves the viewport stuck.

Owner sign-offs (`docs/design/annotation-tools-ux.md`, confirmed 2026-09-30): decision 14.4, "right-drag zooms ... with trackpad handling added (section 3.5)"; section 3.5 for the profile, frame stepping and click-click placement.

How: `lib/viewport/inputProfile.ts` is a pure classifier the tool host consults; tools never look at wheel events. The `Tool` interface gains an `armed` state so the host keeps a tool's state after release and sends it hover moves. The shared-gesture tests from the previous PR pass unchanged except the six right-button rows, which this change is meant to alter.

Not built because there is nothing to attach them to yet: a settings control for the Auto, Mouse or Trackpad override (it exists as host state), the one-time trackpad hint, cheat-sheet text, and picking up a handle with a click.

Checked: the frontend check profile (570 tests); in a real browser, a real drag placed a rectangle, two real clicks placed one, and a click followed by Esc placed nothing.

Known and for the owner to feel:
- Momentum: on constructed tails that decay slowly (0.95 to 0.97 per event) stepping overruns by five to eight frames after the fingers lift. The thresholds need a recorded trace.
- After using a mouse wheel, the first two swipes still zoom, and swipes made back to back count as one gesture.
- Ctrl+click on macOS with ROI or Redact now starts a placement.
- One piece of evidence goes beyond the design's list (the legacy wheel delta); it is recorded in `docs/architecture.md` with the cases where it can misfire.

To try by hand before merging:
- Trackpad: in the Scroll tool on a 50-frame stack, flick gently and hard and count frames after lifting; swipe right after using a mouse wheel; first swipe on a fresh page, also at browser zoom 110% and 125%; click (not tap) a first corner ten times at fit zoom on a large image; pinch in every tool; Option+two-finger scroll.
- Mouse: one notch on macOS Chrome and Firefox; a free-spinning wheel on a fresh page; right-drag with no context menu on release; Alt+wheel on Windows in Chrome, Edge and Firefox; click-click with a middle-button pan between the clicks.

author: major
body:
## Summary

Simplify the `market.ticker.cik` CHECK constraint by removing the all-digits regex that is fully subsumed by the alphanumeric pattern.

## Background

The constraint was introduced by `85ecad6` (`fix(migration): loosen cik CHECK to accept alphanumeric placeholders`) which loosened the check to accept test fixture placeholders like `public-cik`. The loosened form:

```sql
CHECK (cik IS NULL OR (length(cik) BETWEEN 1 AND 10 AND (cik ~ '^[0-9]+$' OR cik ~ '^[A-Za-z0-9-]+$')))
```

The OR clause is redundant: `^[0-9]+$` is a strict subset of `^[A-Za-z0-9-]+$`. A string that matches all digits also matches alphanumeric-plus-hyphen, so the first regex adds no value.

## Change

Reduce the CHECK to the single alphanumeric regex:

```sql
CHECK (cik IS NULL OR (length(cik) BETWEEN 1 AND 10 AND cik ~ '^[A-Za-z0-9-]+$'))
```

## Validation

- `make lint`, `make format-check`, `make typecheck` all pass.
- 247 non-postgres tests pass; the change is migration-only and does not require postgres integration tests to validate.
- The `public-cik` test fixture still passes because it matches the alphanumeric regex.

## Risk

Pre-production project; no production deployments to migrate. The simplify stack (#89) already edited this migration in place, so this follows the established pattern.

## Scope

Adds an isolated, fail-closed reader for the D101 signed Root execution result. It parses the exact §6.3 schema, checks raw SHA-256 before signature or JSON use, verifies the separate Ed25519 result domain with the trusted manifest key, and binds every operation/source/pin/reference to the stored gateway execution and dispatch intent.

The transport uses a fixed constructor origin, exact GET path, existing service bearer token source, no proxy or redirects, 16 KiB body cap, two concurrent calls with no queue, and a two-second caller deadline. C3 owns only the two new D101 source files and one new test file. C8 owns `D101ExecutionService.terminal`, configuration, storage, Root issuer, and canonical settlement. author: mxssnx-creator
body:
## What

### Engine direction acceptance (`wf.engineSideAccept`, opt-in)
- Each group of type family (Normal + Trailing, DCA, Axis) × range × side opens new entries only while its candidates' PF over the last whole hours clears `minPf`.
- It uses hourly buckets and is causal: the entry's own hour is never seen.
- A group with fewer than `minTrades` closes is not judged.
- Replay on x01's paper trades (5 Oct, 3-hour window): shorts it opens PF 1.25, shorts it holds back 0.51; everything it opens PF 1.70.
- Settings page: a switch plus fields for min PF, hours and min closes.

### Axis intrabar fills (from the `axis-fills` work)
- A rung at or beyond the stop in force never fills. A rung inside it fills and exits at that same stop, never better than the fill.
- Revert-mode Axis positions are now returned as open and carried on the tapes.
- Live lane volume for a filled ladder is its execution multiple × ladder weight.

### Keeping the positive coordinations (operator instruction)
- `docs/positive-coordinations.md` lists each kept coordination with its evidence: signal confirmation, signal acceptance and direction acceptance at PF 1.3, hour lock / cooldown / conflict off, signals' own base, the volatility floor, the engine direction gate, Axis on and DCA off on x01, the fill within every budget, and the allocator caps.
- `positive-defaults.test.ts` pins the code defaults.
- A desk prints and logs `positiveCoordWarnings` at start and on every patch that leaves one of them off.
- `CLAUDE.md` holds the standing instruction.
- Signal direction acceptance now defaults to PF 1.3.

### Long/short symmetry test
- Every indication's long count on a market must match its short count on the price-mirrored market.
- The bar simulator must book a short like a long on the mirror.
- The Stable-02 confluence port keeps the desk's own rule bit for bit and is excluded, with the reason in the test.
- `CTS_CORE_SYNTHETIC_MIRROR=1` (tests only) mirrors the synthetic market.

### Memory
- **Root cause:** x01 ran without allocator caps, so worker threads' glibc arenas kept every freed tape buffer: 11 GB resident on a 2.6 GB heap.
- **Fixes:**
  - workers collect garbage after each reply, using the process-wide `--expose-gc`;
  - the status splits memory into heap, array buffers and native;
  - desks and sessions warn when `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX` / `MALLOC_MMAP_THRESHOLD_` are missing;
  - `test:core` sets both.

## Tests
- symmetry 2, engine-side 3, axis 32, axis-variants 4, walkforward 11, block 23, signals 29, signal-gates 5, gating 6, independence 12, memguard 7, pool 7, stable02 31, statistics 5, control-audit 19, positive-defaults 3 — all pass.

author: pdet
body:
DuckLake 0.3 stored some inlined columns using native PostgreSQL types. Newer versions expect different representations, such as `BYTEA` for strings and` VARCHAR` for dates and timestamps. Updating the catalog metadata alone could therefore leave existing inlined tables incompatible with current reads and writes.

To address this, the migration inspects each inlined table using the column definitions from its schema version and rebuilds tables with recognized legacy storage types. This also handles tables created before a column rename. The conversion reuses the encoding logic used for new inserts, preserves row IDs and snapshot boundaries, and correctly quotes column names.

The conversion runs during the `0.3 → 0.4` and 1`.0 → 1.1-dev1` migrations, covering older storage layouts that survived an earlier upgrade.

Fix: #843

author: daniduwijendra
body:
## Purpose
On the deployed customer portal an open page could repeat its user, project and list requests about once a second, indefinitely (about three backend calls per second per tab).

The Asgardeo provider mirrors its client's busy flag into `isLoading` (polled every 100 ms). The flag goes true whenever the client touches the token, including each `getIdToken()` an API call makes and the periodic background refresh. Nearly every data hook gates on `isSignedIn && !isLoading` with `staleTime: 0`, so each of those blips switched every active query off and on again, and React Query refetches stale data when a query is re-enabled. The refetch calls `getIdToken()`, which can raise the flag again.

## Goals
- A transient SDK loading flag no longer triggers refetches once the session is up.
- First load still waits for the session; signing out still disables queries.
- No change to any component or hook that reads the SDK's auth state.

## Approach
One new component, `providers/StableAuthLoadingProvider`, mounted directly inside `AsgardeoProvider` in `AppWithConfig`. The SDK's own `useAsgardeo` reads the exported `AsgardeoContext`, so the provider re-provides that context with `isLoading` held at `false` once the session has been ready and the user is still signed in. Signing out clears it. Every other field of the context is passed through unchanged, and components keep importing `useAsgardeo` from the SDK exactly as before (the SDK's own route components see the same value).

Net diff: `AppWithConfig.tsx` (3 lines, plus indentation of the block it wraps) and the new provider with its test. An earlier revision of this PR changed 110 import lines instead; the second commit replaces that.

## Automation tests
- Unit tests (`providers/__tests__/StableAuthLoadingProvider.test.tsx`): the real, unchanged `useGetUserDetails` hook fetched 5 times for 4 loading flips with a pass-through provider and once with this one; first load still waits for the session; signed-out and sign-out reset; other context fields pass through.
- The real SDK package was run (outside Vitest, which mocks it) to confirm that its `useAsgardeo` returns the values given to a custom `AsgardeoContext.Provider`.
- Full webapp suite: 59 files / 136 tests fail identically on the unchanged branch in my environment and nothing changes with this PR apart from the 7 new passing tests. `tsc` and ESLint are clean.

## Test environment
Node 22, Vitest 4, macOS. Installed SDK is 0.25.6 (the repo pins 0.25.14); the exported `AsgardeoContext` is read by the SDK hook in 0.25.6, and a future SDK that stopped exporting it would fail at compile time, not silently.

## Not verified
- Not run against a live Asgardeo sign-in. The loop appeared on the dev deployment once, during a stretch of token activity, and did not reappear on later page loads, so the mechanism is covered at the query layer with simulated loading flips.
- Behaviour to be aware of: after the first load, queries stay enabled while the SDK refreshes the token in the background; requests then go out with the stored token, and the existing expired-token handling in `useAuthApiClient` still applies.

## Security checks
 - Followed secure coding standards in http://wso2.com/technical-reports/wso2-secure-engineering-guidelines? Not separately reviewed
 - Ran FindSecurityBugs plugin and verified report? N/A (TypeScript)
 - Confirmed that this PR doesn't commit any keys, passwords, tokens, usernames, or other secrets? yes

author: garywoodfine
belphemur
body:
## Summary

Two related housekeeping changes to generated data:

1. **The ingredient autocomplete index** (`public/data/ingredients.json`) goes from a pure catalog census to a usable shopping vocabulary: **338 → 871 rows, +533 hand-authored, 0 catalog rows changed or lost.**
2. **The ADR index** (`docs/design/index.md`) is now *generated*, and `AGENTS.md` links it instead of listing ADRs in prose — so adding a record no longer means editing `AGENTS.md` (ADR-0053).

## Why

The index could only ever name an ingredient some Mealime recipe already buys. Census over all 2,759 docs (349 distinct spellings) found **zero** gluten-free, lactose-free or dairy-free line items — and no oat/soy milk, xanthan, psyllium, bouillon or stock either. The catalog carries no dietary metadata (ADR-0018's premise) and no "instead of this, buy that" dimension, so a substitute is not derivable: it has to be authored. Adding variants was rejected — a GF variant is a *new recipe*, and the catalog is frozen (`sync_catalog.py` is the only way it grows).

## What

- **Tranche 1 (263)** — gluten-free flours/binders/bakery/pasta/condiments, lactose-free and dairy-free dairy, plant milks, vegan equivalents, pantry staples the recipes never name.
- **Tranche 2 (168)** — from censusing a hand-written ~450-name household shopping list, keeping only names with **no whole-word match** in any existing key. That filter stops "fettuccine" being called a gap when "fettuccine pasta" is already indexed; a naive substring diff would have added ~130 duplicates.
- **Tranche 3 (102)** — from the ANSES **CIQUAL** food-composition table (English edition, Zenodo 4770202). `scripts/fetch_ciqual.py` fetches and diffs it so the review is re-runnable; output is gitignored and **nothing consumes it**. Rows are hand-curated because CIQUAL is a French *dish* table — 3,097 of its names are absent from the index, and after dropping preparation suffixes only 563 remained. The rejects are regional cheeses, charcuterie, named spirits and finished dishes, not shopping items. The script is a checklist; the table is the decision.

## The load-bearing invariant

A supplemental row is a **filler, never an override**. Precedence is snapshot override > catalog majority vote > SUPPLEMENTAL, and a row whose nameKey the catalog already produces is skipped. Verified by diff against main: **0 of 338 catalog rows changed, 0 lost.** If a future `sync_catalog.py` brings real dietary recipes, the goldens fail loudly so the table shrinks rather than shadowing real data.

Categories are **stated per row, not inferred** — `bucketFor()`'s keyword lens is tuned for authored recipe prose and misreads shopping vocabulary ("gluten-free bread flour" → Bakery on `bread`, "pea milk" → Produce on `pea`). The lens is untouched. No invented units: there is no observed quantity, and a fabricated `(1 L) cartons` would be advice the app cannot honour.

## Gates

- **16 new goldens** (`scripts/test_extract_ingredients.py`) + a new `--check` mode and a CI step. The goldens read the **committed** artifact and assert it is not stale — a gate that regenerates its own subject cannot fail on a stale index, which is what the first cut did (caught in review, fixed).
- e2e pins a GF flour under Baking & Spices and a lactose-free butter under Dairy, Cheese & Eggs, end to end.
- Wired into CI as `test:data` alongside ADR-0043 and ADR-0041, which previously ran only by hand.

## Review outcome

Four findings raised. Three fixed (the unfailable staleness gate, `silica gel` offered as food, `oat flour` shoppable in a different aisle than its GF twin — the last now enforced across all 22 flours). One declined with evidence: "gluten-free whole wheat flour" is a real retail product name (Bob's Red Mill, One Degree Organics, King Arthur Baking), so the row stays.

**Verification:** `--check` green · goldens 16+14+15 OK · build green · 513 unit pass · 469 e2e pass (Desktop Chrome + Pixel 7).

**Also in this PR:** `AGENTS.md`'s generated-data table now carries rows for the supplemental ingredient table, the CIQUAL dev fetcher, and the ADR-index generator, plus the new commands. Its "Design ADRs" bullet is reduced to a link.

Refs ADR-0012, ADR-0014, ADR-0052, ADR-0053

This PR makes three fixes from the 2026-10-05 site audit. Péter approved them through marveen (2872). Kenshin deploys; marveen re-measures on the live site.

## 1) Mobile chat button (below `lg`)
**Before:** the 56 px floating chat button covered body text on most pages, at 0 px gap in 21–75 positions per page. It also sat on top of the bottom bar's KAPCSOLAT button, overlapping it by 56×24 px at 360, 390 and 412 px.

**Changes:**
- Below `lg` the floating button is hidden, and a chat button in the bottom bar (`MobileCTA`) opens and closes the chat. The two components talk through window events (`brunella-chat-toggle` / `brunella-chat-state`), and the bar's button carries `aria-expanded`.
- The bottom bar is now shown from page load on mobile (before, it appeared only after 400 px of scrolling). Its measured height is reserved as `body` `padding-bottom` (`--mobile-cta-h`, 69 px), so the end of every page stays above the bar.
- The bar's label now wraps to two lines instead of being cut off.
- **`/kapcsolat`:** the e-mail address had no break point and widened the 360 px layout to 392 px. As a result the cookie banner and the bottom bar slid below the visible screen, so the banner's buttons could not be reached. The fix is `break-all`. This bug is also present on the live site today.
- Desktop (`lg` and up) keeps the floating button.

## 2) Hungarian blog posts
**Cause:** `stripIndent(content.trim())` trimmed first, so the first line ended up at indent 0 and nothing was dedented. Markdown then rendered the 6-space-indented body as a single monospace code block.

**Fix:** `stripIndent(content).trim()`.

## 3) Language switch on Hungarian-only pages
On `/weboldal-keszites-zalaegerszeg`, EN/DE now go to `/en` and `/de` instead of the 404 at `/en/weboldal-keszites-zalaegerszeg`. The list of Hungarian-only pages is `HU_ONLY_PATHS` in `LanguageSwitcher.tsx`.

**Chat, mobile:** 360/390/412 px × 8 pages (`/`, `/szolgaltatasok`, `/portfolio`, `/rolunk`, a blog post, `/en`, `/kapcsolat`, `/de/kapcsolat`) = 24 views, scrolled in 100 px steps. Results:
- 0 problems: at every step the chat button is inside the bar and in the viewport, and both the chat button and KAPCSOLAT are on top at their own centres (tappable). They do not overlap.
- No floating element covers any text: 0 hits.
- At the bottom of every page, the last footer text is above the bar.
- Open/close works: the panel's bottom edge sits above the bar, `aria-expanded` goes true then false, and a second tap closes the panel.
- With the menu open, the menu covers the bar.

**Chat, desktop:** at 1024, 1280 and 1440 px the floating button is still shown, the bar is hidden, and there is no added padding.

**Blog:** all 8 posts at 1280 and 390, plus the EN version at 1280 (24 measurements):
- raw `**`/`#` in the visible text: **0** (live today: 6–48 per post);
- no `pre`/`code` blocks; the body font is Inter;
- real `h2`/`h3`, `li` and `strong` elements are present.

**Language switch:** 1280 and 390, EN and DE:
- the zalaegerszeg page goes to `/en` or `/de` (200);
- `/szolgaltatasok` and a blog post still keep the page (200).

`tsc` is clean. ESLint shows only an older warning in `BrunellaChat.tsx` (`set-state-in-effect`, line ~105, existing code).

In the audit crawl at 390 px, the layout viewport is wider than the screen on these pages, so mobile browsers zoom out:

- head: bbee7981

## Architecture Impact
Repository-level change; review the generated file summary and validation evidence.

## Layer Target

## Affected Modules
repository tooling/config/docs

## Evidence

## Changes
```
.agent/active-runs.json
.agent/goals/DAILY-RUNTIME-CANDIDATE-RETURN.yaml
.agent/runs/DAILY-RUNTIME-CANDIDATE-RETURN/run.json
docs/ops/daily_dev_runtime_repo_policy_v1.md

scripts/ops/daily_runtime_bundle_sync.py
scripts/ops/test_daily_runtime_bundle_sync.py
```

## What / Why
The governed daily-runtime mainline entry required an attached `main` at the expected old SHA, so a
daily runtime left detached at an accepted candidate failed closed with
`BLOCKED git rev-parse: fatal: HEAD does not point to a branch`, with no managed entry to return it
to `main`.

This adds one optional identity, `--expected-candidate-sha`
(Make: `DAILY_RUNTIME_EXPECTED_CANDIDATE_SHA`). The remote program normalizes a detached runtime to
`main` only when all hold: the detached HEAD equals the declared candidate SHA, the worktree is
clean, `refs/heads/main` and `refs/remotes/origin/main` both equal `expected_old_sha`, and the
candidate SHA is recorded under `refs/daily-candidates/`. Otherwise it fails closed; the previous
attached-`main` path is unchanged. Evidence JSON adds `normalized_from_candidate`.

No audit, assertion, bundle digest or fast-forward guarantee is relaxed; no new environment or
credential authority is created.

## Verification
- `make verify.daily.runtime.main.bundle_sync` — 9/9 (attached fast-forward, detached
  recorded-candidate normalization, four fail-closed negatives: unrecorded candidate, dirty
  candidate, `refs/heads/main` mismatch, detached HEAD with no declared candidate identity).
- `make ci.local.iteration` — passed.
- `make ci.delivery.freeze.prepare` — passed, no generated drift.

author: bogdaniel
body:
Refs #490

## What

Host verification capacity becomes a third resource owned by the **existing** scheduler/store acquisition (ruling 5993926034). No second queue, no assurance-local semaphore, no new scheduler.

| resource | ceiling | operations |
| --- | --- | --- |
| work | `max_concurrent_runs` | every kind except observation |
| observation | `max_concurrent_observations` | `source.observe`, `github.observe` |
| **verification (new)** | **`max_concurrent_verifications` (default 2)** | `assurance.go` (gofmt / go vet / go test on the exact tree) |

### Enforcement
- `AcquireOperation` gains `maxVerifications`. For a verification operation the **same SQL statement** that takes the lease also requires fewer than `maxVerifications` *other* runs to hold a leased verification operation (counted from the canonical document's kind, exactly like the class ceilings). The memory double mirrors it.
- A verification is still work: it needs a work slot **and** a verification slot. The new ceiling can only narrow concurrency, never widen it relative to today. It is not derived from `max_concurrent_runs`; with work=10, verification=3 ten providers can reason while three verifications use the host.
- Occupancy is durable lease rows, so restart reconstructs it and a held verification is never leased twice.

### Classification
- **Capacity wait** – a refused verification starts nothing, spends no attempt (`Attempt` only moves at `Start`), journals no assurance result and invokes no remediation. The run settles `waiting / verification_capacity_unavailable` when `Scheduler.VerificationSaturated` confirms every slot is held by another run (otherwise the existing `operation_unavailable`). That reason is added to the closed `externalWaitReasons` set, so the wait does not burn active-work budget. Without that, capacity exhaustion would surface as `run_wall_budget_exhausted`.
- **Environmental verifier failure** – unchanged and conservative. The baseline verifier already treats only exit 1/2 of the `sh -e gofmt; vet; test` workload as a verdict. Non-verdict exits (Docker 125, 126/127, signal deaths such as 137) are `transient_infrastructure`, which goes to `RouteRetry` of the same operation and is never remediation. Flaky tests and generic test timeouts are **not** reclassified. A real assertion failure is still `verification_failure`, which goes to remediation.
- Timeouts are not scaled with load, and `attempt_wall_limit_seconds` is untouched.

### Policy (ADR-0003 category S, #346)
- `supervisor.max_concurrent_verifications` and `watch.max_concurrent_verifications` combine stricter-wins. A negative operator value is refused. The repository `.zenchron.json:watch.max_concurrent_verifications` may only tighten.
- Part of `SupervisorPolicy`, so it is in the `supervisor_starts` record and the policy digest. It is cleared in `controllerEffectiveOperator` and never enters the C-only identity (tested).
- ADR-0003 inventory, `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/supervisor.md`, `docs/running-work.md` (wait-reason table) and `docs/spec/runtime-v0.1.md` are updated.

### Status
`Fleet` gains `verification_capacity`, `verifying` (Working runs holding a verification slot) and `awaiting_verification` (Runnable runs whose next op is a verification). These refine the existing six-way partition and do not join it. Text status prints a `Verify:` line.

### Default = 2
This is the low end of the 2–4 band in the ruling. One `go test ./...` of a repo this size already spreads across every core, and ten at once caused the 10-minute `TestReadStoreAndBoundedEventsPage` timeouts. A default of 1 would serialize every fleet's verification behind its slowest. Because a verification also takes a work slot, the default changes nothing at the default `max_concurrent_runs = 1`.

## Acceptance mapping (tests in `runtime/verification_capacity_test.go`)
1–2. `TestTheVerificationCeilingIsIndependentOfTheWorkCeiling` (SQLite + memory): work=10, verification=3. Ten concurrent drivers request verification and exactly 3 are admitted. Seven providers then fill the remaining work slots and an 11th is refused. A freed slot admits exactly one queued verification.
3–4, 7. `TestAVerificationCapacityWaitIsNotAFailure` (engine): another controller holds the only slot. The run waits with `verification_capacity_unavailable`, the verifier is not called, no assurance payload is written, there is no remediation, and the op stays `pending` with attempt 0. Fleet shows it awaiting verification. Once the slot frees, it verifies once with ordinary semantics. `TestAVerificationCapacityWaitDoesNotSpendTheRunBudget` covers active-work accounting.
5–6. Existing `TestBaselineVerifierReturnsAJudgedFailureWithoutAnError` / `TestBaselineVerifierFailuresReachTheConfirmationRerun`. New `TestAnEnvironmentalVerifierFailureIsNotACandidateFinding`: an infrastructure failure retries and never reaches the worker.
8. Fleet/status counts plus the `Verify:` line.
9. `TestVerificationOccupancySurvivesARestart`: the reopened store still refuses, the held op is not re-leased, and attempts are unchanged.

I checked that the scheduler/engine tests fail when `verificationKinds` is emptied, so they detect the defect.

## Not in this PR (so `Refs`, not `Fixes`)
- **Provider-internal test commands are not gated.** Examples are Claude Code running `go test` itself inside `execution.invoke` (the likely source of the six attempt-wall failures) and the brokered `candidate.run` tool. Gating a nested tool needs a durable permit keyed to the running parent operation, which is a separate design step under the same ruling.
- The read-only control-plane projection (`controlplane/api.go`, its JSON schemas) does not show the new counts yet. CLI `status` and the control-endpoint status do.
- A verification-capacity-waiting run follows the existing quiet-run cadence. It is re-driven at least every 4 polls, and immediately when a slot frees between passes in the same process.

## Engineering-policy notes
- No new interface or abstraction. `AcquireOperation` gains one parameter on the existing interface. New unexported helpers: `consumesVerification`, `holdsVerificationSlot`, `verificationOccupancy`, `runnableNow`, `stricterCeiling`. The last two remove duplication that would otherwise be a third copy.
- No `ponytail:` corners. No new dependencies.
- File-size checker: it was already failing on `main`, and the only change here is growth of files that already exceeded the cap: `config.go` 1337→1362, `reconciler.go` 2293→2310, `controller.go` +4, `serve.go` +4, `autonomy.go` +5. Review-zone files grew too: `scheduler.go` 890→923, `fleet.go` 797→838, `sqlite_store.go` 754→773. The new test file is 288 lines.
- Local checks: `gofmt -l .` clean, `go vet ./...` and the windows cross-build pass, and focused tests pass (scheduler/store/capacity/fleet/pause/stopped-run/driver-lease/policy with `-race`). The full suite is left to CI.

author: schramm2
body:
## What

`processor-boot.sh` now puts the `fm_data_annotate` source checkout ahead of `.ros-runtime` on `PYTHONPATH`, so the process supervisor imports the package from source and not from the pip copy.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  setup[setup-processor.sh] -->|pip install --target| rt[(.ros-runtime copy of fm_data_annotate)]
  src[(src/fm_data/fm_data_annotate)]
  boot[processor-boot.sh: PYTHONPATH] --> sup[process_supervisor]
  src -->|imported first, after this change| sup
  rt -.->|was imported first| sup
  sup -->|annotation source digest| gate{digest equals cloud image?}
  gate -->|yes| ok[lane accepted]
  gate -->|no| bad[source_mismatch]
  ci[test-processor-runtime.sh] -->|checks the order| boot
  classDef changed fill:#fff3b0,stroke:#b58900
  classDef added fill:#d4f7d4,stroke:#2e7d32
  class boot changed
  class ci added
```

Yellow: changed. Green: added check.

The supervisor hashes the tree it imports and compares the result with the digest of each cloud lane image. The boot script sets the import order for the supervisor, so it decides which tree is hashed.

## Why

`setup-processor.sh` installs `fm_data_annotate` into `.ros-runtime` (since #232), and the boot script put that directory first. The copy has no `scripts/` directory, which the digest includes. The supervisor therefore computed a digest that no image can have, and refused every lane with `source_mismatch`, also when the image was built from the same fm-data tag.

The line already does the same for `fm_data_perception`.

Closes #242

## Testing

- `bash scripts/ci/test-processor-runtime.sh`: exit 0, 22 PASS, 0 FAIL.
- The new check fails on `main`: with the old `processor-boot.sh` the script prints `FAIL: .ros-runtime shadows the fm_data_annotate source`.
- `shellcheck` on both files: no new findings.

Not tested here: a processor host converge and a real cloud lane start. See Evidence for the local simulation.

## Evidence

Import resolution with the two `PYTHONPATH` orders, against an fm-data `v0.1.64` checkout and a runtime copy of the package directory:

```
before:  runtime-copy  06b602520157
after:   source        a66f21432e65
```

The command prints where `fm_data_annotate.source_tree` resolves and the first 12 characters of `annotation_source_digest()`. The `after` value is the digest of the lane images built from the same tag.

`fm_data_record` is installed into `.ros-runtime` the same way. It has no digest check, so this change leaves it as it is.

## Checklist

- [x] Focused on one logical change
- [x] Commit messages follow `prefix: phrase` (init|feat|fix|docs|refactor|chore)
- [x] Docs updated if behavior changed
- [x] A visible or physical change has a screenshot or recording in Evidence
- [x] Architecture unchanged, or the `.d2` diagrams moved with it <!-- diagram-gate -->

author: zaubermaerchen
body:
An asynchronous events-fd warning can hold the diagnostic mutex while stderr is blocked, preventing a later primary I/O error from returning. Keep ordinary primary diagnostics synchronous, but skip a runtime diagnostic when an event warning owns that mutex so the original exit status can be returned. This introduces no additional goroutine or queue and preserves serialized diagnostic writes.

Define event failure warnings as best effort: disable event output immediately, attempt one asynchronous stderr warning, and never wait for warning delivery at process exit. Align README and `--describe` with this contract and the possible omission of contended primary diagnostics. Events-fd validation, event schema, ordering, and CLI parsing are unchanged.

Closes #44.

Validation:
- `go test ./...`, `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...`, formatting, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Deterministic tests cover stalled-warning EOF and I/O-error exits, original exit codes, no overlapping diagnostics, and ordinary synchronous primary diagnostics; existing continuation and warning-once coverage is retained.
- The stalled-warning I/O-error test failed before the fix because the run waited for the warning.
- macOS/Windows arm64/amd64 builds and test compilation: passed; native execution is covered by CI.
- Subagent review completed with no outstanding findings.

author: serafinijose
body:
iCAR training time grows with the square of the number of coefficients, and every category of a `C()` term adds one. A sub-jurisdiction layer with about a hundred categories can turn a run of a few minutes into an hour, with nothing in the form to suggest it.

## Slow-iCAR warning
- For iCAR, the New model dialog estimates the run time from the formula, the sample size, the iterations and the number of categories of each categorical layer.
- Past ten minutes it shows a warning naming the layer responsible, its number of categories and how much faster the run would be without it, e.g. "about 69 min, mostly because of subj (107 categories; about 77× faster without it)".
- It suggests two fixes: duplicate the dataset and drop the layer, or delete its `C()` term from the formula. Editing the formula updates the warning live.

## Duplicate dataset
- Dataset rows get a Duplicate action. It opens the New dataset dialog filled in from that dataset, named `<name>_copy`. Nothing is saved until the user clicks Save.

## Categories stored at harmonization (breaking: needs a re-harmonize)
- The categories of a categorical layer are now read once, when the layer is harmonized, and saved on it as `categorical_levels`. Reading them in the dialog took 20 to 50 s per dataset on a large AOI, so the warning only showed after reopening the dialog.
- Training uses the same stored list for its `C(x, levels=[...])` terms and refuses a layer that has none, instead of falling back to a bare `C(x)` that fails at prediction.
- Layers harmonized by an older version count as pending, and the Harmonization step names them and asks to harmonize them again (en, es-ES, fr, pt-BR). Harmonize all picks them up.
- Re-harmonizing a layer also updates the datasets that use it, so they don't keep the old copy without categories.

## iCAR training fixes
- `csize` was passed to `cellneigh` as its `region` argument, so the neighbourhood grid was always 10 km, and any other cell size failed in `interpolate_rho` after the whole MCMC run.
- `beta_start` from the form was never passed to forestatrisk.

## Also
- The New model dialog refreshes its formula when a dataset was edited under the same name. Every step tile stays mounted, so it used to keep the old formula.

## Tests
- New: `test_icar_cost.py`, `test_icar_warning.py`, `test_model_form_icar_warning.py`, `test_icar_fit_wiring.py`, `test_dataset_duplicate.py`, `test_categorical_levels_stamp.py`, `test_process_tile_categories_notice.py`, plus additions to the harmonization-status, formula-levels and iCAR subprocess tests.
- Full suite: 2599 passed. The 4 failures in `tests/test_evaluation.py` are the known chart-theme tests, which fail when the local `~/.sepal-ui-config` is set to dark.

author: free-soellingeraj
body:
Two complaints, both confirmed in the logs.

## 1. "The transcription just turns off randomly and I keep talking"

`STT_WAKE_MAX_DICTATION` (120s) called `end_dictation`. The take ended, what had
been captured was injected, and **everything said after that went nowhere** —
marked only by the ordinary inject chime, which is indistinguishable from the
one you get on purpose. Straight from `stream.log`:

```
08:10:52  dictation started
08:12:53  dictation timeout after 120s
08:12:55  dictation injected: 922 chars
```

...then nothing, because he was still talking.

The cap now **rolls** the take: `roll_dictation` closes the current segment,
starts a fresh recorder, injects that segment's text, and stays in dictating
state. A long take becomes a sequence of segments instead of a cliff, and `send`
still ends it.

Order matters — the new recorder starts **before** the old segment is
transcribed, because whisper-cli on a two-minute take is seconds of work and
anything spoken during it is exactly the speech this is meant to stop losing.

Verified end to end with real audio, rolling mid-sentence:

```
LOG dictation rolled at 3s — segment flushed, still recording
LOG dictation segment injected: 54 chars (take continues)

injected after roll : [first part of this ... before the roll boundary. ]
recorder restarted  : yes
.part cleaned up    : yes
remaining segment transcribes to: [and the second part comes after the roll boundary.]
```

Nothing lost across the boundary.

**Also:** nothing watched the `rec` pid. A recorder that died mid-take left
`state` as `dictating`, the chip still saying so, and the microphone going
nowhere until the take ended. It now rolls to a fresh recorder, keeping whatever
was captured, and **says so out loud**. A dictation that stops recording
silently is the worst failure here, because you only find out afterwards.

## 2. "I have to say send 10 fucking times"

`ends_with_send` required punctuation immediately before the word
(`[.!?,;:][[:space:]]*[Ss][Ee][Nn][DdTt]`), on the theory that a real command
trails a finished sentence. Whisper's punctuation is arbitrary, so identical
intent was a coin flip:

```
FIRE    "can you work on those things? Send."
ignore  "can you work on those things send"
ignore  "lets do that send."
ignore  "ok thats the plan send"
```

The 12-word cap also rejected a clear "... Send." on a longer line, which
whisper's 6s window produces constantly during continuous speech.

Now the last word being the send word closes the take, within a 20-word cap,
minus the readings where "send" is a verb rather than the command:

```
ok FIRE   "can you work on those things send"
ok FIRE   "lets do that send."
ok FIRE   "so what I want you to do is ... and tell me. Send."
ok ignore "tell me what you want me to send"
ok ignore "I think you should send"
ok ignore "see if the agent will send"
ok ignore "the send button is broken"
```

16 cases total.

## Notes

- `wav_speech_text` and `strip_edges` factored out of `end_dictation` so the
  roll and the normal path share one implementation, silence guard included.
- `INJECTED_CHARS` now accumulates across a take (reset in `begin_dictation`),
  so the send wait budget reflects everything injected, not just the last
  segment.
- The near-miss logging from #88 is what made both of these findable — every
  repeated "send" showed up as `echo latch for 'send' still armed` *after* a
  successful send, which ruled out the send path itself and pointed at the
  matcher.

BUG-064 through BUG-066.

author: connortsui20
body:
## Summary

Alternative to #10299. Fixed-size failure reductions help LLVM combine signed multiplication overflow checks, but applying them to every checked operation can lose efficient unsigned multiply instructions and add repeated reductions.

Keep chunking opt-in so each operation can select the loop that suits its failure evidence. Enable it for `i16` and `i32` multiplication, which improved across the x86 and ARM targets in the original investigation. Wide integer multiplication needs a separate policy because its results depend on the target ISA.

## Changes

Preserve the default checked visitor and keep its chunked counterpart separate. Sharing callback construction and dispatch between them makes LLVM lose the default ARM i64/u64 loop's two-lane form, even when chunking is disabled. Select chunking inside the primitive-type dispatcher to preserve codegen-unit placement. Nullable dense attempts support the same opt-in while retaining ordinary valid-row retries. Batch-constant inputs in the nullable dense attempt retain their existing loop.

## API Changes

Adds `map_checked_chunked_into`, `RowVisitor::visit_deferred_chunked`, and its prepared form. Chunked failure reduction requires an associative OR operation with `Default` as its identity. Existing entry points keep their behavior, and array, SQL, and Python APIs are unchanged.

author: farrellm
body:
Fixes #87.

## Problem

A column whose element type is exactly `Missing` has accumulator type `Missing` (`sumtype(Missing) === prodtype(Missing) === Missing`), so building a fresh state called `convert(Missing, 0)` (or `1` for `Product`) and threw `cannot convert a value to missing for assignment`.

The issue left the rest of the sum family unchecked. Probing every summarizer under `addsummarycolumns`, `summarize`, a time window and a `Bars` window found the same failure in:

- `Sum`, `SumPower`, `DotProduct`, `AgeWeightedSum`, `Product`
- every dependent of those: `Mean`, `Moment`, `Variance`, `Std`, `Covariance`, `Correlation`, `MeanAbsDev`, `LinearRegression`
- widening from an all-`missing` chunk to a `Float64` one

`Min`/`Max`/`First`/`Last`, the `*Index` summarizers, `Count`, `CountDistinct` and the order statistics already worked.

## Fix

An accumulator over an all-`Missing` input now folds into `MissingState{N,R}`, a count-only state:

- its value is always `missing`, so the output column is `Missing` (as `Median` already gave, and as `Base.sum` of such a column is);
- a fresh state is still the identity, so the running, tree and refold window tiers all work;
- on widening it rebuilds the ordinary state from its `recipe` (a sum-family term functor, or the `AgeWeightedSum`/`Product` summarizer) and hands over the row count as `missing` terms. A window still holding those rows stays `missing` until they leave: a `Bars(3)` window over two `missing` rows then `[1.0, 2.0, 4.0]` gives `missing` ×4, then `7.0`.

The existing hot-path states are untouched. `DESIGN.md` and `src/CLAUDE.md` describe the new state.

## Tests

A new `all-missing column` testset in `test/summarizers.jl` covers the state directly, every affected summarizer across the transforms, `LinearRegression` with an all-`missing` response, and the widening case for `Sum`, `AgeWeightedSum`, `Product` and `Mean`.

### Summary
On HTTP/1 shutdown, tasks reserving channel capacity before close could publish afterward and leave envelopes stranded; this fix closes and asynchronously drains the dispatch receiver until `Ready(None)`, canceling unsent requests with original requests recoverable while callers hold `SendRequest` or `hyper-util`

- `src/proto/h1/dispatch.rs` and `src/client/dispatch.rs`: close and drain dispatch receiver on shutdown until `Ready(None)`

author: sunib
body:
## Description

A round of upgrades, plus the fix for the lint failure on the 0.52.0 release PR (#414).

### The lint failure was not Dependabot

#410 (prometheus/common) was green on every check. The red Lint is on release PR #414, from `lint-metric-names`:

```
gitopsreverser_git_queue_drops_total
    CHANGELOG.md:13:* **git:** gitopsreverser_git_queue_drops_total is no longer emitted; ...
```

release-please copies each `BREAKING CHANGE` footer into `CHANGELOG.md` verbatim, and the footer of the `git_queue_drops_total` → `git_queue_refusals_total` rename (#413) names the old metric. The changelog is history, so `hack/metricnames.sh` now leaves it out, the same way it already leaves out `docs/UPGRADING.md`. Verified against #414's actual `CHANGELOG.md`: `metric names OK: 54 referenced, all registered`. **#414 needs a rebase or re-run after this merges.**

### Go modules

| Module | From | To |
|---|---|---|
| go.opentelemetry.io/otel (+ metric, sdk/metric) | v1.46.0 | v1.47.0 |
| go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/prometheus | v0.68.0 | v0.69.0 |
| sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime | v0.25.1 | v0.25.2 |
| sigs.k8s.io/kustomize/api, kyaml | v0.21.1 | v0.21.2 |
| github.com/go-git/go-git/v6 | v6.0.0-alpha.5 | v6.0.0-beta.1 |
| github.com/go-git/go-billy/v6 | v6.0.0-alpha.2 | v6.0.0-beta.1 |

**go-git beta.1** is the one to watch. Unit tests cannot reach every v6 behavior: they missed the `known_hosts` and `gpgSign` environment reads, and only e2e caught those. So the e2e legs are what prove this bump. Relevant upstream changes:
- dumb-HTTP transport removed (we only speak smart HTTP and SSH)
- ref names hardened
- receive-pack rejects refs to missing objects
- git-style boolean config parsing

**kustomize api v0.21.2** made two changes we had copied:
- **Invalid image-name regex.** It no longer panics on an `images:` entry whose name is not a valid regular expression; the name now matches nothing. We still refuse such a folder before the build: Flux's kustomize-controller v1.9.6 pins api v0.21.1, so the folder fails to build in production anyway. `TestBuild_PanicBecomesAnError` lost its only panic source with the upstream fix, so it now drives the recover net with a filesystem that panics on read.
- **Digest suffix.** The image-name pattern now takes any OCI digest algorithm, not only `sha256`. `imageNamePattern` mirrors upstream, so it follows; the dye matcher now matches e.g. `@sha512:` digests the way kustomize does.

### Kubernetes 1.37 end-to-end

k3s now has a stable 1.37 (`v1.37.1+k3s1` is the `latest` channel). #337 held e2e on 1.36 only for lack of one. The e2e cluster moves to `rancher/k3s:v1.37.1-k3s1`, and the README states a single version again. Recorded measurements against 1.36 (mutation-lab corpus, `docs/facts`) keep their numbers.

### Devcontainer tooling

kubectl v1.37.1, kustomize 5.8.2, golangci-lint v2.14.0, flux 2.9.6, flux-operator 0.61.0, task v3.54.0, markdownlint-cli2 0.23.3, vale 3.24.0, trivy 0.75.0, setup-envtest v0.25.2. setup-envtest has to match controller-runtime, and `lint-toolchain-pins` enforces it. Everything else that has a pin was already current: Go 1.27.1, helm, k3d, kubebuilder, actionlint, hadolint, valkey, cosign, oras, controller-gen, ginkgo, goimports, scc.

### e2e: one agent, workloads off the restarting server

On 1.37.1 the first CI run lost 3 legs at bring-up. The audit webhook setup restarts the k3d server container, and CI ran single-node, so every pod came back at once on the restarted node. The manager sometimes came up with cluster DNS dead (`lookup valkey.valkey-e2e.svc.cluster.local: i/o timeout`) and never went Ready: 4 of 7 restarts on 1.37.1, one recorded case on 1.36.4. Re-runs passed for `full-core` and `full-manager`, so it is intermittent. The investigation is in `docs/ci/k3s-1.37-dns-after-node-restart.md`.

e2e clusters now run one server and one agent, local and CI, with the server tainted `node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane:NoSchedule`. The manager, Valkey and Gitea ride through the restart on the agent; only the control plane bounces. A full local `prepare-e2e` on 1.37.1 put every workload on the agent, CoreDNS included, and the manager kept running through the restart with 0 restarts. The local default drops from 3 agents to 1. The failure dump also gains nodes, kube-system pods, CoreDNS logs and an `nslookup` from the manager's node.

### A flake fixed on the way

`TestWindowTimers_ContinuousActivityStopsAtTheTargetsMaxDuration` (new in #413) raced a 20ms `maxDuration` against the write that opened the window. The deadline is stamped before the waiting CommitRequests are read, and under a loaded `task test` that took over 20ms. It failed once in the full suite and passed 20/20 alone. The test now rewinds the deadline instead of sleeping past it.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] Test coverage improvement

## Testing

- [x] `task fmt`, `task generate`, `task manifests`, `task vet`: clean
- [x] `task lint` passes, run with golangci-lint **v2.14.0**, vale **3.24.0** and markdownlint-cli2 **0.23.3** installed locally, so it matches the image this PR builds
- [x] `task test` passes
- [ ] `task test-e2e`: not run locally; the CI legs carry it (go-git beta.1 and k3s 1.37 are what they prove)

author: driaz
body:
Fixes the loss mechanism characterised in `docs/reads/voice-launch-attribution.md` (#61): voice sessions launched on an edge woven in the current page load landed with `anchor_edge_id = null` (13 of 15 edge-less real sessions all-time; 1 more via a boot-time cache window, `477db21d`). Backfill already done in #62; this stops new ones.

## Server layer (migration 040, commit 3d45a38)
- **`create_voice_session`** (security invoker) replaces the client's direct insert. If the client holds no edge id but passes the launch edge's endpoints, it resolves the edge on `(board, directionless pair, mode)`, the `edges_unique_directionless_mode` key that #62 used. Client node ids map via `nodes.data->>'_clientNodeId'` and must each hit exactly one node. Never guesses.
  - Logged as the row's first `processing_log` entry: `launch.anchor_edge_resolved` (`source: server_resolve`) or `launch.anchor_edge_unresolved` (inputs + reason).
- **`end_voice_session`** appends the client buffer after the server entries instead of overwriting `processing_log`, so the launch entry survives session end.

## Client layer (migration 041, commit 76b9eba)
- `replace_board_contents` now returns `[{id, client_source_id, client_target_id, mode}]`. The body is 030's verbatim plus the accumulation, with DROP + CREATE + re-grant.
- The ids are merged into the store, the local cache, and App's `connections`. A woven connection holds its `edges.id` after one save, with no reload.
- `popupEdge` holds the identity key and resolves the live connection at render.
- Boot-time window: Speak falls through to the server resolve.
- **Clean signature:** it did *not* exclude ids. `computeSaveSignature` now strips `id`, so the write-back is a no-op save.
- Retires the `1d003dc` "accepted limitation" comments.

## Accepted residual gap
Speak within about 500 ms (save debounce) plus one RPC round trip of the weave that created the edge finds no row yet. The session gets null plus `launch.anchor_edge_unresolved` with the inputs. No mitigation, by design; there's one line on this in the read.

## Tests
All 363 pass against Weave-Dev with 040 and 041 applied:
- server resolve with a match (reversed direction)
- server resolve with no match (wrong mode, missing node)
- client-supplied id wins over the hint
- a server-written log entry survives session end
- weave, then one save, then every connection holds its real `edges.id`
- Speak with a cache-era id-less connection still anchors
- unit tests for the merge, the signature, and RPC result parsing

There's no DOM-level App test, because React Testing Library isn't a dependency.

## Deploy order
1. Apply **040 and 041 to prod**: `supabase link --project-ref wndfikmpifyqkgivmnwv && supabase db push`, then re-link to dev.
2. Confirm prod is in the expected state.
3. Then merge.

Older cached bundles keep working: they ignore the new return value, and their direct insert/update still works.

## Non-goals respected
No change to the depth rule, the roster, or the snapshot pipeline. No backfill. The two remaining edge-less rows are untouched.

## Flagged, out of scope
Migration 030 reverted 019 and 020's node path. Node `data` is overwritten wholesale instead of merged, and unchanged nodes are no longer skipped. That's live in prod and is likely behind "client saves clobber server JSONB patches." 041 preserves 030's body unchanged.
