author: andersalm
body:
Part of #89

One release path in place of the never-merged #232 path (4,255 lines of workflows, capacity script and runbook).

What changes
- `.github/workflows/release-package.yml` (manual run): source commit, install version N, update version N+1, and `seed_package` (default false). It builds the Apple silicon pair (N+1 reuses N's support) with no keys and no model inputs. The Linux seed package (Runtime N, `ipfs-provider` and its exact source) is built only when `seed_package` is set.
- `scripts/release-publish.sh`:
  - `prepare`: downloads and checks the Mac artifact, then prepares unsigned input in an isolated data dir with Kubo from the build.
  - `policy`: writes the exact signer policy with the current develop head.
  - `seed`: prints the per-release import with the seed's installed Runtime. Copy 4 signed files and sums, rebuild the rest from the artifact, verify, stop, preflight, import (accepting only the known post-commit gossip error), start. It touches no source root.
  - `seed-upgrade` (rare): prints the seed Runtime upgrade. Create `/opt/elastos` for the service user before the stop, check and install the source, install the Runtime and provider, update the provider pin in `components.json`, verify the provider, start.
  - Seed host, data dir, unit, staging dir, Runtime path and service user all come from env.
- `docs/VERSIONING.md`: new "Publishing a release" section. It replaces "Ceremony Requirements".
- `.github/scripts/release-mac-capacity.py` and its test, run in CI next to the other release tests.
- `canary-holder-linux.yml`: no longer triggers on `fix/89-canary-inputs`. Per the operator decision it builds the Runtime and providers from the PR source instead of admitting the pinned 0.8.0-alpha.1 artifact (that artifact expires on 10 Oct). The frozen helper tree, observer pin and unused packaging steps are gone. `scripts/holder-idle-ci.py` follows.

Checks kept: exact source and tree, on develop or an open same-repo PR head that contains develop, fresh Cargo dirs, N/N+1 version, source and support parity, artifact digests (checked again by `prepare` and on the seed), and every input and signed file hash.

Dropped from #232, and why:
- PR #230 pins and the admission artifact relay: job outputs carry the admitted tree.
- Helper-approval comment hash: the seed source root is now a fixed, neutral constant (`/opt/elastos/release-source`) in this reviewed workflow. Reviewing the workflow approves the root just as well, and no seed username ends up in the repo.
- The `release_publication::` cargo test rerun in the seed job: CI already runs it, and the signer refuses any commit that is not on develop.
- The split-archive self-verification code: `tar | gzip | split` with SHA256SUMS on both sides does the same job.

Net lines: +887 / -451 = +436 against develop, and -3819 against the #232 path it replaces.

Local checks: YAML parses, `bash -n` passes for the script, every workflow run block and both printed seed sequences, the capacity test passes (14 tests), pyflakes is clean, and smoke runs of `policy`, `seed`, `seed-upgrade` and `prepare` (up to the git fetch) used a stubbed `gh`.

Open risks: the release workflow has not been dispatched yet, so the first real run is its proof. The holder workflow on this PR is the proof for the holder change.

author: slop-dev-whatsthebeef[bot]
body:
Slice 6 of the spec (supers): super mode, postplans and slop-started branch deploys, plus the board readiness checklist agreed during s15f1. The gap analysis is in s15f1's postplan; the developer's answers (2026-10-05) are below.

Environments
- A glob's environment is chosen explicitly at creation or pick-up (`slop new --env`, `slop pick-up --env`, sstor `--env`, MCP and REST pick-up/take-over). There's no default, except a board setting for the default environment of subs.
- Intake suggests an environment from the prompt.
- Super pick-up and take-over are limited to developers.
- Environment roles go in an environments KB document.

Deploys
- A `Deployer` port with GitHub Actions and CodeBuild adapters. CodeBuild maps each environment to a project, with a board default.
- Deploy scripts never run on slop's server. `.sstor/deploy.sh <env>` is each repo's single deploy entry point, with catalog templates for a GitHub workflow and a buildspec.
- Every push from a glob with an environment deploys at that exact SHA. Pushes from a superseded run and the `<id>: start` commit don't deploy.
- One deploy runs at a time per environment, and pushes keep one waiting slot (the newest replaces the waiting one). Deploy now is disabled for everyone while a deploy runs.
- Results come back through GitHub workflow events, an EventBridge webhook (`/webhooks/aws`) and a signed callback. `DeployStarted` and `Deployed` are emitted, and a failure sets a deploy failure flag.
- Deploy state shows on the board: a card indicator (deploying, live, failed, replaced by another glob), a Deploy now button and a history line in the glob view, and settings fields for the integration.

Supers
- Super context shows the postplan, else plan.md.
- Super mode reports the deploy state after each push.
- The postplan is updated at least at `sstor --ready`.

Board readiness
- A checklist in board settings, plus a banner on the board when something's missing. It covers:
  - the repo's GitHub App
  - the sub-gate workflow
  - the agent-set version
  - the build doc
  - routines, the routine's repo and the Claude GitHub App (ticked manually; it turns red when a matching run fails)
  - environments and the sub default
- Each item has a Fix link.
- Cards show stuck hints (e.g. a ready sub with no sub-gate check), and routine failures map to their fix.

Spec fixes
- L227 should say supers use mark_ready.
- `get_board` returns the enabled integrations.
- R5 vs L342 (subs with an environment).
- Default-environment wording.

Done when: a super's pushes deploy to the developer's chosen environment (two pushes give two deploys, the second following or replacing the first), the board shows the deploy state, and the postplan's latest version is at the head SHA after `sstor --ready`. The Done-when run comes last, on a board with a real deploy target.

Slop glob **s15f3** (super, feature). Merge from the glob or here; squash merge only.

body:
Port item 6 (wayfinder map #175, ticket #184; research: `docs/research/llmcpp-port-chat-drift.md` C3). Adopts llama.cpp `def4d406a` (#29776), "jinja : skip copying loop scope unless a loop filter needs it".

## Change

`for_statement::execute_impl` (`third_party/llama-jinja/jinja/runtime.cpp`): the per-iteration `context loop_scope(scope)` copy is now constructed only inside the `select_expr && test_expr` branch, instead of unconditionally at the top of the loop. `loop_scope` is referenced only in that branch (the loop body runs on `scope` directly), so unfiltered loops skip one context copy per iteration. Semantics-preserving, pure performance.

The fork's `runtime.cpp` is FrInfer-reformatted relative to fork base `76098465`, so this is a hand-placed 2-hunk port (upstream patch lands with fuzz 1), not a verbatim apply. `README.frinfer.md` gains an "Adopted upstream fixes" section recording the adoption.

author: egil
body:
Closes #175

## What changed

`[DisableHtmxDirectRouting]` (approved in #170) makes a stock-routed component normal-only.

- **Routing.** In Direct mode, `HtmxorDirectEndpointMatcherPolicy` invalidates a candidate carrying the marker, so a direct partial GET or POST gets 404 before authorization, antiforgery, or any component work. Normal, boosted, and `HX-Request-Type: full` requests keep the stock page and layout. `ConfigureEndpoint` never sends a marked endpoint down the action or direct invocation paths.
- **HTMXOR003** (Error, NotConfigurable, CompilationEnd; in `AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md`), reported at the marker attribute: (a) declared in `_Imports.razor`; (b) on a type without its own stock `@page`/`Route` (abstract, base, or non-component); (c) combined with `HtmxRoute`. `HtmxorAttributedRouteCatalog` also throws for (c).
- **#172 point 5.4.** An inferred `@onpost`/`@onput`/`@onpatch`/`@ondelete`/`@onquery` binding on a marked component is HTMXOR002 at the binding. If analyzers are bypassed, the generated-action catalog rejects it at startup.
- **Docs.** `goal.md`, the feature guide, and the `discussion-143-amendment.md` table describe the marker. The public-surface allow-list includes the type.

## Verification

- Packed .NET 10 consumer (`PackedNormalOnlyConsumerTests`): the `.razor`, `.razor.cs`, and all-C# forms answer direct GET and POST with 404 and keep the stock page; a packed build with the marker in `_Imports.razor` fails with HTMXOR003 at `_Imports.razor(line,col)`.
- `Htmxor.AspNetCore10.Tests` (net10.0 and net11.0): direct GET/POST 404 with zero lifecycle; an anonymous direct request to an `[Authorize]` marked page gets 404, not 401; anonymous normal GET still gets the challenge; arbitrary metadata sentinel intact; stock form keeps its POST; `HtmxLayout` has no effect.
- Analyzer tests pin ID, severity, exact message, mapped path, and position for every cause.
- `dotnet run --project eng/Htmxor.Quality/Htmxor.Quality.csproj -- check --profile fast` and `-- check --profile full` both exit 0 at `0562fcc` on a clean tree (fast: `Htmxor.Tests` 438/438, `Htmxor.AspNetCore10.Tests` 298/298 on net11.0).
- Focused runs: `dotnet test test/Htmxor.AspNetCore10.Tests -c Release -f net10.0` 268/268 and `-f net11.0` 298/298; `dotnet test test/Htmxor.Quality.Tests -c Release --filter "FullyQualifiedName~PackedNormalOnlyConsumerTests|FullyQualifiedName~PackedPackageConsumerTests"` 10/10 (inner packed TRX 9/9).
- Standards and Spec reviews at test-contract and complete-change; all findings resolved. Copilot's `_Imports.razor` suffix finding is fixed in `0562fcc` with a red-first test (`18bb137`); the matching pre-existing HTMXOR001 check is #280.

## Residual risk and claims not made

- A marker on a base class is ignored at runtime because the attribute is `Inherited = false` and Htmxor reads only endpoint metadata (probed during review, not pinned by a test). Only its build-time report, HTMXOR003 cause (b), depends on the package analyzer running.
- Host, rate-limit, and cache metadata on the marked stock route are evidenced by proxy (authorization plus an arbitrary-metadata sentinel), not individually.
- The `ConfigureEndpoint` defense-in-depth branch is not independently observed; the matcher policy answers first.
- The packed consumer observes status, body, and shell; lifecycle and authorization probes run in-repo.
- How a dual route resolves against a separate `HtmxRoute` component with the same template is not claimed.
- A boosted request that also sends `HX-Request-Type: partial` is a direct request and gets 404; the brief does not cover it.

author: medvednikov
body:
The pinned V compiler resolves bare `malloc(...)` calls inside the memory module to its builtin allocator wrapper. That wrapper returns nil for zero and interprets unsigned oversized requests as negative, bypassing the kernel allocator contracts; the enabled boot heap selftest therefore failed at its zero-size check.

Qualify the 15 internal calls as `memory.malloc(...)` across realloc/calloc, XNU realloc, selftests and benchmarks. The existing C exports, allocation ownership and free paths remain unchanged. Use the explicit address of the by-reference metadata parameter for its cookie, which both the pinned checker and release compiler accept.

Make the new ELF and metadata host harnesses set `VEXE` to the selected compiler and disable compatibility fallback and automatic error reporting. Mark the ELF fixture's existing synchronous borrowed range return explicitly unsafe so release V accepts its live stack-backed fixtures.

Validation:
- Optimized metadata suites pass at 4 KiB/16 KiB with the explicitly selected pinned V7490 and release0.5.2; both ELF host suites pass under both compilers, with fallback disabled.
- Generated C independently confirms the correct kernel allocator dispatch for zero/overflow, realloc and calloc, plus unchanged free/realloc dispatch and allocation-free metadata address handling.
- Strict pinned debug and production kernel builds/link pass on both architectures. Combined strict SMAP/PAN QEMU tests pass on x86_64 and aarch64 with enabled heap/vmap selftests, ordinary/textrel ELF fixtures and real PIE/interpreter boot. Each big-I/O workload runs 300 valid 64 KiB reads/writes and invalid-read/write EFAULT cleanup; accounting stays flat (x86_64 136→136, aarch64 46→46).
- Independent source/lifetime review covers every changed call; heap selftest expectations are retained.

The branch includes current master with the event, amd64 exception and script relocation fixes. This follows up #211/#213 after checking their integration with the compiler pin in #240.

author: atulchandorkar
body:
## Summary
**1. Accuracy checks on every item** (new `agent/verify.py`), applied before an item is published:
1. **Real source.** The link comes from a Google News entry or the bank's newsroom. The AI never supplies URLs.
2. **Bank named.** The original headline or the article text must name the bank: its English name, Arabic name or alias.
3. **No invented numbers.** Every number in the title, summary or impact line must appear in the evidence. If one doesn't, the title falls back to the original headline and the unsupported text is removed.
4. **Independent Claude fact-check.** A separate prompt checks each claim against the **full article text** when the page can be read, and against the original headline otherwise. Items about the wrong bank, or not about the bank's own AI activity, are rejected. Unsupported title, summary, impact or partner details are removed.
5. **Trusted source.** The item must come from the bank newsroom, an official agency or a reputable outlet. Otherwise it is held as *pending* until a second, independent outlet reports the same story, and dropped after 21 days.

Supporting behaviour:
- Rejected items are logged with their reason in `data/rejected.json`.
- If a check can't run (page unreachable, API error), the item is retried on later runs, up to 3 attempts in total.
- The 59 items collected before these checks existed are re-checked once.
- An interrupted run (e.g. no API credit) puts those items back untouched.

**2. Themes based on the collected news.** The new scheme is multi-label, so each item has a main `category` plus `topics`:
- AI Strategy & Leadership
- AI Adoption in Operations
- Generative AI & Copilots
- Tech Vendor Partnerships
- Customer-Facing AI
- Fraud, Risk & Compliance
- AI Skills & Talent
- Awards & Rankings
- AI Regulation & Policy

Existing items are re-tagged by Haiku on the next run.

**3. Dashboard**
- **AI themes** and **Top tech partners** bar charts on the feed and on each country page. Tapping a bar filters the news. Vendor product names are grouped, e.g. "Microsoft 365 Copilot" counts as Microsoft.
- Each card shows theme pills, a verification badge (e.g. "✓ Trusted outlet · checked against full article"), the **original headline** and **every source** link.
- The About page explains the checks and the themes.
- Telegram messages include the verification result.

## Testing
- Offline test with a simulated fact-checker:
  - a trusted item was published
  - an unknown-blog item was held as pending, then published when a second outlet appeared
  - a hallucinated "35%" (the source said 20%) was stripped, and the title fell back to the original headline
  - a wrong-bank item was rejected ("QNB is not named in the source")
  - a stock-price item was rejected (not the bank's own AI activity)
  - an unsupported summary was removed
- Interrupting the fact-check with a billing error kept all 59 legacy items.
- Retagging with a simulated client set category and topics on every item.
- The newsroom flow still publishes newsroom releases as "official".
- Dashboard rendered in Chromium at phone and desktop sizes, with the theme bars, partner bars, card sources, country themes and About page. Tapping a theme filters correctly, and there are no JS errors.
- Not yet run against live news pages or the live API. The next workflow run applies the checks to all items.

author: dsudomoin
dsudomoin
unidoc-alip
body:
## What was broken

When a manager assigns a corrective action to a contributor, the system tells that person the action is theirs, in the app and by email. But the person then couldn't do anything with it. Every change to a corrective action was reserved for managers and admins, so the assignee couldn't mark it started, write down the root cause, or record what they did. Their only option was to file a suggestion and wait for a manager to apply it, for work they had been told was theirs.

Tasks had half of this already: the assignee could change a task's status, but could not write notes on it.

## What this changes

- **The assignee can work their own corrective action.** On its Actions tab they now see a short note that it is assigned to them, a status control and a root-cause editor. They can also edit its notes.
  - They can move it through every status, including **Resolved**, as decided for this issue.
  - The existing safety check still applies to everyone: a corrective action cannot be resolved while open tasks are linked to it.
- **The assignee can work their own task.** They get a status dropdown at the top of the task and can edit its notes.
- **Nothing else opens up.** Contributors still can't change other fields on these records (title, severity, assignee and so on), and can't touch items assigned to someone else. Managers and admins see the same screens as before.
- **Private tasks stay private.** Before this change, a contributor who tried to change the status of someone else's private task was told they weren't allowed. That answer confirmed the task existed. They now get "not found", the same answer as for a task that doesn't exist, which is what private tasks already do everywhere else.
- **Every change is recorded.** Changes made by the assignee appear in the record's history under their name, like any other edit.

The README's description of the contributor role is updated to mention this exception.

## Not changed

- **Command line:** an assignee can now change a corrective action's status from the command line, but not its root cause or notes. The command that edits those still requires a manager.
- **Incidents** have the same gap. They have extra lifecycle rules (regulatory notifications, lessons learned), so they are tracked separately in #409.

## Verification

- New automated tests cover who may do what, for each kind of user, on corrective-action status, root cause and notes, and on task status and notes. They also cover the private-task answer and the open-task check on resolving. The full server, web and integration test suites pass (integration: 812 passed, 1 skipped).
- We ran every kind of user against every one of these actions, before and after the change: 87 requests in all. Before, the assignee was refused on all of their own corrective actions. After, the only differences are the intended ones.
- Checked by hand in a browser:
  - **As a contributor:** on their own corrective action, they changed the status, wrote a root cause and added a note. All three saved, and the history shows each change under their name.
  - **Someone else's corrective action and task** stayed read-only.
  - **On their own task,** the status dropdown and notes worked.
  - **As an admin,** the screens were unchanged.

## Risk

Moderate, because this widens who can change data. Every new or changed action checks that the person is the assignee before saving anything, and tests cover the "someone else's item" and "read-only user" cases explicitly. The worst realistic outcome is a contributor being refused something they should be allowed. The design and the tests are aimed at making the reverse, a contributor changing something that isn't theirs, unreachable.

Closes #203

author: orieg
body:
Hook and MCP runs resolve the repository's default branch as their base again.

#479 made `hook run` and the MCP `check_diff` tool pass no base to the child `discipline check`, so that a clone holding only the change's own branch is refused. The child then fell back to the literal `origin/main`. RUN on main before this change: `git init -b master`, one commit, one uncommitted edit; `discipline hook run --agent claude-code` exits 2, "base ref `origin/main` does not resolve", while `discipline check --base master` measures the edit.

`hook::run_check` now names a base for the default side when neither `--base` nor the environment names one (`hook::change_base`):
1. the branch `origin/HEAD` names;
2. else, when the repository has `origin/main` or `main`, none: the child resolves those as before;
3. else the first of `origin/master`, `master`, `origin/trunk`, `trunk`.

A candidate is used only if it resolves and has a merge base with `HEAD`. One candidate is refused: the branch `HEAD` is on, under a name outside main / master / trunk, when it holds `HEAD`. That is the #476 shape (`origin/HEAD` is the change's own branch after `git clone --branch <change>`), so that refusal is kept.

| Run | Base |
|---|---|
| `hook run --base X` | `X`, unchanged |
| hook or MCP, with `DISCIPLINE_BASE_REF` or a CI base variable set | from the environment, unchanged |
| hook or MCP, nothing set | as above |
| bare `discipline check`, and `check` in CI | unchanged |

`default_base`, which `audit` and `replay` use for their default `--ref`, is untouched. No flag, environment variable or tool argument is added. The `--base` help text, the `check_diff` tool description and the matching sentences in `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` are brought in line; completions and the man page are regenerated.

**Evidence (RUN).** `tests/test_hook_default_base.rs` was written first: before the fix 5 of its 9 tests failed and the 4 controls passed; all pass after.

| Test | Before |
|---|---|
| `hook_on_a_master_repository_measures_the_uncommitted_edit` | failed: exit 2, `origin/main` does not resolve |
| `hook_on_a_fresh_branch_of_a_master_repository_measures_the_uncommitted_edit` | failed, same |
| `check_diff_on_a_master_repository_measures_the_uncommitted_edit` | failed: `could_not_check` |
| `hook_measures_against_origin_head_not_a_release_branch_named_main` | failed: measured against `origin/main` |
| `check_diff_measures_against_origin_head_not_a_release_branch_named_main` | failed: two files reported, one expected |
| controls: a `trunk` repository; `--base`, `DISCIPLINE_BASE_REF` and `GITHUB_BASE_REF` still win; a `main` repository as before; a single-branch clone of the change is refused | passed before and after |

Both shallow-clone tests from #479 pass unchanged. Six mutants are each killed by a named test, among them: the hook passing no base again (the five tests above), the own-branch refusal removed (the single-branch clone control and a unit test), and `origin/HEAD` ignored (both `origin/HEAD` tests).

**Limits, stated.**
- A default branch with an unconventional name (for example `develop`) that is itself checked out, in step with `origin/develop`, with uncommitted edits only, cannot be told apart locally from the #476 clone and is still not used as the base. A branch cut from it works.
- The #479 shallow tests do not exercise `origin/HEAD` with the git version used here (a `--branch` clone writes none); the new single-branch control writes it explicitly and is what kills the own-branch mutant.
- A CI base variable in the environment still wins over the default branch for hook and MCP runs, as it has since #479.

`cargo fmt --check`, clippy `-D warnings`, `discipline docs --check`, `self-test` (194 cases) and the repository's own gate pass. The full `cargo test` was still running locally when this was opened.

Closes #530

author: miroslav-jokovic
body:
## What changes for a user

On the IFTA page, a jurisdiction now opens (since #1293) on its **fuel as well as its miles**. Each truck shows how many **gallons it bought in that state, how many fills and what it spent**. Clicking a truck opens **its fills there**, newest first, with date, station, gallons, price per gallon and total. The cards at the top now show taxable miles, gallons bought (with the number of fills), money spent and trucks. A truck that bought fuel in the state without reporting miles there is listed too. Fills with no truck attached get their own "Not assigned to a truck" line, so the page's totals equal the ledger row.

## Migration and risk

**No migration.** The fills come through a new reader in the fuel module, `readJurisdictionFills`. It uses the ledger row's own fuel rule from 0256/0258: tractor tank (or none recorded), more than 0 gallons, the state, and the station-local business date inside the quarter, with `fueled_at` bounds one day wider so the query uses `idx_ftxn_org_time`. Every query filters by org. Adds the module link `ifta -> fuel`, explained in `check-feature-boundaries.mjs`. Read-only.

**Measured on production 2026-10-05, Texas Q3:** this reader returns **684 fills / 83,763.1 gallons**, and the ledger's own `fuel_business_date` rule returns **684 / 83,763.1**. 12 of the fills have no truck. Across all of Q3, the stored `business_date` and the function differ on 0 of 5,823 fills, and every fill is canonical.

## How to check it on staging

Open IFTA, pick Q3 2026, click Texas. You should see 83,763 gallons bought in 684 fills. Click unit 717 to see its 10 Texas fills (Waco, George West, Wichita Falls…).

## Tests

- shared: fills land on the right truck, newest first; a truck that only fuelled there; the "Not assigned to a truck" line; the per-truck gallons add up to the total; a missing cost counts as $0.
- api: the quarter's fills for the one state only (the next quarter's first day and other states are excluded); a fuel-only truck's unit number is found; Q4 ends on the next year's first day; `expectOrgScoped`.
- web: the totals, the fuel columns, the "Not assigned to a truck" line, clicking a row opens its fills, and a truck with no fills offers nothing to open.
- Each of these fails when the code is broken on purpose: dropping the fuel read's org filter, dropping the quarter's end date, or dropping the "Not assigned" line.

`src/main/mentions/module.ts` answers an `@agent` posted outside a run's thread (the general conversation, a squad's channel, the squads' channel, a conversation a person opened). author: 514sid
body:
A currency board for a hotel lobby, an airport hall or a bureau window. Daily reference rates from [frankfurter.dev](https://frankfurter.dev), which blends what the European Central Bank and around a hundred other central banks publish: 165 currencies, no key, no account, no quota.

One base currency across the top and a card for each currency against it, carrying the rate, how far it has moved over the window, and the line that movement draws.

## Which way round it reads

Two boards from the same rates. A hotel quoting its guests' currencies wants "100 USD" across the top with each card showing what those dollars are worth. A bureau wants "JPY" across the top with each card showing what one unit of that currency costs in yen, which is how a counter quotes it.

The API publishes one base against many currencies, so the second is the reciprocal of the first. The whole series is turned over rather than just the figure, so the movement and the line agree with it: the yen gaining is the dollar costing less, and the same day's rates send a card green on one board and red on the other.

## Contrast

Every colour clears the 3:1 WCAG asks of large text against what actually sits behind it, in both themes, measured with each translucent tone composited over its real backdrop rather than read at face value. Worst case is 3.25 dark and 3.22 light.

That ratio is only available because nothing is drawn under 25px, including what the text fitter may shrink at runtime. `contrast.test.ts` reads the colours out of the stylesheet and the floors out of `panels.ts`, so changing either one keeps the board readable or fails the build.

## Some things that needed care

The vertical scale of the trend line has a floor of half a percent of the rate. Without it the Hong Kong dollar's 0.08% month, stretched to fit the box, read exactly like the euro's 3.4%. A rate that is pegged rather than merely quiet, the dirham and the riyal among them, gets the line without the wash: filling half the box below a dead straight line draws a solid block that reads as a fault.

Rates carry `max-age=28823` and the request URL only moves at midnight, so a player that fetched in the morning would have served that body from its own cache until late afternoon and sat through the publication it was waiting for. Every request revalidates, which costs an ETag round trip and answers 304 for all but the one request a day that matters.

The grid is measured rather than fixed. The board picks its columns from the room it has, preferring a full last row over a slightly better card shape, and the card's type is a proportion of the card, so the same settings fill a landscape screen four across and a portrait one two across.

A name too long for its card at the smallest size it may be drawn at, "Bosnia and Herzegovina Convertible Mark" among them, is carried across its box instead of being shrunk past the readable size or cut off. It rests at each end long enough to be read from the beginning.

Currency glyphs are deliberately absent: the API gives "CHF" as the symbol for the Swiss franc and "$" for four different dollars, so the full name does that job.

## Settings

`base_currency`, `rate_direction`, `quote_currencies`, `amount`, `trend_days`, `appearance` and `board_title`, ordered in the install form with `display_order`. Codes are typed rather than picked from a list: a setting carries at most 1024 characters of help text, which is about 26 options, and a list leaving out 139 currencies would be worse than a field that accepts all of them.

Codes are read in any case, the base is dropped from its own quote list without comment, and anything that is not a currency at all is named at the foot of the board rather than dropped quietly. A well-formed code the API does not know is filtered out before the request rather than failing all of it, since one unknown currency rejects the whole call.

## Credit

frankfurter.dev asks for nothing: its code is MIT and the rates are not its to license. The credit line stays because several of the institutions behind the numbers ask to be acknowledged where their data is reused, the ECB among them. It says "blended" rather than naming one, because a rate here can be an average across several institutions and is no single one's official figure, and it says "not a dealing rate", because none of them is the rate anyone is offered over a counter.

body:
## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Token Plan subscriptions have no native LiteLLM provider route
- Coding tools cannot route these models through the proxy

How it solves it:

- Adds `alibaba_token_plan/` and 21 subscription models
- Supports chat, Messages, Responses, images, speech, realtime and video
- Reuses existing DashScope translation where the APIs match

Docs: BerriAI/litellm-docs#2085

## User Flow

Before: Token Plan is missing from Add Model and requests fail

1. Open http://localhost:3000/models-and-endpoints and choose **Add Model**
2. Search **Provider** for `Alibaba`
3. See **No providers found**
4. With the shared wildcard config, POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions using `chat.json` returns HTTP 400 `Invalid model name passed`

![Before: no Alibaba provider](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lewisco/litellm/4026719cc081f367b02877d5902025b920f31298/screenshots/before-source-provider-search-annotated.png)

After: the same page offers Token Plan and its models

1. Open http://localhost:3000/models-and-endpoints and choose **Add Model**
2. Search **Provider** for `Alibaba`
3. Select **Alibaba Cloud Token Plan**, then choose the wildcard or a model before entering a key
4. With the same wildcard config, POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions using `chat.json` returns HTTP 200 with `pong`

![After at 45d050e1c1: Token Plan provider available](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lewisco/litellm/4026719cc081f367b02877d5902025b920f31298/screenshots/after-source-provider-search-annotated.png)

## Relevant issues

Relates to #36150, where the QwenCloud docs note that Token Plan endpoints were not yet mapped

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes)

Validation at `5eae427b48`: `make check`, 1,103 focused tests and the recursion detector passed. Nine regression cases fail with the `dbc41e65d9` adapter and pass with the fix

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Current tip is `5eae427b48f4b0707fa42bf763f012947800b545`. Normal 16 kHz voice/tool verification ran on this tip on 2026-10-05. API/UI captures remain at `45d050e1c1`, Terminal panes at `6ac150fc7b`, and rechecks at `57a704962f` and `dbc41e65d9`. Before remains at original merge base `02f61c9c420b9aa9de10ff673098ad7132b78f5b`

The [proof appendix](https://gist.github.com/lewisco/9a4033ea61b04b6f10c2f7c5e17bae53#file-provider-proof-appendix-md) holds commands, payloads, realtime client code, fixtures and supporting captures. Successful calls hit the real Token Plan API


Start the proxy with `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=true`, the Token Plan key and a random master key in its environment. In a second shell:

```bash

AUTH="Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"
```

author: ajavanma
body:
Fixes #681.

The GCS suite can print failed tests while returning success because `defer os.Exit(exitCode)` captures the initial zero value. Read the final exit code in a deferred closure so both `m.Run()` failures and recovered setup panics reach the caller, preserving the existing cleanup order.

Enabling the correct exit status exposes three existing bucket-root listing failures. The GCS mock passes an empty object prefix to `MemMapFs.Open("")`; translate that lookup to the filesystem root while retaining the original object prefix. This fixes the mock without changing MemMapFs empty-path semantics or depending on #679.

Add subprocess regressions for successful tests (exit 0), failing tests (exit 1), and recovered setup panics (exit 2). Against unchanged master, the failure and setup cases both incorrectly return 0, alongside the existing failures in `TestGcsReaddir`, `TestGcsReaddirnames`, and `TestGcsGlob`.

Validation on macOS ARM64 with Go 1.26.5:
- Full mocked GCS race suite passes, including the directory and exit-status regressions.
- Root race suite passes.
- Repository CI lint passes with golangci-lint 2.13.2. An additional nested GCS lint run reports the same six existing findings on both base and patch.
- No live GCS bucket was used; the tests use the checked-in fake credentials and mock client. Live STIFACE integration was skipped without its bucket configuration.

The test harness correction was also proposed in #683, which is closed unmerged. This PR includes the mock repair needed for the suite to pass with failures correctly propagated.

author: lhj6102
body:
Closes #114

The whole test suite now builds and runs on Windows. The `windows` CI job runs `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked` on `windows-latest`. Linux keeps every test and every assertion, and still runs the real `/bin/sh` and coreutils.

## Summary, per area

- **Test fixtures.**
  - Tests now name Unix programs through `support::os::bin`, such as `bin("/bin/sh")`. On Unix it returns the path unchanged.
  - On Windows it returns a stand-in: `tests/support/fixture.rs`, built once with `rustc` on demand and hard-linked as `sh.exe`, `cat.exe`, `printf.exe` and the other utilities the tests use.
  - The stand-in shell runs the subset of `sh` that the test scripts use: lists, pipelines, `if`/`while`, quoting, `$1`/`$$`/`$!`, `${X-y}`/`${X+y}`, `$(...)`, `$((...))` and redirections. `&` starts a real child process in the same job, so `$!` is a real Windows PID.
  - A copy of the stand-in next to an extensionless script runs that script, as `#!` would.
  - Repositories copied from `tests/fixtures` get their commands rewritten to the stand-ins on Windows. The files themselves keep `/bin/sh`, because the docs run them.
  - Tests that spawn the CLI with bare command names (`cat`, `true`) put the stand-ins first on its `PATH`.
  - `ARTIFACTIZE_TEST_STAND_INS=1 cargo test` runs the Unix suite against the stand-ins, so they can be checked without a Windows machine. With it set, the suite passes on Linux.
- **OS helpers** (`tests/support/os.rs`, also included by the unit tests): symlinks, junctions (`mklink /J`), owner-only directories and files, a DACL check, an extra allow ACE (`icacls … *S-1-1-0:(R)`), Ctrl-Break to a process group, NtSuspend/ResumeProcess in place of SIGSTOP/SIGCONT, process liveness and start time through `OpenProcess`, and canonical paths.
- **Assertions.** `/proc` checks stay on Linux; on Windows the same tests check `OpenProcess`/`GetExitCodeProcess` and `GetProcessTimes`. Paths that artifactize reports are compared with canonical expectations built with `Path::join`.
- **Two latent races.** `tools::tests::dropping_call_cleans_process_before_removing_directories` and fingerprint cancellation waited for a marker file to exist, then read a PID that the script had not written yet. The Windows runner hit this once. Both tests now wait for the content. The race existed on Linux too.

## Product fixes found by the Windows suite

- **Every command failed with "Incorrect function" on Windows.** `canonical_target` looked up the bare prefix `\\?\C:`, which opens the volume device. It now pushes prefix and root components without a lookup. Prune's path check had the same bug and got the same fix.
- **Plain canonical paths.** On Windows, `platform::canonicalize` drops `\\?\` when the plain path names the same file (dunce's rules: disk or UNC prefix, no reserved names, shorter than `MAX_PATH`). This applies to the repository root, state, output and scope paths. A logical Artifact path joined with `/` then still resolves, and child programs accept the working directory.
- **Nested Artifact paths used `\` on Windows**, which scope resolution rejects. Discovery now joins them with `/` on every platform.
- **Opening a directory as a selection or fields file** gave "Access is denied" on Windows. `open_nonblocking` now opens directories there too, so the regular-file check reports it as it does on Unix.
- **Credential rotation failed while another process read the old file.** `tempfile`'s persist uses `MoveFileEx`. `Storage::save` now renames with `std::fs::rename`, which replaces an open file on Windows.
- **Tool images given as absolute Windows paths were refused**, because the part below the output directory kept `\`. Those separators are now read as `/`.
- **Fingerprint scripts that end their line with CRLF**, as Python's `print` does on Windows, are accepted there. The value is the same as with LF. Unix still rejects CRLF.
- **`--help` printed `artifactize.exe`**, and no-argument help printed `artifactize`. `bin_name` makes both `artifactize`.
- **Detached launches kept the caller's pipes open.** On Windows a new process inherits every inheritable handle, so a launched program held artifactize's stdout. A caller that captured stdout then waited for the program to exit. The standard handles are no longer inheritable before a detached spawn, since std gives each child its own duplicates.

## Follow-ups from the #114 comment

- **`$EDITOR`** on Windows runs as `cmd /d /s /c "<EDITOR> "<file>""`, with no Unix shell. `EDITOR` may hold arguments, such as `code --wait`, or name a `.cmd` shim that only cmd finds. The default is `notepad`. A unit test runs `copy /y` as the editor on a file name with a space.
- **Browser for the Codex sign-in:** `explorer <url>`. No shell parses the URL's `&`s.
- **User name:** the producer name falls back from `USER` to `LOGNAME`, then `USERNAME` on Windows. The default reviewer falls back from `USER` to `USERNAME` on Windows.
- **Hidden token input under mintty:** when `is_terminal` is true but `GetConsoleMode` fails, login prints a one-line warning to stderr and reads the token visibly. A test passes a pipe named like mintty's pty as stdin.
- **`launch_detached`** now adds `CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB`. If a job forbids breakaway, the spawn fails with access denied and is retried without it. A unit test runs the launch inside such a job.
- **Case-insensitive opens vs case-sensitive rules (security fix).**
  - I audited every place where a scope, mount, exclusion or ignore rule compares path strings: scope routing for mounts, children and family folders, `outside_workspace`, prune's repository checks, content-fingerprint exclusions and ignores, and the image output prefix.
  - Scope routing cannot be escaped by case. Paths never contain `..`, so a differently cased name stays inside its owner's folder, which the scope already includes. Ignore and exclusion rules match on-disk names, so a case mismatch only adds files to a fingerprint, which is fail-safe.
  - **Real bypass:** `prune` compared the state path as typed with canonical repository paths. On Windows, a state folder inside a repository could pass the "outside the reviewed repository" check when typed in another case or with 8.3 short names. Prune now canonicalizes the state path first.
  - Tests (Windows): prune and verify refuse a state inside the repository named in another case, and an ignore rule for `secret/` never hides a change in `Secret/`.
- **OneDrive and other non-surrogate reparse points:** unchanged. They are still refused.

## Gated to Unix, and why

- **Exit by signal.** `runtime::signal_is_an_operational_error`, the `ABNORMAL_EXIT` row in `verify`, and the `kill -TERM` fingerprint case. Windows has no signals; `windows_exit_statuses_are_verdicts_not_signals` checks that an NTSTATUS exit code is a RED verdict. The cache tests that need an operational error use a timeout on Windows.
- **Pseudo-terminal tests.** `pty_review_restores_the_terminal_on_quit` and `pty_session_restores_the_terminal_on_quit` use script(1), and `login_on_a_terminal_does_not_echo_the_token` uses openpty. Windows has ConPTY but no such tool to drive it. The mintty test covers the Windows input path.
- **Parts of tests:**
  - FIFOs and sockets as non-regular entries (builtin tools, image output, selection files); Windows checks `NUL` instead.
  - Taking away an execute bit (`tool_check`).
  - Process group and session IDs of a detached launch; Windows checks that the launch outlives the probe.
  - `nested-alias/../state`: Windows drops `..` before it follows a link, so that path really is outside the repository there.
  - The example's `section.sh`, a real POSIX shell script, under the stand-ins.

## Windows security tests

- **Junctions and symlinks that escape a scope are refused:**
  - scoped inputs, as an internal or external link, a dangling link, and the owner itself as a link;
  - builtin read/list/glob/grep/view_image, as links i

author: lionsr
body:
## Summary
- Define the actual periodic-sector column matrix V and its fixed polar encoder F. The endpoint depends only on the labelled tensor family and ring length, never on the requested accuracy or block partition.
- Prove that F has exactly the original periodic-sector span, including at dependent lengths, and is an isometry when the columns are independent.
- Package the common register seed as an isometry and the simultaneous genuine block-unitary compiler as the whole-matrix identity UJ = W. The circuit is chosen for every logical label at once.
- Prove phase-sensitive polar-frame perturbation and finite-length coherent conversion of the canonical encoders. The complex Gram/cross matrices retain all relative phases. Genuine nearest-neighbor circuit depths add as TA + TB; preparing the common seed is neither asserted nor charged.
- Consume merged QICLean #553 at 075e870322202eb9eaa8f7d166996d4be7920686 and remove TNLean's duplicate isometry-norm declaration. The generic reference-amplification result preserves arbitrary finite external-reference entanglement with no dimension factor.
- Add a source-aligned blueprint section, typed logical-to-physical encoder diagram and three checks, and a scope note spelling out the remaining uniform theorem.

## Mathematical scope
This is the substantial finite-dimensional/encoder-assembly milestone for coherent whole-sector conversion. It is an enhancement motivated by arXiv:2307.01696 Eq. (25), the long-range preparation paragraph, and its discussion/outlook, not a formalization of an invented phase predicate.

The all-accuracy O(log(N/epsilon)) theorem remains open here. It still needs common-partition transfer estimates, the squared-accuracy block choice, and an exact fixed-width whole-encoder sequential fallback for the very-small-accuracy branch. Parent-kernel identification requires an existing valid interaction-range theorem. The biased-versus-balanced chosen-vector obstruction is unchanged. No measurement protocol is inverted.

## Architecture and migration
Generic Gram/cross perturbation and reference amplification live in QICLean. Circuit.CoherentEncoder imports no MPS module. Tensor-specific endpoints and block encoder assembly live in Preparation. The historical polar-factor definitions remain where they are; this change adds their perturbation consequences without duplicating the generic QIC results.

QIC #553 is merged and its full exact-head CI passed. The migrated name Matrix.l2_opNorm_le_one_of_conjTranspose_mul_self_eq_one is preserved, with the old OverlappingBlockGram body deleted.

## Validation
- Strict actual-worktree compilation of PolarFrame, Circuit.CoherentEncoder and SectorEncoder with Lean 4.35.0-rc3, one thread and all repository options: passed. Source hashes and produced artifact hashes were recorded together.
- The prerequisite GHZ compiler closure was compiled with actual imports. After integration, all 59 checked TN source files remained byte-identical and 69 QIC source modules were verified against the merged pin.
- Generated import aggregators, committed added-line prose, integrity/file-size/numbered-file policies, blueprint source synchronization and diagram tests (3/3): passed.
- The new blueprint section was rendered and visually inspected as fragment layout QA. External labels/citations omitted by that fragment harness are left to full blueprint CI. The standalone scope note was rendered with its bibliography and inspected.
- Full local root/migration-closure verification was not run: the warm QIC artifact for Channel.Irreducible.PerronFrobenius is absent. No cold Mathlib/Gametheory build was attempted. Exact-head full TN CI must cover OverlappingBlockGram and its affected import closure before merge.
- Shared-host local PolarFrame timing varied from 22 to 59 seconds; the repository's CI compilation-time gate remains required.

## Review
An independent automated read-only review approved the frozen source, mathematical statements, coordinate conventions, circuit accounting, and final integration provenance. No human review is claimed. This PR will be babysat through full exact-head CI; the coordinating parent owns the merge decision.

Prepared with an OpenAI coding assistant, repository shell/Lean tools, and the connected GitHub app. No unavailable model identity is asserted.

## Current-main integration

The original 2079aad72 checkpoint passed the full production build, direct regressions, linters, and declaration checks. The current 26f839fd integration preserves the four foundation proof files and dependency pins byte-for-byte, merges main 8fd2b5d while preserving both adjacent chapter/bibliography additions, and fixes the reviewed missing encoder-diagram test invocation and path filters in both workflows. Its new exact-head CI is required before merge.

The integration also includes an independently reviewed conservative dependency-only cache fallback. It runs only after an empty ordinary matched key, verifies an immutable main-scoped cache and additive QIC source compatibility, and revalidates/prunes before any seeded Lean build. All current-main full-build and direct-regression steps remain mandatory. Cache availability or a performance gain is not assumed.

author: michael-denyer
body:
`registry > session_shutdown stops every running agent` has timed out at bun's 5 s limit on four of the last ~25 CI runs, including `main` at 614d2f9 (run 37331169012). `stop_agent > ends the child and the bash command it has running` hangs the same way.

- `tests/pi/fake-pi.mjs` now kills its tracked commands on `abort` as well as on SIGTERM. pi 1.0's bash tool does the same: its abort handler calls `killProcessTree` on the running command (`dist/core/tools/bash.js`). `stop()` sends abort, closes stdin, and sends SIGTERM together. On Linux the fake could act on the abort, settle, and `process.exit(0)` before Node ran its SIGTERM handler. The tracked `sleep 300` lives in its own process group, so it outlived the fake and the test waited on it.
- `escalates to SIGKILL when the child ignores SIGTERM` adds a `{ mute: true }` step, so the abort cannot end the run. Without it, the same race lets the child exit cleanly before it logs the ignored SIGTERM, and the test fails in about 25 ms.

Evidence, from a `node:22-bookworm` container with 2 CPUs, bun 1.3.14, a non-root user, and three `bun test tests/pi/` runs at once per round:

- Before: 9 hangs in 45 suite runs. A dump at 4.5 s showed the fake pi gone after logging `settled`, and its tracked `sleep 300` still running under PID 1.
- After: 0 failures in 60 suite runs.

Locally on macOS: `bun test tests/` gives 630 pass, 31 skip, 0 fail. `bun tools/generate.mjs --check` passes.

Only test code changes, so no release is needed.

author: johnlouie-pplx
body:
## Motivation

TCP relay connect failures outside configured known-egress reporting currently emit only a terminal counter. That preserves totals but leaves no sandbox correlation or bounded socket-error detail for investigating a connect burst.

## Changes

- Add a WARN diagnostic exclusively for terminal `RelayFailure::Connect`, with the existing sandbox ID, original destination port/family/scope, `io::ErrorKind`, and an optional numeric errno restricted to 1–4095.
- Share one 30-second warning budget across all connection tasks in a proxy, independent of destination and error cause. The next emitted warning includes the number of suppressed generic connect failures; suppressed failures do not fall back to per-flow DEBUG logs.
- Reuse the existing warning-window state machine without changing TLS refusal budgeting. Skip the new diagnostic when known-egress reporting already handled the failure, without spending its budget.
- Preserve terminal counters and existing stage labels, routing, retries, timeouts, admission, and TLS behavior.

## Fixture Evidence

The extended terminal-outcome fixture checks connect, transfer, policy rejection, TLS rejection, and successful outcomes with and without known-egress reporting. It asserts exactly one connection counter per terminal outcome, no duplicated known-egress diagnostic, shared suppression across proxy clones, and an exact safe field allowlist even when a custom error contains a synthetic URL or an out-of-range errno. Separate controlled-clock and destination-classification fixtures cover the window boundary, suppression saturation/reset, both address families, and IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses.

Representative Linux fixture fields:

```text
WARN TCP upstream connect failed sandbox_id=test destination_port=443 destination_family=ipv4 destination_scope=other io_kind=ConnectionRefused errno=111 suppressed=0
WARN TCP upstream connect failed sandbox_id=test destination_port=8443 destination_family=ipv6 destination_scope=private io_kind=Other suppressed=2
```

## Limits

These are sampled diagnostic events, not failure-rate measurements or a per-flow census. Connect denotes the relay setup stage: errors can arise from local socket setup or a gateway timeout, not only remote refusal. One cause can suppress another within a proxy's shared window. Suppression is reported only on a subsequent emitted failure, is process-local, and resets when the proxy restarts. Destination classification describes the original intercepted socket address, not a hostname-resolved upstream address; `other` does not assert public routability. Exact IPs, arbitrary hostnames, URLs, error text, headers, credentials, and payloads are deliberately absent. There are no new metric dimensions or deployment/configuration changes.

author: yorch
body:
Fixes what a click-through of the running dashboard found once a local stack was available: one crash, and about 70 layout, copy and first-run issues. Most of them were at phone width.

## How this was found
- The stack ran locally: Docker infrastructure plus the gateway and web dev servers, on a fresh database with the seeded admin.
- Headless Chrome signed in and loaded 35 pages at 1280px and 375px, capturing each at its full scroll height. It also recorded console errors, failed API calls and horizontal overflow.
- Four separate reviewers read every screenshot and tied each issue to a file and line.
- After the fixes, the pages were captured again from this branch and checked against the original findings, which caught three regressions. Those are fixed here too.

## Crash
- **`/govern/slack-channels` threw "Cannot change the id of an item"** and showed the error panel.
  - `Select` and `Combobox` passed options to React Aria without an `id`, so items were keyed by position.
  - The channel form's agent picker starts with only the current agent, then fills from the library, which moves that option.
  - `withIds()` now keys every option by its value. A regression test reproduces the original error.

## First-run experience
- **Placeholder repository:** readiness no longer counts the seeded `your-org/your-repo`. A fresh install is now asked to connect a real repository. The seed and the gateway share `SEED_PLACEHOLDER_REPO`.
- **Setup links:** a setup banner's "Fix this →" link that points at the page you're on becomes an in-page action or is dropped. Before, those links did nothing. Banners now also appear on Start work and the Agent library.
- **Home:** the setup card shows a skeleton while it loads, so the page no longer jumps.
- **Channel Assistant:** this built-in is read-only in the library, with a user-facing description.
  - It is hidden from Start work.
  - `POST /workflow-templates/:id/runs` refuses it with 409 `SYSTEM_MANAGED_TEMPLATE`.
  - Channel runs record its current spec.

## Phone layout
- **Headers:** section and page headers wrap, and their actions move to their own line instead of running off-screen. Card headers wrap too.
- **Grids and rows:** platform-settings rows stack, and the label is no longer crushed. Lessons stats, Workflow defaults, Canary and Consolidation forms use one column on phones. Webhook URL rows stack.
- **Stacked tables:** values align consistently, including switches. Skills, eval results and the workflow library tables now stack.
- **Tabs and toggles:** tab strips fade at the edge where they scroll (a mask, so it works on any surface). Segmented controls don't wrap.
- **Scanner:** a "Jump to" bar for its categories.

## Copy and states
- **Docs cards:** descriptions skip front matter and rules, keep blockquote intros, strip inline markdown, and end at a word boundary. Overview, Quickstart and Product overview come first.
- **Platform settings:** every settings group has a title, enforced by a test.
- **Empty states:**
  - Usage shows `$0.00`, not "—", for known zero spend, and says plainly when nothing has run yet.
  - Charts use a compact empty state ("No runs in this range.").
  - Runs says "No runs yet" when no filter is set.
  - Pagination hides when a list is empty.
- **Sessions:** browsers read as "Chrome · macOS", with the full string on hover.
- **Settings:** the user ID is dropped, and providers you can't enable say "Not enabled by your administrator".
- **Labels:** GitHub auth-mode options, scanner built-in badges, and Verified/Unverified wording on bundles. Starter-content origin labels are shared between Agents and Skills. Pluralisation is fixed ("1 member").
- **Leftover jargon removed:** "(Tier 2)", "in Temporal" and "EvalCase's".

## Shell
- **Eyebrows:** the decorative `chapter` eyebrow is removed from every `PageHeader`. The breadcrumb already names the section.
- **Sidebar:** every item has its own icon. The role line is hidden when it repeats the name.
- **Text size:** small text is at least 11px, and `paper-600` is no longer used for text on ink.
- **Login:** a signed-in user is redirected away from the login page, except during an MCP OAuth authorization.
- **Page titles:** `/oauth/consent` is titled "Authorize app", and unknown paths no longer borrow "Not found". An access-denied notice falls back to "this page".

## Limitations / follow-ups
- The GitHub integrations Save button is still always enabled. Each integration tab keeps its own form state, so a generic dirty check could disable Save wrongly. The button now says what it saves.
- The Agent library has a setup banner, but no per-agent "No credential" badge.
- The redirect for an already-signed-in user has no dedicated test, because there is no login page test harness to extend.
- The built-in workflow descriptions still contain internal terms; rewriting them would mean regenerating fixtures. They are now clamped to two lines, with the full text on hover.

## Quality gates
- [x] `yarn install --immutable`
- [x] `yarn typecheck`
- [x] `yarn biome check …` with the explicit paths (`yarn lint` checks zero files in a worktree)
- [x] `yarn test`: 572 files, 7,605 tests (after merging `main` with #294)
- [x] `yarn build`
- [x] `yarn docs:check`, `yarn invariants:check`
- [x] `docker build` for gateway, worker and web
- [x] Visual check: 35 pages at 1280 and 375px, captured before and after, with no console errors, page errors or horizontal overflow

## Summary

Restore #843's shared TOC moving/stretching feedback through one actual public Base-derived family Surface. Native anchors, authored text, unique `aria-current`, and the separate multi-item `in-view` interval remain intact.

- The existing TOC owner reads headings plus at most three range rectangles before publishing native facts or geometry. Scroll remains rAF-coalesced; ResizeObserver flushes already-computed layout before paint through that same pass, consuming any pending rAF. Unchanged geometry causes no style writes.
- One aria-hidden, pointer-inert mount contains the real Shadcn/Brutalist Surface. Existing WC registration, family replacement and batched theme ownership supply paint; no website-only prototype or private selection state machine is introduced.
- The consumer owns the 300ms transform/size transition; reduced motion removes it. Font completion, viewport/history changes and detach/reconnect are covered. Native SSR/no-JavaScript links remain available.

## Exact source and dependency

Current head: `38b816685f0f1d869eb18eed24b7bb954950c36a`; tree: `cd4fa6359b7ca69cd053812acb256d1a7f107f66`.

It does not update either owned branch. #816 remains open and has since advanced; normal dependency reconciliation is still required. The main comparison includes that dependency until integration.

Refs #843 and #420. The original animation baseline is `411c354cfbf76e9da34eafa90f1c8a7b973d043c`; `506b8d58ec` removed the feedback. Applicable draft entities: `P-BASE-SURFACE`, `P-SHADCN-SURFACE`, `P-BRUTALIST-SURFACE`, especially PASSIVE/PROJECTION. No public API, export, normative guarantee, lifecycle promotion or release change.

## Current verification

At 2026-10-05 19:11 UTC, all 13 head-associated workflows and Vercel succeeded:
- [Main CI](https://github.com/Proto-UI/Proto-UI/actions/runs/37359029450): synthetic merge `3b3af3e7ead96bd94a087183d12a7663d1dfc1de` has exactly the same tree as the current head.

- [Exact-head TOC motion](https://github.com/Proto-UI/Proto-UI/actions/runs/37359029733): 23 candidate cases, no failures; two families × two themes × two motion preferences. Each normal-motion matrix mode records 126 intermediate geometry frames; each reduced-motion mode records zero.

author: agent-farnsworth[bot]
body:
## Summary

Guard the Portal's existing authoritative active-run snapshot against a later live run event while a SignalR subscription is in flight. A delayed empty snapshot can no longer clear a newly started internal-origin continuation; a delayed active snapshot can no longer resurrect a completed run.

Refs #4646. This is the bounded subscribe/reconnect snapshot-race slice. The remaining issue scope is the affected browser connection's historical membership diagnosis, actual late-answer receipt/dispatch presentation (coordinated with #4644), and browser evidence for the reported live approval sequence; this PR does not assert those were reproduced or completed.

## Root cause

Current `origin/main` already supplies `SubscribeAll` with live `IAgentHandle.IsRunning` snapshots, hydrates the client on initial subscription/reconnect, repairs a missing `RunStarted` with message/tool events, and reconciles missed `RunEnded`. The unguarded subscription response could nevertheless arrive after a newer live `RunStarted` or `RunEnded` event and overwrite that newer projection. Server-side delivery intent from #3326 is already implemented; no duplicate delivery policy is introduced.

## Changes

- Capture the client run-state revision before initial subscription, reconnect, and connection rebuild; apply the resulting snapshot only if no newer lifecycle event has changed the projection.
- Use the same revision guard on the existing quiescent-run reconciliation path and reconnect snapshot recovery.
- Correct the inherited prompt-evaluator API binding against the current agent-loop contract so the mandatory remote build can run; shrink the existing configuration-authority debt ceiling from 219 to the measured 218 without relaxing its no-growth assertion.

## Anti-reinvention

Reuses `GatewayEventHandler`'s existing run-state revision, the `SubscribeAll` active-run result, `PortalLoadService`'s current shared desktop/mobile path, and the established #4146/#4490 regression fixtures. The current `origin/main`, applicable repository/extension/test guidelines, related issues and open PRs were checked. The two shared gate corrections match existing open PR changes, not new evaluators or test exceptions.

## Tests

- Test-first RED: four new stale-snapshot assertions initially failed to compile because the guarded revision API did not exist. This is compile RED, not a claim of a runtime failing test. The new cases cover an in-flight snapshot followed by `RunStarted`/`RunEnded` and reconnect snapshots arriving after newer continuation/completion events.
- The existing active-snapshot, completed-run, missed-start, tool-gap, mobile and desktop regression tests remain present. The final remote CORE executed all 2,072 BlazorClient tests, 266 mobile tests, and 842 architecture tests with zero failures; no tests or assertions were removed or skipped.
- An earlier remote run failed in the inherited evaluator's obsolete API and, after that correction, the architecture ratchet's stale count. The final candidate corrected those specific shared failures without raising a threshold.

## Validation

- Affected BlazorClient test, desktop, mobile, prompt evaluator, and architecture test projects built locally with zero warnings and zero errors. Local test hosts were not run.
- Strict `Validate-PreCommit.ps1 -ValidationMode remote` passed exact-source CORE run `20261005165028-5e927c38`, verified source digest `a9a49b68951de44bf817c7da41f15417f77fe1f0ddd8317fef06d67a4abe0f39`, staged and committed tree `327ded1e8b86a2feff9e639d4fbd3e2df1f348b3` on base `ba6a3f19b53612199920deb2fb6e9e726e0e2891`. Debug and Release builds passed; 20,678 total, 20,640 executed/passed, zero failed, 38 existing skips, zero fixture failures, complete, exit code zero. `git diff --check` passed.

## UI evidence

No visible UI change — this race guard preserves the existing desktop/mobile active composer and applies no rendered markup or styling change. It corrects which existing run state wins when subscription and live lifecycle events cross. The focused reconnect/initial-snapshot tests prove state ordering, not a real browser capture of the historic approval incident; that separate evidence remains under #4646.

## Risk & rollback

- This guards the client snapshot ordering, not actual SignalR membership or delivery guarantees. If a newer event races the response, the client retains the newer local evidence; subsequent live events or another authoritative reconciliation update it. The global revision can conservatively discard a snapshot after an unrelated conversation's event; existing per-event handling and later reconciliation remain intact.
- Revert the branch to restore the previous subscription ordering; the unrelated evaluator API correction and shrink-only architecture baseline are also present because current main's strict gate could not pass without them.
- The new assertions are additive, and the architecture ceiling decreased by one. No existing assertion, skip, test count floor, or threshold was weakened.

## Merge notes

This is a complete, independently reviewable client snapshot-race slice, not full issue closure. No schema, package, configuration, gateway restart, or deployment ordering is introduced. Shared PR health owns post-publication CI; passing validation does not authorize merge. Jon retains the merge gate.

author: thejackshelton
body:
**What changed:** three follow-ups to the floor merge driver (#183), from its review's Lows.

1. **The never-lower check covers pins too.** For `glyph-clearance-pins.json`, the merged result is now judged with `floorRegressions` against each side, as floors are: no rescued count falls and no dropped count rises. A new case stays free, as in the landing driver's floors check. A side whose pin drops more than the other side's is left as a conflict, as is a new target added under an existing case.
2. **Ours is replaced whole.** The merge is written to a temp file next to `%A`, then renamed over it, so `%A` is always either ours or the complete merge.
   - On a refusal, ours is first restored as it was, then `git merge-file` makes the ordinary text conflict.
   - No temp file is left behind either way.
   - A failure of `git merge-file` itself is logged; the exit is 1, so git records a conflict.
3. **No guessing in ordered lists.** When both sides insert names at the same place of an ordered list, after the same name (end of the list included), their order is known only to the merged sources. The driver now refuses that with "both sides added names after X (… and …); their order is not known".
   - Insertions at different places still merge.
   - Sorted lists, which have one order, still merge anything.
   - An object's key order (the `counts` of `p1-floor`, which nothing reads by order) still places theirs after ours.

**Changed tests (reasons):**
- The "two extensions of an ordered list" case that both appended after the same name now expects a refusal (item 3). The insert-at-different-places case still merges.
- The p1-floor case now adds its two suites at different places. Its counts object still gains both keys.
- The pins case that added a new target under an existing case now expects a refusal, because the floors check would refuse that side too (item 1). A new case still merges.
- In the 2000-pair random never-lower test, the only refusal is now the ordered "both appended" case. The test asserts exactly that refusal, and that more than 1000 pairs merged. It was more than 1900 before item 3.

**What passed:**
- `pnpm typecheck` passed.
- `vitest run packages/parity/test/floor-merge.test.ts packages/parity/test/regen.test.ts packages/parity/test/land.test.ts` passed: 143 tests, 2 of them skipped (regen's opt-in full-chain check).
- **New tests:**
  - same-place insertions refused: at the end, at the start and in the middle;
  - pins lowering on one side refused;
  - the script run as git runs it: a merge replaces ours whole and leaves no temp file; a refusal leaves ours' lines in a conflict with markers, exits 1 and leaves no temp file.

body:
## Summary

Lets an agent correct or remove a message it posted. Before this, the server could post but not edit or delete.

- `chat_update` wraps [`chat.update`](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/chat.update). It takes `channel` and `ts`, plus `text`, `markdown_text` or `blocks`. It also accepts `attachments`, `metadata`, `reply_broadcast`, `parse` and `link_names`.
- `chat_delete` wraps [`chat.delete`](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/chat.delete) and takes `channel` and `ts`.
- Both return `{ ts, channel }`. Both act as the user token's user, so they can change any message that user can change in Slack, including hand-typed ones.
- Both are ordinary `write` tools, on by default under `SLACK_MCP_ALLOW_WRITE`. This follows the **P2 decision, option A**. Neeraj: _"1 [option A], and on by default, both should be on by default"_. The decision is recorded in `docs/phases.md` and in the `docs/ROADMAP.md` locked decisions.
- Both need only `chat:write`, which the manifest already requests. Existing installs keep working with no re-consent, and the manifests are unchanged.
- Docs: README and `docs/coverage.md` are regenerated (21 tools). `docs/extensions.md` retires both tools. `.env.example` fixes stale lines: the manifests are `.json`, and writes are on by default.

An optional bot token for posting was built and reviewed, then **dropped at the owner's request** (`a4915e8`). Existing tools are unchanged from `canary`.

### CI fix (`dba2460`)

`bun audit` started failing on new high advisories in transitive deps.
- `bun audit fix` bumps axios, fast-uri, ip-address, js-yaml, qs and hono within their ranges.
- `braces` ≤3.0.3 (GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm) has no patched release, and it is reached only via the dev-only `globby` in the auto-labeler. CI ignores that one advisory, with a comment to drop the ignore once braces ships a fix. Without the ignore, the audit still fails on braces alone.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun run test`: 55 pass, 0 fail. New tests cover:
  - `chat_update`/`chat_delete` handlers, the args passed through, and the returned shape;
  - a call without `channel` or `ts` being rejected;
  - registry counts;
  - MCP `callTool` roundtrips for both;
  - `allowWrite: false` hiding both.
- [x] `check-types`, `lint`, `format:check`, `check:docs`, `check:manifests`, `build` and `bun audit` all pass.
- [x] End-to-end against real Slack, with throwaway Claude Code sessions and an MCP client running only this branch's local `dist/bin.mjs` on the user token:
  - post, update and read back, then delete and read back (self-DM);
  - edit and delete earlier posts, deleting the thread reply first, then the parent;
  - the full desk flow on two private channels: board edits; archiving 4 real threads (47 messages), each copied byte-exact, verified, then the originals deleted with broadcast copies removed; editing a hand-typed message.
  - Evidence is in the comments. The comments about the bot token apply to the dropped feature.
- [ ] Independent review at the new head: pending.

## Release

Merging into `canary` opens the canary→main release PR, and merging that publishes to npm `@latest`. The owner will say when; please hold both until then.

When squash-merging, set the commit body explicitly, for example `gh pr merge 36 --squash --subject "feat: add chat_update and chat_delete tools (#36)" --body-file <summary>`. author: kanhari
body:
Stacked on #163. Records the theory and notation decisions from today's discussion. Documentation only; nothing is implemented.

## Theories: work-plan L2.4c ([core theories](docs/roadmaps/core-theories.md), new *Revision* section)
- **Carriers are fields with an h-level:** `M : set U;`, `P : prop U;`, or `M : U;` for a carrier with no h-level. This replaces `sort`, and is spelled the way inductive headers already are (`inductive Trunc(…) : prop U`). The fields a model holds are unchanged.
- **The universe is named in the header:** `theory Monoid(U < UU0)`, possibly with several universes. This unblocks L2.10k's `Trunc(U, …)`.
- **`G : Monoid(U0)`:** `Monoid.Model` is retired; `Monoid.make`, `.Hom` and `.Iso` stay beside the type.
- **Theory families:** `F(A : U) : set U`, so `Monad` is a theory and the computation-notation work (N1) can build on it.
  - A homomorphism maps each index separately; no naturality field is needed.
  - Indices must match definitionally; nothing inserts a transport for you.
  - **Variance:** none is needed for checking. Homomorphism generation does need a polarity rule: an operation's arguments may mention carriers only covariantly. `k : A -> F(B)` is fine; `g : F(A) -> A` means no `T.Hom`. This generalizes E817.
- **Combining independent theories:** two theories written by different people can be combined without changing either.
  - Today this is refused: `Magma` and `Action` both have `M`, and renaming both carriers to one name clashes too. I checked this.
  - Decided: carriers with the same name, kind and indices merge into one.
  - Operations, constants and laws stay the parents'. A clash makes the name or operator ambiguous only where it is used, and it stays reachable through the parent's label: `B.magma.mul`, `x B.magma.(*) y`, `magma.(x * x)`.
  - Renaming in `extends` is optional, never required.
  - The acceptance adds the cross-parent fixtures that `cubist-tests/theories.cubist` lacks.
- **Qualified operators:** `a G.(+) b`, `G.(-) x`, and `G.(+)` as a function. Parent operators are reached through labels: `x R.additive.(*) y`.

## Notation ([notation roadmap](docs/roadmaps/notation.md), decisions 7 and 8)
- **One selection form, `open`:** at a file's top level and in blocks, taking a model or a named notation.
  - It binds notation, plus field names for a model.
  - `x.(e)` is the one-expression form, like OCaml's local open.
  - It replaces the proposed `using v;`; `using` stays only in `simpa … using h`.
- **Open questions recorded:**
  - the selection word (`open`, or a plainer one such as `use`);
  - the word "view", which collides with MMT/OBJ theory morphisms and with L2.7's `match … using view`;
  - how a qualified operator's operands are read.

## Work plan
- L2.4c gets its own row, and becomes first action 2, before L2.10k (which needs the named universe) and before N1 (which needs the families).
- `using nat;` becomes `open nat;` throughout.

## Checks
- Every relative link and anchor in the edited files resolves.
- I checked the claims about today's behaviour on small programs:
  - the `Magma`/`Action` refusal, with and without renaming;
  - `Loop` checking with the circle as a model, but having no `Hom`;
  - models not lifting from `U0` to `U1`.

author: meven-clanker
body:
Closes MAG-182 (https://linear.app/meven/issue/MAG-182)

## Changes
- `IngredientFromCiqualResolver::resolve` reports the ingredient it creates through a by-reference `$created` list (no shared state in the service).
- `CreateRecipeHandler` / `UpdateRecipeHandler` call `EntityBroadcaster::broadcast()` for each created ingredient after the flush. The handlers return the recipe, so the Messenger middlewares never saw the ingredient: it was in Postgres but not in Elasticsearch (where `/api/products` is served from) nor on Mercure.
- Out of scope: the other handlers (PR #54).

## Verification
- Tests written red first: `CreateRecipeHandlerTest` and `UpdateRecipeHandlerTest` assert `IndexDocumentCommand` for `Ingredient` and a publish on `/ingredients/<id>`; a reused ingredient is not broadcast again (exactly one update, the recipe's). The Ciqual fake moved to `FakesCiqualTrait`.
- `task wt:test:api -- modules/cookbook/tests`: 156 tests green. `task fix:all`, `e2e:web:lint`, `e2e:web:typecheck` clean.
- E2E: new journey in `recipes-ciqual.spec.ts` (the serial Ciqual file, rather than `recipes.spec.ts`: it shares the food base and the one-worker constraint). A recipe with a never-used Ciqual food (20009 Carotte, crue) makes the ingredient appear in `/api/products` with no reindex. Not run locally: CI runs the e2e.

## Decisions
- **Dilemma**: how the handlers learn which ingredients were created. **Options**: stateful `pullCreated()` on the resolver; check `UnitOfWork` scheduled inserts; out-param. **Choice**: out-param. **Why**: the resolver is a shared service in a long-lived worker, a buffer would leak after a failed handler.
- ES serving verified: `Product` collections use `ElasticsearchCollectionProvider`, so the defect was Elasticsearch as well as Mercure.

## Review
1 round, `ACCEPT`. No blocking finding. Minor left as is: broadcast sits before the meal/grocery sync in `UpdateRecipeHandler`; `$created` is optional so a future caller could forget it; pre-existing duplicate when the same code appears twice in one recipe.
