author: jwinarske
body:
Consumer-camera mode has named the shared world space since rev 2 and never said
what it is. "Producer emits tile-local transforms in the shared world space" is not
a contract until the space is one, and both sides have to build against it.

| term | decided |
| --- | --- |
| units | Web Mercator metres about the origin, times that origin's latitude cosine -- one factor per view, so a model, a speed, a physics body and an audio distance are all true metres |
| origin | the consumer's, tile-aligned, one per view, **not on the wire** -- a tile's placement is derivable from its own id, which is what keeps a bucket camera-free (§5.1) |
| axes | a **relabel**, not a rotation: producer is x east, y *south*, height z; a y-up consumer takes `(x, y, h)` to `(x, h, y)` |
| wrap | the consumer's, `TileId::wrap` times the world span at that zoom |
| heights | metres, **unscaled** -- the latitude cosine is the ground plane's, not a building's |
| depth bias | the consumer's, from `layer_index` and `sub_layer_index` |
| advisory | every per-drawable matrix and the camera block's projection |

Three of those are worth more than their line.

**The axes are a relabel with no sign flip**, because east cross up is south and the
producer's `y` is already south-positive. Verified rather than assumed: raster rows
run "top to bottom" (`tessella-layout/src/raster.rs`), an extrusion puts height in
`z` (`fill_extrusion.mat` writes `vec4(footprint + decimals, z, 1.0)`), and
Fluorite is y-up (Jolt takes `Vec3(0, autostepMaxHeight, 0)`). A z-up consumer has
nothing to do at all.

**Heights are the one place this frame is not uniform.** A horizontal metre is
scaled and a vertical metre is not, so the two are the same unit at different
scales. Said plainly because it is exactly the asymmetry someone tidies away later.

**Advisory means do not bind.** The producer still computes a fused matrix and a
projection in this mode, for its own cover and placement, and a consumer that bound
one would place geometry through a camera a frame stale -- which looks like lag, not
like a contract violation. `pixelsPerMeter` is advisory for the same reason: it is
derived from the producer's zoom.

`CameraMode::Consumer` and the generated C header now point at the definition
rather than restating it; the header diff is comment-only and the web mirror is
unchanged.

Gate: clippy pinned and stable, rustdoc under `-D warnings`, the wasm32 `no_std`
lane, 2199 tests, and the pixel gate with probes rebuilt -- every sweep row at the
gate, zero holes across all `terrain_cover_p` cameras, quad 22 / 22 / 22 / 32 with
`image_stable 1` and no manifest drift.

## Qué cambia

- Cada service vive en `lib/<service>/`, con un archivo por rol: `tables`, `types`, `validation`, `repository`, `queries`, `actions`, `schema.graphql` y `resolvers`. Salen `lib/services`, `lib/repositories` y `lib/types`; lo transversal queda en `lib/infra/` y `lib/shared/`.
- PostgreSQL pasa a Drizzle: el schema vive en `lib/*/tables.ts` y las migraciones las genera drizzle-kit (`db/migrations`), con el `EXCLUDE` de solapamiento como migración custom. Sale el runner propio (`db:status`, `db:rollback`, `db:mark`).
- Las lecturas pasan por GraphQL y las escrituras son Server Actions. El cliente de Server Components ejecuta el schema en el mismo proceso (`SchemaLink`), sin request HTTP a `/api/graphql`.
- Las fechas viajan como el scalar `DateTime` (ISO): la policy de bookings recibe las filas tal cual y desaparecen los adaptadores (`toCancellableRow` y compañía).
- Chat: el historial se renderiza en el server, el worker autoriza el join por membresía (sin ticket) y la reconexión hace `router.refresh()`.
- Auth sin refresh token: el access token dura 24h y sale la tabla `sessions`.
- `.claude/rules/02-services.md` reemplaza a `02-backend.md` como referencia de services; `07-frontend.md` queda al día y el resto de las reglas se marcan como desactualizadas.
- La auditoría de services queda en `docs/audit/02-services-audit.md`, y sus hallazgos de seguridad aparte, en `docs/audit/security/services.md`.

## Por qué

El código estaba organizado por capa técnica: una feature quedaba repartida en cinco carpetas, los tipos se importaban por dos caminos y los services eran largos por boilerplate. Las lecturas iban a veces por GraphQL y a veces directo al service. Con este refactor hay un único patrón, chequeable con la regla 02, para desarrollar y auditar cada service.

> Requiere correr `pnpm db:migrate` sobre una base nueva: las migraciones viejas se reemplazaron por las de Drizzle. Se mergea junto con el PR hermano, porque cambió el contrato de `JOIN_CHAT`.

author: javamomma
body:
## Summary

Adds `/litigation-legal:cite-check`, a skill that checks every authority in a brief, memo, or letter before it is filed or sent. litigation-legal has citation guardrails in its CLAUDE.md and coverage rules in brief-section-drafter, but no skill that runs the check on a finished document.

The skill runs two checks in order:

1. Existence. Every cited case must be located in a primary source under the name, court, and year the document gives it. A case is located only when the opinion itself has been opened and matches; a search snippet, a secondary source, or a similarly named case in another court does not count. A case not located in any source is reported as not located and produces a FAIL verdict. There is no lenient mode.
2. Substance. For located cases, quotations are checked verbatim against the opinion, and parentheticals and characterized holdings are checked against what the court held, including partial support. Statutes and regulations are checked for existence and verbatim text.

Verdicts are PASS, PASS WITH CORRECTIONS, and FAIL. The skill never edits the document.

## Design notes

The workflow is built around four behaviors of the CourtListener citation tools observed on a test passage (documented in the skill's "Known behavior" section):

1. `analyze_citations` deduplicates by reporter string, so a fabricated case name attached to a real citation is merged into the real case's cluster. In the test, "Hartwell v. Superior Ore Co., 463 U.S. 29 (1983)" was merged into State Farm and was not flagged. The skill compares the name, court, and year at every occurrence against the resolved record.
2. The tool's case-name parser produced a false WARNING on "Motor Vehicle Mfrs. Ass'n" (parsed as "Ass'"). WARNINGs are treated as leads, not findings.
3. A real state supreme court decision (954 N.W.2d 584) returned NOT FOUND, the same result as the fabricated citation. Every NOT FOUND gets a second-source search by case name before any conclusion.
4. The `case_name` search filter missed the long official caption of that case; a quoted party phrase in `q` found it.

The skill follows the plugin's conventions: practice-profile citation format, matter workspaces, the reviewer note, source-provenance tags, and the verification log. One deliberate difference: log lines read "checked by /cite-check against [source]" rather than "verified by [name]," because the plugin's CLAUDE.md says a skill's output is never verified by the skill itself.

## Testing

Tested:
- The existence protocol (citation extraction, citation lookup, per-occurrence match, and second-source search by name) on a five-citation sample through the claude.ai CourtListener connector, with web search as the second source. The fabricated name on a real citation and the fabricated citation came out not located; the real case that returned NOT FOUND was found by name.
- `claude plugin validate` on `litigation-legal` and on the marketplace manifest. Both pass; the only warning (plugin-root CLAUDE.md not loaded as project context) predates this change.

Not tested:
- An end-to-end run of the installed `/litigation-legal:cite-check` skill.
- The tool names assume the plugin's `https://mcp.courtlistener.com/` server exposes the same `extract_citations`, `analyze_citations`, `resume_citation_analysis`, `search`, and `read_document` tools as the claude.ai CourtListener connector.

`scripts/validate.py` and `scripts/lint-tool-scope.py` cover managed-agent cookbooks, not plugin skills, so they do not apply to this change.

## Changes

- `litigation-legal/skills/cite-check/SKILL.md` (new)
- `litigation-legal/README.md`: command and skills table rows
- `README.md`: agents and command table rows
- `litigation-legal/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`: 1.0.2 → 1.1.0 (new skill)

author: jesseditson
body:
`ValuePath::add_child` and `ValuePath::remove_child` call `Vec::insert` / `Vec::remove` without a bounds check, so an `AddChild` or `RemoveChild` event whose index is past the end of the list panics inside `Archival::send_event` rather than answering an error. A host applying events it did not build itself, such as a client's stale index or an automated caller batching removals whose indexes shift as it goes, can only recover by catching the unwind. In a wasm host that panic aborts the module.

- `add_child` with `Some(index)` where `index > len` and `remove_child` where `index >= len` now return `ValuePathError::IndexOutOfRange(path, len)` and leave the object unchanged. `path` includes the offending index.
- `without_last` returned `self.0[..1]`, the first component only, so it was right only for a one-level path like `links.2`. It now drops just the last component (`sections.1.items.2` → `sections.1.items`), and an empty path stays empty. Nothing in this crate calls it; downstream callers that use it to find a child's list were wrong for nested children.

**Compatibility:** `IndexOutOfRange` is a new variant on `ValuePathError`, which is not `#[non_exhaustive]`, so an exhaustive `match` on it downstream needs a new arm. `without_last` changes behaviour for paths deeper than two components.

## Testing
- New unit tests in `value_path::tests`: `add_child_past_the_end_is_an_error`, `remove_child_past_the_end_is_an_error`, `without_last_drops_only_the_last_component`.
- `./pre-commit.sh` passes: versions, plugin tests, fmt, clippy `--all-features --all-targets`, `test.sh`, action and schema validation.

The commit used `--no-verify` because the hook fails in a git worktree for an unrelated reason: git sets `GIT_DIR` for hooks, and `plugins/archival/test.sh`'s `site-info.sh` case then sees its temp dir as a repo ("git=yes, expected no"). It passes when run directly, and the full `pre-commit.sh` run above passed.

body:
Desktop apps on macOS, Windows and Linux are tested as people use them, through the operating system's accessibility tree (ADR 0011), with the pointer and the keyboard, as they ship: no build wired for testing.

- Drivers in pure Go, no cgo: AX on macOS (purego), UI Automation and the Java Access Bridge on Windows, AT-SPI over D-Bus with XTest on Linux.
- app-core holds the steps every app takes, worded once (ADR 0012): launched, restarted, a control tapped or clicked, a field filled, a control scrolled into view; what the app shows, a control shown, enabled or disabled, a field's value, a screenshot. mobile-core moves onto it.
- desktop-core carries those steps out on desktops, with keys, a click at a place and a drag; the desktop a scenario claims as it registers its app; the app's home emptied on first use; waits, failures with the window and an outline of its tree; id= and xpath= selectors; screenshots per platform and scale; an app's files through its file context.
- desktop-macos, desktop-windows and desktop-linux register apps per OS (the depot macos app with the following properties:) and reset what each OS keeps beyond the home: a bundle's preferences, the registry keys a registration names (the user's own kept aside and put back). Linux runs desktops of axx's own, a session and accessibility bus per scenario, and with more than one desktop a user and mount namespace in which an app's home is at one path on every desktop. axx doctor checks each OS.
- axx.yaml's apps are services; a files folder names its owner (service:parcels, app:depot) and paths with spaces are quoted.
- The depot desk (examples/parcels/depot-desk) is built with every toolkit: AppKit, SwiftUI, WinForms, WPF, WinUI, GTK 3, GTK 4, Qt 5, Qt 6, Swing, Electron, Tauri and Flutter. One journey through the packs' steps passes on all 9 Windows builds, all 8 Linux builds (two desktops at once too), and 6 of 8 on macOS: Qt keeps its settings there in a preferences domain no registration names yet.
- mobile-ios waits for Notification Center to close before the app takes taps.

body:
## AUDIT-100 B60 (static bundle and shell on free Cloudflare Pages), A3

One switch, `NEXT_PUBLIC_PX_STATIC_BASE`. It is **unset by default, so production behaves exactly as it does today.** When it is set, it moves `/_next/static/**` (via `assetPrefix`), the release manifest and bundle, and the chrome's logo to a separate static host. The service worker serves that host's URLs from the verified release, so offline still works. Every byte is still checked against the manifest. Cache keys and registry hashes do not change.

- `scripts/stage-static-pages.mjs` builds the Pages upload folder from a verified release. It writes `_headers` (CORS `*`, immutable code, `no-cache` on release.json) and a real `404.html`.
- `scripts/publish-static-pages.mjs` runs as `postbuild`. It does nothing while the switch is off. When the switch is on, it uploads with wrangler, keeps the previous release's chunks, and fails the build on any error.
- `scripts/verify/static-pages-live.mjs` is a read-only check of the real Pages host.
- **Deployed:** the free Pages project `projexa-static` at https://projexa-static.pages.dev now serves the live release 2026.10.05-796. All 383 of 383 files and the bundle match byte for byte, and CORS, cache and 404 behave as intended (evidence JSON). A deliberately broken preview (one wrong byte, one missing file) was flagged: 2 bad files, exit 1.
- **Tests:** `static-host.test.ts` (23 unit tests). Seen to fail: 5 tests fail when the SW branch is removed, 4 fail when the installer's base is ignored. `e2e/lf-static-host.spec.ts` uses a real browser on a production build with the switch on and a static host on a separate origin. Measured: **0 static files from the app origin**, the app works offline, and a dropped or corrupted bundle is refused. Seen to fail: with the SW branch disabled, the offline step fails; with the env missing at run time, 6 files came from the app origin.
- `ai-os/audit37/STATIC_ON_CLOUDFLARE_PAGES.md` describes the owner's 3-step switch, which is not done here.

author: jperezdealgaba
body:
## Summary

When encoder CUDA graphs are enabled, replay copies into fixed-size capture buffers. A legal video (or other multimodal) batch whose leading buffer dimension exceeds that capacity previously raised in the padded copy path and terminated the shared engine. Detect oversize replay tensors before the copy and fall back to eager encoder execution for that batch.

## Changes

- `vllm/v1/worker/encoder_cudagraph.py`: add `_replay_exceeds_capture`; return `None` from `_run_budget_graph` when replay does not fit; fall back to `encoder_eager_forward` instead of asserting.
- `tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py`: unit coverage for the capacity check; GPU regression that oversized replay falls back to eager without crashing.

## Codepath coverage

- All encoder CUDA-graph execute paths go through `_execute_local` → `_run_budget_graph` (including DP sharding and multi-path budgets). The guard sits on that shared sink.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open/merged PRs for `encoder_cudagraph`, `max_frames_per_batch`, `cu_seqlens`, and eager video fallback. Open draft #43403 proposes a related per-item `T > frames_per_item` fallback against an older single-path manager; it does not apply to the current multi-path `_execute_local`. This PR closes the sink model-agnostically on current `main` by comparing replay vs capture buffer shapes.

## Tests

- `TestReplayExceedsCapture` (fits / exceeds / scalars-and-missing)
- `test_eager_fallback_when_replay_buffer_exceeds_capture` (GPU; oversized captured buffer → eager)
- Commands:
  - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py -v -k "TestReplayExceedsCapture or TestGenerateBudgets or TestFindBudgetGraph or TestGetCumulativeStats or TestGetInputModality or TestInitInvariant"` → 38 passed

author: gumclaw
body:
## What

The product thumbnail picker advertises `.webp`, but the server rejects it, so a WebP that passes through unchanged fails validation with a message that does not name the format.

## Why

Fixes antiwork/gumroad-private#3272. `Thumbnail::ALLOW_CONTENT_TYPES` (`/jpeg|gif|png|jpg/i`) does not match `image/webp`, while the picker (`app/javascript/utils/file.ts` → `ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS`) offers `webp` and `prepareImageForUpload` passes an already-small WebP through unchanged.

The failure is size-dependent, which is what makes it hard to diagnose: a WebP that needs resizing is re-encoded to PNG client-side and succeeds, so the same format works or fails depending on the file's dimensions.

## Fix

Add `webp` to `Thumbnail::ALLOW_CONTENT_TYPES`.

This matches what the picker already offers, and the rest of the pipeline already handles the format: ActiveStorage classifies `image/webp` as variable, and the configured variant processor (MiniMagick over ImageMagick) reads and writes WebP.

## Scope

- In scope: the thumbnail uploader's server-side content-type allowlist.
- Out of scope, deliberately: the generic "Could not process your thumbnail, please try again." copy for genuinely unsupported types (svg, tiff, …). Rewriting that message is a separate UX change, not this format mismatch.
- Out of scope, deliberately: `AssetPreview` (product covers) still excludes WebP, and its own picker (`CoverEditor`) does not offer it either, so that path is internally consistent. Left alone rather than widened.
- Out of scope: uploaders that embed images through direct upload (description, profile sections) have no server-side content-type allowlist, so they were never affected.

## Design

The allowlist is the only gate that rejects WebP; every other thumbnail check (size, squareness, 600px floor) is format-agnostic. Adding the format is the whole change — no client change and no re-encode, so an untouched WebP stays WebP.

## Build

Four commits on this branch.

## QA

Both spec files run locally at `72679c26ac`.

```text
bundle exec rspec spec/models/thumbnail_spec.rb                     # 19 examples, 0 failures
bundle exec rspec spec/requests/products/edit/thumbnails_spec.rb    #  4 examples, 0 failures
```

The second file is the real-browser system spec: it drives the product editor, attaches a WebP, and asserts the uploaded thumbnail renders in the Thumbnail section. The WebP is built from the existing `smilie.png` fixture at spec time — a committed binary is refused by the review panel and escalates the spec selector as an unmapped `spec/support` change.

Mutation check — reverting only the allowlist line makes both new layers fail:

- `spec/models/thumbnail_spec.rb` → both new examples fail with `Validation failed: Could not process your thumbnail, please try again.`
- `spec/requests/products/edit/thumbnails_spec.rb` → fails because no thumbnail is saved.

The URL assertion checks the bucket *and* that the URL differs from `url(variant: :original)`, because `Thumbnail#url` falls back to the original file's URL when processing fails and that URL shares the bucket; stubbing `thumbnail_variant` to raise makes the assertion fail. The neighbouring png case had the same weakness and got the same assertion.

No screenshot is attached on purpose: this is a server-side predicate change in a backend-only diff, and a still cannot show a file's format. The browser-driven system spec above is the end-to-end evidence — it exercises the real upload path rather than a reconstruction.

## Checklist

- [x] Scope, one line in a model allowlist; no client change.
- [x] Design, as above.
- [x] Build, four commits on this branch.
- [x] QA, specs, mutation check and assertion probe above.
- [x] Shipped, not yet.
- [x] Market, n/a.
- [x] Sell, n/a.

Premerge review: clean @ 72679c26ac62f9aea71f82a8f4f4d737b33b403f

---

author: derobins
body:
hipObject has no GPU kernels. It only calls the HIP runtime API from the host, and the hip::host target already provides the headers, __HIP_PLATFORM_AMD__, and the amdhip64 link. Compiling the sources as HIP gained nothing and caused several problems:

- Every translation unit got a device compile pass for the default offload arch (gfx906), roughly doubling compile work and wrapping the objects in empty offload bundles.
- HIP sources ignored the CMAKE_CXX_* settings, so the library was built with different flags than the tests (e.g. Debug was -g -O for HIP but -g for CXX), and CMAKE_CXX_CLANG_TIDY never ran on the library sources.
- The exported hipobj target set its link interface language to HIP, so consumers needed the HIP language enabled to link it.
- Configuring required a HIP compiler.

Drop HIP from project(LANGUAGES) and remove the LANGUAGE HIP source properties from the library, examples, unit test objects, and the minio-cpp example. Remove the OFFLOAD_ARCH cache variable and its rocminfo detection, which never fed into CMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES.

Remove -DCMAKE_HIP_COMPILER from the CI workflows, the ERNIC local runner, the Cursor environment, and AGENTS.md. Update the compiler requirement in README, INSTALL, and the Sphinx docs, which listed hipcc. CMAKE_HIP_PLATFORM stays, since find_package(hip) still reads HIP_PLATFORM.

body: The stack model's first provisioner, built as `extensions/pulumi`, a Go module of its own (stack-model.md sections 6.5, 6.6 and 13). Every part is tested without cloud credentials. ## Core change (small, breaking for other provisioners) - `Provisioner.Render(graph, dir)` becomes `Render(env *ir.ResolvedEnvironment, dir)`. The program exports every output the environment references, and some references sit outside the graph: an uncalled server's address, binding values, DNS records. Bindings need those exports. `stacktest.FakeProvisioner` and the registry test stub follow the new signature. - `ProvisionRequest` gains `Backend registry.StateBackend{URL, SecretsProvider}`: `gs://` and `gcpkms://` for the gcp target, `file://` and `passphrase` in tests. ## Render: Pulumi YAML - The project is named after the stack (`shop`). Each run is a stack of it: `staging`, or `preview.pr-123` for a member of a parameterized environment. - Parameters are string config, so no value reaches the file. - One resource per node: - its key is the node ID with characters outside `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` turned into `-`, and its `name:` is the node ID, so URNs keep the ID; - references render as `${key.output}`, property paths included; - `options.dependsOn`, and `options.version` from `Extension.ProviderVersions` (the distribution passes `gcp.ProviderVersion`); - literal `$` is escaped. - Inherited nodes are read through a stack reference to the parent environment's stack. - Outputs are every node's `id` and every referenced output, each exported as `.`. - Goldens cover the acme-shop environments resolved by `stacktest`, the integration test's graphs and an edge-case graph. ## Driver: Automation API over the rendered directory - `Plan` runs a preview and maps engine steps to create, update, replace or delete. - `Apply(step)` runs `up --target` over the step's nodes. - It also targets resources the program dropped that depend on those nodes. A targeted update deletes them, and the CLI refuses unless they are targets. - The last step that holds nodes runs an untargeted `up`, which deletes whatever else the graph dropped. - A member first checks that the parent's stack exports what it reads. A stack reference would read a missing output as null. - `Destroy` removes the stack. - `Outputs` drops secrets, and the unknown placeholder a step not yet applied leaves behind. - Clear errors for a stale program, a missing backend or secrets provider, and a missing CLI (`ErrNoCLI`). - A fresh checkout has no stack settings file, so the driver writes the request's secrets provider into it. ## Bindings (`extensions/pulumi/bindings`) The generator reads `environment.json` and `outputs.json` (the new outputs file format) and writes two packages: - **Values:** `shopstack.Staging.ShopAPI.Address` and `.Account.Email`. There is one field per deployable, and outputs are typed from the outputs files. - **Stack references, for hand-written Pulumi programs:** `shopstackpulumi.Staging(ctx)` and `shopstackpulumi.Preview(ctx, "123")`. Goldens, plus a compile test that vets both packages and a program using them, then runs the program's script half. ## Tests and CI - `TestProvisionRandom` runs against a `file://` backend with the `random` provider, pinned at 4.21.2: plan, apply step by step, outputs, a change (replace and delete), a second member, a fresh directory, then destroy. - It skips without the CLI, and fails under `SUPERSCHEMATIC_REQUIRE_PULUMI=1`. - It passed locally against CLI 3.259.0 and 3.267.0. - The module joins `GO_MODULES` and the CI module loop and lint. CI installs the CLI with `pulumi/actions` (pinned SHA) at `PULUMI_VERSION=3.259.0` from tools.env. A test keeps that equal to the SDK version, v3.259.0, the newest whose `go` directive fits Go 1.26.4. - `go-goldens` now runs each package's tests in its own module. - The superscalar pin test checks this module's go.mod too. ## Not in this PR - The gcp lowering (#242), bootstrap, and `stack deploy`. - An environment naming a hand-written program for the provisioner to apply after the stack (6.6). The Stack IR has no field for it. - The parent of a member is named without parameter values, so a parameterized parent isn't supported. The pre-check reports that case clearly. Expect small conflicts with the gcp target PR in `Makefile` `GO_MODULES`, the ci.yml loop and lint steps, and `superscalar_pin_test.go`. Keep both sides. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: vito
body:
## What and why

Every layer that converts identifier casing makes its own guess about acronyms, and the guesses disagree:

- The engine normalizes module names with `strcase`, which lowercases runs of capitals unless the whole name is a registered acronym: `LLMContentBlock` → `LlmcontentBlock`, `MyMod` + `HTTPClient` → `MyModHttpclient`. `core/llm.go` papers over this with one `strcase.ConfigureAcronym` per affected core type, and `withFinalTypeName` exists only because re-normalizing a final name corrupts it.
- SDK codegen has at least seven independent converters. Python, Rust and Elixir generate `prerequisite_sh_as`. The same core type is `JSONValue` in Go/TypeScript/Python/Elixir and `JsonValue` in Rust/PHP.

This PR adds one implementation, `engine/naming`. It parses a name in any casing into words (ordinary words, acronyms like `HTTP`, and terms with a fixed spelling like `GitHub`, `IPv6`) using a dictionary of acronyms and terms, falling back to a case heuristic. It formats those words in any casing (`PASCAL`, `CAMEL`, `SNAKE`, `SCREAMING_SNAKE`, `KEBAB`, `FLAT`), in either acronym style (`HTTPClient` / `HttpClient`). The dictionary is structured so it can later be selected by engine version: an addition must never rename anything for a module on an older version.

Design: [`hack/designs/identifier-casing.md`](https://github.com/vito/dagger/blob/identifier-casing/hack/designs/identifier-casing.md) (parsing algorithm, guarantees, test vectors, rollout plan).

## What's in this PR

- **`engine/naming`**: parser, formatter, initial dictionary. Tests cover every row of the design's test-vector table and the three guarantees (round trip, idempotence, canonical names come back unchanged). A schema test checks every core type, field, argument and enum name in `docs/docs-graphql/schema.graphqls`: all type names are canonical, and field/argument names are canonical except the 7 the design lists (`asSdkName`, `callId`, `filterUri`, `parentShas`, `pushUrl`, `shortSha`, `withoutUri`).
- **Core API** (`@experimental`, visible from `v1.0.0-0`): `Query.identifier`, `Query.formatIdentifiers` (returns plain strings, so codegen formats thousands of names in one round trip), `Query.namingDictionary`, plus `Identifier`, `IdentifierWord`, `NamingTerm`, `IdentifierWordKind`, `Casing`, `AcronymStyle`. Integration test: `TestIdentifier`.
- **Storage codecs** for `Identifier`, `IdentifierWord` and `NamingTerm`. They store the parsed words rather than re-parsing, so a cached identifier formats the same even if the dictionary changes. Covered by the existing restart test.
- **Regenerated** schema snapshot, API reference pages, and the Go, Python, TypeScript, Elixir, PHP and Rust clients.
- **Design docs**: the new design, plus a separate commit that moves three existing root design docs (`migrate-settings-hints-tracking.md`, `single-query-workspace-module-loading.md`, `workspace-location-model.md`) into `hack/designs/`.

## Out of scope

Nothing about how existing names are produced changes yet. Steps 3–6 of the design's plan come later:

- switching the engine's own normalization (`core/gqlformat.go`, `namespaceObject`, CLI kebab names) to `engine/naming`
- selecting the dictionary by engine version (there is one dictionary for now)
- removing `strcase.ConfigureAcronym` and `withFinalTypeName`
- migrating each SDK's codegen to `formatIdentifiers`

## Where the implementation departs from the original design (the doc now matches)

- **Digits stay in an ordinary word's text** (`base64`, `foo_2` → `foo2`); only acronyms and terms take digits as a suffix (`OAuth`+`2`). This is how the test vectors write them.
- **A fourth segmentation tiebreak** (fewest words, counting digit-only ones) so a heuristic word keeps its digits (`ABC2`).
- **`GraphQL`'s capitalized form is `GraphQL`**, treated as a brand like `GitHub`.
- **All-caps input splits by dictionary cover.** Each chunk of all-caps input splits where dictionary entries cover it completely, as runs of capitals do in mixed-case input: `JSONAPI` → `JSON`·`API`, `HTMLURL` → `HTML`·`URL`, while `HTTP_CLIENT` and `HTTPX_CLIENT` are unchanged. Lowercase input never splits. Without this, PASCAL names made only of acronyms (`JSONAPI`) wouldn't come back unchanged. Lowercase never splits but uppercase does, so `SSHFS` was added to the dictionary to keep `sshfsVolume` stable through `SCREAMING_SNAKE`.

Refs #13668


<!-- dagger:sdl-diff:start -->

body:
Drive #558. The return path a device-approval sign-in must land on now travels with the link's token instead of the one browser's cookie, the device code lives 15 minutes, and the mail and sign-in page both say the link can be opened on any device.

Merged `origin/main` into this branch (main had moved auth and the device store into `core/`, and 0020 was already two other migrations). The approve page itself is main's: it names the device and time and does not pre-fill the code (drive#518).

## What changed

- `migrations/drive/0031_signin_return.sql` — one new table `signin_return` (token_hash PK, return_path, created_at) plus its index. Numbered 0031 because 0020 is already two files on main. Expand only: no drop, no rename, no NOT NULL column added to an old table. Phase 1 of 1.
- `core/auth.js` — `storeSigninReturn` / `consumeSigninReturn` (sweep-then-insert in one batch, keyed by `sha256Hex(token)`, single-use by read-then-delete, `safeAfterSigninPath` re-checked on read). The magic-link plugin's `sendMagicLink` writes the row **before** the mail goes out: a row that cannot be written is a 503 (email-failed words), never a link whose landing page is already lost. `signinLinkEmail` still names the asking device and time (drive#550) and adds the #558 sentence when the start carried an approve path.
- `src/signin.js` — `readStart` returns `next: safeAfterSigninPath(body.next)` (a dropped path is a plain sign-in, not a 400); the start forwards it as `metadata: { returnPath }`; the verify tail prefers the stored row over the after-signin cookie (lookup failure is caught-and-logged, the cookie still carries the intent).
- `public/signin.html` — the page shows the device note when it was opened with `?next=`, and the start post carries `next`; a plain sign-in posts exactly what it posted before.
- `core/device-signin.js` — `DEVICE_CODE_TTL_SECONDS` 600 → 900 (the CLI reads the TTL off the server's answer, so no CLI change).
- `core/keystore.js` — the in-memory stand-in forwards `describeUserCode` to the same inner store its other device methods use.
- `test/harness.mjs` — the short sign-in schema list applies `0031_signin_return.sql`.

No new routes, no new dependencies, no new secrets (nothing under 'Secrets to set'), no CLI change.

## Scope

- `scope: core/auth.js` because main moved `src/auth.js` into `core/` (drive#648).
- `scope: core/device-signin.js` because main moved `workers/api/src/device-signin.js` into `core/`.
- `scope: core/keystore.js` because main moved `workers/api/src/keystore.js` into `core/`.
- `scope: test/harness.mjs` because the short sign-in schema list must apply the new table.
- `scope: migrations/drive/0031_signin_return.sql` because 0020 is already two files on main, and a new duplicate prefix is refused.

## Verification

1. The return path travels with the magic-link token server-side, so a second device lands on the approve page:
```
✔ a sign-in started on the approve page lands there from a second browser (drive#558) (28.748356ms)
✔ the stored return path wins over a stale after-signin cookie (drive#558) (23.298895ms)
✔ a start whose next is not the approve page is a plain sign-in (drive#558) (95.622411ms)
```
`node --test test/signin.test.mjs` — 54 pass, 0 fail. Real SQLite write/read of the new table: `node --test test/integration/signin-return-d1.test.mjs` — 5/5 pass.

2. The mail and the sign-in page say "open this link on the computer you ran drive login on, or approve from any device":
```
✔ the mail's device line and the page's device note are one sentence (drive#558) (0.901745ms)
```
Pinned to `SIGNIN_COPY.deviceNote` (`src/signin.js:165`) and `signinLinkEmail` (`core/auth.js`).

3. A device code lives 15 minutes while a sign-in is pending (`DEVICE_CODE_TTL_SECONDS = 15 * 60` at `core/device-signin.js:99`):
```
✔ a code is still pending and approvable at minute 12 (drive#558) (2.293819ms)
✔ a code is still pending and approvable at minute 12 over the real migration (drive#558) (2.098042ms)
```

4. Tests the issue asked for: a sign-in completed in a second browser still reaches the approve page with the code; a code polled at minute 12 is still valid. The four files above: **111 pass, 0 fail**.

- `npm run check` exit 0 (typecheck + Biome; remaining warnings pre-date this PR and are on pages it does not own).

author: sjanel
body:
A write on a connection the peer has already reset raises SIGPIPE, whose default action terminates the process: a client leaving in the middle of a response could kill a server that did not ignore SIGPIPE, and a server closing the connection during an upload could do the same to an HttpClient user.

- Plain transports write with send() / sendmsg() and MSG_NOSIGNAL instead of write() / writev() (and read with recv()), skipping the file layer checks too.
- sendfile() and OpenSSL's own socket writes (records, handshake, close_notify) cannot pass that flag: the new SigpipeBlocker keeps SIGPIPE blocked in the calling thread, where a write-raised SIGPIPE stays pending, and discards it before restoring the mask. The server event loop holds one for its whole run, HttpClient one per TLS or file-body exchange. Blockers nest; the process-wide SIGPIPE disposition is left untouched.

author: frapercan
body:
## La cifra que sostenía el diseño está mal por 3,2x

El driver guardaba los 75 GAF para que la fase 2 los reusara, y su docstring decía por qué: *«the whole series is 247 GB against 654 GB free»*. Medido con `HEAD` sobre las 75 releases:

| | |
|---|---|
| serie completa | **802 GB** |
| release más pequeña | 156, con 3,3 GB |
| release más grande | 226, con 22,7 GB |
| libre | 618 GB |
| en caché | 41 GB |
| faltaba bajar | 761 GB |

El disco se habría llenado bajando la release **182, la 49ª de las 75**. La fase 1 moría a dos tercios, con el disco a cero, unas diez horas después de arrancar.

## El arreglo

Borrar cada GAF tras una pasada con éxito, igual que hace la fase 2. El pico de disco pasa de 802 GB a **una** release. En fallo se conserva, para que un reintento manual no tenga que volver a bajarlo.

Consecuencia aceptada y declarada: cada release se baja **dos veces** entre las dos fases, ~22 h de descarga por fase. Es el suelo del diseño de dos fases —que existe porque la fase 1 tiene que acabar antes de cargar nada— y no un desperdicio que se pueda optimizar.

## Por qué un caché filtrado no lo resuelve, medido

La idea obvia es guardar un filtrado en vez del bruto: el filtro de líneas crudas deja el 0,24% en la 156, así que la serie filtrada serían ~2 GB. **No funciona**, y lo dejo medido en el código para que no se reintente.

La fase 2 guarda **toda** fila cuyo accession esté en el universo y cuyo GO esté en el snapshot. Verificado en `_store_buffer`: son sus dos únicos filtros. **No filtra por código de evidencia, así que el `IEA` entra.** Y el universo no se conoce hasta que la fase 1 termina, de modo que un filtro aplicado durante la fase 1 sólo puede usar lo curado de esa release.

Medido sobre la 156 contra un universo de 1.084.103 miembros:

| | filas |
|---|---|
| del universo en la 156 | 7.997.773 |
| curadas (no IEA) | 1.167.668 |
| IEA | 6.830.105 |

| | accesiones |
|---|---|
| con filas en la 156 | 648.048 |
| con alguna curada **en** la 156 | 131.157 |
| **sin** ninguna curada en la 156 | 516.891 |

Un filtro «curado en esta release» tiraría **5.387.271 filas que la fase 2 necesita: el 67,4%**. Dos tercios del corpus.

El filtro **seguro** —accession en el universo completo— sí deja poco: esas 7.997.773 filas son el 2,85% de los 280.922.746 renglones, unos 23 GB para la serie entera. Pero sólo se puede calcular **después** de la fase 1, y releer cada bruto para aplicarlo ya es la segunda descarga. No ahorra nada frente a borrar.

Y la fase 1 desciende, así que el universo es más pequeño en las primeras pasadas, que son justo la ventana de evaluación 220→227: la pérdida se concentraría donde más duele.

## Estado

La fase 1 está corriendo ahora (release 235, universo ya en 1,1M). El run tiene ~10 h de margen antes del muro, así que el driver se reinicia en un límite de release para recoger el cambio; `universe_done()` lee de la base, así que reanuda sola por donde iba.

`MARCO-DECLARADO.md` recoge las dos cosas: la cifra corregida y la medición del filtro.

body:
## Summary

RFC for **model diffs**, following [discussion #1192](https://github.com/likec4/likec4/discussions/1192) and the approach in [this comment](https://github.com/likec4/likec4/discussions/1192#discussioncomment-11214267).

A `diff` block describes a planned change of the model (an RFC, a proposal). The model stays "as is" until the diff is applied. LikeC4 shows each view before and after the diff, applies or discards the diff as a text edit of the sources, reports diffs that change the same part of the model, and removes elements safely together with everything that references them.

**Please review the decisions D1–D7** in [section 12 of the RFC](https://github.com/edeak-jsq/likec4/blob/model-diffs-rfc/docs/requirements/model-diffs/rfc.md#12-decisions-requested): accept, change or reject each one, in a review comment or in the discussion.

## What is in this PR

- [`docs/requirements/model-diffs/rfc.md`](https://github.com/edeak-jsq/likec4/blob/model-diffs-rfc/docs/requirements/model-diffs/rfc.md): motivation, design, compatibility, security, alternatives, prior art, decisions requested, rollout, approval record.
- [`docs/requirements/model-diffs/implementation.md`](https://github.com/edeak-jsq/likec4/blob/model-diffs-rfc/docs/requirements/model-diffs/implementation.md): how it is implemented, package by package.
- [`docs/adrs/0002-model-diffs.md`](https://github.com/edeak-jsq/likec4/blob/model-diffs-rfc/docs/adrs/0002-model-diffs.md): ADR draft with the decisions D1–D7, set to accepted after the review.
- User documentation of the proposed feature, for review:
  - new page [`dsl/diff.mdx`](https://github.com/edeak-jsq/likec4/blob/model-diffs-rfc/apps/docs/src/content/docs/dsl/diff.mdx);
  - additions to `dsl/intro.mdx`, `tooling/cli.mdx`, `tooling/ai-tools.mdx`, `tooling/model-api.mdx`, `tooling/vite-plugin.mdx`;
  - the `likec4-dsl` skill references, and the docs TextMate grammar (highlighting of `diff`, `add`, `remove`).

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Do not merge yet.** The user documentation describes behavior that is not released. After the review, this PR keeps the RFC, the guide and the ADR, and the user documentation lands with the implementation PRs.

## Implementation

The implementation is complete and split into three PRs, opened after the review (RFC section 13):

1. **DSL and model**: grammar, parsing, model data, validation, core apply, compare views and removal impact.
2. **Edits and tooling**: apply, discard, safe delete, overlaps, LSP requests and code actions, SDK, CLI, MCP.
3. **UI**: diagram markers and style tokens, `likec4:diffs` virtual module, SPA, playground, e2e test.

Each PR has its docs and a `patch` changeset, and passes `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test` on its own. In total: about +7.7k / −0.2k lines in 114 files, no new dependencies.

author: wingfiring
body:
### Description

Three fixes in `ImageBufAlgo::resample()`:

* `IBAprep()` only clamps the ROI channel range to `dst`, so a `dst` with
  more channels than `src` read past the end of each source pixel, and a
  channel range outside `dst` came back inverted, which the kernels turned
  into a negative-size scratch allocation. Clamp the range to `src` as well,
  and do nothing if it ends up empty.

* `resample_hwy()` computed row pointers from the packed scanline size
  rather than the buffer's scanline stride, so it sampled the wrong pixels
  from sources with padded rows.

* `test_resample_correctness()` (added in #5395) is meant to compare the
  per-axis tables against the per-pixel path, but `HWY_TEST` leaves
  `enable_hwy` on, so in Highway builds one side went through
  `resample_hwy()` instead, which is not bit-exact, and the test failed.
  Turn Highway off for that check.

CI doesn't build with `OIIO_USE_HWY=ON`, which is why the last two weren't
caught there.

### Tests

New `test_resample_channel_bounds()` in `imagebufalgo_test` covers the
channel range cases. The stride fix is covered by the existing
`test_resample_correctness()`, which now passes in a Highway build.

Verified locally on Windows with `OIIO_USE_HWY=ON`: `unit_imagebufalgo`,
`oiiotool-xform`, and `oiiotool-xform.hwy` pass.

author: kyleboddy
body:
## Why

We want to serve the control room at `https://dc-boddydev.drivelinebaseball.com/moa-x/` through the shared Apache on 443, instead of on its own port (`:7340`). Every URL in the app was root-absolute: assets, API calls, the SSE stream, SPA routes and the URLs the server builds. Behind a path prefix, each of those requests left `/moa-x/`. The page loaded without styles and none of its JavaScript ran.

## What

- `ProxyFix(..., x_prefix=1)`: with `X-Forwarded-Prefix: /moa-x`, `request.script_root` becomes `/moa-x`. Without the header it is `""`, so direct access on the port behaves the same as before.
- Templates prefix every `href`/`src`/`srcset` and FontFace URL with `request.script_root`. The bootstrap gains `base_path`.
- `api.js` exports `BASE`. `request()`, uploads and `EventSource` prepend it. `app.js` routing strips `BASE` before matching and adds it back on `pushState`. Image literals and run links also use it.
- URLs the server builds inside a request now include `script_root`: agent-card avatars, artifact URLs, upload URLs and share URLs. The provider catalog avatars are cached and built on the monitor thread, outside any request, so the client adds `BASE` when it reads them.
- New profile cookies use `Path=script_root or "/"`.
- The report Share button calls `fetch("../share")` and matches the artifact path without a `^` anchor, so newly generated reports work under any prefix.
- One test covers the prefix and root renders. `docs/webui.md` has a paragraph on the proxy header.

## Verified

I put a throwaway Apache 2.4.58 (mpm_event, h2, TLS, the production deflate and reqtimeout config) in front of an isolated instance that had its own data dir, no worker and no provider monitor. Headless Chromium crawl results:

- Under `/moa-x/`: 0 requests escaped the prefix, 0 responses were 4xx/5xx, 0 requests failed and 0 console errors appeared.
- Deep links `/moa-x/runs/<id>`, `/moa-x/providers`, `/moa-x/new` and `/moa-x/runs` each render the right view.
- Sidebar navigation, Back and reload all stay under the prefix.
- Artifact and share URLs return 200.
- The SSE stream delivers events about 1.2s apart over h2, matching the rate they were written.
- At the bare port, without the header, everything is still clean.

Tests: `test_webui.py` 54 passed. `test_offline.py` 140/140 passed.

## Follow-up commit (d1f28dc)

- `api.js`: `BASE = window.MOAX_BOOTSTRAP.base_path`, with no fallback. `base.html` always sets the bootstrap, and `index()` is the only template render and always passes `base_path`.
- `report.py` `_esc` now also escapes `"`. Before this, `[x](https://x"onmouseover="…)` in a final plan put an `onmouseover` attribute into the report. A new check in `test_report_markdown_subset_renders` covers it. Under the portal, Apache also serves reports in a CSP sandbox.
- Tests: `test_offline.py` 140/140 passed, `test_webui.py` 54 passed.

author: kundanvarma
body:
Dependabot opened #164: Spring Boot **3.5.7 → 4.1.1 across all 42 service poms**. That is a framework migration, not a dependency bump — Framework 7, Security 7, Jakarta EE 11 — and its build never even read the POMs:

```
[ERROR] 'dependencies.dependency.version' for
        org.springframework.cloud:spring-cloud-starter-gateway:jar is missing.
[ERROR] The project com.bss:gateway:1.0.0 has 1 error
```

`services/gateway/pom.xml` imports the Spring Cloud BOM at **2025.0.1**, a Boot 3.x release train, which stops managing that starter's version under Boot 4. **Boot and Cloud move as a matched pair**, and the group pattern `org.springframework*` moves only one of them — so #164 could not have worked, at any amount of CI.

#164 is now closed, and the migration is planned in **#199** instead.

This PR adds the major-version ignore rule so the same unmergeable PR does not return every week. A recurring red PR nobody can act on is how a team learns to stop reading CI — and this session already found three real defects hiding behind gates nobody was reading.

**Minor and patch Spring updates are untouched** and still arrive weekly; only major bumps of the Boot parent and the Cloud BOM are held. Verified the config still parses, with both rules present.

author: juanjogondev
body:
## What and why

Everything that runs locally must also run in CI, and static checks should run once instead of once per operating system. Each OS job now only exercises what depends on the OS.

## How

- `ci.yml` is split into two parallel jobs (no `needs`):
  - **`Quality`** (ubuntu, once, full history): one visible step per gate — Typecheck, Authored source policy, ESLint, Prettier, knip, dependency-cruiser, Audit, and **Commitlint — commits** (PR commit range; skipped for bot authors, whose generated bodies exceed the line limit). Every gate runs even if another fails, so one run reports all failures.
  - **`Test — linux | macos | win`**: install, Chromium, `pnpm test:coverage`, `pnpm build`. No static gate is repeated.
- New **`pr-title.workflow.yml`** (`Commitlint — PR title`): the squash title is the commit that lands on `main`, so it is linted on `opened`, `edited`, `reopened` and `synchronize`, with its own concurrency group so a title edit never cancels the test matrix.
- CI runs for pull requests targeting **any** branch and restarts on every push to the PR branch (`synchronize` + `cancel-in-progress`), now locked by tests.
- Untrusted values (PR title, SHAs) reach the shell only through `env:`; action SHAs stay pinned.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` documents the CI jobs. SDD artifacts in `openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-05-ci-quality-gates/`.

## Testing

- [x] `pnpm quality` (2247 passed, 6 opt-in skipped)
- [x] `pnpm test:coverage`
- [x] `pnpm build`

`tests/unit/repository/workflows.test.ts` (58 tests) asserts the job layout, every gate step, env-only interpolation, triggers and concurrency; the new guard tests were mutation-checked. `actionlint` is clean on both workflows and commitlint passes over this PR's range.

## Risks and rollback

- Check names change: `CI — <os>` becomes `Quality`, `Test — linux|macos|win` and `Commitlint — PR title`. The `main` ruleset has no required status checks today, so nothing blocks; consider marking these as required after merge.
- Rollback: revert this PR.

## Checklist

- [x] The title is a Conventional Commit in English (`feat: ...`, `fix: ...`)
- [x] Tests were written first (strict TDD: RED, GREEN, REFACTOR)
- [x] Docs updated (README, SECURITY, CONTRIBUTING) where behavior changed
- [x] CHANGELOG impact considered: the release notes come from the PR title and labels
- [x] No AI attribution or `Co-Authored-By` trailers
- [x] No recordings or secrets are included

## ML part, Steps 1 to 3

Adds the `ml/` folder with the machine learning work for BugZero. No frontend files are changed.

### Dataset (Step 1)
* **PyVul** (MSR 2026): real vulnerabilities in Python packages. 1,400 vulnerable functions and 822 "hard safe" functions (other functions changed in the same fix).
* **Ordinary safe functions**: 1,363 functions from the same files that no security fix touched, matched to the vulnerable ones by project and length. Collected with `ml/datasets/fetch_ordinary_functions.py`.
* 3,585 functions from 323 projects. Project-wise split: train 2,878 (282 projects), test 707 (41 projects). No project is in both.

### CodeBERT embeddings (Step 2)
* Frozen `microsoft/codebert-base`, whitespace collapsed before tokenizing, max 512 tokens, mean pooling, so each function becomes 768 numbers.

### Classifier (Step 3)
Cross-validation by project on the train set (the test set is not used yet):

| Model | ROC-AUC |
|---|---|
| Always guess one class | 0.500 |
| Function length only | 0.530 |
| TF-IDF + Logistic Regression | 0.594 |
| **CodeBERT + Logistic Regression** | **0.594** |
| CodeBERT + Gradient Boosting | 0.578 |

CodeBERT + LR scores 0.634 against ordinary code and 0.531 against the hard same-commit functions. The task is hard, which matches the PyVul paper. Its confidences mostly sit between 36% and 61%, so the app should combine them with Bandit's own rating (planned for Step 7).

### Files
* `ml/training/BugZero_ML.ipynb`: notebook with outputs (runs on Colab or locally)
* `ml/training/bugzero_dataset.csv`, charts (`dataset_overview.png`, `embeddings_pca.png`, `model_comparison.png`)
* `ml/datasets/README.md`, `fetch_ordinary_functions.py`, `ordinary_functions.csv.gz`

### Next
Step 4: evaluate on the test set (Precision, Recall, F1, Confusion Matrix). Then save the model, add the Pylint + Bandit runner and `analyze(file)` for the backend.

author: evan-onyx
body: ## Description First PR of the connector-editing stack. Every connector edit (config, access type, data-access groups, credential) will go through one flow: the backend makes a plan for a proposed state, the admin confirms it, and apply runs it. The plan step must check a proposed state the same way creation does, but with no side effects. This PR adds those checks. No live path calls the new functions yet, and creation keeps the same checks. **Named checks: run without storing** - New `run_named_checks_within_budget` (`capability_checks/creation.py`): it reuses fresh draft results and runs the other checks within the blocking budget. It writes nothing and enqueues nothing. - `validate_pairing_with_named_checks` uses it, then stores the report as before. **Validate a proposed pairing** - New `validate_proposed_pairing` (`connectors/factory.py`). For a given config, credential and access type, it runs the binding check, builds the connector (constructors enforce rules such as the multi-tenant web UPLOAD ban and the sitemap SSRF check), then runs the legacy validation or the named checks. - It returns the result (an error, check results, unfinished check ids). It records no outcome, claims no report row and starts no background run. - `validate_ccpair_for_user` shares the same helper. **One function for the access-type rules** - New `validate_pairing_access` (`connectors/pairing_access.py`): the SYNC_RESTRICTED setting, a restricted pair needs a data-access group, data-access groups only on private or restricted pairs, groups must be visible, the business tier, and a source that supports permission sync. Same error codes and messages. - The associate endpoint and the mock-credential endpoint call it. `add_credential_to_connector` no longer runs the tier and sync-source rules. **Small behavior changes** - The associate endpoint runs the access rules after GATE 2 (connector edit rights and credential ownership). The tier and sync-source rules name the connector's source, so only a user who may edit the connector sees them. - A missing connector in the associate endpoint returns 404 (`CONNECTOR_NOT_FOUND`). Before, it returned 500. - In the mock-credential endpoint, the tier and sync-source rules run before the connector and credential rows are created. Before, a tier failure left both rows behind. ## How Has This Been Tested? - New external-dependency tests: - `test_proposed_pairing_validation.py` (5): the checks get the proposed config; a failed required check is returned, not raised; a slow check is unfinished and not enqueued; legacy and construction errors come back as `validation_error`; no report row, no enqueue, no recorded outcome. - `test_pairing_access.py` (7): one test per rule, with the real EE tier and sync-source functions. - Existing capability-check, server/documents and Confluence binding external-dependency tests: 104 passed. - Unit tests (connector factory, server/documents, tier, capability checks): 278 passed. ## Additional Options - [ ] [Optional] Please cherry-pick this PR to the latest release version. - [x] [Optional] Override Linear Check 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Adds side-effect-free validation of a proposed connector pairing, the first step of the connector-editing flow: plans get the same checks as creation, but write nothing. No live path calls the new functions yet, and creation keeps the same checks. - New `validate_proposed_pairing` runs the binding check, constructs the connector, then runs the legacy validation or the named capability checks on the proposed config, returning failures as results. It records no outcome, claims no report row, and enqueues no background run. - New `run_named_checks_within_budget` reuses fresh draft results and runs the remaining checks within the blocking budget with no writes; the existing report-write path now uses it. - Access-type rules (SYNC_RESTRICTED setting, data-access group requirements and visibility, business tier, sync-source support) moved into `validate_pairing_access`, called by the associate and mock-credential endpoints. `add_credential_to_connector` no longer runs the tier and sync-source rules. **Behavior changes** - The associate endpoint runs the access rules after GATE 2, so only users who may edit the connector see source-specific errors. - A missing connector in the associate endpoint returns 404 instead of 500. - The mock-credential endpoint runs the tier and sync-source rules before creating rows, so a tier failure no longer leaves connector and credential rows behind. Written for commit 9f963bd62dbb0d1fe1803476cf5da86dd8e5500b. Summary will update on new commits.

author: uhrendoktor
body:
## Supervisor audit

This PR addresses two structural problems found in the canonical simulation path.

### Collision/seam root-cause audit
- The canonical tunic fixture was pairing front shoulder edge 2 to back edge 6 and front edge 6 to back edge 2. The authored fixture defines matching right/left shoulder topology, so these are cross-body seam pairs.
- That explains the previously measured 327.94–574.69 mm initial seam spans and the subsequent large zero-rest stitch corrections much better than a collision tolerance tweak.
- The diagnostic no longer overrides `CLOTH_PBD_SUBSTEPS` to 32; it honors the workflow budget.
- Workflow collision tolerance is restored to 2 mm rather than masking the semantic error with 12 mm.
- Exact collision-surface coarsening remains under audit; full-resolution historical evidence already falsified coarsening as the sole canonical root cause.

### Realtime/performance
- Added a persistent-backend `advance_preview_frame()` path that advances PBD and publishes the existing mesh without entering FreeCAD document recompute.
- RealtimePreview and its benchmark now use that path.
- Added contract tests preventing `doc.recompute()` from re-entering the timer tick.
- Removed redundant triangle installs from Dockerized PBD jobs; the pinned validation image already contains the dependency.
- GUI smoke/animation hard timeouts changed from 300s to 60s; the tunic supervisor deadline is 90s.
- PR turntable capture is reduced to 36+1 frames; main keeps 72+1 frames.

### Research basis
The upstream pyPBD cloth example builds the collision SDF once, sets a small collision tolerance, uses substeps, and performs multiple simulation steps per render. The Small Steps paper reports that many smaller steps with one constraint iteration can outperform many iterations in one large step, including a 150k-particle cloth example at 12.4–13.5 ms/frame.

author: kcorbett-hdx
body:
> **Draft on purpose.** The code is ready to review; the decision behind it isn't settled. See *Why this is a draft* at the bottom before spending real review time.

## What this is

A credentials type, `forwardOAuthExchange`, for a Grafana whose users sign in through an issuer the cluster will not accept directly.

`forwardOAuth` sends the signed-in user's token to the cluster unchanged, which works where the cluster accepts that issuer. Where it doesn't — a Hydrolix Console Keycloak realm, say — the cluster refuses the token on its audience. This mode exchanges that token for a cluster token (RFC 8693) before querying, so the query still runs as the signed-in user.

The datasource stores **no credential at all**. The exchange endpoint and its credentials are operator values read from the environment (`GF_PLUGIN_EXCHANGE_URL`, `GF_PLUGIN_EXCHANGE_CREDENTIALS`). Credentials are a **map keyed by cluster audience**, not a single pair, because one Grafana can serve several clusters and each issues its own — keying by audience keeps each credential scoped to the one cluster it can obtain a token for.

## Two defects it also fixes, both in shipped code

1. **`Connect` pinged the cluster.** `db.PingContext` at connect time is the server handshake, and it ran for every mode except `forwardOAuth` — a literal string comparison a later mode couldn't match. A connection whose credential belongs to the signed-in user can't be verified there: `Connect` has no user. Now behind a named predicate rather than a string.
2. **`Save & test` reported a working forward-mode datasource as degraded**, because the check ran on the bootstrap connection, which has no user. A green tick would also have read as "your access works" when nothing about anyone's access was tested. Both forwarding modes now report what can actually be established.

## Design notes worth your eye

- **The pool keys on the subject, not the token.** The credential is refreshed independently of the connection; keying on the token would discard every pooled connection each time Grafana refreshed a sign-in. `forwardOAuth` is unchanged and still keys on `oauthToken` — its spec requirement is untouched.
- **Native is refused**, with a message naming the HTTP protocol. Native binds its credential to the connection as a password, so a refreshed token could never reach an open connection. A second, worse code path wasn't worth shipping for a protocol these datasources never use.
- **Refresh is synchronous, not a background goroutine.** A caller inside the lead window refreshes while its current token is still usable, so a failed refresh is invisible.
- The semantics are a port of the console's own browser client, whose behaviour was shaped by incidents worth not repeating: client-clock deadlines from request start, refresh ahead in proportion to lifetime, one exchange in flight per user, a bounded retry ladder, invalidation an in-flight exchange can't undo.

## Testing

- ~45 Go tests (new `pkg/plugin/exchange` package plus driver wiring), under `-race`. Includes: the forwarded token can never reach the cluster, *including when the exchange fails*; single-flight under concurrency; refresh-ahead boundaries; invalidate-mid-exchange; and a log-hygiene test asserting no token, SQL or secret reaches any log line.
- 332 frontend tests, 7 of them new.
- Full e2e suite against Grafana 13.2.1, run as CI runs it: **61 passed, 0 failed**, including a new spec covering each credentials mode's fields.
- **Proven live** against a real cluster, 2026-10-02, with nothing standing in for the plugin: a signed-in user's dashboard returned rows, one exchange served six queries, and the control held — the same user's *unexchanged* token was refused by the cluster.

## What is NOT verified

- **One Grafana version.** e2e ran on 13.2.1 only; `compatibility-check` / `nightly-compat` haven't run.
- **Ad-hoc filter key population in this mode specifically.** It's a frontend resource call rather than the backend query path, and the live run didn't cover it.
- Never run from a released, signed plugin build — only local `mage` builds.

## Why this is a draft

This mode exists because of an architectural decision on the Hydrolix Console side that is still open: whether managed Grafana signs in through the console's realm at all. That's under discussion in hydrolix/hydrolix-console#2312 and has an unanswered objection on it.

I'd rather show you working code and real measurements than an argument — but I don't think you should merge a new credentials mode into your plugin before our side has agreed it wants one. Review, pushback and "we'd do this differently" are all very welcome now. I'll mark it ready when #2312 lands.

No HDX ticket yet — happy to file one and retitle.

author: ifaemuh
body:
# Rules: add airline delay-care and missed-connection commitments (AA, DL, UA, WN)

Seven draft rules from each airline's Customer Service Plan and Conditions of Carriage. Each passed an opus legal review (2–3 rounds). Cross-airline rulings: match on `flight.marketing_carrier_iata` (regional brands and marketed codeshares); delay branch on `event.departure_delay_minutes`; cancellations and missed connections need no minutes; the plan governs per 14 CFR 259.5(a). Southwest has no missed-connection rule because its documents promise none.


---

### aa-controllable-delay-care — American Airlines delayed or cancelled your flight? If it's their doing, ask for a meal credit, hotel and transport
**Says:** When American causes a delay, cancellation or missed connection, its plan gives you on request a food credit if your delay is 3 or more hours after your scheduled departure, and a hotel voucher plus transport if you are delayed overnight and away from your city of residence. A hotel is owed if you’re away from your city of residence and not boarded before 11:59 p.m. Nothing is promised if the cause is beyond its control, except after a diversion.
**Applies when:** Marketing carrier AA; cause controllable or unknown; and either a delay with departure delay of at least 180 minutes, or a cancellation or missed connection (no minutes condition; the food credit's 3-hour wait is stated in entitlement and exceptions).
**Sources:** aa-customer-service-plan (delays and cancellations caused by us, beyond our control, diversions, codeshare partners); aa-contract-of-carriage (delays caused by us, force majeure list, Eagle sentence); ecfr-14-cfr-259 § 259.5(a); dot-customer-service-dashboard.
**Quotes:**
> In cases where a delay or cancellation is caused by us, upon request we’ll give you:
> Food / beverage credit if your delay is 3 or more hours after your scheduled departure.
> A voucher for an approved hotel with available rooms if you are delayed overnight if you’re away from your city of residence.
> If the disruption is our fault or you're diverted to another city, and we don't board before 11:59 p.m. local time on your scheduled arrival day, we'll arrange an overnight stay or cover the cost of an approved hotel with available rooms if you’re away from your city of residence.
> Shortage of labor, fuel or facilities of American or others
> Each covered carrier must adopt a Customer Service Plan applicable to its scheduled flights as specified in paragraphs (b)(1) through (14) of this section and adhere to the plan's terms.
**Unsure about:** (1) No overnight fact exists. The delay branch is gated at 180 minutes of departure delay (the food credit's threshold); the only overnight case this hides is a late-evening departure pushed past midnight by less than 3 hours. Cancellations and missed connections have no minutes condition, so the food credit's wait condition is only in the text. (2) Cause "unknown" returns applies, so the summary says it depends on American causing it. A staffing shortage is on the contract's force majeure list, so it may not count as American's fault. (3) Eagle regional flights are included via the contract's "Under the name "American Airlines" we operate ... regional codeshare flights (doing business as American Eagle)". (4) Diversion care does not depend on cause; there is no diversion fact, so it is described in exceptions only. (5) The dashboard's meal cells are quoted as supporting guidance. (6) The contract of carriage lists only the hotel; the food credit and transport come from the plan, which 14 CFR 259.5(a) requires American to follow. The contract also says its sole obligation on a 3+/4+ hour delay or cancellation is a refund and rebooking; I state this factually in exceptions. (7) Force majeure is quoted in full, including labor shortage and unforeseen facts. (8) Flights operated by American but sold under another airline's number: no AA text found that says what applies, so nothing is claimed.

### aa-missed-connection-rebooking — Missed your connection on American Airlines? They rebook you on their next flight with seats, at no extra cost
**Says:** When a delay could cause you to miss your connection, American rebooks you on its next flight with available seats at no additional cost. If it caused the disruption and none of its flights are available until the next day, it rebooks you on a partner airline with available seats at no additional cost.
**Applies when:** Marketing carrier AA; missed connection; single ticket or booking reference. No cause condition: the basic rebooking is promised whatever the cause; only the partner-airline step depends on American causing it (in exceptions).
**Sources:** aa-customer-service-plan (delays and cancellations caused by us, codeshare partners); aa-contract-of-carriage (rebooking your delayed / canceled flight, schedule not guaranteed, Eagle sentence).
**Quotes:**
> When your flight is canceled, significantly delayed, or a delay could cause you to miss your connection, we’ll rebook you on our next flight with available seats at no additional cost.
> If no American flights are available until the next day, and the disruption is caused by us, we’ll rebook you on one of our partner airlines with available seats at no additional cost.
> We do our best to be on time but our flight schedule is not guaranteed and not part of this contract. We are not liable if:
**Unsure about:** (1) `flight.single_ticket eq true` is an inference, not quoted; the sources never say "single ticket". The exception says the plan doesn't say American will rebook a separate-ticket connection. (2) The plan promises rebooking when a delay "could cause" a missed connection, before it is missed; the rule matches once the event is a missed connection. (3) The refund step lists the involuntary refunds policy's four eligible changes, each quoted, including an increased number of connections. (4) Eagle regional flights are included via the contract's Eagle sentence; flights sold under AA's number but operated by a partner get only the "comparable levels of service" language (domestic codeshare partners).

---

### dl-controllable-delay-care — Delayed, cancelled or misconnected by Delta? Ask for a meal after 3 hours, and a hotel if stuck overnight

author: jcogilvie
body:
### Description of your changes

Both issues come from one cause. Crossplane's composite reconciler writes `compositionRevisionRef`, and an apply that leaves a field out does not remove it. `crossplane render` does no revision selection, so a composite rendered without the ref renders against no revision at all. A template that reads the revision name (`{{ .observed.composite.resource.spec[.crossplane].compositionRevisionRef.name }}`) then produced nothing, and the diff showed a change against the cluster that wasn't real.

**xr (#499).** `diffSingleResourceInternal` now fetches the composite's cluster copy *before* resolving its composition (a new helper, `inheritClusterState`). If the input has no ref at either the v1 (`spec.compositionRevisionRef`) or v2 (`spec.crossplane.compositionRevisionRef`) path, the new `CopyCompositionRevisionRef` copies the cluster's ref onto two objects: the render input, and a copy of the object the composition is resolved from. The supplied object is never mutated. Nested XRs go through the same step under the identity `preserveNestedXRIdentity` restores. A ref in the input always wins.

**Claims (#498).** `buildMergedSpec` now keeps the backing XR's ref whatever the update policy, unless the claim has its own. Before, it kept the ref only under `Manual`. There is one exception, in `comp`. When an Automatic claim would re-point to the revision the diffed composition mints, it renders with the predicted name instead, so a template reading the name does not render the stale one (a missed change). The plumbing works like this:
- `collectXRDiffs` records the name on the diff's context with `withSeededRevision`. The value is keyed to that root composite, so nothing else rendered under the same context picks it up.
- `buildMergedSpec` points the backing XR's *existing* ref at that name. It never creates a ref, which keeps the #474 invariant.
- Only re-pointing composites get the name, so `Manual` ones never do, because #474's partition already excludes them.

A package-private context value keeps this off the `DiffProcessor` interface. The interface, the mocks and `ProcessorConfig` are unchanged.

#### Behaviour changes to review

- **Manual-pinned composites whose input omits the ref (intended).** `xr` used to render such a composite against the *latest* revision. It now renders against the revision the cluster copy is pinned to, which is what applying that input would actually leave in place. Because the ref is copied before resolution, the composition client's `Manual && hasRevisionRef` branch sees the pin. This also applies to claims (the claim's own cluster ref is inherited) and to nested XRs. To preview moving to a different revision, set `compositionRevisionRef` in the input. A pinned revision that no longer exists now fails the diff, as the reconcile would.
- **Automatic claims keep their backing XR's ref.** Before, the ref was dropped from the render.

#### Existing tests whose expectations changed

- `TestDefaultDiffProcessor_resolveBackingXRForClaim_CompositionRevisionRef`: `DoNotPreserveCompositionRevisionRefWithAutomaticPolicy` and `DoNotPreserveCompositionRevisionRefWithDefaultPolicy` encoded the old drop-under-Automatic rule. They are now `PreserveCompositionRevisionRefWithAutomaticPolicy` / `...WithDefaultPolicy` and expect the ref kept. The table now compares the whole resulting ref with `cmp.Diff` rather than only checking it exists. It gains four seeding cases (re-points the ref, never creates one, the claim's own ref wins, a seed for another resource is ignored) and checks that the cluster's backing XR is not mutated.
- No existing integration test changed expectation. The closest neighbours (`V2ManualRevisionUpgradeDiff`, `V1ManualRevisionUpgradeDiff`, `V2SwitchManualToAutomatic`, `CompositionChangeImpactsClaims`, `RevisionNamePropagatesToComposedResource`) still pass. The two `*ManualRevisionUpgradeDiff` cases now also guard the rule that the input's ref beats the cluster's: making the cluster's win fails both.

#### Tests

Each new integration test was checked by mutation: with its fix disabled, it fails.
- `TestDiffIntegration/ExistingXROmittingRevisionRefRendersWithClusterRef`: an unchanged XR whose input omits the ref, with a revision-templating composition, shows no diff. Without the fix, `configData` changes to `<no value>`.
- `TestDiffIntegration/V2ManualPolicyOmittedRevisionRefStaysPinned` and `V1ManualPolicyOmittedRevisionRefStaysPinned`: a Manual XR whose input omits the ref renders the pinned `v1-*` template, not the latest `v2-*`. Copying the ref onto the render input but not onto the resolution object fails both.
- `TestDiffIntegration/NestedXRInheritsClusterRevisionRef`: a nested child renders with its cluster copy's ref (3 modified resources without the fix, 2 with it).
- `TestCompDiffIntegration/ClaimRevisionNamePropagatesToComposedResource`: an Automatic claim with no ref of its own, plus a label-only (revision-minting) edit, renders the predicted `<composition>-<hash7>` name. With the context plumbing removed, it reports the claim unchanged.
- `TestCompDiffIntegration/ClaimRendersWithBackingXRRevisionWhenNothingIsSeeded`: when nothing is seeded, the claim renders with the backing XR's current ref and shows no change. Without the fix it renders `<no value>`. This is the no-revision-name variant. A truly identical composition is skipped by `--analyze-on`, and under `--analyze-on=always` it would *be* seeded. So this case reaches the unseeded path through a composition that differs only by a stale kubectl annotation, where the revision name is unpredictable.
- Unit tests: a new `TestCopyCompositionRevisionRef` table (v1, v2, both paths; the target's ref at the same path or the other path wins; source without a ref; malformed source; deep copy), plus the claim table above.

#### Notes for reviewers

- **Real claims usually do carry the ref.** The upstream claim syncers (`syncer_csa.go`, `syncer_ssa.go`) copy the backing XR's `compositionRevisionRef` back onto the claim under Automatic. In that case #474's `seedRepointingXRs` already seeds it on the claim itself. The context-plumbed name covers claims that carry no ref, which is what the fixtures model.
- **Known limitation, not addressed here.** `xr` inherits the cluster's *current* ref. If an Automatic composite is not converged, or the input switches Manual→Automatic, the reconciler would re-point it to the latest matching revision, but the render shows the current ref's name. Rendering is still against the latest revision, so only templates that read the name are affected.
- **Pre-existing and unrelated.** Diffing a claim's composed resources raises a "Resource already belongs to another composite" advisory. `checkCompositeOwnership` is handed the claim, but the composed resource's `crossplane.io/composite` label names the backing XR. The new claim tests therefore don't assert the warning count.
- Docs: design doc §4.8, §4.11, §4.12, §4.13, §6.1, §6.2, §7.1 and §7.2; `diff-call-sequence.mermaid` and its regenerated SVG (the fetch now happens before composition resolution); README (`xr` section).

Fixes #498
Fixes #499
