## Package
HOST-1c part 1, owner-facing text only. HW-8 says the owner's guide lists every change AgentOS makes to the host and that this list is complete. It also says BitLocker is named only when it is the problem, and that the PC is started with the one-time boot key, never with Secure Boot off.

## Before / After
Before: there was no owner's guide. The card's quick-start did not say the PC's disks are left alone (ONB-7). Nothing listed what the box changes in the PC's firmware or TPM.

After:
- **`docs/owners-guide.md`** starts the guide with three sections:
  - *Starting AgentOS on your PC*: use the one-time boot key; you never need to change settings or turn Secure Boot off; internal disks are used only when the owner gives one under Settings > Storage.
  - *What AgentOS changes on your PC*: the whole list, in plain words.
  - *If Windows asks for a recovery key*: the only place BitLocker is named. It points to aka.ms/myrecoverykey for a home PC and the IT department for a work PC, and says this is Windows' key, "not the recovery key on your AgentOS card".
- **`broker/hostchange`** holds HW-8's list as data, with IDs and kinds, for HOST-1e's acceptance diff. A test checks that the guide carries each ID exactly once in its list and lists nothing else.
- **Card.** Quick-start step 2 now ends "Your PC's own disks are left untouched." A test checks that the rendered card names no BitLocker, Secure Boot, BIOS, UEFI, firmware, boot order or settings.

How: the guide items carry `<!-- host-change: ID -->` markers, and `hostchange` tests pin them to `All`.

The list is what the code does today. This is where it differs from SPEC HW-8, which needs an L1 spec-diff (sent to the coordinator):
- SPEC names "a TPM NV index, if systemd-pcrlock is the HW-5a seal". The seal is the Go signed PCR policy (tpmseal T1), so there is no pcrlock index. The code does define **one NV counter per vault on each trusted PC** (V6, `tpmseal/counter.go`), which SPEC does not list.
- SPEC omits **the lockout authorization and dictionary-attack settings**. A boot PIN sets them (D7, `tpmseal.TakeLockout`). `ReleaseLockout` gives the authorization back, but the dictionary-attack settings stay as set. The guide says so.
- The persistent SRK stays conditional: the broker's SRK is transient (CreatePrimary, never EvictControl), so only the image's TPM setup could persist one.

Points for the lenses:
- **UX:** the wording of the guide and of the quick-start line. In the recovery-key answer, the AgentOS card also has a "Recovery key"; the answer separates the two.
- **Security:** that the list is complete and accurate, especially the TPM items and the note that DA settings stay. LoaderSystemToken stays listed until P2-1 decides whether to turn it off.

Part 2 (on BOARD) covers the box answering from the guide when the owner asks about a recovery-key prompt (needs P2-2), and the LoaderSystemToken/SRK image choice (P2-1). The BOARD HOST-1b row is marked part 1 merged (#177).

author: elbert5770
body:
Multi-start used to fit from every sampled start with the spec's own method and take the best as the answer. Opt in with `multistart_method` in `optimizer_kwargs` and it becomes a stage that runs BEFORE the standard fit: many Sobol candidates are triaged cheaply, a few local fits are run from the survivors, and the best point reached is where the standard fit starts. Without `multistart_method` nothing changes.

## The stage

1. Fast pass: every candidate scored once at relaxed integrator tolerances (x0 first, in-process, at the configured ones).
2. Feasibility: candidates the solver fails on are dropped. Evaluations run under a limited `safe_simulate` ladder (default 4 attempts, no subdivision).
3. Ranked threshold: keep the best `keep_fraction` of the survivors.
4. Niching: complete-linkage clusters in log10 space; `cluster_radius` is RMS decades per parameter, so it means the same for 3 and 30 parameters.
5. Reference set: the best point of each niche, plus x0 (always), capped at `n_starts` fits. `n_starts` is therefore the cap on LOCAL FITS and `multistart_triage["n_candidates"]` is how many points are triaged.

Local fits use `multistart_method` (typically L-BFGS-B, small `maxiter`). A failed evaluation scores (worst scored NLL + `failure_dnll`) instead of 1e10, a finite wall a gradient method can step back from. The reference is fixed once so the surface does not move under the line search.

The fast pass runs serially or on the worker pool. `parallel="auto"` times x0 and one warm candidate and uses the pool only when that clearly beats serial (it pays for expensive, numerous evaluations; measured, it does not for small batches). The pool is fed in chunks so a kill costs a chunk.

## Resumable

With a fit cache the stage keeps a checkpoint (`multistart_stage`) after every candidate scored (every chunk on the pool) and every local fit finished. A relaunch after a kill skips what is recorded, recomputes the reference set from the scores (deterministic), and reuses finished fits. x0 is always re-scored first: it is where the noise floors are calibrated, and its score is checked against the recorded one (a mismatch discards the checkpoint). A kill inside one L-BFGS-B fit loses that fit only. With a run stop time the stage stops between candidates/chunks/fits and exits like the standard fit does; on a preemptible partition there is no stop time and only kill-and-resume applies.

## What a run now writes

- The result JSON snapshot gains a `multistart` block: triage counts, the pool decision, the reference set, one record per local fit, the basins the fits ended in (fits ending near each other are one basin whatever their NLL; the verdict is unimodal / degenerate / multimodal), and `candidates` -- every Sobol candidate's score and fate (rank, feasible, kept, niche, leader, fitted, fit_nll), enough to draw a waterfall plot.
- The same report is kept in the fit cache, so a relaunch that resumes the standard fit or reuses a finished fit still reports how the start was found (`from_cache: true`).
- BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: a multi-start run (report present, or `n_starts > 1`) is NOT appended to `*_optimization_results.csv`; that file is for single-start fits. The snapshot is still written, with `metadata.n_starts`. Single-start runs are unchanged.

## Bug fixed on the way

While the stage runs the objective's own best-so-far partial write is switched off. Previously it recorded the best of relaxed-tolerance triage scores and stage fits, and the standard fit then preferred that partial to the start the stage chose (seen in a real run: "resuming an unfinished fit ... after 38 evaluations"). The stage's best is now written explicitly when the stage ends, with x0 as the noise-floor calibration point.

## Other changes

- `Simulate`: `retry_limits(max_attempts, max_depth)` and `relaxed_tolerances(factor)` (process-global, default off, applied inside `configure_integrator`; never tightens; capped at 1e-4).
- `Preequil_cache`: the pre-dose cache key uses the tolerances actually in force, so a state integrated at relaxed tolerances is never served to a normal run.
- `Evaluator`: `evaluate_batch(..., eval_mode=...)` applies those limits around ONE task and undoes them, so they cannot leak into profile points.
- `Fit_cache`: `save/load/clear_stage`, `save/load_multistart`; the new multistart keys are dropped from the fit fingerprint at one start so existing cached fits stay valid. `start_sampler` is likewise ignored at one start.
- `Model_optimize`: the standalone likelihood slice reads `slice_settings` (`n_points`, `range_factor`) from the spec; defaults are the old 20 and 2.0.

## Tests

- The whole tests/engine suite passes (321 tests), including 139 in the new and touched areas (new files: test_multistart_triage, test_multistart_resume, test_multistart_candidates, test_results_csv_policy). They cover each triage step, the pool decision with a fake clock, kills at every phase (fast pass, pool chunk, between fits, after the stage), stop times, discarded checkpoints, the CSV policy, and drawing a waterfall from the saved rows.
- Real model (cook_gsi_ki, 1 parameter), cache on: killed during the fast pass, relaunched and killed after the first fit, relaunched to completion. Same optimum as an uninterrupted run (NLL 184.17405330, GSI_KI_MK0752 1.96427848), stage progress skipped on each relaunch, snapshot reports launches=3.
- Real model on the worker pool (auto chose it for 16 candidates): snapshot contains all 17 candidate rows; the results CSV was byte-identical afterwards.
- PK Aducanumab (3 parameters): pool and serial scores bit-identical for 6 feasible candidates, and both failing candidates fail in both.

## Not verified / known limits

- The pool paying off on a genuinely expensive spec (e.g. 21 s/evaluation, 64+ candidates) is argued from measurements on cheap specs, not measured there.
- L-BFGS-B on a noisy ODE objective can end with "ABNORMAL" (line-search failure); seen once, within 0.0007 NLL of the optimum. It only has to find the basin, and the standard fit follows it.
- The stage's checkpoint granularity is one candidate (or pool chunk) / one fit.
- The `dataviz` palette validator needs Node, which was not available, so the waterfall used the documented reference colours without running it. No plotting code is part of this PR.

author: bivlked
body:
## Summary

AmneziaWG for Android, iOS/macOS and Windows parse a profile strictly: an `[Interface]` key they do not know, or a malformed `HeaderProtectionKey`, makes the whole import fail. AmneziaVPN ignores unknown keys, so a profile that imports there says nothing about these three apps. This adds a test that keeps our client profiles inside what they accept.

- Every content line of a rendered client profile is checked: a known section, `Key = value` with a value, a key from the list those parsers accept, and a value of the right form: keys are 32 bytes of base64, numbers where a number is expected, `H1`-`H4` and `ContentPaddingAddition` a number or a range, `Address` and `AllowedIPs` lists of CIDRs, `Endpoint` host:port with an IPv6 host in brackets. One `[Interface]`, and no key twice in a section except `Address`, `AllowedIPs` and `DNS` (the iOS parser refuses other repeats).
- Both generations, both language versions of the library, and the variants an install produces: without CPS, with `I2`-`I5`, own DNS and MTU, IPv6 in the tunnel, a preshared key, an IPv6 endpoint. Each variant is checked to have taken effect, so it cannot pass by rendering the default profile.
- The 3.1 client key sequence and values are pinned next to the existing 2.0 one.

No change to the scripts themselves: today's profiles already pass.

author: mtraverso3
body:
During a game the desktop client asked the Worker for live champions every 3s, and each request made two Riot calls. That's ~20 calls/min per player: enough to trip the 30/min limit (champion info then silently disappeared) and to burn the Riot key with several players in a game.

**Client**
- A live result is kept for the rest of that game (keyed by gameId); picks don't change once it starts.
- "Not live yet" is retried every 30s, failures (including 429) after 60s. The cache resets on a new game.
- The logic lives in a small pure module, `client/src/shared/live-cache.ts`.

**Worker**
- Riot ID → puuid is cached for 24h.
- The Spectator result is cached for 30s per player, so party members in the same game share one Riot call.
- Errors are never cached.

Tests: `client/test/live-cache.spec.ts` (reuse within a game, retry interval, error backoff, reset on new game) and `test/riot-live.spec.ts` (Riot endpoints hit once across repeated lookups, errors not cached; 3 of 4 fail without the fix).

author: vitbokisch
body:
Fixes #3803

## Validation
Confirmed on main: the static a11y verifier's skip text promises axe-core via `atlas verify-browser`, but `runBrowserVerify` only did reactive coverage + snapshots and carried `a11y` through untouched (axe existed only in the `atlas dev` panel).

## Fix (implements axe, rather than only rewording)
- `runBrowserVerify` now runs axe-core per scenario against the live preview, in the page, through the workbench's own vendored `runAxe` (exposed on `__ATLAS_VERIFY__`; `runAxe` exported from `@pyreon/atlas/ui`, takes optional rule overrides). Fragment-inappropriate page rules stay off as in the panel.
- Result is merged into the scenario `a11y` verdict (`axeReportToCheck` + `mergeA11y`): violations -> `fail` with structured `axe-violation` findings; needs-a-human items -> `axe-incomplete` on a pass; a run that could not happen -> `skip` with `axe-core did not run: <reason>` (never a pass). The static name check's real result is kept (either side failing fails), its "nothing to check statically" skip is replaced, and prior axe findings are stripped on re-merge so reruns replace instead of stacking. `ok`/`checked` recompute via the existing derivation.
- `--no-axe` opts out (verdict stays static; the CLI summary says "axe-core NOT run"); `--axe-min-impact <minor|moderate|serious|critical>` filters by impact. Summary now reports `axeChecked`/`axeFailed`.
- Two additive finding codes; the finding shape `{code,message,fix?}` is unchanged so catalog `version` stays 2.
- Docs/manifest/generated pages, static-skip wording, changeset updated. Also raises the atlas bundle budget to 15936 B (same hand bump as #3807: headroom was below the macOS/ubuntu gzip delta).

## Verification
- Real run in Chromium: `atlas verify-browser examples/atlas-workshop` -> `axe-core run on 27 (11 with violations)`; catalog carries e.g. `axe-core button-name (critical): Buttons must have discernible text ...`.
- Unit tests (report mapping, impact floor, skip-not-pass, merge/idempotency, ok flip, carry-through when absent). Bisect-verified: removing the a11y merge in `mergeBrowserVerdict` fails `axe FAIL flips ok` (`expected 'skip' to be 'fail'`-class); restored, passes. atlas verify-browser/plugins/cli suites: 521 passed; tsc clean; `check-generated-fresh` in sync; gen-docs run.

## Not done / caveats
- Axe violations do NOT change the `verify-browser` exit code (only visual diffs do), to avoid breaking existing CI users on upgrade; they fail the catalog verdict, so `atlas verify --check` ratchets them. Say if you want a strict flag.
- No `atlas.config.ts` opt-out: the command does not load config; options are CLI flags / `runBrowserVerify` options only.
- The `e2e/atlas-verify-browser.spec.ts` suite was not run; I ran the equivalent command manually. Full validate-fast was running under host load ~250 and had not finished its slowest gate (check-lathe-fresh); gates seen: all passed except `check-generated-fresh` while changes were uncommitted, which passes after commit. Pushed with PYREON_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1.

author: sawyerhood
body:
## What was wrong

Every publish re-uploaded every icon and screenshot, one file at a time, whether or not it had changed. In the publish run for `54f38e4` that was 5 minutes of icons and 12 minutes of screenshots out of an 18-minute run, to deliver a single new entry.

## What changed

The publish workflow now uploads only the icons and screenshots whose published copy is missing or different.

- `scripts/changed-assets.mjs` lists the files in one group (`icons` or `screenshots`), asks getbb.app for each published object's ETag, and prints the files that need an upload.
- R2's ETag for a single-part object is the MD5 of its bytes, and getbb.app serves it unchanged. A matching ETag means the object already has that content.
- Any other answer counts as changed: a missing object, an error, a timeout, a missing ETag or a multipart ETag. The worst case is an upload that was not needed, which is today's behavior.
- If the script itself fails, the step fails before anything is uploaded, so a manifest is never published ahead of its assets.
- The upload loops read the file list on a separate file descriptor, so the upload command cannot consume it.
- Object keys, content types and the retry helper are unchanged. The manifests are still uploaded on every run, after the assets.
- It needs no stored state and no new secrets. A run that fails or is cancelled partway is completed by the next run.

This also removes the reason to skip asset uploads on a scheduled publish, which #446 adds; with this change every run is already cheap.

## How you verified

- `npm test` passes (41 tests). The new tests use a local HTTP server and cover: a matching ETag is skipped, including a weak ETag; an edited file, a missing object, a 500, a multipart ETag and a missing ETag are all uploaded; an unreachable site uploads everything; the icon and screenshot key mapping. Breaking the status check or the ETag comparison makes the test fail.
- Against the live site from this branch: `node scripts/changed-assets.mjs icons` reports 0 of 214 and `screenshots` reports 0 of 453, in about 3 and 6 seconds. Run on Node 22 and Node 24.
- The two upload steps, extracted from `publish.yml` and run locally with a recording stand-in for `wrangler`:
  - Nothing changed: 0 uploads.
  - One new icon, one edited screenshot and one new screenshot: exactly those 3 uploads, with the same keys and content types as before.
  - An unsupported screenshot type still fails the step.
  - Published site unreachable: all 669 assets are uploaded.
  - The check script crashing: both steps fail and nothing is uploaded.
- The publish workflow itself has not run with this change. It only runs on `main`, so its first real run is the merge of this PR.

author: onixus
body:
## What failed

`shapoclyack-branches` / `main` #76 (a5963515), second pytest run (with coverage):

```
tests/test_auth_rate_limit.py:101: assert _fail(client).status_code == 429
E       assert 401 == 429
```

The captured log has the three logins at 02:20:31.352, 02:20:32.515 and 02:20:33.687, about **1.17 s apart**.

## Root cause (test bug, not a limiter bug)

The test configured `login_rate_limit_window_seconds=1` against the real clock. `auth_audit.attempt_login` records `occurred_at` *after* `verify()` (bcrypt), and the third attempt counts failures since `now - 1s`. So the lock only forms if the second login (one whole request) finishes in under a second. In the first CI run and on a laptop it does (~0.3 s). Under coverage on the CI container it took ~1.2 s, the first failure aged out, and the third attempt was a plain 401.

The limiter is correct: `_lockout_for` and `_record` both use `auth_audit._now()`, and nothing reads the DB server's clock.

## Fix

- Hold `api.services.auth_audit._now` still with `monkeypatch`, the same pattern as `run_publisher._now` and `mfa._now` elsewhere in `tests/`. Use a 60 s window and advance the clock by hand. No `time.sleep`.
- New check: one second before the window edge, the lock still holds, even for the correct password. Without it, a limiter that decayed too early would pass.

## Evidence

A scratch pytest plugin stretched `users.verify_password` by 1.1 s, which is the per-login time measured in #76.

| | before (origin/main test) | after |
|---|---|---|
| plain, local | 10/10 pass | 50/50 pass |
| with the CI-like 1.1 s login | **10/10 fail** (`401 == 429`, same line as CI) | 50/50 pass |

Mutations of `_lockout_for`, checked against the new test:
- cutoff of 365 days (the window never decays): fails with `429 == 200`
- cutoff at half the window (decays too early): fails at the window−1 check

Also run: whole `tests/test_auth_rate_limit.py` 17 passed; `ruff check .` clean. A fresh DB on shapo-test-pg was used for all of this and dropped afterwards.

Across the 92 Jenkins logs (all branches) that ran this file, the test failed only in main #76.

author: kylebarron
body:
> [!NOTE]
> This PR was written by Claude (Claude Code), not by @kylebarron.

Fixes `VertexNormalsExtension` rejecting the default integer index dtype.

### The bug

`encode` casts indices to `uint32`, but `VertexNormalsExtension` passed them straight to the Cython `add_vertex_normals` helper, which only accepts `uint32`. Indices built with `np.array([...])` are `int64` by default. Passing the same indices to both, as the README example does, raised:

```
ValueError: Buffer dtype mismatch, expected 'uint32_t' but got 'long'
```

This happens on numpy 1.26 too.

### Fix

Cast indices to `uint32` in `compute_vertex_normals`, as `encode` does.

### Tests

`test_vertex_normals_extension_index_dtype` fails without the fix and passes with it.

body:
This pull request addresses an issue with saving `DateTimeOffset` values to PostgreSQL, which only supports UTC offsets. The changes include:

- **Normalization of DateTimeOffset values**: All non-UTC `DateTimeOffset` values are now normalized to UTC in `ApplicationDbContext.cs` before being saved. This ensures compatibility with PostgreSQL's `timestamp with time zone` type.
- **Addition of regression tests**: New tests have been created in `ApplicationDbContextTests.cs` to verify the correct handling of non-zero offsets, including nullable fields like `AddedOn`.

All tests have been run successfully, confirming that the fix resolves the issue without introducing new problems.

author: vl3c
body:
## Summary
Operator ruling (2026-10-06): "Don't retry when the failure is a definite error from the seam, and keep retrying everything that looks like random flakiness. We can recheck failures manually."

- `hlib.decide_retry` = the unchanged `should_retry` plus one veto, `deterministic_seam_error_retry_skip`. The veto fires only when ALL of these hold:
  - **Verdict:** INVALID with a driver-stage subkind.
  - **Step:** the driver-blamed step is a seam step, chosen the same way as `compose_driver_validity`.
  - **Args:** none were filled from a captured `${step.field}` value.
  - **Seam reply:** ERROR or REJECTED, never TIMEOUT.
  - **Reason:** in the closed set `DETERMINISTIC_SEAM_ERROR_REASONS`. That covers protocol rejects, argument refusals, `active-vessel-lost`, REJECTED `not-eva` and REJECTED `not-in-flight`.
- Everything timing- or load-related keeps its retry: timeouts, `not-safe-point`, waits, `recording-active`, `warp-locked`, mission flakes, and every unlisted reason.
- Verdict and subkind are unchanged. A skipped retry logs `[Retry] retry skipped ...` and records `retrySkipped: {rule, reason, stepId, verb, seamVerdict}` in the result JSON. Seam step rows now carry the reply `msg` (only when non-empty).
- A source-sync test (comment-stripped, whole-literal) fails if a listed reason disappears from `Source/Parsek/TestCommands`.

**Replay over the 48 historical retries:** 0 skipped, 0 of the 8 retry passes lost. Every one failed on a timing reason or a reason outside the set. Going forward, a dead-kerbal EVA failure now answers `active-vessel-lost` (#1994) and is not retried; two such EVA-8 retries cost 601 s and failed again.

**Left out on purpose** (each failed again on every recorded retry, but reads live game state): `unknown-tree` / `unknown-building`, `eva-refused`, `stockscreen-no-tooltip`, `refly-gate` / `rewind-gate`, UiAction window / edit errors. Adding one is a one-line edit.

## Review
A clean-context review found nothing merge-blocking. It checked:
- the veto scope (driver-stage INVALID only, never PARSEK-FAIL);
- the blamed-step equivalence;
- each world-state reason against its C# producer;
- JSON persistence;
- that the source-sync test is not vacuous.

Its optional hardening, which keeps the retry when the blamed step's args came from a captured value, is the second commit.

author: facundo-p
body:
«Cambiar foto» en el detalle del árbol y «Reemplazar» en el visor de la botonera pisaban la foto sin avisar. Ahora piden confirmación con un aviso compartido, como ya hace «Quitar».

## Qué cambia para el usuario

- **Detalle del árbol, árbol con foto:** «Cambiar foto» abre el aviso «Reemplazar la foto» con Cancelar / Ver actual / Reemplazar. «Ver actual» abre la foto en el visor (también si está solo en la nube) con un botón Reemplazar que va directo a la cámara, sin volver a preguntar. Sin foto, «Tomar foto» va directo a la cámara como antes.
- **Visor de la botonera:** «Reemplazar» confirma con Cancelar / Reemplazar (la foto ya está a la vista).
- Tocar la foto en el detalle para ampliarla sigue siendo solo lectura.
- Texto del aviso:
  - Foto subida: «{subId} ya tiene foto. La nueva la reemplaza en Bayka y en los demás celulares en la próxima sincronización. No se puede deshacer.»
  - Foto que puede no haberse subido: «{subId} ya tiene una foto que puede no haberse subido a Bayka. La nueva la reemplaza. No se puede deshacer.»

## Implementación

- `utils/avisoReemplazarFoto.ts`: `textoReemplazarFoto`, `confirmarReemplazarFoto(show, foto, { onVerActual?, onConfirm })` y `confirmarReemplazoEnVisor`, que decide si el visor pregunta o va directo. Reusa `NO_SE_PUEDE_DESHACER`, que ahora se exporta desde `avisoQuitarFoto`.
- `FotoDeArbol` suma `reemplazoConfirmado`. Con ese flag, el visor de la botonera reemplaza sin preguntar. Hoy nada lo prende: queda listo para el botón de #751.
- `TreePhotoViewer.onReplace` ahora recibe la `FotoDeArbol` completa en vez del `treeId`.
- No cambia la lógica de `addPhotoToTree`/`updatePhoto`.

## Cómo probar

1. En un grupo, abrir el listado, entrar al detalle de un árbol con foto y tocar «Cambiar foto». Tiene que aparecer el aviso. Cancelar no abre la cámara.
2. Repetir y tocar «Ver actual»: se abre la foto con «Reemplazar». Tocarlo abre el selector Cámara/Galería sin otro aviso.
3. En un árbol sin foto, «Tomar foto» va directo al selector.
4. En la botonera, abrir el visor de la foto de un árbol (desde la tira o el listado) y tocar «Reemplazar»: aviso con Cancelar / Reemplazar.
5. Probar con una foto ya sincronizada y con una recién sacada para ver los dos textos.

## Tests

- `tests/utils/avisoReemplazarFoto.test.ts` (nuevo): textos de las dos variantes, botones y estilos con y sin «Ver actual», que Cancelar no confirma, que Ver actual no confirma, que Reemplazar confirma, y la decisión del visor con y sin `reemplazoConfirmado`.
- `tests/components/TreeDetailModal.test.tsx`: el aviso aparece antes de la cámara, sin foto va directo, Cancelar, Reemplazar, ampliar como solo lectura, Reemplazar desde Ver actual sin segundo aviso, y foto remota.
- `tests/components/TreePhotoViewer.test.tsx`: `onReplace` recibe la foto con el flag.
- CI local: `tsc`, `eslint --max-warnings 0`, jest unit (1915) e integración (399) en verde.

Cambia UI: lo mergea Facu.

Closes #750

author: nvizble
body:
## Summary

Fixes [ENG-19686](https://linear.app/nexus-labs/issue/ENG-19686). The hosted Streamable HTTP server answered an `Mcp-Session-Id` it didn't know with **400**. The MCP Streamable HTTP spec uses **404** to tell the client to drop the id and send a fresh `initialize`. Sessions live in memory, so every idle eviction, restart or redeploy left connected agents stuck on a 400 instead of reconnecting.

**Why it happened:** `handleMcp` looks up the session map *before* any SDK transport sees the request, so the SDK's own handling never ran. SDK 1.30.0 (the version in use) returns `404` with `{"code":-32001,"message":"Session not found"}` for an unknown id and `400` for a missing one. Our wrapper returned 400 for both.

## Changes

- `src/http.ts`: an id the server doesn't hold gets `404` with the same body the SDK sends (`-32001 "Session not found"`), on POST, GET and DELETE. A request with no session id, or a body that isn't JSON, still gets `400`. The JSON parse still runs before the session check, the same order the SDK uses, so a malformed body is a 400 even when it carries a stale id. The two old 400 branches are now one.
- `test/http.test.ts`: new test. It initializes a session, restarts the server (a fresh instance with an empty session store), and sends POST/GET/DELETE with the old id, expecting `404` and `-32001` each time. It checks that no-session and non-JSON requests still get `400`, then re-initializes with a real SDK client and calls `tools/list`. The idle-eviction test now checks for `{ code: 404 }` instead of a loose `/session/i` match.
- `README.md`: the session-lifetime paragraph said evicted sessions answer `400`. It now says `404`, and that a restart or redeploy loses sessions the same way.

## Tool surface impact

- [x] No change to the tool surface.

## API spec impact

- [x] No change to the targeted API spec version.

## Checklist

- [x] `npm run format` is clean.
- [x] `npm run lint` passes.
- [x] `npm run typecheck` passes.
- [x] `npm test` passes (195/195).
- [ ] smoke: not run. The change doesn't touch the tool surface or the client.

## How it was verified

- I wrote the new test first. Before the fix it failed with `expected 404, actual 400`, and so did the tightened eviction test. After the fix, all 195 tests pass locally (Node 22), along with lint, typecheck and `format:check`.
- **CI pending on the GitHub Actions outage.** I haven't re-run or waited on CI. The results above are local.

## Notes for reviewers

- This is a `fix:` and not marked breaking. It's a protocol-conformance fix, and a client that already handled 400 here was just giving up.
- Whether a client reconnects by itself is up to the client. The SDK 1.30.0 `StreamableHTTPClientTransport` throws `StreamableHTTPError` with `code: 404` and leaves the re-initialize to the host. The server now gives the signal the spec defines.
- This doesn't touch release PR #87 (0.4.0). release-please will pick this up for the next release.

author: jelmer
body: GNU make doesn't pair up brackets in variable names, so `x{ = 1` assigns to `x{`, but `name()` returned the whole line. BSD make's `Parse_IsVar` does pair them (with a level that can go negative) and rejects such lines as assignments, so BSD mode now classifies lines the same way. `name()` now ends the name at the operator before the value instead of rescanning with BSD rules.

author: amcmillion
body:
## Description
Adds Indonesian (`id`) as a supported locale across Alliance HQ web, Discord bot, and generated-surface pipelines. This is an initial implementation pass; all Indonesian copy is machine-translated and explicitly flagged for review.

## What changed
- `src/i18n/routing.ts`: added `"id"` to `locales` and `AppLocale`.
- `scripts/i18n/locales.json`: added `"id"` as a translation target.
- `messages/id.json`: generated Indonesian translation from `messages/en-US.json` using the project's i18n script.
- `messages/en-US.json` and `messages/pt-BR.json`: added the language selector label for Indonesian.
- `src/lib/discord/i18n.ts`: extended `DiscordBotLocale`, `MESSAGES`, `AUTHORIZE_MESSAGES`, `normalizeDiscordBotLocale`, and `parseLanguageChoice` to support `"id"`.
- `scripts/discord/register-commands.mjs`: added Indonesian `language` slash-command choices.
- Updated calendar, kills, THP, VR, plunder plan, time-off, VS calculator, member-link, notes intake, and regular-events modules to accept or normalize `"id"`.
- Fixed `web-thp.server.test.ts` and `web-kills.server.test.ts` mocks to include `normalizeDiscordBotLocale`.

## Copy (pending maintainer review)
All user-facing Indonesian strings live in `messages/id.json` and were produced automatically from the approved English source. They have **not** been hand-translated or reviewed by a native speaker. Please review/override `messages/id.json` before marking this PR ready to merge. Portuguese (`pt-BR`) labels for the Indonesian selector were added in the same commit.

## Local gates passed
Run in this session on `feat/indonesian-locale`:
- `npx tsc --noEmit`
- `npm run lint` (0 errors)
- `npm test` (6,619 passed, 184 skipped)
- `npm run i18n:validate` (warnings only)
- `npm run db:validate-journal`
- `npm run build`
- `npm run test:e2e` (687 passed, 5 skipped)

## Notes / assumptions
- The translation script was used to generate `messages/id.json` from `messages/en-US.json` because no hand translation was available. This is the main item to review.
- Discord bot language choice includes `id` and `id-ID` aliases (`Indonesian`, `Bahasa`) in `parseLanguageChoice`.
- No database migrations were required.
- `Events.zip` remains untracked from the previous session and was not included.
